Friendly staff convinced me to buy the $5 per year club card to get lower prices - a decent investment if you shop there as often as I do.  Professionals (bring your license) get an even better deal.  Combs, brushes, flat irons and nail supplies.  Skin care selection is limited.

Nope. Unimpressed.  Yes, it's inexpensive but you are MUCH better off going 1/2 a block down the street to the Asian (Vietnamese) place or across the street for Oasis Lebanese.  We stopped in because the Vietnamese place was closed and we figured we'd check it out.  Both of us had $9.95 bento lunch boxes and mine (Salmon Basil) was not good at all.  Frozen and fishy tasting salmon that was DEEP FRIED (Ick.).  I ate the other stuff.   Miso soup was fine.  $2.00 up charge for Thai Chicken Coconut soup insteadof Miso (also good).  Not a fan.  Sorry.

Everything tastes better on somebody else's dime...  Meanwhile I attended a "heavy app" holiday party at JG last night. Nathan - who took care of our raucous party of 22, kept the drinks flowing and I tried the FABULOUS Butterscotch (supposed to have a bit of bourbon in there??) Latte.  Dessert in a cup.  Beef sliders were cooked very rare - which I did not mind, but others complained. Charcuterie and cheeses (and heavenly fig jam) were artfuly displayed and delicious to eat.  Mini crab cakes (puffs) were fried and fattening.  Flatbread with mushrooms, truffle oil and fried ege was a BIG hit.  Try the beers here, too!  My faith has been restored.  Although I still don;t like paying $30 - $0 for lunch - I just might come here again pretty soon.  Gotta get me another of those $6 calorie-bomb lattes.

Had a much better time now that my little one is 6.5. She was too freaked out by the Spies & Saboteurs Exhibit (there is a KKK part that she found very disturbing)  But she LOVED the 17 minute show in the Kimmel Theater (Freedom Rising) and the "carpet game" for kids on the top floor.  We became members through Groupon, so from now through next June we'll be living there.

They had 1 of the 2 obscure items I needed (wish they carried both).  Helpful staff - friendly service.  No issues here.  Please stock "blue denim" doggie diapers.  My elderly pug needs then (we currently can only get the at MonsterPets in South Philly).

Not nearly as nice as the Union League - but the food is good and maybe even better here - plus you have those gorgeous views of the city.  For a holiday party ofr networking event - it's a great spot.  As long as someone else is paying - I'll be there.  But there is NO WAY I'd join as a a member.  Too much money.  They easily accomodate large or small groups and have some meeting rooms that are cozy for the small ones.

Even though I much prefer to shop at the Giant in Aston (or Whole Foods in Glen Mills when time and budget permits), I stopped in here and customer service was so, so, so much better than at Giant.  I bought a jar of jam for my dad and it turned out not to be the right kind. They took it back 5 days later (unopened, of course) with no receipt. This is a rare occurrence and I was hoping they would not give me any problems.  I am very pleased.

Nearly 5 stars - what a great place to sit and have a drink (try the house made ginger ale - so perfectly refreshing) or a franglo-pub lunch.  The house burger is quite good and comes with frites AND a nice green salad.  A good place to meet a client, conduct an interview or just hang out.

I really love Harvest - but during peak times the acoustics are LOUD!!!!! Our server Ian was terrific and explained the menu and dishes well.  My husband enjoyed the shortrib entree.  Potstickers ($10 - ouch!) were fried and IMO over cooked.  I enjoyed the quinoa salad - and a small was plenty for me ($6) and loved the shrimp (2 large deliciously seasoned shrimp) crabmeat cocktail served over gazpacho and a thick slice of yellow tomato.  Love it here - and can't wait to come back. A little pricey but great for a date or a family meal.

This 3 star rating is for the Deli Department.  I give a MUCH higher rating to the produce manager.  I had a part and ordered (well in advance) a $59.99 cold cut tray and a $19.99 Chocolate-dipped strawberry tray (excellent and a great value).  There were many issues with both quality and presentation of the (medium sized) tray. I spoke to the manager (LeighAnn) who was gracious and promptly refunded my $60 plus gave me a $10 gift card.  (Very nice to do that!).  5 star customer service - but I would have preferred a 5 star party tray. Please "step up your game", Acme Deli.    I am not likely to order trays from here again.  P.S.  We are still very, very grateful to this Acme for supporting our girl scout troop.  I would like to be supportive of Acme as well.  Sure wish that party tray had been good.

OMG - it's still here! This is the Taco Bell from my childhood - and it has been renovated a couple of times since the '90's.  Not a big T-bell fan - but in a pinch, it's here. I avoid fast food whenever possible.

This is such a cutesy place to shop for everything your pooch would ever need.  My daughter loves to browse in here, too.  I have a sweet 12 year old male puggy - and they are so nice to us.  Great advice on pet care, too.
Very bondage oriented but a good selection of toys and adult enhancement items in a no-pressure environment.  Fun to browse.

This place is kinda depressing. Server, Rae, was nice - and attentive. Place was nearly empty on a Monday night.  Salad that came with the meal was pretty bad - lettuce was overly wet, cut into tiny pieces and starting to rust (turn brown).  The 2 slices of tomato and 2 sliced of un-peeled waxy cucumber were at least edible.  The supposedly home-made russian dressing was just awful (thank goodness I ordered it on the side).  The entree itself was OK - veal francese (I know!  What possessed me -next time, if there is a next time as I am not prone to return, I will get a gyro or pancakes or something "easier").  Surprisingly good.  3 stars even - but the salad skeeved me.  Ugly interior - but at least they seem to be re-doing the ladies room.  As I said, I will not rush back.  I much prefer the court diner.

Food was fine - 4 star and service a little slow (2 star) by seasoned waitresses, like Eleanor. Decor?  Ick.  Like an old cafeteria.  Decent for burgers or sandwiches.  I enjoyed my onion rings and patty melt but our 10 year old did not like the Chicken Caesar salad at all.  BLT looked great - at $4.99.  Decent prices.

Horrid parking lot when this place is busy. Otherwise it's fine.  I was able to get the liquor I needed in a pinch for a Memorial Day party.  Usually we try to avoid PA and shop at Total Wine & More in Delaware.  Don;t get me started on PA's antiquated liquor laws.  I feel awful for bar owners, too!

A nice place to hang out and eat/drink/shop.  They've done a nice job with it.  I wonder though, if you live in one of those big, new buildings, does the noise level in the summer (especially on Saturday nights) preclude a quiet family life??  Just sayin'...

Visited 3 times in the summer of 2016 -Liberty Bell, NMAJH, Constitution Center, City Tavern and many local restaurants, cafes and shops.  I am proud and glad to live in the Greater Philadelphia area.

I get my cheapie manicures and polish changes here because they are clean and quick.  I am not feeling secure enough to get a pedicure here though as I am a complete hygiene snob and a pedi-connoisseur.  I used to go to Mint Julip for pedis - but my favorite vernisseur left.  I guess it's back to Salon Royale Court for pedi's from now on.  Meanwhile - need a quick eyebrow wax or a mani (or $6.00 polish change?)  Hurry.  Pick-color!

4.5 stars - just a hair shy of 5.  I just attended a private luncheon event at the Union League in the McMichael room.  The service was "White Glove" and so attentive and wonderful.  Food was good - with a great salad that contained dried cranberries, toasted oine nuts & crumbled bleu.  Also a stand-out were the individually plated pecan pies.  YUM-O!  The entrees, however were just "OK" my fish stuffed with crabmeat bechamel was a tad dry and OVERLY salty.  I can't speak to the other entree choice - roast pork - as I don't "do pig".  But it looked nice.  Great presentation and a great, historic space with lots of portraits to look at - one of George W. was being hung with great care the day I was there.  You can also (try to) have your wedding here - but you really "gotta know someone" to get on the list.  Oh - and there IS an enforced dress code - so don't be the bopob that I was and show up wearing sheakers.  (I KNEW I shoulda hauld my shoes along..)  They snuck me in thru the back.

I came here alone for lunch on a dead-to-the-world August Thursday at about 12:15 PM.  Place was nearly empty and thus, I had attentive and Stellar service from a lovely young lady (I forgot her name).  Good music on in the background (we had just lost Aretha Franklin today so lots of 50's and 60's tunes, including the Queen of Soul and BB King).  But even better was the $9.79 2 meat combo for lunch.  Wow!  I'm gonna need a nap at my desk fter that feast of ribs (2 - but very tender and delicious) and 1/4 chicken dark.   Those corn muffins taste like cake.  $2.99 for a diet soda seems way high though... In any case, Famous Dave's is a chain so you know what you are getting when you go. Decent 'cue in a chain-y environment.

Wow - I can't believe it took me this long to yelp the Constitution Center.  This really is a must-stop place for visitors & tourists as well as residents.  The exhibits are historically accurate and a bit of fun - although kinda dull for the very young (our 4 year old would rather run the halls).  The performance is not a great for young kids - too boring - but we, as parents, enjoyed it.   (And the respite of sitting down for a few!!)
I just can't stop raving about Matyson.  Just had lunch today - House made pappardele with kale and shortribs.  Delectable.    Go there NOW!

I shopped here twice today first before a meeting (didn;t have enough time to try on) and again after the meeting ended AND after a trip to BCBG (see my review on them).  I tried on an exquisite hot pink $248 trench coat (yes, really) and some cute tops.  I settled on a strectch black knit top.  Decent price, too - reduced from 59.98 to 29.98.  SOLD!!!!  Note:  I cam back about 2 weeks later and the tank tops were on sale. ($19.99 each) snagged 2 of 'em and another cute sleeves top marked $49.98 but reduced by 30%. - Morale of story? The sales are good.  Ryan and the other lady at the front counter were very nice and helpful - but probably because the place was nearly empty both times I visited today.  I think they are HURTING for sales.

Wow!!!!!  I am gonna go out on a limb here and give these fine people the full 5 stars (some may argue its a 4 star experience - but what we had last night was truly 5 stars all the way.)  NOTE:  We also went BACK on 4/4/09 and it was fabulous AGAIN!  Starting with the bar and terrific bartender who mixed me a fine Whiska-retto Sour (That's a Canadian Club Whisky Sour with a splash of Amaretto to sweeten it up. - YUM.).  The bar has a retro feel with colored shelves that slant at different angles to display the bottles of liquor.  Next we (there were 4 of us) were seated by our gracious host/waiter/manager (possibly owner?) and ordered lots of tasty treats.  We started with an appetizer course.  I had a terrific goat cheese (mild - not too goaty) and beet salad.  2 of us has the slightly salty but very tasty French Onion Soup, and we all tasted the Chicken Shumai (obviously frozen - but tasty nonetheless.).  Also the stuffed portabello mushroom is SO TERRIFIC.  Since one of the entrees - Pasta "Mikey" appealed to all of us - we ordered one order and split it 4 ways on 4 little plates as a pasta course.  The pasta was penne, coated in a rich, creamy pink sauce accented with shavings of proscuitto.  Very tasty and perfect as an app.  (May be too rich to eat a big plateful.)  For entrees the standout was the lamb - a gorgeous frenched rack of 8 chops total, served with airy riced potatoes and asparagus spears.  The meatlof entree (with more of the delicious mash) and my husband's "special" of flaky-crusted chicken pot pie, all disappeared.  We were nearly stuffed by now, but stayed for delicious rich cups of freshly brewed coffe and decaf.  And split amongst us 1 cheesecake (classic and creamy) and a decadent chocolate bourbon pecan pie.  (The crust of which was outstanding.).  We have returned twuce.  What lovely evenings we have had,  surrounded by gorgeous decorations and the classic portraits that adorn the walls.  This is a unique place that seems like "nothing" when you walk by.  Go INSIDE!!!  Go!!!  You will not be disappointed.

Solid!  A great new choice for lunch ($7 for dark, $8 for white 1/4 with 2 sides).  My BFF and I got a 1/2 chicken and 2 sides for $11.50 - 2 sides were plenty for us to share.  We chose the cornbread mini-muffins (so good) and mac 'n cheese (my friend loved it, I wasn't wowed.)  Meanwhile the chicken is the star of the show.  Not too salty, yet nicely seasoned and perfected rotisseried.  It was very warm in there - even with the A/C running.  (All those rotisseries)/  Decent service, too.

This place is kinda depressing. Server, Rae, was nice - and attentive. Place was nearly empty on a Monday night.  Salad that came with the meal was pretty bad - lettuce was overly wet, cut into tiny pieces and starting to rust (turn brown).  The 2 slices of tomato and 2 sliced of un-peeled waxy cucumber were at least edible.  The supposedly home-made russian dressing was just awful (thank goodness I ordered it on the side).  The entree itself was OK - veal francese (I know!  What possessed me -next time, if there is a next time as I am not prone to return, I will get a gyro or pancakes or something "easier").  Surprisingly good.  3 stars even - but the salad skeeved me.  Ugly interior - but at least they seem to be re-doing the ladies room.  As I said, I will not rush back.  I much prefer the Court diner or the new Aston Diner

Jamie sums it up - this is the Adult version of Plato's Closet. I found some cheap and cute (new with tags on) items but nothing that fit well. I will be back to try again.   Excellent service from Nyra (nyla?) from NYC.

Went to CVS (across the street and down a bit) too get passport pictures taken.  Their camera was broken so I came here.  Should have came here first - much cleaner and emptier store.  Meanwhile the lady running their photo center could not get the proper label to print.  I waited and waited for my pictures.  Finally she just let me HAVE them.  Free.    They need to figure out their photo procedures better.

Valentine's Day weekend and service by Laura was wonderful even if we could only get a 5 PM or 8:30 PM res.  We opted for 5 PM and there was still a huge crowd.  Appetizer sampler ($20) was great as well as Duck App. The kiddo devoured it. Sashimi was MUCH fresher and better this time including the ($27) Blue Fin lover's plate and a few pieces of toro ($8 a pop) and Ikura ($4.50).  No room for dessert but we left happy.

Dear Nail Salon,  I confess! Today I cheated on you, my usual nail salon, with Noble Nails. Kim is an excellent technician and gave me a straightforward, basic manicure with the new OPI Nail Envy Color Formula.  I am anxious to see how many days wear I can get out of it.  My hands were is dire need of cuticle care, and Kim is a true professional. The salon is clean and well run.  If I lived near here, I would DEFINITELY be back. $10 mani, $22 gel and $22 pedis.  (They also have $30 hot stone spa pedis.  YAY!!!!!)  They also carry CND - including my beloved Vinyluxx. I can get 6-8 days out of a Vinyluxx Mani!  Loving it here so far.

OK, I will be nice and cut them a break.  It should be 2 or 2.5 stars, but I am hoping they will work out the kinks and improve.  The menu sounded sooooo wonderful and my friend was keen to try Root - so we went.  The place was dead empty when we arrived, but throughout our meal about 8 people were dining.  Definitely BYO something - they have NOTHING to drink but water.  Turns out this is the site of the former Palate BYOB.  I guess they just couldn't make it.  The food is really not great.  (Which is a shame because they claim to use sustainable and local ingredients and I strive to support it.  The tattoo-covered chef and the server (a nice gal) were hospitable.  Here's what made the food more like 2 stars.  I started with the poached shrimp salad.  It came with 2 large, overcooked a bit rubbery shrimp.   The greens were shredded and appeared to be romaine and napa cabbage in a tangy vinaigrette.  The drizzle of (good quality) balsamic around the plate edge was good.  Now the strange entree.  (We skipped dessert  -  didn't want to chance it.)  I ordered the rabbit and oxtail raviolo with uni cream.  The Oxtail was the best part - rich, and meaty with a delicious flavor.  The rabbit really did taste like dark meat chicken.  And the sauce was heavy - but tasty.  Here's a the bad part - the crepes were heavy as lead.  Kinda like a cross between home-made paste (flour & water) and Bisquick.  Really strange.  Not deelicate at all, and certainly not like pasta - more like a home-made leaden buscuit that fell flat.  It's really a shame.  I am hoping they can figure it out - and they really, really need A/C or at least a few more fans.  Sadly I am not one of them...

This is a review of the Macy's located in the Cheryy Hill mall.  We had a fun day of shopping noth at Nordstrom and here at Macy's.  My friend got 2 amazing pair of shoes at great prices.  The sales are worth checking out.
Many thanks to the Acme on Baltimore Pike in Media for supporting our girl scout troops and graciously allowing them to seel Girl Scout cookies at their stores.  We are so grateful for this!

Took our 2012 Hyundai herefor annual inspection and a few minor repairs. Had a 9:30 AM appointment and arrived early - 9:15.  Inspection was done (including oil change) in about 1 hour while I waited.  Took another 90 minutes for repair work.  Killed the whole morning - but at least not the entire day. TV in waiting area with coffee and a water cooler.  Thankful we got out in about 3 hours.
Our 10 year old LOVES this store and we come in all the time now. Gonna ask for gift cards for her next birthday.  Check out the selection of nightlights of all things.  Wonderful things.

OK, now that my 3 year old is nearly 7 - this place is a wee bit more appropriate.  (Incidentally she had her 6th birthday party and will have her 7th also at North Bowl).  Meanwhile - we popped in for a quick game (she bowled - I watched - our poor server, Dennis (bless his heart) served us 2 glasses of water).  $11.00 for 1 game ($5.95) plus show rental.  Sheesh.  Glad I didn;t order a cocktail.  Meanwhile - the BASE price for a kis party here is now $25 a head.  The music was very loud - but they turned it down for us. Lanes are clean and seating is comfortable.  Very "clubby" - just as it was when we came here years ago.  The 7 year old loves it! (But - she did say that she likes North Bowl better - and so do I for many reasons.)  It sure ain't the crappy old bowling alley that I grew up with!

Did they re-model? Something seems better about this beer-stocked deli - snacks, sandwiches and all the usual suspects.  A wide selection of cold drinks.  Good location - and hours.  No issues from me.

Yup.  This is the place.  This place is worthy of my 600th review on yelp!!!  It has the sentimental factor (CHeck) - we ate here right after meeting with the Judge who would marry us.  It has the location factor (Philly burbs).  It has - most importantly -great Mexican food and free Margarita's in a strip mall.  You gotta love that loosely interpreted liquor law.  Go, Pennsylvania!  In any case we thoroughly enjoyed (and JUSt - I mean just barely - beat the dinner crowd by getting there at 5:25 PM on a weekday. ) our home-made salsa fresca, chips and terrific guac.  I had chicken in a mole sauce - but it was different some how - and really special.  My (then) fiance had lamb - which her really enjoyed.  Not cheap - but so worth it.  What a surprise and a pleasant one. By the time we left the place was PACKED - and i bet they will continue to pack 'em in.  By the way - free or not - the Margarita's were very good, indeed.

Woo Jung (Brother is Woo, Sister is Jung) is a Korean owned Japanese place (with Hwe Dup Bap on the menu!) in a strip mall in East Norriton.  I was honestly scared to even try it but I am so glad I did.  The staff is wonderful and my experience was terrific as a single diner on a dead-empty Friday lunch.  I ordered the $16.95 lunch special which came with 6 pieces of sashimi (all were excellent - included seared/sauced Chu-Toro!  Score!!!!!!) and 3 nigiri (Tuna, Salmon and a white fish - not sure which - not yellowtail).  The accompanying spicy tuna roll was delicious as well.  Miso soup had a slight sweetness of Mirin. Very nice.  I can't wait to return!!  BYO - and a little pricey for lunch but worth it for a special treat. Now, maybe they'll add some galbi to the menu???  Thank you, Jung!!!!!

The food is excellent but Soooooo pricey.  The cafe next door is a better value - and similar food choices.  But what really makes this place special are the sweeping views of Longwood gardens.    I love it there!
Convenient location but super crowded on weekdays during the lunch hour(s) as a result.  I got in and out fast.  THANK goodness they had what I needed.
Top-quality, good looking breakable gift items.  Lamps, baubles, shiny stuff and GOREOUS, gorgeous gifties.  It's been around forever and I love it.

OK - I take back some of what I said. After a year has passed - I returned to Tierra Mia today and found a few things have changed.  The icy-cold receptionist is gone (YAY) and I was treated very well during my visit today.  I started with a $58 pedicure with the coconut oil & fresh coconut shavings as the exfoliant.  It was done by Karina herself and was FANTASTIC.  I hope the polish will wear well - as my feet feel FAB-U-LOUS.  Again - I reiterate the pedicure chair she bought has sounds therapy - ask for the headphones - that vibrates in time to relaxing music.  It is a reall cool, wonderful pedicure chair.  I would pay money just to come and sit in it for a while.  After my pedi - which took about 60 minutes, I got the seasonal cucumber mani.  It was $28 and used pure shea butter, sea salt and cruished cucumbers (they put it in a food processor).  Very cooling and wonderful for summer.  Justin - Karina's fiance was there - and he is a very nice guy and runs things well.  It's a beautiful (pricey) spa.  I am fearful the polish will yellow or chip. (I told them about my previous experience with yellowing - and they said NO SUNSCREEN or bug spray.  Turns out I had, indeed, applied sunscreen after my services a year ago - MY BAD!)  I still wish we could bring our own polish - and I kinda thing it's ridiculous that for the MONEY we are paying (I dropped $100 even today including tip) we can't use our OPI or CND products for fear of destrying her air quality.  That still seems a bit wrong, but anyway - If I can get a decent wear out of her products (all water based polishes), I will come back again.  Definitely for pedis - not sure if I can justify a $28 mani every week - or even every 2.  Tierra Mia - you are a beatiful, unique place.  I am sure you will be very successful.
El kiddo is now 11 and still loves coming here.  Expensive but fun.

Yay to Rebecca Michaels for expanding the Flying Monkey empire.  The new space is small, but so cute - and the color scheme continues the theme.  You can get all the goodies you know and love from the Reading Terminal location here in the gayborhood.  Go, monkey, go!

I can not believe how clean, new, slick, friendly and pleasant my experience was at the new (actually 5 mos. old) Panda Express, fast-food Chinese in the Comcast Center.  Normally I can not stand sloppy, gloppy, steam-table, mall Chinese - so boy was I shocked when the food not only looked great (albeit lots of the choices and all of the shrimp choices are fried) but tasted good, too.  Trepidatious bynature I ordered only a small a la carte (1/2 pint) box of Honey Walnut Shrimp (Fried + Mayonnaise + Sugar = health BOMB) and instantly recalled the bygone era of late 1980's Chinese-American fare.  The Manager, Jay,  was very accomodating and said that now - for large orders (and within a few blocks) they will deliver and the offer party trays and catering.  The even have a deal they will do with schools for fundraising.  The wheels are turning...  Perhaps a Panda Feast (for $30 you get 3 large entress and 2 large sides - enough for 4 (easily) to 7 (tiny eaters) people.  A big pan entree $36 - $48 if you pick shrimp feeds about 8 people.  They also have a small catering package for $96 that easily feeds 16.  I am planning a prty soon and will update my review with the results - but so far I am shockingly pleased with Panda Express.

The Equinox cheese is fabulous!  Birchrun Hills Farm sells cheese at many local farmers market (I usually see them at Media and Headhouse. They also make blue and "Fat Cat" - a semi-soft cheese.  They also supply veal to local restaurants.  Good local stuff!

Still Excellent after all these years.  A gal-pal and I shared the potato latke app with our lunch today - what BLISS.  3 petite, crisp, flavorful (not too greasy) pancakes topped with lightly salted smoked salmon, applsauce and dill creme fraiche.  WOW.  My Kale salad was over-the-top delicious and lightly dressed with the perfect amount of lemon/oregano vinaigrette (You could taste juice and zest) with parmesan slivers and sweet, glorious butternut squash chunks.  I got a small for $7 - but next time I may just get the large ($10).  Good, good, good stuff.  Very nice server, too.  GO TO MATYSON.  So rockin' good.

Ok - I upgraded them to 5 stars based on our last visit (we have now been there about 4-5 times.)  This time we came with our 6 year old at night and had pancakes, a chef salad (with delicious FRESH cooked turkey breast) and FABULOUS home-made pierogi.  Do not miss them.  The re-modelled and added 2 new bathrooms (lovely) and I just love the Court Diner.

This place is more of a shop and less of a tea bar - for a tea bar see Remedy down the street and around the corner - but STEAP has a great selection of fine and rare loose leafs.  I like both Remedy and Steap - but I prefer to buy tea here and drink tea at Remedy.  The Iced Peach White I tried over the summer was terrific.  No sweetener needed.  It was naturally fruity and sweet with a clean finish.  YUM!  Oh - and teas and tea-gear from STEAP make for cute gifts.
An American classic and a Philadelphia GAYborhood staple.  Help save Giovanni's!  This place is a needed gem and a beacon for free-speaking, free-thinking Americans, gay or not.  Love it here!

A solid 4 stars (the Beet Salad was 5 star for me) with swanky decor, clean restrooms, great service from Tim and a healthy wine list.  (A few more sparklers by the glass would be nice.  I loved the beet salad app (Got a small for $5) served with pickled SWEET cippolini onions and served atop a small amount of tasty goat cheese cream (not too goaty).  I also enjoyed the mushroom papardelle - loaded with asparagus, garlic slices and of course - lots of 'shrooms.  My partner's food came out cold - but they promptly heated it up. His sweet potato mash was far to nutmegy for me - but the side of mac 'n cheese ($5) was terrific.  Bison meatloaf was $22 and served with baby carrots and broccolini (a bit salty).  Not 5 stars - but very close - a lovely lunch was $66 without booze and without dessert - so that is a bit pricey.  (My cappucino was $6 - OUCH.

I agree with Caroline AND Emily.  We take our little girl here and she LOVES it - especially all the animals.  They have activities in every season - even winter time. Xmas trees, Halloween Hay rides, Strawberry picking in spring.  Love it!  And yes - we make her wash her hands after petting the goats and before eating ice cream (or apple turnovers!!!)  Aliitle touristy and a few items in the market have HIGH prices - but hey - the loval produce is terrific.  We love it here.

I agree with Alice L.  (Though historically I have alsways enjoyed sampling the Violet and Rose flavors.)  The store is VERY old and has been a New Hope institution for years.  It COULD use a clean up.  I do enjoy the ice cream here - but willl not go during peak tourist season as I will NOT wait in a line for it.  The owner is a character - that said I have never had any bad experiences here.  Only tasy ice cream!

Had dinner at the sushi bar on a busy Saturday night (no reservation so no tables available - but plenty of sushi bar spots early on).  Excellent service by our server and expediter as well as the 2 "junior level" sushi chefs.  DH ordered edamame and chicken teri (yeah, I know) which he enjoyed. I had a small (which was huge - I can't imagine how enormous the large must be) Tom Kha which is one of my faves.  I have had Tom Kha at many places and the Tom Kha hear was overly sweet and thick with too much coconut milk and lacked the lemongrass and complexityy that a good Tom Kha should have.  That said - it was tasty but bland.  not exciting at all. Would not reorder it here unless I am having an intense Tom Kha Craving.  The Blue Fin lovers platter was deliciously fresh - and the complimentary veggie naruto roll was crisp and refreshing.  Since aside from Temaki in Media, this is the best sushi we have found (Yes, we've tried Margaret Kuo's and Azie)  we shall return.  And next time we'll make a reservation!  Oh - and the prices are on the high side.

OK, I am only reviewing the front lobby bar and the meeting facilities and food - all of which were solid and good.  I did not stay overnight here so I can't comment on the rooms.  Meanwhile, I attended a nice corporate event here last night (with dinner included) and a colleague drove - so he knew exactly where it was - BUT even he mentioned that the signage is weak and it's very hard to find this place if you don't know where to look.  We started with drinks at the lobby bar.  I had a fairly weak and not too spicey 3 star Bloody Mary.  It came with a slice of lemon and when I asked the female bartended (very sweet lady) for celery she said they did not have it.  OK.  Points off for that.  If you want a kickin' Bloody Mary by the way - try Bar North Third. but I digress...  Mmmn.  Now  I want a bloody mary.  OK.  Next it was off to the dinner/meeting.  The tables were pre-set with very warm butter (had been sitting out for quite some time).  The immediately plated chilled caesar salads that were very good - basic and crisp.  Not overly dressed.  The rolls were hot - which was a nice touch.  My entree - wild mushroom ravioli - was very tasty - and looked much better that the chicken marsala (1/2 a semiboned breast with a wing drumette attached - looked very banquet - and ONE mushroom.)  I was glad I did not order the chicken - but people ate it and seemed 3 -4 star happy.  Dessert was a moist carrot cake garnished with a single wilted strawberry.  All in all - things could have used a bit more polish and freshening up.  Service was very efficient - a bit too "hurry up and let the staff leave" for my taste.  Coffee was fresh and very yummy.  Meeting rooms was nice - standard hotel corporate stuff.  I have a feeling I'll be back for future events here.
Love coming here to bird-watch and walk around on a nice spring or summer day with el kiddo.  Free - and fun and can e educational.  Good for biking, too.

OMG! What a "scene"- if you want to people watch or have "dinner & a show" in tiny-cramped-Manhattan-style tables, this just might be the place for you.  A friend and I met for lunch - which wound up costing me $23.00 for an iced tea and a shrimp salad ($18.00 - ouch!).  She had a hair in her pizza - Eeeeew! Luckily the staff were gracious about it and whisked it away and didn't charge us for it.  The owners of Serafina chain (we used to go to the one on Madison in NYC and it, too, was a "scene"), were holding court with a bunch of leggy PR ladies.  Plus the Chairman of my old law firm was in the house.  What a freakish afternoon.  Decent, overpriced food served with a generous helping of hype - but so not my bag, baby.  Kudos to our lovely server Ayram - I pray does not have to suffer there too long.  Serafina should do well in Center City.   If you are a displaced Manhattanite and long for the old days - this place will do you right.  (Try the carpaccio - looks great.)

Free internet access and (as I happen to be an ING account holder) access to your banking.  Plus if you wear orange (like that EVER happens??) on certain days your coffee is free.  Kitschy come-ons and cool swag to be had here as well.  I really enjoy banking with ING Direct and the coffe shop is a nice addition.  But they need to clean those bathrooms more often - or else they'll be downgraded to 3 or even 2 stars.  They get GROSS!!!

My daughter enjoys the "square pizza" slices here (She refers to Sicilian as "square pizza") but even she at the astute age of 8 commented, "It's good - but not as good as Brooklyn".  Sums it up perfectly.  Smart kid.  Like her Momma.

Somewhere between Meh and A-OK. I attended a meeting here in the front bar area at the tables behind the bar.  Happy hour was ending so there were some luke-warm mozzarella sticks and dried out wings in a chafing dish.  Yuck.  (But free.)  The food I ordered (albeit a garden salad) was fresh but boring. Others plates looked unappetizing - fish & chips was a huge piece of fish in a THICK coating of batter.  (And chips which I don't eat).  Servers were pleasant and owner is a wonderful supporter of the community and my kid's school - but I am not impressed by the "classic" pub fare.  Also it gets LOUD in there, but that is a sign of a good pub.  Blah.
Surrisingly good food located in the bowels of Suburban Station. Breakfast wraps are made to order and fresh - $3.50 each.  Friendly cashier lady and cooks.

Matyson used to stand for Matt y Sonia - but, alas, the original owners have fled the coop.  However, the place is still run by a member of the family and for a BYOB - this place ROCKS.  I have been there for both lunch (many times) and dinner - just a few.  The $45 prix fixe is a deal - IF you like what they are serving.  Most times I pick and choose - and let me just say that you can not go wrong with the fish.  For lunch a delicious trout sandwich on fresh black bread with watercress for just $11 is terrific.  I have also tried the lobster pop-overs.  A warm, buttery pop-over (man I could eat about 4 of them plain) with large pieces of lobstermeat surrounded in a DECADENT (read: just a bit too much cream, for me) newburg style sauce with fresh chopped tomtato and presh green peas.  They also love morel mushrooms.  Dishes are complex without being "snooty" or "over the top". Desserts are great, too.  LOVE Mat-y-son - even under the new regime.
i went there with my daughters girl scout troop. the reason that i gave it a 3 is because the pancakes were sour and the fruit was not sweet.the rest was fine

Yum, yum, yum, yum, yum!  Yum.  Oh yeah.  Did I mention this is the real italian sorbetto / gelato.  The sorbettos are all dairy-free and still have a fabulous rich texture.  The flavors - sublime - like Blood Orange (the real McCoy), and Campari Grapefruit.  Last night they had a summertime offering of Lemon Opal Basil.  Want something fattening and decadent?  Get a cone (the euro-stle crisp cone) with a scoop of Dulce du Leche or Butterscoth and 1 scoop of deep, dark, ciocolatto sciurro (bitter dark choc.).  FREE home-made whipped cream is UNSWEETENED and compliments most selections.  Or - get a BRIOCHE, baby!  And fill it with frozen bliss.  The unsweetened whipped cream is complimentary.  You can feel your arteries clogging with each decadent mouthful.  OK, gotta go do cardio now...

This place used to be called Zai Fa and was mediocre then and is a touch better (In my opinion) now.  We ordered about $100 worth of food which easily fed our crowd of 10 adults and 2 little kids.  Fried Dumplings were better than the steamed - average and a bit "doughy".  Eggrolls and Shrimp Egg rolls were crisp, contained actual shrimp and lots of shredded cabbage.  Spare ribs were meaty and EXCELLENT. (Even better than Hong Kong Jack's which is our family's go-to for D-town old-school Chinese).  House special fried rice was just OK - Hong Kong Jack's is better. Chicken with Broccoli was ordered "light on the sauce" and thus was not nearly as greasy as it could have been.  They use brown sauce for their Chix 'n Brox.  My husband and Brother-in-law like hot food and enjoyed the General Tso's Chicken (looked very nice - text book Tso!) and Mongolian Beef. Combo platters are a good value and while they are heavy on the fried rice - there is a hefty portion of the entree (in our case Kung Pao Chicken) in there, too.  Very good egg drop, wonton and hot 'n sour soups (all are text book 1975 recipe Chinese American).  While not mind blowing - I can definitely see ordering Quart of Hot 'n Sour or Wonton the mext time I have the flu.  It is take out only (They might have 2 tiny tables out front) and be sure to grab your packets of duck, soy and mustard sauces on the way out.

4 stars for the spa - but 5 STARS for Cheryl Lee - the best damned nail technician that I have ever known.  Her spa pedicure is worth every penny and is like heaven on earth for me.  Well - I am one of Cheryl lee's faithful following.  Cheryl is just about the BEST nail tech you'll ever know.  I came to spa elysium on a very hectic, very icy, overbooked day before Xmas.  The expansive salon (spa is downstairs - nails & hair upstairs) was buzzing with activity and the front desk greeters were just not paying attention.  There was NOWHERE to sit in the waiting room (it was that packed) and many stylists were running late so people were getting grumpy.  Meanwhile, sunny Cheryl was running right on time.  (I arrived by train about an HOUR early.)  I started with a luxurious spa pedicure - which I can not recommend enough.  I also indulged and got a spa manicure ($25 vs. the regular $18 mani.)  Next time I will get a regular mani.  The extra exfoliating scrub was nice - but not needed each and every time.  I just love the way Cheryl does her nail services.  Very clean, thorugh and attentive to details.  My feet were smooth and cuticles neatly cleaned up. The polish was applied precisely and immaculately.  Cheryl - you are 5 stars in my book - but please tell the spa management teamt o shore up their front desk operations.  A busy spa/salon needs freindly attentive people at the front.

I wanted to love it here - and the owners are incredibly sweet - especially the owners mother - but the food just was not great.  I had the tulip dumplings which were slightly hard on top. My husband's drunken noodles were over cooked (chicken was a little dry and noodles a bit mushy).  Also $7.95 for a salad of solely steamed snow peas with a few mushrooms on top is obscene.  I love Thai food and I liked the people here - but we won;t be rushing back. Heng's Thai in Sprinfield or even Nooddi down the street had better food.

I am giving this a high mark based on the ONE birthday party we attended there today as a guest.  The 2 staff members who worked with the 15 kids (aged 2 - 6 - mostly 5 year olds) were lovely especially Sun.  They supervised 60 minutes of Gym activities (including the Air Track - a big inflatable trampoline-type thing that the kids just LOVED).  The parties are based on 15 kids and cost $300 ($320 for non-members) plus $35 extra for the air track.  Cake is NOT included, but all the paper goods, balloons and everything else is all done for you.  I have been to lots of kids parties recently, and this place was well run and a good active place to have a party for a 4, 5, 6 or even 7 year old.  I can not comment on their gymnastics or dance classes.

I called Triple A when I had a slow-leak flat and they dispensed Dan from Jamison;s towing.  Dan is terrific - he was patient and explained everything well.  He also inflated all 4 tires and I was able to get on my way.  Thank goodness for triple A and Jamison's was just fine, in my opinion.  I did not require any major repairs.

We had a terrific time here on opening day (3/27/09) and had makeovers at the jam-packed Chanel counter in the jam-packed cosmetics department.  Scored some great new eyeshadows and Glossimer.  We ogled the David Yurman counter and tried on some fancy shoes.  I adore Nordie's and am so glad there is now one nearby.

Meh.xican Post. Meh.  Bleh.  Blech?  I love the peom the lady wrote.  The service and noise level are just awful.  And yes, this is gringo-philly-mex.  How I miss my Gordo Tacqueria in CA.  In philly I like Xochitl or Tequilas (both are pricey and haute-mex - not taco joints.)  When, oh WHEN will we get a good taqueria in Center City?  And, no, Qdoba does not count.

There are now so many Doggie Styles around it  feels chainish.  Anyhow - this cutesy dog boutique (this is for the one on 20 & Walnut - they are all a little sifferent) has doggie gifts and treat, plus cute gear and clothing for big dogs or small.

It's not bad - but nothing much to write home about.  Brunch is probably the saving grace and they are accomodating - somewhat- to my 3 year old daughter.  Not a fave for me - but OK for a brunch.  Oh, and it's moderately priced - so it's not horrible.  Average food and average service.  A neighborhood place but not a neighborhood RAVE nor FAVE.  (I almost gave 2 stars - but our burgers were quite tasty.)  It's kinda "meh"/"blah" on the decor too.  A bit shabby.

About a year ago, my child attended a classmate's 6th birthday party here. The party was well run and the kids (over 20 of them) had a blast. Parents provide their own cake and refreshments, Bounce U lets the kids play (free-play and organized activities) on their equipment.  Not my idea of a good time, but kids sure do love it.

Need locally grown lavender for soap making or crafts?  Come here!   (But comeon a Saturday only and bring cash).  Not for kids (although my little one is nearly 8 and can now appreciate it here.) Come here on your way to or from Solebury Orchards.

No atmosphere - but pretty decent grub - 3.5 stars really, but I feel generous and will give them 4.  The atmosphere is about a 2.  I love the Kasha Knishes here - warmed up they taste almost like the ones I'd get out in Brooklyn.  They also make a good shrimp salad and it's always fresh.  They have a high turnover in the deli case - which keeps the cold cuts fresh.  Very nice people working there, too.  Oh - and it's very inexpensive to eat here - or pick up some groceries and take out foods if you don't feel like cooking.  I am glad they exist - higher prices and all (for groceries) because the convience factor is a big plus - especially in inclement weather.  Without Kennedy and Whole Foods - we'd be sunk.

A gorgeous arrangement arrived for me today from Carl Alanand so far - WOW.  The Flowers were amazingly fresh and the spring flowers lasted 4 days, roses are still goung strong at 6 days.  (Tulips & Freesia wilt quickly.)  A 6 inch glass bubble bowl filled with 6 white roses, 3 pink ranunculus, 3 pink tulips, 3 light purple freesia, green hypericum berries (fill), pink wax flower (filler), and Salal leaves. (Or maybe it's ruscus?)   Perfect for a spring pick me up.  I love my best girl friend (who sent me this "just because").  She rocks!!!! And Carl Alan did a very elegant job on this arrangement.

I am not a fan of Darden/Chain restaurants and my expectations were quite low when a friend suggested we meet for dinner at Bahama Breeze near the King of Prussia Mall.  I arrived a bit early and sat at the bar and had a very nice (classic) mojito. There is a huge selection of overly sweet and fruity drinks - so a "regular" mojito seemed like a good pick for me.    My friend arrived and the super-friendly hostess took us to our table. To start we shared the crab/shrimp stack - very good and fresh tasting.  So many items on the menu are fried or otherwise dietary disasters.  For an entrée I chose (and enjoyed) the grilled salmon with a mango glaze and pineapple salsa.  It was cooked to my liking and not at all dry.  It came with (untrimmed!!!! ick..) haricot vert and sweet plantains.    I wound up taking about 1/3 of it home - and my kid devoured it instantly.  No room for dessert  - so we paid and left.  I would come back here - but it's not my favorite place. Meanwhile, for my first time EVER at a BB - it was pretty darned good. Great service - which surprised me.

Well, they gutted the old Raindrop Cafe (thank god!). Sweet ending is a cute concept and since we don't have a PINKBERRY (or Red Mango) nearby and I had a BOGO (free) coupon, I caved.  You pay $0.49 per oz and can dispense your own self-serve fro-yo (very tart BTW) and toppings.  The yogurt was meh - but the fruit toppings were good.  Place is brand spanking new and clean - but not nearly as good tasting as pinkberry or red mango.  I predict it will fail in the long run.  Philly people won;t like this very acidic yogurt.  Service was good though and with the BOGO I got 2 small cups of yogurt with toppings for $2.18.  Oh - and the name reminds me of "Happy Endings" which kinda grosses me out - but if i can snag another coupon I'll get over it.  I wish them luck.  There gonna need it. I much prefer the sorbetto at Capogiro (but that is not even a fair comparisson).

Not as bad as it could have been but not great either. I attended a conference here - ate the "banquet food" (Meh) in cramped dining rooms (The room downstairs claims to seat 150 and that is too tight.) with disinterested servers who could not wait to finish their shifts and get the heck out.  "Grab & Go" breakfast was a joke.  Awful  100% pre-packaged foods.  Room seemed OK but now I am paranoid about bedbugs.  Surprisingly, bathroom (in hotel room) looked as though it had been renovated.  Public restroom was a high trafic area and needed re-stocking moreoften than it got. Will let you know.

I am literally in Paradiso after dining with our special-occasion graduation party of 9 last night.  We had a 5:30 reservation and the place was empty on a Thursday night - which was actually great as we got stellar service from the male server, female bartender/water glass filler and the 2 chefs in the back were really on point!  Started with a round of (pricey) drinks including Belvedere on the rocks, Stoli-O and a glass of Prosecco with a hefty splash of cranberry. Also some folks chose unsweetened iced tea.  Appetizers were monumentally delicious, especially the escargot, 1/2 order or sweetbread ravioli and burrata served with thinly sliced golden beets.  One lady ordered the special app - a HUGE charcuterrie plate with 6 different Italian cured meats including prosciutto and GUANCIALE.  Heavenly! (Plus garnishes including crostini and lovely artichokes.)  Our meal continued with entrees (A bit pricey at 25 - 35 a pop and the special - a huge steak for 2 was $70!!!) that were generously portioned.  Hamachi was gorgeous as was the stuffed veal breast.  I had the duck breast (served med-rare with the perfect amount of Quack!) and polenta.  So terrific.  Deeserts were the only place Paradiso fell short.  While the ricotta cheese cake was silken and lovely, the bombolili were heavy as lead.  (Fortunately the house-made Gianduja was lick-the-bowl worthy!).  Service was a dream.  Can't wait to return.

Needed an oil change and had a $10 off coupon (so I paid about $40 instead of about $50. Tried to upsell me on EVERYTHING - filters, fluids etc.  I will do that part myself.  Good news?  Got in and out in 12 minutes.  No lie.

It's ok here.  Pub Grub and a long beer list - alas I don't touch the stuff. So food wise they have Fries with various mayo-based dipping sauces and grill up a decent burger.  It's a bar.  Good - but not mind-blowing by any means. I'd go again.

Came again for my regular oil change, also sprang for the $25 tire rotation.  had a $10 off coupon which helped.  Very friendly guys and explained things well.  Again, they try to upsell with EVERY customer - it's just the Jiffy Lube way.  So far I am having a good experience here and I will be back again in 5-6 months.  Comfortable chairs in waiting room. TV and good tunes on the background music (Classic Rock).

I could write a novel about all the great things we have experienced because of Joe Gunn, Chef Adan and the entire staff at Jose Pistola's.  My 8 year old competed in the 2013 MANNA Guac-Off - where Chef Adan's tuna and sambal topped guac took 1st place (my kid came in 5th - which is not too shabby!).  Since then, Chef Adan and Joe have been so gracious to our family and we finally got a chance to experience a veritable feast of Mexican wonders (some with an Asian twist) with 5 star service all the way.  We truly enjoyed the Scallop tiradito, Classic Guac (and the mango pomegranate one), Freshly muddled pear mojitos, anything with that Korean Rib in it (I had a quesadilla), Lobster Tacos ($18 for two) and HUGE burritos.  (My husband loved the short-rib one.) Choco-Flan and Churros completed the meal - but we were so full we could barely touch them. (Some how we managed (wink-wink).)  The kiddo loved her black bean and BACON (she asked for it special and they made it for her) quesadilla.  Fan-frikkin-tastic!  Can't wait to return.  We were treated like royalty.  We can't thank you enough!!!

Nook graciously supported my kids old day care and donated 24 mini cupcakes. I won them - and used them for my child's first grade class.  They were the perfect size and came in chocolate and vanilla.  Cute sprinkles on top, too.  Will definitely come back for more cupcakes and to try the coffee drinks.  Excellent, friendly service.  We are thankful for their support and yummy treats,

Came for Christmas Eve with the fam and the place was packed with families and people of all ages.  Excellent service and much higher quality sushi - but TINY portions.  Appetizer was $15 and barely 3 bites.  Meanwhile we loved all that we ordered, especially the salmon tartare.  A great "special occaision" place.

What a cute place with unique and fun (some functional!) gifts. Between this and 10,000 Villages your holiday shopping or baby-shower needs are all but met!  Great, friendly owners. Yes - a bit pricey but unique and mom 'n pop are worth more to me.  Support your local businesses before the world is one big chain store!

The cafe(I have not shelled out the $$ for the pricey 1906 restaurant yet) is great food. Yes, it's expensive - but the kids meals (mac n cheese) are huge - get one for yourself if you like the options.  We love Longwood and have been members for 2 years now (10% off for members - still expensive!).
A beacon of light in downtown Harleysville.  Right on Main Street - easy to find and has everything you might need (not gas station - this is an old-school wawa in a strip mall).
It's awful.  Sorry - it just is.  How is it that a place located RIGHT NEAR 2 great fish markets is not selling fresh fish?  It is also mega-expensive.  YUCK!!!!

Ok, it's official.  We are now friends with the owner/baker Mai.  She also has an adorable 7 year old daughert and 1 other child.  They treat my daughter like family whenever we come in for sponge cakes and shrimp dumplings.  And we never spend more than 5-6 dollars - ad you get so many treats for such a small sum.  There are still only 2 tiny tables out front - and today there was a gaggle of elderly men chatting away and laughing over 60 cent cups of coffee.  This place is a gem.  My little one ate her shrimp dumplings, a hot dog bun, a piece of cream-filled sponge cake and then colored in her coloring book while I watched the steady stream of customers come in and out to pick up cake orders, loafs of freshly baked bread and lots of fresh-cut mango bubble tea.  ($3.00)  Don't miss a chance to support a terrific TRUE CHinatown neighborhood, family-run business.  YUM!

I had a party for 11 people and had Panda Express cater it. We ordered 2 Panda Feasts and a tray of 12 Veggie spring rolls.  The food arrived hot, fresh and on time.  Jay - the manager and Rob - who delivered the food - were great to work with and even gave us additional side orders of Fried Rice and Noodles - so we had ample food.  The Honey Walnut Shrimp was a big hit. We also got Chicken & Broccoli and Beef & Broccoli for "safe" choices.  Everyone enjoyed the food - and the price was withing my budget.  I will definitely use them again. I am so amazed at how good this "fast food" Chinese is - especially when they cook it fresh to order.

I have had several good experiences ordering gifts for friends and also centerpieces for my own events from the Broomall location as well as the Center City branch (separately owned).  The chocolate dipperd berries (added to any arrangement) are great.  Big and thickly coated with chocolate.  My 7 year old loved her Valentin's Day arrangement - and it was eaten within hours.  Good service and delivered on time.

We are treated so very well whenever we visit the court (usually for breakfast or lunch), Don't miss the home-made pierogies.  Good coffee and moderate prices. Is the food 5 star (not really)?  No, but the service is so nice and pleasant.  Love coming here.
We still love this place - and it is a great resource for adoption, too.  They get such sweet and friendly dogs.  Love the staff, products and care they all display toward our canine friends.

I am feeling super happy and generous - so I am giving Panini's and our lovely server Breah and the other nice ladies who poured water and served our Mother's Day party of 4 this afternoon.  It may only be a 3 star place - but we had a 4 star experience (with 5 star weather for dining al fresco).  The inside of the restaurant is being renovated (and it sorely needs it) and we had a lovely table reserve outside.  (Luckily no car exhaust fumes and no weirdness - plus the aforementioned PERFECT balmy, non-humid, sunny spring day made for a perfect 2 PM reservation.  My 6 year old chowed down on the (boring coled) bread basket right away and ate about a third of her ENOURMOUS (same size as the grown ups) $7.50 kids meal of spaghetti with marinara sauce.  My mom had an antipasta salad which was chock-full of goodies including fresh mozz., marinated artichoke hearts and marinated mushrooms (I ate her 'shrooms - and found then a tad too vinegary for my liking), but my mom loved it.  Dad had liguine al vongole (white) with small tender clams (in shell) and strangely enough - very LIGHT on the garlic.  (usualy liguini with clam sauce is garlic city - but not here.)  He ate every bite and the sauce was perfectly clammy and olive-oil without being a puddle of oil.  NICE!  I loved every bite of my Fettucini with Eggplant (the little one has decide now that she's tried Spaghetti, Liguine and Fettucine all at one meal that she likes fettucine now - so she at a few twirls of mine).  The pastas were all perfectly cooked.  Al dente.  not mushy, not undercooked either.  YUM.  Too full for dessert.  Not super expensive.  I sure hope the renovate soon.  (They are in progress.) Surprisingly good service.  VERY pleased and will return (We dined pre-Arden Theater.).
This is OUR National park and we must treasure and enjoy it. Great for singles, couples, families, kids, seniors - everyone can find something to learn about and/or enjoy here.

OK - please note that this scathing review (I was tempted to go with 1 star - but I am sure the food is great.) is based on what happened to me here about 3 moths ago.  I pass by Pastoral every week on my way home from Pilates - and one night decided to go in and give it a try.  The place was dead empty (It had to be a Tuesday ot Thursday - as those were Pilates nights) save for one lone couple having dinner.  I was not greeted and sat myself at an empty table that seated 4 but had 2 places set.  A few minutes later a man chucked a menu at me and muttered something about another person coming (no, just me) and a $15.00 minimum.  I just got really turned off and walked out.  I felt bad about walking out - but he really weireded me out.  So I never got to eat here and now I know I will never go back there alone.  Maybe if a friend wants to go.  I could use some good Kalbi and Mandoo.  They treat me nicer at Miran.

Wow!  Famous Dave's opened mini-branch in Center City - and they have lunches for $7.99 - $8.99!  The management was so accomodating to us today - and the staff was friendly - especially Jennifer who greeted us at the door. I hope the high service level continues (they are still new and trying hard - so please don't stop trying!)  Our orders were filled quickly & correctly and the BBQ chicken, ribs, corn muffins & sides were delicious - and just like at the "big" restaurant  (chain) in South Philly.  I am so glad to have them in the neighborhood.  Oh - and they have a $19.99 per person (10 people minimum) holiday party special - includes drink, tax & tip!  Can't wait to take my little one here to see Wilbur!!!!! And maybe ONE day I will try the deep-fried bread pudding with pecan dipping sauce.  (Or dare I even metion the deep-fried oreos?)  Oh, my thighs!

I have always liked browsing in Beans - but since I am in "the industry" and it PAINS me to pay retail - I usually don;t do a whole lot of buying.  However - (especially with a Sephora right across the street and a block over) - I am glad to see them open.  I picked up some Essie polishes (the also have Lippman collection - at full retail) Teraxx Shapoos from Italy and lots of neat things.  They offer hair services in the small salon area in the back, but I have never had anything done here - yet - I just might.  Welcome to the nabe, Beans!  I am so glad you are here!  Oh and the staffers I met (one blonde young woman and a man - older) were both VERY helpful and knew their products!  MUCH nicer (for me) than the vibe I get at Blue Mercury.  A full line of CHI blowdriers and tourmaline charged flat irons.  GOOD STUFF to be had.

The menu has changed a bit and now Korean BBQ is offered, however since we were getting take out we stuck to the basics.  The Beet salad was just wonderful as was the Salmon Ceviche ($11).  Fried rice ($4) was fresh and tasty - basic stuff.  The best part was the Kikku Nigiri platter - very fresh tuna, salmon, yellowtail and a spicy (not super spicy - just right) tuna roll.  ($16)

This was my 4th or 5th visit to Harvest over the years and I still like it.  It's a bit steep on the prices for the amount of food but every plate is under 500 calories (unless noted otherwise) so you get the right amount of food.  I had the summer menu for lunch with a delicious Tuna tartar and a Crab/Shrimp cocktail.  All the seafood was fresh tasting and nicely plated and garnished. My friend had a cedar-planked salmon which looked terrific.  Salads here are always fresh.  A $6 cappuccino (ouch) was my dessert.  Very lovely place for a corporate lunch or a date night or girl's night out.
I am assuming this is the four-bucks inside the Target in Glen Mills. Went there today for a large order for a group and they were pleasant, helpful & quick.  No issues and so glad they are there.

A decent sushi spot. The lunch menu is very affordable. I had a Hamachi Lovers lunch with Miso Soup and an order of Ikura (good) and Tamago (Frozen.).  In general, fish seems OK, but lots of frozen product.  Welcome to suburban sushi!

Louis B., as usual, is right on the money with his review of this convenient but unglamorous Acme.  I get my nails done at Trendy Nails and sometimes use the dry cleaner in the same "strip" so it's way convenient.  Very old-skool.  Honestly - I much prefer the Giant in Aston or Trader Joe's or weekend sojourns to Whole Paycheck (ahem - Whole Foods) in Glen Mills, but in a pinch - this Acme's got what I need - most of the time.

Philadelphia Ladies?  This is the place.  Pefrect for Bridal and wedding needs.  Of course, the main attraction is the selection of dresses.  But this ain't no David's bridal.  (And also, it ain't Kleinfelds)  Be prepared to pay for the level personalized service.  I did NOT purchase my gown here - but I did get a fabulous lead on a seamstress, Teresa - who is just wonderful.
Much improved now that they renovated (it was filthy from 2005 - 2008 or so).  A vast selection of beers, sodas, iced teas and other beverages.  Convenient.

An outstanding performance of "Down Past Passyunk" - truly remarkable. The quality of the acting and directing was high and the set design.  I can't wait to see the next play - "Ritu Comes Home".  Innovative theater at a moderate cost. Support local theatre - thay need it!!!

I just had a 5 star, incredible lunch at Matyson. The crab crepe app ($8) is one of the best things I have ever tasted.  A light, home-made crepe with a delectable creamy-sweet crab filling.  Basil oil drizzle and lightly vinaigetted micro-mache on top.  Mmmmmmn!  And how could I resist (I could not) the KALE SALAD.  My fave! My love!  I love you Matyson. You rock my culinary world.

My little one has nicknamed Asia Crafts the "Hello Kitty" store.  They specialize in Sanrio, gifts & stationery.  There is a wide array of Hello Kitty items including rare and hard to find Sanrio collections.  Prices run a bit high - but many items are on sale.  They also have a small beverage cooler in the front of the store stocked with multi-colored (and sugar laden) beverages from Asia.  If you have a little one and are in Chinatown, check out Asia Crafts for Hello Kitty and more.

OK.  Decent enough coffee - but by no means up to the standars of Old City Coffee, Peregrine or La Colombe (and not nearly as fun as Passero's).  A nice place to sit and chill and use a decent bathroom in Center City.  In the summer I opt for iced coffee, in winter/fall (mornings) I like a cafe au lait.

We have taken our car here twice for tire changes/rotations. Drop off at 8 AM on a Saturday and picked up at 1 PM.  However, the first round of "cheap" tires we selected gave out at 45,000 miles. Let's hope this next round lasts a bit longer.

My parents LOVE it here.  It is not a good place for kids, though.  They have a delicious tomato & fresh mozzarella salad - and of course, there's always the BEER.  (They actually brew a substantial amount of it here.)  Dad likes the sandwiches.  It's a nice choice in the midst of the Peddler's Village tourist-trap eats. I prefer this to the Cock 'n Balls any day.

We took my kid's Girl Scout troop here to have lunch and tour the public areas.  (Would have been 5 stars if we were able to actually tour the facilities).  The food is GREAT.  Sushi, Salads, Hot and Cold foods.  Great soups.  The girls had a good time watching the Koi in the Koi pond, too.

We just moved to the area and joined the Y so our 7 year old can attend the summer camp this summer.  So far we are very pleased and can't wait to use the pools (Kiddo will love the water slide) and sign up for Karate classes.  So far our kid is enjoying the specialty camps. Costly - but we need it!
Decent burgers, salads & sandwiches.  We came in winter, so no outdoor seating when we went, but service was perfectly fine and food was very good.  We'd return.

This is my go-to diner in Media and I enjoy the home made pierogies (even for breakfast!) and grilled shrimp salad very much.  Other items can be hit & miss. They also have some unique specials like the shortrib-stuffed ravioli.  Service is friendly and great - they are nearly empty on weekdays for dinner time but JAMMED for breakfast on weekends.  Standard diner fare with a few unique home-made touches.

So far I am not impressed - but I will let you know once I get my ORDER BACK. I usually drop my drycleaning off at a place on 452 called Victory - and they have been great - in on Monday, back on Tuesday (They also have same day service but I have not tried t).  This place - I dropped off on Tuesday and the guy (who was very hard to understand) who was swamped with bags of clothes (Place looks very disorganized), had me type my own name and address into his computer.  (Weird)  Then he said - "when do you need it?"  So I said, "when would it normally be ready?"  and he replies, Saturday.  He sensed I did not like that answer and then quickly changed it to Friday.  So tomorrow is Friday - we'll see if my stuff is ready. Also his prices are higher than Victory.  I doubt I'll be coming back after tomorrow.

A truly excellent source for kitchenware, cutlery and gadgetry.  They have a large selection and can order whatever you need if they don't have it in stock.  Plus, the Italian Market location makes it easy to snag some fresh ingredients to use in your newly procured kitchenware.  I also enjoy shopping at Kitchen Kapers.

Oh my goodness - my how you've grown.  Knobs 'n Knockers has been in Peddlers Village a might long time - and has changed locations and expanded enormously from when i remember first going there in the late eighties.  They used to only sell decorative hardware - and that is still the main business - but now with the HUGE influx of NYers and the general yuppification of the whole area - the business is BOOMING and morphing into all sorts of home exterior decor.  (And where else can you drop such serious cash on a DOOR KNOCKER.)  They are like works of art.  Maybe one day when my windfall arrives I, too, will be able to outfit my home and cabinetry with swanky-yet-functional baubles from K 'n K.  Keep on Keepin' on!!!!

Your basic pet shop - right in the Genaurdi's (Now Weis') shopping plaza. We go here to get Eukeneuba Senoir dry dog food for our pug if we ever run out while we're in D-town.  Thank God they have it!  They also have many toys and treats for dogs (and cats, too.)  Nice teenaged staff running the joint. Update - 2014:  Have they closed????
This is the Giant near Arch Road and 202 in East Norriton. Salad bar, Hot food bar with decent fried chicken.  Not luxurious and no sushi but it's fine.  Glad it's here. Nicer than ShopRite.

We are loyal customers of the Viso's in Aston and were delighted to stop in today for a cream puff (just ok) and FRESH chocolate dipped strawberries (Perfection).  Love the "cone"ollis and cannolli also. Oh - and the Black Tie Shortcake.  YUM.

If you are a licensed esthetician you can get even LOWER prices. Otherwise, yes, it is worth it to buy the $5 membership - they give you a free gift worth more than $5 when you renew and the discount is worth it.  (Membership Discount is not as good as Esthetician Discount).  Meanwhile, at this location (smaller but not tiny) the manager is NUTS. Really nice to customers and just awful to her staff.  I go in about once a month to get hair care and nail care supplies. I do not get skin care stuff here. (Maybe cotton rounds or sponges.) Oh - and the "Sally Girl" brand of make-up is cheap and junkie - but my 12 year old love it and for experimentation it's fine.  (99 cent eye shadow singles.)

Another outstanding review for nail technician extraordianaire, Cheryl Lee.  I visited the spa today for a standard pedicure (I usually get the spa pedi) and "regular" manicure.  Both were top notch.  Cheryl is only there on weekends now, but I wish she were there more.So book an appointment in advance.  She is worth it and in demand!  I hope the management there knows what a gem she is.  her pedis last for weeks - and her polishes are precisely applied.  She uses a pre-basecoat drying treatment (when indicated) that helps the base coat (Seche Clear) to bond to the nail plate.  She also uses Seche Vite top coat which is an HG (Holy Grail) product in the nail tech world.  Can' say enough good things about the nail services at spa elysium - done by Cheryl Lee.  P.S.  The spa itself is a 4 star operation.  They have a NEW front desk person (at least she seemed new to me) named Amy who was cheerful and a big improvement.  If I lived in Chestnut Hill this would be my go-to spa.  It blows Spa 3000 BC away!!!

It seems just like Naked Chocolate Cafe before it - nothing has changed much.  I got a big box of truffles as a gift - very nice.  I have my daughter's 5th birthday party here (at this location) when it was Naked. I hope the new folks are as easy and pleasant to deal with.

I nned to let you know how great my goat cheese & beet salad lunch was here today and that you need to RUN OVER here this week to try the "Phillies Victory" Chef's tasting menu.  They have a home-made Butterscotch Krimpet.  I am not kidding.  Go this week or you'll miss out.

This place has never really done it for me - although co-workers like it here and Catering uses them for decent - if uninsprired "Faux"-sher (Kosher) sammies.  The tuna on rye I had was a little dry - which I suppose is better than too much mayo.  (Yick.)  It can get very busy at lunch time.  I did enjoy the pickle assortment - but it still ain't like a real NY deli.

I have alot of nostalgic memories about Willow Grove Mall.  (You see, Montgomery Mall was our default Mall until Willow Grove came around.)  We take our daughter here to ride the $2.00 (adult can accompany for free) carousel - which is the highlight of our experience.  This place is now past its prime for sure. (Alas, as most malls are in the USA.)  The food court has a SaladWorks, Taco Bell, Sbarro, a cheesesteak place and a few other mid-range average choice.  Not great.

Absolute mediocrity - but hey, it's cheap and quick.  But - BLargh!  Do not eat the over-salted, plastickly mac & cheese.  Corned Beef is also a salt-pile.  Not a fan - and not goin' back unless dragged (as I was today) by a co-worker.  #BrownBaggingIsBetter

Wow - so much cheaper than the MonsterPets I frequent in Philly.  Big wide aisles STOCKED with doggie & kittie gear - and the fish supplies were cheaper too, and more plentiful.  And in DE - no tax (gotta love that).  Kinda felt like a supermarket - except that a few people had their dogs with them.  We'll be back.

Less impressed than I wanted to be - I am dithering between 3 and 4 stars - and here's why...  A colleague and I had a lunch reservation.  Service was good - friendly and courteous.  He had the (last one) "Blue Plate" special - a crabcake (one) and salad.  I chose the heirloom tomato salad with (one lump of) burrata and an EXCELLENT balsamic and EVOO drizzle.  We split an order of WAY OVERCOOKED duck fat fries.  Awful.  Greasy.  Salted.  Burned.  Mess.  My first bite of the salad was of a red tomato and it was rotten. Thankfully the rest of the salad was perfect.  The food is so close to being "as good as it gets" - in theory - but the puny portion size (my male colleague needed the fries as the crabcake plate was app sized.), rotten tomato bite and charred fries soured our experience. The burrata was the "real deal".  The ingredients are all great - they just need better execution.  Meanwhile, our male server was cheerful and terrific. He even took the fries off the check.  ($40 for lunch for 2 - no apps, no dessert, no booze).  Garces - I love ya - but JG needs some tweaking, please.

We had good customer service from Keith when my husband and I stopped in to test drive the 2012 sonata (and alkso drove a few pre-owned vehicles).  Ultimately we bought elsewhere (got a better price) but we will be coming here for service.  Hope they are kind to us!

Solid!!  Went here again (a few more times since my last update).  Tina is gone - but there are at least 3 fine young gents manning the counter - and the service is still great.  Had a 1/4 chicken dark platter with beet salad (so good!) and corn muffins (love 'em).  They have a new chicken salad now - so I may try it.  Consistently good, tasty, inexpensive lunch staples.  LOVE YOU!
A decent format and good tunes from the old days. We'll listen to 104.5 when 102.9 or 94.1 are on commercial.
A lovely and historic park and greenspace.  Beautiful river and lush foliage in autumn.

This used to be one of my favorite places to go - when I was 10. Really.  They have cards & stickers & gifts & godiva (limited selection) and they used to carry Crabtree 7 Evelyn products back in the day.  The owners may have changed - as Paper Unicorn has been a Doyletown institution for eons.  But I did used to LOVE it.

I do not eat this stuff but my 10 year old wanted fried chicken so we went through the drive- through on a slushy-snowy mess of a night.  Service was extra slow because of this and the person 2 cars ahead of us who needed to wait for her food pulled up but no far enough blocking the rest of the line.  A mess.  Meanwhile - the chicken and biscuit were both hot & fresh and my kid devoured the whole caloric mess right in the car.  So much for a healthy meal.  We'll likely be back - for her - not for me!

Eh. Meh.  It's relatively clean and comfortable - but the best part is that it is located near to my office complex - so we have ALOT of pharma-types staying here.  Food is just bad - so we order off premises.

It's big, it's got lots of show and it's right near my house.  How in the heck do you yelp something like this?  It's no Moscone Center - but it is very useful and they are now expanding it.  We attend the Auto Show and Flower show every year and other trade-related shows in between.  Whatevs.

Just had another FABULOUS Phacial with Elina and she ROCKS.  What sweet, caring, knowledgeable skin-care expert.  Love her and love her treatments.  She used a Vitamin-C exfoliating micor-powder and natural oatmeal, honey and Indian clay (not in that order) to help my face and neck look A-MA-ZING!  Can't wait to go back to Ursula's and see Elina again.  Oh - and try the Nirvana Treatment - it's heavy on the massage and feels so great.  75 minutes of relaxing bliss!!!

This now our pet-supply store of choice. They carry Eukeneuba small-breed senior (which we sometimes could not find) and greenies pill-pockets (we have an OLD, old pug).  Get the petsmart card for sporadic discounts.  They also offer grooming and obedience training, though we have never used these services.
It gets me to Joisey when I need to use it. Relatively timely, inexpensive, fast and (somewhat) safe.  Needs help with the cleaniliness of stations and train cars.

Still lovin' it here - a little pricey ($60 for lunch for 2 sans alcohol/dessert) but so fresh tasting. Try the Swordfish with crab on top if they still have it.  Summer salads are loaded with heirloom tomatoes that actually taste like ripe, sweet tomatoes.  A lovely selection of ($3) mighty leaf teas.  A great place for date night or dinner with the fam.  Very happy.

The food tastes fine - and the cafeteria style of "design your own" burritos, tacos and quesadillas is catching on fast -but don't be fooled.  It's still fast food - and it is super-duper HIGH in calories.  A typical burrito has 1100 - 1600 calories.  (Naked will reduce it by 330 - as the PLAIN TORTILLA is 330 whopping calories alone.)  That said - I do enjoy the Naked Chicked Burrito, no cheese, small (70 cal) taco-sized torilla on the side.  It's just too hard for me to "hold the guac" and save 220 calories.  That guac - for fast food guac tastes muy bien to me.  By the way - I think Jack-in-the-box owns Qdoba - I know Chipotle is owned by McDonalds.  FAST FOOD - people. Eat under a health advisory.

Years ago (and I mean many) ETL was THE only place around for any type of Mexican food.  They were much needed and much consumed by my crowd back in the day.  Nowadays, to be fair, there's alot moore competition - but Chicken Tacos and Quesadilla's at ETL ESPECIALLy after a night of New Hope drinking are always a welcome taste of home for me.  Bring on the guacamole - hold the jalapenos (OK, I'm a wimp) - and I am where I need to be.

The food was terrific at St. Stephen's green today - it just took so. so. so. long to get it.  Part of it might have been what we ordered - I had a divine braised shortrib (fell right off the bone) over fettucine.  "Does this come in a heavy sauce?", I asked.  "Oh, no." replied our server.  LIES!!!  I asked for light on the oil - and true enough there was very little oil.  Just tons of BUTTER on the fettucine.  Oh well.  My hips will thank me tomorrow.  The Isabella Salad is terrific and I will be getting that next time - if I can do a next time.  I get an hour for lunch and we wallked in at 1:05 PM and out at 2:20.  I bit too long for lunch, I'm afraid.  And a bit too pricey for lunch - if you order (as I did) a DINNER FOR LUNCH.  Next time salad or the grilled turkey wrap.   Server was pleasant (a little slow) and one of the owners was there and he is a doll.  I am very close to giving them 4 stars.  But now I need a post osso-bucco nap . It was (rich and) delicious.

Cafe au lait and 3 beignets and I am in total heaven! Be careful not to inhale the powdered sugar - I have accidentally snarfed some up more than once.  Soooooooo greasy and hot and good.  Such a zoo of a tourist crowd.  So worth it though.

I have ordered from the Broomall, Southampton (Bucks County) and 13th Street (Center City) locations of Fruit Flowers.  Ellen in Broomall is a joy to work with.  She made a "Tropical Sundae" fruit arrangement for a co-worker and it was delivered as specified PERFECTLY.  She even added 3 extra choclate dipped strawberries.  These fruit creations really do taste as good as they look - just be sure to order seasonally - pineapples and strawberries can vary in ripeness throughout the year.  Spring and Summer arrangements taste better in my opinion.  Fruit Flowers is a great alternative to simply sending flowers.  Great for condolences, thank you gifts and of course birthdays and anniversaries.  We also had one delivered to the restaurant where we had our wedding rehearsal dinner (that was handled by the BucksCounty/Southhampton store).  I love this concept and the execution!

My daughter and I come here ALL THE TIME for the gorgeous playground, fountain, sand castle sculpture and free historical stories told all summer long.  We occaisionally splurge on the $3.00 a ride carousel (that is pricey if you need to accompany your little one it's $6.00 - and just TRY telling my little one that she can only ride it once.  Good luck.  Anyhow, they also have a mini golf course and a fancy schmancy new snack bar.  Bathrooms that are relatively clean, too.  GREAT PARK.

Now that I am not in college anymore (ahem!), my J. Crew days are a bit behind me.  That said I did come into this branch of J. Crew (below liberty place - on Chestnut) and bought 2 fabulous T-shirts.  Yes, I said Fab & T in the same breath.  These were not any ordinary T-shirts, these were "Tissue" T-shirts - and they were super-light weight (yet not see-thru - thank g-d!) and soft and kinda like tissue papery.  Weird - but great.  I wear them only in the sweltering heat of the summer - when a "normal" T shirt is even too hot.  Good job, J. Crew!  I love those "Tissue T Shirts".

I am having bipolar love/hate feelings toward the brand-new Tierra Mia Organic Nail spa.  While I love and heartily endorse the concept of "natural", "green", and "Organic" nail treatments, I have not found the water based polishes/top/base coats to be long lasting.
