This is now called Altitude. My 13 year old had a blast here at a private group functions (Her group rented the space from 6 - 9 PM and brought in their own pizza, water and cake).  Staff is a bit disinterested and place is way dirtier than the "Sky Zone" we go to in Glen Mills, PA.  Not awful but not great.  Oh - and loud as heck in there.

Nope.  Even thought they renovated (again?) recently and put in a new loveseat and chairs (6 pedi thrones in the back), the techs here really don't care.  I stopped in on a Saturday Morning  - 3 techs all busy and one lady ahead of me - and elected to wait for my $10 toe polish change.  After over 30 minutes (Now there are 5 people waiting - me, the lady ahead of me and 3 more walk-ins) I get in the pedi chair.  And wait.  And wait some more (Not soaking, mind you - as this is a polish change.).  Finally the lady comes over - speaks little english and barely acknowledges my presence - and proceeds to re-load her pre-paid cell phone (in one ear/hand) while removing my polish with the other hand.  Rush job. Uncaring staff. Not worth it.  Never coming back.

Updating my review - and once again terrific food and service (by John). The black belt sashimi plate (great for 3 to share) had Chu Toro, Kanpachi, Salmon-toro, branzino, Saba and many other tasty fresh fish.  NY Strip Strips were amazing - especially the asparagus and "magic" mushrooms it is served with.  Calamari Salad and red miso soup are also good choices.  A  winner!

The Tobin's ROCK!  Mrs. T and her 4 kids (and 4 horses) now have an official fan club - headed by my 7 year old.  Their store offers holistic, healthy foods and supplies for dogs, birds, horses and more.  Plus- they carry California Natural - which is what our 14.5 year old pug ate for years.  We love the owners, the store, the kids, the horses.  Own horses?  Gotta check them own. Own a dog or cat?  Same.  Oh - and birdseed?  Tons of varieties.  LOVE!

Will write extensive comments after our honeymoon in October 2008 is completed.  They are handling it.  It's a touchy thing because my brand new sister in law is our agent - and I normally book all my own stuff.  She is a doll - but young and just learning.  We wanting to give her some business.  It doesn't look like the rating will go higher than 3.

It's FREE and it's just gorgeous in springtime to see the Azaleas here (and aklso at the Morris and Tyler arboreutms.)  Lots of parking - and less crowded, less well-known than Tyler or Morris, the Jenkins Arboretum is a great place to commune with nature and get your filll of big, old trees - and younger smaller ones.  Take a camera!  (Or bring a book and sit on a bench.)  Nice for kids - but a little more sedate (or in kid-speak boring) than Morris.  Our little one likes the pond though - she saw a turtle which made her day.

My 10 year old came here with a good friend after seeing the Pope and got a stack of delicious banana pancakes.  It looks like this place has been here for EVER but it's actually pretty darned good.  Typical diner fare and family friendly.

Had a good chicken parm panini here.  I am not a big sandwhich eater.  Wanted to get a salad but the line was way too long and the cost too high.  ($4.00 just for the lettuce base and then add-ons at 50 - 1.25 each.)  To get the salad with th ingredients I wanted would have been $9.00.  (Although I am sure the ingredients are high quality - they have a selection of organic meats to choose from.)  So a plain salad of lettuce, carrots & celery is $5.00.  No thanks.  Not life altering for me - but OK.  Way nicer than fourbucks.

Ook!  R.I.P. Naked Chocolate Cafe.  You will be so very missed.  The new posseur in your places is awful.  Bitter coffee drinks.  A gorgeous but stale and hard-as-a-rock cranberry scone.  So disappointed.  I shall not return. I will be going across the street to Dunkin' for a fraction of the price and way better coffees.

Baja Fresh is OK in my book.  I like Qdoba/Chipotle a bit more flavorwise, but i really like the concept of Baja's salsa bar.  You can load up on the different types of Salsa.  This location wasn't nearly as gross as Rafael made it seem on the days we came in.  They did announce order numbers over a loudspeaker, though - but I could discern ours.  I like the fish tacos at Baja - that is something that neither Qdoba nor Chipotle offer.  Reminds me a bit of the Maui Tacos chain.  They also do a decent salad in a bowl. Baja Fresh is a good fast food alternative (watch the calorie counts of what you order) if you don't feel like a burger.

2 or 3 stars depending on which hair tech you get.  They do offer Phyto Products though and sometimes I will run in to get what I need (at full retail).  They also used to carry a Caviar Conditioner I liked - not sure if they still do.  The one lady I liked is gone (Cindy) - and you could tell she had "issues" - she was pregnant with spiky blond hair when I met her.  Gave me a decent cut.  The other lady I had claimed to be the manager.  She did me for a last minute updo and was very controlling (she did what SHE wanted to do, not what I wanted) and thus, I was not happy.  I have NEVER (and likely will never) had my hair colored here.  I only came here again (after Cindy left) because it was an emergency.  Oh - and the prices are pretty reasonable - it's a chain - they can do that. And (thankfully) they can usually accomodate walk ins.

We shopped here but ended up going with nearby Raymour & Flanigan.  Service was friendly enough and the salesfloor was CRAMMED with merchandise - a bit too cramped - so we rested on a couple of recliners.  We were looking for a couch and considered a model with 2 recliners built in.  I dunno it seemed too "cheap" in quality and price.  ASo I went with a more elegant piece - still mid price - at nearby Raymour & Flan.

I'm sorry.  I am a product junkie and I am just Sooooooo turned off by this location of Lush.    The staff are very pushy - maybe because of the economy and sales are low?  Not sure - but they follwed me around as if I were a shoplifting suspect.  The manager was kinda snippy when I asked if they were hiring and gave me a business card and snapped "apply online" or something of that ilk.  The "Big Shampoo" is a decent product and the bath bombs are fun, but I can get them elsewhere.  This store needs a makeover!  Pronto.

Yuki is now DD & my go-to place for a mid-priced Sushi lunch.  We even take some of DD's friends there and they all love it.  The $25 salmon plate is a bit pricey but at lunch time you can get a 5 piece sushi plate (with a Cali roll) for $12.95 - comes with (excellent) miso soup and (boring, but fresh) salad.  Service is quick and efficient.  Sushi chefs know el kiddo and treat her great!

It is a classic Philly institution but honestly - not the greatest diner in the world.  What really is interesting are the waitresses and regulars - some who have been coming here for 45 years.  (And a few servers who have worked here that long.)  I had a classic patty melt and it WAS greasy and a dietary mess.  Not sure if it was worth it as the food is really 2-3 stars at best.  Plus:  it's very inexpensive.  Great People watching.  For food - I prefer the Oregon Diner. PenRose is Also good.

This place was the shizzle back in the day.  I am amazed they are still here (and glad of it) and that they still serve that good (if slightly salty) Italian Wedding Soup.  (I think they call it Chicken Holiday - but it is basically IWS.)  In the old days, pre-Applebee's, this was a good place to grab a drink (they used to have a full bar and poured strong ones.) and have a some good food.  The pasta's were tasty back then.  The restroom could use an overhaul.  (One, might argue that the entire place could use a little sprucing up in the decor department.)  Rock on, Tomatoes!  Rock on!
Better!  A good cup of La Colombe coffee served by a lovely Polish gal, and my lemon/butter crepe was now only 3.99 - better!!!!  I'll be back.

Ridiculous prices for teensy portions served by a surly staffer who my companion has nickenamed "The Krusty Krab".  I love lobster rolls - and these (The Classic in particular) are tasty but sooooooo tiny.  And the only sides are soup or chips. No side salad, no corb on the cob or steamed green beans.  I dropped $17 - on 1.5 rolls (got 1 low carb and 1/2 on bread). And a pickle.  So glad i brought my water bottle as a bottle of Fiji runs $2.65. I guess people love it here - and the brand-new decor is lovely but I need more food and more side choices, please.

A fantastic choice for a corporate lunch (or date night dinner) in the "LoMa" - Lower Market area of "downtown" Wilmington, DE.  I had a lunch salad ($16 - ouch but so good!) with pesto shrimp, pine nuts and fusili (just enough).  They also serve delicious La Colombe coffee beverages (I got a latte to go).  Too pricey to eat here every day for lunch but once every few weeks I will be returning for sure!  Fresh ingredients and lovely service.  So pleased.

Stopped in around 6 PM for a $2 promo small iced coffee and a 99 cent donut for el kiddo.  Young teen/college age kids running the show were bored (slow time at 6 PM in August) and disinterested.  Product was fine.  Parking lot truly sucks.
This food court used to be much better.  It now has a saladworks, a chinese place, and Italian place, a cheap mexican place and is only open for lunch.  Super crowded.  I am not a fan.

My (nearly) 9 year old LOVES Annie's - even more than Rita's.  Why?  You can get Jimmies (Sprinkles) on your water ice.  And they have the "pink one" (Is that Bubblegum or Cotton Candy) and the "blue" one (Blue Raspberry) and they have soft serve in cups or cones (just OK - I have had better frozen custards - but this is soft serve ice cream - not custard.).  Friendly young teens (mostly gals) working the counter and a line in the summertime. Gravel parking lot and a big wooden porch to eat on.  If you are a kid?  This is part of a great summer experience.  Bring some small bills - do them a favor.

For a bar this is truly as good as it gets.  We had a Food Coma inducing lunch at TJ's Restaurant & Drinkery today - but soooo delicious. BLTC&E (Bacon, Lettuce, Tomato, Cheddar and a fried egg - on Rye with a light smear of lemon aioli. - WOW!) Everything I have ever ordered here has been terrific and the hostess (older lady) is delightful. Love this place!!!!  My colleague ordered Mac & Cheese with Bacon & Tomato - and it, too, was delicious but a full plate of that would send me straight to nappy-land!   I wish they'd offer a side of the plain Mac or a 1/2 order. PLEASE CONSIDER THIS!!!!!   Oh - and the Turkey Cobb is amazing too (sounds like whatever - but the turkey is fresh roasted and the composition is ON POINT.) #FoodOnFleek

Alma, you never disappoint me.  I hade my birthday party here in March (11 women with mucho mojitos, caipirinhas and many apps.)  Tonight however was a simple evening - executied perfectly.  A close coleague and I shared the divine thinly-sliced scallop ceviche - bright with tangy acidity.  We also shared (gotta have 'em) the tuna tartare tacos and royal palm dates.  A heavy but delicious bowl of duck confit fried rice - brimming with umami goodness, topped with poached egg and studded with currants and edamame beans.  And of course, a sweet side of maduros with a drizzle of crema.  (Who needs dessert?  Heck, who needs entrees? We were stuffed.)  Instead of dessert she had a Mighty Leaf tea and I got a delicioso cafe con leche.  What a meal!  What a night!  And fabulous service from the lovely lady who served us.   I wish i could remember her name, but I just can't.  Oh - and I had 2 virgin Clasicos and my friend had a black cherry caipirinha and a Clasico Mojito.  Still on top of its game.  Love you Doug-y baby!  Even though you beat my sorry a$$ on "Ready Set Cook" in 1996.  Poor me - I was paired with a wimpy pastry chef from California.
New ownership.  Still a great value for (bird) seed (and horse/dog food).

As a sushi lover, I was sooooo pleased to see this placeopen.  Owned by the same people from Shiroi Hana, I went here with high expectations.  My 5 year old and husband also loved our first meal here last night.  My little one spent a long time looking at the live (huge) scallops and giant orange clams still moving in their shells.  We ordered the shumai for the child (who loved them) and an asoortment of tasty and inventive rolls.  DH liked the triple spicy double tuna roll, and I liked the Hamachi Verde - which I ordered without Jalapeno (I'm a wimp).  We can't wait to come back and try more.
Consistently good.  A great meal last night - DD & I salmon-binged on a Salmon plate and a salmon sashimi appetizer.  The kind chef gifted us with some Salmon Toro, too!  #SlamminSalmon
Ordered only one thing and it failed. I sure hope the sandwiches are as good as they sound on the menu.  Sweet potato fries.  Soggy. Undersalted. Bland. Blah.  Not comin' back so fast.
OMG - I just went Liqueur crazy and Lambic nuts in here today - with a wide variety of every alcohol under the sun.  So enjoyable to shop at an alcohol supermarket.

For chain-BBQ, Mission is darned good. Certain items are better than others, IMO. The ribs (both spare and baby backs) were fall-off-the-bone tender and super flavorful (even sans sauce).  That said, there are 6 or 7 sauces you can try including a vinegar-based Carolina one.  The ribs did not need sauce - the (dry) brisket, however, not even sauce could save.  The pulled chicken was also very good.  Brisket?  Too dry.   Sides - mac & cheese, green beans (a little mushy) and cornbread all solid.  A great lunch choice.  And daily they sing the National Anthem at precisely 12 noon - so if you are in a rush get here by 11:45 AM.  The line forms quickly at 12:05 PM.

This review is for CPK's corporate catering.  We eat basically the same 2 sandwiches at EVERY event my company hosts.  Turkey , Arugula & Brie or Grilled Veggie sandwiches.  Sometimes we will have a few pizzas but since they get cold quickly, the office opts for sandwiches.  We also get the salads - served in a large plastic bowl with dressings (herbal ranch is great!) in bottles on the side.  For a catered meal once in a while it's fine - but to  eat often?  Get's old quick.
Breads, pastries and coffee.  Not cheap - but you get what you pay for.  It's GOOD stuff. Small place, gets crowded during the AM coffee rush.

Oh, poor Mother's.  You are passed your prime.  (And you've been a New Hope Main Street Stale for eons.)  We used to love brunch and or desserts here - but lately the food is just OK, and the decor (and restrooms) need a refresher.  Oh, dear.

Quality is slipping a bit at Scoogi's - but hey they've been around for 24 years. Our server Maria was accomodating and understanding when i sent back my $6 (happy hour special) Fuzzy Navel for "dirty ice".  I think they need to clean their ice machines and filters.  Meanwhile the food was good - my friend had a mediterranean salad loaded with shrimp, scallops, salmon AND crab meat.  (I shoulda got that!)  I had athe $17 early bird special.  House salad was great - the balsamic vinaigrette was delicious.  Entree was just so-so.  Shrimp Scampi over mushy angel-hair.  (Again, I shoulda)  I should have asked for linguine or another type of pasta that doesn't over cook so easily.  The pasta was not only over cooked but over sauced.  Drowing in a lemony/buttery/oily/garlicky scampification.  So sad - as my friend and I loved coming here a few years back. They need to give the place a good cleaning and tweak the recipes a bit.  Otherwise - solid. Very lovely hostess.

No more studio fees!  Hooray!  Marcy - the former book-keeper who now owns the place, is a doll and P'nina was lovely and helpful as well.  We had a large event with 16 women there and the Expressive Hand treated us so well.  We could bring our own food - and Marcy even helped us find a Kosher caterer!  The ladies in the group all loved painting their creations.  We can hardly wait to come pick them up.  Thank you Expressive Hand.  We love ya!  (And they still teach ASL - American Sign Language.)  I preedict a childs birthday here in my future.

Zori & Tanya left - they moved to Florida, but the new ladie I had(9can not remember her name but she's been there about 8 months and is VERY nice.) did an OUTSTANDING traditional ($55 - ouch!!) Pedicure.  Luckily I had a $50 gift card so i only had to pay $5 plus the tip. As a regular thing?  I can never afford to come here, but if you have lots of disposable income, Curries is a great place.  I came on a Summer Monday during the day and it was nearly empty - which was GREAT.  Saturdays are crazy-busy - especially around the holidays.  They have a HUGE retail area downstairs also - nothing but retail.  Wow.

This is, indeed, a Viet Namese/Asian Market and they have terrific (and inexpensive) produce.  They also sell a large selection of seafood and meats (including ready to eat ducks and chickens - the onion chicken looked great.  Additionally, there are about 100 types of noodles - Mi, Fun, rice, wheat, Japanese, Ramen, soba - you name it.  WOW!  Rows and rows of condiments and sauces, too.  Plus FRESH eggs by the gross if you need 'em.  Neat place!  Can't wait to go back while it is still new and clean.

Expensive but - they have alot of unique items including an egg-boiler that my dad really wanted.  THEY HAD IT (It was $9 and you can get them online for less - but we needed it).  Le Creuset selection is vast and normal prices (for that line).  Staff (male) was friendly enough and gladly took our $9.

My little brother (who is now over 30) worked here in High school and they were great to him and to our family.  A good local source for all things hardware - and much better customer service than at a chain store like Home Despot.

Uh Oh.  For the first time ever sub par service and a big mistake (likely all my fault and I acknowledge this) that I caused.  Long story short?  I will not order chirasi here ever again.  (I got the blackbelt kind). It had an uni on the top (and I forgot to tell them I don;t eat Uni) and usually features eel.  Luckily I remembered to tell the guy "no eel".  The fish was gorgeously fresh - but there were lots of things I don;t like to eat. Next time I will just order sashimi and specify the fish types I like.  Server (young male - Chuck??) seemed downright annoyed with me (I was on my phone alot on business related calls over lunch).  Probably a fluke (no pun intended).  I will be back again as I truly love it here.  Next time I'll put the damned phone down.  Sorry.  Apologies.  Oh - and I can't wait to try the new spot on 33rd Street.

This is a fairly new Chipotle.  I'm a Chipotle fan from back in my Manhattan days - so I was glad to see one open in Warrington.  While I must admit to liking Qdoba a tad more - Chipotle is my go-to place for a Burrito Bol (Naked Burrito) with Chicken, Black Beans and Guacamole.  It's fast and cheap - but watch those calories - I never get cheese and rarely get sour cream so I can justify that guac!  This branch of Chipotle is in a stand-alone building (did it used to be the Pizza Hut - I forget).  It has a cool-gray ambience - a bit industrial looking.  We usally get take out, though so we don't really care.  On the Sunday afternoon when we last visited, the place was loaded with families with young children.

Delicious - and a heck-of-a-lot more athentic Thai food in the Riverfront Market (3 S. Orange Street).  The owner and chef are so sweet and everything is cooked FRESH.  The Tom Ka (I had mine with Chicken) was spicier than I am used to (next time I'll get it wimp-i-fied) but was loaded with veggies, chicken and goodies.  REAL galangal and fresh kaffir lime leaves.  The real McCoy!  NB:  No credit cards.

MEh.  Raindrop ar posseur juice bars.  We need more places like they have in NYC that serve organic veggie juices - not slushies that all taste te same and have frozen pineapple in them.  The wheatgrass here is nit turned over rapidly enough and they have NO grapefruit juice.  It's what we're stuck with and I am thankful to have them in a pinch, but now... SQUEEZE in Comcast Center is saving my juicy day.

4 for our service (Hailey) and 3 for the food. Cooperage is a soul-ish/southern American Whiskey Bar - with a decent selection of wines as well.  A good friend and I dined here on Friday night.  We made a reservation and sat inside, although the weather was perfect for outdoor as well.  The house Lynchberg Lemonade looked tempting, but my companion opted for a mojito - which he enjoyed.  I had a bunch of Arnold Palmers. (Being a HARD CORE drinker - not!!!)  We both had salads.  My friend's duck pastrami salad was good but a little light on the duck.  My Southern Chopped salad was excellent - and to my surprised I even liked the fried okra.  Once again proof that if you fry something, people will eat it.  I ordered shrimp on top of it- and for some reason I did not catch that they were to be"blackened" shrimp.  It was a shame, too - as they were GORGEOUS big shrimp (4 of them) but so spicy I could not eat them.  Hailey took them off our bill.  So anyhow - we had an enjoyable time at Cooperage. Food was solid 3 stars. Not mind blowing - but really tasty for bar food.

We took our 4 year old to Expressive Hand on Sunday - turns out (thank goodness) they are waiving the studio fees for the month of Januray, 2009.  Normally is costs $10 for adults and $8.00 for kids plus the cost of the pottery you paint.  Our daughter selected a $20 coffee mug (Woulda been $46 if studio fees were applied - that's one damned expensive mug.).  Meanwhile - she had a blast.  The clean, well-run studio allows you to select pottery piece and apply your choice of underglazes and designs.  After your design dries (Allow at leat 90 minutes to be there you need a minimum of 3 coats of color), they with fire and glaze it.  Pick up is in one week.  We can't wait to see our childs creation. And she can't wait to do it again!  Of course, they have birthday parties and other events, too. Plus they offer ASL (American Sign Language) classes and workshops.  A neat place - and more personality than "Color Me Mine".

Scott Goldoor the owner and Jeff Taylor our DJ did an excellent job at our 2008 at the Joseph Ambler Inn.  They were attentive to our and our guests needs and musical tastes.  We sent them a PLAY and (more importantly) DO NOT PLAY list and that was great.  Perfect for a wedding and reasonably (average - not low, not high) priced. We had them for 4 hours.

I had a wonderful spa pedicure ($63 - but I had a $25 gift card so that made it worth it for me) with Zori (sp??) from Bulgaria.  She and her sister are both FANTASTIC nail technicians and this was one of the BEST spa pedi's (CND and OPI products) I have had in a long time.  I chose the Ginger Lime scent (there were 4 or 5 to choose from) and the scrub and massage lotion (plus a few drops of essential oil in the foot bath) smelled heavenly.  Reception was warm and friendly - even though the place was PACKED on a busy suburban Saturday.  I can't wait to come back. The prices are on the high side - but so far, I am so pleased.  Tons of retail products for sale (first floor is 100% retail). ATM on premises.  Must tip in cash.

I echo what many others have said - Wegman's is terrific - and a great choice for a take-home meal.  I got a salmon sushi platter that was so much better than any Acme or Giant (Blargh!) and a lovely selection from the fresh cold salad bar.  Next time I will try the hot foods.  It's such fun to shop here.

Alma - you disappointed me very much tonight - but redeemed yourself a bit in the end.  I had long been planning a cocktail party at Alma for (originally) 10-12 colleagues and friends.  I called the restaurant, as I have had 3 parties here before - and although I am aware they do NOT take reservations for Happy Hour/Bar, I wanted them to at least know we were coming at 4:30 so they would not be taken by surprise.  Well, we were taken by surprise when we arrived and the front door was locked - It' was about 4:10 PM.  So I thought - "maybe they don't open until 4:30??" and we went to a cafe and came back at 4:30 - and one of my friends was waiting at the door (since 4:15).  So I called them and they said "We open the bar at 4." and I replied, "Well, we're standing in front of the door".  So they apologized and came and opened the door.  And things went downhill from there (and then came back up).  We were seated and then told that happy hour ($6 Mojitos and Sangria) does not start until 5.  So basically if we ordered any drinks they'd be full price ($9).  Also there are no more 1/2 price apps - so we were stuck paying $12 - $15 for the apps. (Which greatly affected my plans - since I was to be paying for the food and my friends paid for their own drinks).  Oh - and any apps we ordered would not come out until after 5 because the kitchen is not ready until 5.  Finally 5 PM came and we began to drink and eat - and folks came and went (about 16 in our party in all - and we spent HUNDREDS of dollars.).  The handling of the bill was a huge cluster fiasco - I was able to pay for my drinks and the first rounds of apps on one bill - but Janel, our server, put all the other drinks on another (large) bill and then folks who left had to battle it out with cards and cash to figure out who owed what.  So then we had about 8 people remaining and things calmed down. The manager brought us a small sampler of finger foods (tempura battered baby corn, fried chickpeas and something else) gratis.  A friend and I were still hungry so we split a (delicious) entree of duck breast.  The kitchen split and plated it for us at no charge which was great.  By now, poor Janel - who I really think hated us at the beginning of the night was getting much friendlier.  She brought us a Chocolate cigar (also complimmentary) and we ordered a few dark & stormies and were on our way.  We had fun - but the beginning of the night was very, very rough and we seriously thought about going elsewhere - but stayed since it would have confused the (12-15) other people in our group.  It's a shame really, in 2011 and 2010 I threw similar parties (with 1/2 price apps and split checks) with no issues and great service.  To ask your guests to wait 30 minutes (after waiting 15 at the locked front door) and not honor the Happy hour is poor form.  Next year?  There is NO WAY I will have my party here. Too rich for my blood.

OK - I have figured out the secret:  Order the pizza for dine-in and eat it there. For whatever reason the 15 minute car trip home kills it for me, but when I eat there the food tastes much better.  We ordered a special - any 2 pasta dishes for $13.99 (norrmally the chicken parm with spaghetti is $12/99) so my MIL and I each got parmed.  She got chicken and I tried the shrimp.  Both came with salad and a surprisingly tasty fresh hot garlic roll (made with pizza dough.  Is this gourmet?  No. Fine Dining?  No way. But for a cheap "I don't wanna cook" weeknight meal - it's fine.  Kevin - the manager was very kind to our party of 4. And the 8 year old loves the pizza.  (Whatever.)

Ook!  I call this place Sh**y Nails. I came here about 2 years ago while still on the search for Philly's bext pedicure.  (The search continues but Salon Royale Court and Mint Julip are contenders.)  I requested a parafin dip - but when  saw the FILTHY parffin tub (grey bits of crud at the bottom.) I refused to have it - and left before I even had a service.  YUCK!!!!  This place is not clean.  Don't go here.  I can not speak for the many other businesses called "City Nails".

A brand-new, super-clean, SORELY needed, Starbucks with a busy drive through in "Brookheaven".  Brookhaven had nothing like this shopping center - until now.  A new Giant, a wine/spirits (State) store, Smashburger, Hand & Stone - and finally - a real Starbucks.  My advice?  Skip the drive through - especially if there are more than 4-5 cars ahead of you and just go in and get your stuff.  Hallelujah,

I agree spot-on with Geoffrey S.   The Liberte is a sexy, upscale lounge with a French twist.  The happy hour special ($7 for a cocktail - mine was a Tom Collinsmade with Bombay Sapphire - delish) made it better as the drinks are $12 - $14 normally.  Food is just OK - the burger my friend had was a better choice than this odd "bacon and cheese" pastry-pizza tartine like thing.  Way too heavy.  Kinda gross, actually.  Complimentary wasabi peas, salty almonds and wonderful pitted green olives (salt, salt and more salt equals DRINK MORE.)  A fun place to take a date - lots of sexy couples at the bar and some not-so-sexy oldsters like me (LOL).  Skip the tartine. Grab a drink here from 5 - 7 PM and then get dinner elsewhere.

Meh.  I don't do costume. Sorry.  But my 4 year old can spend 45-50 minutes in here playing and gawking like a kitten attracted to shiny, pretty objects.  It's a great way for me to entertain her for a while. I'll even occaisionally buy her a trinket here - usually a bracelet.

Loud. Ridiculously raucous and loud.  Bartender is a sweetheart and acted as our server - but he was spread too thin.  Menu has changed drastically.  Some things are good - mac 'n cheese.  Calimari with sage honey dip. Some not - salt-crusted, over cooked burger.  (Great toppings though and only .50!) Briche bun (good.)  Awful cheap swill $5 (regularly $9) house prosecco = headache city.  Even the server/bartender warned us NOT to get the bitter, acidic ceviche.  We had a groupon but if not for that - I will not return.  Sorry, Coop.

It's somehow not the same as the store on Chestnut ot Italian Market - but you can get a decent sandwich here - or a breakfast pastry and they have a huge refrigerated case of beverages, yougurt and grab 'n go salads, sides and snacks.  The cooked foods are often dried out and under a heat lamp any time after 12:30.  If you can - get your lunch at 11:30 before the thundering herd.  And after 2:30 it's a ghost town.

Stopped in for a mini canolli but kiddo wanted a $4.25 slab (huge slice) of REAL Italian cheese cake.  Divine.  We love Donna and the staff here.  We just can't say enough great things about the REAL Italian desserts baked here. And thanksgiving pies for $8 - $15 that beat the crap out of Linvilla (Sorry Linvilla - we love you too - but for pies you gotta try Viso's.).  And don't miss $1 canolli day (get in line early and bring cash) every summer.

This place is Sooooooo tiny - seating for 10 at tables and 3 at the sushi bar. My 7 year old loved her shrimp shumai, and DH 7 I enjoyed our maki.  The standout though?  One of the BEST chicken Udon bowls I have ever tasted. Rich broth and perfectly tender udon (not mushy).  So perfect on a chilly December night.  A good, solid sushi spot.

I got a cheap (under $200) pair of glasses made back in early 2006 here.  Service took exactly 57 minutes, and prescription seemed accurate.  Frames were average, crappily made mall quality.  Now that I have eye site (and God bless Alain Mikli) I will probably only return in case of emergency.  Oh how jaded and spoiled I've become.  Oh - and if you're in NYC check our Gruen Optika.

It's kinda dingy-dirty in here - but hey - it's right near the Oreland Train Station and it has cigarettes, cold water & beverages and snacks.  We really NEED this place - so I hope the owner can spruce in up a bit and re-stock the shelves with less dusty items.  I think they also sell lottery tickets here.  It's your basic bodega - but in the burbs.

What a great place! They make their own ice cream (not soft serve) and have great flavors. Caramel Macchiato had a substantial swirl of sot caramel in it. Banana ice cream was rich in Banana flavor. Cake, Pretzel, Waffle and Sugar cones available. Excellent and friendly service (and they get PACKED).  Cash only.  Wonderful, new & clean. Plenty of picnic tables out side to eat at.

This used to be Chong's Garden Chinese restaurant for years 7 years - so for nostalgia alone, I am glad to see a nice, new coffee spot (actually it's been here for a while).  I was a "Bucks County Coffee" and appears to be a Saxby's now.    Anyhow - decent coffee drinks and a great central d-town location.

It is tempting for me to give a scathing review and few stars to Adsum, but I will preface this review by saying that I ate at Adsum as part of a large group event with a set meal (you can't please everybody).  That said, even with the limited (and Kosher-style) menu choices, Adsum really needs to ADD SOME (Some food, maybe?) to their restaurant.  I will also qualify my review by saying that the chef is very talented and was so gracious in speaking with our group.  (Why did you give a bunch of pork, clam and sausage (Lamb Merguez) based recipes to a JEWISH group??? Weird.) He really knows his stuff, though.  The service was also good (save for our new - 3 weeks only - server - who made a few bumbles along the way.)  We started with a choice of soup or salad.  I chose the 100% butter (or is it Bibb?) lettuce salad (absolutely no crunch, kinda limp feeling) with delicious asian pears and honey/cayenne candied nuts.  Crumbled of Maytag Bleu cheese on top and a delicious dressing (Sweet) with black sesame seeds. (This is where our server said they were peppercorns.  Sorry, not true.) The salad - while good in concept was really boring and unsatisfying to eat.   Salade Ennuis.  Now I am hungry.  The entree was sized like a large app.  3 ricotta filled "gnuddi" (Think Gnocchi crossed with ravioli) were delicious sitting atop a zesty lemony-cream.  But the 6 small bites (about 2 per gnocchi) were not enough.  There was also (5 star!) one - just one - fried green tomato presented with an olive oil powder on top.  I got tons of the powder, while my friend next to me had a light dusting.  I think because my tomato had so much powder I could detect a slight "chemical aftertaste" from it.  (The "top note - was great - a dry, green olive oil.)  I would have bet money that somehow liquid nitrogen was involved. I'd have lost money.  They make the Olive oil powder by centrifuging the Olive oil with a malto-dexttin aggregate or something. Maybe that accounts for the chemical aftertaste?  I am getting over the whole "molecular gastronomy" fad very quickly. I am also not a big lover of sous-vide (so much of it is done poorly), but that is the subject for another review.  The other entree choice was a single (JUST ONE) deep-fried cod fritter.  Not my bag, baby.  Delicious gnuddi - just not enough food.  Now I am STARVING...  So dessert comes, and it is GINORMOUS.  (Nice salad, tiny entree, huge hunk of chocolate cake) and so dense and cold and rich you can barely eat it with a spoon. My friend wanted a knife - as did I.)  So I ate 2 bites of the chocolate cake, and felt my blood sugar spike almost instantly.  Not fun.  I boxed up the rest for my 6 year old to enjoy later.  For $46 per person??  I guess that's fair - if you had eaten an actual entree. (Salad, app, huge dessert.)  I literally had to eat a bowl of strawberries at 11:30 PM when I got home. I hate eating late at night but I was absolutely famished.  I am very, very disappointed with Adsum. That said - the regular menu (Foie gras poutine?  The SUPER Poutine is like a platter of pure fat in many forms.) doesn't really do it for me either.  Sorry Adsum.  FAIL. The 3 stars is so you won't hate me.  I am so tempted to give only 2.
Great selection and value for fresh produce (and seafood) plus a vast array of international food products.  Good place.  $10 minimum to use credit/debit.

A teeny-tiny sushi-spot packed with goodness. The platters are a good value and the fish is fresh and many varieties are offered.  My companion had a fresh lobster roll and the meat was sweet and plentiful.  I enjoyed my Hamachi nigiri and watching the big screen TV. Sadly - that TV does overwhelm the tiny room and voids-out the "ambience".  In any case, the owners were there and the chef was friendly. Plus, you can walk to the Franklin Fountain for dessert. It's not Morimoto - but it's a heck of a lot better than Mizu down the street.
Now that I work nearby I stop in for a quick lunch at Wegman's from time to time - but I always spend way too much on sushi.  (13.99 for a 9 piece platter of nigiri.) Delicious and fresh though.

Since I am now working about a block away I will be going here more often.  Today I got a burrito bowl with chicken and it was, indeed, good ($7.50 including tax) - but when I asked for guacamole on it she told me it would have been $2.00 more - WHAT????  Their guac is good - but not $2.00 good.  If I am feeling less lazy and MUST have a burrito - I'll trek down Chestnut Street a few more blocks to Qdoba.

Kudos to Chef Joe (Chef Joe Koye) for a delectable gluten-free meal for our event last night at a private residence.  We had several Kosher and vegetarian people plus the hostess is a gluten-free celiac person, so we really enjoyed the creative buffet as follows:  A gorgeous whole poached salmon - artfully presented on a bed of thinly sliced lemons.  The "scales" of the fish were thin slices of cucumber - stunning!  The accompanying cucumber/dill/cream was yummy.  On the vegan side we had a lovely wild rice salad with black beans, a fresh salad of haricot verts and red peppers (simple and tasty) and my favorite QUINOA - this quinoa was lightly dressed in a lemony/oil (but it was not at all oily) and contained halved, red tear-drop tomatoes, magical mushrooms and sweet, sweet summer-fresh corn.  That Quinoa was a five star delight in and of itself.  What a feast!  I am lovin' Wild Blue and will definitely use them when I have a need for private catering.
I'm in heaven!  Finally some dresses with a full-circle skirt.  Cute shoes.  Wonderful!!! Celeste Giuilano - where are you???  We need your pics on the walls here!

OK, call me a peasant - but I liked my Naked burrtio (with the same mix of ingrediants) at Qdoba better than here.  And it was a bit cheaper - and a LOT more caloric.  El Fuego has done a great job re-doing the space with classy stools & a HUGE flat screen TV which was tuned to ESPN-HD.    As I alluded to, I ordered a Bowl-burrito with Steak, Black Beans, Rice and Guac ($2.25 extra for guac by the way) and the mild pico-type salsa. It was very tasty - but the guac was LOADED with lime juice to the point of  tasting sour.  (I guess all that extra lime juices helps retain the vibrant green color of the guac.  I dunno.  I think I will be back - as I enjoy the shorter lines and less frenetic pace of El Fuego - but Qdoba is a hard addiction to break.  I am glad they are open, though.  WE need more choices in this area.  (By the way - they are not at 24 & Chestnut.  The address seems wrong to me.)  They are at 21 and Chestnut.  Oh - and somehow they wangled a liquor license.  They serve beers and FROZEN MARGARITAS.  I couldn't have one - as I had to return to work - but one lady nearby was drinking one and it looked fetching.  P.S.  The also serve a lime-chicken-ginger soup which I would like to try one day.  (You can't get THAT at Qdoba.)
Yup.  In future I'll book vacations myself.

I had an excellent first experience at TJs today for lunch in the dining room (the bar was too loud and crowded for my liking).  Cobb Salad was fresh and tasty with lots of white meat turkey and bacon. Crisp romaine.  Nice ambiance and a LARGE list of beers, stouts, porters, ciders and ales.  Can't wait to come back.  A little pricey - but OK.

Now that we've moved to a house in the "burbs, how I miss my beloved DOMA more than ever.  I popped in at 5:15 ish (they don't open until 5:30) and was seated anyway - and waited a while and relaxed.  Ordered a Naked Salmon (not a maki at all - but gorgeous salmon over an avocado puree atop crispy fried (evil but so good) rice.  More like a canape.  Tuna Hwe dup bap was sublime - uber-fresh quail egg yolk, crisp cucumber and cool asian pear.  (The toasted pine nuts are no longer on it - too bad.)  I miss it here!!!

Freakin' awesome when eaten in store. Had a $3.00 (tax included) single slice of a fresh white pie with arugula, a sungle large artichoke heart (and stem) drizzled in a sweet baslamic glaze.  For me - this is the penultimate of pizza.  Seating is limited.

Lunch specials for $6.99 are a decent value - a 1/2 cheesesteak (huge - can't imagine eating a whole one) and iceberg salad.  Kiddo had a single slice of plain pizza. Loads of Large screen TVs to watch "the game".  Efficient service.

Not sure what to say about "The Parkway" - but it is an integral piece of the Philly Landscape and Cityscape.  Many events, parades, races and benefits are held here - and when they are the traffic is re-routed and it's kind of a pain.  If you live in the city - chances are you have been on the parkway on your way to a museum or even to work.

Attended a conference here (again) and the conference functions were not adequately stocked with water.  The coffee/tea station was empty within minutes (over 150 people) and never re-filled.  3 stalls in the ladies room is NOT enough for a group of 150.  Many of us went downstairs (to another 3 star facility) and there was a (shorter) line there also.  And they reeked.  Stinky.  Eew.  That said the food was much improved for our luncheon. Free wifi in the lobby area.

Family dinner on a Sunday night (not crowded) at Doma was blissful and AWESOME as usual.  We are regulars now and they ALL know us (for better of for worse, I guess.)  DD enjoyed her shumai and a DIY Salmon roll.  Dh had a plate of various rolls including the decadent Naked Salmon roll (served on crispy rice). I had a Negi-hamachi handroll (lightly chopped upon my request) that was sheer perfection.  A gratis hamachi naruto was our luscious gift from the chefs.  We love you, Doma - see you again May 19 if not sooner. This is my 6 year old's favorite restaurant ever (and she's been to quite a few, believe it or not.)  DH & I love it here too. We thank you for always accomodating our family (some folks cringe when they see a family with kids).  Do you love sushi?  Do you like Korean or Japanese influences?  You MUST try DOMA.    P.S.  If you are a sushi purist - this place may not be for you - I have learned with time which dishes to order sauceless or with sauce on the side.

OK - first of all I got take out - so that might account for the lower review. Secondly, I had bun  (not Pho) - but here's why I thought Pho Ha was good but not great:  Sugarcane shrimp was soggy (possibly due to take out) Shredded carrots on top of the Bun were overly pickled/vinegary.  I will be back to try the Pho and the service was GREAT - so friendly and welcoming, but honetsly?  I've have way better bun at Pho Cali and numerous joints in Oakland, CA.  Good prices.  Update:  I went back for Pho (I got the one with diced tenderloin) and awesome Summer rolls.  Excellent.

My parent's have friends who just LOVE it here - but I for whatever reason, do not.  It's ok.  2.5 stars at best (I gave 3 out of a feeling of generosity.)  I want to love it - as I love deli food and jewish-style deli specifically.  But something here just doesn't quite do it for me. I am still missing the New Yawk and Miami delis of my youth.  I am, however, glad they are here (or else there'd be NO jewish delis nearby) and glad they have the basics like Lox, Knishes, Kasha and Pastrami on Rye.

Went there again!!!!  This time alone - no kid, no DH and ordered the $42 Omakase sushi/sashimi platter and nothing else (and I was stuffed to the gills - pun intended).  I poissoned myself with fresh lucious fish - hamachi, sea bass, salmon, tuna, 1 piece of buttery toro, a single sweet shrimp.  A small piece akimono (fish liver - the foie gras of sushi), a gently torched single scallop and some poppin' fresh ikura completed the mix.  A house-made piece of perfectly balanced tamago was my dessert.  And a roll - topped with chopped hamachi. (This roll changes based on your preference and the chef's choice.  TELL them what you like and don't like).  The chef here ROCKS.  Mmmmmmmmn.  Omakase heaven.  Mine, mine, mine, all mine. Wish I had brought a split of Cava.  No kid!!!!  Bliss.

I have been back a few times and the customer service here is wonderful - Miracle our cashier was so sweet and friendly.  I usually get the spare ribs now - I like them even better than the baby backs. The "Black Plate" special can vary but once it was BBQ shrimp and they were delicious - I hope they bring them back.  Would love to try salmon, too.

Sorry - but I loathe Cosi. Yes, it's clean and comfortable to sit here - but the food and that bread are just awful.  The bread turns to rock after about 90 minutes of exposure to air, and after I eat it my stomach is truly upset.  Service is teen-age "meh" here. 4 stars for cleanliness and big comfy chairs. Zero stars for awful food. A waste of $8.00.

What a lovely store - with everything you need for baby, toddler, young kid and even a few things for parents.  Decor, clothing, furniture and a wall of amazing clocks.  The owner is terrific and we wish her much success.

OMG - It's a veritable grocery store for wine, beer, spirits - even mixers and snacks.  High level of customer service and a the wine tasting man (on weekends - selected hours) offers advice and tastes.  A great place to pick up some wine - or try a new one.
Decidedly mediocre.  Overcooked salmon atop a boring salad.  Overly salted sides.  Meh. Meh. Meh.  Phooey.  Life is too short to eat formula cookery.

A good grocery store to stock up on non-perishables and bulk items.  They often have very low prices on items like tomato sauce, soda, cereal and other staples.  When I was in college I would stock up here - pasts for 3 lbs for $1.00 and other good deals.  This is NOT the place to go for yuppie-prepared foods nor is it strong on fresh produce.  Yes, they have produce - but alot is pre-bagged.  If you are on a tight budget, I'd definitely come here - but you won't be able to get everything you need here.  Leave room for Acme or Wegman's for the gourmet and fresh items.

This LARGE dry cleaners (and tailoring) is located at the corner of 17 & Arch.  Great location for the Phoenix and nearby Comcast Center.  They have cleaned a few items for me at a good price and well done.  They also cleaned and preserved my wedding gown.  (Ouch - that price!!!!!)  I also had a zipper replaced on an expensive jacket.  It cpst $35 to have the new zipper put in, which seemed really high to me, but iot was better than replacing the jacket. (Which would have been a few hundred bucks.)  Ladies who run the place are nice and the computerized systems helps ensure your stuff is really YOUR stuff.

Menawhile, now I am all embarrassed, because a friend of mine is super-close friends with the husband & wife team who own the place. She swears that they "Rock".  That may be so - but why would they leave the doors to their shop wide open and nobody was there?  We even called out for them a bunch of times.  Gorgeous flowers (Fresh cut in the coolers and dried and potted out on display).  I would really like to give them a try - so we'll stop back again and see if we can get better service next time.  (Or ANY service at all.)

FINALLY a decent sushi spot near my new digs. It's not Nobu, nor Doma, but the service and decor were great (on a slow Wednesday night0 and best of all the Green Lobster Roll ($14.95) was amazing. (Fresh basil and lobster salad - get the sauces on the side!  Can't wait to come back and try some sashimi - to see how fresh the raw fish is here.  I'll be back!
A cultural institution in Philly.  We have seen musicals and plays here mostly.  Expensive!
this is for the golf shop and course. The course gets crowded on spring weekends - so consider golfing mid week (if you can) to play through more quickly.  Pretty course and a friendly well-run shop.

Still showin' the love for Doma - same great owners and some not-so-new faces on the staff (Yuli is an amazing server/hostess).  We enjoyed a plethora of uber-fresh sushi and sashimi delights including the ever-popular "Naked Salmon" and the not-to-be-missed Omakase maki.  We also shared a Bento Dinner with Salmon Teriyaki, Chicken Yakitori, a Yellowtail Scallion roll and more.  Korean Taco app is fun (also ask about the truffled-tuna nachos - we did not try but they look terrific).  The triple spicy double tuna roll is a fave with the men in my life. Pachinko roll (not ordered this time) is a hit with the kids.  I truly miss coming here all the time and I make it a point to get a Doma-Fix whenever I am nearby.  P.S. - My now 13 year old kid scarfed down all the leftovers the minute I walkd through the door.  She has been coming here since she was 4 or 5 and it's her favorite restaurant EVER.

This is DELI-sushi and I don't trust it.   And I don't really like it. I am tempted to give 2 stars but I will be nice and err on the 3 star side of 2.5 stars.  But in a pinch I have come here to get a quick roll or order of sitting-under-a-warner gyoza.  I mostly grab a green tea in a can, a cucumber salad (very sweet and good by the way) and run back to the office.  It's fast-food Japanese-American folks.  And that's that.  Beats the heck outta pizza or burgers for me.

This is a review for the Deerhead Hot Dogs food truck. The 2 guys working the truck were very pleasant, but FRANKly (pun in tended) they just could not handle our corporate lunch crowd.  I waited 25 minutes for my $7 lobster dog. The lobster was fine but the cheese sauce was awful and the dog itself had been split and grilled - try BURNT to a blackened crisp.  I basically ate some lobster chunks and a tablespoon of greasy cheese-whiz-like sauce for lunch.  Better luck next time. Next time, go to the store - not the truck.

Yes, it's a chain - but IMO it's wayyyyyy better than taco hell. Be careful though - the calorie counts are ENORMOUS.  Try the Burrito Bol (no tortilla) to save 300 PLUS calories off the bat.  I also am a Qdoba fan.  (I find people usually pledge allegiance to one or the other.)  and I hate fast food - but Chipotle & Qdoba are actually good tasting to me.  You just MUST alter the burrito fixings to try and salvage the nutritional content.  (No cheese, No Sour cream, etc.)
I love Lee's - for decent cheese steaks and roast beef or turkey hoagies with all the fixin's. They renovated it after the fire and it looks great.  Nice guys (and a few gals) runnin' the show.

2 years later - and thank goodness, La Fia is still here and still has my favorite salads and sandwiches ($12 - $20) for lunch.  A good place to take a client or business colleague.  This part of Market Street needs more dining options so we are thankful La Fia is here!
Seasons is a safe choice for pizza. My 12 year old likes it here. Order a whole pie for the freshest taste. Slices are not recommended and (except for lunch) often not available.

The real deal!  Yum Yum is a local chainette of REAL donut shops and they kick ass over Dunkin and other mass-produced chains.  The chocolate honey-dipped donuts are so great!  Crazy fattening - and try to get 'em while they are hot in the early morning (like 6-7 AM.).    Decent coffee and hot cocoa, too.  Love me some yum yum!

I had a very different (and better) experience at Uncle Oogie's.  I thought it was GREAT!!!!  It's a Soufilly pizza joint with a small dining area.  We had terrific platters (each was around $12 and came with an enormous basket of delicious garlic bread.  We shoulda split a platter - because they were insanely huge platters of food.  Chicken Parm (delish) and Chicken Olivia - even better with spinach, roasted red pepper and a light balsamic sauce.   Served with spaghetti and tons of rich "gravy".  The meatballs are fried and the "real McCoy".  Delicious.  The "Old Italian" pizza is, indeed loaded with herbs so if you don't like basil - don't get that - but we loved it's thin square crust and lovely sauce.  They also offer a tomato pie and a Margarita in addition to the "plain cheese" pies.  Plus they offer white and specialty pies.  And the hoagies (especially the chicken ones) are huge, fresh and filling.  I love it here and can't wait to go back - or get take out. (But I bet it's better fresh outta the oven and eaten right there.)

OK Pizza. GREASY (like a quart of oil) Chicken Marsala (won;t be getting it again).  Side salad had fresh greens and cucumber but the 2 grape tomatoes were rotten.  Not impressed, but they are nearby so we've already been there twice and will likely be back.  Until we can find better.

OMG - a hair away from 5 star perfection. We got a dozen small cannoli here for our holiday celebration - filled to order.  Chocolate Italian Cream Vanilla Italian Cream Traditional Ricotta with (not many) chocolate chips)  The shells were crisp and delicious. Just wish there were a few more chocolate chips (my dad's did not have any and mine had 3 or 4).  We are also fans of  the "black tie" strawberry shortcake" - their regular shortcake topped with chocolate covered berries and edged in chocolate shavings. The berries sliced into the filling are fresh and not gloppy.  The whipped-cream based frosting is tasty as well.  A winner!  So happy to have found this place.

A cutesy pink & purple paradise for tweens (and younger) to get prettied up (tarted up?) and parade around on a mock runway for a birthday extravaganza.  My daughter and I went here to look around just as 8-10 screaming, giggling, bubbly little girls with BAD updos ran by on the way to the shocking pink limo.  A birthday party?  Fo sho!  They have a full service salon for girls (including hair, nails - pedicure thrones, make your own lip gloss, the works) and TONS of overpriced sparkley merch for eager 8 year old fingers to grasp at.  Hold on to your wallet, kids!  (PARENTS, too)  Parties for 8 kids START at $250.

OK.  Now I will eat my words.  I went to Argan last night at 6:30 for the THIRD time and it was the charm.  The first night I wandered it at about 7:45 PM.  The doors were wide open and there were 2 little kids running around and 2 men eating at a table.  Turns out they close at 7 and it was just family.  Meanwhile I stood at the counter (alone) for a good 2-3 minutes watching them sweep up (it was dawning on me by then that they might just be CLOSED - duh!!!!).  So finally one of the men came over to the counter and said "Sorry, we close at 7".  OK.  No biggie.  So a week or so later I show up at 6:45.  I study the menu and WOWZA - the prices are high.  So I walked out.  But last night - FINALLY - I got a chance to eat here.  The place was empty - save for 2 men behind the counter.  I stood at the counter watching them chop vegetebles for 3-4 minutes.  They said nothing to me.  I waited, and waited, and finally one man said - "Are you ready to order"?  I was - and ordered a Zaaluk (eggplant salad) sammy with tomatoes, cukes and crunchy blanched green beans,  but the pita bread - wow - so fresh.  They do, in fact, bake it there.  I did not like the $7.48 price tag - for a veggie sandwich - that seems steep - but I will be back to try the lamb for sure!

3 or maybe 4 stars.  I actually liked Vinny T's - for a CHAIN faux-talian they are OK in my book.  They were very accomodating to our little daughter who loved her ziti and meatballs.  I'd go back.  Way better than Olive Garden and less obnoxious than Bucca di Fake-o.

OK, I don't eat pork and even still (menu is pork heavy) this places ROCKS my world.  Hands-down best Mojitos (get the classico - don't fart around with mamby-pamby-fruities) and Caipirinas anywhere.  You could drink yourself silly.  The ceviche is fresh and lovely - if just a hiar on the salty side. The chicken soup came with fresh peas that the ladies shelled that morning.  My husband (back then fiance) had the Lechon - roasted piggy - which I could not eat - but he loved it.  The Vaca Fritta was spot-on old-school style.  EVERY BIT was worth the elevated calorie count.  Yes, it's a "scene" (what Starr joint isn't?) yes it's uber-expensive and YES IMHHHO it is worth it.  Go for a birthday - or if you can expense it, or if a date will take you - but try it - at least once.  It is an EXPERIENCE and I loved every minute of it.

This flower shop is underground - on the concourse near the subway. They offer a full range of floral services including weddings.  The owner is very kind and generous and has supported my daughter's school(s) throughout the years with modestly priced floral offerings and also gift certificates to charitable events.  I wish I had known about them sooner.
Manager was very nice. Parking is a sham - meters are broken.

Meh. Uninspired, slightly dry pulled pork platter with a gloppy side of overly-cheesed mac (velveeta?) and a drink.  Luckily, I got a kids meal so it was less than $7 after tax.  Plenty of food in the kids meal - but a waste of Calories. For a bit more money, I'd go to Mission - a bit closer to Plymouth Meeting Mall and spend more to get a better 'cue lunch.  Not in any hurry to rush back.  2 guys running the place were very nice. Place was DEAD (me with a take out and one other dine-in person) at 12:15 PM on a Tuesday. Not a good sign.

OK - should I say what I really think?  I am a little trepidatious about my review of the STORE vs. my feelings of the owner, Jennifer, who came to my spa in NY way back when for Astara training.  I will review the store - which she really HAS done a nice job with.  ABL carries HTF and high end beauty products - like Astara, Comptoir Sud Pacifique (which by now she probably stopped carrying) Fragrances, Cosmetics and they also offer a limited menu of spa and beauty treatments and eyebrow waxing.  I wish her luck.  I wish she had been nicer to me.

This is a solid 3 start place but i am giving it 4 as the food I had happened to be excellent - but i ordered a special.  Lobster Salad on an English muffin with hollandaise (from a mix?? - I got it on the side and it came cold - so that part wasn't excellent).  Very good service for a relaxing lunch.  Not cheap - but not expensive either. Medium price, medium food, and mediocre decor (needs a re-fresh from 1992).  Lots of older folks eat here - but they often know where the nice quiet places are.  I will definitely be back.  Very good service from our friendly female server.  (Can't remember her name.) And a full bar!

For $15 you can eat like a king or queen with the lunch special. A friend and I each chose apps (Guacamole - which is great here - albeit topped with Cotija cheese that I can do without.).  They offered a salad with pomegranates again!  (Yay - but not too many in there.) The kale and romaine were adorned with a single deep-fried egg (wow) and bits of bacon.  We both got the shortrib huarache (masa-based flatbread) and it it delicious (and rich!).  The plantanos are not available for lunch but they made them for us anyway.  Perfection!  Margaritas and Mojitos here are always freshly muddled and top of the line.  For $60 or so we ate so well!
Fantastic!  Real La Colombe espresso drinks and ice cream AND gelato. My 11 year old went straight for the "creamsicle" gelato.  A small ($3.25) was plenty.

I organized a Happy Hour for 7 women and we had a BLAST last night. Our servers Megan & Jasmine took excellent care of all of us - and even "split off" our bill into different permutations of food and cocktails.  The Happy Hour specials ($6 apps and certain drinks) are a great value.  We had several orders of Tuna & Marlin tacos, Dates wrapped in bacon (so good), Truffled Guac, Empanadas and more.  I even got a side dish of the duck confit "fried" rice.  It came with a scary-looking poached egg on top - but man - once you broke that egg open and savored the rice, pine nuts, currants, duck confit and crunchy goodness - WOW.  It was a flavor blast on so many levels.  For $9 this "side" was more like a meal.  Definitely love the mojitos and alma coladas here.  What a terrific restaurant on all fronts - food, decor and service.  All 5 star.  Douglas - you are a MASTER of your craft.

We had several varieties of Rustica Pizza at the Yelp Philly event on 7/31.  They were so yummy.  I tried the veggie pie with spinach, fresh sliced tomato and ricotta.  YUM!  I also tried a few bites of the Philly-cheese-steak style pie - sliced steak meat, cheese and onions.  (I picked out the onions - as I don't "do" onions).  Even though it's porbably AMAZING if you eat it fresh at their location - it was still AWESOME pizza for delivery.  I can't wait to go to the store and try a fresh pie.  One of the other yelpers has rustica on speed dial - and has it delivered to his home, office and even to certain bars.  Kewl.

We took the "hop on, hop off" double decker bus tour yesterday for $25 total - myself and my 4 yea old who they (not I) suggested was free and let ride for free.  Even at the reduced rate of $25.00 for the 2 of us this is one expensive tourist ride.  The 20-some stop loop encompasses most of the major Philly sites (save for South Philly) including the new Please Touch museum.  If you take it early enough in the day you can even get off and enjoy the Art Museum or Please touch.  We got on at 1:30 and took the entire 90 minute loop.  Then we got off took a break and got on the 4 PM bus (same great driver - Donna, and guide - Ernest - a funny guy) in order to get off at the Chinatown stop (right in front of the arch).  My 4 year old just loved sitting on the top deck (hold on to your hats and watch those tree limbs!).  If I were a tourist who had NEVER been to philly and wanted to quickly see the major stuff - I would take this.

Talbots has conservative (bordering on old lady) clothes for the suburban housewife.  Event the Center City branch has these "classic" types of clothing.  Tailored, neat and clean.  I almost never buy anything here unless its on a sale.  My mama would approve.

Back again and had Mahi Mahi tacos (and a friend got Shrimp tacos) so we each had one of each.  DELISH.  Perfect Arnold Palmer too - and great service in the bar area.   I am lovin' this place more and more. Not cheap though - $50 for lunch for 2 (I paid, lucky me) with 1 beer and no dessert.

It was my first time at Zama and I dined alone and sat at the sushi bar. I had completely forgotten that it was restaurant week - and while the set menu looked fetching, I opted for a few a la carte items.  I started off with a trio of handrolls.  The fish was fresh and excellent - but the lovely server, Roxanne - who explained so very many things to me - forgot to tell me that they come wrapped in soy paper.  Had I known I would have requested nori.  (I like the crunch of nori with a hand roll - espescially with the salmon one.)  No matter - they were so perfect.  I also had a side order of ohitashi (spinach) - which I love.  The portion was very small - and it was a side - so I ordered something else.    Something heavy. Something decadent. I so should not have order this - but I did and I loved it, too.  The braised short rib app over crispy larmen.  Oh.  Boy.  The bill including 1 non-alcoholic drink (a refreshing limeade) and tax 'n tip was $40.  Not bad.  Decor is gorgeous - a giant paper koi on the ceining and great light woods and textures throughout.  Zama - I am infatuated and will return soon.  Can you win me over from Doma? You are nearly 5 stars.  We shall see.

This place used to be the Wawa - and it has since improved in cleanliness and product quality, now thatOld Nelson took over.  A good place to get coffe, sandwiches and packed foods.  Plus it's right across the street from a Dunkin Donuts so you can get all your pre-work coffee/donut & smokes and head to the office.

Just as my prior review of the Bala Cynwyd OG - but only 1 satr because the Center City location is FILTHY!!!!!  (Bathrooms, bar area, floors) and the dis-enchanted under-educated staff is abysmal! (Sp??)  Olive Garden is Faux-talian-American and is really not that great. My inlaws insist on going to chain restaurants like this, Buca di Beppo, Romano's Macaroni' Grill (how the heck do you grill Macaroni??) and other sub-par poser-Talian chains.  Meanwhile, my 3 year old loves it here - so there's no accounting for taste. And it used to be cheap - but no longer.  I had a so-so shrimp scampi (angel hair here is a definite AVOID - ads it is always overcooked and mushy.) and it was $16.95.  The unlimited iceberg & white-bread (Oh, sorry, I meant salad & grease-sticks) are a big turn on to college kids and cheap in-laws alike.  For my time & money - there are FAR better places to go (even in the spectra of Faux-talian chains.) [See my review of Bensi's]

What a fun place for breakfast or lunch. A friends and I had lunch here (ironically nobody had any coffee).  The food was just fine - and the servers are friendly and cool (great hair and ink!).  A great neighborhood place.  Wish they'd stay open later (close at 2 PM) or do dinner a few nites per week.  Also - note:  cash only.

Still one of the best Sushi spots around. The tamago is frozen (bad) but the Spicy Tuna Balls are great and the sashimi is solid. The last time I went I tried a specialty roll (can remember the name) for $14.95 (ouch) and the hamachi sashimi app.  (YUM!).  Ask for sauces on the side if you prefer. Sushi chef Sam is very nice, too.  I'm still a fan!

This place ROCKS my world. The only complaint would be the noise level (we went on a Saturday Night) and the frenetic pace in which the courses were served - but heck - with all that yumminess going around - no complaints here.  I started with a Distrito (read: basic) margarita - rocks, light salt rim - and wow - SO great.  I can judge the margarita when there is no fruit muddled in, no chi-chi twists, just pure Margarita goodness.  My dining companion and I both started with salads - the chopped salad - topped with crispy tortilla strips in a luscious buttermilk-chipotle dressing, and the GRENADA - you HAVE to try this in season - it is topped with a layer of jewel-like pomegranates and roasted pepitas.  Crunchy, crisp and fruity with a bite from the pequin.  YUM-I-NESS!!!  Then we had the House-made chips, salsa and guacamole (10 - yikes!).  The chips and salsa were top notch and re-orderable - but with all the other great things to eat this is (*gasp* - can't believe I'm about to say this...)...  ...the first time that Guacamole was an afterthought for me at a Mexican restaurant.  Xochitl's guac was better - had a better flavor profile and was table-side prepared.  Not so at Distrito.  Anyhow, we had a superb side order on Plantains & Crema (De-lump-scious).  My friend had the chicken tacos (not so great - sauce seemed to be an odd concontion of Hot Sauce, Sugar and Barbecue sauce.  Not a fave - but still edible.  I had the "quesdailla" - which looked more like fried pierogies, stuffed with w super-yummy pumpkin (calabaza) and cheese mix.  So decadent.  We were sooooo full by now - but could not resist the Churros - and were we glad we ordered them.  (Even better than Xochitl's)  9 mini churritos sprinkled with a vanilla bean sugar and served with a small (wish there was more...) scoop of home-made coffee ice cream  (WOW!!!!) and a tall shot glass full of warm Mexican chocolate and a top layer of dulche du leche.  ADDICTIVE!!!!    One could have easily downed the shot and licked the glass.  On weekends (we were in luck) there is a talented Mariachi singer.  He belted out Billy Joel's "Piano Man" in Spanish.  Service was attentive but I did feel rushed - especially when nearly everything came out at once - it was like "SENSORY OVERLOAD".  Our great looking male server helped!  It was also very, very loud in there.  I would like to come back her on a Tuesday at 5 PM or another "off time" so I can hear myself think. I hovered between 4 & 5 stars and went with the five - because it really is a remarkable restaurant.  (Much better than Tinto.  I am jonsein' to finally try Amada.)  The bill for 2 including - only 1 alcoholic drink - tip & tax was exactly $80.00.
No issues - just the same as any Jimmy John's - all cold subs and as they say "Freaky Fast" service.  $6.50 and out the door.

Oh my!  Hooray for Jose - he's on a roll row!  Garces Trading Company (a market/coffee bar and rest-o in one) offers chi-chi cheeses, wines, coffees, pastries and charcuterie/olives etc.  The olive oil tasting area is amazing!  Not sure how the sit-down food is - but it looks lovely.  Tried a chocolate madeleine and it was a bit dry.  Quel Dommage.  The macaroons and lemon drop cookies are heavenly, though.  I wish y'all much success!  Foodie heaven!

This has got to be the cleanest and most well run Rita's that I have ever seen.  The summer-teen/college aged staff is actually pleasant and well mannered.  We stopped by for frozen custards on July 4th weekend and it was a great experience. (As Rita's goes.)  The frozen custard is quite good.  I am not a water ice eater - but I love the custard at Rita's.  News flash! Their "Gelatti" is NOT Gelatto.  It is a bastardization combo of water ice and custard.  Whatever.  It tastes good.  Bring on the coffee flavored frozen custard, please.

I went back for one and one reason only - I somehow managed to get a $50 eversave (or groupon or some deal) for five bucks.  That's right.  $5 for $50 worth of food. So I went back - with the same friend and we had a much better (and nearly free - we tipped based on the real total) experience.  The $5 'mac 'n cheese (they use ditalini - really is good.  The calamari is also light, crispy and served with a honey dip.  Sweet!  Also the candied bacon on the bacon 'n eggs (deviled) app is really tasty stuff.  Salad?  (I got the greek wedge) Just ok. Grilled Tuna was a better choice - served with broclli rabe and GIANT gigante beans.  Food seemed better tonight, service worse, loudness better (It was Tuesday - not Friday).  Still not a holy grail - but for $5???  Who could resist.  Get the mac 'n cheese.  It's gooooood.

Capri's Pizza - now Villa Capri (along with Nat's) was nearly the only game in down "back in the day".  The Mannino Family (who I think still owns and operates Capri) added the dining room and  classic Italian favorites on the Menu.  The location is great - Central Doylestown - and the prices are a bit high.  On weekends they sometimes have a pianist which is a nice touch.  My brother's all time favorite is the tortellini bolognese - which is a generous porion with a rich meaty sauce.  The Chicken & Veal dishes (I am partial to Francese) are quite good too.

I am so happy so say that Aya's is still terrific.  And - if you get the $6.99 daily lunch special (Wednesday it was a chicken pita sandwich), it's a great value, as well.  Love the hot, thin pita, baba ganoush and tahini here.  Super-yum!

2-3 stars.  What in G-d's name possessed me? I was hungry.  It was 9:30 PM on a Thursday night. Where else could I go?  I sat at the bar and had inattentive service from the 22 year old over-worked, stressed out bartender.  I plowed my way through a very heavy cheese burger quesadilla.  (I felt righteous by not eating the fries.)  I left.  Not coming back unless someone else drags me here.  Blargh!

Not bad for a chain - nice sunny, light wood decor, quick service (even on a weekday lunch), and tasty thin crust pizzas with lots of fresh toppings to choose from.  I also like the CPK Cobb salad - the half is PLENTY big - not need to get the larger size.  Tortilla and Minestrone soups are good, too.  Nice.

I stayed here for a 2 day convention. The hotel room was fine and our front desk clerk, Lincoln, was a doll.  We also got 2 free bottles of water in our room so the next day we asked for 2 more - not realizing they charge for them $2 a bottle.  (I can easily drink 6-8 bottles a day.)  Not the end of the world but I would have liked to have known.  Also the catering service for our group was just AWFUL. "Cod" fish with mango salsa was so fishy and old tasting and many of the pre-sliced cakes on display were dry and old.  Not a wonderful hotel but not bad to stay over for a night.  (Loaded with families going to Sesame Place). Just avoid having any catered events here.

Italian Delight really does make a nice pizza.  Not a holy grail - but they offer alot of choices like Tomato Pie, galic knots (that are not too greasy) and a really crispy chicken (or veal - real veal) parm sandwich.  NOTE:  We went again on May 9, 2009 and spilt a chicken parm sandwich (HUGE) and it was terrific.  We go there on occaision with my parents and 4 year old - and they treat us well.  And the 5 (or 6) of us can get out of there for very little money.  Can't wait to try the pasta dishes.  NOTE to parents;  They do not have any milk or juices - only sodas and "junk" beverages - so bring your own.

What a treat! I dined alone (again) at the sushi bar and (again) enjoyed the limeade.  My server, Merci, was so sweet and accommodating. The sushi chefs are each so talented - and of course chef Zama was there doin' his thing.  The "black belt" sashimi app was sublime and included 2 luscious pieces of salmon toro.  I also tried the lobster salad (outstanding) and avocado salsa (also very good). Home-made tamago - branded with the Zama logo - was a thing of beauty and exceptional taste.  Best of all?  Ikura that was poppin' fresh.  Simply amazing.
Hostess Gift Central!  Monther's Day, too.  Wonderful home decor items, chocolates, jewelry items and accessories.  LOVE IT!

I stopped at DiBruno's on a whim at 7:45 AM for a (pricey) breakfast sandwich.  COOKED TO ORDER.  I had scrambled eggs (2), cheddar, spinach and tomato on an english muffin.  Came to $4.49 with tax - yikes - but man was it good.  An indulgence for sure - and you gotta wait several minutes - especially if there is a line (at 7:45 there wasn't) as they painstakingly prepare everyone's sandwich, omlette or oatmeal ONE at a time.  Wow.  A yuppy puppy brekkie for sure!

Went to Doma last night for a rare treat - a child-free dinner. Had the BEST time.  (Brought our own Prosecco.)  Trio of tartares was terrific, as was my usual "Naked Salmon"  atop crunchy rice.  YUM!  My dining companion had a kick-ass chicken katsu. I also sprang for a $10 negi-toro handroll and am so glad I did.  FAN-frikkin'-tastic.  And - I just went to morimoto a few days ago and yes, it is excellent - but for the money?  This place is a steal, a joy and a true gem.  We are planning a party here for my 6 year old this fall.    Can't wait!  Shumai and edamame all-around!

This place is kinda creepy.  It's a luncheonette style counter and serves greasy burgers and junky-cheap lunch food.  I went here exactly once and will never return.  I am tempted to give 1 star, due to the nasty-creepy-skeevy vibe, but I feel kinda generous today so I will give 2 stars.  Food was just Meh. (But it is very inexpensive and quick.)

This mock-meat vegetarian chinese (is kosher, too) has take-out, delivery ($20 minimum) and friendly services.  That's a the good part. Also the pineapple"chicken" is one of my little girl's faves.  The appetizers are a grease-fest.  The stuffed eggplant with inedible. The spring-rolls were only fair (might be better to have these dine-in.) BUT the leek dumplings were delectable.  Hot & Sour soup was nice and spicy - but had a strange "ketchup-y" sweet note to it that I did not care for.  We will come here when our daughter demands it, but for now we shall stick to Square on Square for the BEST hot & sour around.

I have been dying to try Bittersweet and now I can't wait to return. Eli (at the front counter) and the other staffers are so friendly and helpful. Note:  You order and pay first and then sit down and they bring the food to you.  Breakfast and lunch ONLY - except for Wednesday dinner (Dining Out in the Chaos aka Dining Under the Stars).  Creme Brulee Pancakes are a sweet-dessert like treat. I opted for the savory special - Breakfast enchiladas and tasted a terrific side of Vegetarian Chili with Sweet potatoes and Black Beans (I loved that best!).  The cornbread accompanying the chili is house-made and perfect!  I want one of everything! What a great place.
What a great find. Fabulous, family-run Thai with a cute stand at Booths Corners complete with Boba teas.  We'll be back.

Still great - but we had a 4 star experience.  Thankfully we dined early so we could order off both the Happy Hour menu (Nachos with skirt steak was good and surprisingly plentiful for a half portion.) and Dinner Menu (Planytains with Crema!)  Lovely food, delicious fresh cocktails. Great Service.  LOVE IT!  (So close t 5 stars - please bring back the pomegranate salad).  $50 for 2 of us - one drink a piece and lots of bites.

We had a solid 3 (maybe even 4) star experience for an early-bird dinner last night.  We ordered the 3 course special (which is a good value - and much less expensive than the $18 - $24 entrees.  For $14.95 - $16.95 you get a choice of soup or salad (a very boring, but fresh, lettuce house salad), entree (I had a tasty chicken parm, my friend got the crab cakes with potatoes & asparagus), and dessert (she had cheesecake and I had a decent freshly-filled cannolli).  Our server, David, was charming and attentive.  Considering that there are not too many options in this area, Scoogi's is a decent coice for a lunch, dinner or "early-bird".  Full bar - and $5.00 Burgers on Wednesdays during the summer.

We stopped in last night (a MONDAY) when we discovered that DOMA was closed on Mondays.  I had not been back to Swanky Bubbles in about 2 years - and things are not nearly as good as I remember.  The prices are higher, the sushi is "meh" and the lobster/crab mac 'n cheese tasted fishy and reminded me of a $24 tuna casserole.  The $8.00 4 piece "Rain Forest" roll (vegetarian) came with a wasabi cream that I swear was whisked wasabi mayo.  Meanwhile food was a 2 star and service about 4. Dave, the bartender was a swwetheart and treated our 5 year old like a princess.  She loved her (bland) lobster maki.  The best part?  Delicious chocolate fondue. A downer?  STALE poundcake chunks and tasteless melon balls (who puts melon in fodue?  Some pineapple would have been nice.)  Next time we'll probably go elsewhere.

Believe it or not - I like this staples - it's a large one (the one I go to the most is at 1500 Chestnut - which is smaller, less selection and a bit higher prices.)  This one is fine and unlike Nu S., I never had any problems here service-wise - granted it's run by high school and college "kids".  I get toner, post-its, copy paper, highligheter pens, batteries, memory cards/sticks and occaisionally even a case of spring water when it's a decent price.  Glad to have a Staples nearby.  Oh - and terachers - sign up for your 10% discount and they also give credit for school supplies to your school.  Nice big parking lot.  Easy-peasy.

On the LAST Wednesday of every month you can get a Medium 2 topping pizza for $3.99 (Normally it's $4.99).  Seriously?  You can't get a frozen pizza for $3.99  We love this deal and get one pie for every 2 kids and it's perfect for two (or one ravenous adult.).

Tres bien! Magnifique! Et c'est la verite!  I thoroughly enjoyed a sublime almond croissant.  Fresh, crisp, buttery, multi-layered, filled with almond paste and sprinkled with sliced almonds & powdered sugar.  Parfait!  The coffee drinks, chocolates, pastries and tartes here are all so delicieux!  Can't wait to return!  Mon dieu, c'est le meilleur!
