Sashimi puts a sushi joint to the test - and the $13.95 sashimi app is a generous taste of 4 fish (tuna, salmon, seared (cold) albacore, Y.T. and 1 cooked shrimp).  If you love the inside of a spicy tuna roll without the rice try the spicy tuna ball app.  5 bite-sized balls of spicy tuna coated in crunchies.  I am a fan of this place!!!

What?  A line?  A super, duper long line - on a Saturday afternoon at the Springfield mall.  These people must love their pretzels.  They're OK (for junk food) but so not worth a 20 minute wait.  Anyhow - Auntie Anne's is keeping the malls of America in business. (And airports, train stations and other places).  The pretzel and lemonade obsession continues. Carb-a-licious.

Well, it's 6 years later and I am pleased that Jeenwong is still there - and my egg noodles with shrimp ($8.95) came with 6 BIG shrimp and lots of brocoli and carrots.  A little on the greasy side and not spicy at all (I am a wimp so that's fine by me - if you want spicy don;t get this one - or ask them to make it spicier which they will do.)  So pleased to have Thai within a short distance of my work.
This place is just weird.  It's like a walk-up counter and sells Hotdogs, Lemonade & Brisket sandwiches.  Service is fast and prices are low.  No9t a holy grail - but OK in a pinch.

This is a BIG target and it well designed.  I got in and out of here fast and hit all 4 departments I needed - Pharmacy, Cleaing Supplies, Baby Gear and Girl's Clothing.  I always drop at least $100 whenever I walk into  Target and here was NO exception.

I've actually had decent experiences using the trolleys - especially when the Blue line (Market/Frankford El) ain't workin'.  I take the trolleys from 15th Street to 390th usually and not much else - plus during rush hour there are more of the trolley than there are of the El. And you can get out to West Philly easily.  they also have a blue flashing "warning light" to let you know not to go down there if the light is flashing.  (Wish the Broad Street line had something similar.).  I am a BIG proponent of public transportantion and while it is easy (oh, so very easy) to criticize SEPTA - I think the trolley line it a great, great thing.  Please improve the Orange and Blue lines and clean up the stations. And make token machines (better yet - switch to a swipe-card system like every other modern city {suppoedly in the works}) available at all stations.  (I can not believe the Race/Vine station has no place to buy tokens - but that is the subject for another review().  the green line?  It's running pretty well.

We bought our chest freezer from HH Gregg 2 summers ago - and what a great $79.99 investment this has turned out to be.  It fit in our car (we got a smaller one) so we did not need to pay to ship it home and the sales dudes helped us "dollie" it out to the vehicle.  No issues here. And no tax in DE!

Needed some sneakers and didn't feel like paying $100.  Mission accomplished with my brand new Nike's from Finish Line ($70) and a cheap "Pastry" T-Shirt (Pastry is Russell Simmon's daughters Angela and Vanessa's destined-to-fail clothing line) for $6.99.  Sales person was surprisingly helpful and the store was nearly empty.  City Sports is a nicer store, but I scored cheap kicks here and that suits me fine.  SUIT UP!!!

Yuck.  Sooooo not my thing.  I can kinda-sorta deal with a plain turkey sub on whole wheat.  There is little nutritional goodness to be had here.  I simply hate fast food.  But it is cheap.  (You get what you pay for.)

This City Nails is the best of them.  It is relatively safe and me and my 5 year old get manis and polish changes here.  I am still leery about pedis anywhere in Philly.  (Tierra Mia is safe, as is Rescue, but the nail joints in general are not good for pedis in Philly.)

We had an excellent lunch at Concerto - mostly sushi (which was fresh - not off tasting at all) maki and an excellent duck salad.  The staff wqas pleasant and the decor is very nice - sleek and modern as others have described.  I am sad to see some very negative reviews on here - and feel fortunate that we got fresh fish and a great tasting meal.

Ameriflex administers our firms DCA and FSA (Flexible Spending Accounts).  It has been a dream so far to have claims processed and paid so quickly.  These accounts are "use it or lose it".)  It sure beats the old way we did things.

Market Way flowers has changed hands numerous times over the years - and I really can't comment accurately about the current management.  Back int he '80's, however, they were very reputable.  In the mid nineties I wired an arrangement to my parents (who lived in Doylestown) and Market Way fulfilled the order.  And it was disappointing as the flowers, especially the gerbera daisies, did not last as long as we'd expected.  They did, however replace the bouquet free of charge.  I am not sure how to comment so I will award 3 stars as we experienced both highs and lows from dealing with Market Way Flowers.  (This is one of the few flower shops in D-town that I did NOT work for!)

OK, I hate to rain on everyone's Tinto Parade - and maybe I am overly critical - or maybe I just went too early in the game (I went 1 week after  they opened).  I am writing this review months later.  Or MAYBE I am just a jaded ex-NYC chick who can't tell good food when she tastes it anymore?  But, I was distinctly underwhelmed by the dark decor, lackluster service and overhyped food at Tinto.  Yes, there is true Galician cuisine to be had here - which is a rare and refreshing change.  The selection of cheeses and pork products (alas, i don't eat piggie meat) are awe inspiring - as are the tremendous prices for the small, small plates.  I do commend Jose for finding true authentic regional Spanish specialties like Membrillo and other accompanyments.  For that you should really get the 4th star.  For lunch - by myself I had the $16.00 grilled lamb chops (whic, indeed, were grilled to perfection - but HECK - I coulda made that at home.)  I also had the White asparagus gazpacho - which was a true disappointment.  It was far too rich - almost like eating a bowl of cream.  The pluche was the best part - microgreens - the only gree to be found in my $30.00 lunch (with NO BEVERAGE.)  Sorry Jose - but for the master that you are - I should not have to pay $30.00 for a single lunch *(no dessert, no drink) to sit at an elevated (and un-comfortable for short people), hard wooden stool, at cramped tiny tables.  Service was OK - but so NOT friendly.  I cam in a 12 noon on the dot and had the place nearly all to myself.  I have not since returned.  I grill a damn fine lambchop myself.  I wanted to love it here - and in theory I do - but in reality - I just CAN'T. P.S.  If you are Kosher-ish or don't eat Pork or Shellfish - you may want to pass.
A large Wawa with a gas station and decently clean restrooms.  Got in & out and back on 73 with no issues.
Eew!  Taco Hell in 30th Street Station. Combined with a stripped down pizza hut.  I'd rather go hungry.
I have been here twice over the last 3 years. Got my latte and got out.  No issues - but not a HG (Holy Grail) either.

Meh to OK.  Decent pizza - especially if you order a whole, fresh pie. Chicken parm was deepfried tenders with sauce and cheese.  FAIL. Spaghetti was well cooked (not over cooked).  Fries, chicken - basically anything that went into the deep fryer was over-fried and too dark.  Perhaps the oil was too hot today?  Anyhow the kiddo liked it so we were ok with it.  $34.20 including tax for lunch for 3.

A great place for a basic (or not so basic) Turkey sammie.  I love the turkey here - simple, tasty and not dry.  (Thank the lord.)  They offer alot of sides, too - but I usually just get the sandwich and then, if I am still hungry I head to Little Thai Market or Sang Kee for a small bite of something else.

Not as clean anymore (somehow I KNEW that would happen) but still a great place for fresh dragonfruit, enoki mushrooms, many varieties of vermicelli, sauces and other Asian staples that you just don't see in the Ack-a-mee.  Fresh bean sprouts and frozen Har Gow (shrimp dumplings) were on today's list!

Crapplebee's. My 9 year old loves it here - and thus, we sometimes go. Oddly enough her 9 year old BFF's fam loves it here, too - so again - we are dragged here.  The service is actually pretty good if you come at an off- peak time (Crystal is a lovely server).  The food though?  Ech!  The kiddo & I shared a Two for $20 deal and I added $1 extra to get the 7 oz (tiny) steak.  I asked for it rare and it had absolutely no flavor other than salt.  The steamed white rice and brocolli were sitting in a pool of water on the plate.  Blech!  The overly fried and greasy boneless wing app drenched in a sticky-sickly-sweet sauce was all I ate and that was bad enough.  Lord help us! There are so many better places to eat.  I only come here under duress.

A small, family-run shop.  They stock "the usuals" (roses, lilies, carnations, baker fern, leather leaf, bear grass) and can special order other species.  Timely and pleasant service.  A little pricey for balloons, though - latex ballons were over $1.00 each.  Something insane.  I did not buy any for my daughter.  They were STOCKED UP for mother's day (2009) and had tons of mini carnation bouquets for last minute pick ups.

Sorry. Wanted to love this place but my 8 year old and I walked in - to a dead-empty store.  The doors were wide open on a sultry summer weekday afternoon and the shop is beautiful and the coolers were stocked with roses, iris, white hydrangea and stock.  Lovely.  No staff to greet us. Place looked deserted,  Sign on the wall says "Nobody EVER gets to see the Man Behind the Curtain" (or some similar quote from the "Wizard of Oz").  We called out, "Hello?  Hello?" No response. So we walked out.  We'll try again another day and update this review accordingly.  I would like to have a relationship with a GOOD local florist, as Kremp's handles my Bucks County and Center City needs.  I hope Media Florist is up to the challenge! They do have staff, don't they?

Seasons - you have redeemed yourselves.  I ordered our Superbowl pies (2 large - with an array of toppings) and 25 wings 2 days in advance and they were ready,correct and piping hot when I picked them up at precisely 6:30 PM. (Tip:  get the NY Style crust - not too thick, not thin.)  Fabulous! Much better than the pies we had last year (from a different place).  We'll be back for Superbowl food from Season's next year - and I bet many times in between.

A fun place to browse around for pet-gear and treats while on South Street.  Not a holy grail by any means - but they are there when you need them.  Also prices are a little higher than in the big chains like PetCo and MonsterPets.

ook!  Alex - you write well but this Kmart is NOT 4 stars.  No way.  1 or 2 max.  Dirty, disorganized, and disinterested underpaid staff.  Not a fan - but I have come here in a pinch for household goods.

This venue is fine - but our service at the Diva Drag brunch was terrible. The actual drag show was hilarious and fun and well put together, but our server was a space cadet (Another server from a different section actually took over for a while which was good) and forgot to get us drinks, get our food, etc.  They need more servers during the Sunday brunches 3 or 4 was not enough for over 100 people.  All is all, the venue was fine - and the ladies room was clean! We'll be back.

1 or 2 stars tops.  This K-Mart is so "ghetto" and the people who work here?  Well, don't even bother to TRY and get help.  In a dire emergency I have come here twice - once to get basic paper goods and cleaning supplies and once to TRY to see if they had any decent toddler clothing.  I really try to avoid coming here.  Long lines at the check out, too.  Could somebody please WORK here?  None of the employees do any work?  They stand around and chit chat while we all wait in the line.  Do something!  Open another register.  Pu-leeze!

Small, cramped, crowded and even more "picked over" than the "usual" TJ MAxx - for instance the one in Gateway Shopping Plaza inn Chesterbrook is much nicer.  Still, a good place to go for "seconds" and designer bags, accessories, fashions and cosmetics (great place for gift items) at a reduced cost.  Glad it's here - but not the greatest TJ Maxx ever. Avoid pre-Christmas - this was my first mistake. I will come back in February.

Another great, simple, perfectly broiled salmon dinner with rice and cucmber salad at Lobster Claw.  The place was PACKED - every table filled - on a Saturday night.  Friendly service and simple, delicious seafood meals.  (Fried or Broiled).  LOVE IT here.

Honestly?  Way too expensive for what it is - especially after going to the National Aquarium in Baltimore and the Monterrey Bay Aquarium in CA, but it's still a great experience especially if you have children from ages 5 - 9.  The Penguins are always fun and the area with the touch pool (wash your hands!) has a friendly ray.  Beautiful to look at but stinky - especially the hippo exhibit.
I love the vibe of this small shop and the merchandise is gorgeous.  Perfect cruise-wear, beach wear and summer/spring wear.  Pricey - but unique and fun.

Still amazing after all these years. My now 11 year old kid and I had a whopping $85 lunch including a Pachinko Roll (delicious), the Tartare Trio ($15), Naked Salmon roll and JUMBO Ebi Shumai. Also Nigiri and sashimi a la carte (Salmon belly, salmon, REAL home-made tamago and more).  We love this place SO much! We miss you!

Stopped in for an actual sit-down lunch today with a colleague (usually I have been getting take out due to work) and we had a terrific time.  It, of course, helped that we got there at 11:40 AM and the sushi bar was empty (It wasn't when we left!) and we also both love sushi.  The "A" roll - a caloric concontion of shrimp tempura, mango inside, spicy (not too spicy) crunchy tuna outside (sauces on the side - eel sauce and spicy mayo) is tasty - but best shared as it is heavy and filling.  The Yellowtail sashimi was perfectly fresh and artfully presented (Sliced perfectly and no blood-line).  Tuna dumplings (so unique) never dissappoint.  LOVE it here still.
The Lawn. The music. The picnic basket. The Summer.  The traffic jam getting outta there. The bugspray (bring some)  The Mann.

So good for "Italian" hot sandwiches, cheese-steaks and roast pork with greens. Garlicky spinach and sharp provolone (50 cents more).  I had a cheese steak hoagie - and it was one of the best (Tony Luke's and Jim's beat Pat's and Geno's any day!)  Fresh bread.  Good stuff!

The Melrose has renovated its booths and light fixtures (and ladies room - hooray) since I last went.  We (party of 6) had a nice breakfast here yesterday including omelettes, pancakes and all the usuall suspects.  Our pleasant waitress Janice went on break half way thru and our new waitress (Christina??) was even nicer  Not bad!
They have gift certificates!!!!  Lovely service. I can't say enough great things about this place!  Winner, winner, SALMON dinner!

Re-joined Tyler as a dual membership (2 Adults - do not have to be in the same household) for $75 for a year (Admission is normally $15 but they now have reciprocity with PHS - Hooray!!!!)  Brian at the front desk was terrific and the volunteers in the butterfly house (a few of whom were tweens/young teens) knew their stuff.  Nice new restroom facilities (and a meeting room area - and air conditioned - WOW) near the "edible garden".  A few of the (now over a decade old) treehouses have fallen into disrepair.  Please consider donating to help aid their restoration.  Tyler is a wonderful place and an important wildlife and plant refuge right in Delco.  Love it here.

My parents are regulars here and my husband and I love it here, too. The food is truly "as good as it gets" with the exception of the canned green beans (side).  Just skip that and get onion rings, cucumber salad, mac & cheese or rice.  The seafood itself is divine - Shrimp & Scallops broiled in butter were simple but tender and delectable.  Lobster salad ($42 a lb) is terrific and the shrimp salad is fresh and flavorful.  Dine in (simple digs - you don't come here for atmosphere) or take out, you just can't beat the super fresh seafood here - fried, broiled or grilled.  Just so darned good.  And terrific service - but again, we are regulars so they treat us great.

A solid 4 this time for properly cooked Hunan Duck and (Special) Crystal Shrimp Dumplings.  They don;t always have these dishes but if they are on special (or ask - and they if have it they'll make it!) consider these.  Ian and staff are excellent and attentive.  No issues. Our go-to for "Classic" Chinese-American in Media.

Love the service here from Katie who dotes on my parents (Mom gets the same meal EVERY time - A flounder sandwich, no bread, side of sliced tomatoes).  Wonderful seafood that is always fresh and tasty. Cucumber salad is refreshing and sweet.  Love it.  My Shrimp salad sandwich was bursting with plump shrimp.  LOVE IT HERE.  Prices have gone up - $16.95 for the salmon dinner now.  Wow. $19.95 for Ahi Tuna.  Still, love it.

Came here for my birthday dinner - just me and the husband (DH) - and poissoned myself on fresh sashimi (appetizer), Tuna Tartare (a bit oversuaced - heavy on the ponzu, but still tasty) and a delicious Salmon Belly, Cucumber hand roll.  Lovely food, decent enough service. Best sushi around for the price (cheaper than Teikoku or Azie, closer than Sushi Nami).

Sadly, now that Vic is gone - the magic is, sadly, fading. Want the old Vic's?  Try Jay's Favorite - Jay & Vic know each other and steal each others recipes.  Again, reminder:  sauce on the side if you don't want an over-glopped roll!

For $12.69 ($11.75 plus tax) I had the lunch platter which was a plentiful amount of protein (I had the brisket and it was very good), 2 sides (Try the carrot fries or the Brussels Sprouts - both are good) and the green goddess salad with a delicious sweet honey citrus dressing.  I liked everything I tried and I left with a bunch to take home - it was plenty of food.  Good healthier choices than at a typical fast-food joint - but they are also right next door to Mama's and I just love it there, too.  Decisions, decisions - we are blessed.  Kacey at the front counter was terrific - great customer service.

A solid 4 now - we have been back at least 3 times for dinners with our 7 year old who gobbles down edamame, shumai, meaty delicious spare ribs (or boneless ribs) and fried rice.  (Good - but a bit greasy.)  Reasonable prices, great service from Annie and Ian, and Panda Cookies (from Japan) for $1.50 to take home at the end.  Oh - and they raise and release butterflies.  You can view the chrysali at the register.  A good, solid, delicious, "classic" Chinese-American joint.  LOVE it - and cheaper than Maggie Kuo.  (But we like it there, too, for fancy-schmancies.)

While I am partial to Morris Arboreutum - I also love Tyler. It is beautiful in the spring when the trees and gardens are blooming - late spring May - June is awesome here.  No, you can't bring your dog - but do bring a blanket or find a bench and read a book or paint or take pictures and just relax.  And if you are a member of PHS (Pennsylvania Horticulture Society) you can NOT go for a reduced rate. That irked me a bit.  Very nice front desk staff.  It's worth the trip!  (And visit Morris, too.)

I used to come here with my BFF from Jr. High and H.S. back in the day.  It was a nice, quiet (and back then) safe park to hang out in.  We would walk on the paths.  In more recent years (albeit that's still 5-7 years ago) I brought my little dog here.  A nice park - and we need those!

I stopped in to Vic's after not coming by in a long while. The place was SO crowded that I ate in the window. I had the Ocean Brother Roll (sauce on the side) and it ROCKED.  I still love it here - but it's just so tiny and cramped.  I sometimes go to Jay's now.

Consistently 4 star.  I thought quality was slipping there for a while - but I went here again tonight and had the (always great) tuna dumplings (thin sashimi slices of red tuna pounded flat and stuffed with an avocado/tobiko/sauce and pulled together to form a litle red pouch.  Glop (er. I mean sauce) on the side.  YUM!  I also had the (ouch) $13.95 "Crazy" roll which is similar to my "usual" the Ocean Brother roll.  Both are topped with a luscious REALL lump crab topping.  (I get my sauces on the side).  The Crazy has spicy tuna & 'cado inside, While the Ocean Brother has Shrimp Tempura inside.  I think I found me a NEW fave.  The Crazy Roll is less heavy (not fried) and I love that fresh crab topping.  I am STUFFED from eating all that myself - and (including the bottle of Fiji water - it still pisses me off that you have to BUY a water.  They won't serve you any.  Only green tea.) the tab came to $28.    It's not cheap.  It's very small and cramped. It's still GREAT food.

Slight upgrade for tonight's dinner here - my 6 year old LOVES it here - and I am a sucker so, of course, we went.  She knew immediately what she wanted to get. Lobster & Crab mac 'n cheese.  $24 smackaroos.  Ouch.  Thank god it tasted really good tonight.  Sometimes, I swear, it tastes fishy.  I got a $9 plain-ole hamachi maki.  6 tiny pieces.  Ugh.   For that price Doma or even Morimoto are a better deal for freshness as well as price.  Dessert, of course, was the small $13 chocolate fondue.  This time we were smart enough to ask for "no melon" (who dips melon in chocolate?).  The fondue itself is delectable and the small is big enough for 3 people easily.  This time, also, the pound cake was not stale.  Thank G-d!  Service was just OK.  The owner/server (maybe she's not the owner but she was acting owner-ish) kindof ignored us and seemed annoyed when my little one dropped a piece of penne on the floor (though I can't say I blame her -but you could at least FAKE that you were happy to see an actual customer on a DEAD Monday at 5 PM.)  My little one and I listened to the friendly bartender count bottles of flavored vodkas in preparation for restaurant week.    Finally more customers came - a couple in their 40/50's were MAKING OUT at the bar at 6 PM.  We left soon after.  Oy vey.  Verdict remians:  prices too high, for food that is just OK and COULD be stellar but seems as faded as the decor.

This place is teeny tiny - so know that before you go.  Also when I went and asked for a glass of water I was told they have no water and I'd have to buy a bottle - which I did.  I went again today and again had to buy a $1.80 bottle of Fiji.  Vic offers a great roll cominbation special and also serves some creative and (fattening - too much rich sauce) non-traditional rolls. Order the sauce on the side and problem is solved!  One item worth getting though is the "tuna dumplings".  This is really a sashimi type appetizer.  Thinnly sliced raw tuna is filled with a creamy avocado mixture (again - fat-city) and molded into a dumpling shape.  Worth a try if you are into avocado.  Also try the Sansom Roll. It is a meal in itself.  Recently I also tried (and now have dreams about) the Ocean brother roll - a huge roll stuffed with shrimp tempura and avocado,  and outside has a delicious mildly-spiced CRAB SALAD (real crab) and wasabi tobiko.  It is usually drowned in eel sauce, so again - I get mine with brown rice, sauce on the side.  (I know, I'm a picky pain in the ass.)  I prefer to go to Vic at Lunch time as it is not a dinner place.  Way too small - only 8 seats at the bar and NO TABLES.  Note:  As of July '08 prices have gone up and there are no more 2 roll lunch combos - you must now get 3 rolls for $11.95 - which is still a good deal. (But I usually only need 2 rolls. Oh well.)

Had a fantastic experience at Dining Under the Stars (often more like "Chaos out in the Heat") at Bittersweet.  Normally, they do not serve dinner - but I sure wish they'd consider it.  A group of 5 ladies enjoyed burgers, fish & chips (a special) and the FABULOUS (calorie bomb) french toast BLT.  A side of Brussels Sprouts (again with bacon) made life complete.  Service was amazing - even on a crazy Wednesday night and the weather was great, too.  Can't wait to try more items on this sweet & savory menu of comforting favorites.

This store seems somehow better now.  Maybe the flow is quicker during the morning rush?  Maybe its now that the lady cashier knows me by face I get better service?  I still cringe when I spend over $7.00 on coffee/espresso drinks and a breakfast sandwich - so I am not in here often.
Consisently high quality fish and friendly service for take out lunches. The 3 roll combo is a filling meal and a good value.  Tuna Dumplings are delicious.  MUCH better than Jay's favorite.

I used to love WMMR before they changed formats years ago.  I still listen on occaision but now that I am officially older and fartier I listen to WMJK (which used to be the valium station and is now classic rock and DiBella).

This starbucks at the corner of 20th & Market serves the local lawyers and stock exchange folks and they really manage the morning line well.  Staff is decent enough - and the bathroom is usually OK - kept locked.  Not bad!
We ordered from Uncle Oogie's for a company event - and my chicken.avocado salad was delicious.  The pasta and 'parm platters looked great, too.  Love it here, still.

Last night's visit was sooooooo fabulous.  We were smart and made a reservation for the 3 of us - we took our 5 year old DD who just LOVES (and ate 6 of) the jumbo shrimp shumai.  Service was great considering how frantically busy they were (they had to turn people away) on a Friday night.  My husband's sushi was great - especially the crunchy spicy tuna roll. I had the (ENORMOUS) Zen bento box which came with delectable tempura and 4 pieces of sushi, plus kalbi, 1 shumai (we got a little shumai'ed out) and a spicy tuna roll.  (Yum!)  If you are a big eater consider the $36 Zen box - comes with miso soup (GREAT and homemade), salad (tasty soy-based dressing) and dessert.  As a surprise - and mostly why I am giving them 5 stars is that they brought our daughter a HUGE platter ($14 on the menu) called the Doma Dessert Sampler.  (FOR FREE.)  The dessert sampler came with:  Vanilla ice cream topped with green-tea cream cheese and a fresh blueberry  Mochi-covered Strawberries (home-made mochi) with a small pot of fudge to dip them in (WOW).  3 fried banana-tempura drizlled in (more) chocolate sauce and caramel sauce.  And a MOLTEN chocolate lava cake.  It was a HUGE platter of dessert - and easily fed all 3 of us (who, by the way, were already stuffed from dinner).  Somehow we managed to eat it.  (Ha!)  What a treat.  And how nice of them to do this for us.  My little one already adores DOMA and now I am quite sure it has surpassed Roy's and Swanky Bubbles (2 of my little one' faves) as her favorite restaurant.  Man, I wish my parents had taken me to places like Doma when I was 5. (Yes, she was the ONLY kid in the joint - this is not a kiddie place.)  Kid's got good taste.  Not a chicken nugget in sight.

I am not a big fan of four-bucks, but - Chrissy - I know that lady of which you write.  She is such a nice lady that I have to give this four-bucks 3 whole stars.  I don't drink the coffee drinks but a light-ice 2 pump classic green tea lemonade is an occasional treat when my paycheck will allow it.

I am stuck between a 3 and a 4. I came solo for an early lunch on a DEAD Saturday at 12 noon.  I asked for the special "drunken beef shortribs" (There was a big sign in the window $14.95 for dinner $7.50 for lunch but was told there was no lunch portion available.  The menu seemed old-school and limited, so I went with Moo Goo Gai Pan - and to my relief it was excellent.  So good, in fact, that the leftovers I brough home from my hefty $8.95 lunch portion were gobbled up by my 7 year old.  So I might bump them up to 4 stars once I get a taste of some other items, but so far it's a solid 3.  FYI - good, but greasy, fried wonton skins and duck sauce on every table.  GUILT-inducing yumminess.

Oh how my family - especially my parents who eat there nearly every week when they are "in season" - loves the Lobster Claw.  Run by a mother and her son and his partner, this home-town seafood joint has a casual feel (GREAT for kids) and tasty fresh fish, seafood and sides.  They are just such nice people and have been around for years.  My mom gets the fried flounder sandwich and dad is partial to the grilled salmon plater.  The cucumber salad is light and sweet - not too vinegary and JUST delish.  I like the mac 'n cheese.  Last time we went I had tilapia - but the fresh blue-fish was on special and it looked fetching as well.  W love it here.  They also sell loads of take-out. The fried food is never greasy - the onion rings are so tasty.  You gotta try this "little nothing place" becuase it's really all-that.  5 stars for food and about a 3 for decor. (No atmosphere..)
4 stars for nostalgia and 2 stars for how it is today averages out to a 3 star mall experience.  Time for an overhaul, me-thinks.

Went in yesterday and hit BIG - a Tommy Hilfiger Dress for $40 and a Calvin Klein Dress - also for $40.  Restrooms are filthy, dressing room attended was not a happy camper, but I managed to get in and out - tried on 8 dresses and bought 2.  Not bad!  Gotta love that "no sales tax on clothing" in PA thing!

We joined as a family for $60 - so now we have to go at least 4 times to break even. We went yesterday to roam the vegetable garden (and eat a few tomatoes) and sit in the many "sit a spell" chairs and benches designed by a multitude of artisans.  Well worth at least 2 visits here per year.  We'll see if we go 4 times and it so, we'll re-join next year.  Note:  NO RECIPROCITY with PHS (sucks!) but they do have a discount for AHS members (which I am not.).  Excellent front desk staff - we left our credit card there and she called me on both phones.  Also the volunteer/docent in the butterfly house (maybe he is a paid staffer??) was so kind to the kids and knowledgeable.

Wow there sure are alot of La Toltecas in DE.  We stopped for a quick lunch (and we were famished) at 11:45 AM on a Sunday on our way home to Philly.  DH enjoyed his Toleca Enchiladas.  Chicken burritos/enchiladas topped with white cheese sauce and green tomatillo sauce.  He borrowed the spicy sauce that came with my fish tacos to give it extra kick.  It was NOT a spicy dish.  I had the aforementioned fish tacos that were great but boring.  No veggies - only fish on tortillas (sauce and guac along side, but not enough).  So I asked the waiter (very nice and attentive man) to get me some lettuce & tomotao - which he did and then proceeded to harge us $3.99 for them - the price of a side salad.  Listen, had I known this, I would have ordered a salad and gotten more guac and pico.  This was a big buzz kill! (And we hadn't even had any of the ga-zillion margaritas they offer).  We enjoyed our (first basket free) of chips & salsa, and DH had a diet coke (with 1 free refill).  It was reasonably priced and reasonable quality.  If I lived near here I MIGHT return but I bet there are better choices.

Surprisingly good and what a value - $5.00 gets you a whopping big portion of rice (mostly), salad (iceberg and 2 tomato slices), chicken or "lamb" or both and white and/or hot sauce.  AND you get a can of soda and a bottle of water.  Whata value - and it's pretty tasty, too.  Nice guys running the show. $5!  FIVE!  Wow.

Azie has evolved into our "special occasion" restaurant as it is just too overpriced to dine there on the regular.    Meanwhile, my daughter was turning 13 so for the 4th consecutive year we booked a party of 9 here and had great service by Dan, Tom and Ashley (who remembered us from last year). The service was great and we were seated upstairs in a lovely semi-private area.  Why not five stars?  The sushi here is just "meh".  A few of the white fish varieties (Snapper?  Fluke?  Who knows) were not fresh tasting, although the 3 biggies (tuna, yellowtail and salmon) were all just fine.  Stick with the tartar - the sauce is tasty and 2 orders of salmon tartar disappeared quickly.  Cocktails are delicious here - my Pom-Pop was so easy to drink, and the F.I.G jam is amazing, too.  The strip steak, diver scallops and crab (or shrimp) fried rice are all terrific.Feeling simple?  Salmon or Chicken Teriyaki (Usually so boring) are delightful here.  $4 cappucino and $8 creme brulee for dessert capped off a wonderful experience. Many thanks to the staff for making a special birthday even more extra-special.

Ever since Tom's Dim Sum opened, we have not been to Da Shin for a while. Today my kid was home because schools were closed.  So I ordered lunch for 3 including Shu Mai (delicious), Steamed Pork Dumplings (Very good but a bit doughy) and Sesame Chicken.  (Not my fave but my kid loves that fried dark meat chicken.).  Excellent service. They seem to have updated the menu a bit and changed owners (again??)?

A great place to get upscale (a bit pricey) gear for the garden and cute gift ideas - like home-made jams in elegant jars from Gregory Benjamin.  Love it!  Garden tools, too (spades, hoes, rakes, trugs and gloves) and potted plants.

My precocious 9 year old is no longer interested but from ages 3 -7 this place was Da Bomb!  Swing sets, a huge castle, climbing areas.  Clean and fun all around.  Love Central Park for walking the dogs, also.  (And a big sledding hill in winter.)

This location at 19/20 & Market is my "old faithful" when I am on my way to the office or running errands in this area o Center City.  There is usually a longer line during peak hours but moves quickly (hello, mobile ordering!).  They have occasionally screwed up my order but always make it right if they do - thankfully they don't mess it up too often.  Between this 'Bux and the one at 18 & Market I am well-stocked with overpriced caffeine to get me through my stressful rat-race of a week.  Mad props to the barristas who are "workin' it".  Especially the nice young man who works 3 - 7 PM ish.  Gotta have my latte. #DiabetesInaCup

OK, here's my long awaited review of Nineteen (I'm not gonna call it XIX, just 19 is fine for me.).  Even though my "special" birthday was almost a whole month ago, a very kind & generous girlfriend gifted me dinner at 19 tonight.  Chuck, our server was fabulous - I want to make that clear- as I am about to say some critical things about the service.  Here's how things shook down...  I arrived for our 6 PM reservation early - at about 5:45.  Since it was a lovely evening, I decided to have a drink on the terrace, and selected a table out in the open air.  I put down my water bottle and asked the (very pregnant) hostess where the ladies room is.  She explained that I needed to go down 1 flight on the elevator.  Great.  Fine.    When I get back there is some guy sitting at "my" table and my water bottle is gone.  So I move to another outdoor table - and the host (not the hostess) brings me a bottle of water (huge 27 oz. bottle of fancy-schmancy water from Norway - which - by the way - was damned tasty water.) to replace it.  I order a virgin Mexican Mojito - which was perfect, by the by, - a refreshing libation of club soda, fresh lime juice and basil-infused (you really could smell it) simple syrup.  Limeaid with a twist.  FAB-U!  So I drink my mocktail and quite happily sit and chill until way, way past 6 PM.  At 6:15 or so I call my g.f. - guess what???  She's seated in the dining room and has been there for half an hour.  Nobody came to get me.  Nobody told her I was there.  No nothin'.  So I ask to move to the table, and we chat and order.  Decor:  5 stars.  The dining room with it's pussy willow & pearl theme and MARVELOUS rotunda is so breathtaking.   Service: 2 (Chuck gets a 4 or 5 - he was great), everyone else was snotty and/or pre-occupied).  VERY SNOTTY.  Food - varies - 3-4 - here's why:  We started with salads.  I splurged and ordered the lump crabmeat salad which was truly delicious and lightly dressed in an orange-champagne vinaigrette.   The tomatoes were red, ripe and actually tasted like tomatoes.  The small chunks of avocado were smooth and buttery.  The bibb lettuce was right on!  For $15 bucks (whoa-momma!( that was my kinda salad.  For $15 bucks you could put a little more crab - though I must say the crab that was there was sweet and PURE lumbo lump meat.  Nary a shell!  We both had the(only vegetarian) tagliatelle entree.  The pasta was hand-crimped, and light and luscious.  It was bathed in a lemony (very sharp, but I got used to it) buttery sauce and LOADED with various hoity-toity mushrooms including morels, hen-of-the-woods, oyster and others.  If you don't like shrooms - do NOT order this.  Quite frankly I was mushroomed-out by the end of it and left (no joke!) over 1/2 cup of these precious morsels - I ate all the morels - plate side).  I also chased down all of the succulent beans (small fava - large lima - something else??)  and fresh sp[ring peas.  Oh - and there were ramps and FIDDLEHEADS.  A nice spring dish.  High-end veg for sure. But quite alot of mushrooms.  For dessert had a kickin' strong cup of Illy cappucino.  Good - but somehow not as good as the cap at Davio's.  A bit bitter.  Wesplit ahome-made waffle with nutella & berry compote.  The waffle itself was great.  I would have preferred less "glop" on top of it,but my friend preferred the sauces to the waffle. She digs nutella.  Oh - and they put a little green candle in the scoop of (homemade??) vanilla ice cream on top of the waffle.  Thankfully nobody sang!   Since someone else paid, It was a 4 star time, but honestly?  Forthe money there are much. much better places to eat - and drink - not only in Philly - but in Philly high-end hotels.  That said - the private dining room is nice- and I would definitely do a business lunch or dinner here.  But for my own life?  I doubt if I'd run back here.

Still there - Still just $5 (for lunch WITH a drink - I get a bottle of water) - Still as good as you can expect for street-cart food.  I get the lamb over Salad with "white sauce" - and it is plenty of food for lunch.  And - it's five bucks!

When I grocery shop in Doylestown I usually go to Giant, Acme or Weis'. Of the 3 Acme is my least favorite choice.  Meanwhile, it has been remodeled since I reviewed it in 2011 and I was able to get in and out (that parking lot - OMG - on a weekend it is cray-cray) relatively quickly.  They have everything you need.  Do I love it here?  No, my first choice for a chain supermarket is Giant in D-town.  But it is super-centrally located and I do come here from time to time.  (Weis' is one block away.)

5 star service from Kelsi last night. We tried to go to Dining Under the Star (aka Chaos out in the Humidity) but there were no outside tables.  So we sat on the 2nd floor (roof deck was also full) and enjoyed Kobe (actually Waygu) on a hot rock, sushi rolls, Crab meat Pad Thai and a delicious chocolate fondue for dessert (same as Teikoku).  Our 9 year old had never been here before and she loved it - especially the fondue and hot-rock beef.  She also devoured a California roll.  Good times!  About $100 for the 3 of us with no alcohol ordered.

5 stars for Camp Chill, Learn-to-skate and Birthday Party programs. Our (now) 9 year old started last summer for 2 weeks at Camp Chill - the figure skating camp.  She liked it so well we got her in for 2 MORE.  Now she is in the Learn-to-skate program (weekly classes) and once she gets "good enough" she is considering the Junior Competitive program. (Her coach, Mojca, is terrific!)  We also had her birthday party here and all 13 little girls loved it - and Patty, Carleigh and the staff were so easy to work with.  (We brought our own cake - but all other food came from the iceworks snack bar).  What a great place.  So glad we live closer now.

This is my go-to Giant when I am in Doylestown.  I much prefer it to Acme as I know the layout of the store (I start in Produce and work my way aisle by aisle).  The freezer sections are clean and adequately chilled. The Milke, OJ and Dairy are right on my way to the check out.  (Line up, folks, it's COVID time)  The young-ish cashiers are friendly and do a fine job.  No issues.

A strong four stars - but not five.  The service is rather spotty and some of the hostesses and bar staff need to up their game.  Meanwhile I had ($6) 2 pieces of Salmon nigiri - fresh and good, a spicy-crunchy tuna roll (very good but not the best ever) and a beet salad (loaded with blue cheese - next time I will skip it) and served over crunchy iceberg that others may scoff at - but I enjoyed.  Pork Belly app ($13) had barely a smattering of pricey foie gras on top (best part) and delicious braised kale underneath.    Honestly - this is my favorite place in Media so far. Great food and when the service is good it's a great spot - but twice now I have been made to feel as if dining alone there is a no-no.

Acme - you have redeemed yourself!  I desperately needed a roast chicken the day before Xmas (Christmas eve day) and they were not only open (and a bit crowded but not awful) but had fresh birds ready.  Psyched!

It really depends on what you order. Beef and Broccoli?  Great. Beef with String Beans (special)?  Great.  Shrimp and Snow peas?  Gelatinous goo. Shrimp toast?  Burnt.  I am going back to beef & broc. Every time I try something else I regret it.  Also - no ice, no water unless you BUY a bottle. I try, try, try to remember to bring my water with me.  This is SUCH a take out place.  A lady came here to dine in with 2 little kids and asked for a cup of tea and they served it to her in a tupperware soup container.  Decent Chinese food, take out is the best way. NOT a fine dining experience, or even a mediocre one.

We are big theatre supporters and wanted to support Hedgerow, however the Production we saw of "The Hitchhikers Guide to the Galaxy" was just not very good.  The parking lot is a mess - no lines - so you just park "anywhere you can".  The actual theatre was OK - odd seating - long benches. Free coffee and water (from a cooler) at intermission.  Amateurish. Just OK.  Arden Theatre or People's Light are so much nicer. But it's close to our home so we'll be back - if there is a production we WANT to see.  Chekov's Uncle Vanya?  Not so much.

Happy Hour from 5 - 7 PM (Monday thru Thursday) is a great option with $5 cocktails (try the Azie Blue) served up by Juan - the long-time, friendly bartender.  Lovely atmosphere, great (albeit pricey) food and a good date or special treat place.
We were here for a private event and it RAINED.  Even so, this was a fun venue - and nice scenery on the pier - but the food is "average" bar food.  Drinks were strong and good.

My good friends go to this Chili's and took me there for dinner.  The 2 for 20 is the real value here - if you happen to like the food.  It's just not my thing. Food is 2 stars at best. Service here was good the evening we went - and we were on a tight timeline and were able to get in and out quickly on a slow Monday night.  The "loaded" french fry appetizer was good.  The steak was over-salted and over cooked.  Corn on the cob was surprisingly sweet and good (did they add sugar??).  Meanwhile, I am grateful to my friends for their generosity - but Chili's is just OK.

It's a Wendy's,  If you've been to one - you've seen them all.  This one is fairly clean and has a decent clientele - being that it is located in the Doylestown Shopping Center.  The only reason we even go here is to placate the 4 year old who simply must have nuggets.  Whatever.  I have been to far scuzzier Wendy's.  I loathe fast food. BLAH.  3 stars is pretty damned generous on my part.

Take out lunch for me and my 14 year old came to just under $25. She still loves that (fried) Sesame Chicken.  Pork Fried Rice.  Egg Drop or Wonton Soup.  I had B&B  - Beef 'n Broc.  Solid.  Great service, too.
Listened to XPN alot growing up and in college.  Nowadays it just doesn't cut it for me, but for a college station it's pretty well run.    For real.
Seems like an extension of the other Christmas Market across the street.  Lots of fun to browse around but nothing I felt compelled to buy.
5 stars for the Black Plate Holiday special - Smoked Prime Rib.  $10.99 and deeeeeeelicious. The creamed corn is pretty amazing too.  Get there for the holidays.  P.S.  They cater.
We love Wolff's for fresh produce and local baked good - plus very good pulled pork (in the refrigerated case).  Family owned local business. Great for plants in the spring, too.

Open from 7 AM - 4 PM only (sometimes even closing a bit earlier) this  breakfast & lunch spot (No alcohol served) is lovely for "Breakfast for lunch".  My Eggs Benedict (California - with Avocado and a slice or tomato instead of Canadian Bacon) was delicious. Came with slightly bland and slightly underdone hash-browns.  Plenty of food for $9.95. Friendly service - and you pay at the front.  It was jam-packed at precisely 12 noon on a Wednesday - so come earlier if you can. Parking is also a drag - but the end result is worth it.  Sit on the patio under an umbrella if the weather permits.  NICE!

What a treasure.  We were members for 1 year and then it just got cost prohibitive - so we try to visit on Sundays when admission is on a "donation" basis.  The long-time head curator just passed away.  So sad.  We enjoyed the special exhibits on Renoir Landscapes and Frida Kahlo.  Our 3 year old can recognize Renoir's works.  Amazing.  (We didn't take her to see Frida - too gory & depressing.)  We also sometimes attend "art after five" and have some over-pricedcatered apps and listen to Jazz or Classical music,  Very gentile.  So classy.  Love the Museum of art - and the "discount gift shop" on the Balcony (The Balcony Shop?).  We never buy in the main gift shop - usually if you wait a while - you'll find the item on sale in the Balcony shop.  Also the restaurant is nice for brunch or dinner.  (Dinnner on Friday nights only.)

During rush hour? Fuggetaboutit!  I agree with Steven B. below about all the gas wasted - and this happens every day!  It's a necessary evil when I have to get to Philly from where I currently work, but I avoid it whenever possible.

It's old-faithful Acme in Doylestown.  The parking lot is a ZOO and the produce can really variable from great to "you're kidding?".  Staff are generally friendly and lines move quickly.  It can get crazy crowded on weekends - and now the SuperFresh of D-town is gone (yup - the recession at work) we are left with this or Genuardi's.  So acme - for 40 years we've known and loved/liked/hated you and now you're nearly all we've got!!!

Had a 3 star service (4 star food) experience here for my birthday party (11 guests). We were seated in the front bar area at two 6-top tables.  Splitting the check at the end was a nightmare, plus the pre-added gartuities rangesd from 21 to 40%.  (40%??  What???)  Everything got corrected eventually.  Meanwhile the best bites of the night were the Salmon tartare (magical) and the Chilean sea bass.  Very expensive for what it is - but it's one of our go-to spots for special occasion meals. I wish the service was better - they get so busy on a Saturday night that I tend to not go there on weekends.
Still a great place for sushi (don't miss the tuna dumplings) and sashimi.  Same friendly owners and wonderful service at a tiny bar that gets PACKED at lunchtime.  Great find!

Many thanks to Matt and the gang for hosting my class's High School reunion at Villa Capri.  We basically took the place over with about 65 people in attendance for light apps (Calamari, bruscetta, "Brooklyn" pies, salad and mini cannoli).  We all had a great time and the bar was well run.

Excellent.  Excellent cheesesteaks. I had the Italian (Sharp Prov and Broc. Rabe) and added mushrooms - $.75. My friend had "The Works"/  About $11 a pop - but huges and delicious and NOT dripping with grease.  Crowded and cramped to eat there - but so. worth. it. Teeming with tourists - NATCH.  CASH ONLY  (ATM on site)

Honestly, I had a 5 star first experience at Chrome with Abbie and the fabulous Sherri M.  I was referred to Chrome by several friends who are "moms" at my kid's school.  I never went because I was loyal to another stylist, but she recently left her place to have a baby and since I am not sure when she'll be back I decided to "try".  Well, I am glad I did.  Sherri gave me a color and blow-out (no cut this time - but likely next time) and used Redken permanent color, single process.  It. Is. Lovely.  Abbie served as receptionist and shampoo-person - and she was working hard.  I can't imagine how busy she must be on a weekend.  (They are closed Sunday and Monday).  Parking was a little tight but OK - you can always park at the nearby firehouse and walk over.  Pricing is mid-priced ($85 for color and blow-out, before tips to both ladies).  I will be back. Thank you!

I visited Azie for the first time alone - and it sure won't be my last. Expensive - yes - but I had impeccable service on the (now open) rooftop deck and tried the delicious (and huge) Chicken Noodle (rice noodles) soup. Simple - but great.  Good selection of cocktails, too.  Can't wait to come back and try more.

Came here for the amazingly cheap breakfast with a friend while we were both unemployed.  We got a big pot of coffee and 2 breakfast plates of panckaes (she had bacon, I had one egg - man, one scrambled egg is kinda small, but when you're broke?...)  Enjoyable food, very cheap and they let us sit and linger for a while.  Luxurious?  No.  But it got the job done!

Had lunch here with a colleague and it was just OK. She had a $7 cheese quesadilla and I had a $14 shrimp and pineapple salad.  Both were fine but the service was really weird.  They were nice but kind of ignored us. We were on a tight time frame (lunch hour on a work day) so we really needed to pay our bill and go.  Not a bad place but not mind blowing either.

Kinda boring, actually.  You wait and wait (timed ticket entry plus a security tent) and then hear a lecture and then see 3 rooms.  Whoopie!  But it's HISTORY so you kinda have to do it.  I did it as a kid 30 years ago and did it again today with my 11 year old.  Done.

Got take-out out of desperation during the Covid19 Scare and thank goodness they were open, but I do NOT recommend take out from here.  The food gets cold (not their fault) and sushi gets warm (again not their fault) and its just so much better eating there.  But in any case we had a birthday celebration during a "lock down" so this was as swanky as we could get.  The salmon tartar is always a winner. The beet salad (my go-to fave) was honestly not good.  The beets had a bitter taste to them.  Odd. I love this salad and order it many times but this time was a fail.  My husbands crab and cream cheese maki were cold and a bit soggy by the time we brought the food home.  You gotta dine in. For the high prices to be at all worth it do NOT take out. Once the Covid thing is over hopefully things will go back to normal.  THANK YOU FOR BEING OPEN at all.

Used the online ordering for carry out and my order was complete, correct, ready and waiting when I went to pick it up.  Delicious for fast-food BBQ and so easy for a hungry crowd.  Staff are so smiley and friendly.  Great!!!

Ook!  Really?  My kid's friends (and their parents) all love it here - but i just don't get it.   Strip mall decor and "meh" service with bland pizza on a too-thick (for me) flabby crust that does NOT taste like NYC pizza one bit.  I have had better at Season's!  (And worse, too - to be fair).  Maybe the non-pizza items are better?  But I am not rushing back to try again.  Not impressed, Pappone's.

On par with Linvilla Orchards (but no petting zoo, less crowded and better for a purely Farmer's Market experience.  They don't grow the produce here (yet - they are buying up land across the stree) - but they carry a ton of plants, flowers, produce and cider.  My house cookies!!!   Cider donuts A smattering of gourment goodies.  We love it here.

Like a supermarket for booze. Love it.  Except perhaps on New Year's eve or right before the superbowl.  Can you say "uber-crowded"?  Also a great source for free cardboard boxes.  On weekends there can be a police presence so do not overload your car with booze and drive to PA.  Be smart, people!

Honestly - the food was exquisite my last time to Zama (in June 2017) with a colleague for a $100 (no alcohol, no dessert) lunch.  Sushi, salads, appetizers, all sorts of wonderful fish.  Delightful.  Every bite was perfection.  Wish I could afford to dine here more often.

My experience at this location of Jared was fine - the place was nearly empty which surprised me as it was the week before Christmas. They had a ton of staff available.  This seems like they focus on wedding/engagement rings.  I was seeking something very specific - a 14K (or platinum but budget won;t allow it) charm shaped like a number 3.  Believe it or not they had Pandora charms in 2, 4 & 6 but no 3.  In any case I may or may not return if I need something but I tend to buy online or even on ebay.
Much improved over the years and in winter my teen enjoys the River Rink.  Lots to see and do in summer, too. Famous for Fireworks (and crowds) on July 4th.

I disagree with the 3 star people.  The landing is all about the view and the FABULOUS deck - and for this alone they could serve garbage.  But they don't.  They serve really nice food - a little yuppified and for a wedding here - the prices are way out of line.  (We contemplated having our reception here but it was just cost prohibitive - and the place is a bit smaller that we wanted for a big wedding.)  That said - I sent my parent's here for their 25th anniversary (albeit that was 17 years ago...) and they enjoyed it enormously.  Over the years owners have changed - but it's still "in the family" and a great, great place.  An all-time fave for me - with lots of nostalgic memories.  Oh - and they have a nice wine list.  Including a few bubbly selections which I enjoy.

A new, fresh, clean and well-stocked Giant that already is crowded on weekends and during peak shopping periods.  Way better than the crapolla Acme in Granite Run.  I still visit the Giant in Aston because i know the store layout (or at least i knew it before they renovated a piece of the store) and can shop faster there.  I am a Giant shopper for sure - more than Acme, Shoprite, Trader Joe's Wegmans's (too far) or Whole Paycheck (love it, too far, can't afford).  For my every day groceries, look for me in line, at Giant.
Lore's makes the custom chocolate bars for my child's school.  They are delicious and come in Milk, Dark or White - and my kid has tried all of them.  A pleasure to work with!

I will not be rushing back here - even though the service was great (I came early before the 12:15 hoards arrived) and the dumpling sampler ($14 for 8 dumplings - 2 each of 4 varieties) was great.  I got dan dan noodles to go. What a disappointment,  Never again for that dish (Go to Han's for the real Dan Dan).  Sauce was awful.  Beautiful decor, pleasant service, overpriced "meh" food. I spent $26 for lunch (after tax and tip) and no beverages, no dessert.  Yikes.  Such a shame.
A much needed addition to Brookhaven/Media/Aston area as the existing Giant was getting super crowded.  Large aisles and (CoVid excluded) usually well stocked.  Yay!

Celebrated my kids 11th birthday here (we celebrated her 10th here last year) with a party of 7. Service by Ashley was top-notch, 5 star all the way - but there are some serious food errors that occured.  My mother & I shared the Strip steak, and while the flavor was delicious the meat was gristley and not pleasant to eat.  We also asked if we could have veggies instead of truffle fries and we got ONE sprig of asparagus each.  (What??!)  Luckily a plate of light cooked vegetables (quite al dente) arrived but over half way through the meal.  Dessert was divine as always and service good - but that steak?  I can and have made better at home.  Oh - and skip the shrimp shumai.  They're frozen.

I lived in Center CIty for 6 years from 2005 - 2011. I also lived in near West Philly (Univesirty Cityish) from 1991 - 1993 - probably would have given that about 2 stars.  So many classic things to see and do - the Museums, Reading Terminal Market, Italian Market, South Street, Old(e) City, the Historic District.  Philly is on the rise - the shopping, dining and entertainment have all improved even with the recent economic unrest.  Mayor Nutter is doing the best he can.
I had no issues - there was a long line but they quickly opened another register.  i did NOT have any prescriptions filled - just ducked quickly in and out to buy a few things.

First Watch (alot like Turning Point) is a casual breakfast/brunch/lunch place. On weekends it gets very crowded but we were able to snag an outdoor table after a 35 minute wait.  (Thanks, Vince!)  Avocado Toast, Eggs Benedicts, Salads, Veggie Sandwich, Fresh juices and delicious (sweet and caloric) iced coffee.  All the food was great.  Pricey for egg dishes but a fun brunchy spot. Large portions.
A delicious selection of coffee and espresso drinks, smoothies, pastries and other treats.  A chill, laid-back atmosphere.  Love it.

I only eat at Chili's when my friend (who loves it - why, I will never know) drags me here.  So last night we dines here - my first time to this location in 8 years.  We got the 2 for $25 - shared an app of onion petals, I had baby back ribs and she got chicken fajitas.  Dessert she took home - we were too full to eat it.  The best part?  Dinner for 2 with tax, tip and 2 soft drinks was $40.40. The worst part?  That food is so salty - it's like a sodium bomb.  Kudos to our server Mahnyah who was working her tail off - she was so friendly and great - unlike the aloof and disinterested hostesses.  The service here in general needs an upgrade.  Avoid if possible and take your blood pressure meds. Chili's is not for me!

When we lived in Philly we were stuck with the Class of 1923 rink, so now that we are suburbanites, we take our 8 year old to IceWorks (not for hockey - just for open family skating).  She loves it - especially watching the Zamboni. Plus they have classes here - but we have not yet had her take any. We also enrolled her for 2 weeks of "Camp Chill" - the ice skating camp (they also have ice hockey sumemr camp).  I will update my review once camp has come and gone. And they offer birthday parties.  Wear a jacket - it's COLD in the rink. At Christmas they have a few "Skate with Santa" sessions.  Fun.  They also have a snackbar on one side and a full "bar-bar" with hot food on the other.

Just a hair away from a 5 star experience last night.  Dining Under the Stars was poorly attended due to spotty rain - but that was great for us as we snagged a prime table on the roof deck and had a fine and wonderful meal.  Great service and food. Bulkoki spring rolls, Kobe Hot Rock, Sushi and Salmon teriyaki were all terrific. El kiddo devoured her food - including a shrimp tempura roll.  So what's the problem? No more green vegetables served with entree - only mashed yams (excellent). I was craving some green beans or broccoli or kale.  Anything.  There is an $8 side of mixed veg - but we didn't go for it.  The entree was $22 alone for salmon and yams.  they used to include a vegetable but no more.  Also $10 for a side (huge - but still) of plain fried rice with only egg is CRAZY!  PLEASE BRING BACK the GREENS!

Our now teenager has been skating here for over 8 years and we practically live here.  The facility is well managed and well run.  There is a focus on hockey, but the figure skating program is also very strong.  We have sunk alot of money here between coaching and ice fees, competitions and the annual ice show to benefit the IWSC - Iceworks Figure Skating Club.  Her head coach is amazing and we can't say enough great things about the family we have become a part of at Iceworks.  4 ice surfaces, locker rooms, Pro Shop, Cafe, Bar, Gym.  It's really great when you visit other area rinks who have 1 or maybe 2 ice surfaces if you are lucky.

Our kid has been a figure skater for 5 years now and we practically live here.  If you or your child wants to learn to skate (figure or hockey), this is an excellent facility.  Caring coaches, trainers and staff.  A cafe AND a full bar/restaurant.  Locker rooms.  Party rooms.  A banquet room.  Iceworks is our second home. No lie.
Our kid has been enrolled in the Junior Competitive Figure Skating Program for 2.5 years and We can not say enough great things about the sport and this facility.  LOVE IT!
A perfectly made Iced Latte and a Smoothie for my friend with a clean restroom (need a code to use it) and friendly service.  No  issues.

I am fairly certain this is the correct location of Papa John's that we order from.  My 6 year old loves the plain pizza here and pepperoni. I find it to be cardboard-like with plasticky cheese.  And a weird garlic margarine comes with it.  Eeeew.  She hates the sausage and finds it "too spicy".  Meanhwile I am unimpressed - I ate a salad. Thankful they deliver, though.

Fergie's latest creation has transformed Oh! Shea's into the Goat.   Either named for the Goat statue in Rittenhouse Square or perhaps aspirational as The Greatest Of All Time?  In any case the bathrooms are clean, everything has been painted and the menu is re-vamped.  A full bar with any and everything you need plus short rib poutine?  All we need now is Chris behind the bar.  Good work and best wishes!

Will be closed nearly all of January 2022 for much needed renovations. Meanwhile, we will miss those (pricey but tasty) homemade soups.  The Italian Wedding, Tomato Bisque and Corn Chowder are all excellent.  A great place for produce.    See you in 2022.

This is the Saladworks in Liberty Place - and the lines get long but move quickly.  Everyone here works fast and constantly making salds, soups, pastas and sandwiches.  I usually get the Cobb Salad with a few substitutions. You can also do a "Create Your Own" - and it's usually around $10 - for a large salad and a roll.  A good choice when I need something in a hurry and the line is not too bad.
2 words.  Pulled Pork.  You must try their version - sweet and delicious.  My 10 year old LOVES it.

We usually visit the CFA in Lima, and this one has the same owner. We finally got a chance to visit the drive-thru during the great Corona-scare of 2020.  That said the drive-thru moved very quickly except for an error when the cashier rang us up.  This was quickly corrected and we were on our way except - no ketchup.  They forgot ketchup packets.  Oops.  Thankfully we were going home and have ketchup there.  Also, did you know CFA serves FISH during Lent?  They are delicious - I got the filets (no bread) but you can also get them on a sandwich.  If you like fried fish - and happen to be here during lent - try the fish.  Surprisingly good.

Wawa is a necessary evil.  I have a love/hate relationship with it, but all in all we are lucky it's still here.  The cigs, sodas and water bottles are there when we need them.  A quart of milk. Some sliced Mango (really) and in a pinch, a wrap.  (Blech.)  Glad to have you nearby, Wawa.  Wish you had more parking.  The spots are nearly always full.
Attended a big (350plus) event in the grand ballroom. Excellent service and surprisingly good food.  Recommend..

I love DuRoss - the man and the store.  He is a doll.  And he is a damned fine saponifier. The soap "popsicles" are just soooooo cute.  And the Mojito body scrub (the sugar based one) is really heavenly in the shower.  They even have a men's line and carry a few Italian and HTF (that's hard to find) bath & body products made by people other than Steve Du Ross.  Great staff and cute, cute shop.  LOVE IT!!!!  Oh - and they also did a private event for our group and it was such fun.  If you can, grab a bunch of gals and have them do a soap & lip balm making workshop for you. It's a blast and you take home the goodies you make.

A good friend (who was a regular at their old location) and I had lunch at the new location of Taqueria Moroleon.  While the new "Italian Diner"-feeling location is spacious and clean (full bar with LED color-changing lights and tequila bottles shaped like skulls), it has lost some of it's charm from the "old days".  Thankfully, the food is wonderful (at least, we were very pleased). My friend had a specialty burrito (can't remember which one) and I had the Lunch combo #2 with a chicken burrito (instead of beef) and a GREAT corn-tortilla wrapped cheese enchilada.  The tortilla tasted super fresh.  Service by Suri (Suril?) was great - what a doll!  Prices are a bit high - especially for dinner - but for lunch it's a decent value and the portions were huge (both of us took home about 1/2 of our meals).  Fresh (slightly greasy) chips and 2 kinds of salsa (not pico) were a refreshing change from the "Old El Paso"-style "ketchup" we are used to getting at El Tapatio.  (Sorry El Tapatio - we love you for different reasons).

A step above Olive Garden and not as good as Carraba's in the scheme of faux-talian chains.  Our server Sean was kind and attentive at our casual business luncheon here last week.  Today's server, Meghan was just as nice.  My colleagues & I each ordered 1 soft drink and 1 entree each.  Some have "make your own" pasta - for $9.99 (Salad additional).  I had a delicious lunch portion of the chicken with artichokes & mushrooms in a (fattening) lemon sauce (Full of butter or oil - but tasty none-the-less). I have also tried the "Antonio's Rigatoni"  (Rigatoni with braised beef - tender and delicious - in a tomatoe sauce with caramelized onions.) which is really good.  I have it with cremini mushrooms added.  My colleague's chicken parm looked good - but not spectacular - which is just how Romano's is.  Good but not spectacular.  Oh - and the Olive Oil they serve for dipping on each table is pure bitterness in a bottle.  It's cheap garbage. Please consider upgrading your olive oil.  It is literally inedible.  The bread (which comes out hot as a small square loaf) - is pretty good.  Desserts were very inexpensive ($1.99 - $3.99) but we were too full to partke (BIG portions even at lunchtime).

Will update review after I pick up the car. Drove mby and saw this in my corporate parking lot.  Expensive ($17 for exterior, $14 for interior only, $27 for both) compared to my drive through place.  We shall see.  Very courteous guys running the show.

I will try again - but - for now 1 star and here is why.  Very disappointed.  Walked in at 8:25 PM on a Wednesday night and was told "Sorry, Kitchen is closed"  It's a DINER for goodness' sake! I just wanted dinner and a quiet place to eat and take a conference call.  Who closes a diner at 8 PM? Oh wait - the 352 Diner in Delco also closes pitifully early. Don't people in the burbs eat dinner? Please consider staying open until 9 at least.  I wonder what they do on Friday and Saturday nights??

This is for the NEW Capriccio that opened near Love Park.  So far so good - my 4 year old and I have been here 3 times and had ice cream and chocolate covered pretzels and milk for snacks.  She loves it here and usually when we come iot's pretty mpty.  It is brand spankin' new - and the bathroom (ask for a key) is still clean and fit for use.  It has pretty much the same menu as the Old Capriccio on 17th Street.  The manager, Liz, is really nice and has a son about my dd's age so that's cool.  I wish them much success.  Hope they can keep in clean and new looking.

Old-school Chinese in ZERO atmosphere. BBQ spare ribs were big and meaty. Mango Chicken was awful - too much gloppy ketchup-based sauce Steamed Chicken dumplings had a delicious wrapper and MSG-laden filling.  I won't rush back - there are far better places, but for a post-flower show respite with the fam, this was just fine - and inexpensive.

So far so good - my 4 year old and I have been here 3 times and had ice cream and chocolate covered pretzels and milk for snacks.  She loves it here and usually when we come iot's pretty mpty.  It is brnad spankin' new - and the bathroom (ask for a key) is still clean and fit for use.  It has pretty much the same menu as the Old Capriccio on 17th Street.  The manager, Liz, is really nice and has a son about my dd's age so that's cool.  I wish them much success.  Hope they can keep in clean and new looking.

Mellissa - my 8 year olds FAVORITE stylist from Mastercuts and about 3 or 4 other ladies (mostly or all from Mastercuts) have left and opened their own salon on the 2nd Floor of the Granite Run Mall.  The space used to be a salon and you can tell they re-did it on a budget - but the dated digs are not why we come here.  We come her for Melissa whom we love and the great $12 kids and $15 adults cuts ($25 for a wash cut and blow dry).  Melissa is a talented stylist and has done updos, braids, cuts' bang trims, flat ironed styles and more on my 7 now 8, soon to be 9 year old who was PETRIFIED of the salon until we started coming here.  Check out Shear Bliss - if you are ever near Granite Run Mall - and ask for Melissa. She's the best!  (And Margot is great for color, too.)

I am taking a gamble - made an appointment due to good service when I walked in. The next day I took my (adorable) 8 year old in for photos.  The session itself went very smoothly even though our photographer was a trainee which had me worried. The other lady (an experienced photog) trained him and they both took pictures during the session.  We had about 50 shots to choose from and narrowed it down to two poses.  Sheets of photos are $18 each (or a package of 10 sheets plus a CD for $135). We only got two 8 by 10s and would have loved to buy more fbut they wanted $105 (talked them down to $75) for just the CD filled with .jpgs.  No thanks.  Also they tried to sell us a $12 "club membership" where you get $10 off every visit and "free" sheet.  This would be a good option if we ever were to return - but I will not be rushing back here.  That said, there is no seating/session fee and I like that alot.  We'll be back if we ever need more shots of el kiddo.
The renovations have REALLY helped this creepy old station to look alot nicer.  There are still a ton of creepy homelss folks hanging out here, though.  I try to go to Hamilton instead.

I will be generous and give 4 stars - it may be more of a 3 star place for most people.  We were treated extremely well here todayfor our holiday luncheon - a party of 19 with a nice set of choices for a prix-fixe menu.  We all got the Tuscan Bean soup (good - not great) and choice of Caesar ir House Salad.  I had the house with Balsamic vinaigrette - and it was fresh and tasty.  I had the Chicken Parm as an entree - which was deep fried - but otherwise good.  Dessert was a chocolate mousse coated profiterole.  Tasty but unappetizingly presented.  Service was surprisingly attentive and timely.  And yes, just as Chrissy R. did, I heard the Broad Street line train rumble on by when I was downstairs in the ladies room.  3 steps up from an Olive Garden.

I went to Oggi today and saw Henry - who has been there for 17 years.  I had a great single process color and a simple, classy haircut.  I also bought a great Kerastase leave-in treatment - and I love this line of products.  It was a pricey day - dropped about $175 including tips - so I won't be back often, but I will be back.  One big turn of- black hair all over the floor at Henry's chair when I sat down.  And nobody came to sweep it up at all during the nearly 75 minutes I was there.  Eew!

Well, the Boat House has clearly "jumped the shark".  It's hey-day long over, fading decor and aging facilities along with a "typical" fried-seafood menu.  (Bar food with shrimp, fish and clams added.)  Service was fine - but we were asked if we wanted to eat on plastic plates because - as our server mentioned - "The Dishwasher isn't doing his job".  Eew.  So we opted for the disposable plates.  Weird.  Rumor has it this place is closing soon - and I can certainly see why. I would never go back here. Perhaps years go this was a "happening place" but not any more. Rest in piece.

Wow!  Finally a clean, safe, fabulously-stocked (and equally highly priced) convenience grocer.  The have milk, shrimp shumai, honey candies, go-go squeeze (applesauce) and boar's head deli.  All the neccesities.  Thank goodness they opened!

Believe it or not we had a 5 star (As good as it gets for sure) experience at the average (3 star) Folsom/Ridley Staples (next to the Acme).  We needed some last minute and CHEAP school supplies on LABOR DAY - the day before the first day of school.  We found exactly what we needed (Folders and single subject notebooks for 25 cents piece!!!) Plus a "graph paper" notebook for that pesky math class.!  Got in and out with minimal lines (WOW) and a fabulous cashier - she is brand new and her name started with "A"  I wish I could remember her name - she deserves a big, fat raise.  Staples saved our asses!

Even though my daughter did not enjoy her veal parm (she said it tasted "like soap") and my father did not enjoy his lamb chops (they were "just fair").  My husband, mother and I enjoyed our dishes.  (My mom and I shared the Veal Francaise - which was delicious and, thankfully, not drowning in butter-sauce as we asked for it "light" on the sauce).  Salads were super fresh and the best part for me was the screppelle soup.  Awesome.  Good service, too.  My 10 year old wanted to give this place 2 stars but I like it here and next time I am coming without her.  Meanwhile, she polished off her New York Cheesecake for dessert with no problems and I enjoyed a perfect cappuccino.  So there!

So awful it makes the Warrington Chuck E. Cheese's look like paradise. We had our DD's 4th birthday party here about 2 years ago, and came back here on July 2, 2011 during the July 4th weekend madness.  After trying unsuccesfully to use the broken credit card machine to pay for $10 worth of tokens (There was a long line for tickets and tokens)  I succumbed and boought them at the counter.  It was DEAFENING in there and 3 of the machines DD tried to play were broken.  The manager was summoned and agreed to give us a refund.  Not happy!  Fortunately my kid will grow out of this phase of life very soon.  AVOID on holiday weekends!  Giggleberry staff:  FIX YOUR MACHINES!!!!

Brand new - huge and much needed in this part of town. A big improvement over the dinky "State Store" they closed on Chestnut.  So happy to be able to get a few bottled of bubbly for the holidays or a bottle or liquer or vodka when I need them.  (And an easy walk from 20th Street Station).

I realize that 5 stars may seem high - as it's really more of a 3-4 star place but our experience for dessert tonight was way above and beyond our expectations.  After a fairly LOUSY meal at El Camino across the way, we came over just to check out this new "retro-style" diner.  As we could not see any signage we came in and chatted a long while with the adorable, friendly hostess who said that this is "Darling's".  "Darling's"?  I asked.  As in the 20th street and the the other little tiny cute cheesecake makin' Darling's?  Yup.  Wow.  I am blown away - this looks NOTHING like the other two Darlings.  The place is huge.  And immaculately clean.  And Airy  And fabulous.  And the cheesecakes and slammin' Mac 'n cheese are on the menu.  (Con't miss the Bananas Foster Cheesecake.)  And I got quite a caffeine buzz from my STRONG and tasty iced latte. Went well with the chocolate chip muffin style pound cake.  (Try heating it up, guys!) Yum!  To top it off the Owner came out to chat for a bit and was so kind to us.  Can't wait to come hear with my kid!  She will love it. I wish them all the best and hope they make it.  There are some pretty bad reviews on here - but to me this place whipped the pants off of El Camino. (Service wise - can't comment on the food - but the desserts at Darling's are really AWE inspiring.)  Go to Darling's!!!!!  Any one of them.

Our company sponsored the truck - with a limited menu - to provide lunch for 2 hours (12 noon - 2 PM) for over 200 people.  The choices were 1/2 a cheese steak (with our without onions), a crispy chicken sandwich (with cheddar cheese sauce and bacon, if desired) or a falafel and grain bowl to satisfy the vegetarian crowd.  I opted for the cheese steak and after about a 6 minute wait it arrive - the meat was cold. Meanwhile the sauce was warm (Melted American) and the fries were piping hot.  Excellent service and OK food. Not orgasmic, and no holy grail but for a corporate event, it was fine. (for "free"?  Bring it on!) I would try a different item next time - the chicken sandwiches looked better than the cheese steak - so maybe I just ordered wrong?  #GratefulButHonest

Holy smokes, it's hot as blazes in here! All those freezer cases in a tiny cramped (dirty) space.  Service is slow as molasses - but they are trying. For Dining under the Stars - they had ONE person in addition to the kind but over-worked owner.  Cash only.  Meanhwhile my year old ADORES this place.

Met up with an ex-yelper for a quick lunch today.  Had the $5.99 lunch combo - Tomato Bisque Soup (very good) 1/2 Chicken Avocado wheat wrap (good, but not awesome) and a terrific tall Cafe au lait.  This place is a good choice to get away form the crowds and relax for while.  It's very 3 star.
Wawa, is, indeed, the Native-American word for munchies. And smokes.  And this one is convenient - although smaller than some.  Gotta.  Have a.  Wawa.

So I picked up my car and the interior windows were NOT done - all smudged and smeared (my dog leaves nose prints).  So the manager said I could bring it back next week and they will redo it.  We shall see...  Customer service so far is good, but for the high cost ($17 after tip/tax) - for INTERIOR ONLY) I would prefer that it be done correctly the first time.  I will report back after next week. I want to LOVE IT, as it is so convenient and the guys seem hard working and friendly.
Closing for good/Going out of Business 12/22. Everything at least 50% off - selling down to the bare walls.

I really, really, really wanted to give Happy Rooster more stars - especially since I know the chef - and his family and he is a really great guy and has re-vamped the menu.  The menu itself is very nice - we especially enjoyed the asparagus app - with a luscious poached egg on top and truffle-infused pecorino cheese (Oh yes, and Bacon.).  It harkened to a traditional French preparation - with a lemony twist.  I also really liked the house-made gnocchi, but the oxtail on top of it was very oily (even moreso - and yes, i know - oxtail is not a "light and healthy choice".)  That said, they offer an app & entree portion and I should have gotten the smaller app portion.  I took about 1/3 of it home.  It was very tasty.  (Just a wee bit oilier than I'd like.)  My friend had the (again house-made) agnolloti - which were good, but not spectacular.  After eating the asparagus salad - the sauce for the agnollotti (which also has butter and lemon in it) seemed a but redundant.  Maybe that was our fault for a bad ordering choice??  In any case, the fresh fava beans were EXCELLENT.  (I'm a fan of teeny-beanies!)    The 2 (male) bartenders who also served us were prompt and couteous.
