Alas, my chef-friend, had already left for the night - but he is doing a great job in turning this place around.  A vast improvement on the menu front.  Dinner for 2 ran us just over $50 - but we did not order drinks or dessert.  (Alas, no room for the home-made zeppole. )  Maybe next time.

This salon is featured on the stye networks show Split Ends. It is located in a "Strip mall" type setting.  It is a busy, high energy salon.  They offer highlights, color and cuts.  The stylists all look very professional and wera high heels.

Just a note that we still love Cafe Cret - although it is very expensive and a cup of soup is $4.75.  OUCH!!!!  BUT we have to let you know about the fabulous Le Bus chocolate chip cookies.  They are the reason my daughter is giving Cafe Cret 5 stars.  If you get them heated up (ask the guy to do it) they are heaven on a plate.  For $1.08 (with tax) it' s a great winter warm up.  Terrific service from the guys & gals who work here, especially Emily (who may have left by now).  Many are college and post-college aged students.

Not bad - but not great either.  The best part?  The super cheap price for the generous lunch special.  Mine came with Mediocre Miso, a tasty entree (Tofu with Eggplant in garlic sauce) and brown rice.  For a side I chose green salad (bad idea, and I should have known better) which was iceberd with 2 tomato slices and 1 cucumber slice.  Lame-o!  Next time (if there is one) I'll try the mushrooms.  Service was fine - efficient and quick.  Water was refilled promptly without asking (score).  OK, Maybe this place is 4 star foor/service but the 2 star decor needs a refresher pronto!

I am giving them 5 stars (when in reality they are more of a 4 star place) due to the PHENOMENAL service we received.  Angela - the (then) event planner helped us plan and cater a 70 person party.  They provided 2 (high school aged, but very competent) servers, all the pans, sterno and GREAT, GRAT food.  We had a fresh green salad, tomatoe pie (cut in squares on platters), Insalata Caprese, Sausage & Peppers, Pasta with mini meatballs, and a delicious Chicken Francese.  The food was marvelous and the amounts we ordered fed everyone with some (not not a ridiculous amount) of leftovers.  Perfect budgeting and execution.  Lovely!!!  I receommend them for catering for sure.  In our case (big order) they delivered and set up everything (for a fee).

Roosevelt Memorial Park is a Jewish Cemetary and it is NOT closed - I attended a funeral there a few days ago.  I also attended a funeral there 5 years ago and sat under the SAME blue awning.  The rabbi officiating was very good and the service was a nice commemoration of a life well-lived.  Yes, it is a crowded, old cemetary - so maybe it lists as closed because maybe there are no new plots available?

Wow- nobody reviewed this?  I am close to giving them 4 stars.  I enjoyed my chicked dish and chatting with the chefs in the semi-open kitchen.  My husband, however hated it here and so we never have gone back.  he got a Pizza Margarita which was slightly burnt and not worth the high price in his opinion.  I would definitely go back there though - with a friend - not with DH!

OK I split the difference and gave 3 stars.  here's why:  Food selection - 5 stars Beer selection - 5 stars Food quality - 4 stars Service - 1 star Prices - 1 star - soooooo expensive! Cashiers are rude and inconsiderate.  I dropped over $50 on random groceries and they rang it up incorrectly and swiped my card.  They then asked me to pay for the 2 items they forgot to ring up in cash.  It was a nightmare.  I basically spent $54 on a dozen eggs, an apple, an orange, a bowl of cut fruit, a chef salad, a turkey wrap, some hummus, a quart of OJ, 2 boxes of raspberries, a container of mixed nuts, a container of dried apricots, a package of sliced organic cheese.  $54!  Ack!!!!!  For one small bag of groceries.  That said - I am glad they were there when I needed them.  I paid the price for the convenience.  And for organic.

This is a scathing review of the way this practice is administered.  The actual care and pediatric dentistry we received here was quite good 3 or 4 star - but Terry - the front desk manager of the South Philly branch of Doc Bresler's cavity busters has made it difficult for us to stay with this practice.  To start - reaching the South Philly office is difficult - you call the main office and are routed through the phone system. Often calls and voice messages are not returned and appointments are only sporadically confirmed.  Our daughter had a coveted Saturday AM appointment at 9 AM (their alleged opening time).  We arrived at 8:55 AM and the doors were locked.  So we waited (outside on Snyder Avenue) and waited with our 5 year old, and finally I called the main office from my cell phone.  "Oh."  the man said "That office closed today".  Well it was news to me!   And to the 14 other parents who showed up that day.  So we forgave them and came to another appointment about a month later - terrible front desk experience again.  Meanwhile - my kid had her $255 fluoride tx, prohpy and 2 bitewings. In my head I am thinking - "I need to change dentists".  So I have.  We'll be seeing them soon - and yelping accordingly.  Terry - you are sometimes nice and sometimes very brusk with the parents.  Maybe it's just me and you hate me?  Whatever the case - you need to confirm ALL appointments and return phone calls more promptly.

3,5 stars - but I will give them 4 due to excellent service from Cathy (??) and the hostess.  It was our first visit but we will return.  I had the Grouper (special that night - but I have a feeling often) with fresh tomatoes and lumps of crabmeat.  The fish was perfectly cooked and not dry at all.  Delicious but a bit salty and over-sauced (lots of butter.)  DH had the Chicken sorretino with spaghetti in a blush sauce.  (Again, way oversauced - but delicious).  The food is good and portions are large (we both took some home) but there are definitely some areas for improvement (salt and oil/butter content are too high).  As I said before - very good service that night. (Saturday at 6 ish.) I will be back!

We ordered 3 large Cheese pies and 2 orders of Cinnamon Sticks (pizza dough with cinnamon sugar on top with icing). It was a veitable carb-fest for "Take your youngins to work" day.  Kids liked it - adults tolerated it.  Decent food - but not a holy grail.

Awesome and free!  And a great oplace to find a bathroom, a map, a place to rest for a bit and/or get directions to tourist attractions or general info.  Even for locals like me!  I have taken my little one here since she was 3 and we come a few times each summer - usually between trips to the Liberty Bell or Constitution Center of the National Museum of American Jewish History.  We even took the (now ill-fated) duck boat ride a few years ago (before all the problems) and enjoyed it.  But event if we are not doing "philly stuff" we know we can always duck in here for the bathrooms just in case!

If you can take the noise level (excruciating - even when it's not busy) and the crowds - and you have a kid from age 4-8, then take 'em over to Giggleberry for the overpriced birthday experience of a little lifetime.  They have a gorgeous carousel (best part of the joint, if you ask me.), overpriced food & pizza, and Giggleberry Mountain - a place where your kid can run off some energy.  Lot's of video games and "token" gobbling machines, too.  We plan to have our daughter's 4th birthday party here.  I'll let you know how it goes.  I had to BEG the management to let us have milk & juice instead of soda (can you imagine feeding soda to a group of 3-5 year olds?)  No outside food is allowed, so you are stuck with their overpriced, non-nutritive package.  I hope the "free" cake is edible.  God help us!

Well, it's one year after our wedding already - can you believe it? We had a special anniversary dinner at JAI last night for a party of 7.  The recreated our wedding menu and it was out of this world.  Tender filet mignon, rich smoked cheddar mac 'n cheese, tender, bright green beans and crunchy parmesan chicken in a light buerre blanc sauce.  To top it off we special ordered 12 chocolate dipped strawberries - that disappeared in a flash.   The pastry chef also sent out (gratis) 6 chocolate espresso truffles - hand made and yum-city!  Teg the sommelier and GM is a doll and there were 2 weddings that night (it was a perfect 80 degree night).  One 36 party small wedding in the conference center and a huge (for JAI) 115 person wedding in the Wheelwright room.  It was fun to re-live our wedding day again (except that ours on 6/7/08 was in 96 degree heat!).  The service was great and we just can't recommend the JAI highyl enough.  For a wedding, a special dinner - or just to come and enjoy the food or lodging.  Try the JAI - you won't be disappointed.

3 stars is being pretty generous - but this location is better than the one in University City (but not by much.)  Yuck.  I really loathe chain restaurants and Chili's is no exception.  The one nice this about this Chili's is it's proximity to the Convention Center and the universally cheap and greasy burgers and other fried foods are the same at any Chili's nation wide.  My friend loves the Southwest eggroll app.  It's not so clean in here - and the place is run by illetrates and teenagers.  I guess it beats TGI Friday's - but again, not by much.

I went here for a drug test for a new job.  Arrived right at 8 AM but they did not open the doors until close to 8:15.  There was one guy ahead of me and they I got in and out right afetr that.  Friendly staff, clean waiting and treatment rooms.  No issues.

Surprisingly good food here.  Especially for a local bar. We had salads with grilled chicken, pecans, dried cranberries and goat cheese crumbles.  All for $6.95.  It does reek of beer though.  And the service was excellent.  A cool lady bartender with "Trust Me" and 2 crossed handguns tattooed across her chest.  She was cool!  Considering that I now work right across the street, I will likely be a lunch time regular.

Not a good choice for food but a GREAT choice for your morning coffee/latte/Muddy Waters (Coffee with Espresso shot added).  Super friendly staff and clean comfy digs with FREE wifi!  Breakfast sandwiches are $5 and up.  Ouch. a Medium Latte and egg-cheese-bacon on a bagel was $9.  Can't afford to come here daily but maybe once every 10 days or so?  Super friendly barrista and cashier in the AM. Line can move SLOWly..

Famous Dave's has our family hooked on their version of inexpensive, decent BBQ.  It is great for our 6 year old (she can get BBQ chicken or mac 'n cheese and DH 7 I can get an elegant meal presented on a trash can lid.  Tyrone & Alicia are the BEST servers!  Give them a BIG raise!  The management treats us so well here - and Wilbur (the pig mascot) entertains out little one.  Try to come here at 3 or 4 PM when the lunch rush is over and dinner has not yet begun. And you can get the lunch-size (and price!) specials ANY TIME which is great.  3 ribs for $7.99 includes a side, a corn cobette and a mamoth sweet cornbread muffin.  Carbo-loaded BLISS.

Makes me happy, happy!  I will edit my review once I try the meat ravioli I just bought over the weekend.  I am so anxious to try it and to find a great new source for pasta and ravioli and sauces in the Italian Market area.

Brand-spankin' new Bruegger's Bagels (of the chain popular in Boston and other cities) has come to Center City.  The offer a vast selection of bagels - baked fresh on premises - including abulous Rosemary & Olive Oil, Sesame, and whole wheat renditions.  Lots of wraps, ciabatta and "Softwich" - sqaure soft bagel-like bread sandwiches.  The have 2 soups per day and offer salads.  Everything is under $8.00 and a few sandwiches are about 5-6.  I will be back.  I hope they can keep it first-day fresh and clean.

For chain it's a solid 3.5 stars (I'll be generous and give 'em 4).  The Chicken Marsala and pasta are good.  Ask for light on the sauces if you are watching your calories - they are loaded with fat.  Service was surprisingly good and effcient.    I would NOT wait in a line though - so try to avois Friday & Saturday nights.  It is easier to eat here when it is less crowded & less noisy.  Again - for a chain it's way better than the dreaded Olive Garden - and I loathe Macaroni grill (friends and family love it but we had  awful food at one) with their bitter, cheap olive oil.  If you must do fauxtalian - this is a better bet. It's ain't Le Castagne, and it sure ain't Lusardi's but it's tasty and easy/family fun.
We've stopped in here a few times to grab sodas (and gas - but we usually go to a different place for cheaper gas).  It sure ain't Wawa, but it's nice to have it around when you need it.

Wegman's certainly has established its formula - with grocery, cafe, pub and many pre-prepared meal options.  I stopped in for lunch on a snowy day and it was still fairly busy.  Sushi was good but not great (Grocery Store Sushi but more varieties than most) and steam-table Chinese/Asian-American was OK and fresh.  Inexpensive and lots of choices for lunch.
Wow - no reviews for Oggi?  They are pretty well known salon. Haircuts are pricey.  They also offer single process color and highlights.
This location has closed - but they have re-opened a brand spankin' new one in Love Park (17 & Cherry ish).  Can't wait to try it - as I miss my Vanilla Italian Sodas.

We had such a great experience at the Center City Staples today - now granted it was about 10:45 AM on a Thursday and the places was dead empty - so that alone was a novelty.  My little one and I peacefully shopped for scotch tape, markers, posterboard and other art supplies.  the cashier we had (the only one on today - wish I knew her name) was funny and friendly and awesome.  What a surprise and a treat!  Upgrade.  (During an off time.)

We had the "set meal" here (They are all prix fix menus) prepared by the AI students.  It was very nice.  I had a Kentucky Hot Brown - and I am a big fan of those when done well.  This one was.  It is a nice experience to eat in a culinary school where the students are being graded on their product.  You are ensured there will be no messing around.  I would recommend reading the menu on the website and if you happen to like what they are serving - then by all means GO!

We had a lovely late lunch at the counter of Front Street Fountain. Andy and the other servers were attentive and patient with our 8 year old who gobbled up a pulled pork sandwich and then ate a Basset's cone with Orange Ice Cream and Rainbow Sprinkles/Jimmies.   Instead of lunch I had a deep fried Oreo sundae.  Oy-caloric-vey.  Ice cream and 2 HOT deep-fried batter dipped oreos, home-made vanilla-scented whipped cream (rich and wonderful) and hot fudge,  El kiddo ate the cherry.  DH enjoyed a Taco burger.  Can't wait to come back but next time a proper lunch and no ice cream for me. A wonderful place for families and kids.

We celebrated our 3rd wedding anniversary at JAI last night - and the weather and scenery were PERFECT.  We come back to the JAI (where we were married on 06/07/08) every year on our anniversary for dinner.  the past 2 years we brought our DD and both sets of parents.  This year it was just us and our DD who is now 6. She had a delicious lobster mac 'n cheese with smoked Gouda. She also ate one of my 4 lamb rib chops which were divine. She also had 3 bites of my husbands salmon which was perfectly cooked.  (All that stuff was 5 star).  Here's the bad part - HIGH salt content for sides and sauces.  My sauteed mushrooms were so salty I had to say something and send them back.  Inedible.  They promptly cooked another (only slightly less salty) batch which I took home - and may toss.  DH's salmon was on a bed of soba noodles drowning in a sweet/salty sauce that, too, was over-salted.  What a shame.  Meanwhile the apps wre AWESOME - some of the best sweet potato fries we've ever tried (and we try them at lots of places) .  Served with a warm marshmallow "fluff-like" dip.  HEAVENLY.  The smoked duck tostada was great, too.  (If a bit on the smokey side.  Yes, it is very smokey indeed.)  Dessert coffees at $8.50 are a delcious indulgence - topped with a cloud of REAL whipped cream.  Chocolate covered strawberries (call ahead to speacil order these) are LARGE, plump, red, sweet and juicy coated in luscious chocolate.  We love it here - and got to watch the end of a Saturday wedding and the rehearsal for a Sunday wedding.  Lots of weddings, showers and events are held here - and we know why - it's a GREAT venue for events.  (And now they can accomodate a larger wedding in the expanded ballroom.)  We love ya, Tegue & Neil!  Best regards to Wendy, too.  See you in June 2012.

My 4 year old dd & I love to browse around the Shanghai Bazaar and gawk at all the kitch-y souvenirs, silk clothing, parasols and other China-town goodies.  She loves the red & gold chinese writing and the twinkly lights.  They also have a great book and musical instrument section on the 2nd floor.  A fun place to take your kids.

Downgrade.  Went to Lamberti's for abusiness lunch. Service was too slow and food was just MEH.  I had the flounder lunch special which was swimming in an oily sauce.  The asaparagus pieces were a drab olive green and obviously over cooked.  Not great, guys.  Still - delicious bread that comes with the meal.

They still serve the most awful, bitter tasting olive oil to dip the bread in.  Don't do it!!!! Our server was sub par - and dod not get us items like napkins/cultery, sweetener (for my $3.75 teeny-tiny cappucino) until asked.  Food was OK - but so SALTY - seriously, people - tone it down (the meatball "small plate" and pasta sauce are over salted.)!  Not a fan - and not rushing back here.

Came here in the dead of winter and tried the "Blueberry Pancakes" ice-cream (a special, seasonal offering).  very good - and they claim to make the ice cream onsite.  The decor is cute but very dusty - place could use a good cleaning - especially the display case in the front with the ice cream cakes.  Interesting nostalgia swag on the walls - but again - DUSTY.  Please clean!
Could use a good cleaning, but the owner (a one-man show as far as i can tell) is very patient and kind with the kids. A good assortment of "retro" candies, too.  Fun - but not a HG.

Pretty pricey for what they are - but the cap-sleeve Tee here fits me well and is very cute.  Certain articles they make should NOT be worn by anyone with any extra pounds - so if you are not a super model, steer clear of the skirts and ultra short shorts.  You can get AA stuff at lots of non AA locations.  Wait a second?  AA?  My name is Karen F. and I'm a tee-shirt-a-holic! ("Hi, Karen!")

I agree with Spa Girl.  WHile not a plus size woman - I do gfo to City Sports for sneakers and have found 2 great pairs over the past 3 years there.  Sales people were sooooo helpful and when they have a sale the prices are OK.  (Not cheap - but you get what you pay fir.)  I also like the Life is Good brand for Tees and tops. I was also able to snag some comfy socks that "wick away moisture" for a reasonable price.  Yay City Sports.

Ashley Power of Power Catering events is a true professional.  She recently catered a "heavy hors d'ouvres" reception for about 50 people at my cousin's home.  The food was delicious and elegantly presented.  The lamb chops with pesto and duck 'n onion crepe were highlights.  Standards like shrimp shumai and asparagus tempura disappeared along with delectable mini-mugs of home-made creamy tomato soup served with grilled cheese triangles.  Her staff of server and bar tenders were on point in both serving and clearing. The blueberry-mint lemonade was refreshing and perfect for the event.  (The open bar was also great.)  Stationary displays of fruit were as beautiful to look at as they were tasty to eat.  For dessert?  Butlered mini desserts like freshly torched creme brulee and petit lemon tartes.  I am considering hiring her for my own events and would urge yelpers to do the same!  She does Philly area, suburbs and South Jersey.  Love Power Catering!

We had a 5 star experience from Bill (our attentive server) and the entire staff at Capital Grille.  I was treated to a delicious birthday lunch here - and everything from the greeting by name when I arrived, to the f9ond farewell was top-notch.  The food was the star of the show - and our table was decorated with rose petals and confetti in honor of my birthday.  They also snapped a picture of me and my dining companions at dessert.  My meal consisted of truly perfect french onion soup (A cup was perfect for me - they also offer a crock), and the lobster salad.  I asked for extra tomatoes and they added a variety of heirloom cherry halves and beefsteak slices.  Delicious.  Topped with a shelled lobster claw.  Scrumptious.  Every bite was blissful. Truly.  Can't believe it's a chain - but I have dined now at a few CGs and all are excellent.  very expensive - Lunch for 3 was over $150,  so plan accordingly.  A special treat, indeed.

I had a decent experience at the Wayne outpost of Blue Mercury.  Picked up some Caudalie and Kiehl's goodies plus a sample of MorrocanOil mask.  All wrapped nicely.  Pricey?  Yes. Snooty?  Yes. Still shopping here?  For now, yes.

My husband and I had dinner here last night.  We walked in at about 4:55 PM so there was NO crowd yet at all.  Our server Morgan was friendly and EXCELLENZT.  The food was better than I expected.  I am not a chain restaurant person, so I expected the worst.  The food was actually pretty good. 3 stars.  I had the "special" summer salad which had strawberries, grapes, mandarin oranges and pecans in it.  It was like dessert!     My ribeye was overly salty - which was a shame as it was grilled PERFECTLY.  Next time (if there is a next time - I am in no hurry to rush back here) tell them "No prairie dust" - the salt seasoning they put all over the steak.  I also has a sweet potato (minus the cinnamon sugar topping they usually put on it) which was great - but it's pretty hard to mess up a plain, baked sweet potato.  Prices were high for a chain - but low for a steakhouse.  It ain't the Palm - but it's OK.  3 stars.  OK.  Not nearly as bad as it coulda been.
Needed a low-beam headlamp for my car and had no problems this time.  Came in, asked the "parts" guy, got the bulb, paid.  Got 10% off with my PepBoys card, got out.  No issues.  Much better.

This is a review for the BBW in the shops at Liverty Place (1st Fl.). The manager here is an older lady who has been here about 1.5 years and I love her!  So helpful and friendly.  I try to shop here often to keep up on what's new.  BBW has a 90% market saturation for women from 18-65 in the US - that means nearly EVRYONE has shopped at a BBW at some point.  The products are NOT top quality - but for the price they have some very good items.  I like to buy the anti-bacterial soaps here in bulk when they are on sale and I have a coupon.  Shop wisely and use coupons and sales together and you can score big at BBW.

Very fun for little kids especially.  My little one went here at age 3 and again at age 4 to try on fireman's gear and learn about the history of firefighting in the US and Philadelphia.  And it's free!

Just had a "Taste of Philly" catered lunch at our office - cheese steaks, chicken cheese steaks, caesar salad (with chicken breast chunks on the side to add in), fresh fruit platter, individually wrapped pretzels, TASTYCAKES and more.  Very well done - and a nice change from pizza, pizza,pizza. That said - at an April 2012 lunch we had the tomato pie (square pie covered in chunky sauce with circles of fresh mozz.) - sooooo good!

Can not...  ...write.  Too...  ...weak  Lapsing into... food... coma...  4.75 Stars. OMG - Have you ever had a meal that was such a calorie bomb that you literally felt all of the blood rush to your stomach to try and equalize what was happening in your system?  I seriously feel weak from my anniversary dinner at Union Trust. Dh & I had a very romantic, dimly-lit, 5-star service (Fabian, you ROCK!), unforgettable meal here tonight.  I may need days to recover.  We started with cocktails/wine.  I had the Flyin' Hawaiian and with what little I normally drink (Being the Empress of the Arnold Palmer and all), after a few sips I was nicely buzzed and after one I was flyin'.  (2 might make me crash land.)  Once the buzz was on, out came our delectable apps.  A very good lobster bisque for DH and an icy-chilled crab cocktail perfection for me (better than Parc!).  We each had massive slabs of cow-on-a-plate. He had the ancho-rubbed strip, garnished with salty (a bit too salty for me) finely-julienned frites.  I had a perfectly cooked cowboy ribeye (so huge I took over half of it home - and, I should mention DH took about 40% of his home.)  My major complaint (which nearly cost them a star) was the crust of the ribeye was WAY salty.  Not Arizona-desert salty, not inedibly salty - but noticably biting with salt.  Dommage!  Meanwhile the spectacular (and for $9 - $11 a pop they outta be) sides saved the meal.  Mac 'n cheese was enough for 4 people (again, half came home - which our kid will appreciate).  The crispy top gave way to bubbling, hot, melty-cheesey-creamy-yet-tender (not at all flabby) elbows.  (I had been expecting shells based on other yelp reviews - but got elbows.)  I love mac 'n cheese and the mac here is worthy!!!!  So good.  A platter of donut-like sweet, tender Onion rings - battered to perfection and (the only thing?) NOT salty.  Wonderful.  I lterally ate 1/2 of one ring and was satisfied.  DH also got a $3.00 dish of caramelized onions to go with his steak.  Not needed - but so tasty - with a light balsamic/demi sweetness to them.  The floor manager, our server (Fabian) and "bus" Valetin, were all on point with the service.  truly excellent.  Dessert (Come on now!  We have come this far - why not just succumb to the madness) was an I.V. of lipitor.  No, seriously - dessert DH had the s'mores (which did, in fact, look like a marshmallow-meringue hedgehog) atop a scoop of house-made peanut butter cup gelato.  The even wrote "Happy Anniversary" on the plate.  And put a little candle on it. Cute.  I had a latte (delicous Saxby coffee - not Peregrine, but fairly good stuff) with a few spoonfuls of Frangelico in it.  Basically everything - with the disappointing exception of the overly salted crust of the Cowboy rideye - was top-notch.  We hope to return again in about a year. It'll take that long to recover my arterial walls.  Alcohol, caffeine, salt, fat and sugar. A dietary disaster - but oh, so much fun.  back...  ...to the sofa.  I feel a pleasant numbness coming on in my left arm.

This place is getting a little "old" in more ways than one. When I first landed in Philly - about 3 year ago, I was looking to find a replacement for my old NYC sushi spot.  Fuji Mountain, at that time, was close to my office and offered a profusion of rools.  The Sunshine and Florida rolls are really, very tasty.  Now the prices are up and quality is just OK.  I did order a lovely Toro-lover's platter which was a special and it was a good value and had lots of toro.  2 pieces of Chu, 2 pieces of  "O" and a negi-toro roll.  I still dream about that one!  But lately when I go for lunch and sit (solo) at the bar, I am not treated really well.  Seems odd to me.  Anyhow, I have also taken to Shiroi Hana as of late. Even more recently, I have discovered Vics - right nearby. I guess Fuji Mountain is just not for me anymore.  There are better places to go now.

I have been seeing Melissa M. (and nicole, Danielle and Ali) at the Shear Bliss in Brookhaven - but now they've really outdone themselves.  They've opened a brand-new second location in Center City - right near my kids old school.  I love their colors, cuts and styles.  And the new digs look FABulous.  Come check them out.

Surprisingly OK.  Very nice front desk person (one guy - works=ed at least a double shift) and housekeepers.  Breakfast is included and is semi-decent including a 1 minute pancake (not waffle) machine.  Rooms are small but clean and comfortable. Strange lighting - bathroom area is super bright. No complaints.

Yes, is may be a bit over-hyped and it is certainly pricey and pretentious - but you get what you pay for.  The fish is swimmingly fresh and the dishes are NOT traditional.  The sizzling bowls (one with Yellowtail another with Kobe Beef) and desserts are outstanding.  It budget and appetite permits, say "omikase" to the chef and you will be well taken care of.  This is a special occaision (or expense account) place.  FOr every day sushi eating, I go to Shiroi Hana.  Don't miss the succelent toro tartar.  What a treat!  The upstairs bar is a nice place for dessert and drinks afterward.
Avgolemono soup and dolmades for the win!  Can't wait to come back and have a REAL gyro - or even a shrimp gyro.  Fresh veggies.  SO happy to have found this place.

The food was surprisingly really GOOD for a chain and the decor was nice enough.  Service was good as well - but the noise level?  Deafening and the place was loaded with kids - mine included.  The veggie salad is great - and it's enormous - 2 of us shared it easily with leftovers.  And for $7 a slice - the ginormous piece of Red Velvet Cheesecake (sooooo good) was enough for 3.  This was (shockingly) my first EVER visit here - and I really liked it.  Not a healthy place, as Michelle C. says - but tasty grub for sure and not too pricey.  (Save for the cheesecake.)

I am only rating the facilities for conferences/banquets.  I stayed in a different (cheaper) hotel overnight while attending a conference here.  The facilities themselves are 4 star and the hotel provides a variety of room sizes and configurations for meetings.  However, the plated meals were absolutely bland and awful.  Chicken was dry and bathed in a (jarred) marinara sauce and an overly sweet balsamic reduction.  Brown and wild rice was overly salted - to the point of inedibility.  The best thing?  Steamed asparagus.  Cheesecake for dessert was frozen for sure.  Gives a whole new meaning to the "rubber chicken" dinner.  In the mean time, the meetings themselves were fine - and water/cold drinks were provided for during breaks.  No major issues, but based on the food I sure as heck would NOT have my wedding here. Or any other event where guests want GOOD tasting food.

Solid, nostalgic, "traditional" Chinese American food - with BIG portions and great values for eat-in at lunch (weekdays lunches are 5.95 - 6.95).  Lunch for 3 of us WITH TIP was $24.  Wow.  Friendly service and clean comfortable digs.  The Moo Shu Chicken for lunch comes with 2 fresh pancakes. My 6 year old enjoyed her steamed "light & healthy" chicken and broccoli.  It's not Asian Fusion, It's not "modern" Chinese, it's old-school combo platters with white or fried rice (which was freshly made and good, by the way - loaded with pork and egg!).  NICE!
Ok - they re-did my car and it looks GREAT now. I shall return.  Very, very good customer service.
Note - Credit Card tips are NO LONGER ACCEPTED so bring cash to tip your stylist, please!  Still a great salon and I still LOVE MElissa, Nicole, Aly and the gals!

I had a manicure here many months ago.  It was not particularly memorable nor was it unpleasant.  It was just middle of the road.  There are better - and worse - places nearby.  It was, indeed, quick. And they are accessible for walkins.

The Charcoal Pit is a local landmark and institution.  A friend of mine worked here as a teenager serving up burgers and soft drinks. (Lots of shakes.)  It's fun for a family to come here, too.  Not healthy - but nostalgic and fun.
Fabulous and free (and air conditioned with decent bathrooms). Gift Shop.  Mission Control for tourists doing the Historic Philly thing!

Nicely laid-out, large, chain-style pet store with supplies for dogs, cats and small animals. They had the Eukeneuba my pup eats - but the price was just average - not low and not high. Good in a pinch.  They also have a grooming area.  Seems better than "big chains" like pet smart and petco. More and more I order dog food on line. (Especially if shipping is free).  The best place for inexpensive bagged dog food?  Newtown Square's Seed & Feed - it's small and dirty but so cheap!!!!
A great location for conferences and conventions.  It is CONNECTED to the Convention Center and right next to Reading Termincal Market.  Rooms and Restaurants are average Marriott Corporate fodder.

While my go-to is Victory cleaners in Aston (awesome!) I  have found Apex to be on my way some times and they are WAY better than the cleaners near the Elwyn Train station and also better than the one near the Giant in Aston, so these are my "second place" winners for Dry Cleaning in Media/Aston.  The lady (owner?) is friendly enough and has my clothes ready when I need them.  Wish they were open on Sundays.

Why oh Why do i keep coming here?  The service is painfully slow - and there were only 2 people in the line (one lady ahead of me and then me).  It took about 7 minutes to get a toasted bagel with butter.  And I asked her to cut it in half (sometimes they do, sometimes they don't) and when I got to my office - not cut in half.  And Britney (sp?) the morning cashier is soooooo not into working.  You can tell she'd rather be elsewhere.  Oh - and a bagel with cc and (g-d forbid) tomato is over $3.00.  YOUCH!  Not gonna come back for a while.  It's a shame because 2 of their bagel flavors (Rosemary Olive Oil and Cinnamon Sugar) I find very good.  A whole lot better then the rat-infested Au Bon Pain down the block.  Please step up your service and lower your prices (even by 10 cents would help).

Oh wow.  Yes, it really is all that IF you order the right things. (I am torn between 4 and 5 stars, but I will be generous due to the fabulous entree and app I am about to describe.)  First of all the Green Room is a great special occaision place.  The ornate, grand dining room, complete with a gilded music gallery (balcony up above) with a pianist on weekend nights.  The food and service are AAA 4Star for good reason.  Not only are you paying for the decor and ambiance, the food and ingredients are terrific as well.  The Hudson Valley Foie Gras app was out of this world, and the $39 lamb chop entree - with 2 double cut, frenched rib chops (total of 4 ribs) kicked the baaaaaa out of the chops I've had at Joseph Ambler Inn, and Tinto (2 of the places I have recently had good lamb chops).  The desserts are $8-10 and the signature dessert - a White Chocolate Amaretto & Fresh Raspberry Napolean is a work of art and worth the price and calories.  Skip the deconstructed Pear tarte Tatin - but if you like get the fresh house made ice cream (the small orb of vanilla ice cream that accompanied the tarte surpassed it with each yummy, creamy, chilled bite).  Oh my widening butt!!!!!  Anyhow - back to reality and my diet.  But don't miss a chance to have DINNER at the Green Room.  Especially if someone else foots the large bill.  Oh - valet parking is $14.00 unless you are a hotel guest. And also - someone re-train the hostess.  She is a bit green (2.5 years in) and it shows.

An Italian Market staple - and a great resource - if pricey - to the city. I also like Claudio's - just a block or 2 away - for Ricotta and fresh made mozzarella.  Dicbruno's has a great and vast selection of meats and cheese and they do catering, too.  Also a nice Olive bar (also try Talutto's Olive bar - smaller but nice and fresh.)  They get very crowded around the holidays and on weekends - so try to come on a random Tuesday to avaoid the crowds.

We have since returned many times - including their wonderful"family friendly" new year's eve celebrations from 5 - 7 PM - complete with Karaoke for the kids and anice cream toppings bar.  They also have trivia nights on Friday's.  The now 9 y.o. loves the pulled pork sandwich and we like the burgers and grilled cheese.    Wonderful home-made whipped cream is a treat, indeed.  Great fun for families with kids from infants through about age 12.

Whoa - expensivoso!  But very friendly nice Korean lady at the counter and GORGEOUS looking stock - a copious amount of produce and groceries stocked floor to ceiling.  Reminds me very much of some of the NYC mini-markets I used to frequent.  A nice addition to the nabe.  We got a nice container of chunked mango for $4.00 and they threw in a free banana.

This is a review of the Le Nails on the STREET LEVEL of the Gallery Mall near the 10th Street entrance.  I had a mani pedi ($35 for both, $12 mani, $25 pedi) yesterday and "Lisa" at table 1 (they have 9 mani stations and 5 pedi thrones) did a nice job.  While I am still leery of pedicures and santitation, it "seemed" OK here.  They use OPI polish and decent base & top coats.  The pedi inculded a short exfoliation with scrub and a decent massage.  I would not RUN back here, but if I need a manicure and am nearby I will return.

Got 2 big hoagie trays (with numerous little bags of Herr's chips) hamt, turkey, roastbeef. Very good - pickles and peppers on the side.  Delicious and budget conscious and a change from Pizza for a crowd.

A beautiful and renovated Wawa with gas, food and everything you might need. Getting out of the parking lot during the morning rush hour is not easy so be careful and take your time.  Love me a Wawa iced coffee in summer. My teen likes the new-ish "create your own" salad bowls.

Still my go-to for hard Italian grating cheese, fresh ricotta and certain cured meats (I also like DiBruno's, Downtown Cheese and Claudio's).  I buy certain things certain places and Salumeria is TTOPS for selection and value of Grana Padano, Parmegiano Reggiano and many others.  Great customer service - and a tub of Marcona Almonds to snack on.  I am ALL set!

Beats the heck ouuta Mazella's.  The HUGE portions of perfectly al dente pasta (try the pappardelle bolognese) and chicken parm run about $12 - $14 for lunch.  We took over half of it back to the office.  Delicious - and great service from Barbara the hostess.  She is a doll!  We'll be back for sure.

Just OK - we like the Pep Boys in Broomall or Wilmington, DE better. We come here on occasion for parts.  Lackluster service - and one time I needed help there was literally nobody at the front registers.  Someone eventually came up from "the back"n I called out for them.  Odd.

Ok, my best friend calls this place Icky Vicky's - because if you are a big gal - this is NOT the place for you.  Victoria's secret is a place to buy "every day" underwear.  It is mall-quality, mass produced bras, panties, sleepwear, loungewear and now - really poor quality fragrances and cosmetics that bilk thousands of teens and young 20-somethings out of millions each year - and their mama's too!  If it sounds as though I am being harsh - well...  ...I Kinda am.  anyhow, I get my typical five for $25 plain cotton string bikinis there and whenever I get a "free panty" coupon in the mail I run right over.  I am definitely not a a Power Shopper at VS - I much prefer high end lovelies like La Perla or Agent Provacateur for the specialty goods.  But for an everyday comfy cotton undie?  VS is my go-to spot.  Just don't ask for help from the teen-aged, undereducated, underpaid staff (although they'll probably offer to help you).  And don't even THINK about coming here over a busy lunch hour when the lines are crazy long.

I  was so excited to try poke on, as I love poke and chirasi bowls, but there were a few things that are in need of improvement, the main one being that the salmon did not taste fresh to me.  Now, it is hard to tell under all the toppings and sauces, but I could still tell.  The staff was friendly, and all the toppings looked great, save for the wilted cucumber slivers, which I thought were pickled cucumbers - they looked that wilted.  Greens are fresh, but no romaine available.  Only spring mix.    Next time I will get a bowl sans fish.
Good value - 2 kiddie cones (with sprinkles/jimmies) for about $6.00.  Black Cherry was excellent with big pieces of cherries in it. Brownie Batter was dark, rich and super chocolaty.  Yum!

Extremely slow service but...  BUT...  the clerk (female) was extremely knowledgeable and helpful when I finally got up there (They have 4 or 5 registers but only one was open).  Finally a second lady appeared. And then vanished.  And later appeared again to start working a 2nd till.  I needed to ship a package to Canada and this is not my "usual" USPS office, so I am glad it was here. It was a long wait but in the end everything was fine.  They sell some basic packaging supplies, greeting cards and postage related products here, also.  Do not expect to get "in and out".  You will wait.

These are like little apartments with a small kitchen and bath. Andrea at the front desk is terrific. I would stay here again but would request an upper floor as everyone walking by could see inside the room, so I had to keep the shades drawn all the time.  During the summer there is an outdoor pool.  Breakfast (meh) is served daily and Monday - Wednesday they serve light supper/snack items.

5 stars for Melissa, 4 stars overall for Shear Bliss - Nicole, Margot (only in a few days per week), Ali and the gang are terrific.  I had a color, highlights and a cute cut from Melissa.  Don't be turned off by the strip-mall location - Melissa is well worth seeing. And she is the only one who will cut my 9 year old's hair.

No issues with this Chipotle location near the Walmart and PetSmart in Springfield. Parking lot on this side is fine - on the Walmart side it gets crazy.  Line moved quickly - but we came at an off hour (5 PM on a Sunday).  Standard Chipotle grub.

I have definitely had better - this place is a mix of Halal, Fried CHicken, Pizza and Indian dishes and seems to get none of them quite right.  Very cheap - $6 for lamb platter over rice - but lamb was dry and stringy.  I may try again - but not rushing back,

Walked in for a lunchtime slice (to go, definitely to go - people!) today.  Got a mushroom slice for $2.00 even and walked in and out.  Ate the cheese-coated slice (not greasy though - bonus) with a very fresh crust, - at my desk.  The crust was definitely the best part - I was able to eat all of the crust and not throw it away as I often do.  It was medium thick (not too thick) doughy but COOKED and not at all burnt.  Nice crust, Brandywine!  Now I need a nippy-nap.  I feel carbed out!  Sorry, Brandywine - but I'm sticking with John's Place (no slices there, though - only Red-Sauce veggie pies for me.)  I would definitely consider ordering a take-out pie from Brandywine in the future.  Oh - and the service I got was fine. A nice hispanic?? lady was behind the counter and 2 guys were cooking in the back.  And in case you care, they sell Red Bull.

OMG!  I am beyond thrilled and delighted to find Bill's - a real 100% BUTCHER shop with custom cuts available and exotic fare like Muskrat (seasonal) and rabbit (pre-order). I wonder what Muskrat tastes like?  The beef is top quality. Chicken is average price - no better no worse that the supermarket.  But for custom orders?  This is a dying industry and I am so lucky to found these folks - 2 blocks from my office.  SCORE!  I will be placing an Easter Lamb order very soon!

OMG - this place s great for $3.99 Bubble tea and a variety of espresso drinks (my latte was terrific).  NO DECAF available.  Cute theme with movies and TV shows.  Froyo, Korean-style shave ice, RAMEN (did not try) and Liquid Nitrogen ice cream.  The lady (and her artsy husband) who run this place are terrific.  Service can be a bit slow as every order is made by hand. We loved it here.  Oh - and we bought 6 macaron to go.  FAB!

Chocolate peanut butter bar was great - a friends kid was selling Gertrude Hawk for a fundraiser (I did not know they did that?). Sometimes stop into the Springfield Mall store for a treat for my own kid.

I am a big Fellini's fan - and have been to multiple locations (none of which are owned by the same people).  The Berwyn Fellini's can get very crowded, but luckily the night we went it wasn't.  My usual go-to is the Penne Sophia Loren (or the classic Linguine Scampi or Vongole) but on a sweltering August night, we opted to share the (enormous) Mediterranean salad.  A simple bed of crispy-fresh romaine topped with 4 shrimp, a big blob of lump crab meat (so good) and seared tuna slices, plus hunks of tomato and (we omitted) red onion.  The lemon vinaigrette served along side was delectable.  Service from Victoria (she is a hoot!) and 2 expediters was terrific as well.  WINNER!  We'll be back.

You can sample a gazillion kinds of pickled items - including pickled eggs and pickled tomatoes - however noe of them are the "Real" jewish half sours that I love.  Theirs are OK - but not that great.    That said - their non-pickled items (they sell all kinds of slaws, salads, puddings and mixes) are expansive.  They also make terrific sour cream & onion flavored popcorn (of all things!) all served up by kind young ladies.  If you need potato salad they offer at least 3 different kinds.

This is a hidden (head North up Broad) FREE treasure that all should know about.  It has weird Science stuff - some of it creepy (Things embalmed in jars) and much of it old and historic in nature.  The Wagner is just $20 a year to join (they are free - but the donation really helps them stay around.).  They educate TONS of school kids every year - many from bad nabes in N. Philly.  They also had my daughter's preschool class up for a feild trip and they loved it.  The PHS (Pennsylvania Horticulture Society - aka the folks who produce the Flower Show) also offers several EXCELLENT lectures in conjunction with the Wagner each year.  If you are a PHS member - the lectures are FREE.  (And awesome!)

Kailon catered a sushi bar fopr my husband's corporate party held at the DuPont country club.  He is such a great guy and makes terrific sushi including rainbow rolls, unagi maki, shrimp tempura & california rolls.    Good party sushi - can't wait to dine in the restaurant and get some nigiri!  Thanks, Kailon - we love Okura!

OK - Now they get the fifth star.  If you read Pat D.'s review - you'll hear all about the yummy treats she orded when we had lunch here today.  I had the greek salad - and they were kind enough to "hold" the feta cheese for me.  The greens were crisp and 3 types of olives were used (2 green and 1 black variety) along with batons of red pepper and home-made dolmades.  The scrumptios  - and simple - lemon and olive oil vinaigrette made it SING.  Presented on a white rippled plate - very clever.  The plate allowed the dressing to pool away from the crisp greens and thus I could dress the salad as I wished.  YUM-MY!  The I had the Asian Dumpling soup.  The single dumpling had a shrimp-based filling and was scrumptious, as were the veggies in the soup.  The broth was a bit salty for my liking - but I am a no-salt added kinda gal.  Next was the star of the show - and what I was WAITING for - Chicken & Waffles.  It was accompanied by tender-crisp southern greens (with a healthy shot of garlic) and thin-ly julienne deep-fried sweet potato strings.  Damn, what a great waffle!  The pulled chick on top was tender and delicious - but my one complaint was the copious amount of bland sauce.  It nade it a bit too "a la king" -ish for me.  Dessert for me was a simple - yet perfect fruit salad of watermelon (sweet and seedless) bites, blackberries,and a single slice of orange.  Service was good - I felt so bad for the guy in crutches who had broken his femur.  What a trooper.    I will be back - hopefully SOON. (And maybe even with Pat D!)

Sorry - but with the passage of time the SLOW service (I cut them a break because they were brand new and i thought they'd get their act together) is now unbearable.  It took me 12 minutes to wait in line (only 2 people ahead of me), order, get the sandwich made, get the salad made, pay and leave.  Also without any more promotional coupons a bagel & cream cheese is $249 plus tax and over $3.00 if I dare to put a slice of tomato on it.  I am getting discouraged - because I do love the rosemary olive oil bagels.  But not at $3 a pop.
Had fingerprints taken for a security clearance here (gateway Shopping Center Location) . No issues.

I love Seasons 52.  Yes - they are a little pricey , but the food and ambiance are terriic. Big comfy booths, a gorgeous bar area with orange and strawberry infused vodkas displayed in large glass urns.  Terrific iced tea and REAL lemonade. Tast flatbreads, sandwiches (at lunch) and fish dishes.  Never disappointed here. Great on a date or for lunch with the girls.
Visited the Art of Jim Henson exhibit.  Great for kids and grown-ups.  Not to be missed.

I am not a Fry-eater - but when my company so generously comissioned the Philly Fry Truck for a 2 hour corporate event - I could not resist - I asked for a 1/2 order and it was plenty.  We were given 2 choices (both with "regular" fries) - one was a "loaded" baked potato with cheese whiz sauce, sour cream, chives and bacon (or not - if you wish).  The other - which I tried was "Philly Steak" - with melted american (so good, so bad), steak meat and bacon.  Decadent.  So bad for you. So tasty.  Perhaps my employer wants us all dead?   Serve with a side of Lipitor.

We had an amazing meal and enjoyable evening at Teca along with stellar service from Jen and "Baba" the manager.  Initially we were told there would be a 20 minute wait for a table so we sidled up to the long bar and started to read the drink menu.  All of a sudden our table was ready!  (So great - because we were hungry by then - and the wait was only about 8 minutes!)  In future I would recommend reservations for Friday or Saturday nights here - the summer Gay Street scene is pretty hoppin'.  The tables are pretty close together (we sat outside on a lovely night) so we got to know a couple from Atlanta next to us.  Everything they ordered and everything we ordered looked amazing. We enjoyed our drinks - I had an $8 Kir Royale and DH had a Belgium Raspberry lambic that smelled and tasted so sweet and fruity (you better like fruit!) that even I could have easily drank it.  Our proscuitto and melon app - at $13 - was 5 star perfection.  The large ball of creamy fresh Mozzarella (di Buffala!!!) was divine.  It was served with 2 slices of panini-pressed bread that was good for dipping into the lemon-noted olive oil on the plate.  DH & I both ordered pasta as our main dish - mine was a special of pappardelle (house made - and a little on the thick side but perfectly cut and cooked to a toothsome al dente) with shrimp (5 medium sized ones) and lumps of crab meat (sweet, shell-less and delectable).  DH had the penne a la vodka and I did not taste it but it looked great, too.  We shared a delicious creme brulee (the top was stll warm from being blow-torched) for $8.  Cappuccino (at $5 - ouch!) was a let down.  Extremely bitter tasting and I fear the beans were burnt.  I could only drink a few   They are sooooo close to 5 stars on food - but there are a few areas for improvement that are holding me out on the 5th star. (Fix your ladies room stall doors and the lights on the stars, please!)  Food snobs from NYC or Philly may shun the 'burbs - but Teca was a big winner for me last night.  We'll be back - hopefully soon - to see if they can keep it up.  Oh - and I wanna buy a bottle of that olive oil that is supposedly pressed at the owner's place in Italy. Good stuff!

This is the rating for the eye Doctors downstairs - not for the glasses/upstairs part of the store.  My 6 year old had a thorough exam with Kimberly Toscani and it went very smoothly.  No issues.  So far - no glasses are needed, but we'd certainly consider getting kids frames here - they are pretty reasonable, too.

It's OK - as Kmarts go.  I am glad its around though - for cheap kids clothing, pullups and paper products.  It's kind of an emergency only place for me.  Again, as Kmarts go this one is clean and relatively well staffed.  They also were very nice about accepting a product return we had one time.  We used to stop here more when the SuperFresh was open in the same strip mall, but alas, the Superfresh has closed.

My kid recently attended a classmates party here and it was run beautifully.  She enjoyed the ball pit, trampolines and especially the Zip Line.  The 2 hour party with about 20 5 & 6 year olds had 3 staffers running the show - and they ran it smoothly and well.  They also offer gymnastics classes and "drop-in" play sessions.  FUN!  (Similar to the Little Gym in Narberth - but not as nice decor.)

It's OK.  Just OK.  Now that Thai Chef & Noodle Fusion is open right near my office I may never need to come here again.  I gotta have my Tom Yum fix every now and again and un until now Erawan was just about IT in terms of Thai-near-my-office.  The service is always friendly - that I will say - very, very nice gals waiting tables and very smiley.  I usually get Masaman Curry - tofu or chicken - and of course some Tom Yum or Tom Kha Soup.

I have been here twice even though the first time I vowed to never return.  What a MEH experience both times.  (We had sushi both times - not hibachi.)  The place is never crowded - because it is not good.  The fish is not truned over rapidly enough and is not at the peak of freshness.  I will not come back here.  Uck!

I am not a big Panera fan, but my coworkers are. I usually get a "pick 2" combo for lunch and in winter, I will try a soup with salad.  This time (summer) I tried the watermelon salad and it was very nice.  I always get dressing in the side, in case I do not like it, and to control the amount.  My kid likes the Mac and cheese here.  It's a safe choice for lunch. Spent  $11 with no drink.  Seems high for glorified fast food.

I'm sorry but both times I went in here I was treated to badly by the snobby, ultra thin chicks who work here that I never bought a thing - and one time I went literally in and out.  It's a shame because it looks like they have cute stuff.  Horrifyingly snotty salesfolk.

Last night I went over to Vietnam Palace to see Tracey Nguyen who is putting together a large (about 30 people) party for my child's kindergarten class.  Since I was there anyway, I had some dinner - including a freshly squeezed glass of lemonade (perfect on a 77 degree and humid day) and a delicious place of extra-thin bun (rice vermicelli) and grilled beef.  Tracey is terrific and will be on hand next week when we have our big dinner.  I will let you know how it goes, but as of right now - and can't say enough good things about the service and food and Vietnam Palace.  It's a great place for couples, singles and families with young children.

I have passed by Joe's (often noting the long lunchtime lines) and NEVER gone in - until today.  And, boy am I glad I did.  I had a delicious slice of tomtato pie topped with spinach (no cheese).    It was very good and $2.75 for the slice.  My friend had a tomato, cheese & spinach slice which also looked good - but she got the EGGPLANT (which I had not noticed) and that looked Awesome!  Next time I'm gonna try the eggplant.  Nice decor for a pizza joint, too.  I will be back (but not often - as I am not a pizza-lover).

I stand by my previous review.  I came here for a "ladies luncheon" in the larger event space - again - beautiful at first glance but then you notice that rugs/carpets are old and chandeliers are loaded with dust.  The ladies room with 2 stalls was inadequate for our group of 88 people and stunk.  No ventilation in there.  Eew.  Service was fine but the 4 servers were way understaffed  (4 people for a seated group of 88 at 10 tables.)  Food was lukewarm - we had a choice of pasta primavera (again - I skipped it now!), a cheese omelette or salmon.  I opted for salmon which was edible but boring.  They use the cheapest possible foods to keep cost low.  Parking is kinda weird, too.  They have a very good looking European guy flagging in cars - later he served us coffee.  The place is very, very odd.  But it is inexpensive so my group keeps having functions here.

Sterling Leather (and now the other shops) has been around a loooooooong time.  A good friend of mine used to work there as a summer job in the late '80's.  Sterling offers mid to high end leather clothing and goods.  Lots of gift-y ideas too - and now they have more than one shop.  (They really have expanded.)

I buy about 85% of my cheese here (sometimes I go to Downtown Cheese a few doors down, but Salumeria almost always has the best price).  I get 100% of my grating cheeses here - Grana Padano, American Grana, Parm, Romano, and more.  Love it!

Surprisingly excellent non-pizza items.  I had an extremely fresh garden salad - chock full of tomatoes and cucumbers, served with balsamic vinaigrette.  DD enjoyed 3 garlic knots (lighter and "fluffier" than what we are used to) - so fresh and yummy and a small plate of ziti.  Friendly service from "the guys" at the counter. Reminded us of our favorite spots back in Brooklyn - but Bravo's is much larger and cleaner.  We'll be back!

Fabulous service by Mylissa for our impromptu party of 18 on a sunny Friday Lunch. We ate outdoors and enjoyed a mountain of wings (with various sauces - try the Kickin' Korean, Mexican Garlic or BBQ), excellent cheese steak nachos (so bad for you, but tasty stuff), burgers and salads.  My $12.99 "special" salad with 7 tiny shrimp was just OK, but the $5 Strawberry Mojito made up for it.  It's really 3 star food but we had such a good experience I am giving 4 stars.
Just not my bag, baby. Formula cooking by disinterested college kids - wearing "flare".  So not my thing.

This place is odd. For every positive there is at one corresponding negative.  At first glance, I thought, "Oh, this place is nice"  but as I explored the place (like a big 3 story old house with the owners living on the top floor, party rooms on the other 2 lower floors), it looked dated and in need of a good clean-out.  This is NOT a restaurant. Inexpensive foods were used - tasted fine - but nothing to write home about.  I have pasta primavera - penne in "red" sauce with a few green beans and carrot slivers on top.  Salad had precisely ONE grape tomato and ONE slice of cucumber.  (Could you spare it?)  Tiny, tiny glass of diet coke.  Not bad -  and nice for a gathering if you need it due to location - but I would NEVER have a wedding here.  Possibly a luncheon or "shower" but not something truly important.  Service, too - odd.  One waiter was smiling and friendly and attentive - the other cold and grumpy.  You win some, you lose some. This place is decidedly middle-of-the-road.

It's OK - the one in Doylestown (not the same owners - at least i don't think so...) is better.  Allessio had italian sandwiches, salads and pasta dishes.  It is right on 611 and the traffic to get in & out can be tricky.  It's really not that good.  It's also quite affordable.  Sorry.

A small bowling alley that is somewhat underground - it almost looks closed even though there is a big lit sign saying "Open".  Clean and very kid-friendly.  2 pool tables.  BYO (food) B and bowl a game!  Tip:  There is a coupon on their website for $10 off.
Decent coffee in a bar (or is it a decent beer in a coffee shop?), plus they have live music at night.  I usually get a cafe au lait and leave.

Del Val has nearly always had a farmstand - but when they tore down the old one on Rt. 202 years back, they built a MAMMOTH Market.  It was pricey and closed.  Well, it re-opened and I gotta say it's better than ever. We took our little one to the October Fun Weekend (Weekends in the fall from late September thru Halloween you can go on weekends from 11 AM - 4 PM).  It was a glorious 90 minute afternoon filed with organic produce, pony rides ($4 a pop) a corn maze, a FREE rope maze for little kids, Bouncy Castles ($2.00 a go) and free pumpkin painting (but you gotta buy the pumpkins - $.79 per lb.  Lots of mums, gourds and of course, Creamery Ice Cream  What a great place.  I hope they make it this time.

I sincerely hope this is the right Tonelli's that I am reviewing.  We had them cater an event for about 30 people - ordered pizzas, tomato pie (excellent) 2 kinds of stomboli's, a hoagie tray and pasta salad.  All were promptly delivered and tasted great.  Would definitely use them again.
Raina Rocks!  She did my hair for a pin-up shoot. I hope to try her place ASAP.

I do not like this chain at all! This one is marginally better than the hellish one in Doylestown.  The Gyro is a joke. The tortilla I had was cold.  Not good. Chipotle and Qdoba are better for "fast food Mex".  Uck!  Cool things:  Cheap prices, wall of hot sauces and "mix your own" soda flavors.  Otherwise - I'll pass.

Alas, Nicole has moved on, but Melissa and Ali (Aly?) are my go-to stylists for cuts, color, high/low-lights and fun styles for special occasions. It's not a fancy salon - but the prices are fair (They charge extra for using a flat iron or curling iron - so be aware of that) and I have been with Melissa for 6 years.  Love her.  Love them.  I finally found my place for good hair.

A wonderful selection of cheeses (and meats) in Reading Terminal Market.  I get fresh ricotta here as well as Grana Padano and other grating cheeses.  They have a house blend for $8.99 a lb and other types like reggiano and stravecchio for much more $14.99 or even $16.99 a lb.  Regardless, I pick up a few Olive oil tortas from spain, or Marcona almonds or figs.  A great gourmet find!

I love TD Bank - and go to this one primarily to use one of the 2 ATMs.  One big complaint though - when the changed their ATMs so that only a few are "full service" (Only a few ATMs take deposits, sell stamps, etc. - the rest only dispense cash)  I feel that all the machines should take deposits.
My 8 year old loves getting her picture taken here and has done since she was about 4.  And she's never seen any of the Rocky Movies (to my knowledge).  It's fun to watch her pose like Rocky.

World's apart from the vile, horrid Chuck E. Cheese's in South Philly. This Chuck E.'s is actually, barely, mildly tolerable.  Less crowded, more games than work, shorter lines to get food and redeem tickets for cheap plastic "prizes".  My 5 year old is in Heaven here.  My husband and I?  Not so much.

I am updating my review - we just got take out from Jack's tonite and it was really great (can't give that 5th star though as the decor is in SERIOUS need of rehab and take out is better than eating in because of this.)  Our meal consisted of very good (mild - if you want it hotter ask) hot and sour soup, non-greasy spare ribs that were moist & meatty, delicious 10 ingredient rice rice. Shrimp & Lobster sauce (normally a dish I loathe!) was full of big, perfectly cooked shrimp.  Not so good?  Beef lo main was too oily.  Steamed Pork Dumplings while tasty had a heavy dough.  Good but not great.    Jack himself was there when we picked up our order, and his manager gave my 5 year old a lollipop - which made a big impression.  This is pretty much the best & one of the only Chinese take out joints left in D-town.

I have been coming to Grandpa Hicks since the late '80's when i worked at Accents & Images (before the expansion) across the road.  The lady who owns it is so nice and they have a great selection of cheese, coffees and CHAMPAGNE mustard - which is just the best.  In days gone by you could get old fashioned lemonade (in the summer only) served with a lemon stick (a candy stick) that you would use as a straw.  They cater, too - and make lovely gift and holiday baskets of goodies.  Gotta love Grandpa Hicks.

Prices must have been adjusted because today my beloved Rosemary & Olive Oil bagel with lite veggie CC and tomato and cucumber was a mere $2.89.  Servise is still slow as molasses and I was the first one in line (2 people in line at 11:50 AM).  Try to go BEFORE the lunch rush and after the breakfast rush or you will be waiting and waiting.  If I didn't love that darned Rosemary & Olive Oil Bagel so much (and I really shouldn't be eating them that often anyway - calorie and carb-city!) I would never come back here - but the siren's song is hard to resist.

I am giving 4 stars because of the great, great special treatment we got... because...  Believe it or not -we had our wedding rehearsal dinner here. Yes, really.  It was either that or the Olive Garden (Don't ask - but my future and now current father in law had 2 out of 3 of his son's rehearsal dinners at Olive Garden - and wanted ours there too.)  There was no FREAKIN' way I was gonna have my rehearsal dinner at an Olive Garden.  Bensi's is about 1-2 steps above an Olive Garden.  It is a Jersey-based chainette with Red-Sauce favorites. The General Manager, Joe and his staff did a SUPERB JOB with our crowd of 18.  We got the whole back room to ourselves.  We designed a custom menu with 4 entree choices (plated) and family-style salads and apps.  The Bensi Salad (we substitued fresh tomatoes for sun-dried) was GREAT.  The bruchetts - less so.  The mozzarella sticks (and I don't usually indulge in fried foods) were surprisingly tasty.  The Tilapia Francese (special ordered) and Chicken Marsala were very nice, too.  Dad enjoyed his sausage and peppers - but was not floored by it.  I had a dessert brought in specially - and it was very nice that they let us do that.  (Incidentally - Fruit Flowers/Incredily Edible Delights makes for in impressive dessert option)  The bill for all of us was very, very resonable (which made my father inlaw happy).  Incidentally, our neighbors had a party catered from Bensis - Chicken Marsala & Penne Pomodoro - and it was very good.  They also catered my "surprise" bridal shower.  In real life - this is a 2-3 star place - but for what they did for us - 4 stars!!!!

Probably one of the most happenin' places at the slowly dying Plymouth Meeting Mall - especially weekdays for lunch.  Try to come before 11:50 AM when the line forms out the door and down the hallway.  Standard Chick-Fil-A fare which my 12 year old loves.  Chicken Strips (or nuggets) a decent side salad (if you can wait 5 minutes they'll make you one without cheese.)  Wish they'd bring back the long discontinued Cheesecake - my kids loved it.  The "Ice Dream" will have to do.

Rocky Bluewinkle. Mr. Celery. A great family night of fun. Baseball.  My 5 year old adores the BlueRocks and we take her to a few games every summer.  What a nice stadium, too.  A great asset to baseball, to the city of Wilmington and to the community.  (And this coming from me - a chick who hates sports and is bored to DEATH at games.)

Well DD (dear daughter) and I visited Shanghai Bazaar again today - as we do very often.  And while upstairs a GORGEOUS, young looking woman greeted us and gave the l'il one a red balloon and a tiny, shiny pink star.  We soon realized that we were speaking with Ms. Lily Song - owner of Shanghai Bazaar, Opera singer and a great resource of Chinese Culture in Philadelphia.  That seals it - we totally LOVE Shanghai Bazaar and will come here for all things Chinese-Culture that we could ever need or want.

Well I have been to BOTH Vietnam and Vietnam Palace and the srvice and decor at Vietnam PALACE were better than that "place across the street".  Food at both is excellent and comparable in price.  I really enjoyed the Tofu Spring rolls (under vegetarian selections - last page of the HUGE menu) and at $4.50 an order - they were a good value, too.  My BIG bowl of Banh with grilled shrimp was excellent - and for $1.00 extra he added 2 beef-stuffed grapeleaves - which I really wanted to try and never had.  Glad I did!  Good stuff all around anf the have a HUGE private room upstairs for banquets - even a wedding. I am seriously considering have a private event here. Thanks to Victor and my lovely (male) server - don;t know his name.  Oh - and they have a full bar.

Took my 6 year old to VP for the first time and we were lucky enough to meet Tracy - who is coordinating a large party we plan to have here in April.  The party room upstairs can seat 90 and is roomy and lovely.  You could easily have a baby shower, brunch, dinner or even a small wedding here. Our group will probably only be about 25 - but still - can't wait to have it!  My little one ordered Tamarind Shrimp Skewers which she loved and Shrimp Bun - so we had a shrimp fest.  It was delicious.  The Vietnamese iced coffee was sweet and a jolt of much-needed caffeine.  (We had just come from the flower show so we were TIRED.)  This is a great place with reasonbly priced, tasty food.  We can't wait to see how our party goes in April.

Dr. Carla Patton and Madeline Brown are both bright, articulate, caring and compassionate doctors.  I had been seeing Dr. Patton in my late teens/early 20's until I moved away from Doylestown.  When I returned I desparately needed care, and then met Dr. Brown who has been a true life-saver.  The office can be crowded and there is often a wait time, but they do their best.  Call ahead as soon as you know you'll need an appointment.  They are worth seeing - and a great practice for women.

We hosted a large event at the College of Physicians and Catering by Design was the in-house caterer.  Our event had an open bar (3 different bar locations - so never a long line - whoo-hoo) and fancy hors d'oeurves including a pad thai bar (awesome) a slider bar - falafel, chicken and beef burgers and a goreous display (under the 2nd floor rotunda) of charcuterrie, olives, spreads, breads and dips.  Great job! Great tasting, plentiful food - within our limited budget. And - as i mentioned - plenty of booze flowing all night long with little to no waiting.

Had a very mediocre $13 lunch here. It was summer - so the place was nearly empty.  Age-Dashi Tofu was cut into 2 HUGE chunks and swimming in dashi. That was (sadly) the best part of the meal.  Beef Bi-Bim Bap had very little meat that was nearly flavorless.  Not great at all.  Will not be back.

I am not a big Cosi Fan but this location (in a strip mall in Wayne/Berwyn/Paoli ish) is close to my office and the Salmon Salad I got ($10 ish) was decent.  Iced coffee was bitter.  Service was quick and very pleasant.  A decent lunch alternative.
Another spectacular cut, color and a few foils by Cynthia.  She is a true artist.  Much love.  Enjoyed my visit to Oggi - and Natalie (Shampoo/Assistant) is a doll, too!

I wanted to love it.  Really, I did. I had the fried Chicken, mac 'n cheese and collard greens.  All were they way they are supposed to be.  (By the book)  But the mac was way to heavy - and I didn't happen to get any of that good crust on the top layer.  The chicken was sooooo salty.  Like eating saltines in the Sahara. And very, very greasy (but hell - it is FRIED chicken.)  The greens were perfect.  I give them a 3 stars for food and the grotty digs of the RTM and the SURLY (down-right nasty) service I got from the counter lady really made me feel like just leaving.  The 30th Street Station location is WORSE.

As saladworks go, this one is pretty decent - and in the vast culinary wasteland of this neighborhood, it is a welcome and convenient (if pricey) choice.  Home of the $8.00 salad, saladworks offers salads, soups and panini sadwiches (which I never get - as I do not like them).  I have figured out the exactly right salad for me using the "create your own" option.  Thus, I rarely deviate from my "usual".  The greens are sometimes rusty - so I opt for spinach or spring mix. I also do not care for the rolls, so I never get one.  It's an option for a quick lunch and I am glad they are here so I don't have to eat pizza every day.

We were married here on 06/07/08 and everything went so swimmingly well.  From our initial site visiti in the Summer of 2007, to a FABULOUS tasting dinner in late 2007 to the actual "big day".  The tasting dinner, for starters, was such a great experience.  My fiance (now husband) and both of our sets of parents tasted 6 entrees and 6 apps, along with 4 sides.  We ound up selecting some GREAt choices which were well executed on the wedding night.  Our wedding had 79 guests (8 of which were kids and 4 of which were three year olds).  We served buffet style - but could have opted for a sit down and had 4 hours of OPEN BAR.  (Whoo-hoo.)  It was 96 degrees on the day of our wedding, so it was really hot.  We wound up having the cocktail hour indoors, to save guests from the heat.  The food, service and accomodations were all top notch.  Wendy (event Manager) & Teg (General Manager) along with our day-of coordinator (you get one included with your wedding package) Wendy treated us very well and our every need was met.
JC Penny is trying hard to resurrect its failing business. Prices are, indeed, somewhat lowernow - no coupons or a sale every other week.  Decent variety of ladies and kids clothes.

We are thrilled and delighted to have a greek place in Media. The chicken souvlaki is thigh meat (delicious - and I prefer dark - but keep that in mind if you only eat white meat chicken).  My 12-year-old scarfed down a traditional lamb/beef gyro, and I had the pork souvlaki (tender and juicy - so good.)  Avgolemono soup is one of my favorites ($4.95 for a nice large bowl of it) but this one was only fair.  Everything comes with fries - costs more to have a greek salad instead.  (The salad is on romaine and is very fresh and tasty.  Decor is brand-spankin' new and clean looking. They really gutted this place and it shows.  WELL DONE.  We wish you the very best - and I will be headed back in soon for some Dolmades and Baklava (have not tried them yet.).

Toro tartar plus Tuna Pizza plus $75 chef sushi platter fed 2 of us with ease (and leftovers).  Fish of many varieties - and all were top quality and uber-fresh.  We still caved and split the chocolate pot de creme.  Topped mine off with a glass of the Veuve and Mama was veddy veddy happy.  Our server, Eric, was workin' it and everything was 5 star all the way!
I agree with Valerie S.  I frequent this Wawa when i need gas on my way back from Brinton Lake or other shopping spots.  Never a problem - get in, get gas, get out.

Makes me happy, happy!  I will edit my review once I try the meat ravioli I just bought over the weekend.  I am so anxious to try it and to find a great new source for pasta and ravioli and sauces in the Italian Market area.  Once I taste them I am hoping to make this review a 5 star!

5 stars for our actual balloon ride - safe procedures, take off and landing by Barry who is clearly a pro with over 23 years of experience as a pilot.  The 1 star off is for customer service - I was proactive and called alot but they are slow to return calls and use texts (one of which I never got).  Once I clarified that I need to be CALLED not texted they complied.  Our flight was rescheduled twice due to weather- but the 3rd time was truly the charm. Much fun!  Perfect Flight.

My experiences at Oggi just keep getting better & better. I went to see Cynthia today - mostly because she made @Susan G. look HAWT and I wanted to look HAWT, too.  Well, I wish I had a picture - b/c she just colored my hair a GORGEOUS (and volatile) shade of red and cut it to perfection.  She is a sweet & talented lady - and has been with Oggi off & on for 14 years.  Cass who shampooed (and I mean SCRUBBED) my color out was a doll and I wish her the best of luck with her career.  Can't wait to come back.  I spent just under $200 though - Ouch. (Includes tips and a bottle of $13 shampoo.)  Cynthia - you ROCK!
Better (selection-wise) than Spice Corner in the Italian Market but still not as good as Penzey's.  The prices are not that great - but they do have a good selection.

You're kidding? Far from as good as it gets. This store is disorganized and often out of stock of the MSM/Chondroitin supplements I buy. Prices are high (except during an amazing 30% off everything in the store event that was great) and staff seems disinterested.  Messy floors. Please sweep them. Please re-stock your shelves.  The good part?  They do have alot of the things I need - like Eukaneuba Small Breed Dry food and the aforementioned Joint Care supplements.  Not my favorite pet store - but it is closets to my home and I am thankful they are here.

Very Upset. Since my initial review - which was terrific - we have been here several times.  Each time the food quality was a bit worse - maybe 3 stars.  But this last time - now I am so angry, I cam in at about 4:15 PM and was hungry so I got 2 garlic knots to go for my kid and asked the (albeit young and feisty, but apparently clueless) counter gal how much a side order of the chicken tortellini would be.  She said $2.99 and I said "fine".  Got to the cashier (same manager guy as before) and he rings up my order at nearly $7 - and I'm like "What??".  He says it's $4.99 for the chicken tortellini.  I reluctantly agree and pay for it. I sit down and start to eat it and it tastes slightly sour.  Then more sour.  I threw half of it away and walked out.  I will not return unless my kid demands it.  I bet that had been sitting out since lunchtime - and shame on me for ordering it.  NOT COOL, Bravo Pizza.  Not cool at all!

I had a gift certificate for a Wash, Cut & Blowdry with Toni and she is a terrific lady.  The salon itself is not fancy - and they don't push you to purchase products - in fact I was not asked anything about product at all which was kinda refreshing.  A great blowout.  And a cut is just $17 ($25 with the blowout.) Single process color is $55 (with or without a cut).  Kids cuts are $12 (under 10 years old).  I'll be back to see Toni again for sure!  Update - 2017:  Toni is gone - but Renee is there now.

Not nearly as bad as I had feared. Room was satisfactory. "Hotel" Food at the event I attended was fine.  Not awesome - but perfectly good.  Check-in/out went smoothly.  They even have an indoor pool (wish I had known - I did not bring a swimsuit).  I stayed here for a corporate event, otherwise would not have picked this location. Female bartender in "Blue" lounge was a doll.  Oh - a BIG thing - please fix:  NASTY SMELL in lobby and elevator.

I also heart cheap gas - and Like Sarah K. (who is right on!) I shop at Giant so I can get that cheap gas - right across the street from the grocery store is the BIG (and always busy - but not as busy as the Wawa) gas station.  I usually get 20 - 30 cents off per gallon.  Sweet.

3 or maybe 4 stars - but too "average" to really justify 4 stars. I stopped in for lunch and needed quick and cheap.  That may have been a mistake - this place can be quick, but it ain't cheap.  So I cheaped-out and got the express lunch (Which says it's $9 on the front door menu - but then it says is $10 on the blackboard.)  So for $10 you get a choice of soup (Minestrone OR Italian wedding) or salad (House or Caesar) and then a choice of a personal pizza OR a 1/2 sandwich.  I got Caesar salad and 1/2 a chicken parm. The chicken parm was very good and served on a fresh, hot toasted roll (carb overload - especially since they also give you garlic rolls - which are LOADED in garlic.) Do not eat those garlic rolls if you have an important meeting or presentation after lunch, LOL.  I brushed my teeth at the office and I still taste the garlic.  Wow.
