Please note that I have not actually dined here since the mid nineties and I am quite sure the menu, chef and prices were all drastically different back then.  But it was terrific - I had an unforgettable duck breast that was PERFECTLY cooked.  No idea if the current menu offers duck.  Meanwhile IF YOU CAN FIND IT - you gotta check out the C-ville Inn.  A great "date place".
OMG - I can't believe they've survived for all these years.  It's fruity-drink, frat boy, college chick central.  Not my kinda place - and never was.

I haven't been back to Giwa in over 2 years - and boy am I glad I stopped in for a Galbi lunch special today.  Delicious and quick.  Sub multi-grain rice for white for $1.25 extra.    Good stuff!  Next time I shall try the Korean Tacos.

Wow - I can't believe I've waited this long to yelp Square on Square.  I have eaten here many times -mainly for lunch as they do a filling, mid-priced lunch special.  The Hot & Sour soup here is some of the best EVER .  Really.  5 stars for the H&S Soup.  We also had a large group party here in February 2008.  They offered a set meal with soup, appetizer choice of 6 entrees and dessert.  It was very well organized and our group of over 30 people left well-fed and happy.  The manager, Steven, is very nice and easy to work with.  The only detractors here (preventing the 5 star rating) is the extremely long lines at lunch time.  (Don't come at 12:30 on a Tursday of Friday) Also the decor is in need of refreshment.  Kinda grungy.  Don't miss the Mango Chicken and Filet Mignon - really tender and nice here.

Got this to-go (eating here is a bit depressing)( but Judy and Beth - working the lunch line were friendly and polite.  Got a 3 piece dark meat platter with brocolli and green beans on the side.  (Came with cornbread).  Not good for you - but better than the 980 calorie BOMB chicken pot pie that my friends all got (It's tasty.).  An acceptable alternative to Tony Luke's and IHOP.

Happy freakin' brithday to me!!!!  Ok - I'm gonna do it.  I'm giving Davio's 5 stars.  I read all the yelp reviews before we went (and many were bad or just fair) - and I have to tell you - last night we had a true 5 star experience at Davio's.  Lemme break it down...    Before last night's soiree I had pretty much ZERO desire to go here.  I walk by all the time and the menu seemed kinda small and boring and PRICEY as heck.  I wanted to go (and still want to go) to Butcher & Singer.  (And I will - one day.)  Our party of 7 (Originally to be 9) sat at a lovely LARGE round table, and our server (Rodolpho?  Renaldo?) was terrific and gave great expalnations and recommendations.  The space (a former bank) has high ceilings and gorgeous wood floors.  Chairs are big and COMFY.  First class all the way.  After a round of drinks (2 of my friends had drinks at the bar while waiting for the rest of us to arrive - but they were offered to sit at the table by the host had they so desired.) including Bellini Martini's (YUM) and Veuve Clicquot - simply perfection in a glass - we ordered or apps & entrees.  The round of apps included several standouts.  My friend LOVED the Philly Cheesesteak Spring rolls.  I had the beet salad - which I shared with a friend) and she shared her chicken livers - sauteed in balsamic with cherries.  Both were simply popping with flavor.  So great.  We also passed a big "honkin'" slab of Insalata Caprese around the table.  Now, I have had this salad (mozzarella & tomato) umpteen times in so many preparations - good, bad and indifferent.  This one was good - but not great.  The supposed "Buffala" mozz was fresh - but not as creamy as some.  The tomoto was a thickly cut beefsteak.    I definitely reccomend the chicken liver app and the beet salad with lemon zest, walnuts & fresh micro-watercress.  Both "sang" on the palate.  My DH had pasta for his app - and I had 2 delectable bites.  One of the fresh tagliatelle (WOWZA!) and a second mouthfull of the thick, meaty bolognese.  I would order this again for sure.  Entrees were just as good as the apps with Osso Bucco, Shortribs, Ribeye Steak and RACK OF LAMB (Best in my opinion - and I ordered the osso bucco - BFF had the lamb) were standouts.  Fresh Branzino fillet was served atop a mound of risotto puttanesaca - rich with flavor.  My good vegetarian friend has angel hair arrabiatta - which he loved.  (But at $16 I would NEVER have ordered.)  Service between courses was perfectly timed.  Not too attentive, not too stand-offish.  Desserts ROCKed.  Yes, it's trite - but 3 out of 4 of the ladies (myself included) ordered the molten chocolate cake (allow 10-15 minutes for prep - we were in NO hurry).  Served with Vanilla Gelato - it was plate-lickin' worthy.  A friend had tiramisu - looked more like a layered torte - another had a luscious sour cherry tart - which was more like a glamorous muffin top.  (I happened to enjoy the bite I snagged of it.)  Last but not least 2 of the gents tried the rich, yet light & fruity lemon pudding.  We were all treated to a chocolate covered strawberry on each plate (which I requested).  Many of us had coffees - and I had a lovely cappucino (yes, I know that nobody in Italy drinks capp past 11 AM - but hey - I wanted one - and it was damned good.)  What a lovely evening.  Pricey as heck - and in my opinion this is a "special occaision" or "expense account" restaurant - but if some wants to take me here?  You bet I'm goin'!  And I fully intend to grab a girlfriend or two and order drinks & apps at the bar.  Those chicken livers are calling me...
We go here often.  Children's room.  Computers.  Books.  you got it!

I would never stay here.  Absolute mediocrity.  We attend events here and the event people pick this place for the (reasonable) price of conference space.  Yuck.  Depressing.  Please renovate and clean - bathrooms and public spaces, too!

I coulda sworn I wrote a review for ladder fifteen a while ago - but alas - I guess I did not.  I am basing this review on a large event my group had in there upstairs, private space.    We had about 90 people, an open beer, wine and well drinks bar (excellent) and appetizers (not so much).  Firstly, there was not enough food (in quantity) and the quality of the small platters of apps (place on the bar - not butlered) was pretty meh.  Pretzel nuggets with mustard dipping sauce (cheap!), Mediocre quesedillas, and a strange bruscetta with an unidentifyable brown meat-or-possibly-eggplant on top.  Still have no idea what the heck that was all about!  Anyhow, service was fine - bartenders were quick with our moderately-drinking crowd of adults in there' late 20's to early 50's.  Will I rush back here?  Probably not.

I am still working out a few issues we had with our move (2 items were slightly damaged), but in general our experience with 2 Men and a Truck went well.  Ben and David in dispatch were great.  Our moving team (3 men and a truck) were just OK.  Brandon was the best of the bunch.  The other 2 guys seemed to really not care much one way or the other.  It's a crappy job and they did fine in the beginning (loading the truck) but toward the end things fell apart.  Items wrapped in plastic were not unwrapped on arrival - leaving us to unwrap and dispose of yards and yards of plastic wrap.  (Not earth shattering, not a tragedy - but not fun either.)  They came in 15 minutes under estimate. Boxes are available but very expensive.  We bought 4 boxes (2 big wardrobe boxes and 2 mediums).    PACK YOUR OWN STUFF and use your own boxes!

Reservations with Miah and Michele were great, the actual flight with Cody for our group of 4 was perfect, however a few things were not perfect.  Ordering video clips did not work well - we somehow missed one clip and we are still waiting for it.  Hopefully we'll get it soon.  Also we waited about 25 minutes late for out 2 PM flight (we arrived at 1 PM) - took off at 2:25 PM.  Meanwhile all the kids LOVED it and can't wait to do it again.

Initially I did not have high hopes for La Belle Epoque - having read the menu and passed by many times - it just never appealed  French food?  Not my fave.   Meanwhile, we went here last night and had very good service and EXCELLENT food. And the best part?  One of the tastiest French 75 cocktails ($10) made to perfection.  The only food downer?  The French Onion Soup which had way. way toomuch rosemary - as in sticks 'n twigs of it.  (Not salty though - and served in a Big bowl for $8). The best part?  Both entrees- mine and DH's.  He had the Duck confit crepe - which I tasted and we both loved.  I had the duck with raspberry sauce - cooked to perfection (I like my duck with plenty of quack still left in it).  The haricot vert and fluffy (buttery-chivey) mashed potatoes were also divine.  I shall return. And I will bring our 9 year old - she loves duck, Very pleased!!!  Nice place for a date night,too.  Much smaller inside than I had imagined.

5 star service from Shana (sp?) and Kaitlyn (sp?) but 2 star food. Absolutely DRY al pastor burrito - but I was too full from scarfing down over-salted chips to eat much anyway.  Took over 1/2 home.  Drinks were good - the pineapple cilantro Marg being the best of the lot.  Considering it was "Dining Under the Stars" (we had a prime table in the front of the house near the open window) it could have been worse.  I really want to give them higher marksand Ionly come here a few times per year - and the service is great but the food needs work.

I love it here.  I just do.  The table by the window - especially when the weather is nice.  The bar with it's unique wine storage, and especially the food.  Trennette pasta is house made in saffrom suace. The stuffed tomatoes (side dish) are so yummy The mixed antipasta platter is near perfect.  So what if the staff is aloof?  The receptionist cold and sterile?  The decor is sleek and not warm and welcoming - but beautiful nonetheless.  I love eating here.  It ain't perfect - but I feel 4 stars is too low. I'm giving it 5.  The fish - oh I forgot about the fish - whatever the special fish is - GET IT!!!!  It will be fresh and delectable.

A nice, affordable Italian BYOB.  We had a very, very large group in the private party room and had a choice of 3 entrees - and all were delicious.  Services was attentive and not pushy.  Decent atmosphere.  We also came here once on our own and had mediocre pasta dishes.   We will be back, but not in a hurry.

Stopped in to Mulberry today for a snacking emergency - and they graciously made my little one a PLAIN turkey (no mayo, no mustard, no veggies, no nuthin') on white (untoasted).  Not MY choice, but what-evs.  She dug it and devoured it and I willingly forked over $4.79 for it.  OUCH.  Great service by the counter staff.  Oh - and I got me an INKO Iced White tea.   - I luvs that stuff!  Mulberry Market is all THAT and a bag of gourmet chips!

This place has been here for years and it's, well, odd.  They have a create-your own salad section (similar to Saladworks - but cheaper), and a Japanese Food/Sushi section.  Very inexpensive.  Food is OK.  Just OK.  A cheap, quick lunch choice.

Pure fare tasted better when it was on somebody else's dime. Yes, I LOVE the green detox juice - but it's $5.00 (and it's served warm - so ask for ice in advance if you can't stomach warm veggie juice).  My salad was $7.60 and tasted great - but again - I came in at just under $14 for a juice and a salad.  And service is painfully slow - as the barrista has to drip everyone's blue bottle coffee one slow drip at a time.  Bring cash and your patience if you want lunch here.

Average CVS - well stocked and clen but does not stay open late enough at night (Pharmacy closes at 8 or 10 PM?  Too early for those "sick kid" emergencies.  We had to go to Walgreen's for dat.  Right next to Chick Fil-A so we stop in quite a bit.

Brunch here is the real showstopper.  (Not really a 4 star for other meals).  The food is American-ish with a twist.  I enjoyed the bread basket offerings - they were really fresh and tasty.  Nice alcoholic drinks, too.  Pricey - but very genteel and worth it.  Gorgeous decor and professional service.  CROWDED for brunch - but worth it.  Make a reservation.

We shop at AC Moore alot - usually at the one on Comubus Blvd - but also at this location - which is nicer and cleaner.  They all have the same layout - so we head straight to the scrapbooking and paining supplies.  If you have a coupon - you can get some good deals.

They are now cash only (except for large catering orders). Still a great "safe" choice for lunch or brunch.  The crispy honey fried chicken salad is my favorite, and any "fish of the day" is great (Salmon, mahi mahi).  For dessert don;t miss the delicious chocolate cake with buttercream frosting.  So good!  Nice salad and hot specials. Friendly service from Wendy and the crew.  (The cashier lady is lovely - I can never remember her name, though.)  And the support my child's school!  We love Day by Day!

Just got yet another GREAT order from Peregrine - freshly roasted Brazilian Cerrado - and right on time for our Thanksgiving feast.  If you have not had your FREE (seriously - they will come right to your home or office) bespoke coffee tasting yet - you need to check this out. right. now.  Kevin & Louise, the owners are so accomodating and they roast up some of the best KenyaAA, Kona, Guatemalan (DH's fave) and the aforementioned Brazilian.  I LOVE PEREGRINE!!!

I stopped in after receiving a flyer in the mail.  This is a brand new location - and I have heard many mixed reviews (and some bad ones) for Massage Envy - disinterested practitioners, high turnover, etc.  So - with trepidation I booked a $59 Intro Murad Facial with Billie Jo.  She is terrific and thus, I "drank the Kool Aid" and became a Massage Envy Member ($60 per month and you get 1 massage).  I will have my first massage in a few weeks and will update my review at the time.  Front desk staff is very good!
A very nice, spacious and apparently well-run Staples. Found what we needed on a Sunday AM and got in and out super quickly.  Friendly staff. No issues.

Get a facial with Billie Joe. RUN - do not walk for a Murad (they have to use Murad - it's a corporate thing) facial and ask specifically for Billie Joe.  She is the best part of this ME location.  The massage therapists come and go and come and go and frankly, I have not yet had one (since Hudson - who left and I knew he would) that I can say is excellent.  They are fine.  Not bad and not awesome but fine.  Alot of the therapists are fresh out of school or looking to establish or re-establish a following and then they leave.  I have only had one truly BAD massage here and the therapist was let go shortly thereafter (She was a true "space case").  I have also had some GREAT massages here and then the therapists have left (Hudson [who was reverse commuting in from Philly] and Sam - who had personality problems).  Mindy and Mary seem to be good.  Mindy has treated my kid and my kid LOVES her so I am praying she will stay. Please STAY for a while, Mindy!!!!  Meanwhile, the front desk staff (also a bit of a revolving door - I hope they keep Celeste as she is terrific!!) is quite good and the owner seems to really know her stuff. Go, Celeste!  As a former spa owner, I am truly picky about who(m) I let touch my face - and Billie Joe is a gifted esthetician (formerly was at Toppers, I believe).  So like I said - try out Billie Joe for a facial (I like the Vitamin C one) .  Oh - and if you get a good massage therapist - I hope you will encourage them to STAY. I really miss Hudson.  He was great.  I am hopeful who(m)ever I get next will be a "keeper". Billie Joe and Celeste are keepers. Please do right by them!  Oh - and the facility itself is gorgeous and clean and well-maintained.  Love it!
Fun to browse here - but I rarely ever buy anything any more.  It was better when I was a teenager and could actually use this stuff. It is VERY touristy nowadays - or maybe it always was.

So far so good.  We took our newly adopted rescue dog (from Delco SPCA) here for a check up the minute we brought her home.  The vet tech we saw was very kind and the vet himself was also good.  Seems like a decent practice.

Zio's can get very chaotic and crowded but the "Grandmom" pizza is terrific.  Sicilian is a bit thicker and cheesier - my 9 year old gets that.  Traditional cheese-steaks and a few goodies like rice balls and zeppoli keep us coming back.  No problems here - just good, reasonably priced pizza and sandwiches.
Update!  In November 2014 they opened at Penzey's at the Bourse in Center City.  Can't wait to go!

I have been coming to this particular old-skool (no gas station) wawa since grade school.  Smokes, coffee, tasty-kakes, hoagies and the day's newspaper.  No problems here - the parking lot gets crowded so PAY ATTENTION - but this is our go-to D-town wawa.  And we love it.

I was gun-shy at coming back here after my awful dinner experience - but I have eaten many lunches here in years past.  I got the $10 lunch special (includes soup and rice) and had the terrific hot 'n sour soup.  Large portion of food for lunch - took some home.  Avoid for dinner - but fine for lunch. You have redeemed yourselves, Square on Suqare. See you again for lunch.

So disappointed.  We bought a groupon (eversave?) that is only valid for dinner (dine-in only),  So we tried to use it the day after hurrican Irene - and Square on Square was packed so we left.  Fine.  No biggie.  So last night (a few months later) we go to Square on Square at 4:30 PM.  We had called earlier to ask if we'd need a reservation and the man said, "no".  So we show up and the place is open, but dead empty.  No staff to greet us, no nothin'.  So we call "Hello!"  "Hellooooo!".  Nothing.   My husband and I waited around a good 5 minutes and then left.  So disappointing.

543 is Urban Outfitter's answer to the (pricey) corporate cafeteria - and there are a bunch of good choices including soups, a salad bar, sushi (too expensive for what it is - Salmon Avocado roll is $8.) and sandwiches.  Hot entree's rotate. Lovely salads - around $9.  If you work here - it's one of the only options, so I hope even more places will open up down here.  Lo spiedo is wonderful but too expensive for a "regular" lunch.
Ran in and out for yet more Caudlalie Eau de Raisin (this time it was $18 plus tax for the 6.7 ounce spray).  Got a few samples of NARS and Bobbi Brown, too.

This is a review for the Drycleaner/Wash 'n fold services.  They also own the adjoining Laundromat next door.  Parking can be tight so be careful!  Meanwhile, I stopped here when our dryer broke for the $1 per lb wash 'n fold service.  BUT - they are not open on Sundays (The laundromat is, but the dry-cleaner is closed Sundays) so I waited and just dropped off some "regular" dry cleaning.  Whoa!  Dry cleaning here is more expensive that Victory - but Sharon (owner? manager?) was a sweetheart and gave me 20% off because I was a first time client.  Whew.  A few days later my dryer was still out of commission so I dropped of 12 lbs ($12.00) of necessities and they were washed, dried and folded neatly ready by 12 noon the next day.  I will definitely come here for wash 'n fold, but if I only need dry cleaning, I will go to Victory (unless you come here on a Wed or Sat - 20% off when you drop off on those days).  Sharon - you are terrific!
A super-small theater - and not a bad seat in the house.  (It's so small that even the back row is fine.)  Support your local theater!!!

Tampopo has gotten better - at least now that I know what to order (and what not to order).  Today I got a side order ($2) of egg cake (tamago) and a veggie and tofu (fried but still so tasty) bibimbop.  Called it in, picked it up, no lines, no worries.  Sweet.

Went back again and service was much better but still a few off-putting things. (Food is great - especially chicken parm and anything with rosa /aurora sauce)  Charged $2.00 extra to have aforementioned sauce on kids meal (pasta and meatballs - and then no meatballs arrived.  Owner came around to see how things were BEFORE any food had arrived.  And he seems grumpy.  Weird.  Meanwhile our 8 year old likes it here so I bet we'll be back. Wish they were friendlier.

Finally used my eversave (valid only during dinner - and I sure know why!)  Service was just awful - very cold female server worked her butt off - while other guy stood there (not wonder she's so angry).  The food was good.  "Happy Hour" small plates are $5 - I tried the "Fried Shrimp Joe" which was kinda like shrimp-toast filling deep-fried and cut into chunks.  Tasty - but so greasy - will not get that again.  Sliced beef with eggplant (and I added brocolli - no charge) for $16.50 was a HUGE portion (Took about 1/2 home) and the beef was tender and delicious.  Great food - but this place is a LUNCH SPOT - and is truly cursed at dinner (dine-in). Dim lighting, borderline mean servers and just not fun.  Won;t be back so soon. Meanwhile - for takeout I love the hot and sour soup here. Again - they have GREAT food. It's a shame my dinner "dine-in" was so MEH.

Where do I begin?  Well - for the Green room dining alone it's 5 stars - please see my review of that - but this is for the hotel.  Wow.  Impressive - from the valet parking and reception upon arrival, to the $40 rosew petal turn downservice to the $25 lavendar relaxation bath complete with those FAMOUS and delectable macaroons (get a box to take home!), our King Room with sitting area and huge tub was well worth the nearly $400 per night.  (Room about $300 dining package in Green room well worth the extra $100)  Bellhops, Front desk, concierge and all staff were attentive without being obtrusive and our 1 night stay was heavenly and TOP NOTCH.  In addition there was a rockin' good Jazz Festival that just happened to be that same night at the adjaecent Rodney Square - so that was fun, and we peeked in on one of 2 lavish weddings held at Hotel Dupont that Saturday.  What a great venue for a wedding!  My DH gets brownie points for at least the next 3-5 months! We have an anniversary getaway to remember.  Well worth the money.

I pretty much agree with EVERYBODY (and I mean everybody) else on N. 3rd.  Great food, great & busy artsy eye-catching decor and perfect for brunch.  (SCORE!  A near-perfect bloody mary with a great kick to it.)  We enjoy it here - but it can be a crowded cluster-f&%k at peak times.

Normally I'd give Bertucci's about 3 stars - but this location is BRAND new (aboput 5 weeks old) and we had excellent service.  Come early - they get CROWDED and the places is loaded with kids & babies.  This is a very, very family friendly place - and mom & dad can get a drink.  I recommend the Tialpia served over Spianch if you are watching your carbs, as the Bertucci's menu is a carbo-loader for sure!  My 4 year olds loved her kid-sized pizza and even moreso loved watching the pizza ladies (and men) make pizzas).  A safe suburban bet for those with kids.

A nice, basic Irish (real Irish owners & bartenders - and Irish music playing) pub with Irish and American pub grub.  I like it better than Tir Na Nog.  We had cute little "mini burgers" and a chicken quesedilla made with Boxty (really - the potato boxty like in Ireland) instead of a tortilla.  I would go back!
A big Lowe's with everything you need. Got in & out (self check out) for light bulbs the other day. No issues.

We came on a super-busy Wednesday for Dining Under ste stars - and miraculously our table was ready & waiting even though there were throngs of others.  The service was surprisingly good.  The food?  Just OK - and yes, I had read the reviews on yelp and yes, they are accurate - this place needs to step up their game on the food front.  Pizzas are not my thing - but 3 of our group of 6 (well - 5 and an infant) have pizza.    They seemed very doughy to me and many do not have sauce.  (Cheese and coldcuts on bread.)  My kid had the lobster-stuffed arrancina - and they were leaden with a greasy crusty exterior.  I have had better but the 9 year old loved them.  My dish was a fail.  Tasteless salmon with too-vinegary chopped tomatoes on top.  I ate the mashed potatoes and brocolli but left most of the fish.  Azie's Salmon Teriyaki puts Ariano's salmon to shame!  I will not be rushing back here. Disappointing menu and food.

I love the food here - but the prices are high. The quinoa salad ($7) is amazing but it's not enough on its own to satisfy me for lunch.  Luckily a lady split it with me so I could also get a salmon platter ($11).  So instead of $18 I spent $15.  Still a high price for lunch - and I really wanted to get a veggie juice, but that would have been another $5.  So it's one thing at a time for me.  Oh:  Even my 8 year old loves it here - she ATE the quinoa salad and enjoyed it and also LOVED her mango, strawberry, pineapple smoothie.  (But who wouldn't love that?)

I have lived in the Pacakrd Building for 3 years now - and while the rents continue to rise & rise, the building is still good for us.  Great location and basically well run and well managed.  We wish they'd replace the 22 year old washer dryer in my apartment though.  It takes FOREVER to dry clothes and is a waste of electricity.  The entire building is 100% electric - so there's no gas bill - but the electric bills for heat and a/c - especially with our 15 foot ceilings (a plus and also a minus) - the bills are SKY HIGH.  (Pun intended.)  Some of the front desk staff are lazy - but most are very nice and willing to help you with dry-cleaning and packages.  Rita is the nicest of the bunch.  It's a gorgeous apartment for a luxury price.  Smack dab in the middle - of NOTHING.  (Broad Street bet. Vine & Callowhill).  There is "The Sunday Breakfast Club" aka homeless shelter 1/2 a block away so there are quite a few unsavory goings-on in the alley next to the building.  AND little police patrol.  Once we get home after work - we stay there!!!

Amazing!  A hair's breadth away from 5 stars - so I'mma gonna do it and give them all five - and especially Marina our kind, patient server who was so accommodating.  Firstly, my dining companion and I walked in 45 minutes EARLY for our 8 PM res.  This is a hostesses nightmare and we were prepared to be told to "sit at the bar" but we got a table (in the bar area) right away.  I had 2 of the tastiest Arnold Palmers you can imagine - made with the herb-infused house sun tea.  Everything we ate from the fluffy warm brioche rolls with ramp butter to the delicate "handkerchief" pasta (mine with umami rich rabbit, my friends was vegetarian) to the luscious side of garden beets (at least 2 varieties of beet - possibly 3 it was hard to tell) and candied orange peel and a touch of creamy fresh ricotta. - All was wonderful - but the real showpiece was the special of SEASON ONLY squash blossoms (which I love!!!) delicately fried - stuffed with goat cheese and herbs.  Calorie-city!  But so tasty - and we shared an order of 4 - so 2  seemed just about decadently perfect.  We also splurged and shared a Millefuille (more like quatrefuille - please tell me somebody gets my jokes...) of thinly sliced banana, toffee and chocolate served with a rich yet delicate quenelle (aka the Quenelle from hell) of dark chocolate sorbet.   Wow.  Beets (pun intended) the heck outta Parc. Similar price points but somehow we spent WAY less (no $60 seafood cocktail tonight, thank you very much).  Dinner for 2 with soft drinks and 1 dessert (no alcohol) was around $75 before tip.  I can't wait to go back.  GO TO TALULA'S.  Go! Go! Go!  And ask for Marina - what a sweetheart. Tatiana was a doll, too.  Great service, great food, precious decor (a little too cutesy for me, but it's Starry-eyed splendor in the grass.).  You got me!

We bought a microfiber sofa from Raymour back in 2007 (For about $600) and got very good use out of it, so we headed to this location (Yay for no-tax in DE) but wound up buying elsewhere.  Decent prices - and our sales lady (Shelly??) had been there for years and was so helpful.  We wound up buying somewhere else solely due to price.  We'll let you know what happens.

Pure Fare was better today.  $11.88 for a green detox juice (I just LOVE this one) and a wheatberry salad.  Salad was scrumptious and quite filling. Sweet potatoes, beets and all things I like in it.  Service was a bit sullen - fortunately I came at 11:45 AM before the lunchtime rush kicked in.
Not sure if this is for the Hotel or the Green Room restaurant but believe me - both are 5 stars and well worth a visit.  There is also the DuPont Theatre which offers great plays.
Pretty good for a hotel restaurant.  Nice view of the river and the terrace is a great place to have drinks when the weather is nice.

I have gone to the 21st Street location a few times - mostly when I first moved to Philly and did not know about other (better) places.  There is no atmosphere - but it is very, very reasonable for a quick bento lunch.  They used to serve a DELICIOUS inexpensive kalbi box but no more.  You can still get the bul-goki though - but it is not as good as the bul-goki at the Korean Place on Chestnut (I am spacing out on the name of the place between 20 & 21 on Chestnut).  It's MIRAN - that's the name.  MIRAN!!!  But I digress...  Menawhile do NOT order any sushi type items here.  The spicy tuna rolls were NOT fresh.  Stick to the cooked meals and rice bowls and you'll be fine.  You get alot of OK (some is good, even) foor and a LOT of rice for very little coin.  When you want the good stuff though, so elsewhere. For dinner.  This is a lunch place.  Really.

Haven't been back to Tampopo in such a long time, so today I had the fresh salmon BBB (salmon was not as fresh as it should have been - but the veggies and asian pear were great, brown rice at no extra charge.  But what brought my 3 star lunch (take out) up to 4 stars was the amazingly fresh (still warm) tamago.    For $2.00 - you bet I'll be back for more "egg cake".  P.S.  Bring back the Galbi Box!!!!

Very disappointed.  Came back to Pure Fare after being away for a couple of years. My kid ordered a $7 Strawberry Banana Smoothie (Strawberries, 1 Banana and Ice for $7!!!!  Highway robbery) and the cup was not even all the way full.  Not comin' back.  Used to love it here.  So sad.

Had a wonderful lunch for 4 adults plus my 9 year old. Excellent lunch specials (Chinese) and sushi, especially the "Flamingo Roll"  ($15 - ouch) with Mango, Avocado & Salmon over a shrimp tempura roll.  Wild salmon Nigiri ($3.50 for one piece) was heavenly. Hamachi nigiri ($3.00) was very good also.  Great lunchtime service and bill was around $80.00 (no alcohol, no dessert ordered).

The four of us (my 9 year old, her 8 year old BFF and the friend's mom) stopped in and found all sorts of giftable goodies - so we got a balloon animal kit and a paper doll book of "Boo" the world's cutest dog.  What a fun place! Great for giftables.

The fish is indeed, always, always fresh and delicious.  The prices are very high - and the preparation is old-school (no creamy crunchy over-suaced Americano rolls here!).  If you want quality fresh fish - this is a good place to get it.    Genji has been around for-ever - I went to the old University City location back in 1991-1993 before the owner (killed himself?) died.  The present location on Sansom is the "new place" - and it, too has been here for-eh-ver.  Meanwhile - service.  If you are a regular (which I am, sadly, not) you will be treated well.  If, like me, you fly solo and sit at the bar - you may well be ignored.    I favor Shiroi Hana these days which has both old-school hand-rolls and nigiri as well as a few "new-fangled" gourmet-rolls.  But Genji is a great placed for the sushi loving purist who seeks a wide variety of fish.  They had the most delicious Madai (Japanese Pink Snapper) and Kanpachi (baby yellowtail).  A good safe (fresh=safe) bet.

I came here yesterday early in the AM expecting to meet a friend at Pumpkin Cafe - but they don;t open until 10 or 11, so I got a FABULOUS fresh-juiced, juice of ABC (Apple, Beet, Celery) plus parsley and a bit of ginger.  $4.75 (ouch) but worth it.  The banana was .50 cents.  They also have delectable Almond Croissants from Metropolitan Bakery, Fresh Duck eggs for a buck each, frozen locally sourced meats and lots of great goodies.  The lady at the front counter/barrista is a doll!  NICE!

3.5 stars really.  Day by Day has been a reliable lunch spot and catering go-to place for me and many people at my firm.  The fried chicke toss salad is delicious and they serve a "safe" selection of sandwiches.  In the summer-  the gazpacho is a refreshing and tasty choice.  The specials of the sday - often fish and omelettes are also really, really great.  They often sell out of the fish special - so come early for your lunch.  They don't do dinners - although last summer they briefly toyed with a "dessert cafe" concept which I wish had fared better.  Anyhow - it's a great place to grab a safe, reliable lunch.

We were stuck at Jefferson for 4 hours and needed a place to go to have a cappucino and kill some time.  Friendly staff - decently clean bathrooms, good coffee (I had an iced coffee, Mom had a capp.)  Not great but not awful.

Ooh!  I can't believe I forgot to Yelp Rose Tattoo.  It's an easy walk from my apartment so we've been there numerous times in the past 3 years.  Took my parents there, too and they enjoyed the meat dishes and tasty salads.  There are several dining rooms, but I love the bar which is canopied by green plants and flowers.  (There are 2 bar areas - maybe 3.)  From the outside RTC looks kinda like a biker bar - and it always looks closed.  It's not.  Inside - wherever you sit - you'll get great food and lots of drink options. We really love the desserts.  White Chocolate 7 Strawberry bread pudding was a delicious special one night.  Really.  Try the desserts. Sometimes I just get an appetizer and a dessert and I am FINE with that.  Can't wait to go back.

Wow - am I ever glad I finally got a chance to eat here.  It is MUCh better than Miran.  (Sorry, Miran.)  I got a Galbi for dinner and upgraded (for $1.00) to the multigrain rice - which I am so glad I did.  The rice and grains were so healthy-tasty.  The Galbi was "textbook perfect" with a delicious BBQ flavor and just the right amount of fat. (Not greasy - but tasty and beefy.)  The side dishes of Kimchi and Sweet Yellow Soy beans were also "textbook perfect".  The Gabli and rice came with a mixed green salad dressed lightly in a soy dressing - fresh and good.  Also steamed carrots - naturally sweet and a few YUMMY edamame.  What a great meal.  Can't wait to come back again.  (Wanna get a Dolsot Bibimbop next time.)  Oh, and the man behind the counter (who I am guessing is the manager and possibly the owner) was very nice.  It's counter service, but he was so friendly to me. (It was not busy when I came.)  Also the clean bathrooms have really cool tiles.  BONUS!

Pure Fare, in theory, is my kinda place.  Fresh, natural, often organic ingredients.  Blue Bottle Coffee.  Fresh Juices (I got the Green - and it was awesome!).  Prices run high, but the food is very fresh and good.  I did not like that the sandwiches were premade (I wanted to get one with no onion.).  Lunch was $15.12 for a salad and a juice.  Man!!!!
We donate gently used baby and toddler clothing and toys to NOVA and the work they do is so valuable.  Great for donors and customers alike.

We had a nice Saturday lunch here - and believe it or not - it was good and not too crowded when we came.  Now you can't compare this to Xochitl or Tequila's in Center City - but it ain't no Qdoba neither.  This is a middle of the roadMexican party-house with a good pre-mix margarita, fresh chips and tasty pico (salsa??).  We enjoyed our enchildas, thank you very much.

Just ok. Service is spotty, food is hit or miss (decent but greasy beef fajitas, dry plantains and just-right black beans).  Meanwhile - a good place for a blackberry margarita (the classic one was a bit tart for me) or mojito (better).  Wish the food were better - especially for the price point.

Stopped in today for "Linner" (We wanted to try Temaki but they close from 2-5.  DRAT!) with my 8 year old.  Service was cold as ice at first (maybe they were leery of the kid, but they warmed up.  They tried to seat us in the back (so dark back there) but we asked to be closer to the windows and they obliged.  Linner for 2 cost $50 with tax and tip - small plates.  1 cup of hot & sour (very good) for me, edamame (Huge portion for $4) for sharing, Shrimp Shumai (just Meh - 5 tiny pre-frozen ones) for the 8 year old (She likes Doma''s better - she's a shumai connoisseur), "meh" sushi appetizer (came with Cali roll and I never would gotten it had I known that - I was expecting all nigiri).  We also got VERY delicious seafood and spinach dumplings - these are a MUST try if you like fish (and an avoid if you don't).  The hand-made pasta/dumpling skin was light and pan fried on one side.  PERFECT.  Agedashi tofu was a bit soggy - but the dashi was delightful. That said, I WOULD get it again as I love fried tofu.  We'll be back - but I sure wish folks would give me and my kiddo the benefit of the doubt.  She's a well behaved kid and not at all bratty. And she knows her food!  Meanwhile - skip the sushi here - but I can't wait to try the Moo Shu Chicken here.  Their Chinese dishes are great,

There are 3 - yes THREE Auntie Anne's in 30th Street Station. The "main one" where they can bake pretzels is larger and back by the bar abd Surf City Squeeze.  There is a kiosk (they cart the pretzels over) on the concorse floor (near Amtrak) and another small store near the SEPTA area.  Like obese Philadelphians really need 3 of these?  Anyhow - it's not good for you - and while a hot cinnamon sugar pretzel (especially fresh and hot) tastes good to me, I nearly always feel ill afterward and regret the 470 cals.  Skip it.  Get some fruit or hummus from Old Nelson's. Or better yet - leave the building and go get "real" food.

I am going to be generous and give Tony A.s 4 stars (they may only deserve 3) as related to the DELIVERY ORDER we had for a large catered party (25 people) tonight.  Our group of professionals met at a nearby office complex so we needed a place that could deliver and provide a low cost alternative to Pizza.  We ordered a large hoagie tray (2 large platters) with Italian hoagies and Turkey & Provolone (no onions) with oil & mayo on the side.  Also we had 1 tray of wraps, vegetarian (GREAT - full of spinach, eggplant, peppers etc.) and Chicken Caesar wraps.  Additionally there was a large bowl of romaine salad with tomato, cucumber, sliced bolied eggs and sides of 2 dressings.  The pasta salad was not great - overly dressed in a vinegary dressing.  Yuck.  The dessert tray of brownies and cookies (Sugar, Chocolate Chip and White Chunk macadamia) were very yummy.  All in all a great experience.  Everything arrived on time and as we specified.  I can not speak for the ambience of the dining room as I ahve never set foot in the place.

I have actually eaten here.  Yes.  Gasp.  So shocking - seeing as I usually don't even consider fast food - but I have a weakness.  Every once in a business-trippy-blue moon, I grab an egg McMuffin here on my way to catch the AMTRAK train.  300 calories. $2.99 (sometimes they have a buy 2 for $3 deal - but who can eat 2 of them?)  Egg Mc Muff.  What evs,  Oh - and believe it or not the Muslim ladies who run the place (at least on the morning weekday shift) are pretty darned pleasant. I was so shocked!

Yick.  First of all -it's take out only.  There are (maybe) 2 card tables on which to eat.  Mediocre pizza and OK hoagies.  If you work at the Mercer Museum or nearby, this is a decent enough lunch spot, but for "hoity-toity" Doylestowners there are much nicer choices.

A stronger 3 star update based on ANOTHER large group function that we had in the upstairs party space.  Food was much better and much more abundant this time.  We also had an open bar with beer, wine and well drinks.  We had about 70 people this time and the atmosphere was more relaxed.  Thank you to Ladder 15 for accomodating our group. The butternut squash dip was delicious and the Kim-chee Shortrib tacos were a unique twist.  The ubiquitous (and inexpensive) soft pretzel nuggets and odd quesadillas (what the heck is in those things??) were ever-present.  Getting better. Kick it up a notch and put out SIGNS for the food items and maybe you'll get to 4 stars.

I used the Edible Arrangements location in Commack NY.  I can't find a listing for it.  I will write a complete review when i know where to put it.  Note:  You can also order from FruitFlowers.com - a DIFFERENT company called Incredibly Edible Delights.  Both companies are great.

Stopped in here for a quick cafe au lait ($1.75) just before the yelpy awards. Staff was a bit "snotty" - but not horribly so.  Coffee was perfect - so delicious - I love La Colombe and they even did our wedding favors for us back in 2008.  This branch is in a great location - right near city hall - and offers some respite from the high traffic area. Clean, wood seating, wood floors.  Very chic looking.  Oh - and no splenda (tons of other sweetners thought). And - as per usual - no menus so just order what you want (Latte, double macchiato, whatev...)  That's a bit uppity to me - but that's La Colombe.  Uppity coffee to get you UP!

This place gets 5 stars when it doesn't deserve it for Big Sue and Mountain John.  I cut my teeth at Juan y Pedro's and for me, it feels like home.  I knew Big Jen Ran when she tended bar here - and saw many great Dead-COver bands and jam bands and all kinds of great musical acts here.  A great, great, great place.  Even better in the dead of winter when the tourists have all gone away.

I always go to the Aveda store in Liberty Place to redeem my aveda coupons - for free samples or products on my birthday.  Service is very (sometimes overly) attentive - and I usually feel guilty if I don;t spend money that day.  I like the new GreenScience skin care line very much.  Not as fond of the hair care.

When they're hot - they are just heavenly - especially the White Chunk Macadamia - but DAMN they are expensive.  (And way too caloric for me to indulge in regularly.)  If you time it right you can get a free sample - which is just a bite or two and can be just enough to prevent you from buying and eating a whole one.  The buy 3 get the 4th free is a standard "special" - so that's really not so special after all.

Hooray!  The Thai Chef folks that I loved so well on Chestnut Street have an outpost in a stripmall in Glen Mills.  The Tom Kha is terrific - with a bowl of light jasmine rice, it's a meal in itself.  So glad to have found themand can't wait to return.
Support the independent pharmacies before they all disappear! Pickwick has a great selection of cosmetics, too - like OPI and Essie nail polishes.  Glad they are still here.

I stopped in (and got out quickly) for a much needed Blu-Ray player for a holiday gift.  Because I was shopping so early I was/am concerned about not being able to return it if the recipient did not like it but they have assured me (as writted a note on my account) that a post-Xmas return is fine.  Meanwhile, at first I did not see all the models of Blu Ray players - and the one I wanted appeared to be out of stock - but the sales associate brought one out from the back.  So far, so good - but I have not bought any "big-ticket" items here yet.

The food here is just awful.  My (now) 11 year old, however loves the $2.99 bubble tea - and until we can find another place to get bubble tea (she is partial to honeydew) we get it here.  The young lads running the front counter are always kind to us. Wish the food were better. I do not and will not eat here.

We had a private event for about 20-22 diners in the back room at Effie's and it was handled beautifully.  We had many vegetarian restrictions so the following dishes were served, family style:  Spanikopita (delicious!) Tyropita A large mixed plate with hummus, baba, feta, olives, peppers and dolmades (awesome domlades by the way) Chopped Cucumbers & Tomatoes in oil & vinegar Penne with Onions, Kalamata Olives and Onion in tomato sauce.  The food was wonderful and the 2 ladies serving worked their butts off.  Wer had an amazingly good time. (And the good weather helped.)  The outdoor courtyward is a fun place to eat as well.  I can't wait to come back and have some lamb chops!  Great job, Effie's!

I come here when I just GOTTA get my galbi fix - the meat is so delicious and the pan jan - while small - is always tasty.  I had diced pickled turnips, bean sprouts and kimchee that day.  I love the multigrain rice, too - $1.25 extra but worth it for me.
Sooooo dirty.  Eew!

Not a great Shoprite - but a little better than the one near the Target. NO customer service at all - and lines were pretty long on the (Saturday - duh) day we were there.  We go to the (also yucky) SuperFresh on Columbus for our bi-monthly shopping trips and supplement with Farmer's Market Fruit & Veggies (in spring/summer) and Whole Foods or Trader Joe's for other things.  Oh - and Target.  We're there a few times a month also.  Pro:  This shoprite has a BIG parking lot and we found a space easily - even though the store was busy and lines were long.  (Hey - open an extre couple of registers on the weekends, OK?)

Since I now work nearby and there is not much in the way of choices, I walked in to Alessandro's for lunch today.  It was about 12:45 and crowded but not mobbed.  A nice lady named Christina took my order for a Chicken Gyro - no onions - and a drink to stay.  The total was just under $8.00.  My gyro came out (they announce orders over a microphone) in about 6 minutes and was hot and fresh - and loaded with sliced chicken breast.  Tables were clean and new looking.  Pizza slices (under a glass display) did not appeal to me, so I can't comment on their pizza yet - but for a quick gyro lunch - this was just fine.  I will porbably be back once I have tried out all the local lunch spots.

Starting to use this CVS more & more due to it being next to Chick-Fil-A and having a kid.  No issues and stays open a bit later than the Aston one.  The parking lot is a bit tricky so be careful leaving.  (Getting in is no big deal.)

Auntie Annes' is the McDonalds of the soft pretzel.  High in sodium, fat and carbs (unless you skip the butter dip) they are tasty when hot & fresh.  They also have very sweet lemonade that, alas, my 4 year old loves and is almost never allowed to drink.  Once in a while, OK - but don't make it a habit!

Absolutely horrendous service. My husband, 7 year old and I stopped in for an early (5:45 ish) dinner on a Sunday.  Only a few tables occupied and 3 staffers seated in the back corner. Several minutes passed before the cold, bitter hostess reluctantly got up to seat us.  Even my kid asked "Are we supposed to seat ourselves?".  We were given a table way in the back near the kitchen and eventually asked to be moved due to the loud banging and pounding (we could hear every aspect of the food prep.)  Meanwhile the food, once it arrived was surprisingly good - 4 star even - but due to the awful experience we won't be back - at least not for a long while. The rosa sauce is great, but I can get it other places where the servers are kind and attentive.

Ok, here's the deal.  If you're going on somebody else's dime - do it!  It is really high-priced for faux-pub - but I gotta say they do a few things there really, really well.  For instance, one of my dining companions is from England and ordered a Bomdardier which he said was well poured and not "too fizzy".  It was however, served much cooler than you'd get back home.  My entree of Hake was delicious served in a buttery lemon caper sauce over a small bed-ette (to small to call it a bed) of kale.  Not dry - in fact it leaned toward the underdone side - and thus was tender and large-flaky. I also enjoyed the cold poached shrimp (5 for $14 - large ones) with lemon mayo & cocktail sauce.  Simple - but so tasty!  Desserts are not a strong suit save for the hot chocolate pot. (worth the 15 minute wait - order this with dinner if you are in a rush). Skip the Eton Mess unless you like TART fruit.  My decaf cappucino (not listed on the menu - but ask and ye shall receive) was EXCELLENT.  Try a Pimms Deluxe (or a classic Pimms cup) for a refreshing treat. Oh - and they have (for $5.50 each - OUCH) fancy-schmancy organic bottled sodas from the UK - I had a Luscombe's Sicilian Lemonade that was great and worth the 134 calories of sugar-water.  (THat's ORGANIC sugar water to you!).  And they carry Ribena (a blast from the past!).  I may be back - but for the price point, I'll be waiting a while. Oh - and I won't be missing Mantra!

A lovely - and brand-spankin'-new cafe at Sister Cities Park. Not cheap - but on par for Center City - and greatly needed.  Please put in another register and speed up your lunch-time service.  You're really on to something here. Delicious coffee drinks.  Quiche.  Sandwiches. (Great ice pops, too!)

The service here is excellent. The parking is still pretty awful - and now there is a "Super" Wawa next door. Nonetheless, I still come in every month or so for a $5 latte. I love it, it's expensive, I feel guilty when I do it - but I gotta have a starbucks fix every once in a while.
Yuck.  I don't really like fast food anyway - and Wendy's is barely tolerable, but this location (a busy one due to location for sure) is pretty awful.  Not a good choice.

You're kidding right?  This Au Bon Pain should probably get 1 star due to the vermin infestation.  But anyway - the over priced, high calorie sandwiches & soups are a godsend when it is raining and I am too lazy to leave my office building, but other than that?  I am so over au bon pain.

Cedar Beauty Supply has an enormous selection of hair products (Weaves, Wigs, Hair, Accessories).  It does have a bit of a "'hood" feel to it and the lady who runs the salon next door seems to know alot about wigs and weaves.  I picked up a $4.99 styforfoam wig head for my teen daughter's project. Also notices a bunch of VERY cheap pantyhose in the back ($1.39 per pair?  Whoa!)   So I got one and, as predicted, it ran/ripped less than an hour after I put them on.  Disposable hose.  Anyhow - I did not like the vibe here but I would come back if in the neighborhood and needed a specific item.  They have a small selection of MorrocanOil products in a locked glass case.

I wish I could give them higher marks, but the reviews here are pretty much right on.  This place is in between Meh and A-OK.  I will be kind and give them 3 stars - but the food is 2 stars at best.  Service was fine - although they screwed up my DH's steak burrito (He wanted cheese and jalapenos - both are an extra charge - they brought out a plain burrito.) It also ticks me off that for tacos and burritos - EVERYTHING (even pico) is an up-charge.  For $9 - 12 (base price of burritos) you'd think they'd allow you some salsa and cheese.  TICKS ME OFF.  Also the salsa they serve with the chips tasted likeywatery ketchup-y shir-acha-ish sauce.  (The cholula on the table was better.) Chips were fresh and fine.  Shrimp Ceviche was good - but not nearly close to the best I've had.  Jicama atop the ceviche had turned brown and was likely prepped hours before.  FAIL.  Side of Platanos were a bit woody-potato-ey (I like Maduros - nice and sweet - and I had JUST had the plantains at Distrto last week.  Distrito kick this places ar$e.)  So - will I be back?  I won't say never, but I certainly would not rush back here. I plan to try the other MEH-diocre Mexican in Media (M, M, M - I think I'ma gonna make new list) first.  PROS:  Cute place, Menu reads well, Good Service, OPEN SUNDAYS, Happy Hour is a GREAT value for margarita's and $2.50 STELLA ARTOIS!  CONS:  Mediocre food, upcharges for EVERYTHING on the taco/burrito menu, lousy salsa. No reservations unless party is 6 or more.  Please, Diego's - step up your game!

Buddy's is getting better and better. They have great looking salads now - and the sauteed shrooms & spinach (FREE) are blissful on top of a burger or grilled Chicken.  Service (you place and order and pick it up - but they usually will bring it out to you) is great and friendly.  We are having our future class dinner here next time! 3rd graders love it. (Especially that snazzy Coke freestyle machine.)

Ook!  I had a horrible ordeal here - albeit years ago - in the emergency room.  I was left waiting in a triage room for HOURS & HOURS because they could not decide whether or not to admit me.  They eventually decided not to admit me and let me out at about 3 AM in West Philly with no cab fare and I was scared to death.  Thank god a local cop drove me home.   Meanwhile the doctors & nurses there seemed very confused and did not display good judgement in my treatment.  I was in need of care and they failed me.  Very, very disappointing.

We went to Rose Tattoo AGAIN last night and man, was it ever good. But the BEST part was dessert.  (They are now $8.50 a pop - but easily split by 2 people.)  Try the Paris Brest (yes, that's what the call it "BREST").  It's a puff pastry (very buttery - almost tastes fried but is baked.) split in half and filled with not-too-sweet whipped cream, home-made chocolate mousse and sliced straberries (no red gelatinous glop - thank god!).)  The whole thing is topped with a chocolate covered strawberry and served with a scoop of strawberry sorbet and garnished with chocolate and strawberry sauces on the plate.  SKIP DINNER - EAT DESSERT.  (Or order apps or sides - the side of Gnocchi is generous for $7.00)  LOVE THIS PLACE even more now.

We ate here last night and normally, I am not a fan of chains - and the RT in Liberty Place is awful - but - and here's the BIG but...  We had an excellent meal and great service.  I had the (fresh, and many choices) salad bar and a side of lobster mac 'n cheese.  The menu seems to have been upgraded.  FIL had a gorgeous and huge burger - so big he took half home. MIL had a steak & lobster dinner (2 tiny tails - but buttery and cooked nicely). DH enjoyed the pasta carbonara but I tasted it and did not like the overly salty-smoky flavor.  Meanwhile - we had a great time and believe it or not, I would go back again.  Soon.

First of all, I don't even LIKE sports - but this has got to be the NICEST sporting goods store I had ever seen - or set foot in.  A huge selection of baseball bats, gloves, balls, basketball gear - you name it.  Got a sports fan who needs higher end gear?  Go here.  And the guys who work here are so helpful and nice.  A great, surprising find - in downtown Wilmington.
GORGEOUS - plus great products and top-of-the-line services. Terrific!  (Expensive - yes - but appropriate for this "upscale" area).

A neccessary Evil - glad it's here.  "Makes life in suburbia bearable" (to coin a phrase from below.  Just wish there was a La Colombe out this way - at at least a hipster mom 'n pop coffee shop.  Go, Media!

5 star service from Jo Jo on a busy summer night - the place was hoppin'.  We needed to get in and out quickly and Jo Jo helped us do just that.  Pan-seared rainbow trout ($20) is always good for me and my husband enjoyed a southwestern chicken salad.  Nice place and very reliable.

OK - I dare not tell you when I used to walk "up town" to Nat's - because then you will know that I am older than Pink.  Hell - I coulda baby sat for little Alicia Moore and her brother - but I digress..  Nat's has been a D-town staple.  For years. Generation after generation of Jr. and Sr. High schoolers congragate here after football games and dances to have a (greasy) slice or a "wooder" ice in the summer.  I always liked Capri's Pizza better - but Nat's Sicilian pie is still a cheesy baseline for me to this day.  God bless 'em.  They're still here.
We adopted a 2 year old mixed breed female. Jury is still out but so far so good.
A nice neighborhood market with cigs, bottled water and some good gourmet items.  Staff seems pleasant and prices are high but not crazy.  We need more markets like this in Philly.

4 star food - Excellent and not too greasy. However the icy service I received knocked them down to 3 stars.  I walked in on a Thursday night at around 8:25 PM.  It turns out they close at 9 Anyhow the place was dead-empty - nobody dining in but me and the only other person who came in was a local cop for take out (good sign).  The lady folding napkins when I arrived seemed genuinely miffed that I dained to eat dinner.  Anyhow - I was able to elicit a smile by the end of the night. I ordered Chicken with Broccoli ($9.0) and brown rice (no extra charge - nice!).  I asked for it "light on the sauce, dry" and thus - it was perfect.  Fresh crunchy broccoli that nearly tasted sweet when I bit into it and lots of slices (not slivers) of tender whit meat chicken.  I will return - maybe next time she'll WANT to see me.  Oh and the teapots and silverware were very clean.  As Dan H. mentioned there is a $5 per person lunch, $8.00 per person dinner minimum.

I have lived in the Pacakrd Building for 4 years now - and while the rents continue to rise & rise, the building is still good for us.  Convenient Center City location.  Parking available in a covered lot.  We wish they'd replace the 22 year old washer dryer in my apartment though.  We asked & ask and they claimn that even a new unit will still be the same motor.  It takes FOREVER to dry clothes and is a waste of electricity.  The entire building is 100% electric - so there's no gas bill - but the electric bills for heat and a/c - especially with our 15 foot ceilings (a plus and also a minus) - the bills are SKY HIGH.  (Pun intended.)  Some of the front desk staff are lazy - but most are very nice and willing to help you with dry-cleaning and packages.  Rita is the nicest of the bunch.  It's a gorgeous apartment for a luxury price.  Smack dab in the middle - of NOTHING.  (Broad Street bet. Vine & Callowhill).  There is "The Sunday Breakfast Club" aka homeless shelter 1/2 a block away so there are quite a few unsavory goings-on in the alley next to the building.  AND little police patrol.  Once we get home after work - we stay there!!!

DELIVERY REVIEW ONLY - never ate in the restaurant. Super-speedy delivery ($1.25 charge, $10 minimum) which is 5 star - but the quality, as I feared, is not superb.  Maybe I am just spoiled by Vic's and Doma.  That said I am so glad there is finally a non-pizza, non-Chinese place in the area. We got a yellowtail scallion roll, yellowtail nigiri (not great), spicy crunchy salmon roll (also not so great - not terribly spicy),  TheCrazy Tuna roll was impressiv looking ($11.95)but the tuna on top was not that good either.  I dunno.  Not impressed, but it's not bad.  Nothing was spoiled - just not "uber" fresh. Lady on the phone was nice, delivery guy was great.  (They said 40 minutes on a Friday night and showed up in 20.  Sweet!)  Update:  It is the next day.  I got food poisoning from the sushi. Yup.  I spent last night vomiting.  Not fun.  Nevery again.

PureBread is a great lunch option.  They used to offer a full coffee/espresso bar but they don;t anymore.  So, mostly I go for soups (the mushroom bisque and lobster bisque are delicious but caloric) and salads (I like the Cobb).  All the menu items are named after dog breeds and there is dog related decor and monitors with local dogs.  I love dogs so this is great for me.  A great choice in Glen Mills near tons of shopping.

This is my 2nd attempt at China Aston Inn - this time I placed a $40 take out order (I did not call it in - just sat and waited for it - took about 12 minutes).  When I arrived on a Monday night at 5:40 PM - again - the place was EMPTY. So empty that there was no staff - so I said "Hello?  Anybody Here?" a couple of times and finally a lady came out and took my order. She seems a bit pissed off at first and I wonder if it was the same woman from before.  This time I was able to soften her up a bit.  The food itself was fresh and hot when i got it home - chicken with String Beans and wonton soup were good.  Other dishes - not great - the Kung Pao was loaded to excess with water chestnuts and mushrooms.  Hardly any peanuts - and not very spicy even though we wanted spicy and asked for it that way.  Orange Beef was better - that one we asked for mild so our 9 year old could eat it - and she liked it.  (Fried, dark meat chicken chunks).  Not a holy grail - but a change-up from our usual Chinese place.  The place is always deserted - and maybe the odd service vibe and mediocre food is why?

A strong 3 - maybe even a 4 - for the expertise of Laura who help me to plan a small happy hour event for my office.  We enjoyed the Raspberry Wheat beer (3.50 is a decent price for it) and other drinks.  We also tried the salmon spring rolls (excellent) cheese-steak eggrolls (good not great) and southwestern springrolls (my husband liked these).  In addition the Hawaiian Pizza was very tasty - and the crust was freshly baked.  I also tried the Ale & Onion soup which tasted good, but was very, very oily - almost greasy from the oils in the cheese.  Eew.  It was OK as "french"-style onion soup goes but I have had better (and I have had worse.).  The place is MASSIVE - a great idea for private parties -especially on a night when you can enjoy the deck.  The best part of the night?  Meeting fellow yelpers Jessica E. and Chris from Delaware!  Thanks for coming out!

It's huge.  Between the Court & The Plaza you can literally get everything here- if you don't mind paying retail.    I usually eat at Ruby's with a girlfriend and then hit New York & Company.  (See my other reviews.)  Avoid at holiday time - it's a giant parking-lot filled with chaos and annoyance.  If you are a teenager - this place is 4 - 5 stars but I am officially a grown up now - so 3 stars from me!!!

Audrey Claire is weird.  I wanted to like it.  I wanted to love it - but it was only "meh". The homey wood-tabled decor was nice - but the acoustics were awful.  So loud.  The white-aproned staff was kinda snotty - especially when we asked alot of questions - which we always do.  The food was just OK.  The standout being a plate of whole grilled artichokes that we had for an appetizer - but for the 7-8 bucks - I coulda done that myself.  The food is very elemental here - simplistic.  Not Horrible (in fact a 3 or even 4 stars for food) but as a total dining experience?  I probably won't be back.  And its a BYO.  So bring something - - you'll need it.  Oh - and bring cash - no credit cards.  Whatever.

This Wawa, we affectionately refer to as the "magic" Wawa as it is about 1/2-way between my home in Media, and a friend's home "out west".  It's got gas, food/beverages, a rest room and plenty of parking. Everything we need to meet up 1/2-way and transfer our kids, sporting gear and other stuff from one friend's house to another.  Hooray for the "magic" Wawa!

Came here on the strong recommendation of a friend that their Sicilian Pie (or Tomato Pie) when baked fresh is some of the best. ever.  I agree - gives Corropolese a run for their money.  Meanwhile, today I tried a panini (on an enormous Ciabatta loaf) with pork, sharp provolone and broccoli rabe.  Asked for a bit of sauce on it - PERFECT.  This is amazing.  My friend had a small (still plenty) sausage and pepper sandwich/sub/hoagie and it was old-school and very tasty according to her.  Jeanne-Marie (sp?) our server was friendly and wonderful but way overworked - she was serving 2 full dining rooms at the lunch rush by herself.  Ouch.  Nice place for a casual red-sauce Italian meal.  Can't wait to come back and try a pasta dish. Molto bene!

Lunch with a party of 5 (co-workers) and while a bit pricey it was perfect for a business-casual lunch. Service was fine - our male server (Mike??) was on point with drink refills and bringing the check (it was quite busy on a rainy Thursday from 12:15 - 1:30 ish). Restroom was clean and comfortable.  Decor is very nice.  My only complaint?  The chicken tostada was fried - as in battered and fried and dripping in grease.  Next time (if I get that item) I will ask if they can do it with grilled chicken.  Steamed spinach (by request) was perfect and I am glad I asked because one colleague's meal came with sauteed spinach which he said was loaded with salt and oil.  Please folks, ease up on the fatty foods and we will return much more quickly.  Thanks!

I stopped in here on a whim - when I noticed the HUGE Grand Opening Sign (They just opened in Nov. 2012). Place is brand-spankin' new - and all the staff used to work at the now closed salon in the Springfield Mall.  For $12 (plus $5 for 2 designs) I got a very good mani by Jenny. For the Grand Opening I was charged $15 total. Cindy - the manager/type (senior technician??) was friendly and offered me green tea or wine.  I have since been back to see Jenny (she is great) for 2 more gel manis.  They have 8 brand-new sparkling clean pedicure thrones. (And 8 mani stations) Meanwhile the place was empty on a Wednesday Morning.  A hot stone pedi is normally $30 - but I will go back before 12/31 to get the $35 mani/hot stone pedi special.  Can't wait to try it again - and it's new, so it's clean. Give me 6 - 9 months and I will re-review.  SO many Nail Joints start out great and then decline.  Please - keep it nice and I'll be back!!! We need more NICE nail salons in Media.

My 6.5 year old kid and I popped in here on a dead Monday at about 5 PM.  Thankfully the place was nearly empty.  There are signs everywhere clearly stating their "Pizza Nazi" policies like, NO TOPPINGS, Cash Only, No restrooms and best opf all - box $0.25!  Wow.  I especially remember the sign "The customer is always WRONG".  Meanwhile the tatted-up, nose-ringed gal behind the counter was sweet as could be to my little one - who was the reason we got a $2.75 Ginormous piece of "Lorenzo's Oil" (Remember that movie?  They named it so for the pizza grease!).  She ate it at Supercuts next door.  She enoyed the pizza but said, "Mommy, it's not as good as the place I go to in Brooklyn!".  Out of the mouths of babes.

This is a review for the Bacco (new location) in the Doylestown shopping Center.  The food is excellent and the poritons are enormous.  Prices are moderate (about 13 for entrees).  But it took forever to:  1.  be greeted 2.  be seated (we wound up seating ourselves) 3.  get menus 4.  have someone wait on us 5.  get our food (cooked to order so that was OK) 6.  get our bill  It was like pulling teeth getting service - and the place was not busy.  Our party of 4 ordered Pasta fagiole soup (huge bowl for $3.95), linguini with (REAL) clams - so good, Chicken parm (served with a delicious side of mezza-rigatti pasta in a crushed tomato sauce), and I had the Chicken florentine.  It was terrific.  We'd like to go back but only if we have lots of time to wait around (for the servers) and thus I would never bring my little kid here.

Had another massage with Mindy and she is terrific. I love her - and hope she'll stick around for a while.  Billie Jo - the WONDERFUL esthetician and Celeste (Front Office) are great, too. I am having a facial with Billie Jo in a few weeks.    I am very pleased with my Massage envy membership - but I do wish and hope that they can keep the "good" therapists longer.  They work very hard.

Not bad.  I have only had a basic mani here - still too scared to risk a pedi.  Most Philly nail salons are soooooo filthy.  It seemed pretty clean here.  Better than Gomo and waaaaaay better than City Nails (aka Sh&tty Nails).  Bring your wn base coat if you want something good - they used cheap base coat on me.  But they did have Seche Vite top coat - which I love.  And they had chair massage - it was pretty meh - but I needed it - however lame it may have been.

Really good - buttery - hand made Amish-Style pretzels.  Reminds me of when Auntie Anne's wasn't a chain - and really did have good pretzels.  These are so much better.  Get 'em while they're hot and eat them on the spot.  Carb-y goodness.  Little white head covering not included.

SUPER SLOW SERVICE. Decent food once you get it.  This is a review for the Bacco (new location) in the Doylestown shopping Center.  The food is excellent and the poritons are enormous.  Prices are moderate (about 13 for entrees).  But it took forever to:  1.  be greeted 2.  be seated (we wound up seating ourselves) 3.  get menus 4.  have someone wait on us 5.  get our food (cooked to order so that was OK) 6.  get our bill  It was like pulling teeth getting service - and the place was not busy.  Our party of 4 ordered Pasta fagiole soup (huge bowl for $3.95), linguini with (REAL) clams - so good, Chicken parm (served with a delicious side of mezza-rigatti pasta in a crushed tomato sauce), and I had the Chicken florentine.  It was terrific.  We'd like to go back but only if we have lots of time to wait around (for the servers) and thus I would never bring my little kid here.

Yum Yum is a small, local chainette of donut shops.  I am glad they are still around because, as a kid their donuts and fried delights - like apple fritters and bowties were kick-a$$.  Waaaaaay better than Dunkin'.  (Although Dunkin's cofee is better than yum yums.  A cop and fire fighter-haven, yum yum used to be open round the clock - or at least until midnight - and then they'd open at 5 AM to start the morning baking (or frying, as the case may be.)  I loved it there as a kid.  Can't afford the caloric intake nowadays.

Trendy Nails and the staff - Nancy. Lily, Mandy, Peter (Kevin? LOL), and especially Jen and Cyndi take such excellent care of me and my 10 year old daughter's nails.  They are always happy to see us and make us feel welcome.  Best of all the gel manicures and pedicure last a long, long time.  (Regular manicure are good too - but i am now a dedicated gel gal!)  We are so thankful to have found this salon.  Clean, comfortable and excellent service!

A bright, sunny shop with a nice selection of white, green, black, roiboos and herbal infusions. Excellent service and at least 3 or 4 free samples available each day.  Also a small selection of Cadbury confections, honeys and tea ware.  Lots of fun for the tea lover.

Need a bike or supplies/parts for one?  They've got it.  Nice Center City location, too.  We shopped here for a tandem stroller attachment (trailer) for our bike.  Ended up not buying one though - way too cost prohibitive.

I have only ever had take-out pizza from La Fourno - but it was GREAT (We got mushroom and plain cheese).  The owners are the best (LOVE THEM!) and are generous supporters of our child's school.  I don't even usually eat Pizza - but La Fourno's was really great.  (Traditional Neapolitan Style) Delish!  Can't wait to eat a full, REAL meal here.

I just was not thrilled with the food here.  Yes - it's a busy, Asia-inspired, zen ish decor - even the ladies room has been dollied up to the hilt.  (Maybe it's a little over the top, even??)  The food was just not good.  I had an average sushi roll app and an entree so unmemorable that I can't event tell you what it was.  We went for lunch and I will not go back.  There are way better places.  Maybe the drinks (which we did not have at lunch time) are why the high reviews?  The food was pretty lame.

Super yay!  Love the turkey burgers here.  They are NOT dry and so tasty.  I pass on the big bucket o' fries in favor of their YUM-CITY mac 'n cheese.  I order mine sans the tomato "jam" garnish.  They also have kickin' sides like greenbeans (crisp and studded with tomotoes) and sweet potatoes.  (Grilled with butter and cinnamon suger - like dessertm baby!).  It can get crowded and crazy - which is why it is not 5 stars -but the price is right and this spot ROCKS."

The Broad Street run goes right passed our apartment.  Kewl!  Great fun to watch but there's no way you'll see me running in it.  My body was simply not designed to move faster than 4.5 miles per hour.  Ah well, I can dream...  Go, dim sum!!!!
When they're hot - they're HOT - and sooooooo delectable when fresh out of the oven.  these pricey, large, thick, butter-laden cookies scream with flavor and taste sublime.  Oh, my hips!!!!

This Chik-Fil-A is just OK.  Not as good or well run as the stand-alone shops in the suburbs - but the service is quick - and my little one loves the Chik-Fil-A nuggets kids meal.  Chik-Fil-A is just about the only fast food I ever let her eat.  We are not proponents of it.  I enjoy the side salad (minus the cheese) and it comes with (fattening) tasty croutons and honey roasted sunflower seeds.  If you ate all the condiments and dressing Chik-Fil-A offers with the side salad - you can easily pack away 500 calories.  Sheesh.  So be careful out there folks - it's a nutritional mine field - but it's decent fast poultry.  And your kids will eat it. (Not sure how great of a thing that really is.)

So glad that Animo is still around and still delicious and a good source for a healthy meal.  The green Lemonade is still my fave - and I tried a Brisket and eggs breakfast bowl - made with love by Darnell (Yay Darnell!) that rocked my day!  Love it here and I keep coming back.  Even my vegan teen can find good choices here.  (They are not a vegan restaurant and serve cheese, eggs and meats).

Yes it was a mem'rie filled, exhausting all day (take a personal day) extravaganza for my 3 year old and husband & I.  Even on a random TUESDAy at 10 AM (when they open) the place is freakin' mobbed and highway robbery for the admission.  (Not to mention $15.00 ($18 for us - we sprung for "elite" parking) for parking and $15 to rent a locker - which was a much needed evil.  Long lines for every attraction.  Water rides were PACKED.  There is no shade.  ROASTING!  I told the toddler - as she sleepily collapsed into her car seat with visions of Elmo dancing thru her pretty little head that she best remember this happy day for the rest of her life, because Mama ain't NEVER comin' back.
Love it!  Wish it were bigger and more days - but I will take what I can get.  Support Philly's Farmer's Markets. Support Fair Food. Support Farm to City.  Join a CSA and patronize local farmers!

I had not been back in over 2 years - so 2 ladies from my office and I had lunch here.  Good but not great.  It also took a long time (15 -20 minutes) for the lunch to come out (nobody ordered apps nor drinks and we were on a strich time frame).  My fried-green-tomato blt was great!  But the side of green beans with tomatoes was nearly inedible.  I chose green beans as a healthy alternative to fries, but they came swimming in oil and loaded with a salty spice blend.  NOT what I was expected.  Next time I'll order them steamed or plain.  Also they gave each of us a $2.50 up charge for subbing a different side for fries.  Not the end of the world, but it would have been nice to know that before we ordered - and not as an added "bonus" when the bill came.  Meanwhile, I'll be back but I won't rush back. Years ago I loved it here - but over the years it seems less thrilling.

This is now my go-to 'Bux as I work at 18 & Market (I used to frequent the one at 20 & Market).  During the morning rush it gets absolutely mobbed - use the mobile ordering if you can and you can swoop in and out to get your over-priced #DiabetesInaCup.  Meanwhile, I treat myself to a latte about twice a week.  Trying to cut down but I love them.  I know people claim to not like Starbucks but the long lines here (quick moving) seem to indicate otherwise.  Gotta have my FiveBucks aka Charbucks!

This 4 star rating is based solely on the ONE item I ordered (to go). I got a Little Buddy (single patty) burger to go, on a busy "Dining under the Stars" Wednesday.  UPDATE:   We went back to Buddy's a few weeks later at my 9 year old's request. Chicken sandwich was good (fried) but Sweet potatoe Fries were soggy and studded with big crystals of salt.  The sweet fries at Front Street Fountain are way better.  (And the burgers here are better than Front Street).  The burger was cooked fresh and there were loads of free toppings to choose from. I got Lettuce, Tomato and sauteed 'shrooms.  (Garlicky - but not overly so and delicious). VERY good burger for the price.  Super fresh - served on a squishy seeded (Lots of sesame - so be aware) roll.  My 9 year old - who doesn't even drink or like soda - seemed obsessed with the Coca Cola freestlye console. She got an Orange/Vanilla Hi-C - talk about a sugar high!  Friendly young gals running the counter. Very good service. Especially Amanda - she is so kind to us and even gave my kid a plush toy when my kid did not win one from "Tha Claw" machine.  We'll be back - way better burger than Zac's! Next time I will skip the sweet potato fries (but maybe I'll try a milkshake).

I had wanted to try La Padella for months and finally got a chance to dine here.  It was worth the wait and I can't wait to return and sample more of their fabulous Italian menu.  The meatballs are large and very tasty. If you enjoy Brussels sprouts, don't miss the Brussels sprouts app - with lump crab meat and a rich remoulade. Super fattening and heavy, so share with friends.    Service from the amazing Laurie is top notch.  We love her.  Great food and even better service.

In general I really lurve Weggie's.  The bulk foods, the prepared foods, and the superb cheese section are stand outs for sure.  I wish there was/were one in Center City Philly and I would surely shop there.  we spend a little more when we come - not so much due to pricing (the prices are competitive for most items) but because we splurge on all sorts of specialty foods and unique items we just can't get at Is-It-Fresh (Superfresh) or Ack-A-Mee.  Go to Wegman's - but don't go if you're hungry and bring your shopping list so you don't impulse buy!

I love Whole Paycheck -and this location is no exception. The Taco Truck on the roof, the hot and cold food bars for a quick lunch option, and the ability to shop here at an off-peak time (parking is bad during the weekday lunch rush).  Plentiful seating options (2 floors) and enjoyable. Expensive - sure - but worth it to me.

This place is toooooo cute!  We came here twice - both times with our (then 2 no 3 year old) daughter.  The second time we came was for a kids music concert and it was way, way crowded - but such fun.  The food and coffee drinks are great and it's a cute place to hear live music.
This appears to be the Starbux inside the Target. They are remodeling the store and closed it down for a bit but are reopening any minute now.  No real issues here - but I come at "off" times.
Had a superb Chicken Cacciatore ($10) with orzo for lunch. As usual, friendly service and great food.  We love Day by Day!

Airport quality pIzza that capitalizes on the NYC Famous Famiglia name. Old dried old heat-lamped pies.  High prices.  Sub-par service.  One star is being generous.  But you are trapped in the terminal, so go to Chickie's & Pete's or Dump-kin or Mickey D's.  Just DON'T come here.

I am a Saladworks gal - but this location is just OK - I have seen better (and worse) in size, layout and cleanliness.  That said the ingredients are usually fresh enough - I had a spinach-based salad with shrimp & artichoke hearts.  $10 every time I go.  Super crowded during the weekday lunch rush - go before 11:40 AM or after 1:30 PM.
