Need a Mother-of-the (Bride, groom, Bat Mitzvah girl) dress?  Prom Dress?  Elegant suit to wear to a wedding?  Cocktail attire?  Penina and her daughter have what you need!  Great cusomer service and lots of sizes (from petite to "big gals").  We love Penina.

Ran in, got my Caudalie Eau de Raisin ($22 plus tax) and ran out. Had to BEG for samples - but eventually got a few.  Expensive, higher-end brands.  Glad they exist.  NARS concealer is $32 now.  Ouch.

Penzey's rocks my spice world. Yes, I am officially a spice girl.  Smarty Spice.  I love Sunny Paris Sunny Spain Shallots Shallot Salt Chives Turkish Seasoning Lamb Seasoning Chinese 5 Spice Powder Tellicherry Black Peppercorns Sarawak White Peppercorns Vanilla Sugar Double-Strength Vanilla Extract Parisienne Bonne Herbs Rosemary Garlic True Ceylon Cinnamon Penzey's Cinnamon Baking Spice Cake Spice Brady Street Cheese Sprinkle Minced Onion Toasted Onion Red Pepper Flakes Mural of Flavor  So much more.  I LOVE YOU, BILL PENZEY! Congratulations on 25 years of making food with love.

We had a very different experience from Mark J. below.  My husband ordered a whole small pie (baked fresh to order) - took over half of it home - of the "meat lovers" pizza - topped with ham, bacon, pepperoni, sausage and meatball slices.  (heart attack on a pie)  It definitely was not frozen.  I had a small veal parm sandwich light on the cheese.  The place was empty on a Tuesday night - and the pizza was good (not NYC quality - but HELLO - it's the PA suburbs) and the veal parm was on a great-tasting Italian roll.  No complaints here. And they deliver to Wallingford!

Go see Tina - she is so nice - and does fabulous HAND DRAWN nail art on my little girls nails.  I also had a spa pedicure (35 vs. 25 - and they throw in a wimpy massage - next time a regular pedi for me) and regular mani (13).  Tina is great!!!!  (She did not do my pedi - she does my kids nails)

Absolutely the best!  Went to another event (smaller) - also buffet style.  Perfectly cooked salmon, chicken (bones in and roasted to perfection), rare to medium sliced of beef roast.  Fried sweet potatoes to accompany the beef.  A delicious fresh cucumber salad and the best rosemary-scented polenta I have ever tasted.  Lynn is the BEST and her helpers are very kind, caring people.

La Maison has been a central-D-Town staple for generations.  It has also gone thru 2 possibly 3 ownership changes over the past 35 years. Meanwhile, they offer a nice variety of standard and rare domestic and imported cheeses, as well as pates, spreads, bread and cracker products and all the making for a good catering company.  You'll pay Doylestown prices - but they are nice ladies and run a good show.  Years back they'd bake their own croissants - especially on weekends. Not sure if that is still done - but the treats that came out of that oven were rich, buttery and blissful.  I wish them generations more of success!

Ah yes, the Dublin DQ - brings back pre-teen memories from the '80's.  And today the place has not changed all that much - still crammed in the summertime with fat, white mommas and their 2-3 kids in tow getting cones and such.  Cheap, soft-serve and mediocre fast food.  But when your 11?  It's a blast!

I stopped in for a quick polish change at 6:30 on a Monday (they apparently close at 7).  They tried to talk me into a mani ($13) and the polish change was $10.  The lady who did my nails (I honestly can't remember her name - she told me and I promtply forgot) seemed a bit disinterested and ready to call it a day.  Fortunately she did a decent job on the nails.  I also sprung for $15 (15 minutes) of chair massage.  It wasn't bad - not a "real" Licensed Masasge Therapy massage, but it was relaxing and I needed it.  I am hoping my polish lasts a long while.  I am only on day 2 so I will let y'all know.  Based on the other people's reviews I am not sure if I would gamble a pedicure here - but they do have about 5 pedi thrones and they looked "visually" clean.  The salon is big and has clean, wood floors.  A little more expensive than Nails by Chau or City Nails on the Square.  Oh - and the offer OPI Axxium gel nails.  Haven't had the courage to try this yet.  not sure how much they charge - and I won;t get them done here anyway when I do take the plunge.

I admire what Katie Cavuto is tyring to do here - especially in this area of the city. However, nothing really appealed to me other than the $2.25 bottles of hint water (which I bought immediately).  Couscous looked good - but too expensive. Love that they carry Griggstown Farm products.  Wish it looked more appealing. And was more affordable - but the prices reflect the organic and higher-priced ingredients.  $10 minimum for credit cards.

I am so NOT a fan of COsi.  After eating in the in NYC in the early 200's when this chain emerged - it seemed cool at first.  And - if the bread is fresh and hot (before it solidifies into cold cardboard) it actually tastes pretty good.  The hungrier you are the better it'll taste.  Meanwhile - the overpriced sandwich fillings are mediocre at best. There are better places to waste (I mean spend) my $7 bux.  Sorry.  Not a big fan.  If it's in 30th Street Station and I REALLY need food - I would eat here over McDonalds or Au Bon Pain - but that's really not saying much.

The Doylestown BK has been around for a long, long time - at least 32 years.  (The McDonald's up the road came first, though.)  As BKs go - and I am not a fan - this one is decent.  often tables and restrooms need more cleaning, though.  It's a reliable fast food option - though I loathe the stuff.

A strong 3 - maybe even a 4 - for the expertise of Laura who help me to plan a small happy hour event for my office.  We enjoyed the Raspberry Wheat beer (3.50 is a decent price for it) and other drinks.  We also tried the salmon spring rolls (excellent) cheese-steak eggrolls (good not great) and southwestern springrolls (my husband liked these).  In addition the Hawaiian Pizza was very tasty - and the crust was freshly baked.  I also tried the Ale & Onion soup which tasted good, but was very, very oily - almost greasy from the oils in the cheese.  Eew.  It was OK as "french"-style onion soup goes but I have had better (and I have had worse.).  The place is MASSIVE - a great idea for private parties -especially on a night when you can enjoy the deck.  The best part of the night?  Meeting fellow yelpers Jessica E. and Chris from Delaware!  Thanks for coming out!

I stopped in at Roller's during the Chestnut Hill Festival basically to get away from the street crowds and hopefully, to score a decent lunch.  Not so great.  The service was a bit familial and weird.  2 very nice ladies ran the "front of the house"  the server was nice - the manager (maybe owner?) not so friendly.  She was way more attentive to the couple to my left and the family to my right - but I guess since I was dining solo - maybe I wasn't worth it??  I asked if lunch was being served (it was 2 in the afternoon) but told olnly brunch and breakfast.  So I ordered a Turkey BLT on Le Bus multi grain toast (menu said 5.75 - was eventually charged 6.25) and the nice server lady said, "I'm not sure if we have lettuce.  I'll have to go check."  (I was like, "What?", but did not say anything.)  Turns out they DID have lettuce.  Maybe that's why they charged me more?  But it's a BLT.  The L supposedly stands for LETTUCE.  Oh well.  You can't win 'em all.  Meanwhile, I rested my weary self a while and escaped from the throngs of yuppies and suburbanites, and ate a tasty Turkey BLT.  With Lettuce.  Will I rush back here?  Likely not.  2-3 stars for food.  1-2 for service.  Oh - and bring cash - NO CREDIT CARDS

We drop lots of money at Target - and this is the first time we tried this one.  We sure came on a BAD day!  The center of the store was all roped off due to water damage - and there were water-pumps and fans humming loudly.  So we got what we needed (lots of paper goods and cleaning products) and left.  Yech.

This SMALL branch of Walgreen's is located across the street from Hahnemann Hospital and gets five stars because of one reason: Pharmacist Vince Meo.  No - you won't like the questionable clientele - but YES - you will love Vince Meo.    He cheerfully fills my prescriptions and has given me manyhelpful pieces of information over the years concerning pharmacology and which prescription drugs I need.  He even saved me time and money once, when I was very ill one winter.  Helen at the front counter is a doll and the people who work here are so nice.  Bring your insurance card - and be prepared to WAIT if its busy - but Vince - man, I love ya!

Got my hair and my MOH's hair and makeup done here for my June 2008 wedding.  Got a feeling the gal who did my hair is not there any more.  Prices were fair, and the ladies were very nice but NOT the most talented hairdressers.  In fact, the lady who did my trial did such a bad job I got a different person for the actual wedding day (who was much better.  They did do a better job on my friends hair and her makeup looked nice.  Going to a prom or wedding?  This is an OK choice.  But not mind blowing.  The also have nail services.

I have lived in the Pacakrd Building for 3 years now - and while the rents continue to rise & rise, the building is still terrific for us.  Great location and basically well run and well managed.  We wish they'd replace the 22 year old washer dryer in my apartment though.  It takes FOREVER to dry clothes and is a waste of electricity.  The entire building is 100% electric - so there's no gas bill - but the electric bills for heat and a/c - especially with out 15 foot ceilings (a plus and also a minus) - the bills are SKY HIGH.  (Pun intended.)  Some of the front desk staff are lazy - but most are very nice and willing to help you with dry-cleaning and packages.  It's a gorgeous apartment for a luxury price.  Smack dab in the middle - of NOTHING.  (Broad Street bet. Vine & Callowhill).  There is "The Sunday Breakfast Club" aka homeless shelter 1/2 a block away so there are quite a few unsavory goings-on in the alley next to the building.  AND little police patrol.  Once we get home after work - we stay there!!!

We went there last night - 4 of us, after tasting the fantastic timballe de scripelle (like an Abruzzi-style lasagna made of home-made parmesan crepes, with mini meatballs) at the SlowFood Philly event in HeadHouse square.  We ordered 3 apps & 4 entrees between us.  The breaded Olives - which we loved, the Riceballs - were Good but not WOW and a truly terrific tomato, fresh fior-de-latte mozzarella and grill artichoke salad.  It was so great.  Then the entrees came.  I had the Timballe, my husband had the home-made pasta (herbed pappardellle-like sheets) with duck & beef ragu.  So delectable.  Our friends both had terrific grilled entrees.  Lamb chops and skewers of  Chicken and home-cured sausage.  Both entrees came with roasted potatoes.  We had no alcohol - just soft drinks.  Oh yeah, my husband did have a beer - a good one - and orange-blossom scented pale ale.  Nice.  For dessert the chef - who was kind enough to chat with us, comped us a platter of 3 desserts.  A traditional cassata-like cake (good - not great), a silky panna cotta (YUM) and the best - LIMONCELLO-soaked tiramisu.  That would be worth the usual $7 for-a-dessert charge.  I really, really like this place and would welcome the chance to go back. The patio in summer is nice, although we sat inside.  It was a lovely time.

They re-did this Sunoco a while back and the mini-mart has really improved with better restrooms, a Subway (inside) and hot foods.  The gas is "market priced" and it's easy to get in and out here - right in "downtown" Media (LOL - I have to laugh at the phrase "downtown Media").  No issues - and I come here quite often when I need gas in Media.
Hey - it's a Wawa and was there when we needed it. Cigarettes, bottled water and wait - Girl Scout Cookies?  Sold out of somebody's trunk in the parking lot. And the DO have a parking lot.  Yay Wawa.

I am treated so well here and have been since they first opened (I was not a client when they were in the Springfield mall years ago).  I will say, however, they are much more considerate of "regulars" than walk-ins so perhaps, call first and ask for an appointment with Cyndi, Jen or Nancy.  All 3 ladies are terrific and I get pedicures (regular and spa), manicures (regular, gel, Vinylux/Hybrid, French and nail art) and waxing (eyebrow or underarm) here as needed for both myself and my 14 year old.  We love coming here - the pedi chairs were recently re-done and are much nicer now.  Large selection of over 800 polishes (300 classic/hybrid) 400 gel and about 100 "dip" colors.  I tried 5 or 6 salons (including the much lauded "Zen Nails" and the now defunct and awful "Nail 452") when we moved here and Trendy's got my money and my vote every time.  Plus, you can walk over to Starbucks if they are too busy to take you right away (again - walk-ins).  Tip:  Come here on a weekday morning for much better service.  Saturdays and Sundays are crazy-busy.  Cyndi, Jen and Nancy are who I see (all 3 are equally wonderful).  A few of my other ladies have left and new ones are here but I do not yet know their work.  Cyndi's gel work is amazing, Nancy is great at everything and Jen's pedis and Classic or Hybrid manis are long lasting and meticulously applied.  Good nails are only as good as the strength of the nail technician and these 3 ladies know their stuff. Go Trendy!
It's convenient - and the Gallery Mall is right above it. Pretty dirty, though - the bathrooms are awful.

This place should be called the Philadelphia Dosa Co. - they are really skimpy with the chutney - you get 1 little container (there are about 6 to choose from), and can purchase more.  Service is just OK.  Prices are fine.  Good for lunch - not great for dinner. Oh - and they do not have any ice (We wanted some for our water - it was so hot in there (it's been a heatwave all this week in Philly).  The sell only bottled drinks - so no ice is available.  I tried the #7 - Avocado, Arugula, Tomato and what??  American Cheese? WTF?  WHo puts cheese in a dosa?  And American at that? Kraft Singles?  Whatever.  The idli were lightly steamed and fluffy - easy to eat.  A nice addition to the culinary landscape - but by no means a holy grail. A good choice for vegetarians. (Hold the American, please!)
OMG - sooooo busy on a crowded Saturday around 1 PM. Meanwhile got a much -needed oil change.  No issues.

No issues with the Media "martini glass" bouquet delivered locally for a party and it arrived fresh and on time.  My 9 year old & I stopped by the store - because we had never been inside and the nice lady GAVE us each a free chocolate-covered strawberry.  Made our day!  EA is a nice alternative to a cake at a party (you can add chocolate covered berried or banana chunks) or instead of sending flowers to someone.
Ah, the Troc.  So many shows - but so many that I saw soooooooo long ago.  Loved it back then - can't really comment on it nowadays.  And they get some really great acts in here!

The food tastes fine - and the cafeteria style of "design your own" burritos, tacos and quesadillas is catching on fast -but don't be fooled.  It's still fast food - and it is super-duper HIGH in calories.  A typical burrito has 1100 - 1600 calories.  (Naked will reduce it by 330 - as the PLAIN TORTILLA is 330 whopping calories alone.)  That said - I do enjoy the Naked Chicked Burrito, no cheese, small (70 cal) taco-sized torilla on the side.  It's just too hard for me to "hold the guac" and save 220 calories.  That guac - for fast food guac tastes muy bien to me.  By the way - I think Jack-in-the-box owns Qdoba - I know Chipotle is owned by McDonalds.  FAST FOOD - people. Eat under a health advisory.  Note:  In the summer they make a very tasty mango salsa.  You can get it on ANY burrito if you ask.

Better.  A big Target with everything we needed.  Except for the picked-over shoe department.  I have come to the conclusion that unless its for a young child or flip flops that Target is NOT a place to buy shoes.  Luckily DSW is right nearby!  In any case we got a bunch of household products we needed.

Peregrine Coffee, owned by Philadelphia husband & wife team of Kevin & Louise is a true find and gem!  They offer a "Bespoke" ocffee tasting service where they will come to your office or home and fresh grind,brew and allow you to sample numerous types of single origin or single estate beans.  Ken is a true "coffee geek" and is extremely knowledgeable about all aspects of coffee production.  He buys his beans green and roasts them in the Peregrine Roaster in Tacony.  We had 5 friends over for a Bespoke Coffee Tasting party and could not have been more pleased.  They will even package smaller amount of coffee as wedding favors.  (Oh, where were they when we needed them 6 months ago!!!?)  All this, and to top it off they are the nicest, smartest people you could hope to meet.  We hope to have more tastings with them.  That KenyaAA was something to taste!  (So complex and delicious.)  You will never want Dunkin' again!!!!   (Don't even get me started on Charbucks.)

Another delicious lunch of orzo salad, Salade Nicoise (with freshly seared tuna) and of course the honey fried chicken tossed salad.  Wendy is still there and the gang is always friendly and happy to see us.  Love lunches at Day by Day!

I have gotten 3 oil changes here over the past 18 or 20 months and there is always a wait.  It gets busy.  I have tried lunch hour (bad idea), Saturday (worse idea) and after work (not as bad as lunch, but maybe that is because I don't feel the stress of having to rush back to the office in under an hour).  Staff is competent and prices are fair.  No issues and so far I will keep coming back. Gonna try a random time (like 10:30 on a Tuesday or 2:30 on a Thursday) one of these days to see if it is any less crowded.
Ollie's is a hit or miss place for housewares, beauty products, books, cleaning supplies, non-perishable food items.  It's "odd lots" of stuff that changes for any or no reason.

I am ever-so disappointed with Gennaro's - and just went there again for the first time in years as it never is good.  Well, I was right - my cappucino came out with curdled milk.  Ick. Fortunately the very kind server, Wendy, brought me another one and took it off the bill.  My close friend eats here ALL the time and loves it, but I just don;t get it. It's never "quite right" for me here.  Friendly service, old-school digs (they need new carpeting) and a menu to match.  People/Locals love it.  Maybe New Yawk has spoiled me for Delco-Italian.

A very cute "strip mall" salon with a clean reception area and Kerastase Products for sale. Prices were too high ($38 for a blowout - no use of flat iron) for me to justify coming here. I spent $25 for a blowout - no upcharge to use flat iron. (And in Center City I spent $30).  I would like to inquire about other services/prices but they have no web site. Good news - they take walk ins.

Of all the places in Philly why, oh why, would I ever come here? Three words.  Fifty Dollar Gift-card.  Or is that 4 words (2 words and a compound word?)?  Yes, folks, I won a $50 gift card good at ANY Hard Rock location from a charity auction so a good-sport friend (I love her - and she put up with Hard Rock well) and I decided to play cheap-meal roulette.  I read the menu online before we went and luckily, they sat us is the back room (the Philadelphia room) which is much less loud and crowded.  Our self-effacing server, Stewart, was attentive and kind - especially since I can be such a pain in the a$$.  I ordered a pomegranate martini and ask for it NOT to contain Sierra Mist.  (I mean, really, Sierra Mist?)  The $8.50 martini was basically vodka, Monin Pomegranate Syrup and seltzer.  It was fine and I was able to cultivate a buzz in about 12 minutes.  My friend wisely chose the shrimp fajitas which were served on a sizzling platter and tasted pretty good.  I poorly chose a great steak which was so gristly I had to send it back.  Poor, Stewart took it back and the next one they brought was at least edible.  But flavorless.  I literally had to put salt and pepper on it and was eyeing the A-1 (I HATE A-1!). A good steak should have flavor on its own.  Maybe that's why they put "Cabernet butter" aka Country Crock on all the grilled items?  Anyhow - dessert was a BOMB. Over sweet cheesecake on a cardboard and wood-shaving crust.  Do not even think about getting the syrup-ed-out creme brulee here. At least it was cheap ($2.99 for the dessert "bites")  Believe it or not - I am giving them 3 stars (they really deserve 2) because they were very accomodating to all of our requests and we had a fun time.  Would I come here again? Not unless I had another gift card - and even then - I think I would re-gift!

Cathy, our sassy server, was a delight.  She is a pro and has been here for about 6 years.  We sat in their outdoor "Covid Tent" on a busy Sunday morning at 11.  We got a table for 4 right away and juice/coffee/tea.  The eggs Florentine are terrific but they come with cheese.  Next time I will skip it and also get the copious amount of hollandaise sauce on the side.  A calorie/fat bomb for sure.  Too about 1/3 of it home.  Now I need a nap...

5 stars for my amazing practitioner, Dr. Nonack - he is truly a kind, caring and competent physician.  The administration of the practice needs work though and this is systemic throughout the PENN healthcare system.  Please bring back late Monday night appointments.  Please consider Saturday appointments - even once per month would help.  Kielie at the Media office (I probably spelled that wrong) is terrific and runs the desk well.  The in-house lab for blood draws (alas - Michael has left circa 2021) is so convenient, too.  Staff do not seem well compensated.

So pleased to see a healthier alternative for lunch - the petitio burrito (small) is plenty big.  Prices are high and ordering system is too slow (no big menu - you have to read the small menu) - plus my juice was wrong.  (They re-made it with no issues.)  Love the food choices, not liking the slow ordering procedure (line is huge at lunch hour) and innacuracies.  Also the up charges for Guac and Meats is too high.  (The small burritos are 6-7 as it is - I don;t wanna pay $10 for a SMALL - when I could get a regular sized (large) burrito for $8 anyway.  A few kinks to work out - but I will generously give them 4 stars - for now - I sense trouble ahead, so please get it together and re-structure the burrito menu a bit. (Add ons.)  Keep the steamed kale - it's great! Also, I am getting green lemonade (ask for it with less apple, more green) every morning for about a week now and I LOVE it.  P.S.  The breakfast "beans & Green" petitio is terrific and at $4.5 is a decent value. The eggs & greens is also a good and filling breakfast for $4.75
When it's fresh - that vanilla pound cake is simple, heavy and rich and DE-FRIKKIN-LICIOUS.  For $11 a pop - get 2 and freeze one.  So good.  A neighborhood staple and a "real" Philly treat.

Le Virtu - I love you. We were greeted so warmly by Fred - and sat at the bar enjoying delicious Italian wines by the glass.  We were seated at a corner table and started the meal with a delicious sausage and red peppers over polenta and fried olives (Crispy, hot and stuffed with porchetta - they are little bombs of flavor exploding in yout mouth).  So wonderful.  After the delectable apps (and foccacia dipped in tasty olive oil), our primi arrived - pappardelle (housemade) with rabbit ragu for DH and handkerchief pasta with duck ragu for me.  MEMORIES are made of this.  Who could eat more? A secondi? Not tonight...  But We did have something else - a perfectly made cappucino (yes, at night - I know, I know) for me and grappa for DH.  We also split a luscioud dessert of a fresh crepe with chestnuts paired with 3 freshly fried ravioli stuufed with chocolate and chestnuts (So sinful, yet so delicious.)  A mouthwatering, memorable, five star evening.  We love you, Le Virtu. And thank you for participating in the Friends Select School "Dining with friends" promotion.

This starbucks is deceptive. First of all, parking is horrendous - there's just not enough of it. Secondly there is hardly any seating - a few bar stools and a few tiny tables for 2. Thirdly, the retail area - used also to barricade off the drink line area - is too bulky and wide.  This location is deceptive in size - it looks like a big store from the outside but is cramped and crowded inside.  Meanwhile the usual Fourbucks menu items prevail. Service was fine.  It's just too small.
I support Planned Parenthood.  This location is smaller and has limited hours (funding cuts have been a problem for all Planned Parenthood sites).  They have my support.

7-Eleven is so old skool, but this particular location has saved us with a Sunday NY Times on more than one occaision.  I don't buy any food nor beverage items here.  Just grab an old-skoool printed newspaper and leave.  Wawa country, indeed - see Steven B.'s review - he is "spot on".

They do not carry Eukenuba nor California Natural (The only foods my dogs(s) eat, so I can't really come here.   They had a few toys and treats on sale.  Seems more fish/aquarium centric than mammal centric, so if you have fish - this could be a good option for you.  Now that Pet Supplies Plus is going out of business, their business should pick up a bit.  Please consider carrying Eukenuba so I can come here.
Hosted a private event here for 5 ladies and we were treated like royalty. Fantastic service and wonderful manis & pedis.  I truly love this place!

Our party of 6 had a truly wonderful lunch during "Taco Week" at Condesa.  We all opted for the $22 three-course deal - choice of app, entrée and dessert.  The Aqua Fresca that day was a delightful guava, lemon and mint.  It reminded me of guava lemonade.  I had a splash of it over sparkling water to cut my carbs - and it was mighty tasty.  The fresh guac was truly flavorful with fresh cilantro and sliced mini-jalapenos.  Just the right amount of kick.  For an entrée I opted for the Platos of pork with onions and nopales - which I happen to love.  The pork itself was just perfectly seasoned and the right amount of fat and lean.  Juice.  Succulent.  Rich tasting.  And oh-so-not-Kosher.  Sorry, G-d.  3 of the 6 people got lamb tacos (on bluecorn tortillas) and everyone was raving.  For dessert there were a variety of fresh Mexican pastries and a moist, warm (again, delightful) Olive Oil cake.    Too many carbs for me - but worth the splurge.  The food, décor and service here (even the mod-chic ladies room) were all stellar.  So great.  Pricey, yes - but the $22 three course is a great deal if you can get that.  I can't wait to come back.

This Wawa was literally my savior as I was trapped in a huge area-wide traffic fisaco when 95 was literally shut down (in both directions) as was 476 due to 2 major overturned truck accidents.  Traffic was crawling on 291 and all arterial roads.  A 35 minute drive took nealy 2 hours and I. Had. To. Pee.  Thank heavens for this Wawa - and the friendly female cashier who directly me safely out of the parking lot back on to 291.

I was treated so poorly here that I had to leave, which is a shame because I love a good diner and was looking forward to coming here.  I will give them another chance on a future date but I am not in a hurry.  Here's what happened:  I arrived early to meet a friend at 6 PM but he was not there yet.  It was freezing cold so I went in and figured I'd relax for 15-20 minutes and have a coffee and review some paperwork.  2 men were chatting up front in Italian when I arrived, and they seated the 2 elderly ladies in front of me.  Then they asked me"How many" and I said "2".  And the guy basically left. I asked if I could be seated and he said "Not until your party is here" and I said I wanted to get a coffee.  He said I could sit at the counter.  There were plenty of tables open.  The delivery of his words were what made it so rude.  It could have easily been handled better. I left and called my friend and we went elsewhere.

A cutesy & kid-friendly (family mecca) bakery in Chestnut Hill right on "The" Avenue.  Cakes, cookies and other sweet treats at medium (not cheap, but not ridiculous) prices.  They also have ice cream.  My little one is sold - and I am not too far behind.  (Although I prefer cakes from the Night Kitchen bakery a bit farther down the hill. - see my other reviews.)
2 pretzel dogs and 3 free pretzels for $4.59. Everything was hot and fresh (I arrived at 7:30 AM).  No issues.  Carb-y goodness.

OMG, Weber's!  I haven't been here since I was a kid. Meanwhile, yesterday (a Sunday) about 6:30 PM we were driving back to Philly - and attempted to go to the Cherry Hill Mall - which was closed. So we wound up on a whim, stopping at Weber's.  The Elvis impersonator in the driveway was an interesting touch.  Nice guy - actually (and he's available for parties).  DH & I both got cheeseburgers, DD got a hot dog with ketchup AND a cheeseburger.  We shared a chocolate milkshake - which the lovely female server offered to split into 2 cups for us.  So great!  DD & I each had a few sips of the thick chocolate goodness and then called it quits.  I can't imagine drinking a whole one.  The burgers tasted great and were so juicy. A little small - but they were heavy so that was fine.  DD liked her hot dog and ate a good bit of the burger, too - and of course then felt sick and stopped eating.  A little too much of a good thing. A rare indulgence, for sure. CASH ONLY.  So nostalgic on a cool summer night to be served by a "carhop".

Average food, service and décor with average University City prices. Tomato soup was good, Cobb Salad was just OK.  Brunch items looked like a better choice but I am low carb and many entrees were super high in carbs and/or calories.  Crowded  even on a Sunday for brunch.  Family Friendly (Surprised at how many little kids were here in addition to the college crowd.)  Good but not great. A safe choice.

Yuppie diner where clientele and staff are all straight out of a J Crew Catalog.  Excellent and good looking (mostly female) wait staff and FABULOUS albeit higher priced diner classics with a twist.  Turkey chili was terrific as was house-made oatmeal and Eggs Benedict (pricey) with a variety of add ons including spinach and crabmeat.  So good.  LOVE!  Can't wait to return.

Super yay!  Love the turkey burgers here.  They are NOT dry and so tasty.  I pass on the big bucket o' fries in favor of their YUM-CITY mac 'n cheese.  I order mine sans the tomato "jam" garnish.  They also have kickin' sides like greenbeans (crisp and studded with tomotoes) and sweet potatoes.  (Grilled with butter and cinnamon suger - like dessertm baby!).  It can get crowded and crazy - which is why it is not 5 stars -but the price is right and this spot ROCKS.

Stopped in to reminisce about old friends and the "old" Doylestown at Nat's - what better a place?  Tim was off (it was on a Sunday) but the pizza slice my daughter had was fine, and the cherry water ice (kid's size is prlenty) turned the children's mouths red.  Nice to see it's the same as I remember - even though so much about Doylestown has changed.  Nat's is a D-town institution.
4 stars for the food.  I try to ignore the surroundings.  Great Duck.  And hands-down best steamed dumplings.  LOVE 'em.  Wonton Duck Soup can be a little greasy - but man, it's a tasty indulgence.

We went here AGAIN for New Years eve and the food was amazingly good. And they treated my 4 year old so nicely. She loved the mango sorbet and vanilla ice cream, of course.   They had a "special" somewhat limited and pricey NYEve menu. I had the mushroom ravioli which was absolutely delicious. My friend had the Chilean Sea Bass and LOVED it. We are **this close** to giving it 5 stars, but my husbands fillet mignon (came with lobster) was overcooked.   The appetizer of HUGE bacon-wrapped, vegetable stuffed jumbo shrimp was divine - served over 2 sauces: rich horseradish cream and raspberry coulis - swirled together on the plate. At first I thought $15 for 2 shrimp seems INSANE - but they were, indeed, HUGE.   The desserts were, of course, the BEST part - and on New Year's eve they were each garnished with gold-leafed chocolates that said "Happy New Year" on them. (My 4 year old gobbled down the chocolates with glee.) The Black & White creme brulee was perfectly prepare with a hot crispy top and cool creamy sweetness beneath (My husband & I shared it). My friend got the espresso chocolate torte - which really was overkill. Just a bit too-too if you know what I mean - but if you are a chocolate/espresso lover you could catch a wicked buzz off of that! (Served with 3 chocolate covered espresso beans - which alone would make me buzz.)   Our server was friendly and attentive - although i think she secretly was not thrilled about us bringing our young child in.   Oh - and I had 3 Arnold Palmers - you know what a big drinker I am.  They were terrifically refreshing.   The chefs are great guys who can really "throw down". I just love the rose tattoo. They are really, really, close to 5 stars for me.

MInella's redeemed itself - specifically George, our wonderful server.  A friend and I came during Covid and the place was nearly empty so we could sit and eat.  We each got burgers - big (8 oz) juicy burgers.  Topped with whatever you can think of.  If you wish side of fries and (2) onion rings.  Massive pile of fries.  Very good experience, thank goodness.  I had all but given up on Minella's.

Sooooooo hard to get an appointment here - and no late nights or weekends.  We came at 9 AM as a walk in and were turned away.  Very hard for parents who work - my teen comes here for birth control and preventive health care.  We love and support Planned Parenthood but it is darned difficult to get seen.  The doctors (once you get to see one) and practitioners are excellent and knowledgeable.  Parents:  educate your kids about reproductive health.  It is so very important to maintain an open dialogue from an early age.  Prevent STI's, unplanned pregnancies, abusive situations and so much more.  Sex is not a bad word.  Talk to your kids about sex.  Openly. Now.

I have since been back to Talula's 3 more times - including last night.  Each time was a true 5 star experience.  But not last night.  Service was still great. Food was not 5 star.  (The cheese plate was still 5 star - best bites of the night including Délice de Bourgogne and a fantastic onion-y Abbott's Gold Cheddar.  (Had that last time and swapped it into the "World Travel" cheese plate.)  The cavatelli app was superb.  But tiny. TINY! Yes, I know it's an app - but they presented it in a huge, deep "pasta" bowl and it made it look even smaller.  Maybe serving it in a more propotionate vessel?  My friend ordered the spring foraged salad which sounded heavenly on paper and in real life was just OK. The ramps were over powering and the foraged lettuces were a bit bitter and odd tasting.  The beets and ricotta side still rocks my world.  It was a strong 4 for food, 5 for service but... ...here's the BIG but...  The cocktails have somehow gone awry. Even my Arnold Palmer was just "meh. (Did they change their iced tea??) My friend ordered a "The Painter" - a champagne cocktail and it looked like a watered down mimosa with lemon juice instead of orange juice ($12 - FEH!) And the enormous wine glass that the rose came in (Reidel crystal??) made the skimpy less-than-6-oz. pour look positively puny.  ($10 - FEH again!)  I am deeply saddened to have to downgrade Talulas as it was one of my absolute faves.  So sad. So sad.  Meanwhile - come have a cheese plate here - but be wary of the new barkeep.

We came on a Sunday for a late lunch and had great service from Luna. Cheerful (loud - they turned it down) music and Horchata (ask for it).  Delicious Al Pastor (I got it in my tacos) and fresh guac.  My partner's burrito (veggie) was chock full of goodies.  Very fair prices and portions. Good tasting food.

I went here 2 years ago - exactly ONCE. My former co worker just LOVES this place and comes here regularly - for all sorts of things - even their overpriced manis & pedis (They wanted alot more than I pay at my "regular" nail bar).  Anyhow it's a lovely salon and the gal who did my hair (I forgot her name) was good, but for the price? Nope.  Can't do it.

Upgrading to 2 or 3 stars as I finally got to eat a mediocre meal here. Service was much better - our server Melissa was a doll, but I had a rotten avocado sliced all over the salad I ordered.  Blargh!  They comped dessert to make up for it.  French onion soup (in a chicken stock??? Sysco chicken base?) was on the salty side, but good.  I think I have given up on Minella's.

It's not horrible - maybe I' should have given it 3 stars?  It's been around forever - and has the cliched Monday night "colonial Kitchen" and King Henry's feast.  The chicken pot pie tastes like it was made with frozen veggies.  I have never been too impressed with Cock 'n Bull's dining room meals (nor brunch - which is tourist0filled and pricey.)  That being said - we actually had a CATERED event here in the summer of 2004 - my baby shower.  It happened to be great.  Well managed by Peddler's Village staff and the food was actually GREAt - 3-4 stars for chicken francese, fresh, crisp buttery green beans and caesar salad were stand outs.  OK.  I'll relent and give it 3 stars.  2 for dining room meals and 4 for catered events.  Hell, it's been around for eh ver!  (In junior high we'd call it the cock and balls.)

Just got another STELLAR Vinylux Mani from Cyndi and waxing from Jen. Fantastic, long wearing (7-8 days!!!) and a great value ot $13 all performed in a clean, comfortable salon.  LOVE THIS PLACE SO MUCH!
A lovely scenic greenspace with trails for walking or running.  A great place to take your kid or your dog or both.  What fun on a spring or summer day!

I honestly don't know WHAT to review. My husband hated it - too high priced for him and old, dated decor and "meh" food to him.  Our 8 year old loved it - but she only had a $5 Bindi (pre-fab) frozen Coconut Gelato (served in a coconut shell).  We love those Bindi desserts - and so does half the restaurant world!  I enjoyed my food - Fettucine with Chicken in a pink sauce with a few peas (wish there were more). The dish is supposed to come with rigatoni but I asked to sub fettucine which they did.  Portion was small - but the sauce is very rich so I was fine with it - even though el kiddo nabbed a good 1/3 of it!  (Ha ha!  She loved it here.) Oh - and the dinner rolls, while served hot, were a bit stale (sorry).  The meatballs my husband had were just ok.  Kinda bready.  The ones I make are better (sorry, Gennaro), but the service here is better than Casa Prego.  Food is about the same and some things are less expensive here and others are more.  It has been in business since 1992 (according to the menu) and they need a makeover STAT.  Other than that it is a quiet, family-friendly spot with classic, "old-skool" Italian-American fare circa 1974.  And I kinda dig it.  Won't rush back - but I will be back - so please take note - and I pray things will have improved when I do.  Classic Italian American Family Friendly Medium Priced (Could argue too high on certain items, very fair on others.) Small - seats 50 max - largest table seats 6. Family run.

OK.  I'm a convert now. I come in 3-4 times per week (ouch - my wallet!) for green lemonaid - light on the apple, heavy on the greens.  Every now and then I get a petito beans & greens burrito which is way too much for breakfast and I am full until lunch or beyond.  The lady in the AM is so nice to me.  I am much more into this place at breakfast when there is no line. Wish you could get lunch items at breakfast (I'd get a chicken burrito and take it to the office and eat it at lunch!)  Loving it here now for sure!  P.S.  Please put a hook in the ladies room to hang your purse on. P.P.S.  Please consider posting a big, easy to read, professionally printed menu board up above to hlp the ordering process and lunch line speed.

Eatible Delights catered a meeting I attended on a Saturday in Center City.  they provided a nice continental Breakfast but lunch was just Meh.  Lunch boxes were a choice of sandwich (I picked tuna - and it was on soggy wheat bread) with packaged cookies, a piece of fruit (I got an apple - some folks got an orange or banana) and inedible pasta salad.  Disappointed in the lunch, happy with the basic breakfast.

Haven't been to Devil's Alley in years (try 5 or 6 of them) but stopped in for lunch on a not-so-busy Friday (It was 11:50 AM - so the rush had not yet hit) and had a great, basic cobb salad (I subbed Salmon for pulled Chicken) and it was terrific.   The Honey Mustard and Blue Cheese dressings (I sampled both!) are very good and the lettuce was fresh and crunchy.  Service from the hostess (Alyssa/Alicia??) was outstanding, too.  She is young but been in restaurants for 7 years.  So kind.  We'll be back - and in less than 6 years, too.  Devil's Alley is still a good choice - even after all this time. Keep it up!

Just had yet another astounding Gel Mani by Cyndi (Also ask for Jen, Nancy and Nita).  I.  LOVE.  THIS.  PLACE.  Clean, reasonable, fun atmosphere, friendly but BEST of all?  Top quality mani's, gels, hybrids manis and pedis/  I can't wait to return.
Just like every other Manhattan Bagel - and in some ways, better than many. A wide variety of bagels and spreads - to go.  Don't eat there.    Staff works very quickly so know what you want.

Service is quick, but lines at lunchtime are very long. Be patient, they are doing their best.   CFA has now offered salads for a few years and I enjoy the Cobb Salad, no cheese, grilled chicken instead of fried nuggets.  It's still not healthy as it is loaded with bacon, but it tastes good.  The Avocado Lime Ranch dressing also tastes great, and adds on 310 cals per pack.  I try to use less, but sometimes I cave.  CFA is about the only fast food we eat. My vegan teen loves the waffle fries.  CFA is taking over the nation. I wish their political views were more in line with mine, but they just aren't.  Not LGBTQIA friendly.
Attended a formal dining event here and everything from service to delicious food to the valet/car parking was TOP NOTCH.  Love it here.

I attended here in the mid nineties as a grad student at the School of Dental Medicine - and believe me, 3 stars is as generous as I can be.  I was harassed by a sadistic Bay Instructor, chased down Baltimore Avenue by "Hatchet Man" and generally had a miserable experience which may or may not have been the fault of the school.  Meanwhile, I got good grades - but transferred out to escape the scourge of West Philly at that time.  (It's alot nicer there now.)  I have a feeling the undergraduate experience would have been better.

A fantastic find on an unseasonably warm November day.  Lentil Soup, Horiatiki Salad -topped with salmon - so perfect - and "greek" waffle fries.  Great service from Ian.  We loved that house-made pita, too.  Everything was so tasty and moderately priced.  Lovely!

Honestly, my expectations were very low and I fully expected Barnaby's in Havertown to suck.  (The one in Aston is just awful) Guess what?  It's didn't!!!!  We sat on the deck on a rainy Covid day at about 12 noon and had very tasty Irish coffees and standard bar food.  Prices were mid-range and surprisingly, service from Tina (she and one other lady were running the entire deck and bar) was good.  She is a doll - albeit way overworked.  I bet it gets crowded here on weekend nights.  Seems like an OK place for a happy hour. A bit of a "frat -boy-turned-middle-aged-male" vibe. Lots of big TVs for watching the Iggles.  Kudos to Tina. Don't expect a top-tier dining experience - it's a BAR.  Totally a BAR.

Delicious linguine with clam sauce (whole clams, in-shell) and just enough garlic in the not-too-oily sauce.  The long-stem (fried) artichoke appetizer is truly marvelous but so heavy for an app.  I had it as a lunch entree and was stuffed.  (The panko-coated artichoke halves are smothered in a rich rosa sauce - delicious but so caloric.)  A diet bomb but a special treat. Attentive and efficient service.

For whatever reason everything seemed way better at Diego's during Margarita weekend.  The $4 frozen margs didn't hurt!  The special - Shrimp Tempura Tacos with Mango Salsa were great ($15 for 3) and the queso fundito is basic but tasty.  Chips & Salsa and service with a smile were constant and we had a great night - even if the place was "ear-splittingly" loud.

We are big supporters of the Mummers - and my little girl just loves the parade - especially the comics.  I am partial to the Fancy Brigades, myself.  Anyhow, this SMALL museum (kind of a glorified practice hall) is a once-must-see Philadelphia experience.  Neat.

Ah, target - that's tar jhay - the french department store. Not really - but as target's go - this one is clean, suburban and has everything we need.  We come here when we are on the way back to Philly from Doylestown - it's right on the way.  Loves me some target!

Still a solid choice for lunch, dinner or drinks and munchies. Very good quality food - but also high priced.  Heirloom tomato salad ($10) was small but very delicious. Cheese Plate is always a fine choice as is the pint of Prawns or house-cured salmon.  Lovely food - simple, fresh ingredients. Complicated drinks and high priced soft drinks ($5 for luscombe's!)  Ok service but a few little mis-steps. For example - we were not served any bread & butter until we asked for it - late in the meal.  A good pick for a Center City lunch.

On our way to LBI - Red top (and Green top next door) are our go-to "touristy" farmer's market stop.  yes the prices are a bit much and we ask which produce is local (some is not).  Picnic tables yes. Restrooms - no.

3-4 stars - I will give them 4 as our service was excellent (we came on the Sunday night of July 4th weekend) and the food was surprisingly excellent.  Our party of 3 sat in the back dining room which was a/c-chilled to a crisp.  Bet that comes in handy on crowded nites - but it was DEAD at 6 PM on that particular Sunday.  We started with a DELICIOUS order of chicken nachos and they were served with blue corn tortilla chips, salsa, guacamole and a good amount of melted cheese.  YUM!  My friend ordered the grilled chicken (her usual - she's been 3-4 times and unlike other reviewers - she likes the grilled chicken here), my husband got the pork burger and I got and LOVED the (fried) fish tacos.  At 3 tacos per order for $9.50 - that was very fair.  The only culinary "oops" were the twice-fried french fries.  They were hard as rocks and cold.  Kinda greasy and blah tasting.  I bet they sat around due to the low-turnover night.  I bet they taste better fresh outta the fryer.  Too bad.  Oodles of beers on tap and by the bottle - even a choice "by the cask".  Hubby got a Blueberry wheat pale ale - which tasted great.  The chocolate beignets and other choices tempted us from the dessert menu, but alas, we did NOT order dessert as we were too stuffed to manage it.  Less pretentious (and less cutesy) than Pub & Kitchen - this is not a gastro-pub - it's simple bar food with a fresh tasting twist.  I live walking distance so I'll be back for sure!

$5 includes a soda or bottle of water and your choice of lamb or chicken gyro meat over rice or salad (I get salad which is iceberg, tomatoes, cucumbers, chickpeas and onion [optional]).  White sauce?  Hot Sauce?  Green Sauce?  Whatever yu wish.  Five bucks.  Not bad.

A bit overpriced and underwhelming.  The decor is very nice and service was fine, but the Steak Quesadilla was $10.99 (plus .65 - very cheap actually - for a small side of guac).  It tasted OK but for $12 ($15 with tip) that's a bit steep.  I would come back but I will not be running back there.

We went to Indonesia last night as part of the foodie group (Shout out to Foodie M!) of 31 people.  For $35 (including tax & tip - BYOB) per person we had an absolute banquet of food. 2 Diet Cokes we ordered in addition were less than $3.00.  Dang - I should brought some bubbly!  Our hosts (the owner and 2 attentive, hard working servers) treated us so well.  We had the entire private banquet room upstairs, and it was lovely, with fresh flowers on the long table, and ice water ready for us.  Our appetizers were balls of sticky rice stuffed with aromatic chicken, wrapped in a banana leaf.  (The banana leaf is used prevelantly in Javanese cookery).  I liked it, but it coulda used some dipping sauce.  Next we had a choice of soup - Chicken with coconut - different than Thai - and a little thinner - or an EXCELLENT Lamb soup.  The soup did have bones (lamb ribs) in it - so that turned a few people off - but I loved it - as the flavor was so tasty.  Lime leaves and lemon grass - and not at all "too hot" nor "too spicy".  I really, really enjoyed that soup.  After the appetizer and soup I already felt full, but I tried to pace myself (and failed) for the formidable feast.  Each couple was served a lazy susan with about 6-7 different dishes on it.  Large bowls of yellow aromatic rice (so delish) were placed on each table so we could all have as much rice as we liked.  (The rice had a faint jasmine tea aroma to it and was so sweet and wonderful. - Carbo loading at its best.)  The dishes on our lazy susan included a succulent and tender beef curry.  Now, I am not a curry person - but this was terrific.  A lovely "barbequed" chicken in a sweet red pepper sauce was fragrant and tasty.  All the meats were flake-tender.  I was not a big fan of the mackerel - again steamed with spices and wrapped in the ever-present banana leaf.  It tasted too fishy and cat-foodish for me.  The Udup-Udup - mixed vegetables with FRESH crispy bean sprouts and crunchy green cabbage was a good palate cleanser.  Fettucine-like strands of egg omelette were simply delicious as well. Nasi goreng and Sate (yummy chicken sate) were on the platter, too.  Another stand out was the crisp, slightly sweet and calorie-laden corn & egg fritter.  Two of them were perched atop the center of the lazy susan and DH and I ate those right away while they were hot and perfect.  By now I was so full I could barely try the tempeh with shrimp and green beans (sounded better than it was) and Potato-meat croquettes (not my thing, but other people loved them).  Not one but 2 dessert courses followed. Fried bananas - one of my favorites - were served with a small pitcher of syrup.  "They're not just for breakfast anymore"!  The batter evokes a french toast (sans cinnamon) taste.  They were a little thickly breaded (I am accostomed to Japanese Tempura bananas) for my liking - but I was so stuffed that I really didn't mind.  The final dessert was really. Well.  Weird.  It was a warm "soup" of sweet (slightly chalky) coconut milk, with pieces of (yummy) jackfruit), tapioca pearls, mung beans, shredded green jello (eeeew) and pieces of white bread.  Maybe it was because I was now too full to enjoy anything - but this type of dessert (take every tpical Javanese dessert item and put it in a bowl) would not ever be my cup of tea.  (Or soup - as the case may be.)  The best part of the evening was the terrific conversation and friendships made.  Foodie M.'s mom and sister sat near us - and that was terrific. We also met another couple who were smart and funny and had been to Indonesia before (Though Balinese cuisine and easter Javanese are quite different.)  I would highly recommend trying Indonesia and supporting this wonderful local business.  A great time was had!

This outpost of Smashburger is infinitely better-run than the one near my home. The red-shirted managers were serving the lunch crowd (Quite busy on a Friday) and very attentive.  I actually ordered the Kid's meal and the portion was just fine for me. Glad to see this option.  Still, I wish they'd allow upgrades to sweet-potato and/or "smash" fries from "regular" fries.  The sweet potato fries (to me) are much tastier.  A calorie-bomb for sure - but if you stick to salads and get grilled (not fried) chicken or the (fairly decent) turkey burger you can get away with it once in a while.

I brought my 4 year old daughter here for Dim Sum after the flower show, once we discovered that Ong's Noodle shop has closed.  We first tried Pho 75 but my dd wanted DUMPLINGS and Pho 75 doesn't have them.  Joy Tsin Lau sure does.  We had Har Gow (excellent), Shiu Mai (just OK) and Steamed Dumploings - very heavy/doughy with vile, bone-chip-laden, mystery meat filling.  BLECH!  Meanwhile, we also ordered Chicken fried rice with extra scambled egg - and dd loved that.  An enormous plateful for 5.95 - took alot home.  They treat us very well - but the digs are ancitent and the bathroom was freezing cold and FILTHY.  The floor was literally sticky.  Eeeeeeew!  1-2 stars for the dining digs and 3-4 stars for food (but skip the dumplings on the menu and get dim sum.)

You pick your seats in advance (online) and order food and drinks (full bar) when you get there. Food is sub par and way over priced.  Movie experience was fine.  Movie tavern is a hair better but also sub par food (like an Applebee's) and pricey.  The kiddo loves it, so we continue to go.

Wow - I honestly can NOT believe that nobody reviewed this venerable (old, ancient, classic, etc.) Media institution.  "The" Townhouse has held countless High School reunions (even weddings), corporate luncheons and functions in their numerous party rooms (and the large "ball room" downstairs).  I attended a small (25 people) dinner last night - but before it began we sat at the (again) classic bar downstairs where Barbara kept those refreshing Arnold Palmers coming!  She is a doll.  (And the $2.00 off each drink at happy hour (4-6 PM) and free munchies were a plus.  They also offer $3.00 bar snacks - but we saved room for our meal upstairs.  Once upstairs I had a ball looking at all those classic photographs from events long past (The 25th class reunion of the Class of '42, and even a picture of Mr. Biddle - when he was about 20 - from Drinker Biddle & Reath).  Nicki - our server has worked at D'Ignazios for 40 years!  We started our "set" meal with a very fresh green salad.  I had the tasty lobster ravioli and others had chicken or a veggie option.  Dessert was an uber-rich flourless chocolate cake.  It was drizzled in a raspberry sauce and tasted like eating fudge.  It was OK, but a bit much for me.  Other folks RAVED about it.  So, yes, I would definitely come here on my own for dinner - or book an event here.  They are "old" pros.    One possible con?  It is an OLD place - so some of the decor is really authentic - so if you want a more polished look (like for a wedding?  I would, personally never do a wedding here) you may be turned off.  For a High School reunion or Corporate event?  PERFECT!!!!!

I am not an Applebee's fan.  I have been to this one twice though - once I was dragged here by my inlaws - who LOVE chain restaurants.  (I guess they make them feel "safe"),  The food was marginal and the service was, of course, by disinterested teenagers.  Not my idea of a good time.

It's pretty small and there are lots of homeless who gather here - but when they have an event it can be very nice on a warm summer evening.  Philly needs its green spaces - so I am glad its here - I just wish we could help our homeless community more.  My 5 y.o. is frightened by many of them.

We live walking distance from PAFA and I take my 5 year old here often.  She is well known in the (free) student gallery and the great gift shop.  Additionally, PAFA'a new annex (not so new anymore) was the site for my child's school's annual charity auction.  PAFA was a terrific venue for this and the administrative staff os PAFA were so friendly and great to work with.    The exhibits change throughout the year and we are always looking out for the next "big" thing.  So happy to know about the art classes for kids and teens, too.

Cute little place with a limited menu and a selection of Viso's partries.  We come here for cannoli when we are too lazy to drive to Viso's in Aston.  Friendly service and nice & clean inside.  Pleasant.

This is my go-to CVS as it is nearest my house. The (one and only) guy at the cashier was cute and also personable.  I had run-in to get Cadbury Cream eggs (not for me - really- for my boss.  I am trying to butter him up.  Seriousy - I don't  eat that $h!t.) and he told me exactly where to go.  Not bad.  Will be back.

We held our group's holiday party for 10 people here with an open bar and a small buffet and everything went so well.  Great service and good filling food like roast beef, ham and great mac and cheese. They also served individual garden salads in small torilla bowls - cute and tasty!  Fun and great times always at Oh! Shea's.

Ook.  I never want to go here EVER again. So bad.  Dim gray lighting, scattered merch and disinterested staff sporadically placed.  Just frikkin' awful.  It made the affluent suburbs feel ghetto. It made me long for the Target on Columbus Blvd in Philly.  (Still not as bad as the Walmart on Colombus).

I actually had a good experience here.  When I cam - about 7 PM on a Wednesday night - the place was nearly empty and I had a great cooked to order chicken cutlet sandwich. The food was great and the side salad I also ordered had fresh (iceberg) lettuce and lots of nice tomatoes and cucmber slices.  I would definitely pick up another quick meal here.  Npot sure about the pizza - the slices didn't appeal.  Maybe a whole pie - freshly baked would be a better option.

We have enjoyed coming to OOka for years now.  Whenever in Doylestown and we want sushi -it's where we go.  They offer alot of Americanized (fattening) non-traditional rolls, and the sashimi parfait (with strawberries).  Also some seared nigiri - one with foie gra which is a decadent treat.  I was not as impressed with the kitchen entrees - having tried the veggie yaki-udon which was bland.  My fiancee likes the chicken dishes, butusually we stick to sushi creaions here.  It can get crazy-crowded on weekends.

Very good.  Nearly 5 star for a yogurt place.  Vast variety of flavors - including a no-sugar added french vanilla that (to me) tasted better than the Tahitian Vanilla.  Double Cookies & Cream was great and the kiddo loves the NY cheesecake variety.  Oodles of candy and fruit toppings - and whipped cream if you ask.  Very friendly young female staff.  Clean and inviting.  Crazy parking lot - always is (Outback takes up half the spots).

Considering the limited amount of dining choices in the (dying) SPringfield Mall, my 8 year old was excited to get a chicken cutlet sandwich from Tony Lukes.  It was fine - but nothing to write home about. I know Tony Luke (and his lovely new-ish girlfriend) and have eaten at the Oregon Avenue location many times.  It rocks.  This location does not rock. But it is affordable and a viable alternative to the other mall choices.
Nice location in an affluent shopping center that is always crowded on weekends. Clean and comfortable,  Medium sized with seating and a retail area.  (Not a teeny one and not huge).

2 or 3 tops.  Run of the Mill off the rack mens suits and separates. If you don't care about looking like everybody else - or have little fashion sense or interest - then shop here.  It is CHEAP.  (And it can show!)

Now they get 5 stars!  They offer gift cards. Between this and the $25 fruit baskets (I bought 4 of them at Thanksgiving time) and my everyday fruit & veggie needs, Gentile's can't be beat!  Much love!

CM is like PC (Plato's Closet) but for grown-ups. I boil everything I buy (or dryclean it).  That said, you can sift through the racks and sometimes find nearly new or tags-on-new clothing at a fraction of the price.  Caveat Emptor, baby. Happy Hunting.

The Clay Studio is a great find.  If you have kids - they have Clay Camps and programs for kids of all ages to learn about pottery and ceramic arts.  For adults there are ever-changing exhibits and great merchandise.  The organization is well run and we worked with Clay Studio to host a silent auction and reception there for the Friends Child Care Center.  Management was great and the have a kitchen facility.  Can't wait until my little one can go to clay camp (starts at age 5).  You can have your garage parking validated at Parkominium up the street.

Better - much better - but still very heavy-handed with the Olive oil on nearly every dish. The burrata of the day ($16 was truly outstanding - served with paper thin slices of speck and roasted peppers and beets (purple and gold).  Gorgeous and delicious.  The table-side filleted whole branzino (enough for 2 to share at $36) was perfectly cooked and served with roasted veggies (terrific) and potatoes.  A side of broccoli-rabe was textbook - but again - drowning in garlic and olive oil.    Service was perfection.  Decor is beautiful. Love this place.

Even on a PACKED Saturday night my 9 year old & I had a terrific time at Ruby's.  We opted to sit at the counter rather than wait for a table and watch the plethora of fries & burgers being whisked away.  El kiddo had an "Orange 50/50" milk shake and a fried seafood platter (so healthy, i know!).  She even likes the coleslaw here.  Not gourmet, not fancy - but good family fun.  Surprisingly good service on such a busy, busy night.

Love these guys!  The name-sake ravioli is delicious and affordable - usually frozen and many varietys.  Great tortellini, too - meat or cheese (I love the meat).  Great hoagies and sandwiches.  SHARP Provolone.  The real deal - straight from sou-philly.  Oh - and they support the Mummers - so go to P&S!
Spacious, clean and well stocked Staples with office supplies and computer equipment too.  Convenient to my office.
Too expensive but I wash in a pinch and needed gas N.O.W. They also have a car wash.  No issues.
believe it or not we had a sandwich tray CATERED from Barrels (to a swanky law firm no less) and the food was Di-VINE!!!!!  The chicken cutlet with rabe was perfection on a roll.

3 stars is really stretching it. I have never, ever, EVER been an Outback fan - but my parents seem to love it there for some reason.  Anyhow, a female co-worker/friend suggested it so we went for a very early dinner at 4:30 PM.  The good part was because we were so early the place was empty and we got decent service.  The food?  Sub-par at best.  The best bite of the night was the steamed broccoli (which was loaded with butter, I think.)  Everything is oversalted/overseasoned.  I ordered the 10 oz. ribeye, rare - and it was tasty but way, way too salty.  Had I known (or remembered - as I have not been to an Outback since 2012) I would have asked for lightly seasoned. Supermarket quality steaks.  Definitely not Choice and NOT Prime meats here. It's a CHAIN, people.  The "steakhouse" mac & cheese was a salt lick.  Inedible to the point I had to send it back. I asked for plain cavatappi pasta in its place.  PLAIN.  It came drenched in butter.   So if you are like most of middle America and like over-buttered, over-salted, heavily caloric food?  This is your place.  Meanwhile - we all ate and all survived. I can grill a better steak dinner myself at home. Seriously.
It's been here for eh ver. Not much good I can say about McDonald's.  Clearly I'm NOT lovin' it.

Always a long line during the weekday lunch rush.  I bide my time in line by picking through the toss-displays of umbrellas and boxer shorts.  Oh - and a sample of DREAM or HEAVEN if they have the testers out.  I have found good deals here - and it is an outlet so pickings can be slim.  If you are patient and don't mind a complete LACK of customer service, you may be able to find some decent clothing here for your kid or yourself.  I get socks here when I can find the kind i like - they are $7.50 a pair at the "regular" GAP and $3-4 a pair here.  SAME exact merch.  Just cheaper.  I love that!

I have only gotten juice here - not any food - but for juice (if 4 seasons is closed - which is was) in a pinch this place is fine. (Smoothies and fruit juices, a few vegetable choices).  Nice selection of middle eastern parties, too.  With so many choices in the RTM - this one is not up too high on the list - but seems OK. Been here for years!

OK, I gotta update my review of OOKA, as we just had an incredibly GOOD night here.  Our first time coming with our 4 (nearly 5) year old and sitting at the teppanyaki grill. (No, it's not Hibachi.  It's teppanyaki, thank you very much.)  We made a same day reservation for 6:45 PM on a Saturday (tonight, actually) and were accomodated and got in just before it started to get packed & crazy - as Saturday nights at Ooka D-town are known to be.  Service was truly excellent.  The waiter and teppanyaki chef were both extra accomodating to the little princess - the chef even made an extra Onion Volcano during the teppanyaki grilling portion.  She was mesmerized.  The place had an unusually high number of kids and families - I guess I never noticed this before because every ogther time we have come sans bebe (thank god!) and usually we sit in the sushi dining room or at the sushi bar.  Once again I ordered the Seared striped bass with foie gras suishi and once again it was melt-in-your-mouth delicious.  Next time 2 orders!  It's that good.   Toro was a bit of a disappointment (but at only $7.00 I had to try one).  I also ordered 2 pieces of Maguro ($5.50 for 2 pieces vs. $7 for ONE toro - they said "O" but I bet it was "Chu".)  Anyhow the toro was a little gristley and the Maguro was perfect.  Next time I'll be skipping the toro and loading up on Hamachi (perfect and ocean-fresh) and the aforementioned seared bass with foie.  DD & DH had teppanyaki meals -which are never a HG for me.  DD loved her shrimp, noodles and rice.  She wouldn't touch the veggies. Hubby ate his chicken meal but said (as predicted) it was too heavy on the soy and the margarine (yes they slather that grill in grease).  Bringing kids?  The teppanyaki will keep them very entertained.  Want a better meal?  Order sushi based dishes.  (Just my opinion.)  Go Ooka.  What a change from the Domino's pizza and ultra-conservative Christian Bookshop that used to inhabit the space.

It's basically a pizzzaria - with BRIGHT orange & yellow decor.  It is mobbed with families and toursts (and tourist families) who have no rel lower priced options in Peddler's Village or Penn's Purchase.  A quick slice of pizza and a drink - and use the bathroom - and off you go to shop some more.  I wish they would have been more accomodating to us - as we had planned to take a large group here for my daughter's birthday. No reservations on weekends.  Whatever.  It's OK.  And it's there.

Went here for a late lunch yesterday (a recession Monday) and the place (huge dining area) was nearly empty.  My friend insisted on coming here as I likely never would have (Can't deal with Public House aka "the Pube" and knew I would likely not like it here anyhow).  Well, It's a sports bar (big f-in' surprise) - and they brew LOUSY iced tea. Service was fine (there were 3 waitresses just standing around so the one assigned to us jumped at the chance to do something).  My friend had the Fieldhouse Burger - which he enjoyed, although I snagged one of his good lookin' french fries and OOK - a mouthful of salt.  My fieldhouse salad (dressing on the side, no bacon) was surprisingly 3 star.  If I am ever forced back here I will order it again.  So 2-3 stars it is.  Blasting loud '80's music (Billy Ocean's "Get Outta My Dreams - Get Into My Car" was blaring) and ESPN and ESPN2 on every other flat screen.  It's so not my thang, but OK for what it is.  A MEH sports bar.

OMG Amazing!  The adobo pork, smoked chicken salad, OMY Fingers (kinda like tiny fried lumpia stuffed with pork) are all wonderful. Elaine (LaLaine?) and her staff (family) are terrific.  Can't wait to come back and try the brisket and rubs.  A true gem! Go there NOW!

Nearly 5 stars - the food is 5 star for sure! I had a huge platter (ate about hald) of Chilaquiles with 2 delicious fried eggs over top.  ($8.00 for lunch)  Wonderful service and delicious, authentic selections - like Chiles en Nogado (the real McCoy with Pomegranate seeds - in season!)  My friends had the Burrito Maya and it looked great (I had one small bite - and it was!).  What a find!

Stopped in here for all things - breakfast?  A freshly grilled laffa with egg & cheddar. A little light on the veggies - it was early in the AM and nothing was prepped yet.  I will come back and try them at lunch time.  Laffa was super fresh (grilled to order) and tasty.

Let me preface this by saying (again) that I am really not a steak 'n hoagie kinda gal. But Lee's makes a darned good one (both steaks and hoagies are good here - and believe me, they are 2 entirely different species in the sandwich kingdom).  I have had a very good chicken cheese steak with shrooms here within the last 5 years.  Prior to that - probably 12-15 years ago (yes really) I used to have roast beef hoagies with lettuce, tomato, no oil, no onion.  (But this is probably too far back to comment on.  Decor is sparse - and functional.  Fairly clean - BIG PLUS and I would feel just fine taking friends or my 3 year old to grab a meal here.  Take out is even better.  (wink, wink)  I honestly don't remember if they sell Beer. I highly doubt it given PA's restrictive liquor laws.

I really want to give them higher marks as this GORGEOUS (large) facility has enormous potential, a top-ranked chef and a fabulous sounding menu.  Service was good, but dish execution had too many things wrong to be ignored.  My Kir Royale was made with flat prosecco - I clearly got the last of an opened bottle, but that is even forgivable if the meal was good.  My husband's dish was excellent - if a bit over-sauced (tender, home-made Cavatelli in s rosa/blush sauce).  I would discover first hand how heavy they pour the olive oil. I ordered the burrata of the day (m.p. was $17 - OUCH - but OK.) but that was NOT what was brought to me.  Instead i got a "doctored up" caprese - and I am a HUGE fan of caprese so I agreed to accept the (beautiful) plate and began to eat it.  Drowned in Olive oil, and the Plum tomato (served quarted) tasted fermented.  It was not visibly rotten - but it really, truly was.  I am happy to say they took the salad ($14) off the bill. Please ease up on the sauce and oil!  Next time - and yes, there WILL be a next time - but not right away - I am getting a pasta (folks one table over had the pan-grilled chicken parm and another table ordered rigatoni with one enormous meatball) - they looked amazing.  This is really a 4 star place - and has potential to be a 5 star place - but we are off to a rocky start with 'Teca.  Oh - and the $8 Tira Misu in a mason jar is light as air and delectable.  Prices are far too high for this neck of the woods - but they have ALOT of overhead to pay for including party rooms and glorious pizza oven-bar that seats 16 and a HUGE cocktail bar, wine cellar and much more.  And they are STILL building.  WOW.  I am hoping they will make improvements and hit their stride soon.  We had a far better meal at the "original" West Chester "Teca in 2013.  See you in 5-7 months! (Can't afford sooner.) This is a great special-occiasion or date (not neccessarily a first date) place.

Well, this is what we're kinda stuck with - considering that we can't afford to get ALL of our shopping done at Whole Paycheck (aka Whole Foods) or Trader Joe's.  Cleaner than Ackamee and less Ghetto than ShopRite (some may argue this).  SuperFresh is our big-chain grocery store of choice based on location and convenience.  A few of the checkers "K" and "Sophie" are actually nice, and know us and our DD because we come here nearly every Sunday.  The produce can be marginal so you must be careful.    The deli usually has a line, so we nearly always skip it. We tend to shop aisle by aisle based on a list and coupons (yes, I am currently both BROKE and anal.).  DH like to get 12 packs of canned sodas when they are on special, and I usually get snack foods (healthy-ish when possible, Orange Juice boxes and yogurt for the l'il one.  We need this SuperFresh - for better or for worse.  It's where we've chosen to shop and although it's not super clean, it's THERE and that's why we're there as well.  Oh, and as mentioned by another yelper - they always play SLAMMIN' classic rock - usually loud enough so I can hear it!  (Pink Floyd, Jethro Tull - amazing!  I love that!)

While i can't speak for the other baked goods (and I have had many at the RTM location), the traditional cheese and chocolate chip filled-to-order cannoli at the Comcast outpost of termini Bros. are TERRIFIC.  Very crisp cannoli shells and a thick, but not gelatinous, creamy ricotta based filling.  Soooooo good.

2 words:  Tomato Pie!  Corropolese tomato pie is truly wonderful (and a huge one will feed an army of guests - which is exactly what we did at my sister-in-law's house for a family party) - rich and tomato-ey with a dusting of parmesan cheese on top (no mozzarella).    Eat it hot - or room temp - or even cold the next day is still pretty good.  They also make enormous hoagie trays - replete with Italian meats and cheeses - onions, lettuce shreds and tomatoes sliced paper thin.  A great catering option - Superbowl, birthday or otherwise.

I am giving a high review to Aerosoles because both myself and my 5 year old (yes, 5) enjoy trying on shoes here.  I was even able to find some decent, low priced (39.99 - 59.99) comfortable "classic" shoes that are great for work.  There is a very nice man at the Walnut Street Aerosoles (Jax?? Jack? - white gay guy - very nice) who has sold me now 2 pair of "moc croc" loafers.  Plus they humored my little one by letting her march around the store in faux leopard, high-helled ankle booties.  She was in heaven.  Had they not been $99 I might have bought them just for her dress up!   Meanwhile - I like the shoes here.   Not a holy grail - but good, cheap workaday shoes that (sometimes) don;t look too old-lady.

We did not stay here - but we did stop here for a dire emergency bathroom break for our 6 year old.  Lobby was nice and clean and the front desk staff cheerfully directed us to the restroom.  Asked about room rates on the way out and rack rates are $159 - $209.

Believe it or not I am pleasantly surprised in a good way by Rex's Pizza.  If you go from 5-7 PM Mon - Thurs you can get $1.00 slices and $2.50 beers.  My little daughter loves happy hour here - the slices not the beers!  I also got a tuna melt and a slice of Baklava to go one time.  The melt was really good.  Hot & fresh on rye bread.    The baklava was little dry.  I wouldn't get it again.  Meanwhile, this place is a little run-down and old-school (with plastic swivel chairs and orange booths.  But it's on our way from school to home - so for $1.00?  Ya can't beat it.  (Regular price $2.10 for a plain jumbo slice.)  Not sure how they are for take out - but i do know they have delivered MANy pizza's to my little one's old day care.  Every Wednesday was Rex pizza for lunch.  Oh - and the owner (maybe manager) guy is really nice.  And kinda cute - but he probably thinks I am waaaaay old.

Tom at "I Hate" Steven SInger treated us great and even hooked us up with "swag" when we visited recently with "the real" Steve SInger.  A good selection of full and 1/2 eternity bands in a variety of metals and settings. Very "eye clear" stones that appear to be well cut.  So happy.

So glad this place is here! They carry all the "health food" standards and a few unique packaged goods and products.  A small fresh produce section - but all organic and good. Clean, well stocked aisles.  So happy to support them.

Vernalicious trekked to the 'burbs and boy are we ever grateful. The menu is limited - but everything is delicious!  I had the BLT & A and it was perfection at $8.50 - or add Smoked Salmon to it for $12. Many others tried the pulled pork grilled cheese (or plain grilled cheese) and it looked great, too.  Thank you, soooooo much for hauling out to Chesterbrook and PULEEEZE come back.  We need you!  WhooHoo!  As good as you can get from a truck with door to door service. Oh - and the lady called me "hon".  Adorbs!

Food still sucks - but we had such great service for our group of 6 (CinemaSuites seating is great!) by Dell and others.  Dell is so friendly and wonderful.  Give her a raise!  Do NOT order any of the sushi - blargh! Also the food pricing is ridiculous for the crap quality that you get.    I had a frozen Mango Margarita and it was fine. The movie itself was great - and we all had an enjoyable evening.
A quick iced coffee from the kind Indian lady at the DD on the corner of 16 and I'm off...  This location is smaller than some.

Ok - I am being nice and giving 3 stars, but I really want to give them 2. Don't get me started on UO.  We have a long post collegiate, complex relationship.  When they first opened and had only a few stores (I shopped at the one near Penn in the early 90's and will review that one soon) they seemed so cool.  Now it's a bit played out and man, they jacked up the prices.  I mostly get accessories and socks here now - the pants fall apart.  (And for 60 bux??)  Oh I miss the good old days.  It seemed better back then.

I concur wholeheartedly with Emily.  My family and I have been coming here for year.  We especially crave the summer peaches.    My nearly 4 year old daughter has been apple and blueberry picking here. And don't miss the fresh-fried cider doughnuts in the main shop.  ($1 a piece or you can buy more and save.)  They are worth the calories.  I adore Solebury Orchards.  I hope yelping it won't give away our secret.

Penn's Purchase is not like it was by long shot.  The Eitienne Aigner outlet is gone.  Many of the outlets are not really that discountred anymore.  But I still go to the Aerosoles and Leggs/Hanes/Bally outlets.  Just never at Xmas time.  The place is a mad house of displace New Yorkers.  Loved it more a few years back - still like it, just miss my old faves.

Brand-spankin' new.  I hope they can keep it this clean and well maintained. Everyone is on their best behavior.  Fresh produce, pre-cut veggie trays and fruit bowls, gorgeous deli counter.  I will be back - but again, I hope it can STAY this way.
This place is no=w called Delicatessan with new management, staff and menu items.  Please see my complete review under"DELICATESSEN"

OMG!!!   Order the OMG -  it's so good!  A perfectly cooked REAL Italian Chicken Cutlet on a seeded Italian loaf (not a roll - a LOAF) with thinly sliced tomatoes, FRESH milky mozzarella (not that plasticky garbage) and pesto sauce (I get mine light on the pesto) which is fresh, bright green and uses a very goodtasting olive oil.  Near perfection!  LOVELOVELOVE IT!  Can't wait to try the pasta - and the salad with eggplant and mozz.

Went here on the recommendation on a friend and was NOT disappointed.  Came in early (5:30) on a Saturday night and it was still slow.  By the time we left at 6:40 it was filling up.  Even though most people probably go to the Outback Steakhouse next door - I would say to come here instead.  Great service and solid Thai dishes.
