We only oredered one item off of the Japanese section of the menu - a Tuna/Avocado Salad - served in the avocado shell.  YUM! ($12).  My fave - classic Tom Kha - was heavy on the lime juice but still delish. Steamed Thai dumplings were light and luscious.  (Will definitely get these again.) Drunken Noodles were a tongue-tingling treat.  Perfectly cooked noodles - tender not mushy.  LOVE IT.  Good service.  Why not a 5?  They neeed to CLEAN the fabric ceiling drapes - they are loaded with dust.  Eew. Also the Thai iced coffee was not great - and I usually love this.  There's was clyingly sweet and the coffee was so bitter. ($3) Won;t get it again.  Meal for two (no alcohol, I think it's BYO).  Note:  I have now been back 2 or 3 more times and the dishes are all good - sushi is fresh and Thai food is great.

I finally got a chance to try Estia - I walk by it all the time. We were part of a LARGE private event held in the huge downstairs ballroom.  You could easily have a wedding here (150 people or less is probably best - we had 187 in our gfroup and the room holds 180 max. We were crammed in like sardines).  The tables were pre-set with salad (romaine with dill dressing - quite tasty), bread, pita and hummus (yum!).  Entrees and dessert platters were served family style.  Food was delicious and excellent - especially the Branzino over "greek-style" roasted veggies - potato, zucchini, eggplant, peppers) - all were terrific.  Pasta alla Greca is an inexpensive way to feed a crowd.  Tasty - but too light on the spinach, IMHO.  Deseert of a very nutty baklava (good but not the best I've tried) and a moist bordering on wet-with-syrup walnut cake.  People either loved it or hated it - I enjoyed it, but it is WET and very, very, cloyingly sweet.  Note:  They have a private wine room for dining up tpo 14 people. I sense a party in my future at ESTIA!  Great for pre/post theatre, too.  They know how to get you in and out.

Chambers offers a terrific brunch, and great lunches and dinners.  Our family has gone there for years.  At brunch time (which can get really crowded so go early) they have an omlette station and a very nice (and cute) young man pouring waffle batter.  It's a bit of a wait but so worth it for a fresh hot waffle that you may top with fruit or whipped topping (alas it was NOT real whipped cream).  Yum-my!  For dinner, my mom favors the petite filet which is cooked to order, and the strawberry salad.  I adore the pear salad with goat cheese and a sweet poppyseed vinaigrette.  Add a heavenly grilled, sliced duck breast from just $4.00 more.  (I add it every time!)  I have dreams about the "duck salad".  That duck breast was crispy-skinned and yet medium rare inside and soooooo tasty.  Chambers is a marvelous place to go and it's right in the heart of Doylestown.  And, Matt - the Chef - is a doll!

This is now my go-to local Walgreen's. So far it';s been just OK.    Yes, the store is clean and well run.  Plenty of parking. Not crowded.  But - they did not have my medication in stock (to be fair they got it in the next day and I did not have an urgent need for it), but it was inconvenient to have to stop by twice.  Meanwhile - the 2 female pharmacists I have spoken to were both great.  I'll be back.

We had a delightful lunch for 5 that far surpassed my expectations for in-mall Chinese.  Edamame and Gyoza apps were tasty.  Lunch entrees were reasonably priced and perfectly sized.  Some of the best (basic) Chicken and brocolli - tender white meat and not gloppy.  Outstanding shrimp lo mein with thinner than usual noodles - not overloaded with onion.  NOT GREASY.  A pleasure.  Rainbow shrimp was great, too- and not skimpy on the shrimpy. Friendly, efficient service and lovely decor.  Full bar and sushi (did not try it yet.).  We can't wait to return

This supermarket is very nice and BIG - it's basically a re-do of the old Superfresh - and now it is a GIANT.  The produce department had many GOOD selection (even in snowy January) and my little girl loves to use the label printers - where you can weigh and pre-scan your produce so that check-out moves way more smoothly.  Tom, our "bagger" and Felicia our cashier were lovely.  NICE market!

Matt Ridgeway (formerly at LaCroixand other top NYC restaurants) is back to his Buck County roots.  He has become a purveyor of unique charcuterie products, particularly honey cured bacon, guanciale, duck proscuitto, duck rillettes, and smoked salmon caviar.  (Steelhead)  Using his fathers home-avaiary-farmed honey and other local ingredients, Chef Ridgeway provides delicious products for chefs and home cooks.  He reall knows his stuff anf boy can he throw down.  Check out porcsalt!  (Even if you don't eat pork.)

A sub-par Chipotle with a "long, skinny" weird  layout and not enough trash receptacles.  They seem incapable of making a Quesadilla here - stick to the burritos and bowls.  Not awful but I won't be rushing back.  Fast food at its classic mediocrity.

We had a vey nice experience on a CROWDED summer Sunday around noon ish - we had a party of 6 and were amazed at how short the wait was -  it could have been much worse.  We all ordered different breakfasty things - Croissant sandwiches were a big hit.   I had crepe - real crepes (actually just one big one) stuffed with FRESH sliced strawberries (not strawberry glop) and sliced fresh banana.  So good!  A nice gathering place with a salad bar and all the diner staples. Parking lot was JAMMED with cars.

Ah, yes, the Chinatown Wawa.  It's a Wawa folks, so it's got smokes, drinks, junky snacks and most everything you need in a pinch.  This one is usually crowded (right near the bus station and the Gallery) and a little grungy.

I wanted to love it.  Really, I did. I had the fried Chicken, mac 'n cheese and collard greens. After all, if OPRAH loves their Mac (and I think she won against Bobby Flay in a mac smack-down), then so should I, right?!  All were they way they are supposed to be.  (By the book)  But the mac was way too heavy - and I didn't happen to get any of that good crust on the top layer.  The chicken was sooooo salty.  Like eating saltines in the Sahara. And very, very greasy (but hell - it is FRIED chicken.)  The greens were perfect.  I give them a 3 stars for food and the grotty digs of 30th Street.

Ok yelpers and oenophiles - hold on to your hats!!!!  Moro in Wilmington - tucked away in a semi-residential area - is a real find.  The chef-owner has an ENORMOUS wine collection and the selection of wines - bottles and by the glass is astounding.  The 2-level restaurant - open for about 7 years - is scheduled for a re-model soon - but we hope they won't change the FABULOUS 5 star menu choices.  DH & I sat in a lovely round booth on the 1st floor.  The upstairs was FULL with a private wine dinner party - maybe 60 people - and LOADS of stemware.  We started with drinks - a $12 red wine for him, a Moro (Sicilian Blood Orange) Bellini (made with house Prosecco) for me - $10.  We read over the extensive menu including a mind boggling array or antipasti (for 2 or more).  Eventually we decided.  DH started with a delectable Duck Confit salad with FRESH greens, shaved parm (the good stuff) on top and a mouthful of buttery-shreds of confit in EVERY bite.  I had the tuna tartare - which was served over "smashed" avocados - so it was kinda like a tuna tartare guacamole.  It was lightly sprinkled with Hawaiian pink salt (I told them to go light and they did!!!) for a terrific crunch.  YUM-CITY!  Our 5 star entrees did not disappoint - with the daily special of proscuitto-wrapped venison over polenta for him, and a decadent papardelle with crispy pork jowl pieces and fresh green peas.  Here's the only negative (which is why I am giving them 4 stars instead of 5,) - the a/c on the first floor was simply NOT sufficient.  We were seated near the wood-burning (gorgeous) oven and we were FRYING.  I mean sweating-hot frying.  SO hot, in fact - we moved upstairs (about 10 degrees cooler) to have dessert on couches in the bar area.  Dessert was great, too - a berry creme brulle (a little too soupy) topped with a generous assortment of vanilla-sugared berries - black, blue, straw, rasp) and FLASH-FRIED mint.  You could taste the olive oil on the mint leaves.  I could have just eaten the topping.  (The creme itself was not the greatest ever - but still very tasty, indeed.)  Our server Michael is a pro - and a great guy. The upstairs bartender whop handled us from dessert on (Grappa or Limocello, anyone?) was also very personable.  I can't WAIT to return - but you GOTTA solve the a/c problem.  Soooooooo close to a 5 star night!

Our group hosts not one but TWO parties here every year - one for the Holidays and one in late June.  Chris, Pat and the rest of the bartenders and servers treat us like good friends and keep the booze and tasty bar food flowing.  This time they had an EXCELLENT, truly excellent crab cake (sandwich or over a salad).  It was packed with crabmeat and very tasty.  Yes, this is a casual bar with "bar food" but every time I come it gets better and better.  Great classic rock tunes, your favorite sport on big TV screens and a place to just be yourself and relax.  There is no pretense at Oh! Shea's and we love them for that!
No issues, quiet, clean, has a kitchen. Easy check in and out. Breakfast included.  Right near Mall and walking distance to Joe's Crab Shack (next door) and Capital Grille.

Our 8 year old just LOVES ruby's.  Everything from the train that runs around the track on the ceiling to the red & white decor and uniforms and the "old fashioned" feel.  It's really 3 star food - salads, burgers and fried chicken and fish - but it's a fun place to take the kiddo. Kiddo always gets a (small) milkshake. I usually splurge on a vanilla diet coke ($2.89 - but free refills).  She also loves the huge gumball machine in the front.  Service is OK - can be great if you get a good server.  (Lots of teens and college-aged folks working here).  Not bad!

Stopped in here (cash only) after a production at Arden Theatre. Our 7 year old said it was awful and the cake batter flavor made her sick.  The heat from the 4 yogurt machines (one was broken) was unbearable and the cashier was more interested in picking up her chinese take-out.  Will not go back.  There are many, many better fro-yo spots in Philly.

This is a smaller outpost of Rita's with a few places to park and friendly teenaged gals running the show during peak summer months.  Our 8 year old loves it and a kiddie size is perfect (plenty) for her or for me.  Custard, water ice, blendinis - yum!  We like the Ria's in Aston a touch more for the big parking lot, though.
They're there when you need them for smokes, snacks and coffee. Decent location and service.

Support local and sustainable agriculture! Shop here.  (And say hi ti PICKY of messy & picky - who works here.)  Some of the best seasonal produce and cheeses from local dairies.  I only wish they had larger digs - and i here they may be expanding very soon.  Hooray!  (P.S.  I think they may also be affiliated with the White Dog Cafe.)
3 words:  Butter Bean Honey.  'Nuff said. Go there now!

If you can get a seat at the nearly-always-packed- counter, Profi's is a welcome respite from the bustle of RTM.  I enjoy the fruit filled crepes and get mine with banana & strawberries - no "glop".  I do not like saucey crepes and Prfi always makes mine to order.  (They do a great job - and I really enjoy the crepes themselves which are lightly sweet.  I have never tried their savory crepes - but I'm always tempted to. I am glad they are in the Market.

It has everything you need for crafts at reasonable prices.  A good place for DIY wedding favors, kids crafts, art projects, framing and more.  And I am not one for glue guns - but wow - such a selection.  The staff is underpaid and pretty disinterested - so do your own research and then buy your stuff and move on.  There is a nice selection of Crayola and other kids craft items.  The lines on weekends can be painfully long at holiday times.

I LOVE coming here.  The guy who runs the place is terrific and best of all - even among the dusty, cramped aisles - I get the very best price around for Eukeneuba bagged food and supplements for my pampered pooch.  No, it ain't Petsmart (and thank goodness for that!) but it is wonderful in its grimy glory.  Long live Delchester feed! (And you can go to Gentile's next door!)

Hit or miss - but tonight, thankfully I hit big on girls clothing. And no line (But I went at 5 PM on a Tuesday).  This place can really bomb so the 4 stars is a generous offering. But when I hit here, I hit big!

I was super hungry and Delilah's (at 30th Street Station) actually looked good to me tonight so I got a chicken leg/thigh (fried) for $3.50 and a small mac 'n cheese ($5.00) and I gotta say - they were both great.  The mac, I still think is over-rated - but the fried chicken was not over-salted this time and was greasy but not disgustingly so.    For whatever reason - it worked better for me tonight.

Service by Drew (Andrew) for out group of 6 ladies was terrific.  The food itself?  Meh.  Overpriced and not healthy.  But meanwhile we had a grand time and this is a mid-priced option for a girls night.  Relaxing (we went on a Monday evening and the theatre was nearly empty) and you can drink alcohol (albeit overpriced mid-grade stuff) and eat (calorie laden "fun foods") and watch a flick.  No issues.

Walked in. Walked right out.  Yes - a cute little dog with an eye infection happily greeted me at the door, but the place REEKED of polish fumes/acetone.  Get a better ventilation system and I might come back. Beauty Nails down Pennell Road is better - and China Nail or Treny Nail in Media are better still.  Unhealthy.

Lia's is a great choice for a group luncheon. They have catered 2 events for our group (over 200 in attendance) now and both were excellent from both a food and service perspective.  One event was at the Boothwyn location, the other at the Austin Room (Nicer - in my opinion).  They have 3 locations.  Buffet style food and an open bar (or cash bar as you prefer). You teens/young adults passed a few (frozen) hors d'ouvres.  Excellent carving station with roast beef. We brought in our own cakes.  Well executed - so happy.

I am seriously not kidding when I tell you that I came here with my (now) husband when we were dating and could absolutely not get any privacy.    We stayed for one night only - maybe 6 hours really - and found the room to be clean and comfortable.  Don't ask, don't tell.

Garden Bar and 2 sliders (I got 1 beef and 1 turkey) comes with fries - I subbed mac 'n cheese for 1.99 more - NOT GOOD.  Gloppy Cheese-Wiz/Velveeta with 5-6 flabby elbows buried.  Meanwhile, the garden bar/salad bar was surprisingly good. Beef slider was nice, turkey on was dry (Granted for both I requested mayo and ketchup on the side).  High calorie, moderately priced, bug portions. Middle-American "safe' chain foods which I usually loathe.  Had a surprisingly decent time here. (This is the one in Springfield Mall - there is also one at Granite Run Mall).  $8.95.  (Plus $1.99 - but I would not do that ever again!)

I loathe Domino's so 2 stars is pretty darned generous coming from me. The only reason we got pizza here is because my frugal father in law had a coupon (He normally gets Papa John's - which is still mediocre at best).  This is a teeny-tiny take-out only "kiosk" - small store. Not for eating in!  Yick.

We ate a lovely lunch here today.  Service was slow, but pleasant.  Our server, Lisa did a terrific job with our party of 8 and everything was served as ordered.  I had the Chadwick's chopped salad (minus the bacon, dresssing on the side) which was terrific.  And for $10.95 it is gargantuan.  Topped with a warm, sliced, grilled chicken breast.  The interesting addition?  Shaved white chocolate.  YUMMY.  CInnamon sweet potato fries were cold, but still addictive.  A nice place - very upscale "country club" decor.  The only complaint?  Very slow service.  Slow for a hostess to greet us, and slow to order and get our food.  Don't come here if you are in a rush.  Thankfully we weren't or I'd have to give it 2-3 stars.  Food is GREAT!

I actually like this branch of Staples - the manager Mark is very nice.  He may not be there any more.    I get items printed here for work and also have purchased school and office supplies for my 12 year old middle schooler.  No issues.

The have "Black Velvet" apricots (Apriums/Pluots) - a succulent cross between plum and apricot, this summer.  Also Mango Nectarines.  They are CASH ONLY.  Don't forget to check out the refrigerator case WAY in the back where they stock Claudio's fresh mozzarella - straight from South Philly.  YUM!!!!

A well organized, well executed group trip (all 30 of us in canoes - no tubers nor kayaks this trip) for the 2.5 hour trip (Left in the AM at 9:30 AM (Actually got into the water at 10:05).  Dave, our bus driver, was friendly and helpful.  A wonderful and SAFE experience for all including our 10 year old and a friends' 4 year old.  We'll be back!

A fine selection of meat and poultry products and friendly, attentive service, but boy do you pay for that.  I wound up getting 2 lbs of fresh chicken breast for 3.99 per lb. I also tried their steak tips.  They offer good looking prepared foods, salads, sandwiches and there us a cheerful place to eat there if you wish.  We need more butcher's so I will support them, but I pay less for my duck breasts direct from D'artagnan. So glad you carry D'artagnan, though.  I'll be back!

Chambers offers a terrific brunch, and great lunches and dinners.  Our family has gone there for years.  At brunch time (which can get really crowded so go early) they have an omlette station and a very nice (and cute) young man pouring waffle batter.  It's a bit of a wait but so worth it for a fresh hot waffle that you may top with fruit or whipped topping (alas it was NOT real whipped cream).  Yum-my!  For dinner, my mom favors the petite filet which is cooked to order, and the strawberry salad.  I adore the pear salad with goat cheese and a sweet poppyseed vinaigrette.  Add a heavenly grilled, sliced duck breast from just $4.00 more.  (I add it every time!)  I have dreams about the "duck salad".  That duck breast was crispy-skinned and yet medium rare inside and soooooo tasty.  Chambers is a marvelous place to go and it's right in the heart of Doylestown.  I can't believe D-towners have not yet tried this place.
This one's not bad.  I get a small for $3.00 and it;s full of fruit - grapes, mango, melons, oranges - and they give you a banana with your order.

Pagano's is A-OK - just as yelp 3 star joints are.  An over-priced salad/hot food bar.  Good soups, pricey platters of hot food (often chicken cutlets and pasta) and pizza.  Plenty of seating and boy do they need it during the lunch rush.  A vast selection of yuppified bottled beverages.  Great if you work at Commerce Square - especially on a snowy or rainy day.  Convenient.  Lots of options, priced a bit high.

This is a true treasure for Philadelphia providing much needed green space.  It needs to be better maintained and I am fearful that this year's budget cuts will adversely affect the park system in Philly.  There are wonderful mansions to explore, ball fields, picnic areas and bike trails.  Love this park.

We go to both the Aston Library and the Middletown Library. Aston is newer (building is in a Municipal facility with nice bathrooms, etc.)  Easy to get on a computer (you can be on for 30 minutes) here. Also the children's area is well organized.  They don't seem to have as many kids activities here as at Middletown, though. If you have a young child (under 5 especially) check out both libraries for great FREE children's programming.  Oh - and READ.  read to your kid and have your kid read to you.

This is the "big-momma" state store on Chestnut - that is packed to the gills with both product and patrons - especially on a Thursday or Friday evening in spring/summer.  Wow.  The lines were so long you'd think they were giving it away! I got my chilled Prosecco and out the door to Kanella I ske-daddled.  Thank goodness they were here.

Wow!!! Such good values on certain things -like Globe artichokes, Haas Avocados and mini pumpkins.  (I won't ever buy pumpkins at Linvilla again!)  I am so glad I found this place - and starting at $20 they make fruit baskets - great for holiday gifts.  Oh - and it's mobbed.  I went on a Thursday at 4:30 and the parking lot was nearly full - I can only imagine what weekends must be like.

A definite improvement!  I had a wonderful facial (although it was pricey - at $120) with Kim who is an experienced and knowledgeable aesthetician.  5 stars for Kim for sure!  Her technique is excellent and my skin looked and felt wonderful afterward.  I also had a much anticipated "Raw Earth" pedicure with Cati - a 41 year veteran who has won Best of Philly several times.  This was a 3 star disappointment.  Cati herself is a sweetheart and does excellent work - but the pedi was rushed.  She worked on me for 35 minutes max, and then the next client was there - waiting.  Cati is in such high demand that she is just waaaaaay over booked (a compliment, yes, but to the detriment of client service).  I don't care to spend such high prices for an in & out.  That said, I will come back again - but next time for the regular pedi.  $15 - $20 more for a quick application of CND Raw Earth Scrub & Mask - not worth it.  The spa itself is gorgeous and well managed.  Aside from high prices, I would now recommend Phoenix - especially for tourists.  UPDATE: Crap!  its a day - and two days later and I broke out from the facial.  Nothing major but a bunch of small raised itchy bumps (pink - not red) along the jaw line and all over the face.   I think that nifty gommage she used was too much beta-hydroxy for me.  Too bad.

Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays the townhouse is offering a HUGE 3 course meal for $21.95 (ad $5 if you want the "slab" of tender prime rib.  Plus we had a $25 gift card from a friend so - what a great night with plenty of food and stellar service from Chris (Kris?) Christie who has been a server at TowneHouse for over 16 years.  The hostess greeted us like regulars even though we're not. I love to sit at the bar and chat and nibble of the free munchies(get there early for that).  My only complaint?  Clams casino - the topping was good but the clams themselves were not quite as fresh as they could be.  (A little fishiness detected.)  Veal parm was classicly prepared and so good. Oh - and they now have curbside caterin (Minimun 12 people) for $14 for App or salad and entree.  I will definitely be using this for my late summer bash!  A comforting, nostalgic, huge meal. Safe to take the parents or grandparents here, too!

Hadn't been here in a while and I was long over due. Delicious made to order crepes.  Prices have been raised since 2009 - but that's to be expected. Very good customer service from the gal up front and the man making the crepes.  (Choice of white or wheat flour - NICE!)  Love me a good quick crepe.
Jes had my first Jes-made glazed donught.  So fresh and perfect. Nice!

I am assuming this is the Starbucks on the lower lever of the Target at Springfield Mall?  If so - I had a perfectly acceptable experience here - ordered my usual Venti light ice green tea lemonade.  No issues.  Fourbucks aka Charbucks is pretty standardized.  I went on a weekday morning and it was not crowded - but I have seen it on weekends and it can get busy.

I am so saddened and frankly I am angry.   You know what - scratch the saddened.  I am angry.  In fact - I am mad as hell.  DH & I decided to have a late lunch (It was about 3:20) on a sunny Saturday afternoon and meandered into PYT.  There were about 5 clad-in-black young folk at the the hostess stand and before we were seated they said "cash only" (thank goodness they warned us - apparently the credit card machines were down).  This did not affect us - but the two tables near us had to write checks which were reluctantly accepted.  Things went from bad to worse once we were seated.  It was taking a long time to get out food (I ordered the PYT EAT BLT, DH ordered a double burger.).  Our male server came by (as if to ask "so, how is everything?") and I said, - any idea when our food will arrive?  He said "It will be here soon" and scurried away (I would bet money to quickly enter the order that I bet was never placed.)  15 minutes later a DIFFERENT male server plopped down the 2 plates and zipped off.  No cutlery, no napkins.  I called after him - no luck.  So I got up and followed him for a few feet and he turned around, apologized and got us some silverware.  OK, so we're eating - and then we see the table tent that says "A 20% gratuity will be added to your bill" (or something like that.  Well - we're a party of 2 (not 6 or more).  And we sure as hell don;t want to give them 20%.    But wait - it gets worse.  So I'm eating the BLT and there's no avocado on it (which there is supposed to be per the brunch menu).  I'm hungry and I'm not bothered much - but they charge $2.00 to put avo on a burger - so I would like them to not charge me for it on my avocado-less BLT.  So the first male server comes over and assures me that I will not be charged for the avo and offered to bring a side of it - but I don't want it now (I am 1/2 way through the meal.).  So we finish eating - and we ask for a check.  And we wait.  And wait.  And we're pissed.  Nobody ever comes.  So we estimate our bill (sans 20% assholes!!!) and leave the cash on the table and walk the F out.  The ladies at the table next to us (who had the personal check fiasco) said it best.  "Because they are guaranteed a 20% tip for EVERY table - there is no incentive for good service."  I will never, ever, ever go back to PYT. I was looking forward to the McThrill-made-famous Milkshakes, too.  The BLT was fine - very good.  Dh said the burger was fine. The service (and loud, pumping, headache inducing music - we heard a club-mix of Dolly Parton's 9 to 5) is just freakin AWFUL!!!!!  Such an epic service-related fail.

Expensive - but you get what you pay for - decadent treats at Miel.  Not a place for an "everyday coffee" - although some will beg to differ - but I love the mini-sized cakes and tarte tatin that is old-school elegant in the true (vraiment) French tradition.  Bonne chance!

Absolutely disappointed in a private event held in an upstairs room. ONE waiter passing tiny fried hors d'ouvres and ONE bartender at a jam packed cash bar.  Not enough staff and not enough food for the crowd of 100 plus.
A wonderful place to stock up on Asian sauces, seasonings and ingredients (ramen, noodles, frozen treats).  Also fresh veggies & meats (a little pricey).  Love!
I was a huge C21 lover when I lived in Manhattan, so I was thrilled to see an outpost in Philly. Snagged a Calvin Klein Dress for $70 (Marked down from $134).  We'll be back!

My 8 year old participated in the first annual Guac-Off (a guacamole conptetition) held at the Fleisher Art Memorial in South Philly.  We all had a blast preparing and serving guac for over 150 guests.  The folks at MANNA were terrific to work with and raised over $3500 to help feed critically ill Philly-area residents.  Their nutritious meals are literally, life-savers!  (And they taste great, too.  We support MANNA and the valuable work they do - plus they organize creative and fun FUNdraisers.  (Special thanks to Chef Keith, Katelyn, Lydia and Dan.)  Much love to MANNA!  (And don't forget to buy your holiday pies this year at one of the many MANN Pie in the Sky pick-up locations. (We like the pecan pie!)
I do not like shopping here.  The produce is never what I want - or it's wilted.  The prices are OK for somethings, but that Freezer (frozen food) section is like navigating a maze.  Not a fan.
Sometimes I find joy in the "little things"  - like the freshly baked anise biscotti from Termini Brothers.  Bliss!
Super crowded on a Saturday Morning around 11. Waiting in a very long line - and then again to pick up each hand-pulled drink.  Just OK as S-Bux goes.  But I was jonesin' for a $5 latte.

A great place to see a show (downstairs at any rate.)  We got great seats for Black47 and had dinner there pre-show.  The food was Irish themed (for Black47 and it was March 16!!!)  I thought my "boiled" dinner of corned beef and cabage was good. The rest of the menu was typical bar food.  Not great - but not inedible as others have said.  The show itself was great and we had a balcony front row sofa to sit on - and beer to drink.  No problems for me.

I shopped here today and altough i wound up not buying anything - I did try on about 8-10 pieces and LOVED 2 of them.  Lisa, the sales associate, was very helpful fetching my size and I felt bad tat I did not buy the $118 jeans - nor the $488 mauve/grey dressy jumpsuit.  I just can't justify the prices right now.  But it was fun to get some new fashion ideas.  I loved the dresses.  So flowy and light.

This seed/feed store is where I get Eukaneuba dry food and California Natural for my small breed dog.  The guy who owns/runs the place is very kind to me every time I come in.  They have better prices than Concord Pets in Aston, but not as good as the prices of the "big guys" like Petco and Pet Smart.  The store itself looks "grungy" - seed and stuff on the floor and the aisles are small and cramped - but they have EVERYTHING you could ever want for birds, cats, dogs, small mammals and horses.  I stop here on my way to Gentile's next door. I will continue to come here as I like to chat with the owner and he now carries the MSM/Glucosamine supplements that my dog actually likes.  (And again - slightly cheaper than Concord Pets and way cheaper than Drs. Foster & Smith.)

Nope.  Not very good Sorry - even though it's been around for-eh-ver, the food is just OK.  (Italian "red sauce" fare) and the place needs an overhaul.  I guess what makes it so awful for me is that a spider spun her web down onto my plate while I was eating there.  There was dust and cobwebs in the windowsill and that spider just clinched it for me.  I couldn't even finish my baked ziti.  Won't return.

Yes, you can EAT HERE - a very filling old-skool Polish lunch.  Our group of 11 tried nearly everything on the menu and it was all terrific.  Plus we got to go shopping afterward and stocked up on all our Polish faves like Ukranian style borscht, pierogies (oodles of different kinds) hams and kielbasi, chocolate covered marzipan and the BEST stuffed cabbage I have had since Czestachowa.  What a find!!!  Even takes plastic.  And they serve $3 beers.

One's experience at MAC can ary greatly depending on the make-up artist/sales person you get.  As a true product junkie, I have alot of MAC products - but in fairness I also have alot of other brands some more expensive and some less.  MAC does charge for Bridal and special occaision looks and they also offer lash application - which is great if you want it done right.  I like to get the bronzer and foundations from MAC. Once you know what color you are (I am NC15) you can not go wrong.

Better.  I have been back a few times - and they HAD the items I needed (and my very commonly prescribed medications in stock).  Friendly service. CLEAN store that never seems crowded (at least when I go.).  Plenty of parking.

Get your Griggstown Farm Duck Breast & Quail here! Plus Pot Pies!  Plus all that great seasonal, local produce.  LOVE IT HERE!!!!  Today I snagged some purple string beans, white eggplant, miniature sweet peppers (expensive but so cute), and some raw-milk cheese. Oh - and a box of teeny tiny red miniature cherry tomatoes.  Poppin' 'em like candy.  LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE!

Shopped here for dresses today - and Ann, was very helpful.  While I did not purchase the dress I liked most (it was $458 which is too high for me), I will check back in a few months to see if it goes on sale.    I absolutely LOVE the dresses here - light, flowy fabrics and fabulous fit.  (If they have your size.)  Of course, by the time it's on sale my size (fat cow 10) will probably be gone.  I fel very fat when I shop here as usually they only go up to size 10 or 12 and they are usually gone.   If you are a size 4 or smaller (lucky, lucky, you) you'll have better luck.  Are you a big girl?  Don't come here!

We took my 3 (now 4) year old to see the STAR WARS and Real Pirates exhibits and both were terrific. We also saw the Chronicles of Narnia - which was just ok.  This is a must-see for kids - and there is enough to keep the grown-ups interested, too.  Try to NOT go on a weekend when it is packed.  Also there were alot of broken exhibits and/or construction going on when we last visited.  Membership is a cost-effective option if you plan to visit multiple times.  BRING YOUR OWN FOOD/SNACKS - dining options are poor.

Smile Cafe has better food that Erawan which is why I am giving it 4 stars to Erawan's 3.  But I happen to like the new Thai Chef & Noodle Fusion place that just opened on Chesnut even better.  The service here is quick and friendly and the place is as big as a minute.    Seriously - it is very tiny in here and somewhat cramped.  It's like you are eating in someones apartment,  Lunch prices are reasonable.

I ate here in the early nineties and have not yet re-visited - so this review is based on a distant - but positive memory.  A great date place!  We had seafood and lobsters.  Large portions and stiff drinks.  I will review in more detail once I visit it again in the 2000's.

It's hit or miss at Daffy's for me.  I usually miss, but when I hit, I hit big and it's usually Children's clothes or shoes (women's or kids in my case.)  I have scored some fine Italian-made kids wear for a fraction of retail here.  If they HAPPEN to have the size you need - you're golden.  Otherwise - don't count on much help from the under-paid, under-educated staff.  The lines at lunchtime can move at a snail's pace - so come after work or when you have time to check out.  And don't miss the shoe department.  I got some Timberland Sandals (one season late) that I still love to wear.

We held a surprise 70th birthday luncheon at Chambers for 20 people and it was an amazing success. James (the manager - NOTE:  He left about a month later - fall of 2012) and I communicated for months beforehand and the actual day was picture perfect.  Delicious food (We offered a soup/salad course and a choice of 4 entrees) and wonderful service by Lucas and the other servers. People raved about the perfectly cooked salmon and filet mignon as well as the delectable chicken/penne dish.  Chambers even allowed us to bring our own cake - and graciously sliced and served it for us.  We are so very pleased with our 5-star party at Chambers! I wish James was still around.
No issues - I got in and out quickly and picked up just a few needed items.  Granted, it was a Wednesday at about 12:30 Pm so not a peak time.

I am split on Sa Va - I like some of the designs and want to support sustainable sources for clothing, but I just haven't found anything I actually WANT to buy here.  Fun to browse though - and when I see it - I'll snatch it up.  And I thought the owner was very nice.  They are right near UrbanFront Pilates - so I hit them up on my way to or from class.

Uck!  Really?  You're kidding.  Jo Jo's is AWFUL - everything from ZERO decor, Zero service to yucky tasting food.    Doughy dumplings, greasy chicken & brocolli & overly salted wonton soup broth.  I went once - reluctantly (the place just looked unappealing) and have NEVER returned.  Try Square on Square or A Mandarin Restaurant, nearby.

A close gal-pal of mine and I both tried Tangerine for dinner for the very first time last night.  We arrived for our (early) 5:30 PM reservation just as they were opening and thus, were the only people there.  The interior is very dark/dim/romantic and GORGEOUS.  The right hand wall is completely votive-lit in small arch-shaped alcoves.  The low leather chairs were very comfy - but we are both short, petiit women - not sure if a big guy would feeel the same.  We started with non-alcoholic drinks at the bar area (iced tea and Limonata).  The custom drink menu looked great - but we were driving.  Then off to our table for dinner. We split the YUMMY arugula salad with tasty candied almonds.  Then she (vegetarian) custom ordered a $22 veggie/side dish plate and I had the Kobe beef appetizer in lieu of a full entree ($16).  My friends fava beans and kale "casserole" were delicious. She did not like the farro much.  My app was great - but not light.  It came with a rich parmesan crema - so good you could lick the plate.  We shared 2 desserts.  As mentioned by others - DON'T MISS THE CREME BRULEE.  Ours was banana  and was accompanied by 3 house-made 'Nilla-style wafers.   We also got the Chocolate Chocolate Chocolate trio which was not realy that great. The mouse cake was cold and very dense, the Napoleon had delectable house-made ice cream (choloate of course) and there was a torte-of-sorts with a delicous fresh whipped cream blob on top.  Meanwhile with tax and tip our bill (no alcohol - remember) was $95.  OUCH.  Thus 4 stars.  It is great - but simply not a 5 star value.  This is a good place for a guy to take a girl to impress her. She may still not like you after the meal, but she'll have had a good time.  Oh - and it's $17 to valet park your car.  (My friend drove - I walked.)  Service was excellent.  (But it was early and we were the only guests until about 6 when a few LARGE party groups came in.)  Also -if I ever go back - I will go for cocktails "mezze" and dessert only.  The desserts are really worth it. That creme brulee is one of the best I've tried - complete with black specs of vanilla bean at the bottom, cold cream and a hot crackling sugar crust encasing the paper thin banana slices.  Kudos to the pastry chef!!!!
It's CLOSED.  So sad.

A tiny, tiny grocery store - but it's got what you need - maybe not at the greatest prices - and for a long while it was all Dublin really had.  Brain-dead clerks & cashiers - but they will smile back if you smile first.  It's a grocery store - and I am glad it's here - but it sure could use an overhaul both physically (clean up the aisles and floors) and customer-service-wise.  The older lady at the deli counter was really nice, though - 4 stars for her.  Darned if I can't remeber her name, though. She sliced up some turkey breast for me and 3 slices of liverwurst for my sweet little pug.

3 cheers for Dali (co-owner of all 3 Gianfranco's Pizza Rustica locations) and groupon user.    Last night I took my 5 year old for Pizza here using a $16 groupon (that I paid $8 for) and I must say it was so worth it.  She had plain pizza - very, very good.  I had an excellent chicken sandwich on fresh-made bread (kinda pizza-doughy but a bit denser) with sharp provolone and delcious chopped broccoli rabe and spinach with garlic.  It was so good.  Ambience? Don't look for that here - it's a local pizza joint. Great service and good, solid pies.  Can't wait to come back.  I also bought a gift card - they give you 10% more that you put on it and the don't expire.  So if you buy a $10 gift card you get $11 on it, $20 gets you $22 etc.  We'll be coming again for sure.
OMG - so good - even worth the ridiculously long wait (and kinda pricey if you add provole, long hots AND broccoli rabe.  But about twice a year I just gotta get a sandwich from DiNics in RTM.  YUM.

It's soooooo old school that it's actually fun to come here once every couple of years.  I attended a group meeting here and the upstairs banquet rooms are FULL of history.  The meals are like eating at a 1978 wedding or a 1983 prom.  COmplete with pre-set iceberg based salads, white dinner rolls with no nutritional value, and surprisingly tasty salmon with 55 gallon drum hollandaise sauce.  I actually get a big kick out of coming here - not because the food is so great (it's really not) but for the walls that reek with history.  (There are pictures of proms and highschool reunions from the 50's - and lawyers/legal assocaition meetings, and other stuff.)   Such a cool places with old-school service and food.  And a reasonably priced place to host a group function.

So very disappointed and actually... SAD.  Yes, I left Ooka tonight feeling sad.  Sad - for the fact that we had food (entrees) so bad that we had to send it back. Sad - to see my favorite D-town sushi spot be anything other than the wonderful we usually expect. Sad - to have had to defend my right to consume undercooked meat or seafood products.  Just sad.  Do not order duck breast here.  I did - and asked for medium rare - and that duck had the quack cooked right out of it.  As usual the seared striped bass with foie gras was excellent.  Everything else?  MEH,  So sad to have to give out 2 Meh stars to Ooka.  We pray that when and If we give them another chance that they will redeem themselves.  Sad Sad Sad.

It is a pretty sorry site for a bar.  The only reason we went here is because we needed a table during the lunch crowd at RTM.  Now, mind you, you have to be a customer to sit at a Beer Garden table - so we bought some drinks and then discretely ate our "good" food from the other vendors.  The food here?  Chilli and Hot Dogs. - and who wants to eat THAT when there is so much wonderful culinary goodness to be had at RTM?  Meanwhile at the bar were some pretty shady lookin' characters.

Let me preface this by saying that I am a "verge-atarian" (On the verge of vegetarianism) and even I can appreciate the carnivorours, juicy joy that is Five Guys.  The "little" burger is big enuf por moi and I load that bun with all the complimentary veggies.  (All the toppings are free - other than cheese and bacon - which are not even neccessary - given the amount of artery clogging fat already present in aforementioned juicy burgers.)  I have also never gotten the fries - as after eating the burger my grease quotient has been met for the day.  But I do occaisionally indulge in a single little burger from five guys.  It is worth the 8-10 minute cooked to order wait.  Yes.  It's worth it.

Even my daughter (age 7) agrees that the yogurt here is 3 star - not as good as tutti frutti or yogorino.  On par with Sweet Ending.  The sushi is just "meh" - we tried the tuna triangle, BBQ Chicken triangle and shrimp nigiri. Harmless enough.  If you come after 5 everything is discounted. Manager is very kind to us.
We saw "Menopause: The Musical" here a few years ago - but the sound was so loud it was deafening!!!  Otherwise - a great small theatre with decent productions at moderate prices.

Over-priced and OVER hyped.  I have not yet tried SKIN CARE SERVICES here.  A massage, however, is fine - its not as practitioner dependent.  I had one from IKE - and he is a gifted healer.  The product lines for hair and skin are upper-tier (and full retail prices, of course.) and the receptionist was professional without being "icy".  But for $100?  I can get more mileage from Ananda or my fave, Body Restoration.  They also offer nail services, but I have not yet tried these either.

Good inexpensive lunches and of course, my all-time favorite soup Tom Khai Gai.  After all these years, Thai Singha House is STILL in business (though the decor looks about 20 years old) and a great place to grab lunch when in West Philly.  I also enjoy the Pad Thai here.

NYAJ had surprisingly decent bar-food. Our bartender, Abraham was attentive and friendly.  The $5 Fresh Fruit sangria tasted like fruit punch and was so cloyingly sweet that i did not finish it. $5 guacamole and chips (chips were huge and freshly made) had bland guacamole.  Tasty - but not at all spicy.  More like Avocado dip.  The best was the entree - a Pappardelle loaded with asparagus and kale in a garlicky pesto sauce.  Very tasty and the grilled chicken on top (you can get this dish sans chix) was juicy and perfectly grilled.  I'd come back here - but with Harvest across the street (which I much prefer - but it's more expensive) I won't be rushing back.  All in all this place is a BIG improvement from the Outback Steakhouse that was in this spot years ago.

Upgrading to 4 stars based on FANTASTIC Customer service by both the pharmacist/pharmacy tech (lady in the back) and the nice young lad out front.  DD & I came here with a 25% EVERYTHING in the store (excluding sale items - which excluded alot) and literally took a cart (a CART - sho does tha?) and loaded up with Advil, Vitamins, Hair dye, Cosmetics, Cleaning products, all sorts of stuff.  We snagged a great deal. And the 2 aforementioned CVS staffers helped us find it all.  And the nice young lad up front even processed a return of one item a few hours later when I realized I bought something we didn't need.  Wow. My mid is changed on this location. For the better!

OMG!!!! I love it, I love it, I love it!  The chef-owner is a total hottie (but he IS married and has a brand new baby girl.) and man can he throw down!  This re-vamped BYO in Northern liberties (bring a nice RED!) served a mean duck breast with fraggola and a tasty Lobster Udon app scented with vanilla butter.  Sooooooo yummy.  We loved our 4 separate  meals here.  Only 1 bad thing - (and I almost downgraded to 4 stars). - once when we came with another couple (and ordered many things) they charged us for splitting an appetizer.  (We did not split any entrees - we ordered 2 apps and 4 entrees).  When we objected they removed it from the bill - but it just seemed cheesy to charge $5.00 to split an app.  (The split-plated it for us - but we did not request that and would have happily picked off each others plates).  Also, the desserts are kind of a downer.  (Only2 or 3 to chosse from and no pastry chef on site.)  Save room and head to Capogiro for dessert!  But you gotta try that duck breast.  (Cherry gastriche)  HEAVEN on a plate!

Completely against my better judgement I stopped into this grotty looking nail joint just off of Market Street.  I got a mani/pedi ($25_) and prayed that nothing fungal would happen to me.  So far, the pedicure g-ds have been with me.  No problems.  A decent, sheap mani/pedi - but the place looks pretty awful anf the nail tech spoke almost Zero english.  Oh - and it was DEAD empty (just me and then toward the end of my services another lady came in for a mani/pedi.  On a summer Wednesday.

Let me preface this by saying that I am NOT a hoagie gal. I don't "do" cheese steaks and I like to eat healthy.  But I must insist that Primo is the best - I get the Chicken Suprimo - as a wrap (that bread is fresh and yummy - but waaaaaay to many carbs pour moi.).  I also like Nonna's veggie - as a wrap - no oil, with fresh mozz instead of provolone.  This is the real deal!  Even for a non-hoagie eater.

Little Italy delivered oodles of pies (Plain cheese, mushroom and veggie) for a large block party I attended.  Very good pizza.  "Class" neapolitan pies - not too thin (not pizza-on-a-cracker) not too thick.  Very good.

An old-fashined five 'n dime style "everything" store - stationary, household goods, kid stuff, party goods, wrapping paper, tools, socks.  A vast variety that is as close as Media, PA gets to the "Vermont COuntry Store".  A note of nostalgia and fun shopping here and a sweet lady at the cashier in the evening time on weekdays.  Louis B. gets it right! There is also a Deal Stationary store - 1/2 a block down the street.  (Same Owners)  FUN!

Bucks County Ladies?  This is the place.  Like a one-stop shop for Bridal and wedding needs.  Of course, the main attractin is the bridalboutique with dresses for the bride, Maid of Honor, Bridesmaids and MOMs too.  Even flower girl dresses.  But this ain't no David's bridal.  (And also, it ain't Kleinfelds)  Be prepared to pay for such wonderful personalized service.  I did NOT purchase my gown here - but I did get my shoes and alot of great accessories here.  Also a good place to go for proms and evening dresses.  Oh, and its been around for-eh-ver.

i am not a big Macy's shopper - but even for a Macy's this one is lame. I used to shop at the Wanamaker/Macy's (in Center City) and if there were sales you could get some decent clothing, shoes and kids clothing.  Here in Springfield?  Not so much. It's hit or miss and I usually miss. The Calvin Klein dress I wanted was full retail at $134.99 - and I got a very similar one at Century 21 (in Philly) for $69.99 - so, I am not too keen on Macy's these days.  For kids clothes?  Entirely too pricey.

Old Navy is Disposable Clothing,  The Gap's low-end merch. The dis-interested, underpaid staff has a n "I'm too busy stocking to talk to you" vibe here - but all in all you can still get mass-produced, el-cheapo clothing here.  I very rarely get anything for myself at ON - the snooty law firm folks I work with could sniff that out in a minute.  Instead, I lavish my pre-schooler with $5.00 sneakers and 2 for ten jammy sets.  Oh and socks - love the cheap socks.

This family-owned and run outpost of Lee's is a good, quick option for hoagies, cheese-steaks (try as a wrap) and sandwiches of all sorts.  They also make wings, fries and a few appetizer/snack items.  Chips and soda, of course.  Healthy?  No. Well run?  yes!  The owner/owner's wife is a doll and has been running the place for 17 years.  Walls are covered with sports memorabilia.  Love me some Lee's from time to time.

Products?  Great. Service?  Needs work.  I called and left a voice mail weeks before my daughter's birthday to see about getting a quote for a custom donut order (Their donuts are the best in this area - so good, especially when fresh.)  Unfortunately nobody called me back until the night before the event and I had already purchased donuts elsewhere.  I was getting desperate so I went somewhere else and they won't be as good.  I sure wish they had listened to my voice message sooner.   Will try again and next time I will call multiple times.

A little dirtier than Midtown 2 - but the same basic old-skool diner vibe. Good for breakfasts and cheap dinners.  It is creepy though - but my 5 year old loves to get one pancake and one scrambled egg here.

t's soooooo old school that it's actually fun to come here once every couple of years. A Media tradition - has been here for-eh-ver! (Some of the waitresses have worked here over 30 years and you can tell.  I attended a group meeting here and the upstairs banquet rooms are FULL of history.  The meals are like eating at a 1978 wedding or a 1983 prom.  COmplete with pre-set iceberg based salads, white dinner rolls with no nutritional value, and surprisingly tasty salmon with 55 gallon drum hollandaise sauce.  I actually get a big kick out of coming here - not because the food is so great (it's really not) but for the walls that reek with history.  (There are pictures of proms and highschool reunions from the 50's - and lawyers/legal assocaition meetings, and other stuff.)   Such a cool place with old-school service and food.  And a reasonably priced place to host a group function.

I attended a company party at Winterthur and EBE was the entertainment.  For cocktail hour - the first song I heard when we arrived through the doors was a brass instrumental of Nikki Minaj "Starships".  I then went to the ladies room to freshen up and met one of the 5 vocalists (FIVE! 2 guys, 3 gals) who was super-sweet.  They played softer music during cocktails and louder pop and a few oldies during the party.  The also played "Happy" by Pharell 3 times.  (That was a bit much.) They also played "Starships" again with vocals.    Very good bassist (in the back corner) and brass.

I am very pleased to report that things are improving at "the Pit". Better tasting hummus (supposedly now sourced by Sabra Salads) and fresher toppings.  I tried the Greek God (no onions, no feta) and it was very good.  My faith is restored in the Pita Pit! Keep it clean, keep it fresh  - and I'll be back for sure.  Hooray!

We love you, Chris!  (And Chris's son.  I forgot your name.) The staff at Oh! Shea's treat our group like family - which is why we'll be having our annual holiday party here for the 5th year in a row.  Reasonably priced, tasty food and good strong drinks (and beer). Classic Rock - with lots of Rolling Stones for Maryellen and Tom on the jukebox.  It all adds up to a fun, fun, fun event!

Peter Mac does it again - with great assistance from Joey - they have opened a catering/take out place with terrific Italian (and American) sandwiches, platters and catering.  We sorely need this.  Do not miss the smoked wings and ribs - fan-flipping-tastic.  We attended the Grand Opening event on 10/1 and all the food was terrific - especially the sides of roasted red peppers and brocolli rabe.  I am thrilled and delighted that La Porta and now La Porta Via (next door) are here!

My friends have come here and are regulars - and have been for years. Chris and the other bartenders know them and what they like to drink - and that having the Rolling Stones on the sound systems is a must.  The french dip sandwiches hit the spot after a long night out when you are hungry and the drinks are moderately priced and strong enough.  Love coming here and relaxing in a non-chi-chi atmosphere.

Terrific service and a toy shop for kids downstairs loaded with Melissa & Doug toys. Mushroom items for gifts or for eating and they'll ship mushrooms to your loved ones.  An old educational display in the back teaches about how mushrooms are farmed.  Lots of fun - even if you don't like mushrooms.

We have worked with Linda and Maureen at State Farm for our auto, renters - and now home owners insurance policies.  So far - everything have been very smooth and Maureen, especially, has answered all of my questions.
Honestly, this was fine. Needed bottled water desperately and 7-11 was there.  Got in, got out, got hydrated.  Done.

I want to love it here - but the sushi is just Meh.  My salmon roll had no taste and husband's tuna nigiri was "not as fresh as it could have been".  Stick to the Thai dishes and you will be OK.  But even those need some tweaking - Tom Kha ($6 for chicken $7 for shrimp) was loaded with onions.  So. Many. Onions.  The Pineapple fried rice was tasty - but a bit greasy and again - so. many. onions.  Yes, it's winter.  Yes, onions are cheap.  But carrot, onion and a bit of zucchini is not enough for me.  I need some more green veggies - broccoli?  Peppers?  Something?  No more Thai iced coffee either.  *Sad Face*.  I like it here but I do not love it here.   Every few years I come back and remind myself why.

Manna PA provides nutritious meals (3 meals a day, 7 days a week) for over 1,050 people with life threatening illnesses.  They may be best known for their annual "Pie in the Sky" fundraiser each holiday season (Thanksgiving pies for $25 or $50 and proceeds benefit Manna).  Definitely check them out.  I have bought pies for 3 years and for the last 2 have been a pie seller.  A great organization.

This is a review for RAINA CLARKE - who is an extremely gifted stylist and an expert in retro hair styles (30', 40' & 50's).  She did my hair in a pin-curl roller set for a photoshoot and it was great.  If I ever travel out toward Springfield - I will definitely see her again!  She rocks!

The lunch buffet offers many choices - including several hot entrees both vegetarian and with chicken. The Naan is fresh and the breads baked to order (Roti, Poori - not on menu just ask) and delicious.  We had a large group of 10 here for lunch. Very nice - and new.  Clean.  Can't wait to come back.

I finally got around to trying Polaris (thatnks for the recommendation, Spa Girl!) yesterday.  I got a "regular" manicure ($16) a "callus remover" pedicure ($47) and 20 minutes of chair massage while my nails dried.  There are 6 pedi-thrones and 8 manicure tables at this colorful (green & orange) cheerful and CLEAN spa.  The pedicure I got was very good - not a holy grail by any means but it was throrough with a nice scrub and massage.  for $15 extra (too high if you ask me) I got the "callus removing treatment" which basically was a bit of high % glycolic in plastic wrap for 10 minutes.  Big whoop.  They also have an even MORE expensive ($62) SPA pedicure and the highest priced, POLARIS SPA pedicure (which - for another $10 - making the total a whopping $72 - you get a paraffin dip.)  Double whoop-de-doo.  Now don't get me wrong - I am a pedi-afficionado and these are nice treatments - but the price points when you add them all up seem a bit above the norm.  They also have a weird pricing structure where you get a $1-$2 discount if you pay cash.  I didn't have enough cash to cover all my treatments so I paid some with cash and some on my debit card (Including a $10 tip - I spent $98.00). NOTE:  You can not put the tip on your credit card - so bring SOME Cash with you.)  The lady who did my pedicure, Wanty, also did my manicure (very good, by the way) and and the chair massage (not great.)  I would definitely go back here for nail services but no way I would book a body massage nor a facial here as I doubt these girls are estheticians.  What they are - is nail technicians.  And decent ones, at that.  Good find!

Had not been to Firebirds in quite a while, maybe years?  Lunch with a corporate party of 4 was very good with stellar service (it was not crowded at 12:15 on a summer Friday) and solid food.  Deviled eggs with a candied bacon garnish were indulgent and spicy. (The fresh jalapeno was strong and kicking.)  My entree was a simple grilled salmon, served with broccoli and mixed veggies (zucchini, carrots, onions, sweet red peppers and yes, more broccoli).  The fish was done just to my liking.   Colleagues dishes all looked great.  I would definitely come here again and it us great for a corporate event or even a date night.    Great Lunch! Kudos to Jessica and Phil who served us.

Beautiful restaurant with ambiance and a young, good-looking, friendly staff. Bar is gorgeous and colorful. Our group of 3 enjoyed the $23 Three-course feast and $80 kids meal- 1/2 a rack of ribs.  I can see how this is likely "formula" cooking and college kids are running the joint - but they are running it well.  We enjoyed the crab cake app and grilled salmon.  Many items are way too salty (smoke flavoring??) though.  Good stuff and strong drinks, especially the ($10) double black diamond martini (akin to the Flyin' Hawaiian) which is basically pineapple juice infused vodka.

I love coming here for an old-school memory.  I first came here with my parents as a child and had shirley temples and Chicken Cordon Bleu in the '80's.  I have been to luncheons here and weddings - but to simply come and dine off the regular menu is the best.  Great service and conutry-style decor. (Could use a bit of a re-fresh)  I will bring my daughter now!  Shirley Temples all around!  Oh - and it is beautiful for a Christmas or Winter dinner - lots of twinkly lights all around,

An asset to women and education - and the community.  Our 8 year old attended a girl scout leadership conference here and the student volunteers were just amazing.    Gorgeous, pristine campus, beautiful architecture and a friendly vibe.  I hope our daughter can get in when the time comes! (ANd pray we can afford to send her.)

Now they get 5 stars!  They offer gift cards. Between this and the $20 fruit baskets (I bought 4 of them at Thanksgiving time) and my everyday fruit & veggie needs, Gentile's can't be beat!  Much love!
Better than the Merriam - but it ain't the Kimmel Center. Still, it's a grand old-time theater and we have seen numerous productions here, including Jersey Boys.  Well staffed.  Crowded ladies rooms.

It's rare for me to grant ANY starbucks a 5 star rating - but this is for SERVICE, SERVICE, SERVICE.  Isiah and David? was on point and greeted my like an old friend.  The other customers were all so friendly - it felt like a neighborhood coffee shop and not like a chain-Starbucks at all!  My drink (a basic latte) was perfectly fine, but the chit-chat made my day. It made me realize how comparatively unfriendly my "regular" Starbucks (in Media) is.  And I am at that location several times per week!  Wish this was my defaut bux.  Shout out to Isiah and team for the beauty tips!  Ya'll rock some serious balayage!

I was dragged here again tonight by the inlaws who desperately wanted that 2 for $20 deal.  Honestly - the food, service & cleanliness were all way, way better than in the past.  I still loathe chain restaurants - and even moreso loathe crowds, but tonight wasn't too terrible from a culinary perpective.  The frantic (almost) 5 year old had a $4.99 hot dog (what a rip) with a cup of applesauce and an OJ.  The inlaws had a 2 for 20, as did my husband and I.  I played it safe with a burger - which was edible and not bad.  DH's chicken cheese penne was overly salted and the noodles were over cooked (so NOT al dente).  The inlaws split a vat of Spinach dip and MIL had a rather sweet 1/2 rack of baby back ribs.  FIL did not like the Quesedilla burger, because the tiny burger pattie was lost in the vast recesses of the large floppy torilla.    Oh well.  At least the kid didn't scream.  Plus the 5 of us escaped from Applebee's for around $50.  Not bad.  I won't rush back but I expect to be summoned here yet again next summer.  I think once a year is far too often.

Our party of 9 (6 kids, 3 adults) received great service from Nicole - and ordered a wide variety of pizza, sandwiches, pasta and salads.  Food was very good - my 12 year old enjoyed an enormous plate of penne a la vodka.  Linguine with *white) clam sauce is a classic preparation with plenty of garlic and red pepper flakes.  Whole baby clams were plentiful and tasty.  Caprese salad was solid. Pizza was average in my opinion - but nothing bad about it - just a plain cheese pie for some of the kids.  All in all - a good experience.

This is a review for the event space and the Downton Abbey exhibit. We were at Winterthur for a private event during the evening so we did not get to tour the grounds - but the museum was opened late especially for our group/.  Awesome!  I knocked off 1 star for the "tented" seating area - not enough seating and also very drafty - so spots were over heated and others very cold.  For that reason alone I would not have a winter event here. (And not a wedding.) I bet in summer/late spring this is a better idea.  Boy, those DuPonts had bank!

Thai food was excellent but sushi last night was just "meh". My 10 year old did not like her maki but I loved the Tom Kha (sup) and Dumplings I had.  I still love it here but can no longer take the kid here.  Service was terrific.

OK, now that I have tried Crepe Maker in 30th Street station I am even more impressed with Profis.  The crepe batter here is far suprior - much more flavorful.  I am lovin' the crepes at Profi's.  It's hard to get a seat - but once I snag I stool you best believe I am ordering!!!

Finally got back to Moro for a special occasion dinner with DH - and we were in for a treat.  FANTASTIC service and cocktails (All were $10) and great wines (as always).  DH had a smooth, delicious Malbec.  My cocktail (and later iced tea) had blood orange (aka Moro) juice in it.  Best bite of the night?  Watermelon salad with pine nuts and flash-fried basil.  Super delicious.  We enjoyed the risotto side (a steal at $5) and duck breast entree.  The ony disappointment?  The "classic" bolognaise sauce (atop perfectly home-made strotaprezzi - yum) had a sour vinegary note to it and I did not love it.  We were too full for dessert but nearly ordered the spring special - a strawberry rhubarb crostata.  (We passed - we were just too stuffeed.)  A memorable, beautiful, gourmet evening. Can't wait to return!  Does Wilmington know what a gem this place is???

Back again for the 4th consecutive year - and our 3rd year shopping for unique ornaments from Kathe Woklfahrt (The big white tent).  Our 9 year old loves it here - so we go (and spend) every Christmas.  Great fun and great for kids.

I agree with McThrill - why soooooo many Dunkins so close to each other?  (And amazingly - even in this economy - long lines at each during the morning rush.  (There's your answer.)  I trek through here very often - although not nearly as often as when I commuted in on my beloved-behated R5 (but that's for another review - see SEPTA).  I disagree about the juicebar.  It is not great - the one in the Comcast Center is way better (Sook Hee's Squeeze Juice Bar).  I really liked Pasero's Coffee before they were taken over by Juan Valdez - byt still, it beats Charbucks (Fourbucks - whatever).  Meanwhile, it's a necessary evil.

It has everything you need for crafts at reasonable prices.  A good place for DIY wedding favors, kids crafts, art projects, framing and more.  And I am not one for glue guns - but wow - such a selection.  The staff is underpaid and pretty disinterested - so do your own research and then buy your stuff and move on.  The lines on weekends can be painfully long at holiday times.

Just OK.  Great concept though and big comfy seats with tray-tables so that you can dine (in total darkness) while watching a flick.  The bad part?  Awful formula-cooking food cum Applebee's-meets'TGI Friday's served by dis-interested twenty-somethings.  The good part?  You can't actually see that horribly wilted salad in the dark theater.  Meanwhile, my 10 year old went gaga for this place so we shall return. Oh - and they serve booze.

There are Qdoba people, Chipotle people, El Fuego People and none of the above.  I am more a Qdoba (sans tortilla, sans cheese, try to get the calorie count down).  Meanwhile, Chipotle (which is now corporate fast food owned) is an inexpensive and FILLING (even the salad or bowl options are HUGE) lunch or quick dinner.  Their meats (Chicken & Beef are the only ones i have tried) are spicier (more peppers??) than Qdoba.  Also they use white meat - Qdoba uses thighs.  It's OK by me.  A-OK - in the true yelp 3 star way.  This location is new and relatively clean (crowded at lunch time on weekdays - deserted at dinner.).

Just awful. Our server Lara was nice enough - and thankfully the manager (who looked about 18 years old) comped my in-edlible over-cooked salmon. Dry.  Awful.  (And I asked them to cook it less than they usually do - which is Medium-well).  Thankfully it was very inexpensive (we got the 2 for $25 lunch deal - one app, 2 entrees, dessert).  The food was just not good - and the service was so slow. Like watching paint dry.  45 minutes to get the app, 20 more for entree.  Will NOT return.

The service was great but we happened to come just before the shop was going to close for a week-long vacation, so the shelves were nearly empty - which is actually a good sign that they make everything fresh.  My 9 year old bought a $2.00 White Chocolate (confection) Golf Ball-shaped lollipop and she enjoyed it.  Can't wait to come back at Easter or Christmas and see everything they make.  Limited hours - so be aware of that.

Practitioners are good but it can take for.eh.ver to get an appointment and they have no evening nor weekend hours.  I now see Teresa (Dani left) for my routine skin-checks. I also have visited the "Cosmetic" side once.  You can get things like Cool-Sculpt and Botox there as well as super-pricey facials.  I will continue to use this practice but know that the administration is tricky.

Hart's Tavern - right in PV servs an important purpose - to give shoppers an alternative place to grab a bite and a brewski at a place OTHER than the Cock 'n Bull.  I miss Jenny's - the old restaurant that is now Earl's Prime.  (Don't get me started) and Hart's is easier to deal with than the spotted hog - which is loaded with strollers.  You can get a decent (if overpriced) sandwich here and chill out for a while before returning to the throngs of holiday shoppers.

Honeygrow is now on my heavy rotation for work lunches and I try to stick to salads and limit the dressing and carbs.  Service is good and ingredients are fresh and tasty.  Lots of choices.  Improved performance on new app.  YAY!!!!  Shout out to Steve who works the lunch rush - a very pleasant man.

The spotted hog is one of the lower-priced options within the confines of Peddler's Village.  It is certainly way cheaper than Earl's Prime or the Cock 'n Bull which are the more high-end PV establishments.  You can take the kiddies here and refresh yourself on mediocre food and sandwiches before another round of shopping.  Avoid during the holidays.  It gets mobbed.

Lunch for 23 for my parent's 50th wedding anniversary (They just love this place - and especially Matt and Linda) was a terrific and memorable occasion.  We are so thankful to everyone here who cooked, prepped, served and cleaned up after us.  Especially delicious were the petit filet mignon and chicken zinfandel pasta entrees (which we have enjoyed before and are so happy to see they are still on the menu).  Chicken Sante Fe soup was tasty as well as crisp fresh beet and garden salads.  They even helped us cut and plate the 50th anniversary cakes.  THANK YOU SO MUCH!!!!

Barnaby's is simply a bar. That serves food.  It can also accomodate large and rowdy groups.  We came on a relatively quiet Monday night (thank goodness) with our 7 year old who promptly told me she hates it there.  DH & I both had half priced burgers (Which for $4.50 each was a great bargain.)  Service was fine - nice young gal. Food was unremarkable.  Not my cup of tea, but I bet we'll be back - it's very close to our new house.
Decent coffee and a few sandwiches and snack items.  Plus:  It was actually open at 4 PM.  (Most places close at 3.  UGH!)

The best place to sit in the Sugarhouse casino.  A simple bar with a TV showing "the" game.  Go when it's not crowded.  But truthfully, Sugarhouse is just not my bag, baby.  Honestly?  Were it not for proximity - I would NEVER here  - I'd sooner go to AC or even Bethlehem, PA.  Philly fought long & hard to get a casino - and THIS is what they get?  Sorry - Unimpressed.

I am upping this location to 4 stars (even though it is more of an urban 3 star location).  I got in and out of there on BLACK FRIDAY WEEKEND - and the super-friendly checkout dude "K", even scanned coupons for me - when I had forgotten mine.  We got $1.00 sale ink pads for 33 cents after the discounts. We also got lots of great worsted wool yarn and knitting needles (Needing Knittles) for my 7 year old budding fiber artist.

I hadn't been to Smile Cafe in a long time - and got the Pad Thai lunch special as take out (it's a small place).  Very good value - a small (iceberg) salad, two little dumplings and a nice serving of Pad Thai with 2  (yes only 2) Shrimp in it.  Hey - for $8.50 including tax - who cares?  Tasty and cheap.
Closed.  I didn't think they'd make it and they have closed

Kudos to Tony (executive Director) and Andrea (Director of Educational Programs) for a wonderful private event and tour they hosted for our group.  We even got to bake in the (10 year old replica of a) colonial bake oven.  It is so interesting to learn the history of the mill (founded in 1704) and watch as the water wheel turns the corn into corn meal (available for purchase).  The pond is stocked with trout ($5 to fish - including kids). The grounds are gorgeous and we even saw a nice fat bullfrog.  October 1 is the fall festival - DON'T MISS IT.  I did not find the staff here abrasive at all - quite the opposite. They even have a summer camp.  Definitely check out the Newlin Grist Mill.

I honestly am at a loss for words.  I went to Franco's tonight as part of a VERY large group (35-40 ladies) with a set menu (that sounded great on paper.).  Franco's had a lovely decor (once we managed to find a spot in the jam-packed lot) and the hostess (a pretty young Asian woman) was friendly and professional.  Our group had a semi private portion of the restaurant. We began arriving for cocktails at 5:30 (dinner was to start at 7) at the packed bar.  By 7:20 dinner had still not started. At 7;30 the first few salads (all of us were to have the SAME - BORING - mixed greens with 2 grape tomatoes and barely a whisper of balsamic vinaigrette.) started to arrive.  By 8:00 (we were so hungry we devored the baskets of Uber-SALTY focaccia (UCK) and decent Italian bread), they came to take our orders (IMO they shoulda done that much sooner.)  My entree (eggplant parm) arrived at 8:45. I ate 2 bites (it was just OK) and had ot wrapped to go.  Meanwhile the 4 entrees we have to choose from were Cheese ravioli Marinara, Eggplant Parm with Penne, Tilapia with Capers or Salmion with Olive Oil & Herbs.  Our tablemates had the tilapia and claimed it was under seasoned (perhaps the over-seasoned foccacia would have helped)?  Meanwhile the sweet young boys (er, men??) bussing and serving were clearly way, way, way overwhelmed by our party.  Badly handled. Mediocre Food.  I had high hopes for this place, but I am in no hurry to rush back.  (Menu prices for the entrees our group had were from $14.75 - $19.75).  I did not get a chance to try the profiteroles for dessert.  The service simply started too late and ran too long.

Excellent choices but yes it gets pricey - especially the honey bar which is over $6 to $9 depending on all the fruit you add.  The stirfries are tasty but sodium and sugars (carbs) are high unless you opt for lettuce cups (no noodles, no grains).  I will be back.  And bringing more money.  Very clean store and friendly staff.  I spent over $11 - no beverage for a beef-based stirfry.  (At Qdoba next door it's about $8.50) Trying to watch carbs so avoid the "sweet soy" - loaded with sugar. Tried the (spring only) pesto.  Very good.  I wonder how many carbs that one has?

TJ Maxx can be a pick-through situation where you can hit it big or miss. Often look for shoes, women's clothing, hosiery (small stock here), cookware (some are good deals on open stock - name brands) and even pet supplies (check the dates on anything edible for your pet or for you).  Excellent for hostess gifts (fancy wrapped soaps, candles, etc for $5 or less).  Check the clearance areas carefully.  Do not come here if you are in a hurry - especially over the lunch hour and/or during the holiday frenzey, as you will not make it back to your office in time.  The line for cashier and/or parking lot madness can eat up time.  Come when you can wander the aisles and pick through clothing racks item by item.  When you miss, you miss, but when you hit you can hit BIG at TJ Maxx (Calvin Klein dress for under $40!!!  Coach loafers for $50, etc.)   Oh, and natch - Delaware is tax free so if you are from NJ or PA this is a great reason to choose this particular TJ Maxx - right over the state line.

Eh.  Meh.  Whatever.  It's OK.  I prefer the pits at Aya's or Mama's. It is a nice alternative to fast food though.  Maybe I should give them 3 stars?  They are a solid 2 and a half. Staff are CLUELESS. Prices are low (which is helpful.) It's relatively clean.  I just wasn't BLOWN away by my chicken pita sandwich.

We have gone here for 3 consecutive years and our (now 8 year old) kid loves getting a sweet treat, picking out gifts, Russian Dollies, uber-expensive Nutcrackers, ornaments and everything you could want or need for your holiday celebrations.  We really enjoy this.

Sally and Ronnie were our servers again and they KNOW what they are doing.  We had exemplary services and top tier food and beverage from the moment we walked in and enjoyed beverages at the bar (Frose all day! Plus pints of Guiness for the dudes) to the time we were seated in the main dining room.   Seafood Wedge is delightfully simple and well executed. Do not miss the perfectly tender seared scallops.  WOW!  My friend was celebrating a special birthday (30 again??) so they brought out a dish of white chocolate house-made (and so thick and rich) ice cream with "Happy Birthday" written on the plate in chocolate.  An elegant touch and a surprise for the birthday boy.  I highly recommend Blue Bell Inn for any special occasion, corporate dinner or fancy date night.

I happen to love this location of Starbucks - the people who run it make the difference. There are usually several people sitting at the barstools chatting with the barristas.  It's alot of fun and makes dropping $4.72 on an iced tea or coffee that much easier.

I am not a pretzel lover - but man, these are good.  I eve like the pretzel dogs here.  The dough is just perfect.  The salt ratio is right on!  Chewy but not tough, wheaty flavor and FRESH out of the oven.  Tip:  only come to this brnach - Philly Soft Pretzel Factory has alot of chain branches - this one (as grubby as it seems) is best.

We took our 7 year old to a performance of "Hershel and the Hanukkah Goblins". The facilities are not as nice as the Arden, and the performance was not as good.  We love to support the arts and will continue to attend plays here, but we really like the Arden better - especially since tickets here were also not cheap $25 for adults and $16 for kids for this particular show.  Also there are no refreshments offered - so bear that in mind when you come.

Good thing come in small packages.... When you enter (cram into) Sue's tiny storefront - the myriad and variety of vegetable and fruits is just astounding.  It's amazing what they can pack into that store. Great prices - and yes, the long lines move quickly.  Berrie& cherries in July, and a feast of apple varieties in the fall.  LOVE SUE's!

I have never been to the "skin care" (spa) side, but I see a Dermatologic NP ( not a Dr. but she is excellent) for routine skin (mole) analysis.  She also got me some Rx retinoids which I needed and Hydroquinone for brown spots.  I see Dani (Danielle) and love her - but getting an initial appointment took MONTHS - so if you had a true skin emergency i am not sure how they'd handle it.  I also took my 10 year old here to check out a "suspicious" mole - she saw a different female NP (mostly female practitioners and staff here.)  Lovely office with a LARGE waiting room with coffee & water available.  (NICE!) Easy check in and check out - but getting that FIRST appointment takes patience.  Oy Vey!  Meanwhile if you need a derm - check them out.

This place is both dated and weird.  And I KNOW Madams Saito (I went to Dental school with her son years ago).  She was, back in the day, the sushi queen.  Now her place is in serious need of a makeover - menu and decor wise.    The sushi was just "meh" and we did not care for the "french" (was that really french?) items we tried.   Sorry to be so negative - and my 3 stars are generous - but it's time to get with the times, Mme!

Still lovin' PAFA - even moreso after seeing the Henry Ossawa tanner exhibit - and the yummy brunch sponsored by PECO.  We love the gift shop, too  - for unique gifts with an artsy twist.  Don't miss PAFA!

Karla's has been a New Hope institution for eh ver (well maybe not quite as long as Jon & Peters) and it draws out the tourists a-plenty.  The food is good and it has typical New Hope prices.  The drinks are also mixed well and they offer specials - summertime grets a little crazy - but a winter weekday is the best time to go.  Great mixed drinks.

Believe it or not - Christmas Village manages to mix cool and kitsch and still come out Kool.  My little girl and I have been here for 2 consecutive years - and this year visited 3 times.
