3 stars is the absolute most I can grant to a pre-fab chain with average food and cattle-call service.  We were dragged here for my mother in law's birthday and it happened during "Lobster Fest".  For $30 I got the Lobster lover's plate with a very nicely done rock lobster tail, a tough, dry overcooked Main lobster tail and a small blob of baby shrimp and lobster micro-bits alfredo (I luckily was smart enough to get mine with no alfredo sauce).  Edible?  yes. Good?  Some of it was good.  But I am still not a fan of this place.

3 or MAYBE 4 stars if you get good service.  (Ours was fair.) We arrived at 1:15 on a Wednesday - 2 of us - for a late lunch.  Our cheerful (and obviously new) server seated us and brought water right away.  After a while we each ordered chopped slads but with different items omitted and added.  After a VERY very long wait (for salads!) they salads arrived but neither mine nor my companions had tomatoes (and we wanted them and they were supposed to have them).  So very quickly the salads were brought back with the tomatoes and were fresh and crispy and very good.  Then the bill came - my friends salad (which last at $8.50) was $8.50 but mine was $12.00.  Wow.  I sure wished I had known that omitting bacon and adding chicken would cost me $3.50.  Again - not the end of the world but considering I omitted one protein in exchange for another, I kinda hoped they cut me a vbreak or tack on 2-$2.50 max.  Even LaCroix Rittenhouse only charges $4.00 for a chicken breast.  OK - enough raggin'.  The salad was good - crisp romaine and delicious dressing.  I will return - but I'm not in any great hurry.  (We picked it for location near my friends school.)  Oh - and they serve Capogiro Gelato (nice) - but we didn;'t get any.  They also have some outdoor seating, and an espresso bar.

This was the "Y" I grew up at.  Day camps in the summer, Indian Guide, Indian Princesses, The seekers, swimming in the indoor pool, working out at the fitness center, the locker rooms, classes in art & music, theatre & cooking.  But wow - now it is expanding and getting absolutely HUGE.  A great commuinty resource.  Expensive to join - but if you will use the facilities and take the classes - well worth it.  Got kids?  cConsider joining!

Every once in a while I splurge on a $5 Breakfast sandwich to go.  It's supposed to come with a free Illy coffee, but the lady usually lets me get iced tea.  Well today was not a good day at DuJour I guess - the place was much busier than usual (usually mornings are slow there) and the guy at the counter wanted to charge me for the iced tea (Their unsweetened iced teas are great - by the way) but I told him that I always get iced tea in lieu of coffee.  So I waited for my to-go sandwich and waited some more and the girl at the vcounter packed up my order and then let it sit under a heat lamp. Never called my name or anything.  So I waited some more and then I noticed my name on the bag and said, "I'm Karen" and she reluctantly got me my sandwich.  Whatever.  I won't be back for a while - but that said the sandwich (made to my specs - egg, cheddar and tomato on an english muffin) was great.  I wish they'd be a bit more friendly/service oriented.

I am giving K of T a 5 stars - mostly for the following LARGE party event I am going to describe.  In reality this is a 4 star place, but the way our group of 31 people (20 of which were children ages 2-7) was treated deserves kudos.  Kumar and Mohammed helped me to plan and execute a large Indian dinner for my 5 yesar old's Pre-K class, their parents and siblings.  Orinigally we planned on 12 -15 guests and each family would simply order what they wished and pay for their share.  Well plans changed..  and the guest list ballooned to 20, then 24, then 27 and finally 31.  We decide to go to a set menu - and people got to choose from 5 entrees including Chicken Tikka (plain for the kids or Masala), Lamb Korma, Shrimp Shag, Malai Kofta (for our vegetarian friends) or 3 kinds of Biryani.  Appetizers were great and included a smooth Muligatawny (Lentil) soup, Crispy Samosas (yum!) and Chana Chat - chikpeas in a tamarind sauce.  The kids plowed their way through 18 Lassi in Mango, Strawberry and Pomegranite.  We had our tables arranged in a large "U" shape for lots of interaction. I only pity the other diners that night (a few tables on a Wednesday night) who witnessed the chaos.  Those kids had a BLAST.  The servers and kitchen worked hard - and in the end the dinner was enjoyed very much.  Plus we introduced a whole group of young children to many new foods - including the yummy breads (which the loved) naan, paratha and poori.  It's not on the menu by itself - but ask them to make you a poori - it's (fattening and) delicious.  Oh - and those who stayed for dessert (many left early for bedtime) enjoyed Mango and Pistachio kulfi.  THANK YOU to the staff of King of Tandoor.

Wow - i am surprised at the negative reviews here.  We came here back when they first opened and were so new there wasn't even any signage.  Honestly, I can't really remember what we had but mine was good and I remember a terrific drizzle of very high quality balsamic vinegar was used on one of the dishes.  My compnanion did not like her meal at all, but i loved mine.  Also it was very loud in there (semi open kitchen) and for a small space, it was cramped.  Not the best I've had - but not bad. Perhaps they've tweaked things since?
Dayum that's some expensive-ass popcorn. But it comes in a scrillion flavors, sizes and packaging options.

Hit or miss - but when you hit, you hit big. You gotta be prepared to wade through the scattered, disorganished racks and try things on,  Cheap? Yes. Pain in the neck to shop here? Yes.  There are better and worse Marshall's locations.  This one is just MEH. Avoid during December and 1st week of Jan (holiday lines are long and sooooo not worth it).
They moved!!!!

This starbucks is located in a big "Gateway" shopping center and is my go to after I hit up Saladworks or the deli or the Taco joint at lunch time.  In the morning it's swamped but at lunch I can usually get my four-bucks (try almost $5 for a Grande Iced Macchiato) caffeine fix.  Le sigh...

Motions was recommended to us by Donna at Broadway Bound Dance Academy in Media, boy are we ever glad. (They even gave us a 10% discount for BBDA and/or IceWorks)  Leotards, ballet shoes, tights, lyrical and praise dance costumes, footwear for ballroom, accessories, just about everything a dancer, gymnast, figure skater or active person might need.  Spacious shop with a super clean restroom and 2 changing rooms.  They even have a small ballet barre and mirror for when you are fitted for shoes.  Donna - (also named Donna) who works here was so great! We'll be back - you can bet on it!

Update 2015:  SO SAD!!!!  They are closed. Such a shame.   A great old-school German Wurst-maker. They also supply to Steven Starr (Frankford Hall).  The Weiss Wurst and (believe it or not) Liverwurst are excellent.  I hope they stay open for many more years of success.

We had a corporate pizza lunch for about 40 people and brought in Anthony's salad and 15 pies including a very good Margarita pie, meatballs with roasted peppers and of course pepperoni.  They also had a cauliflower crust pie which disappeared so quickly that I did not get a chance to try it.  While I am not a big pizza fan, Anthony's is quite good. A nice alternative to the ubiquitous sandwich trays we usually get for catered lunches.  Good job!

What can I say anout Dunkin Donuts - really?  Some people love the coffee here - I think it's just OK.  (I mean, once you've been spoiled by Peregrine it's hard to turn back)  It's better than Charbucks - and cheaper.  I have also tried the regular and white hot chocolates.  They are mixed from powders and come shooting out of a dispenser.  The white hot chocolate is like drinking a cup of sugary fat.  It's sickening.  The "regular" hot cocoa - while also sugar laden is at least drinkable.  The donuts are not baked on premises and thus sometimes are not too fresh.    I guess I'm just not a DD gal. America may run on Dunkin - but I'll be running away.  Oh - my 5 year old LOVES DD - especially munchkins - but she's 5 and will eat anything sweet.

This is the CIBO carry out in Terminal B - and even though it's airport food (overpriced and usually awful) my 8 year old got a kids penne & meatballs (one meatball actually) that was cooked to order and actually quite tasty - and $8 after tax.  The male cashier was funny and provided comic relief while we waited for the food and my $3.26 bottle of Fiji Water (Oy vey!)  Meanwhile - el kiddo munched down that penne and seemed to really enjoy it.

Brand-spankin'-new Whole Paycheck in Glen Mills. So happy to have access to my beloved Hint Water, Frozen meals, Fresh fabulous produce, bakery items, olives and so much more.  I love Whole Foods - prices be darned -sometimes I just gotta blow $70 on maple syrup, water and fruit. My husband will freak, but hey - we gotta eat. It's not like I'm buying meth.  Anyhow - I am grateful that a Whole Foods opened near us.  (I miss my branch in Center City.)

This location has been a coffee place, a somehthing else (I forget) and now it's Old Nelson - which sells a little bit of everything.  Cereal, coffee (La Colombe, even!) and breakfast foods, sandwiches at lunch, snacks, chips, beverages, paper goods (at a pricey premium - but convenient).  Glad they are here and hope they make it in this highish-rent ever changing location.

Ah yes, the D-town-D-Q. Brings back memories - of Quickies and Arby's and the multitude of fast-foodie places that once occupied this spot .  Oh, and the short-lived catering place that had delicious mocha cake - but I digress.  There is now - and for years has been a Dairy Queen in D-town.  Decidedly less "white-trashy" than its longstanding Dublin counterpart, this fine, soft-serve selling establishment gets busy mostly in the summertime with lots of kids screeching for their cones.  The food at DQ as a chain has historically been really awful, although I have heard their hamburgers and sandsiches have been recently re-vamped.  I usually stick to blended shakes, blizzards and small kiddie cones for the little one.  DQ.  It helped make Britney Spears who she is today.  I pay hommage...
We have had keys made here and purchased supplies.  No issues.

I've had 2, 3 and 4 star experiences at du Jour - but the food is always great.  The service (and crowds - especially on rainy lunch hours) can make or break the experience.  Today, however, the stars were all in alignment.  Perfect iced tea. Delicious (grilled mahi) fish tacos Speedy, friendly server  Hooray!  A bit more money that I usually like to soend at lunch - but perfect for business and much better food than Bistro St. tropez or the other places we are often forced to visit.  AVOID during peak times, if you can (12:10 PM - 1:45 PM is the height of the madness).  Get there at 11:50 AM and the place is EMPTY.

Between 2 & 3 stars.  I feel generous today and they HAVE renovated oveer the years so that is a plus. Not a holy grail by any means, but they have friendly "lifer" waitresses along with new "young kids" who serve you and service is QUICK and good.  The food - however - is "classic" (read: heavy) and not that great. Breakfast or burgers are a safe bet.
kKnda grungy - but they DO play classic rock tunes while you shop. I get a few staples/non perishable items here and then hit whole foods for produce and hormone-reduced dairy.

Very nice staff! I popped in (famished) to the Chetserbrook Manhattan bagel and needed to get both breakfast AND lunch.  The Avocado BLT (Turkey Bacon) thin on whole wheat was delicious - and the added cucumber to it upon my request.  The also sell FIJI water for $1.79.  (My fave - and yes I can tell a difference.)  The iced coffee was very strong and a little burnt tasting - but suffice nonetheless.  The staff were just so friendly and accomodating - I can't believe it.  I'll be back!

Now that Granite RAun Mall (on its last dying legs) is our  closest shopping place, we came here on a Tuesday night.  My 7 year old desparately needed a new pair of sneaks and some winter boots.  SCORE!!!!!  The boots were priced as marked, but the $44.99 sketchers rang up for $14.99.  SWEET.  No lines at all - the place is a ghost town.  Bonus:  Sears carries (limited) land's end products.  I loveeeeee Land's End.

What a great place!  This is the "real deal" Italian Food, the way it is meant to be - Concetta is lovely and there is an abundance of great food.  Chicken picatta is perfect in its simplicity.  Veal (or chicken) Marsala is delicious.  Bruscetta, marinated carrots, roasted red peppers and what?  Cornbread!  (Yes, you read that right - cornbread in with the Italian bread.)  Loud and raucous bar area, but it lends to the jovial atmosphere. Parking is a NIGHTMARE.  Otherwise 5 stars.  You gotta come to Pesto.

I failed to consult with yelp before I purchased a $119 groupon for a (allegedly) $450 Boudoir photo session. After the fact I messaged my fellow yelpers who all told me that it would suck at Tommi.  I have to say - I was very pleasantly proved wrong.  There are, however, some areas that need improvement.  Firstly, you must realize that the owners, Tommi & Nikki (Photog husband and his studio-manager wife) had great troubles with the (now) former manager.  They fired her - and most of the staff and brought in Pierre & Carlo (remember them from the bottom of the Bellevue??).  The new spa manager is a doll and customer service oriented.  She also wound up doing my make-up because... (area for improvement)...  They only allowed 30 minutes to do my hair & makeup for the photo shoot.  The (sweet, 23 year old) newbie hairdresser spent over 40 on my hair alone (and it was not what I wanted so she cheerfully re-did it and it was better then).  The 23 year old then had to leave so the manager (Raeleah?  I know I spelled that wrong) jumped in and quickly did my make-up (AWESOME job, By the way( before rushing off to do a waxing client.  They need to schedule a bit better.  OK, so now I'm all prettied-up and Tommi, Nikki and the Pierre & Carlo owner's wife (can't remember her name) - who I thought was "just" a photog assistant - did the shoot.  They shot for over the promised hour and took over 100 shots.  I am very pleased with the three 8 X 10s (they gave me one extra - the deal was for 2). and the retouching.  Tommi is, indeed, a good photographer.  I would consider him for a wedding (but the package prices are high) and am now considering having my child photographed (NOT Boudoir!!!).  For $119 - this was a great value.  (Hair & Makeup alone can easily run $100.)  I see improvements in Tommi already - so if you were here a few months ago or longer and got "burned" consider giving them another try.  I can't wait to test out their pedicure services.  I am STILL on the search for a decent spa pedi in Philly.  (Tierra Mia is the best I've found but soooo expensive and the "natural" polish doesn't last and she won't use my toxic OPI from home.)  The search continues.  Much love to Tommi & Nikki though - for a wonderful experience. It's not every day that I get naked in front of total strangers.
The Black cat is a gift shop right next door to the White Dog Cafe.  They sell alot of cute, cute gift-y things here and jewelry.

I get sausage from Billy and his crew at the Media Farmers Market - and I just pulled a link of pork/broccoli rabe/sharp provolone outta the freezer, defrosted it and grilled it up.  Served it in 1 inch chucks over orzo pasta.  BLISS.  These are some of the best artisanal (Wilmington Made) links ever. Please make more chicken and turkey with greens (spinach, rabe, kale whatever you got!)  Seasoned to perfection.  Love!

Two words.  Taco Tuesdays!  They now offer (carry out only) $6.99 Daily Specials - and on Tuesdays - you can get tacos.  I got the fish tacos.  For $7.45 with tax - this is a great lunch!!!  Call your order in and they'll have it ready and waiting.

OMG!!!  On the advice of Danny Bonaduce (yes, really - we hear his ads for them EVERY morning on YSP) we took our 5 y.o. here for the $9.00 back to special hair cut.  It was perfect!  Even with the $4.00 tip we spent way less than we usually do.  (A kids cut at my guy is 20-25 - OUCH).  We will be back for sure - for a kid its great. Not so sure if I am brave enough to actuallly get MY hair cut here though.

I am dithering between 4 & 5 stars - because we did have 2 dishes that were NOT 5 star - but the decor, service and most of the food was great.  The wood floors, wall paper and paint are just stunning - and OH, that gorgeous bar!  We arrived early and sat at the bar - so we were able to order off of the Happy Hour Menu, Dirt List and Dinner Menus.  The 2 female bartenders were great and the vast array of home-made biters boggles the mind.  Drinks do contain bitters - so I asked for mine light on the bitters and that was a good thing for me.  The highlights of the menu were the corn with aioli (so sweet and fresh), golden beet/avodaco terrine-like salad with cucumber dill sauce and rye bread (a Horizon's holdover and fave) and the in-season heirloom tomato (at least 3 varieties on the plate) and mushroom salad over a thick green-goddess puree.  I am loving it here and can't wait to return.  There were at least 3 desserts we wanted to try (can't believe some of these are vegan).  Pot de Creme? But alas - we were just too full.  See you again, soon, Vedge!

It's a chain and it's 2 steps above the Olive Hell-Hole. My little daughter loves the pasta here and portions (even the non-family style ones) are ginourmous.  You'll need a doggie bag for sure.  Cheap, decent red-sauced fare heavy on the garlic.  A good time, but by no means a holy grail.

In the old days when 94.1 WYSP was classic rock (with Andre Gardner and Debbie Calton) I loved it.  Now all the good Classic rock is at WMGK 102.9 (Oddly enough that was the lite hits - valium rock channel back in the day.)  Also John DiBella (from WMMR is now on WMJK in the mornings - and is still as wacky as ever.  But I digresss..  Anyhow, now 94.1 plays alot of commercials.  In between the have a good mix of harder and softer well-known and lesser known rock and urban-rock hits.

Yonny - the guy who own's this TINY spot - is a doll.  And his Cherry Street hideaway serves up a mean breakfast (even grits!) and cheap lunches.  Wish they were open on weekends - or even for dinner, but alas, Breakfast and Lunch M-F only.  All the teachers at my kid's daycare (Friends Child Care Center - next door) get their coffee and breakfast sandwiches here. They also serve hot grits - which I love to get "to go" in the winter.  Philly needs more places like this. Especially in the culinary wasteland of Broad & Vine.  Quizno's just won't cut it.  I only wish they were open for dinner!

Good food and GREAT service but the parking lot at lunchtime (mixed with the drive through line is an accident waiting to happen.  Treacherous.  Be very careful driving in and out of here.  So busy at lunch (Monday - Friday) you would think they were giving it away.

Beautiful architecture in a partially remodeled old building. Decent food and stellar service from Erin (our server) and Christine - at reception.  Food was just OK though and perhaps it was just that I ordered a salad. A nice selection of Bigelow teas.  Great place to take a client.

It's a little more expensive than other fro yo joints, but yogorino rocks! The chocolate sauce with torrone in it is my 5 year old's fave, and I love to top it with fresh fruit (they even had kiwis and nectarines.).  Yummy!  And if you get a small (and only get fruit - not pistachio or chocolate) it's not as bad for you as some other treats.

I have been back several times for decent 3-4 star lunches now - usually alone. Today I ordered the Tuna TarTar which was excellent but 1 problem.  It says PINE NUTS and mine came with PEANUTS.  That is a BIG difference in taste and in price.  I wanted Pine Nuts.  Meanwhile the tuna chunks and avocado were delicious and in a lovely dashi/soy.  The dinosaur eggs (Special)  are too gloppy for me - I much prefer the cripsy eggplant (also a Special) topped with a dollop of (not-very) spicy tuna. I now ask for "sauce on the side" as a common mantra.  It has saved many a dish for me.  2 pieces of (supposedly home-made) tamago (sushi or sashimi - I got sushi)  for $3.50 were good but not the best ever.  Home-made tamago is a thing of beauty and this seemed frozen - although they swear that the hef made it himself.

Stopped in at 11:45 on a Monday and the place was empty. Started to fill up a bit by the time I left,  Very tasty (and bug) BLT for $6.75.  Basic, good "bar food" and sandwiches and lots of beers on tap.  Not bad!
Maggiano's catered a large company meal for the holidays and did a great job (in our office).  Food was hot and tasty and the dessert platter was surprisingly luxe for a chain catering/dining place.

Update:  Took my 10 year old here for an early (4:30 PM) dinner and she just LOVED every bite of her Alaskan roll and Shrimp tempura roll (garnished with eel sauce).  She wants me to give this place 5 stars.  She also gobbled down a fair bit of my (pricey at $14.95) specialty roll (can't remember the name) with lobster salad.  Sushi chefs treated her well (we sat at the bar). We'll be back very, very soon!  Smart kid!

Better than it used to be - and schedules are still often late/behind. Take the train if you can afford it - Greyhound is just awful.  Septa or Amtrak are much better than the buses.  Surly service from underpaid workers.

TJ's is a fun place to shop with really friendly, quirky, tatooed and pierced staff.  I think a pre-requisite for employ is that you must let your freak flag fly.  But anyhow, if you go on a non-peak time, it is simply a PLEASURE to shop here.  At "peak" times (like after work or Saturdays) it gets a little crowded and the lines can be long.  But the selection of merchandise is what keeps me returning again and again. Oh - that and that it's NEXT DOOR to my office.  SCORE!!!  Anyhow, this is not the greatest place for produce - alot of it is pre-packaged, but for FROZEN meals and appetizers, plus non-perishables from around the globe (Thai noodles, Indian curry kits, organic canned salmon, and dried fruits, nuts 7 trail mix.)  My ex-fiance SWORE by their coffee.  (And its a great value, too.)  I love Trader Joe's.  Now if only they' d figure out a way to have an entrance ON MARKET Street.

Food was 4 stars, service about a 2. I was dining alone - and is often the case - they tried to put me at the bar (high top) and I asked nicely to please be seated at a lower table.  They gave me one (it was not yet busy - early part of lunch crowd, and I know what a pain it is to seat a single) and then basically ignored me.  That said, my $9.99 half BBQ chicken salad was delicious - I added $3 worth of avocado. I love their herbal ranch dressing.  I will be back but next time with other diners.  Dining alone here is not fun.

We purchased my solid platinum, high-polish, 3 mm, comfort-fit wedding band (got my husband's at Carroll's jeweler's in Doylestown and the e-ring at Blue Nile - we really shop around.) here at Barsky's.  Ray Feldman, our sales consultant really know the jewelry biz - and pulled no punches in getting us the best deal for the gram weight of the ring.  (Platinum prices were sky high at the time.)  I would definitely consider Barsky's again.  We had a great experience.

3 star service (Danny is terrific but the food came out rather slowly and we were on lunch break) 4 star food - upscale "gastropub" type bar food.  I had been wanting to try Roots, and my group of 5 coworkers came for lunch - we only had an hour and lunch took easily 85 minutes.  Next time we will advise the staff that we are on a tighter time frame.  3 of the crew had burgers and they looked terrific with any toppings you could want - cheddar, bacon, fried (a little over cooked for my liking) egg.  I had the $10 lunch special of French Onion Soup ($6 on its own!) and a 1/2 sandwich (I chose the Chicken, Avocado and Pork Belly panini - yes, please!).  Both were scrumptious - albeit caloric.  Best of all?  The French Onion was not overly salted.  It was perfect.  I will return - but not on a day when I have a 1 PM meeting! Great selection of beers - and a full bar ('natch!)

Not nearly as bad as I had imagined. We have lived in Media for almost 5 years now and I have passed by Q's many times and it just "never appealed" - but we needed a bite (and some booze) after 9 PM.  On a week night.  And it Media - they roll up the sidewalks at about 7:45 PM.  So we had quesadillas (fine), prime rib egg rolls (just Meh) and a few mid priced drinks ($6 - $7 mixed drinks)  It's a bar, not fancy.  Mediocre "bar" food.  Plus they have Quizzo on Wednesdays.  I just might be back!

Meh.  Meh-xican. The good?  It is very inexpensive - I got a single enchilada for $3.50 and Guacamole for $5 and that was quiteenough for me.  Platters are $10 - $12 and cheaper at lunch.  Decent service - and it was nice & quiet when we went (late - like 8:30 on a Wednesday).  Not great - but not awful.  I wouldhave likes some pico de gallo with my chips (the salsa was just ok) but it was $3.00.

Tried K of T again - this time for lunch with my vegetarian, Indian friend.  We split an order of Chana Chat - a cold chick pea appetizer that is very good.  (Still served on the bed of iceberg.)  I had the same shrimp appetizer with a freshly fried poori - it is an appetizer but for me was perfect for lunch.  It came with 4 medium sized shrimp in a tomato based (tasy) sauce with onions and green peppers.  The sauce was so good on the poori (or over rice - I snagged a bit of my friends HUGE veggie biryani).  I have never been a big Indian food lover, but I can deal with the food here and find it very good.

I shop here. I admit it.  I do.  And I love that they carry Hint Water and a select aisle of organic goodies that I know and love.  Decent prices - and never that crowded on evenings or off hours.  (Weekends can get hectic.)  I prefer it to Acme, but will also shop there.

This place is too high priced for an every day lunch (at least for me - maybe it's fine for the attorneys with expense accounts) but - but - BUT...  TACO TUESDAYS!  (Take out only) gives you the (normally $11) fish tacos (2) with a side of black beans - to go - for $6.99 - about 7.60 with tax. Guac, Sourcream and some sort of chipotle crema (I get them all on the side).  That, I can live with.  I love Taco tuesdays at Du Jour.  Oh - and today I got a free breakfast sandwich (regularly $4.95 served with a small coffee) for signing up for their loyalty card.  The sandwich was great!  (Not sure if I can afford spending $5 on breakfast normally, though.)

Much better yogurt than Sweet Ending (even my 6 year old agrees) but we all like Yogorino's yogurt best (for taste - but not for toppings and certainly not for price).  Meanwhile, for 51 cent per oz., Tutti Frutti is a good "bang for the buck" in fro-yo land.  My little one got Orange, Pomegranate, Cheesecake and Plain (Tart) Yogurt) and covered it in fruit and candy.  I opted for a small bit of the tart classic plain with come blueberries and 2 mini-cream puffs on top.  The yogurt is so cold it froze the berries!  (The guy behind the counter - who is a doll and also easy on the eyes! - said than many people opt NOT to put gummy bears nor jelly beans because the yogurt freezes them rock-hard.)  So anyhow, we like Sweet Ending - sure - and we frequent the Rittenhouse one - but whenever we venture East of Broad and feel a fro-you craving coming on - the little one and I head straight to Tuttti Frutti.  Good stuff.  Stick to the Original Plain - it's the best (IMO).

This place is getting better and better - faster checkouts, they take credit/debit/food stamps (and cash).  Be a little cautious of the very cheap aisle (on the left) - it's "Eat now or forever hold your peace" but i saw a lady with a big bag of Donut peaches for $2.73 (89 cents a pound!).  Today I scored some pluots, nectarines, cherries, baby bell peppers, BIG spotless white mushrooms and a bunch of leeks.  I also ran into an old friends.  5 stars at RTM and IOVINE's today.

About 3 to 3.5 stars for friendly service, a clean restroom and decent dining area. Out of our group of 5 - not one of us had pizza.  Kids enjoyed their jumbo hot dogs and fries, chicken tenders. Ladies liked the basic, but crisp iceberg house salads. (I got mine without onions.) A small chicken parm sandwich here is plenty big - and the veal with spinach was - just OK.  We'll be back - and we'll let you know how the pizza is. Great for kids and families - lunch prices much cheaper than dinner - and big portions of (just OK) food.

I haven't been to Shiroi in a very long time - their other restaurant Doma is closer to home and is now our go-to place - but Shiroi never disappoints me.  We are even planning a big party here in April.  Love the spicy tuna hand roll here, house-made tamago, ohitashi.  Sublime!  Fresh and yummy.

Service and food waxes and wanes depending on the day/server/cook on duty.  In general I usually find something to eat here - especially breakfast food - like pancakes and omelettes.  My parents like the chicken pot pie here - which is extremely rich, caloric and loaded with chunks of white-meat chicken.  Not my fave - but a solid option for a cheap, no-fuss meal. And big pots of decent coffee.

An Italian Deli with a good assortment of REAL Italian meats and cheeses, plus dried pasta and olive oils.  A few hard to find items, too - and tomato pie and DiBruno Brothers products (a few) to save you a schlep to Philly.  A little taste of Sou-filly in good old "white bread" Aston.  The lady and young man working there were very nice to my 9 year also - who devoured a 1/4 lb of macaroni salad right IN the store.  Kudos to Ellen G. for telling me about this place.  It's in a strip mall which is one of 3 strip malls on 452 and that all look similar. I had driven right by many times and never thought to go in.  Big mistake - you gotta try this place.

I enjoyed my meal at Roys.  I had the 3 course prix-fish and the buttery fish (mahi mahi) was delicious.  Roy's has a hawaiian/asian fusion flair to it.  The non-alcoholic version of a ginger mojito I ordered had fresh mint, limes, ginger and pineapple.  So refreshing.  The deseerts and apps were tasty too.  It's hard to believe it's a chain that OutBack owns.

I returned at the RR with good friends and colleagues last night and we were treated to stellar service (Thanks, Dave!) and fantastic (El Rey) food.  We ordered literally "one of everything" - cheese plate, charcutterie platter, chrimp cocktail, salsa/guac and chips, 3 kinds of tacos and gorditas.  All were terrific.  Drinks ($8 for the special to $12 for bartenders choice) are works of art and magic.  Such mixology.  However my simple glass of Marqui de la tour with a swirl of fresh raspberry in it was a refreshing treat.  Try the Meloni Swizzle.   Also the "Blackmail".  YUM!!!!!  Love it here.

Love coming here for all my Italian Market needs without schlepping to Souffilly.  Correpolese Tomato Pie on the weekends, good Parm, prepared foods, San Marzano Tomatoes, Eggs, Milk and Bread.  Love it here.

Stop here and at Ok Lee  (as aforementioned) to nab the freshest produce and a few bargains that must be consumed quickly.  Fresh berries and citurs are cheaper here than the grocery stores. A large variety of greens and apples as well.  A great place for the home cook to buy whatever is needed. Gotta love it!

Prices are too high for the 1 oz sampler (4 one ounce bottles for $20?  Ouch). The regular bottles (Oil or Vinegar) are all $16.95.  Truffle oils are (of course) higher.  I enjoyed sampling the single-note olive oils but the flavored ones (butter flavored??) did not thrill me.  Also the White Balsamic (I tried the Lemon one) was entirely too tart.  I really love REAL balsamic from Modena - so for me the vinegars were just OK - best ones are the fig and black cherry. (Sweet - of course) but the underlying vinegar is not the best I've ever had.  Good but not a holy grail.  That said - I bought a $17 bottle of arbequina oil for a friend and think she will enjoy it.

2 star service, 3 or maybe 4 (for fast food) star food. Maybe.  I can here at an off time ( 3PM on a Wednesday) and the place was empty. One table of 2 eating in the front and 6 (yes SIX) uniformed staffers eating and chatting at a back booth.  Order counter?  Empty.  So I asked "Anybody working?" and one guy got up and walked to the kitchen door and shouted "You've got a customer".  I guess taking a break is priority over customer service.  Anyhow - they are young kids running the joint.  So I ordered a chicken sandwich and classic fries (showstring) for my 12 year old at her request.  Came to $9.80 after tex - no drinks.  Ouch.  She loved it though - even their own "private label" ketchup.  I would return - but I am not a fast food chick. It's a glorified fast food joint.  The true test will be when I try a burger here. The chicken seems fine.  Like any other chicken sandwich.

There are alot of Bonte's around. This is for the one on 17th Street near Chestnut.  The waffles here smell better than they taste.  To me they were just OK.  The coffee, however was very good and not "burned-tasting" like Charbucks.

The DD inside 30th Street Station near the McDonalds is fine - the one up by SEPTA is a bit grosser.  All in all - they are the same-old-same-old  DD we all know. I get my occaisional Iced decaf french vanilla with lowfat milk and a splenda here on my way to the train.  Nice Indian-American staff move as quickly as they can during the rush.  I give them alot of credit!

Started out GREAt and was all down hill from there.  In the fall of 2007 I went to Mission grill and had the most AMAZING lunch.  A delicious salad with shrimp & crab - fresh avocado and mango.  Cilantro-lime-yumminess for dressing and cute little tortilla strips.  Four to Five star food and great service.   It was so good - and the place so new (I had yet to realize that "The pube" - public house - owns it.) that I even RECOMMENDED others at my firm to try it.  I had another good lunch.  And another.  And then my (now husband, then) fiance and I went for New Years eve. And it was about 3 stars.  (Now, I know, I know, NYE is a bad night on which to judge a rest-o - but wait...)  In February 2008 I retuned for another lunch - and lo... the menu was completely changed.  No more salad. No more empananas Mediocre gazpacho.  And service has gone waaaaaaaaay downhill.  I also came for a happy hour in April 2008 where I had a "$5. Margarita" that tasted like lime pixie dust.  Sorry.  The place has peaked and is now on the way down. I hope they'll turn it around.

Damon, Rick's son is a terrific guy and the food we had at our 200+ person corporate BBQ was good - but honestly?  Not great.  The ribs were definitely good - falling off the bone but very charred tasting.  Pulled pork was a bit dry, but totally "saveable" with sauce.  Chicken was dry as the Sahara.  Not OK. Again, over-charred for my liking.  I really wanted to give higher marks, but due to the "burnth taste" (some people love this) I just could not.  I bet in the restaurant (our event was onsite - not at the restaurant) the quality is higher.

I had not been back to gomo in a long, long time - over a year - since my last experience was so "meh" - but on Friday I was pressed for time and in serious need of a polish change (no time for a full mani, even).  By some miracle - even though gomo's was "hoppin'" busy they squeezed me in for a quick polish change and I even got 10 minutes of (just OK  but so needed) chair massage while they dried.  Big con:  The "therapist" (and I use that term loosely) chatted in Korean the entire time she massaged me.  Chattered LOUDLY.  Not relaxing.  Big pro:  the older Russian lady who did my polish change clearly knows her stuff.  She's been at Gomo's since they opened 19 years ago.

I want to give this place higher marks, but I just can't. Why?  Because the food it just not that great.  Here's why...  First of all this place is VERY kid friendly - so if you want a quiet spot, this is not for you.  We were seated near the front door (which blasted us with frigid air each time someone opened it) and next to us was a table of 15 middle schoolers.  Oh my.  So that aside, our lovely young server (Blake?  She told me her name twice and I still did not retain it.) was attentive, friendly and 5 star all the way.  By now the noise is nearing deafening. We get our apps/snacks.  French Fries (an enormous order for $4) and $12.50 for the tuna tartare which was drowning in 3 types of sauces.  All sauce .  Could barely taste the fish.  It's a shame because in concept this could be a wonderful dish.  Next came a cup of beef chili with sour cream which was good but the beans were a little hard/tough.  Not too spicy (which for me was a good thing) but if you are a chili lover you may find it too mild.  Dessert was the best part and even it was not that great.  A home-made "Chipwich" - 2 chocolate chip cookies with chocolate (or vanilla) ice cream in between.  Enormous - and we took part of it home.  All that said, I will return to Christophers - but with Teresa's and Matador and Paramour all nearby - there are better dining experiences within a quick walk.  Christopher's is a great place to take your over-indulged, entitled children (Mine included - but even "the princess" would balk at the over sauced tuna tartare).

Let's hear it for my 1400th review on yelp. Well - here it goes...  I just got back from a delicious lunch at Mixto with a good (vegetarian)  friend of mine.  After we each had a stiff, refreshing Classic Mojito each (and I was beginning to feel the buzz). Our friendly - if a little slow- waiter took our orders.  I had the Plato Vegetariano and my friend had a Salad with Avocado added on top.  Both were fresh and excellent.  I asked them to omit the tostones (green plantains) on my platter and sub maduros (sweet plantains) and thus I had an abundance of maduros to share with my friend.  I also gave him some of the Yucca, black beans and 1/4 of the SCRUMPTIOUS white corn arepa.  Wow.  I can not wait to go back.  Why not 5 stars?  A few reasons - in fact I was dithering between 3 & 4 stars.  Service here is, indeed, weird.  Since we arrive just before noon and the place was dead empty our service was better than it could have been - but I imagine at peak times this place is just NUTS.  They do kind-of check you out upon arrival.  The hostess was icy-cold.  Bus person (male) was very nice.  Also some might say that there are not enough vegetarian options - you basically can have salads or the plato - and that's it.  Fortunately I loved the plato - that arepa and the maduros were PERFECT.  It aslo had steamed (bland) veggies, yellow rice and a clump of mixed green salad in a tasty sweet dressing.  The mojios were STRONG and well muddled.  We went back again a few weeks later and had Vanilla and Pasion Fruit mojitos which were, indeed, sweeter but so delicious.  Oh - and the LARGE ($13) really is large.  I can't wait to return.  Again - I'll try for a non peak time. (The weekend madness here is just not for me.)  Oh - and they DON'T take reservations unless it's a party of 5 or more.

This is pretty much as "good as it gets" for a Fourbucks. There is a drive through - but the walk-in service is even better with a spacious dining area - and super clean (brand new) facilities.  Excellent service and a full staff during the AM rush.  Plenty of parking.  Yay!!!

The staff here is terrific and remember me from the days "across the street" at the old location.  This location is much larger and has a drive though and takes up a large portion of the parking lot - so there is less parking for the stores in the strip mall and Acme.  Media needed this!!!

OMG. This is truly "as good as it gets" for a Qdoba.  They have a Bar! A BAR!!!!!! In a Qdoba.  I can't believe it!  And Kelly the bar tender is fantastic.  Love her.  The house margarita  (regularly 4.50) is just $2.50 during Happy Hour.  Plus free chips and salsa or queso???  OMG run here!!!  Before they come to their senses.  I am so shocked, surprised and PLEASED.   Puts the shitty Springfield Qdoba to SHAME!   Wow.

A safe place to take the kids and grandparents in one fell swoop.  Avoid peak times (like Saturday and Sunday breakfast, and you'll be fine.  The $4 "Five" breakfast - 1 eggm 2 pancakes and 2 pieces of bacon (or sausage) is a good value.  Kids meals are also decent here for kids 12 & under.

OMG Romano's is just AWFUL.  Yes, it's a chain.  Yes they serve sub-par bitter (often rancid) carafes of inedible olive oil on every table.  Yes, the food is loaded with salt.  No, this is not what Italian-American food should be.  No, I do NOT want to ever come back here.

Taste of Puebla has set up a stand at the Media Farmers Market selling guacamole, pico de gallo and salsa fresca (verde). They are there every Thursday from 3 PM -8 PM.  All are very good as are ther chips.  Can't wait to go to the restaurant now!

Customer service is slacking - especially if you order inside the store (They are all busy dealing with the drive thru).  You need better counter people - some of the old crew has left and you can tell.  Step it up, Media, Starbucks.  We need you!

There is little atmosphere and as a result - prices are low.  You can get a very good massage here from Katherine.  (Dawn - my favorite - moved away.)  Linens are clean and tables are comfortable and adequate.  There is alot of turn over in the therapists, and I suspect they do not make much money.    It is NOT a spa/luxe experience - for for a chair massage - or a quick 30 or 60 minute table massage its a solid quick fix.  Often you can just walk in - but I like to call and make an appointment.

5 stars for the donuts (have not yet tried the chicken). I got 6 hots (2 of each flavor - strawberry, vanilla spice and coffee) and they were devoured by my friends and I.  SO good.  But - the line/queue system neeeds better signage and direction (like, chicken over here, donuts over there... etc.)  The crowds are crazy!!  Oh - and the fancy donuts sell out FAST so get there early.

Finally got to try house - and while the food was very good beware - service is SLOW.  Do NOT come here in a hurry.  It took 35 minutes to be served entrees (My friend's cup of tomato soup arrived right away and we all stared and watched him eat it.)  I tasted 1 spoonful of the tomato soup - it was drizzled with olive oil (just a bit) and tasted good but as others have said - not mindblowing.  The eggs benedict was EGGs-xcellent.  The crab avocado one and the spinach/tomato one were both great.  It took me a long while to come here and now I will definitely be back. But not when I am in a hurry - and I will not come at 12 - closer to 11:30 is better.  The place gets packed at lunchtime.

This is my favorite sushi spot in Philly.  And I have been to Morimoto (twice), Raw, Fuji Mountain, Mizu and many, many others.  Shiroi is not a "show place" but it serves very fresh product with a wide variety of fish.  The kitchen entrees are well prepared and there are some great values to be had.  The Tuna Lover's platter and Vegetarian Special (a bento box) never disappoint.  I enjoy eating here and have many times and intend to come back many more times.

When corporate cafeteria meets expense account meets cliché meets enormous beer list, you get a place like City Works.  I was treated to lunch here on my company's dime (Thank goodness because the food - while good - is not awe inspiring.)  It's actually about 4 stars for Food - the prices, service and NOISE are what makes this place less than ideal.  I am glad my coworkers are good conversationalists and smart however...  I could not hear them.  You can not hear yourself think in here. I am not old.  I am not an old fart, but man, Lunch on a Friday was crowded (we somehow got a table right away so that was lucky) and NOISY.  I had a $15 salad that was worth about $11. Copious amounts of "parsley" fries were served to everyone BUT me.  (Salads don't come with fries - and that is just fine.  Pineapple Cider sounds intriquing as does Space Dust IPA.  It's amazing what a little marketing can do.  Corporate America should keep this place afloat for years.

Poco's has been in the bottom of the Courthouse Motor Inn on Main Street in D-town for years.  And in all those years the food has never improved - yet people still go here and many, many people LOVE it.  Just not me.  I don't HATE it - it's just "Meh"xican.  Boring, nacho-esque Ameri-mex.  (Or worse, Pennsy-Mex?)  But I do love Doug Esch - and all the D. Esch boyz.  Lot's of nostalgia for me at Poco's.  Save me a barstool, pour me a margarita, rocks 'n salt - and I'll be downing nachos along with the rest of 'em.

I used to work at the Mercer Museum - as a summer day camp counselor \many years ago.  We would take the kids to Fonthill for tours as well.  Anyhow, Fonthill is the steel re-enforced home of Henry Chapman Mercer who also built his workshop & tile works right next door.  His beloved horse Lucy and dog Rolo took part in the construction.  Kids and Adults can both learn from the one hour tour at Fonthill.  A trip to the Mercer Museum is also a must.  (Especially during the annual Folk Fest.)  You can also get married on the grounds of Fonthill. and it's a great place to have a picnic in the summer or fall. Christmas is a gorgeous time at Fonthill with an enormous tree in the great hall and candle-lit tours.  (Not sure if they still do these.)  What a marvelous piece of local history.

It a basic, fairly clean, safe, cheap, Perkins, Not my choice for a gourmet experience - but if you want coffee and pancakes - and if you have kids and are budget conscious it's a fine option.  This location (Doylestown) gets packed on Sunday mornings after about 9 AM.  So go early or very late, or else there will be a wait for a table.  Out party of 7 was seated right away at 8:35 AM on a late summer Sunday.  The kids breakfasts are huge and caloric - the chocolate chip covered Pancake Bear or the Sprinkle & whipped-topping laden "Rainbow panckaes" are a big hit with our little girl - but man are they BAD for her.  Service is a bit spotty and often there are no creamers, or no jam or something is missing that we need.  If we ask they will get it for us.  Weird.    The breakfast rush is quite a scene for sure here at Perkins.  Oh- and there are sometimes COUPONS in the Daily Intelligencer - so be on the lookout for those.

I've had Old City iced coffee many, many times at the RTM location - but it was not until today that I had the pleasure (and it really, really was a true pleasure) to sit and linger (we scored a great outdoor table - they only have 2) over a yummy iced coffee (my friend had a HUGE mug of cappucino with a hearty cap of yummy foam in it - PERFECT!) in Old City today.  We had such a great time - and spent nearly 2 hours just drinkin', smokin', yakin' and having a great afternoon.  Thanks for NOT being a Charbucks.  Great coffee and a fun place to just hang out. And 2 nice, young, handsome barristas - eye candy never hurts.

LOVE it here!  (Nearly gave then 5 stars) Bountiful acres has been supplying Bucks COunty gardeners with plants and shrubs and floral supplies for YEARS and Years and years.  They have a large selection of live plants - and seasonally (especially in spring) there is an annual rush for annuals.  The staff (the ones who aren't teen-aged kids of the people who work there) are very knowledgeable about gardening and horticulture.  A great source for the home gardener.  The prices can be high (for some things - like flats of begonias or impatiens) but the quality is much higher than those same cheapie flat you could buy at K-Mart.  I really enjoy shopping here.  Oh - and Halloween at Bountful is SUCH fun.  Pumkins and gourds galore.  Great source for Christmas tress, swags, wreaths and greenery, too.

We had a marvelous time at RR last night - but we came with a group of 9 - a few straggled in later and seating for large groups is less than ideal.  Drinks were $12 as usual and the bartender's choice was perfect for me.  I had 3 "Blackmails" and one of my friends had 2 French 75's.  The Maloney swizzle is a colorful sweet treat as well.  Food was just OK. The cheese plate and chocolate mezcal popcorn were a hit, but the best bite of the night were the 2 orders of $10 (ouch) guacamole from El Rey's menu.  The charcutterie plate was uninspired and the raved about meatball sandwich was "meh" to me.  (Try the Turkey club instead.)  Service was good - but we got there the moment they opened and as it got busier (round about 8 PM) servise slowed down.  (This is to be expected).  Try to come early and leave before the "cool kids" arrive.  I still enjoy Ranstead - but now that I have been here thrice, no need to rush back. And the $200+ tab was no joke!  P.S.  Bring a flashlight!!!!
It's OK.  Not too bad for diner food. We had brunch/late breakfast here and the french toast and pancakes were just fine.  Decent South-Philly.

Seems very chain-y. Food was greasy and they do use American cheese. Food was meh - and chips are indeed, thick and stale tasting.  Service was fine (Thus the 3 stars) as we came early (11:50 AM) before the lunch crowd got going.  It was edible and "meh". If a coworker insists, I would return but I am in no hurry to rush back.

Don't hate me, but I prefer Starbucks, Dunkin or even Wawa to Saxby.  That said this is super convenient - right inside the doors to the Liberty Place shops.  I have gotten a latte here before and it was fine.  Not amazing, but what I "needed" at the time.  Same kinda (high) prices as a Starbucks.  Beans taste roastier, if that is even possible.  The best coffee is still La Colombe in my opinion.  (Or Blue Bottle if you can get it freshly made.)

You gotta love this place.  The unique selection, the Amish, VietNamese, Asian, Italian and American stands all crammed in together.  Sure it's a bit grimey and can get mobbed at lunchtime, but give me Iovine's Produce, Och's Chicken Breasts, Some Tom Kha Gai from Little Thai Market and a hot fresh macadamia nut cookie from 4th St and I am good to go.  It is a blessing to live nearby.

Well - I think they are finally out of business. I was told that the chef and menu had changed and was gfiven a coupon for free guacamole and 20% off the bill.  Sounded OK so I made a reservation. When I needed to change the reservation a lady answered the phone and said they are closed.  For good..

I am not an Old Navy fan and generally regard them as "disposable clothing" that you can wear for a summer or three, but I was in dire need of shorts and Old Navy delivered.  Not a bad choice - and as ON's go this one is well organized with plenty of cashiers at the front counter.  Lady running the changing rooms was friendly and nice as well.  Got in, got shorts, got out.  Bam!

Kafta Lamb Kebab over salad was great, Chicken Shwarma was too dry for me - but that said I did not load it down with sauces and tahini.  I did try the (very good) baba gahannouj and (not as good) garlic whip - on the side.  The Yogurt-Cucumber was very nice also.  Tomatoes and cukes were fresh.  I got in and out for $10.50 (including tax) and had a BIG whompin' bowl of Lebanese-inspired goodness.  I shall return.  The Qdoba of Middle Eastern.

Very, very pleased by our service from Sandy (and also Carol herself on the phone). We were able to transfer title and tags easily.  Brava!  Note:  $5 fee for using a credit card to pay.  (They like cash.)
I have purchased pretzels and pretzel-dogs at a few locations in Center City Philly and they are always fresh and tasty.  Carbo-loaded goodness.

Nicely presented food - but the quantity was pretty skimpy - but that may be because of the reduced bugdet our building had for parties this year.  Anyhow, Miles catered our building's annual holiday cocktail (really beer, wine & soda) party and set out some antipasto (delicious olives, caponata, artichokes with long, tasty stems) cheeses, dried fruits and fresh grapes, a few dessert items. (Frozen creeam puffs and pre-made tartlet sheels filled with gloppy cream. A few cannoli.)  Uninspired. (But it beats chips 'n dip.)  As said before -presentation was lovely.  Service was great.  The also butlered a few platters of seared tuna with a wasabi "cream cheese" on a crispy-fried chip.  They were delish!  The cranberry chicken spring rolls were odd tasting.  The beef brisket sliders looked vile.  I passed.  Friends enjoyed the mini crabcakes and toasted "grilled cheese" one biters (with goaty-goat cheese.  Baaaaah!).  All in all, the servers were friendly and efficient, but the food was just OK - and there was not enough of it.    But hey - it was "free" (we pay enough in rent throughout the year to justify a holiday bash!).

We came with an extremely large (over 25 people) group and had reserved the big green tent outdoors. Our server was a little "snippy" but very efficient and a good server.  She just seemed a bit pissed off for most of the time we were there. Note:  they will NOT split the check on weekends,  The food was very salty and heavy (especially what we ordered) but presented nicely. Most of all though - it was over priced.  $15.50 for a pulled pork sandwich?  $17.50 for my 10 year old's fish & chips?  Ugh.  Oh - and sodas are $3.25 each NO refills.  OUCH!  But there are cute doggies there (a very dog friendly place) and it's great fun to sit outside. We do not live near here, and unless we are going canoeing again and North brook or coming here with locals we likely won't be back any time soon.
Such wonderful foods - freshly grated Parmegiano Reggiao, fried eggplant slices, deli meats and cheese, long hots, pastas.  So great.  They also stock Corropolese tomato pies!  Love it so much.

The frozen custard is quite good.  I am not a water ice eater - but I love the custard at Rita's.  News flask their "Gelatti" is NOT Gelatto.  It is a bastardizion combo of water ice and custard.  Whatever.  It tastes good.

We had no real problems with the service at Bistro 24 - and clearly breakfast is a better way to go than lunch/dinner fare.  I had a seafood Cobb salad that was just OK - the avocados was very under-ripe and I did not eat them.  My friend had blueberry pancakes and they looked great.  Young servers and trainees following them around.  Clean restrooms.  No issues.

I truly love this place (looks like nothing in a strip mall but PLEASE seek this place out).  Parmagiano Reggiano for $14.99 per lb?  Amazing.  Viso's cannoli shells.  Cookies.  Pastries. Pasta.  Eggplant (grilled in store).  So many cured meats.  The REAL deal Italian - plus deli stuff.  Snagged a dozen eggs for 89 cent.  89 CENTS!!!!!  Cheaper than any supermarket.  Owner is a very kind man and related to Claudio's in South Philly.  WE NEED MORE PLACES like this!  We need a REAL butcher shop.  Any takers?

They did our wedding flowers and came in at just under our budget of $1,000.  Amy was terrific and the flowers were upscale and just what we wanted.  They were excellent in their communications via email and phone.  We paid for our wedding in 3 installments.  Most of our flowers involved Bluebird roses, blue hydrangea and different colored irises (light & dark blue and purple).  The colors were vibrant and the arangements, bouquets and boutenieres (all but one - which contained white freesia) survived our 96 degree wedding day.  The flowers on the cake were gorgeous, too, as were the 10 small centerpieces.  We love Kremps.

Shiroi - how I've missed you. The sushi chef who knows me "by face". The older waitress who brings me genmaicha.  The incredibly fresh sashimi.  I miss it here so much!  I stop in whenever I can - which is about once a year now.

Stopped in to inquire about wheatgrass - and they DO carry it. Will be back later this week to get some.  Update:  Got a shot of wheat grass for $1.99 yesterday - EXCELLENT. I will be back several times per week, budget permitting.  Friendly service - place was nearly empty at 12:45 PM on a Monday.

An old-fashined five 'n dime style "everything" store - stationary, household goods, kid stuff, party goods, wrapping paper, tools, socks.  A vast variety that is as close as Media, PA gets to the "Vermont COuntry Store".  A note of nostalgia and fun shopping here and a sweet lady at the cashier in the evening time on weekdays.  Louis B. gets it right!
2 word have restored my faith in YSP.  Danny Bonaduce.
Meh.  Just ok, but my elderly parents love it here. Inexpensive and "safe" breakfast, lunch and dinner, too.  Avoid the fish (salmon, talapia), ick.  Stick to eggs and pancakes

Food is consistently good here and the market is great for Covid-Takeout when you don't want to cook.  The pistachio Chicken is amazing.  The full bar is great and live music when Covid and weather permits.  Sarah our server was friendly and attentive.  An enjoyable evening.

I don't come here often - but when I do, I make it count. To me, the "hots" are the clear attraction here - and the plain hot donut that comes when you order fried chicken.  I walk it - get ONE (and only ONE - although I would love two) hot, eat it on my way to getting coffee and go.  This time I got Cinnamon Brown Sugar and it was HOT and fresh and just a bit greasy and perfect.  So bad for you, but so good.  Oh - and at 11:30 AM on a Wednesday?  No line!

Since there is no Sephora in Media, we head to ULTA to play with SOME of the brands we like.  Lorac, Urband Decay, Murad, Dermalogica, Alterna, Redken, OPI.  The staff is not nearly as knowledgable as you might think - it really depends on the person and a few of the "gals" seem harried and hurried.  Also there is ALWAYS a line at check out. (At least on weekdays after 5 PM and Saturday mornings, which is usually when we go.  Read the circular, use your points - and some GREAT sales (Like LORAC glosses 50% off - $8 instead of $16) can be found!
Visited El Gran Rodeo with a friend and we sat in the bar area. Enjoyed our Drinks (Mojito was perfect) and Hot Queso app.  Delicious burrito and chimichanga.  So great.

What a great spot for Mexican - and in a strip mall, no less. Our excellent server (kinda looked like the guy from Entourage on TV) got my friend and I in and out of there quickly during a weekday lunch.  Oh - and they serve not only chips and salsa - but a spicy creamy ranch-like dip, too.  Good stuff.  Great lunch specials and reasonably priced.  Can't wait to try it again!

At the risk of the yelp-police removing my review, I feel I must say what I am about to write:  We were so looking forward to trying this place but as we walked in I could already smell rotting/dead fish, faintly,  in the vestibule.  When we opened the door I could not make it passed the hostess stand.  The smell was just. not. good.  A sushi place should NOT have any sort of a fishy odor.  We walked out.  Might try again but I am in no hurry.

Very tasty food - but a bit too rich for my blood. I would love to be able to cater my next party using DiFabio's - the pistachio crusted Chicken (fingers or breast") are truly delicious.  Friendly service.  Sigh...maybe next year.

Got some much needed dry dog food and dog supplements here - no issues and the manager was very helpful.  Prices are just OK but sales (if you can get 'em) are good.  Bonus - next door to Target so we can do both stores in one trip.

This place is so cute, it's PRECIOUS.  Everything from the cutesy sayings about their cash-only policy, to the old-fashioned cash register that rings up your order (manned by a very cute man dressed in white with a white paper soda-jerk hat!).  This place is a gem.  A true taste of nostalgia with home-made ice-cream and old-time soda fountain treats.  You can even get a NY style egg cream.  I would definitely come here.  It is a like a modern day trip down memory lane.  (And yummy, too.)  But bring the cash!  You'll need it.

This place is way passed its prime.  It's been around since the late eighties - and back then was one of the only "Adult" shops around.  Frankly, I can't believe they are still here.    But yes, you can stock up on toys and party favors here - and other "naughty bits".  And yes, it is in the BASEMENT - and theirs just something psychological for me about going DOWN into a sex shop.  (Ba dum, bump!)

3.5 stars is probably more accurate - but I am rounding up to 4 because my husband enjoyed it (he says it's better than Alma de Cuba - I disagree) and they were very accomodating to our 7 year old on a bustling Friday night.  Alma de Cuba is also great for its bar and party vibe.  My $9 Classic Mojito was perfect - not too strong (but if you like a strong drink you might not agree).  Vaca Frita, Ropa Vieja, Maduros, Chicken Empanada (a little small) and Classic Bean Beans & Rice were all they way "they are supposed to be".  Excellent Food, a bit high priced for cuban.  Better than Mixto, not quite as good (nor as pricey/trendy/hoity-toity) as Alma de Cuba (IMHO).  Go and enjoy.  Ryan - our server was cordial and attentive.  A great guy!  Many thanks to Alma de Cuba for participating in Friends Select School's Dining with Friends program.  We hope many people will come here!

So happy to have found this place - and for lunch ($7.95 Bun or Broken Rice Plates) oit is a steal.  Delicious Wonton Soup and Bun (Rice Vermicelli) bowls. At dinner the carpaccio appetizer ($7.95) and  DELUXE Bun - with pork, chicken, meatballs (grilled to perfection and so juicy) and spring roll is super filling at $10.95.  Perfect Summer rolls. Wonderful service from lovely ladies.  We'll be back - and I hope soon.

Hallelujah!  Penzey's is here! I am so grateful there is a Philly location (alas, Chestnut Hill is closed). Picked up some Shallot Pepper, BBQ 3000, Onion Powder and Chicago Steak seasoning.  I have been a HUGE Penzey's user for years.  Welcome to the city!!!!!

Most people LOVE the Barnes Foundation - and I bet the new Center City space will be a true spectacle.  My parents had dragged us here since childhood and mom is/was a member and supporter, so we kids had art & culture shoved down our throats.  Thus, I too, love the Barnes foundation.  And the arts.  Thanks, Mom!

Pretty darned awful.  We were cajoled into coming here by our 5 year old after dining at the illiustrious IHOP next door.  After purchasing $10.00 worth of tokens it was off to the filthy, sticky, germ-laden "rides" and games.   I could feel myself contracting a rhinovirus by the minute. Oh - and when I put a token in the mini carousel (my kid was the only one on it) about 5 little kids sensed "free ride" and pushed their way on board freaking her (and me) right out.  NO PARENTAL supervision of these kids.  Ugh.  We also played some "ski-ball" and then the little one fed the tickets into the "ticket muncher" to have them counted which took about 23 minutes.  The 103 tickets got her a cheap plastic ring, stickers and some small plastic object that I still don;t know what it is.  And we still have about 8 tokens left over for next time.  Next time?  Oh dear g-d please don;t make me come back here.

I can not say enough good things about Roz and her generosity. She provided Kosher Catering for an event we held at "The Expressive Hand" (a paint your own pttery place) and the food was simple and delicious.  Perfect for our group of 20-ish.  The cupcakes had a delicious icing - hard to believe they were dairy free! I did not find the cupcakes to be "dry" or "lacking flavor" - I had the chocolate with chocolate icing and it was very good.  There was also a gogeous crudite tray with several types of hummus.  YUM!  Thanks, Roz.  We love working with you.

People are raving about this - but my experience was just OK. I spend nearly $5.50 for a large iced latte (more than Charbucks) and it was warm.  Not enough ice.  The line was long and moved very slowly.  This is not a place to come for "commuter coffee" - it is way more leisurely.  The ladies working up front were friendly and kind but moved oh-so slowly.  Maybe my inner Manhattanite is showing but for the speed, price and lackluster latte, I'm sticking to Wawa or Charbucks.

Omg! Came back to Shiroi after nearly 7 years and they treated us like celebrities.  The tuna lovers plate ($42, includes 2 pieces of chu-toro), naked tuna on crispy rice, oshi-tashi with bonito and succulent salmon tartar were all sheer perfection.  Swimmingly fresh.  Fabulous service, nothing "shi-shi" or hipster or fancy, just amazingly good sashimi, nigiri and maki.  We love you and sister-restaurant Doma, too.  Run, don't walk, to Shiroi Hana today!

I like Grand Rodeo - mysterious "ranch dressing" white sauce and ketchup-y salsa and all.  It's great for families with or without kids.  Service (Kudos to Ricardo) was terrific even on a jam-packed (20 minute wait) Saturday night.  Love it here.
I have now been to 3 of the 5 (or is it 6) El Limon locations and I have just two words to say:  Al Pastor.  Seriously.  I have dreams about it.
Brand-new CFA serving up all your favorites with a cheerful "My Pleasure". Closed Sundays.  Double-laned drive thru.  Always busy but so well managed.

Three cheers for Ethan who provides amazing customer serviceI stopped in on an early Monday morning (They open at 7 AM) to get a dozen "hots" for my work colleagues.  So fresh (made to order) and wonderful.  $15 a dozen puts Dunkin to shame.  I can't eat donuts often - but when I do, I make it count and FedNuts ROCKS.

OMG - a BIG 5 stars for Melissa (not Missy!) who has now been cutting my 6 year old's hair since September.  She is great (the place - probably 3 stars - but she gets 5).  So patient and great with my little one.  And for $12 - what a deal!!  Thanks again to Danny Bonaduce (love him!  and he married Amy - a yelper - so Go Danny!) for sending us to Supercuts.  They make my kiddo SuperCUTE.

A great place to pick up authentic Mexican products - and produce. Plus fresh baked pastries and breads, canned goods like beans and chiles en adobada.  Nopales. Chiles. Frijoles.  Everything you need.

Soooooo close to 5 stars - and definitely 5 star service from Jack today for a leisurely, late lunch (L.L.L.) including that fantastic "power green" soup.  I just love it.  (Does contain dairy so not vegan - and very rich with cream and parmesan cheese thus negating the veggies.)  You gotta try that soup.  So delicious.

Still terrific and now some brand new digs! Went to Gran Rodeo at the new location (down "the block" from the old building) twice now.  Much more space and a bigger, nicer bar area.  Food was great - cheese dip (with chips) never disappoints and shrimp fajitas and Chili Colorado were both tasty.  Pineapple Mojito (I asked for it light on the pineapple so it would not be too sweet) was spot-on!!!  Service was good but our one server was a bit grumpy Bartender was friendly and funny and the lovely 2 hostess-ladies are so sweet whenever we come.  Love me some Gran Rodeo.

Mid-priced sneakers, shoes and sandals for men, women and kids. Decent selection and decent prices - often buy one get one 1/2 off, etc.  Better quality than payless. Not as good as "real" shoe stores.  I can usually snag decent summer sandals here and my husband who favors a "casual" work shoe got 2 pairs here recently.  The Doylestown store is much cleaner and nicer than the one in South Philly.  We're pleased enough to be repeat shoppers, but true fashionistas may balk.

My review from 2 years ago still stands - service is slow but everything is cooked to order and tastes great.  The "green soup" - a hot soup with kale, broccoli and other greens, garnished with Parmesan, was delightful (special) and once again, I got the crab eggs Benedict.  Fan-flipping-tastic.  Amanda our server was terrific, too.  It's worth the wait (and there usually is one on weekends) so bring friends to chat with or a book or magazine and settle it for a leisurely brunch, lunch or breakfast at house.  We love it.

We were greeted in a very friendly manner and offered free chocolates.  After being seated though, we just had to leave.  This is not an appropriate venue for a business lunch.  Loud, distracting decor and a predominantly chocolate menu made it hard to choose from the over priced snacky-type lunch menu.  Save this place for a date or (if you're rich) bring the kids who are sure to be entertained here.  This place will fail if they don;t offer some sensible lunch choices (Salads were $13.95) or lunch specials.

Brand-new, super clean and well-run (double-lane drive thru) Taco Bell. They ripped down the ancient Burger King and now this Taco Bell is hoppin'.  I don't eat this food but my 16 year old likes it so about once per week (less if I had my way) I let her get it.  Clarice at the cashier window (They have 2 windows - you pay at the first and pick up food at the 2nd) was friendly and fast.

Fluctuates between 3 & 4 stars - our service happened to be wonderful - the food is always the same.  Reliable, good, not mind blowing - but the shrimp and beef filled items are very nice.  Our 11 year old just LOVES it here.  Guacamole is very bland - but made fresh.  Salsa tastes more like watery picante sauce.  Not a holy grail but OK for east-coast suburban.  For better Mexican try Dos Gringos in Media.
One of my close friends and i enjoy the food here - and the service is great - but today there were soooooo many flies.  In the rest rooms, near our table.  Eew.  Please do something about this!
My kid and all her friends LOVE it here. Especially the Burrito California with steak or shrimp (extra charge).

Catering by Miles catered our holiday party again this year. The service is fine and presentation is nice - but the food is just "run of the mill".  We had hot & cold butlered hors d'ouvres - a few were good - lobster pot-pies and pigs in a blanket, some (again) vile-looking pulled pork sliders.  2 table stations had a variety of nice cheese, vegetable crudite and dips, plus steam tables with hot bow-tie pasta in a marinara sauce with bits of vegetables and meatballs in it.  My 7 year old loved it.  Desserts were also butlered.  Frozen cream puffs, tiramisu bites and mini cannoli.
Well stocked Russian and Eastern European market with a vast selection of treats, snacks, candies, dairy, meat and prepared foods.  Really great.
Stick with salads, skip the overpriced drinks and you'll be ok.  The herb ranch dressing is actually fresh tasting.  I never get pizza here.   Service by Ciara was very good.

Fantastic service for our pre-arranged buffet luncheon of 27 people by Jackie, Kaylie and the team.  Mustard Crusted Pork loin, Stuffed mushrooms, penne with chicken, Caesar Salad and rolls.  Parfaits for dessert.  Wonderful place for an old-school (bring your grandparents) luncheon.

Our little one loves it here - the fountain, the water area, the trails, the garden/landscape and Milk & Honey Cafe.  Plus 24 hour security to keep the homeless folks from settling in permanently.  A great place for families with kids.

This Acme has beer & wine (a pretty decent selection, too) available.  They also have a sushi section, next to the deli and hot foods bars.  Crowded on weekends - but a great place to get everything you need in this area of Ridley.

We love sitting in Brett's section and get treated royally whenever we come to RAH (which is now about once a month).  Food is OK - wish they had some healthier (veggie) side items.  Steamed Broccoli or Spinach?  I'm in!  I had an old-school "Fuzzy Navel" and it was delicious and not too cloyingly sweet and got me quite buzzed.  (I know, I know - LIGHTWEIGHT!).  Good times!

My man bought me a gorgeous ring at the Deptford location of Pandora. In general, Pandora has beautiful stuff - but it is costume jewelry.  Rose gold PLATING over a mixed metal base and CZ's - not real diamonds.  In any case, I really like the ring and I love him so I wear it all the time. We'll see how it stands up to handwashing, lotions and creams (yes, I take it off - but still).  A nice place for gifts.

What an AMAZING occurrence that we ended up here after another barbecue place ran out of food!  So yeah, we started out at another spot and they were out of food when we got there. Super bummed and still in the mood for barbecue, we started wandering around Mid City and my trusty Yelp app guided me to this place. We were greeted by the super nice woman working the counter and she explained the whole process.  I decided to get the one-meat plate with "wet" pulled pork, grits and potato salad, I also got a medium mac and cheese, because I can. My boyfriend got the two-meat plate with brisket and pulled chicken with potato salad and fries. The food blew us both away! It was delicious from beginning to end. The pulled pork was perfect and had the perfect amount of sauce without being drenched. I could tell that if I hadn't ordered it wet it still would have been able to stand on it's own. The mac and cheese was incredible, and after the pork, was my favorite part of the meal. The stone ground grits had a different type of flavor (almost smoky) that I enjoyed and the potato salad was served cold and had that nice crunch that I like in potato salad,  We both agreed that the food was excellent, and a good deal to boot, and that we would both make the trip back out to Earhart, just to have more of this delicious food. The owner himself was bringing the food out to folks and he was really friendly and made sure that we were happy with everything. I like when the owners take the time to make sure that everything is okay. The atmosphere is casual and comfortable and the entire process was a breeze. I will definitely return to LA Smokehouse and I'll be adding it to my "BBQ Favorites" list for future reference.

My dad and I were here for lunch and after reading some of the reviews, I was excited to check out this restaurant located where an O'Henry's once stood.  The place was fairly empty at 1 on a Friday and we were lead upstairs. Honestly, there's not much going on up there and it was a bit warm, but we decided to stick it out. Everything on the menu looked great and I decided to get the Catfish Acadian, which is catfish topped with crawfish and sauce with a side of vegetables. My dad got the pork chop.  My dish was great! I have no idea what was in the sauce but it was delicious and it was a perfect pairing with the fish. The vegetables were also really good; they were nicely cooked and fresh. My dad wasn't overly blown away by his pork chop, so if you find yourself here you might want to stick to the seafood.  Bria was our waitress and she was wonderful! She was attentive, kept the fresh iced tea coming and she was extremely personable. She was probably the highlight of the visit.  I'm not sure if I would go back. The food was good, but the atmosphere left something to be desired and I feel like I can get good catfish at plenty of places without going out of my way. I might go back at dinner, when the weather is cooler, and sit on the balcony outside as Harry suggested.

Probably the best thing about Target is that it isn't Wal Mart.  Target is awesome because it has everything from clothes to toys to electronics to makeup.   I usually stop in here (if I remember) to pick up my makeup, because it's at least $2-3 cheaper than other stores.  They have a great grocery section and their selection of household items (microwaves, etc.) is fantastic.  They are always good about having enough registers open for the number of shoppers in the place, and I rarely have to wait in a line.

I've been here a few times for different items. A few months ago I was here looking at appliances for my new kitchen, and while they had a nice selection, they seemed a little overpriced for what I was in the market for (I don't need a refrigerator with a camera in it). Then I was looking for a new TV, and again I found the prices to be a little much. This is a good place to shop if you are in the market for cell phones, music, movies and things of that nature, because they have a wide selection.  Like others, I have utilized the recycling center and have brought old laptop batteries and other computer parts to be recycled, which is very convenient. Also, if you have an electronic thing that needs to be repaired, they will recommend someone, if they can't do it themselves which is pretty neat.

When I'm in the quarter, I always like to stop in at Flanagan's.  It's one of those bars that's off the "beaten path" and a nice escape from the hustle and bustle of Bourbon (if you're a tourist) or even Decatur (if you aren't).  The bar is open 24 hours and the bartenders here are really nice and friendly.  This is more of a bar to go to, if you are a liquor drinker, as their beer on tap is pretty limited, but the atmosphere definitely makes up for the lack of beer (and one beer that they DO have on tap is Harp, and you can never go wrong with that).  It's definitely a great place to check out, if you have something to celebrate, as they have a lot of room.  The room in the back is my favorite, because it's semi-secluded.  $10 min on cards.

Since it's Spring, I decided to get the yard together. I recently had to have some plants pulled out of the yard because they died, so I was in the market for some new tree-like shrubs to take their place. I had a specific type I was looking for and after calling around to a few different places, Bantings had what I needed.  The process here couldn't have been easier. After I called them, I went over there and they showed me exactly what I was looking for. After helping me pick out the better looking plants of the bunch, they loaded them onto their truck, I checked out, they loaded them into my car and I was on my way.  Bantings is HUGE and probably has any type of plant you could ever want. They even have veggies and herbs, in case you want to start you own garden. All of the plants look very healthy and well cared for and I saw multiple people on "water duty" on the day that I was here. Fast service and a wide selection will have me returning to Bantings in the future.

I stopped in here for lunch, even though the reviews were less than stellar. I mainly came in because I had been craving fried seafood and this place had what I needed.  It was later in the day, so the restaurant was pretty empty and I was seated immediately I decided to start with a bowl of the corn and crab bisque. The bisque wasn't anything overly special, but it was pretty good and I enjoyed it. I also got the Des Allemands catfish, which was one of the lunch specials of the day. This was great! A generous serving of tender catfish that was lightly battered and very tasty was presented with diced potatoes and green beans. The fish wasn't over cooked at all and the potatoes and green beans were a good addition to the meal.  Service was good and the food came out quickly, probably because there weren't a lot of people here. I would say this is a good place for lunch, but the atmosphere feels a little "cold" for dinner.

My dining companion and I ended up at Three Muses by complete accident.
