It's dimly lit, sofas are everywhere, they are cozy corners with tables that you can sneak off to and it's decorated like only a super secret hideout can be, with cloth on the walls and interesting art everywhere.  I totally "get" why membership to this place is so expensive ($1,000/year for just the "Bronze" package).  This is one of those places where the New Orleans elite come to relax without fear of being bothered or harrassed.  Also, there is naturally no photography allowed inside.  I didn't get to experience any of the food...maybe one day.  It's just neat that I can say that I have actually been inside this "inner sanctum".

I'm not sure if it was specifically The Fudgery, but when I was a kid me and my parents used to come to The Riverwalk and they would buy me fudge as a treat.  When I saw this fudge shop I was really excited to get a slice of rocky road fudge and relive my childhood. The fudge is just as I remember it: nice and thick with pieces of marshmallow and nuts in it. A slice costs around $10, but I do feel like that's a deal for the amount you get. I like to cut off a piece and enjoy it with my coffee, so it lasts longer. They have a lot of different flavors to choose from and they have ice cream at this location as well.  I don't know if it's a regular thing, but when we bought one slice they offered us a free slice with the purchase of a second slice. We didn't take them up on the offer, but that seems like a deal if you want a few different flavors.

When I saw that yet another restaurant chain was coming to the Westbank, naturally I rolled my eyes.  I mean, between the Friday's, Chili's, and Zea's, Manhattan Blvd is becoming everything I hate about food in the suburbs.  I was skeptical when this place I opened.  I tend to steer clear of any restaurant with "New Orleans" in the name.  If the food is good, the place doesn't usually have to associate itself with arguably one of the best cities for food in the country.  But I digress.  I have never had a sit down meal here.  The two times I went, I got take out, but the food is the same either way, right?  The first time I went here, I got the *thin* sliced catfish.  I love catfish.  If a place has fried catfish on the menu, most of the time I will give it a shot.  They weren't kidding when they said that this catfish is thin.  It's really thin.  It's so thin, it probably more batter than fish.  It came with fries, hush puppies and bread and was about $10.  I think the thin catfish would be perfect for a lunch.  The second time I went, I got the *thick* fried catfish, which is basically what you think of when you think of fried catfish.  It was really good.  It was lightly battered and had good flavor and came with the same sides as the thin fish.  I was pleasantly surprised by this place and I would love to go back here and actually have a sit down dinner, just to see what the experience is like.

Before I discovered the 24 hour breakfast spot  that is IHOP, Coffee & was my "go to" for late night food or doughnut craving.  It's a typical doughnut shop, they serve all types along with coffee, juice, milk...the basics.  The also serve regular breakfast such as bacon, sausage, eggs, grits, toast.  They have a nice "lunch" selection of sandwiches and fries.  My favorite is the club sandwich with sweet potato fries and a chocolate milk.  Service is pretty fast, depending on the time of night, which is good, considering the place is always packed.  This is a JPSO cop hangout, so I never feel weird going in here with friends, even if it's late.  You can order in or get food to go.  If you want a more personal experience than IHOP or Shoney's for breakfast, than this is definitely a good stop.

I love when a business owner greets his customer with a smile and Chef Johnson did just that. I got to try Chef Johnson's at the Terrytown Food Truck fest and I am so glad they rolled over there. My boyfriend and I split the crawfish and grits and it was out of this world good. Not only was there A LOT of crawfish, but the grits were perfect and creamy and the dish was nice and rich. They really knocked it out of the park with this one. Also on the menu is a mac and cheese burger that looks outstanding and a grilled cheese that I am eager to try. Service is fast and friendly and I will be eating here again.

This is the MAC store I frequent the most. The staff is friendly and fairly knowledgeable and the service is always really good.  I was here recently to pick up some lipsticks and a couple of other things. I prefer to come to this store, rather than the MAC counter at Dillard's, because although getting here is a bit of a drive for me, I am usually guaranteed that they will have what I want. Also, this store doesn't sell out of the limited edition sets that they sell. When the Wonder Woman collection came out a while back, the MAC store at Dillard's sold out immediately, but this one had everything still in stock a week later, so I didn't have to rush over to get what I wanted.  My one complaint about this store is that some of the staff isn't as great at matching makeup foundation to your skin tone as others, so be sure to check it out for yourself when they help you, or you might end up buying a foundation that is a little too dark for your complexion.

It was one of those rare "not so humid, not so hot" New Orleans summer days when David and I decided to finally check out City Putt. Yeah, I know that we are totally late to the party, but I like to think of it as being fashionably late.  We were here in the late afternoon, so lucky for us there was no line or wait, We paid, picked our golf balls and headed out. There are two courses you can choose to play or you can play both. I hadn't played mini golf since my "Putt Putt" days as a kid, and I thought I would be rusty, but I caught on pretty quickly. I like how the course is set up with different "water hazards" and there are misters going at every hole to cool you down if you get really hot. The landscaping of the whole space is lovely and I like how each hole has a different theme inspired by a different city in Louisiana.  My only complaint is those greens. I don't know what happened, but SO MANY of them are torn to shreds and falling apart to the point where it interferes with the game. I don't understand why they haven't made some effort to replace them. I understand that normal wear and tear happens over time, but on some of the holes it looks as if someone (kids?) have tried to actively pull up the green. That was the only thing that prevented this from being a 5 star experience for me.  I had a great time and, while the game was really close, I ended up winning by 3 strokes! I want to go back and play the other course. This is a fun way to spend an afternoon, if you are looking to do something for an hour or so.

Add this to the "places I will shop, when I'm rich" list.  I had a Maple St. shopping day so I popped in here to look around. The woman working was extremely friendly and greeted me when I walked in, and I headed over to the racks to see what was what. They carry a lot of cute dresses and tops here, but they definitely aren't cheap. They had a linen t shirt for $100. Seriously. No shade, but this stuff is just a little out of my price range.  They had a few things for sale, so I picked some things out to try on. Nothing really "worked" for me, but I can appreciate the quality of the clothing here and I am sure that it is worth the money and will likely last you years.  If you are looking for higher end clothing, this is the place for you.

This gallery is so great and is filled with cute and quirky art.  I am sure that I had definitely seen the art of Matt Rinard before I set foot into his gallery. His painting, in a "cartoony" style and mainly of animals in funny situations is sure to make anyone happy and bring a smile to your face. Here you can buy originals and prints, and the art makes the perfect gift for someone with a sense of humor. Postcards and small prints are also available.  The gallery also has photography prints and art prints from various other artists. I like that the gallery is wide open with a lot of space and the woman working was sure to ask us if we were looking for anything in particular. Even if you aren't in the market for any art, this gallery is worth checking out.

This place is a hidden gem on Esplanade. Ok, maybe it's not so hidden, but this restaurant has eluded me for years. It's seems as if I have always wanted to try it, but every time I end up somewhere else. I FINALLY got to have dinner here, so it was pretty exciting.  It's a small place, and we had to put our name on a list and wait a bit, but that was no big deal. We were seated after about 10 minutes. Although it was a cool night, we were seated outside on the enclosed patio that was equipped with heaters, so it wasn't too cold. Honestly, if I had it to do over, I would wait to be seated inside but it wasn't terrible sitting on the patio.  Our waitress (Jessica) was extremely attentive and made sure that we were happy with everything. Complimentary chips and salsa were delivered to the table as we looked over the menu. The chips were fresh and delicious and the salsa was very tasty. I only wished that there was more of it! For my entrée I ordered the chicken and portabella mushroom quesadillas. They were SO good and came with sour cream, guacamole, lettuce, tomato and jalapeños on the side. It was really big, so that you could eat the pieces (4) like a sandwich and I even had a piece left over.  I found everything really good and well priced. I can't wait to go back to Santa Fe and see what else they have to offer.

Before you get nervous about my 4 star rating: no, that was not a typo. I am giving Carrabba's a "chain 4". I rank all of these places differently, so try to keep up.  After reading some of the reviews for this place, I was a little apprehensive when I stopped in here for lunch last week. However, when I walked in, everything seemed nice enough, so I just decided to go with it.  As I was looking over the menu, the waitress was nice enough to bring out a basket of bread and olive oil that I munched on while deciding what I was in the mood for. The bread was warm and fluffy and went perfectly with the oil. If you go for lunch, the menu is a bit limited, so keep that in mind if you are looking at the menu, ahead of time, online. I decided to start with an order of fried calamari. I'm a huge calamari fan and I try to order it whenever I see it on the menu. For my entree I got the Mezzaluna, which was basically ravioli stuffed with cheese and topped with a tomato cream sauce.  The calamari was great! I won't say that it's the best that I have ever had, but the batter was nice and thin and the dish was good, and even though I ordered a "small", the portion was huge and plenty enough for two people. The Mezzaluna was amazing. The shells were a perfect size (not too fat) and the cream sauce was delectable. I liked that this was a "lunch" portion of food, so that I was able to finish it without feeling too full. As a treat, I decided to get an order of "mini" cannolis "to go" and I enjoyed them later with a bowl of ice cream- perfect!  My waitress, Kristi, was super sweet and attentive and made sure that I had everything I needed. She was fast, even though she had a lot of other tables to wait on. For lunch, all of the prices were spot on and this would be a perfect place for a mid week meal.  Yes, Carrabba's is a chain, but I enjoyed my experience here. The food was good and the staff was friendly. I would return if I were in the area and in the mood for some quick pasta.

I was brought here and I was blown away by how nice this market actually is.  First of all, usually when I hear the word "Wal Mart", I go into a little bit of a panic, so when my boyfriend told me that this was actually a "nice" one, I didn't know what to think.  In a way, I would almost say it's the Westbank's answer to Whole Foods.  Not really, of course, but they carry a lot of stuff that you probably wouldn't find in you everyday grocery store.    They have a great fresh veggie selection and they have snacks that you wouldn't expect to find like pretzel chips and dried fruit snacks.  Everything is low priced, just as it is at a regular Wal Mart.    One star is lost, because the lines are always ridiculously long.

I stopped in here on a Sunday, during a Saints game, so naturally the place was empty but the game was on! On Sundays, they give their sushi chef the day off, but they were serving poke which was exactly what I was in the mood for.  I got the Rainbow Bowl that came packed with Ahi, Salmon, Yellowtail, Shrimp, Snowcrab cucumbers and avocado topped with Lava and Waikiki sauces, sesame seeds and green onion. The food came out quick and it was fantastic! The fish was fresh and the bowl was huge. I especially liked that it had just enough rice, but not too much, like other poke bowls.   The owner was friendly throughout the meal and the atmosphere is cool and laid back. As a consumer, if I had one suggestion it would be this- the menu is really big; there's breakfast, sandwiches, poke, sushi, salads, a ton of sides and spam. I would pare it down a bit and maybe stick to sushi, poke and spam- I don't think you need to offer a ton of sandwiches, salads and sides. I would say offer maybe one or two signature sandwiches, one or two salads and let the rest be sushi, poke and spam (to stick with the Aloha theme). Those are just my two cents, but I really did enjoy my experience here.

I'll be the first to admit that I am not a huge fan of the "wood fired" pizza trend that seems to be sweeping the city. What I usually get is pizza with crust that is cooked to different consistencies and that just doesn't do it for me.  This place is basically a Chipotle for pizza. You get in line, tell the people making your pizza what you want, they throw it in the oven and it's cooked in about 3 minutes.  I stopped in for lunch and it was a weekend, so the line was pretty long. I got in line and after deciding on the "meat eater", I ordered, added a few extras (veggies) and, as promised, it cooked quickly.  Here's my complaint: the crust (what they call their regular crust, not thin crust) is really thin. It's almost too thin and if you have too much "stuff" on your pizza, it's not going to stay on there. My other complaint is that the crust just lacks flavor to me. It's pre-made, so I don't know if it comes from a package, but it just doesn't have any kick to it. Finally, what makes pizza good (in my opinion) is when it gets a chance to bake and all of the ingredients get a chance to cook into the crust and kind of meld together. That doesn't happen when a pizza is cooked in only 3 minutes.  A lot of people seem to dig this place but it just isn't my style and I will stick to some other pizza places around town.

Such a CUTE store! It's basically a Forever 21 type store that is focused more on jewelry and accessories than clothes, although they did have some cute tops.  I like that everything in the store is arranged by color. There was jewelry that was grouped by: orange, green, pink, clear, etc. They had a really cool sale section that was "buy one get one free" and some of the stuff was super cheap ($8 or less!). I didn't buy anything this time, but I will definitely be back next time I am in the market for some jewelry that has a little "flash" to it.  My favorite section was probably the tiaras! Yes, I will definitely be picking one up when my birthday rolls around. Heck, it might not even take that long! Sometimes a girl just needs to wear a tiara, you know? They also carry a nice selection of evening "clutch" style bags.  It's nice that the Westbank finally has a cute accessories store.

We stopped in here for my dad's birthday. This is now the only Rotolo's on the Westbank and although I had been here a few times before, this was my first time dining in.  I love Rotolo's because their pizza is always consistently good and the service is pretty great at every location. On this visit, we decided to get a medium pizza with sausage, mushrooms and peppers. Because the pizza is made to order it takes a little longer, but it's worth it. The pizza was delicious and we had leftovers to take home.  Our waitress was super nice and after she saw the name on the credit card, she revealed that she has relatives of the same name. Typical New Orleans experience: go to lunch and discover that you are related to the waitress. I will return for another good lunch.

When I saw a new "fancy" restaurant was opening in my hood, I was pretty excited. Super bonus: they have shrimp and grits on the menu! I am giving the place a 3.5 stars just because they have only been open about a month and they are still working out some issues.  We were here for lunch and there was a good crowd, but it wasn't packed. They have a pretty diverse menu with things like fried catfish, shrimp and grits, pasta and even lobster. I decided to be less predictable this time and I get the corn and crab bisque and the fried catfish Lafitte lunch special which came with sausage jambalaya.  The waitress brought out my entree before my corn and crab bisque. I had intended the bisque to be my appetizer, but I guess I should have mentioned that, The catfish was interesting. It was topped with red sauce (which the waitress mentioned ahead of time) and it was fried nicely. The jambalaya was okay, but didn't really dazzle me.  The corn and crab bisque was just okay, as well. It didn't taste the way other bisque I have had in the past tasted. I don't know how to explain it, but I was expecting more. My dad got the shrimp and pasta and wasn't that into it either. He was so not into it that he let me take his leftovers home so I could eat it later. When I tried it, all it was was flavorless pasta and overcooked shrimp- disappointing.  Our waitress was beyond sweet and made sure that we were happy with everything. Like I said, this spot has only been open a month so I expect them to work out the issues and do okay. One suggestion: you offer an entree of shrimp and grits for $19; I would love if you would offer an app size for maybe half that price.

Bourbon Bandstand used to be Bourbon Street Blues Company and it's the same type of place.  Places like this are touristy, but they serve a purpose. On the night I was here there was a band playing and a few people in the place. The band was pretty good, but sadly we came in at the end of their set. After the band there was just a woman onstage who was singing along to the radio and dancing awkwardly. Does she work there? What is happening here? Also, there was an area where you could go get a cold beer out of ice (for a price, of course) and the bartender girl was go go dancing on top of where the beer was in the ice. Like...right on the edge of the cooler. It was awkward and a bit weird. I'm sure they tell her to do that, but I really didn't get the point, especially since there were only a few people in there drinking and hanging out.  This isn't one of the better "tourist trap" type places, so I would skip it on your next Bourbon adventure.

I love the Ruby Slipper locations and I am so excited about their new venture on Metairie Road!  This is a great location and, being a Westbanker, it might actually be easier for me to get to this location and park, rather than weave all around uptown getting to the Magazine St. location. I'm pretty excited that this is here.  We were here for brunch this morning and I love what they've done with the place. Of course, the restaurant is decorated in their signature red accents and has the cozy feeling of their other locations. Monica was our waitress and she immediately took our drink order as soon as we sat down and she told us all about the specials.  Ruby Slipper's Chicken St. Charles is one of my favorites. It's two biscuits topped with fried chicken, poached eggs and their special benedict sauce. It's really one of the best things ever and it works well for breakfast or lunch. I got that with a side of grits and David got the catfish and grits.  As usual, my Chicken St. Charles was phenomenal. The chicken was juicy and fried golden brown and I love how the poached egg oozes onto the chicken and biscuit bringing the whole thing together. The grits were fabulous, as usual, and I just love how creamy they are. David loved his catfish and grits and we both agreed we would order all of this again. One thing that I really want to try is the French toast batons. Sliced up French toast that's all sweet and sugary? I'm in!  Monica was a fabulous waitress and she really did her best to make our experience memorable. This Ruby Slipper is going to be a great addition to the area and I expect it to be pretty packed every weekend. I can't wait to return.

That's it. This is the last time I take Beyoncé's advice on where to eat. I know I've said it before, but I mean it this time. Look, I knew better, but I had the bright idea to get takeout from Red Lobster. Why, when there are so many better, locally owned seafood places in this town? Well, I don't have a good answer. I thought this would be a good idea; it wasn't.  I got takeout from here last week and looking over the menu, it all actually sounded good. I got the crab linguini alfredo, since I thought it would be kind of hard to mess that up. It came with a side salad that was actually really good and a pleasant surprise. The pasta on the other hand...no. When I get takeout, I usually eat half and happily save the rest for later. Y'ALL. I took a few bites, got up and threw the rest in the trash. I never throw food away, but I had to make an exception this time. The overall taste of the pasta was non existent, which was shocking considering it was doused in cream sauce. The crab tasted distinctly fishy to the point that I was afraid that if I kept eating it I would get sick. I wasn't expecting gourmet pasta, but I was expecting something better than what I got. I read Emily M's review the night before I made this decision and I still went through with it. Next time I am just going to follow my instincts.  I'm giving two stars because I enjoyed the salad and service was friendly.

I have always encountered this food truck on my travels, but never when I was hungry enough for it.  When I saw that Frencheeze was going to be making an appearance at Gretna Food Truck Fest, I put it on the top of my list of trucks that I had to try. Yes, I had an actual list. I got there about an hour after the fest started and Frencheeze had the longest line ever!! Seriously. They even had to park in a special spot in order to accommodate their line. I re-worked my plan and decided to wait until the end of the fest to try it. Luckily, this plan of action worked.  After waiting in a (shorter) line, I ordered the Molly which is bacon, tomato, goat cheese, and avocado on a toasted croissant. I waited about 5 minutes and my order was ready. Okay, so this thing is no joke. What I got was a sandwich that was so packed with bacon that it was actually falling out of the sandwich. After the first bite, I was hooked. There was something about the combination of crispy bacon, cold tomato and the cheese that really worked for me. It was outstanding, and on par with a sandwich you would get at an actual restaurant.  The folks at Frencheeze impressed me: they were out at Gretna Food Truck Fest for 4 hours and they had a solid line the entire time- even after the lines at other trucks dwindled. They didn't run out of food, they were friendly and they were fast at getting the orders out. Combine that with a delicious sandwich (of which I had leftovers to enjoy later) and you get an experience that is worth way more than the $9 paid.  I will absolutely be eating out of this truck again and I will be seeking them out the next time I am in the mood for some deliciousness.

I really like the space. It's in a nice part of the city and when there is nothing going on here, it makes for a great place to relax and take in the world around you.  I have attended a few events here and event organizers really need to analyze the space/crowd size before they consider having another big event here. During Wednesday at the Square, it's perfect. The crowd isn't too big and there is space to move around. During other events or festivals it gets SUPER packed to the point where you are hot and uncomfortable and can't move around without bumping into people. On top of that, there is zero organization, so the area quickly becomes a mad house.  Check out this spot if it's a quiet afternoon with nothing going on. Avoid it if there is a festival that half the city shows interest in attending.

We stopped in for lunch on a work day and the place was packed. We had the choice of waiting 30 to 45 minutes for a table to open up or just eat at the bar. We ate at the bar.  This restaurant is lovely with a really cool vibe. There was a lot of hustle and bustle happening and it felt like the place was really special. We started with a order of stuffed mushrooms and for my entree I got the grilled chicken with onion rings and a side of red beans.  The stuffed mushrooms were beyond great! I could have eaten way more than just one and a half. My grilled chicken was cooked perfectly, juicy and spiced well. The red beans and rice tasted like home made and had a little bit of meat in them that made them just perfect. The onion rings were just okay. I'm pretty picky when it comes to onion rings and, with these, the batter fell off of them before I had a chance to eat them. They were still pretty good, but I've had better.  The staff was super friendly and checked on us regularly to make sure that we were happy and had everything we needed. If I got back, I'm going to leave some "wait time", so that I can sit at a table instead of the bar.

#prayformoe  I am so disappointed, y'all! I struggled with this rating and I so badly wanted to give this place 3 stars, but I just couldn't do it.  When I heard we were getting a Moe's on the Westbank, I was excited. I knew that it was a Felipe's/Chipotle type of place where you could go in and order tacos and burritos and get them made fresh to order, like a Mexican subway.  We went in on a Friday night and the place was dead. Maybe it was the holiday- nope, scratch that. The dude working there said that the place is always dead: not a good sign. I stepped up and ordered a taco salad with pork and all the fixin's. First of all, the guy making the salad started with filling the salad shell with a huge fist full of lettuce. This salad was 90% lettuce. Then all of the other stuff was placed on top. There was barely any pork on this thing. I was super disappointed.  On top of that, I got queso on the side and that was an extra three bucks. Granted, they give you a huge tub of it, but I'd be happy with a little solo cup that costs a dollar.  The chips and salsa is free and that's pretty much the only good thing I can say about my experience here.  I most likely won't be back.

This is a cute little book shop that I've visited a few times, now. I really have no idea how they stay in business because I have never seen another shopper in the place, but considering they have been around since 1978, they must do well.  They have a nice selection of different books. A lot of John Grisham and Nora Roberts, if that's your thing. The books are broken up into different categories and they are clearly labeled. Many of the books show serious wear, but that's to be expected at a used book store. You definitely get some good deals here.  They will give you store credit, if you bring in books that they can use, so that would be good for anyone who is an avid reader.

The fly is a great little spot here in New Orleans.  It's perfect for relaxing when the weather starts to warm up in the Spring. A lot of people have crawfish boils and picnics here or they just go and hang out with friends. You have a nice view of the river and you feel as if you are in another world when you are relaxing here.

Mr. B's is one of those legendary New Orleans restaurants that I hadn't ever been to, so when it was time for "Marielle eats her way through another birthday, 2018", this was my top pick. Also, I'm trying to eat at every Brennan restaurant in New Orleans, so I was happy to add this one to my list.  I made my reservations on Open Table about a month in advance and we were seated as soon as we arrived, even though there was a nice line of people waiting for tables. Trust me: it ALWAYS pays to make reservations, even if you just make them the day you're planning to eat out.  The waitress quickly came and took our drink order and we looked over the menu. We skipped appetizers and went straight to entrees because I wanted dessert (ha). I got the bacon wrapped shrimp and grits, which the menu describes as sauté of pecanwood smoked bacon wrapped jumbo Gulf shrimp served with creamy stone ground yellow grits and red eye gravy. It was amazing! The bacon was nice and crispy and wrapped around tail-on shrimp and the gravy and the grits was a delicious combination. It was full of flavor and even had a bit of a sweetness to it which I thought was delectable.  For dessert, David and I got a bread pudding which came with a candle in it for my birthday, which I always think is a nice touch. The bread pudding was delicious and was topped with a tasty sauce which put it over the top.  The Mr. B's staff did everything they could to make my birthday perfect and they completely succeeded. We had a lovely dinner and a memorable night for sure.

We came and ate here on a cold, rainy night. We had reservations, so we were seated immediately, and although I wasn't crazy about where we were seated (against the wall), the place was packed, so I wasn't going to be "that person" and complain.  I had a glass of the cabernet, which was lovely and for my entree I got the drum which was served with squash, beurre blanc and caviar. The dish was amazing! The entire thing was flavorful, unique and beyond delicious. My boyfriend got the pepper pot and I was able to try a bite, and that was good as well. For dessert, we got the chocolate cake with lemon ice cream, which was quite tasty without being heavy.  As good as the food was, I did have a few complaints- the waitress seemed to disappear for long periods of time. The place was packed on the night we were here, and I think that she was a bit overwhelmed with the crowd. She was very nice, but after she dropped off the food she vanished until we were ready for the check. Also, it was really loud here. If I had known that my date and I would have to be shouting at each other to have a conversation, I probably would have picked a different place for dinner.  If I go back, it might be for lunch.

I'm always trying to eat well, but I seem to sometimes gravitate toward heavier food, especially during the holidays. I was eager to stop in and try some homemade vegan cuisine for myself at Sweet Soulfood. I like that the food is laid out cafeteria-style, giving you the opportunity to look over the offerings and find something that appeals to you. At the hot bar, you can get up to four items, so I decided to go all out and really treat myself. I got the mac and cheese, chicken fried cauliflower, okra gumbo, and greens.  I have to mention the portions here are extremely generous -- my four items were $15, and this was easily enough for two meals or even to share. I dug into the chicken fried cauliflower first, mainly because I was so intrigued and I had never had anything like it in my life. WOW. Any hesitation I had about being able to enjoy fried cauliflower went right out the window! This was fantastic -- big pieces of cauliflower lightly battered and fried. There's no mistaking that it isn't chicken, but if you're craving that yummy fried crunch, this is a must. Next up was the mac and cheese. I'm not sure how they get it so creamy, since real cheese isn't involved, but I loved it. It had that good "chew" that you expect from mac and cheese and it was so good that I actually forgot that it was vegan.  The okra gumbo was excellent and even had some non-meat sausage in it, which was quite tasty and reminded me of a leaner meat sausage. The roux was on the milder side, but it was packed with flavor and, after a few bites, I didn't miss the meat. I really like okra, but if it isn't your thing, you might want to skip this, as this dish is packed with okra as its main bulk.  Finally, I dug into the greens, which were seasoned well and flavorful. At first, I was afraid that I was going to miss having bacon and ham in the greens to add that extra fat, but Sweet Soulfood's version was so good that I didn't even think about the fact that it was meat-free.  In a city that is known for delicious, maybe not-so-healthy food, Sweet Soulfood absolutely fits in and stands out. As a gal who does enjoy her meat, I finished my lunch feeling completely satisfied and excited that I had leftovers to enjoy later.  Even if you don't plan on going full veggie anytime soon, Sweet Soulfood is a great place to enjoy a wholesome lunch.

St. Louis Cemetery Number 1 is one of the most famous cemeteries in New Orleans and maybe even the country. A lot of famous people are buried here like Marie Laveau and a lot of famous people want to be buried here like Nicolas Cage (or so they say). Unless you have a pass (which I do) it costs money to get into the cemetery and you have to be with a tour group. On the day we were here the weather was nice and the tour groups were out in full force. Fortunately, the tour guides are very respectful of folks who just want to visit their loved ones and one tour guide informed us that we were welcome to join his tour, if we desired. My dad mentioned that the last time he was here the cemetery was a ghost town (heh), so seeing all the tour groups was definitely different. It's all an effort to keep vandals at bay, so I can appreciate that.  My dad and I visited because he realized it had been 20 years since he had visited the tomb where our family is buried. My grandfather, great grandparents and many many others are in a tomb here. St. Louis #1 certainly isn't the neatest or most visually pleasing cemetery. Don't get me wrong, many of the tombs are very nice, but there are also piles of bricks that used to be tombs, understandable considering this is the oldest cemetery in New Orleans and the space has survived hurricanes, floods and Lord knows what else.   Walking though the cemetery, you get a nice sense of the history here. Unfortunately, many of the graves have fallen victim to vandals who have knocked off pieces for souvenirs. If there's such a thing as bad juju, that's a good way to get it.  St. Louis #1 is worth seeing at least once for locals and tourists alike.

I have a long history with Restaurant des Familles. I have been coming here with my family since I was a child. I have spent many Mother's Days here and I celebrated my high school graduation here. This review is long over due.  It had been years since I had eaten here, but walking in it felt like I had never left. The gorgeous dining room, with the view of the swamp, was just as I had remembered it. We were here on a lovely clear day, so we were able to look out onto nature and I even spotted a "baby" alligator.  We were here for lunch and there was no crowd or wait and we were immediately seated and given menus. For my entree, I decided on the Catfish Almandine and I swapped the veggie side for grits, because...grits. The meal also came with a small garden salad. The salad was delicious and really fresh and the Catfish Almandine was tasty. I chose to get it grilled and it was just perfect and topped with toasted almonds. The grits were jalapeño-cheddar grits and were SO good! They definitely hit the spot and were creamy just the way I like them.  I will probably always love this place. It's pretty much in the middle of nowhere and there is just something special here.

I was lucky enough to go on a private tour on a Saturday afternoon with a few friends. Co-owner Andrew was our guide and he did a fantastic job telling us all about the rum making process and explained everything in an easy-to-understand manner. Roulaison is a small and new rum distilling company and, I'll be honest, I know nothing about liquor production. Everything here is handcrafted and it's all local. All of this was pretty new to me, but I found the tour very interesting and Andrew was extremely nice and was happy to answer questions.  After the tour came the tasting and I'm not a liquor drinker, so this got real interesting. I can usually handle liquor if it's mixed with something, so I was thankful for the teeniest little thimble full of samples that we had to try. Some of the rum burned, but that's probably because I "can't hang". By the third taste I had to reach for water- I'm such a lightweight. I did, however, really enjoy the rum liqueur that was offered, mainly because it had some sweetness to it. You can actually have them mix you up a cocktail, if that's your thing.  I highly recommend the tour, especially if you like learning about new things and how things are made.

Every time I go to this place, I feel like I'm going to get stabbed (and I'm pretty adventurous).  I went here a lot before Katrina, so last summer when a friend's band was playing here, I jumped at the chance to check it out.  The place is smoky and gross.  A complete "guy" place, complete with pool tables.  Horrible for bands now.  The sound system just sucks.  I saw bands here all the time, Pre-K, now something is just off.    There was only one bartender for the whole place full of people, so you had to wait forever to get service.    I know people will say that places like this are what make NOLA unique.  Uh uh.  Places like "Lafitte's" make NOLA unique.  This is just a scummy hole in the wall.  Trust me, I am NOT a prissy snob who can't have a good time in a dive.  This place is just BEYOND.  I just thank goodness I didn't have to go to the bathroom while I was here, or I might not have made it out with my sanity.  ;)

Tucked away in a little strip mall on Gretna Blvd is this little treasure.  I rarely have to get things altered, but recently I had to bring in two tops and a pair of jeans that were way too big on me.  The shop is very small and has two or three people working at a time.  The woman who took care of me was extremely knowledgeable and knew exactly what I needed done, without me having to explain.  As soon as I put the tops and the jeans on, she had them pinned and ready to go.  I got the clothes back today and the results were just as expected and exactly what I had hoped for.  My tops were altered perfectly, and the jeans that were way too big on me, are now perfectly tailored to fit me.    The alterations just took a week. The tops were about $4.50 each and the jeans were $20, because they had to be totally redone to fit.  I will definitely be returning to the Alteration Center for any future needs.

Do I live here?  No, but I wish!  Jess pretty much summed it up with her review, but I'll add to it.  I've been here a few times to visit friends of friends and the place is really cool.  They have nice condos (a one bedroom runs about $1500/month) as well as a common area.  The common area has tons of seats and sofas and a HUGE projection screen where you can watch Saints games, or pretty much anything.  It's a real community there.  The residents are mainly made up of young business professionals and everyone seems to know each other and hang out.  It reminds me of Melrose Place.  There is a picnic/deck/pool area where you can grill with friends and then catch up on your tan after a long week.  The best part is, 930 Poydras is in one of the best spots in the city, especially if you are a Saints fan.  It's located right across the street from Walk Ons and Happy's, so you can go watch the game there if you need a change of scenery.  It's also right next door to fancy pants restaurant Ste. Marie and on the other side there is a Jamba Juice (I had no idea New Orleans had one, either).  Rouses is pretty close for groceries.  930 Poydras is one of the places I'll probably live when I'm super rich.  ;)

I almost can't even believe that I haven't been to this legendary New Orleans lunch place before now.  My dad and I decided to have lunch here on Christmas Eve to remember my mother on her birthday. We got here at a little after 11 in the morning and the place was packed. I was pretty surprised that so many people had the same idea for lunch, especially on Christmas Eve, but I was happy that we were seated quickly despite the crowd.   They have their main menu and then they have the specials board, so be sure to take a look at that when you go. I decided to start with an order of onion rings because I had read some raves about them and I got an order of the shrimp and cheese grits which also happen to come with pieces of bacon sprinkled in them.  The onion rings were piled high with a super generous serving and the batter was thick and the onion was cut thick as well. These were great for dipping and they came with a sauce on the side. I coated them with some hot sauce, just for good measure-you can't go wrong with that. The shrimp and grits was extraordinary! The dish was very rich with tail-off shrimp that were cooked to perfection. The shrimp were plentiful and the cheese and bacon blended nicely with the grits. All of the flavors worked well together and I could tell that this must be a popular dish because it was so well executed.  The atmosphere of the place is super casual with TVs on the wall and a bar area where you can sit, if you want to stop in for lunch by yourself. The staff was great and attentive and the food came quickly. I enjoyed everything and I will return.

This was a really tough call, but I think I'm going to go with three stars on this one.  All this talk about the best fried chicken in New Orleans got my inner fat kid hungry, and since one of the candidates is located right in Algiers, I decided to head over and try it for myself. Now, when you go to Chubbie's don't expect bells and whistles. It's just a small store with a few tables where you walk up to order and wait a few minutes for your food to be ready. Yes, it's an old Popeyes that has been converted into another chicken place.  I went in for lunch and placed an order for a two piece white with potato salad, a drink and a biscuit. There wasn't much of a crowd, so there wasn't much of a wait. When my food came out, I was delighted at how crispy the chicken looked. There was seriously a thick layer of crust on the breast, the likes of which I rarely see. As I dug into the chicken, I noticed that it was perfectly cooked to tender perfection. The meat fell off of the bone and there was plenty of it.  The skin was light and crispy and practically melted in my mouth.  My only real complaint with the chicken was that there was no spice added to it. I like my fried chicken to have a bit of a kick (I am a Southern girl, after all) and this chicken had no kick at all. It was without a kick.  Also, the potato salad tasted store bought. I apologize right now if it wasn't. Maybe I am super picky when it comes to potato salad, because I've had the homemade stuff. While it was good, I think I will opt for the mashed potatoes next time.    All in all, for a little over $6, my meal was good and I enjoyed it, I left Chubbie's satisfied and promising myself that I would eat healthy for the rest of the week. I wouldn't hesitate to return to Chubbie's with a bottle of hot sauce in tow.  If chicken isn't your thing, Chubbie's has daily hot plate specials as well as poboys, burgers, salads and other sandwiches. They even have a drive thru!

I am loving One Stone!  I'm so excited that my little neck of the woods is starting to get non-chain coffee shops! One Stone is a welcome addition to the Old Algiers landscape. I stopped in here after some friend raved about it and after following One Stone for a while on the 'gram, I was happy to see the place for myself.   The atmosphere is downright cozy with nice tables and chairs and two big sofas for lounging. They offer a variety of coffees and teas as well as well-priced bites. Today I had the cold brew which was delightful and rich. I was also happy that they offer a variety of milk options. The owners are super friendly and are more than open for a chat.   I can tell that a lot of thought was put into the design of the cafè and it didn't go unnoticed. I loved the small details of the sugar skull salt shaker and the nice wooden chairs and stools. From beginning to end One Stone is all about personal touches and making the customer feel at home.   I'm delighted that a spot like this is on the Westbank and I can't wait to make this a regular stop and try some of the food!

When I heard that a new Indian restaurant called Turmeric was opening in Gretna, I was eager to try it.   The lunch buffet is $12.99 and changes daily and is served from 11:30 a.m. to 2 p.m. I was impressed at how vast the selection is and I took the opportunity to sample a few things.   Yuca Rolls- These were excellent. I don't think I have ever had yuca before. For those not in the know, it's a delicious vegetable that seems to be popular everywhere, except in the West. Pieces of yuca were lightly battered and fried. The rolls were soft and full of flavor, making a great start to my lunch.  Dal Makhani- This was so good I went back for seconds! It almost reminded me a bit of a jambalaya/gumbo hybrid, in a way. If you're new to Indian cuisine, like me, this would be a good "starter" dish, because it's packed with flavor and the spices aremild. There was a wonderful balance between the lentils and the sauce itself, which was rich without being heavy.  Mushroom Matar- I treated myself to a bowl of this delicious concoction, another dish that had a wonderful balance of flavors. The spices added taste to the food without completely overwhelming me.  Bhindi Masala- I am a huge fan of okra, and this dish was one of my favorites of the day! The okra is stir-fried, so it loses the "slickness" that I think puts a lot of people off of okra. The combination of the okra with onions and tomatoes was excellent and I would actually encourage people who think that they don't like okra to give the Bhindi Masala a try. It's hard to not like something that's stir-fried.  Chicken Tikka Masala- This is what I think of first when I think of Indian food. This is pieces of juicy chicken cooked in a spiced curry sauce. It was the only dish that had a bit of spice to it, but the seasoning was perfect and the tastes balanced well. One good thing about this being served buffet-style is that you can get as little or as much sauce as you want, and that's where the majority of the spice is.  I like that Turmeric has a wide variety of vegetarian options; I didn't even realize most of my lunch was plant-based until after I ate all of it! Turmeric is a wonderful addition to the New Orleans food-scape and the burgeoning Westbank Asian-food scene.  *Portions of this review was originally written, by me, for Very Local New Orleans. Read the full story here: https://nola.verylocal.com/turmeric-restaurant-brings-indian-food-to-the-west-bank/110119/

An upscale hotel bar located in the heart of the CBD.  Great atmosphere and crowd.  A great place to stop in after work for a drink.  I dated a guy who worked in this area a while ago, and we would get together to enjoy a happy hour together after work on Fridays.  The have nice sofas by the windows, where you can sit with a group.  The bar is completely smoke free and the crowd is a little older, so it's a good place to go if you want to get away from the youngsters and their hangouts.

I simply could not wait to get on Yelp and rave about my experience at Carrollton Market. The food and service were top notch and it was one of the best dining experiences I have ever had.  We made reservations so we were seated immediately upon arriving. I had been  in this space previously when "One" was here and I have to say I like the decor of CM much better. It's brighter and feels new and fresh.  The menu here is pretty simple, which I can definitely appreciate. We started with the Oysters Goodenough which is 4 grilled oysters topped with a cream sauce and bacon. If you are an oyster lover you MUST get this dish. It was incredible and I couldn't get enough. I almost wanted to order another plate for myself and just call that my meal. Check out my close up picture of the oysters and get ready for your mouth to start watering.  For my entree I got the potato crusted drum, which was served on a bed of brussels sprouts and other vegetables. The fish was perfect. The potato crust added a nice flavor and the fish itself was flaky and delicious. I've been on quite the seafood kick lately, as I've been eating out a lot, and this is perhaps some of the best I have had.  We skipped desert, but we did decide to get coffee. Even though our dinner was late (we arrived 30 minutes before closing- a usual "no no" in my book), we didn't feel rushed at all and the waiter was kind enough to let us take our time and chat. At one point I joked that we could take our coffee to go but he said he was happy to have some company as he cleaned up for the night. What a sweetie!  This place is fantastic and I will definitely return. I am so excited to bring friends here in the future.

Wow. This space has certainly come a long way since it was Happy's and I really have to commend the owners on the change. It honestly looks nothing like it used to and there's even a fancy upstairs area now!  David and I were here for his cousin's birthday celebration and we were seated upstairs. We didn't have a full dinner, but we did have some really good fries and we had a few cocktails. First, since it's a wine bar, I started with a really good malbec that was reasonably priced. I like that they give you the option of a half pour or whole pour, I guess in case you want to just do some tastings. Even though they mainly specialize in wine, they do have a full bar and a pretty decent beer selection. I had the Holy Roller IPA which was a fairly priced $7, especially considering the atmosphere of the place.   We hung out at a while and they didn't rush us at all as we basically just sipped drinks and enjoyed conversation. Every now and then I did feel that they forgot about us (I ordered coffee that never came), but all in all it was a good experience and it good place to start your evening.

Gogo booth is so fun and it's a really cool twist on the photo booth idea.  I got to experience this at a bridal show I went to recently. It's a big mirror, so you get to see yourself as it takes your picture, then you get to write messages on it with your finger that print on the photos and the photos also upload to their website, which is really cool. I like that it's similar to other booths in that they have a lot of props for your to play with and I enjoyed writing messages on the mirror and interacting with it. It also makes cool sounds as you are posing for the pictures. Pictures are high quality and the experience is fun!

There's nothing that makes a Wal Mart experience better than not having to talk to Wal Mart employees. It's not that I have an issue with anyone who works here; the entire process is just faster if I don't have to interact with people. It's the future; get used to it.   So, I needed a few things and Wal Mart makes it super convenient where you can just order off of the website and go pick up your order at the store. So, I ordered my item and the next day I got an email telling me my order was ready to be picked up. Great! All I had to do was walk over to their magic "order pick up" kiosk, scan my phone and my item was delivered to me bagged and ready to go. Then, I needed another item from the store, so I hunted it down and paid for it at self-checkout within minutes. I didn't speak with one employee the entire time I was here. Seriously- why don't more people do the self-checkout?  I found everything I needed quickly and ordering and picking up my item was a breeze, so I'll be back just for that. Note: I find that this Wal Mart processes orders faster than the Manhattan location. Not sure why, but that's been my experience.

Since the Gretna Breaux Mart has decided to close up shop, this is now going to be my regular grocery stop.  I love this Rouses. It's a better "fresher" than the Belle Chasse Hwy. location, they have great stock of items, and the place is clean and organized. I was here most recently for one of the cheap $7 king cakes they have and I was not left disappointed. They have a whole variety from plain to filled and they're a good size for the price. Look, not every king cake can be a $25 king cake, especially when the season lasts two months. Rouses king cake will satisfy any king cake craving you might have.  I also like that Rouses has a large deli selection, a really nice beer selection and they even have a place where you can "build your own" poke bowl. That's convenient, since poke is the new super-cool thing and there are no places dedicated to the stuff anywhere on the Westbank.  The lines here always move quickly and the staff is great.

I just loved this cozy little bar tucked away in the French Quarter.  David and I stopped in here on our anniversary night and the first thing I noticed was their menu. Sure, it's a bar, but they have some seriously good sounding food and I ALMOST wished that I hadn't eaten before I got here.  The feel of the bar is meant to be like an old library with booze, and I'm all about that. The place is pretty dimly lit, which adds to a nice cozy vibe and I loved that they had a pretty good beer selection. They have a few comfy chairs to sit in, but we just hung out at the bar and took it all in. The patrons seem to be neighborhood regulars and we enjoyed just sipping our drinks and people watching.  The bartender was amazingly nice and welcoming and made our evening just perfect.

My session with Marianne was very personal to me. My grandmother passed away last year and among other things, she left me her collection of vintage hats. I'm not a big hat wearer, but I knew that I didn't want them to just sit in a drawer untouched. I decided that I wanted to pick a couple of my favorites and do a glamorous photo shoot, not only to honor my grandmother, but to have nice pictures of me in the hats.  I contacted Marianne with my idea and she immediately went to work helping me plan it. She helped me pick out a location and from there I went ahead with planning which hats I would bring along with different outfits.  On the day of the shoot I was super excited. I had picked two of my favorites along with matching dresses. We did the shoot at Audubon Park and Marianne and her husband Steve were great in not only making me feel at ease, but at directing the shoot, telling me how to pose, and choosing the perfect spots for the pictures.  When I got the pictures back, I was so excited! They were exactly what I had hoped for and I even gave my dad a print of one, since it was his mother's hats. He loved it. Marianne and Steve made the entire experience easy and wonderful and I would love to work with the both of them again.

This review is written from the standpoint of someone selling to Magpie.  Right now I am going through the process of sorting through my grandmother's things and deciding what I want to keep and what I want to sell.  When I found myself with a surplus of vintage jewelry, a quick search of "New Orleans vintage jewelry buyer" introduced me to Magpie. The owner, Sarah, was nice enough to drive to my grandmother's house on the Westbank and look through her jewelry to find pieces that she would like to buy and resell. She was extremely nice and thorough. She took her time looking through TONS of jewelry, and was able to give me a fair price for a few select pieces. Sarah also mentioned that she buys certain vintage clothes and handbags.  If you are looking to sell estate jewelry, Magpie should be your first call. Sarah was personable and nice and I would happily do business with her again.

This shop is really neat and has a little bit of everything: jewelry, furniture, costumes, prints, art, and more.  We ended up here while we were just strolling around the Quarter and I love everything here! This is the type of place I would shop if money wasn't an object and I had an old mansion to decorate. I think my favorite of the offerings was the old furniture- some of it needed some work, but some of it was in really good shape. They also have a nice selection of old and unique vintage jewelry.  This is a good place to shop if you are looking for a gift, for that special someone, that's a little bit "different". Whatever you end up getting here is sure to make an impression.

Wow. Finally a decent dress shop on the Westbank.  Not only does The Pink Veil have wedding dresses at reasonable prices, but they have all sorts of dresses for any occasion. They have dresses that would be perfect for prom and dances and dresses that would be best for a night out on the town. The staff was super friendly and attentive and although I was just looking, they were sure to ask if I needed help with anything.

WHOA! Okay, so this place is a dream spot who anyone who enjoys a nip and also enjoys saving a few bucks. It's basically CostCo for liquor of all types.  I had heard the hype about this place, so I took a field trip to Metairie to see what it was all about. WOW. Total Wine has it all. I know that it's a chain, but that doesn't seem to put people off. The booze is cheap and plentiful and they are bound to have whatever you're looking for.  I'm a beer person and their craft beer selection can't be beat. They have a ton of local brews as well as national brands and they are all well priced.  Every section is packed with everything you can imagine and they even have snacks like beer nuts and cheese poofs. The staff is super helpful and they have a whole section for "sampling", if that's your thing.  If you need alcohol for a party or just a Saturday night, this should be your first (and likely only) stop.

So, this isn't so much a review of the hotel itself, as it is a review of the bar area. I'm not sure if there's a separate listing.  I stopped in here for "Art for the Arts' which is a weekly showing of the work of local artists. This week, my friend was having a showing here so I decided to check it out. The bar area is nice and spacious has a nice retro/mod kind of feel. There is a happy hour from noon-7 and there are drink specials during "Art for the Arts", so it won't be hard to get something you like for a good price.  They also have food specials. We decided to munch on an order of mussels in a cream sauce and shrimp and crawfish beignets. The mussels were small, but good. The beignets were really doughy, but my boyfriend had the bright idea to soak them in the mussels' cream sauce. They soaked up all of the sauce and that made them DELICIOUS. We were seriously tempted to suggest that they serve the beignets in that sauce because it improved the dish immensely.  This is a great spot for a happy hour when you are looking to spend some time in a nice place.

I always love when I find myself in the Marigny/Bywater area because there are so many good food places that I have never tried. Enter Horn's. I had heard about how good this place is, thanks to a food group I'm in, but they're only open until 2 so I would have to conveniently have to make sure I was in the area for lunch.  The cafe is small but mighty, with plenty of seating packed into a small space without feeling crowded. I ordered a big cup of coffee (and it was HUGE). I had already peeked at the menu online and decided that the grits and etouffee had my name all over it. I got a side of bacon, just for good measure, and I counted it towards my protein for the day. The whole thing came with a homemade biscuit on the side. Yes, please.  This dish was amazing. Creamy grits and down home crawfish etouffee is the perfect combination, especially when the richness of the etouffee starts mixing in with the grits. The bacon was cooked to crispy perfection and I indulged in some of my biscuit and saved the rest for later, because it was so good.  Everything on the menu sounded so delicious and I am definitely going to have to go back and sample some more goodies sometime soon. My one issue with the place is that it was pretty warm because it was the middle of a summer day and the place was packed. They had the ac on, but it's an old building and it was struggling to keep up. It wasn't a big issue, but if I had been there for a long time, it would have gotten to me. Service was great and the staff was friendly.

We have another case of a mysterious disappearing review on our hands.  I have been coming to Pho Cam Ly for years and it is always consistent and good. I get the pho with brisket and it's perfect. The broth isn't overwhelming and everything is balanced nicely.

Yum! I love places like this: home cooked food served by nice people.  I stopped in here on my birthday morning to grab some yummy breakfast and since I had never been here (but had always wanted to try it) I considered it an adventure.  We were seated at one of the booths on the side and the nephew of the owner was our waiter. You should know that this is a full on family place and Slim Goodies takes pride in the fact that they were one of the first places open and serving food after Katrina.  I decided to get a pretty basic breakfast of eggs over easy, toast, bacon and grits. This seems to be my "go to" and I guess it's because when I try a new breakfast place, I like to order something that I know can't go too off the rails. Everything was cooked to perfection. I probably would have liked it if the toast wasn't as "toasty", but I'll just remember to mention that next time.  Our waiter was super friendly and was full of personality, especially considering it was an early and rainy morning. He had his iPod playing a nice mix of tunes and made the entire experience really enjoyable.  Next time I eat here I will definitely be a little more adventurous. CASH ONLY.

I stopped in for lunch, and the ordering process couldn't have been easier. You order your food at the window, pay and make your way to the side patio and await your meal. I ordered the Duo with Chips ($8), which comes with a sizable serving of salsa roja and queso.  The salsa had a nice zing to it. It was flavorful without relying too heavily on the spices -- it had nice body and I loved how nicely it balanced with the queso. Both the salsa roja and the queso are made with roasted tomatoes, onions, peppers and spices.  I knew that I had to try the Carne Asada Torta ($11) for myself. This was tender carne asada served on bolillo bread with black beans, avocado, mayo, lettuce, tomato, cilantro, onion and cotija cheese.  It was so interesting to have all of the flavors that I enjoy in really good Mexican food in a sandwich. I feel like so many of us reach for a burrito, when we want all of those flavors, but this torta was such a different experience. It more than lived up to the hype.  I wrote about this restaurant for Uptown Messenger. Read the full article here: https://uptownmessenger.com/2021/01/el-cucuy-serves-up-mexican-street-food-in-the-irish-channel/

This is a really cool shop that seems to sell a lot of local wines and other liquors. They have a wide selection of all types of wines as well as some flavored rums. There's a bar in the back, if you are in the mood to do some sampling. The only two issues I have with the place are: the bottles aren't marked with prices and you have to ask how much they are. This just seems inconvenient if you just feel like browsing. Also, it is very loud in here. There was a group sampling when we were here and they were talking at a fairly normal level, but it sounded like they were shouting. That might be a weird complaint, but I found it distracting.  This place is worth checking out if you are in the mall, but not worth going out of your way.

What a fantastic work space!  I had no idea this spot even existed until I was invited to check it out on one of their "Freelance Fridays". On Freelance Fridays you can stop in, without a membership, and see what the space has to offer.   First of all, the whole area is gorgeous. There are wide open spaces and tables for meetings, sofas for lounging and working and individual "pods" where you can set up your work station and work in peace. There's a kitchen area filled with coffee, water, other drinks, snacks and even beer. If you use a dish, please wash it and replace it when you're finished- keeping this place neat is a team effort.  I don't really have any need to become a full time member, but I can definitely see myself stopping in on another "Freelance Friday" so that I can work in a different kind of space. The Shop is what I imagine any modern work space to be and I really liked it and I would absolutely recommend it to anyone who needs a nice, quiet place to work.

David and I always like to do a little something special for "big" events, so when our two year anniversary came around, we knew we wanted to eat at one of New Orleans' classic restaurants. We chose Ralph's on the Park.  We made our reservations for 7:30 on a Saturday, but we got there at 7 and we were seated immediately. I immediately loved the "old New Orleans" feel of the place and I can always tell that a restaurant is going to be good when I see people of all ages dining there.  We decided to start with a simple appetizer of cheese toast. There wasn't much to this, but we both enjoyed it and, in my opinion, you can't go wrong with cheese on bread. Also, as we waited, they brought out a little taste of their crawfish balls that were really good.  For my entree, I was torn between a few dishes, but the waitress recommended the Redfish, their signature dish, so I went with that. It came cooked perfectly topped with almonds, a delicious sauce and green beans. It was light and I felt like I was indulging in something special without over doing it. David had the rabbit and he said that was really good, as well.  We had told them that it was our anniversary, so after we ordered our dessert, they brought out two complimentary glasses of champagne. I thought that was such a nice touch and I love when restaurants go a little bit out of their way to do something special for little celebrations.  For dessert, we enjoyed the banana bread pudding, which came topped with ice cream. This dessert was delicious, and I was happy that David and I were sharing because I could have easily eaten the entire thing by myself.  The service and food here was excellent and this was the perfect place to have our anniversary celebration. Everyone was so nice and welcoming and I loved the atmosphere, dining right across the street from City Park. Ralph's gets bonus points because of the fact that they have valet.

Man, it's been ages since I ate here. I think it was back in my pre-Yelp days, even.  I stopped in here with a hankering for a burrito (pretty commonplace for me). I first started with some chips and queso and the restaurant's own bean dip and salsa. It was all perfect.  For my entree, I got the Burrito Gigante with shredded chicken and cheese sauce. It was incredible and, of course, I had plenty left over. It definitely satisfied my burrito craving.

Really cute antique shop among all of the other antique shops in this area.  This store feels like you are going through one of your grandmother's closets. They have a little of everything here, from vintage salt and pepper shakers to different hats, clothing, books and records. Everything is fairly well priced and would be good to give as a gift that is a little "different".

Superior Grill is one of the places you go to because someone brings you.  The margaritas are great, but the food is just mediocre.    If you are a fan of good Mexican food, you will leave disappointed because this place is nothing special.  I know this might sound weird, but I would describe it as "Mexican food geared towards white people", only because the few times I have eaten here the food has lacked flavor.  I think they are more concerned with keeping their uptown St. Charles Ave. clientele happy than spicing up the meals.  The margaritas are fantastic!  I usually like to go and hang out on the patio with friends and just have a few drinks and maybe an app.  It's nice to sit outside during the nice months when the weather is pretty.  BUT, it's not really worth fighting the crowds for this one experience.

This was my FAVORITE gallery on Dirty Linen Night.  For starters, I LOVE any type of art that has a spooky twist. It has nothing to do with Halloween: I'm a year round, spooky decor type of person. The art here is right up my alley: leafless trees silhouetted against a dark, or dimly lit sky, moss hanging off of cypress trees in the shadows. The paintings make you feel as if you're looking out of a window onto a swampy scene at midnight.   There was one piece that I particularly loved of shadowy trees against a red background. The forest seemed to call for you to come explore. In a perfect world I would have endless walls on which to hang all of the art that I covet. Until then, I'll have to make due with admiring these lovely works at Tanner Gallery.

This is one of those places that I've passed dozens of times, over the years, and always wondered about. When the opportunity presented itself to eat here, I was excited. This is a pretty old school type of place and the restaurant definitely has that "my grandparents probably used to be regulars here" type of feel.  Strangely enough, the restaurant wasn't as packed as the full parking lot would suggest, when I visited. I decided to start with the French onion soup and Caesar side salad and I got the lasagna as my entree.  French onion soup- This was great! I'm a huge fan of FOS and their version is really good. It came out piping hot and topped with a generous serving of melted cheese. It was a great start to the meal.  Caesar salad- This was a pretty basic, no-frills Caesar salad, and that's okay. The lettuce was crispy and good and I thought the dressing was nice without being too tart, as some other Caesar dressings tend to be.   Lasagna- Okay, so I hadn't had lasagna in years, so when I saw it on the menu I was quick to order it. Their version comes with Italian sausage, ground beef, marinara and a five cheese blend all served in what is basically a skillet. The portion is huge and easily big enough for two people, especially if you get apps. I really liked it, but I had one complaint- TOO MUCH marinara. I like marinara as much as the next person, but the lasagna was drowned in it and I actually didn't taste much else other than the sauce. I saw the meat and cheese, but there was a lot of tomato happening here. If I go back, I would definitely ask them not to dump all of the marinara on top and maybe give it to me on the side. Other than that, I loved it and I would totally recommend it- sauce on the side is an easy enough fix.  The staff was friendly and had everything out in a timely manner, although I think my lasagna did take a little longer than an average entree would take, but it was worth it.

This TJ Maxx is okay, if you're in the area.  I was here just to look around, mainly at purses and they have a decent selection, but nothing overly great. A lot of the items seemed outdated and there was no real organization. The clothing was a little better and there was a fairly big selection of items, if you're willing to look through the racks.

Woo hoo, I finally made it over to Pho Cam Ly!  The reviews were awesome and my friends were raving about it but it seemed to take forever until I was finally seated (near a window) at this fantastic restaurant on Magazine. My experience here did not disappoint.  I met a friend here for lunch and walking in, I was immediately blown away by the renovations that had been done to the place. Small world time: after I checked in here, a woman on twitter informed me that her husband was the one who did all of the renovations (I swear, I think I am linked to everyone in this town via social media). Kudos to him! There is a gorgeous wood floor and plenty of tables and space. You would never guess that this place is as a big as it is, just by looking at it from the outside.  I was in a coffee mood, so I ordered a Vietnamese iced coffee so that I would have some caffeine to sip on. As for the food: this place has everything you could imagine. In fact, I think that they have the most expansive menu of any Vietnamese restaurant in the area. For an appetizer, we decided on the spring roll with pork patties. This came with two large rolls to and order and it was fantastic. The pork was tender and had a lot of flavor. For my entree, I got the raw eye of round and brisket pho. I found that the broth had A LOT of flavor and a bit of that earthy quality that i like in a good bowl. The meat was perfect and there was a lot of it. I definitely left here full and satisfied.  If you are feeling adventurous, you can always try the Pho challenge: finish a huge bowl of two pounds of meat and two pounds of noodles in one hour and it's free. If you fail, you gotta fork over $30. I have no idea if anyone has actually completed this challenge, but I could see it making for an interesting UYE, if anyone is ever hungry enough.  I will definitely return to Pho Cam Ly. I am putting it up there with Tan Dinh, Pho Bang (on Manhattan) and Magasin as one of my regular Pho haunts.

I was having a major hummus craving when I decided to make the trek out to Metairie and meet a friend of mine for lunch. I've been trying to open my horizons a little more and explore Metairie, so after some research, I found myself at Albasha.  The place itself is easy to find, and surprisingly wasn't packed for lunch. I started with a Lebanese iced tea as I looked over the menu. I knew that I was getting hummus, so I decided to order some Mediterranean hummus that came topped with olive oil, olives, sun dried tomatoes and feta cheese. I really could have just eaten an entire bowl of this stuff and called it a day- it was delicious!  For my entree, I decided to get the chicken shawarma. This was grilled chicken that came with hummus on the side (yay!), rice, and a salad topped with feta cheese. This was a HUGE portion of food. The chicken was good, but I did find some pieces to be a little dry. The hummus was delicious and the salad was small, but got the job done. I had plenty of leftover for dinner that night.  I liked Albasha. The service was good, the food was delicious and the atmosphere was nice. It's a great spot for lunch and I would return.

Don't let the fact that this spot is located in a small strip mall deter you. It's some of the best pizza and Italian food you will ever have. I had lunch here a few days ago and it was delicious.   I enjoyed the margherita pizza, the white pizza, boudin egg rolls, Mount Vesuvius shrimp, meatballs, and spinach dip. Yeah, it was a lot! Thankfully, I was sharing with a few people.   The pizza here is authentic New York style pizza with that perfect thin crust and cheese and sauce that speaks for itself. The place is family owned and the service is super friendly. It's a small spot, so give the crew some heads up if you plan on being in a big group. Otherwise, take out is a great option. I love the food here and I will absolutely be back.

If you are anything like me, you are pretty faithful when it comes to your hair stylist. I have been with my same stylist, Jeff, for 14 years. When he told me that he was moving his operation over to Salon Elle, of course I followed.  I stopped in yesterday for a later appointment and Jeff took me right away. He did a fantastic job as always and when I left, my way too long hair was trimmed to a manageable and stylish length for the summer.  I love Salon Elle. It's an old house that has been converted into a salon and the layout is just gorgeous. There is plenty of natural light that flows into the place and everything is clean and well organized. I look forward to coming here and seeing Jeff for many years to come.

Am I seriously admitting to eating one of these things in a public forum? Ugh, I guess so. Admitting to eating street meat is one of those things that is usually followed by some explanation. Something like "...but it was after a long night." or "...I was super hungry after saving those kids from that burning building!" There really is no other excuse for eating a Lucky Dog.   With that being said, my only real excuse for eating one was that I had honestly never had one (and prided myself on that fact) and one evening curiosity got the best of me. Now, I'm not going to sit here and admit to you that I got any enjoyment out of this thing, but I will confess that it wasn't nearly as bad as I thought it would be and the good news is that it didn't make me sick or kill me, so that's a plus.  Would I go out of my way to have another one? Probably not unless I was starving to death, but for what it is, it isn't horrible.

I like wine.  I like cheese.  I like fancy food for super cheap.  Bacchanal is a place that has the potential to grow on me.    Pros: insanely huge wine selection, they also offer beer and water, they have a cheese plate, a "guest chef" from a fancy pants restaurant cooks food and it's cheaper than you could ever get at said restaurant, the place has live music and a cozy atmosphere.  Cons:  it's all outside, it's all outside, no seriously...it's all outside.    I love being outside.  Ok, that's a lie.  This is New Orleans.  I love being outside during the months of November, part of December, the end of March and April.  During the summer...outside is hot.  In the winter months...outside is cold (yes, 30 degrees is cold to me).  Also, what happens when it rains?  Where do you go?  Does the place shut down?  I don't want to rain on anyone's parade.  This IS a cool place.  I can definitely see going here for a romantic night out, on a date.  Otherwise,  I would probably avoid it, at least during the summer.  I can put on a coat in the winter, but the good folks at Bacchanal might frown on me showing up for wine and cheese in a bikini, in an effort to stay cool.  I'll admit it, I hate to sweat.  And in New Orleans, in July, you're gonna be sweating... even at night.  It's called humidity, people.  It's a cool idea, might I suggest a really big fan?  ;)

I had wanted to visit this bar for ages and I finally made it over.  What a cute spot! I love the laid back vibe, the dimmed lighting and, of course, the fancy drinks. They have a fairly extensive menu, and a few of their drinks are a bit different from that other tiki bar a few doors down. I enjoyed everything I had here and I dug the atmosphere.   This is really one of those spots where time really flies, because it's pretty dark. I liked that there was a lot of cool seating and all of the decor really made you feel as if you were in an island paradise.

This is a review of a wedding reception that I attended here.  I had never eaten at Muriel's before so when I found out that I would be attending a wedding reception here, I was pretty intrigued and I had no idea what to expect.
