When we arrived, the entire group was lead upstairs to the reception area. There were two rooms: one for music and dancing and one for socializing and food. Upon our arrival we immediately dug in. The first thing that I tried was a delicious brisket that was thinly sliced and served with a delicious cream sauce. It was out of this world and I probably would have been happy just eating that.  The next thing I tried were the sweet potatoes with pecans mixed into them and the pecan encrusted drum. Both were AMAZING! They also had salad available, which I didn't get a chance to try, but I did try the cheese and fruit plate! There was an assortment of amazing cheeses accented with strawberries and grapes.   Out of all of this amazing food, my favorite definitely had to be the raw oysters. OH YEAH! This isn't your mama's wedding reception. There were fat ice cold oysters and they were incredible. I had about 6 of them and I honestly could have eaten 12 or more. I like that they had already been cut of their shell, and they were just sitting nicely in there. It made them really easy to eat. And they went really quickly and the staff was quick about getting fresh ones out immediately.  As for the venue itself, the place is just beautiful and very classic New Orleans. We were able to walk out onto the balcony and chat and look out over Jackson Square on this nice evening. The staff was EXTREMELY attentive- as soon as we were finished with a plate, it was taken from away. If I needed something, the staff was immediately on it. I was really impressed.  All in all, my experience here was amazing. I will definitely return to Muriel's for a proper dinner. I would love to spend a birthday or another celebratory occasion here.

This was a really cool little parade. It's more of a walking parade and there aren't a lot of big floats, but it's still a really cool idea.  Although the title is inspired by Star Wars, Chewbacchus covers everything from Star Trek to zombie movies and everything in between. It's really cool because people make their own costumes and get really into it. This isn't one of those parades that you come to expecting to get a lot of throws. You really come just to have a good time and admire the costumes and all of the work that people put into their different themes.  I think that next year I will do two things differently: I will stand in a better spot. I think that I was at the beginning of the parade and the group was kind of just getting used to the walk. And I will go to the Chewbacchanal after, because I think that would add to the experience.

This is it. Today was the day that I gave Starbucks one more chance and they failed me. I really never buy iced coffee anymore. David gave me a very nice coffee maker, so I can make iced coffee at home, but I was in a pinch today so I thought I would stop in here and grab a quick cup. Big mistake. Huge.   Time and time again they fill the entire cup with big chunks of ice and then put in the coffee. The result is a cup of coffee that I finish before the ice even melts. My grande was probably a quarter cup of actual coffee. Last time I asked them not to do this and they did it anyway. This time I totally forgot to mention it, but I feel as if it's common sense.   Just for the record: I don't blame the employees- I know they are only doing as instructed. I blame Starbucks HQ for being stingy with their coffee. As much as they are charging, they should be willing to be a little more accommodating.

This truck was a welcome addition to the Gretna Food Truck Fest. She had iced coffee ready to go for the warm afternoon. The owner of the truck is really cool, and although I knew what I wanted, she didn't mind taking a few seconds to explain to other customers exactly what she offered.  The iced coffee I got here was delicious, full of flavor and well priced. I can't help but wonder if this truck will eventually end up being a brick and mortar store. It would certainly be a nice addition to the area, but I'm sure it does well wheeling around the streets of New Orleans.

It was a cold December evening when I stopped in; the restaurant was bustling as I settled into my table and looked over the menu. I started with an order of the "Shanghai Spring Rolls," fried pork and cabbage roll in a tasty, crispy wrap. The pork was tender and savory; it made for a perfect start.  I opted next for the "Monkey Snack." This is salmon wrapped around a sesame-seed crusted banana with a sweet, spicy sauce. Chef was right--this was an interesting combination that worked surprisingly well. The fruit balanced nicely with the fish, and the spicy sauce was a nice touch that brought all the flavors together.  Finally, to warm my bones I opted for the "Spicy Dan Dan Noodles." This is a large bowl of chicken and black bean and homemade chili sauces and it really hit the spot! The noodles are on the thicker side, so they do a good job of soaking up the yummy broth. Speaking of the broth, it already has a nice kick to it, but I liked that they brought a little extra chili sauce on the side, just in case you want to bring it to the next level. If you get this dish, be sure to stir it all well and let those ingredients really combine for the full flavor experience.  If your tastes lean more toward the vegan side, Luvi's menu includes "Pan Fried Vegan Lover Dumplings" with bok choy, mushroom and green bean noodles, "Spicy Stir Fried Bean Curd" with jalapeno, red onion and black bean chili, and "Stir Fried Napa Cabbage" with ginger and garlic.  I wrote about this restaurant in my column for Offbeat Magazine. Read the whole thing here: https://www.offbeat.com/articles/luvi-restaurant-specializes-raw-seafood-with-asian-flair/

This is a fancy little place with a speakeasy feel.  I was here for an afternoon cocktail and I immediately dug the vibe: a classic cocktail bar that makes you feel as if you have stepped back in time- except for the tvs (can we PLEASE have some cocktail bars that don't feel the need to have big screens on the wall?). I got the Frenchy which was a tasty vodka and champagne concoction, which I enjoyed. They have music practically every night, but sadly I arrived too early and I wasn't able to catch the band.  This seems like the perfect place to start an evening and I will return.

I like it here. I have no idea why the main picture for the place is a picture of the men's room, but okay.  I attended my first ever Pelican's game here, as you do, and I really liked the place. There's a nice gift shop where you can pick up all of the Pelican's fan gear that you could ever want. Upstairs, there are plenty of food and drink stations, that will keep you hydrated and well fed during the game, or any other event that you may be attending here.   One thing I noticed was that there is staff EVERYWHERE and they are very friendly and help you find your seat or anything else that you might need. We were high in the seats for the game, but had no problem seeing all of the action and had a really good time.

Apparently where we're going we don't need roads. When I walked into this place the first time, it was as if Doc Brown had fired up the Delorean and kicked this baby all the way to October 21st, 2015 and took every kid from Rocco's with it.  In other words, this place went from being a college kid bar to being an old man bar in the matter of maybe a week. Trippy, man.   In all seriousness, this bar wasn't too bad. Before, it was a not so great college bar and now it's a "finding it's sea legs" older person bar (which is right up my alley). Yes, I am afraid I have finally become one of those people who prefers to sit and have a drink rather than dance all night to club music. It was bound to happen, so here we are. We're old. Join me, won't you?

You always see those shows on tv at night about little gourmet cupcake places full of good looking treats.  The sad thing is that all of these places are usually located somewhere in California, where you wonder if they eat the cupcakes or just look at them.  Imagine my delight when I heard that a gourmet cupcake place was open uptown!  I was excited to try it.  The only cupcakes I think that I've ever had were sadly from bakeries who I don't think specialized in cupcakes (does that make sense?  I'm saying that they weren't good.).    Anyway, at Kupcake Factory they have a huge selection of cupcakes from strawberry, to Boston creme, to carrot cake.  I decided to try the Birthday cake cupcake and the Wedding cake cupcake.  Both were amazing.  They were super soft and fresh and you could taste that they had been cooked that day.  They had a nice think layer of icing, and to top it all off, they were nice to look at!  They also sell "day olds" for a little cheaper, if you aren't as picky about "freshness".  I really doubt one day would make that much of a difference, since they are stored in a glass case.  I can't wait to go back and try all of the different cupcakes they have here.  I'm hooked!

I like this Little Tokyo a lot because it has a very upscale feel.  The dining room is very nice and the huge window let in a lot of natural light on nice days.  When I went here with a friend we were feeling experimental, so among other things, we decided to try the tofu steak appetizer.  It's 3 blocks of grilled tofu topped with eel sauce.  It was actually pretty good!  The tofu soaks up the taste of the sauce and gives it really good flavor.  It was interesting to try, although I probably wouldn't go out of my way to get it again.    We also got some rolls. The mid city, uptown, Philly and spicy salmon rolls were all really good and very well made.   This would be a great place to bring a date due to the nice atmosphere and upscale feel.

I'm pretty amazed. I had never heard of this place when a friend suggested that we get dinner here.  Walking in, the restaurant is small but nice. We were here during the week, so there was no huge crowd and there were a few empty tables. We sat down and the waitress was quick to come over, bring us a bread basket and take our beverage order.  Looking over the menu, everything sounded delicious. I decided to go with the Penne Alla Vodka which is penne pasta, mixed with a delicious cream sauce and huge pieces of crab. It was delicious and creamy and I was delighted that there was plenty of crab. The dish had a lot of flavor and wasn't overly filling.  My only complaint was that service was pretty slow.  Considering it was a week night and there weren't a lot of people in the place, it took a while to get our food. We weren't in a rush, but from the time we sat down until the time we left, two hours had passed. It took about 45 minutes to get our entrees, even though we didn't order anything crazy complicated. It's not the end of the world, but just be aware of this if you are looking to grab dinner and you are on a schedule that you have to keep.  I would return to this cozy little French Quarter restaurant and would recommend it for a date.

So, you know that thing where you had something all the time as a kid and then it went away? And then all of your memories are of how amazing this certain thing was and "if only" it was still around life would be so great? That's how I am with Krystal Burger, or at least I was.  I went in here for lunch and...well, I was left disappointed. I had always remembered Krystal being so good and the expectation didn't meet the reality. I got combo #1, which is 4 Krystal burgers, fries and a drink. First of all, the fries really had no flavor and they were definitely underwhelming. The burgers were good, but they were more bread than meat. You can't have a small patty of meat with a super fluffy bun. I mean...it was good, but it wasn't great.  Would I go back? Uh...maybe, but I wouldn't go out of my way. It IS nice, however, to have more fast food options on the Westbank for lunch.

This was such a great time!!   I was lucky enough to score tickets to this through the magic of Yelp and it was fun being among the "beautiful people". Outside, there were a lot of different vendors including tables that were selling hats and fascinators, jewelry and fancy ties and pocket squares for men. Re was doing a great job of representing Yelp at the Yelp table and people were able to vote on their favorite designer.  I headed in as I waited for Deborah, my plus one, and I was told by an official person that we could sit in the front row VIP section. Score! We were right on the side of the runway, sitting next to the judges, so we had one of the best views in the house as all of the fashion came down the catwalk.  Deborah and I had a good time doing some "judging" of our own and commenting on all of the designs. We both agreed that Brik Allen had the best looks and he ended up winning the design competition AND the Yelp people's choice competition! So, I guess we have some pretty good taste.  The one tiny bummer was that the food and drinks were a bit expensive, but it wasn't earth shattering because I didn't come to eat or drink. It would have been nice if they would have offered some free non-alcoholic drinks, however. Oh well.  If you have the opportunity to check out any of New Orleans Fashion Week, you definitely shouldn't hesitate.  Thank you Yelp and Morgan for the hook up!

My boyfriend turned me onto this place, as I am a Taco Bell fan, and he said that this is a step up.  He was right.  I have only ever had the burrito, but it is HUGE and I can never finish the whole dang thing!  Great prices, although it is in a sketchy area.  I have and would never go by myself.  My boyfriend has had pretty much everything on the menu and has said it is good.  It's cheap, so it's worth trying.  It's not restaurant quality Mexican, but it's better than the Bell.

Such a great shop!  Whenever I passed Blue Frog, I always kind of assumed that it was just a "do it yourself/build your own box" type of chocolate shop. While you can pick and choose chocolates from the case, they also have an assortment of all kinds of chocolates that you can give as gifts or just enjoy yourself. My faves that I saw were the chocolate musical instruments, chocolate water meters, chocolate streetcar tokens and chocolate gators. A definite "must" for anyone who is visiting NOLA and wants a "different" kind of souvenir to bring home.  They have a TON of cute gift ideas and I could never go through them all, but I will say that I thought that the chocolate gavel geared towards someone who just graduated law school was SUPER cute.  Stop in here and look around. You are sure to find something that you like. I can't wait to see if they get anything special in for Halloween!

During my formative high school years, I spent a lot of time at this library usually doing research for a project. I know what you are thinking: "why didn't you just go online?" Well kiddies, back in my day (the late 90's, early 00's) the internet wasn't what it is today. It was still fairly new, as far as research went, and the teachers at my school decided (in their infinite wisdom) that they would require 4 different sources to be cited on a paper or project. Out of those 4, only ONE could be an internet source. So, I had to go to the library and look information up in books. Oh yeah, it was a lot of fun.  Anyway, this is a really nice library and really big. I like that they have little study "nooks" that you can go into if you need to be totally alone to study or do research or work. They have special reading events for kids and other fun things for them to do.

Becky is a self made artist who is naturally talented and fantastic at painting and she adds her own unique twist to all of her work. Not only does she paint one of a kind pieces, but she offers prints at a reasonable price and she does commissioned work. If you are short on wall space, you can wear Becky's art on your body via one of the shirts she sells with her prints on it.  Positioned right on Magazine St., I like that the gallery walk-able from other little galleries and shops on the block and makes for a fantastic addition to the neighborhood. Gallery B Fos is set up perfectly with nice flow and wide open space, so that you can view all of her artwork and the staff working here was super helpful in making sure that I was being taken care of.   Gallery director Felice helps with the art consumer's needs and answers questions when the artist is off site and soon Gallery B Fos will be offering jewelry inspired by Becky's work, so stay tuned for greatness.

City Park is a fantastic "getaway" in the city, especially when the weather is really nice.  It is really gorgeous and has come a long way since Katrina with the help of local and visiting volunteers.  The shady oaks are huge and are perfect for a picnic or for just going somewhere nice to read or enjoy the day.  Throughout the park are covered areas with tables and chairs, if you are in the mood for a barbecue or a crawfish boil.   The park is close to the museum, so you can visit after a nice lunch.  There is also a tennis court, Storyland for the kids, and the botanical gardens.  A definite must for locals and tourists alike.

Fancy cocktail place that is WAY less pretentious than Cure.  One of my major complaints about Uptown is that there really aren't any cocktail bars. Well, this is pretty much as close as you are going to get. Nice place that caters to a somewhat older crowd. Smart and capable bartenders that are happy to help you figure out exactly what suits your tastes.  I do agree with Joi when she said that people here are casually dressed, considering the atmosphere. It really feels more like one of those places that you would dress up and make a night out of, but maybe that's just me.  I definitely want to go back and try some of their delicious (looking) food.

I would like to start off my review with a little lesson on how a business works. When a new place opens it needs a minute to find it's groove. You can't go into a place on the first day and expect everything to be flowing like clock work. There are going to be hiccups. To go into a place on the day it opens and then rate it two stars when everything doesn't go perfectly is a little unfair in my opinion. Yes, they are going to run out of things. Yes, they are going to be a little slow. If the place has been open less than a month, please go in prepared for that.  Just putting that out there.  Today I had the delight of trying the new burger place in town: Charcoal's. As soon as I heard about the unique menu, I was in. I couldn't wait to try it out. Among some of the items besides the basic beef are antelope, elk, bison, salmon, venison and veggie.  Being the adventurous spirit I am, I decided to try the antelope burger. I got it topped with cheese, lettuce, tomato, ketchup and mayo on the brioche bun. You can get all kinds of fancy ingredients on it like bacon and avocado and grilled onions, but I decided to keep it simple.  The burger itself was so good. It didn't taste crazy or anything like that. It had a bit of a "gamey" taste, but nothing overwhelming. It was a really thick, juicy patty and it was cooked to perfection. The bun was soft and flavorful and really good. I got a side of sweet potato tater tots. I had never had them before, and they were obviously house made and delicious. They were almost like small sweet potato hash browns. They were crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. All in all, really good.  Although a little expensive, I would definitely check out Charcoal's again when I am in the mood for a special burger treat.

Katie wasn't lying, this store really is dangerous.  I have been here a few times now and I never made it out the door without having bought at least one thing. I know that this is a chain, and I usually prefer shopping local, but this is a good place to start if you are looking for stylish home decor. You will find it all here: pillows, bedding, candles, kitchen ware and the list goes on.  I stopped in here because I have had my eye on a big pink wool pillow. I need this pillow. It will be mine. While I was pricing it, of course they were having a 20% off sale on other bedroom items so I broke down and got myself a throw. Hey, winter is coming. No matter what your style, you are bound to find something here that will fit your personality and they are always having sales, so keep an eye out.

Someone told me the other day that my Yelp reviews are "too nice". I'll admit that unless service is horrible and I really hate the food, I will be pretty generous with my ratings. However, my four stars for Juan's were totally well earned.  Juan's is a New Orleans classic for Mexican food. I headed over here for dinner, and since I was in a "burrito" mood, I got the "wet burrito". This is a burrito packed with beans, rice, lettuce and salsa and topped with red chile sauce, melted cheese, sour cream and jalapeños. The burrito is HUGE and was so good. I was going to snap a picture, but before I could, that burrito got ate.  The service was friendly and I like that the restaurant itself is dim and kind of cozy. Juan's is small, so there is going to be a bit of a wait for a table, if you go during busy lunch and dinner hours, but I waited less than 10 minutes at 8:00.

Aaah! Another cute new boutique on Magazine St! And it JUST opened! I happened to just stumble into this place because I had never seen it before and then I realized that today was their opening day.  Lucy Rose has a lot of cute clothes for all body types. I think I would call them "happy" clothes: a lot of skirts, dresses and tops in a lot of bright colors. I was only able to quickly stop in here today, but I will definitely be back. Lucy Rose will definitely make a nice addition to Magazine St.

If jazz fest is for tourists, then the French Quarter fest is for the locals.  Tons of local bands playing music for free!  What could be better than that?  Food?  Oh yeah, there is plenty of it here.  All the food you could possibly want.  The best thing to do is go out there with a blanket, get some food, set up a picnic and enjoy the musical sounds of the city.  One of the best times you can have in New Orleans.

Guess who just discovered the "festivals" category.  This chick!  I love the poboy fest!  My boyfriend and I went to the last one with some friends and had a great time.  Be sure to get there early, because the place fills up fast and gets packed with a capital "P"..err...Packed!  By the time we decided to leave, it took us about a half hour to get from one end of Oak to the other and that was before the afternoon crowd really hit.  But you don't want to hear about that.  You want to hear about how awesome the food is.  Well, that goes without saying.  Restaurants from all over town set up booths and sell small samples of their best po boys.  Now, here's a hint.  You're gonna wanna eye up what the po boy looks like before you drop your money.  Some of them just have one ingredient like shrimp, but some of piles of stuff like sausage and yummy dressing on it.  Those are the ones you want, if you want to get your bucks worth.  No matter what you choose, it's all good and you won't be disappointed.

NOW SMOKE FREE!!  DBA is one of my favorite places to enjoy live music.  They have a fantastic beer selection and the atmosphere is great.  You can either sit in the window that faces Frenchmen and watch the world go by, or you can enjoy the live music in the stage area.  There is also a nice little "lounge" area upstairs, if you want to get away from the crowd.

I can say with complete honesty that Cane's is the ONLY fast food place that I have ever been to that has NEVER screwed up my order!  I have been going here since this place opened.  It is what it is:Chicken fingers.  They are hot and delicious and fantastic.  I LOVE their sweet tea and whenver I order a large with "easy ice", I actually get it with just a little ice!!  I have always been satisfied with Cane's and have never had reason to complain.  The way all fast food place should be.

Such a lovely little shop on so many levels!  I stopped in here because I have had this place bookmarked for a while and I finally found myself in the area, so I decided to visit. The shop itself is set up in such a lovely manner. There are glass cases full of pretty little trinkets, vintage and new alike, and everything is so sparkly and inviting under the lights.  I've found things extremely well priced here, and if you are in the market for vintage costume jewelry or accessories, you are sure to find a bauble that suits your fancy. On the day that I stopped in, a sweet woman named Eleanor was working and she engaged me in lovely conversation about old New Orleans, how much things have changed since she was a girl and the differences in dialect from one area of the city to another. I was having a pretty laid back day, so I was happy to get to know her a little better.  I will definitely return to this fantastic little treasure chest, if not for the jewelry, than for the conversation.

I am normally not really a fan of Academy. I find A LOT of their pro team related things over priced ($60 for a "licensed" Saints shirt?? No thanks.), but I do realize that the place serves a purpose.  Well, this place saved my life recently when I ended up here on the hunt for a birthday gift for my favorite Saints fan. Do you know how HARD it is to find anything "football team" related during the off season? It's real hard, y'all. It's darn near impossible. I was SAVED when I stopped in and found an awesome gift that is sure to be treasured forever (one can hope!). Needless to say, I was a happy camper.  I looked over some of the team jerseys that they had for women and I was a little less than impressed with the selection. I think once the season gets underway, they will be packing the store with goodies.

I'll be the first to admit that I usually don't go for donuts. If I'm going to go for something sweet, I just go for cake, but Joe's might change all that. For some reason, I've become kind of obsessed with their donuts. More specifically, their chocolate sprinkle donuts and their glazed chocolate donuts that actually have a really rich chocolate flavor. Either one will make for a perfect dessert when a craving hits. They also have a variety of other sweet and pastries that I have to resist when my sweet tooth kicks in. Did someone say McKenzie's turtles?! Oh yeah.  I've been here for lunch once and the experience was great. Even though the restaurant was packed, service was attentive and friendly. I got a club sandwich with a side of grits and some donut holes, because when you're eating in a diner, and all of that is available, you go for it. The sandwich was really good, but curiously only had ham and bacon on it as the meats. I guess that's their version of a club and that's fine with me, I enjoyed it. The grits were yummy and, of course, the sweets always hit the spot because they're known for their donuts.  I have yet to try breakfast here, but I'll be doing so soon. I'm glad there's a Joe's in Terrytown.

I am so excited that this tasty restaurant has made its way out of the French Quarter and into the fold of Uptown.  I LOVED El Libre when I visited their French Quarter location, but I rarely found myself in the area whenever a craving for a really good Cubano hit. Well, that problem has now been solved as El Libre is now conveniently located on Calhoun.  I stopped in on a Monday for lunch and the place was empty. It's an "order at the counter" type of place and they serve a few signature Cuban dishes as well as their legendary Cubano, made the classic way, as well as a vegetarian Cubano. I got the classic with pork and an order of waffle fries. I knew going in that the sandwich was pretty massive, but I had forgotten that it is PACKED to the brim with perfectly seasoned pork. It hit the spot and satisfied my months-long Cuban sandwich craving. The fries were perfect. They were extra crispy and the generous serving was shareable.  The menu is limited, but what they do, they do well. I do wish that they had plantains on the menu, but you win some and you lose some. If you miss the old Bud's Broiler that used to be located here, they got you covered and have a burger on the menu. They also have an assortment of classic Cuban cocktails, but I didn't partake because it was a weekday at lunch and I had a job to get back to. I definitely want to come back on a weekend and get some drinks, though.  With so much good stuff packed into this spot, I am sure to be back.

I've been passing Mae Mae's for months just waiting for someone to review it. After reading a few reviews, I was hopeful that I would have a good experience here, so I decided to stop in for lunch.  First of all, I love the counter system: you walk up and order, you pay and you sit and wait. I got an order of Vietnamese iced coffee and a large bowl of the eye of round pho. As I waited, the man working was nice enough to bring out a small sampling of fried pickles. They have a lot of different types of Asian food and non-Asian snacks on the menu, so I guess they were testing these out. It made for a nice little treat and I enjoyed it.  The Vietnamese coffee came out pre-made. I usually prefer when they bring you a glass of ice and you wait for it to steep and then pour it in yourself, but this wasn't a big deal. My main complaint was that there was too much ice and I felt like I didn't get as much coffee as I would have gotten at other places.  The pho came out and I was really excited about the size. The large was actually large and for $7 it seemed to be well worth the money. They didn't have the normal pho soup spoons that other places have, so I had to make due with a tablespoon to sip the broth. Tedious, but not the worst thing in the world. Unfortunately, the broth had NO flavor- NONE! I was so bummed. I had to actually add sriracha to it to give it some "pop". I don't understand what could have gone wrong- there was plenty of meat, onions and cilantro and the broth was the perfect color. It was just bland as all get out. Maybe it was an off day or maybe they make it more bland for the Westwego crowd? I'm not sure.  I will probably go back and give them another shot. The staff is friendly, the place is clean and the atmosphere is nice. Maybe this was just growing pains.

Fantastic new music venue on Frenchmen St.   Came in on opening night and the staff was friendly and welcoming. They have a nice size stage for performances, plenty of seating and they serve food! The place is beautifully done with murals on the walls and an entirely renovated space. The band was on a break for most of the time that we were here, but I will definitely be back to check out everything that this new venue has to offer.

I had heard from a lot of people how good Maurepas is and I was told I had to try it. The person with whom I had dinner had been raving about it. Sadly, I was left disappointed.  Stopped in here on a weeknight, there was no crowd at all and we were seated immediately. Looking over the menu, there isn't a lot of selection, but I'm okay with that as long as a place does the few items they have on the menu well.  I started with the stone ground grits which were excellent. They were creamy and had a lot of flavor and if I were to return, this is what I would get. For my entree, I decided on the fish. It wasn't the gulf fish that was on the menu, but it was another fish special which was lightly fried and served with a cole slaw type mix. I was pretty disappointed with it. The fish was pretty dry and didn't have a whole lot of flavor and the cole slaw salad mix was pretty flavorless. Considering the fish was about $17, I would say that it wasn't worth the money at all.  After dinner we ordered coffee, and the cream that came with it had curdled. They quickly rectified this issue, but come on- we just paid a good bit of money for dinner, you should know if the cream had curdled or not.  I would go back, but I would probably get the grits and another appetizer and make that my meal. I wouldn't order a full on entree again, although I hear that the chicken leg quarter is good. The staff was super friendly and accommodating.

Um yeah. I have now eaten here and I can say with full certainty that this place sucks. We ordered the burger medium and naturally it came medium well. This is irritating mainly because I only eat red meat once a week, so this was my one shot and it  was terrible.  Before the burger, we got the egg roll appetizer. It was okay. I mean, it was as decent as deep fried frozen egg rolls can be. The beer? The beer was a "no" and had ZERO flavor. To refer to this place as a "brewery" is a joke. All of the beer tastes the same and just makes me sad.

"Good not great" would be an accurate description.  Had dinner here on the advice of a friend. I had NO CLUE this place even existed, but hey, Magazine St. is a long street! I really like the atmosphere of the restaurant. We were seated by a window so that we could look out as we ate and that was nice.   I ordered the taco salad with chicken. It was okay. I liked that there were huge hunks of chicken in it, but there wasn't nearly enough of it. The salad also came with lettuce, black olives, cheese, sour cream and guacamole. Honestly, the shell was kind of stale but it wasn't terrible. I hear that the tacos are amazing, so I will be getting those if I go back.  All in all, not as great as my beloved Felipe's, but still a valid spot if you are looking for quick Mexican food.

I am updating and bumping up to five stars because this thrift store has become my first stop whenever I am looking for something from clothing to cheap electronics.  Over the past year I have found multiple working, great condition Polaroid cameras for a photographer friend of mine for $4 a piece. These cameras can be resold online for good bucks- score! I have found multiple dresses brand new with tags that I was able to snag for less than $10. I have found collectible gifts for next to nothing that cost WAY more online and that friends will cherish for a lifetime. Just today a found a practically brand new denim jacket for $6. If you aren't a regular thrift store shopper, I know you are rolling your eyes, but trust me- you will be surprised what you find here.  I constantly see brand new items for men and women that are selling at a steal. I wouldn't go so far as to buy swimsuits or shoes here (that's where I draw the line), but when I need a new dress for a casual event, this spot is always my first (and usually only) stop.

I recently had a "20's" inspired photo shoot with Make Me Up, and they sent me here (right next door to Make Me Up) to get my hair done all fancy.  They decided that they wanted to put a finger wave in my hair, which is apparently pretty complicated. It consists of putting a "wet set" in the hair, forming the waves with your fingers, setting it with hair gel and then sitting under a hair dryer for over an hour while it sets and dries. Even though the style was hard, my stylist Madeline did a fantastic job. She worked quickly and efficiently to get the waves perfect. The hardest part really was just sitting under that dryer for a really long time while it dried and set.  She did such a good job, that my hair didn't go anywhere for the rest of the day, and I'm convinced that I probably could have slept on it and wore it the entire next day without it looking any worse for wear.  If you are looking for a "different" or somewhat "complicated" hairstyle, Albert Brown is the place to go.

Well, here's a part of town I really wish I lived in. The Garden District seems to have it all: gorgeous houses, great restaurants and good shopping.  This is one of those classic New Orleans neighborhoods that is perfectly walkable and as picturesque as a postcard. It's nice to imagine living in one of these gorgeous homes and sipping coffee on the front porch, whilst looking through the newspaper. You really aren't going to see homes like this anywhere else. Well, maybe in Natchez or a place like that, but the Garden District really is the epitome of Southern charm.

The CAC is a great place for local events and parties.  I have been here for Bourbon and Burlesque. I love how wide open everything is. There are different levels and there is a lot of space for entertaining. They always have different exhibits and events happening here as well as performances in the theater area.  Although the theater is pretty small, by theater standards, it's still a really nice place to see a performance. I watched a Burlesque performance here and had a really good time.

This is the main parking lot for the French Market area.  I like this lot for two reasons: #1- if you get here after 4 or so, parking is painless- there are always a lot of spots. #2- This is one of the few remaining lots that has a real life actual person taking the parking lot payment. I am no fan of the machines, because when I go down to the Quarter I don't know how long I'm going to be down there. Paying for my time ahead of time is a pain. I want to go down there and wander around and not worry about, "okay, I have to be back to my car by 3 because that's as long as I paid for." I don't know why they changed all of the other lots to machines.  In this lot you have a nice view of the river and it's the perfect place to park if you are going for a ride on the Steamboat Natchez or if you want to just sit on the river and enjoy a nice afternoon. It's also perfect proximity to the French Market, Jackson Square and Cafe du Monde. Long story short: this is my "go to" lot when I'm in the area.

Thanks to the magic of Yelp, I got to experience my first ever Pelicans game and it was a great one! The Pelicans set a franchise record with their score of 139 points in one game and the game itself was non stop action.  I loved that there was constant entertainment throughout the game: people running around with signs, the dancers getting the crowd pumped and even a fun game of Simon says at half time. Thanks to social media we were able to participate in little activities with the jumbo tron and the crowd had a great time.  I can't wait to go back and see another game!

First things first.  You may be wondering, "Where the heck is this place?"  Well, I had no issue finding it, since I live on the Westbank, but in case you don't, here are some landmarks.  First go to Lapalco past Barataria.  You will see a Pizza Hut, then a shopping center, then a Ryan's.  Daiwa is in the shopping center, in the far corner.  For those on the Westbank, it's in the shopping center right across the street from the Red, White, and Blue thrift store.  I included a pic of the outside of the place.  Ok, now onto the place itself.  After hearing tons of good things from Jen L., and other fellow yelpers, and being a huge sushi lover, I decided to try this place out.  It only opened a few months ago, and from what I understand, it has some ties to Hana, which is located Uptown.  For those not aware, Hana is my GO TO for sushi 95% of the time.  I couldn't wait to try out what I had been referring to as "Westbank Hana".  Walking in, like others, I was immediately impressed with the decor.  Sure, it still had that "restaurant in a shopping complex" kind of feel, but I think that they did a good job with decorating it and giving it that authentic Japanese look.  The menu of this place is HUGE.  They go far beyond rolls, sashimi, sushi and the other basics.  They have a whole eclectic choice of things, all at reasonable prices.  Be sure to check out the menu on their website, to see what I'm talking about.  Since it was my first time, I decided to keep it simple with a tuna roll, a Philly roll, and a Metairie roll.  You can check out how it all looked, in my picture.  It was so good.  I would definitely say that it's as good as Hana, or any other sushi place on the Westbank.  Also, the waiter was really nice and attentive and was sure to keep my water filled, which is a biggie with me.  I can't wait to go back and try some of their other speciality rolls and dishes.

Blue Plate Mayonnaise is THE mayonnaise that is used on most of the Po Boys in the New Orleans area. Po Boy experts will tell you that no other mayo will do.   Blue Plate is a staple throughout the South, but is "stationed" in New Orleans. It's as classic as any other product that is manufactured here and every true New Orleanian has a jar of the stuff in their fridge at all times.

I like pizza. "Hey, who doesn't??", says this observer.  I have tried so many pizza places around this glorious city, but until recently I had never tried Naked Pizza. It's pretty shocking; Naked Pizza has been around for at least 6 years, they have a pretty good social media presence, and they run ads in the Gambit and other local publications fairly regularly. So, why did it take me this long to try them out? It's a mystery.  I was hanging with a friend uptown, when he suggested we order some Naked Pizza. I was down, as I love trying new places (you know this). I looked at their menu online, and I decided to try the margherita pizza. It comes topped with mozzarella, basil and pesto. I'm trying to keep it a smidge healthier these days, so I skipped the meat.  I got a "small" for myself and that was more than enough for me for lunch. The pizza itself had a nice crust- not too thick and not too thin and the ingredients seemed to be really fresh. Even though I got a pretty "simple" pizza, it had a lot of flavor and I enjoyed it.  As I'm sure everyone knows, Naked Pizza has a really wide selection of healthier pizzas and they even have vegan-friendly options. I will, no doubt, try Naked Pizza again.

Picture this: a friend of mine was in from California for the second weekend of Jazz Fest. You know, the one that was rained out. He texts me at the last minute, on a Monday, and asks me if I want to grab dinner. Yes! Okay, where? That's a tough one- restaurants that are open on Mondays in New Orleans are hard to come by. A quick Yelp search told me that The Flaming Torch was open. I had never been, so I crossed my fingers and we headed over.  I made reservations, but they were completely unnecessary because we were the only people here on a Monday. Everything on the menu looked fantastic, but I decided to start simple. The soup of the day was tomato basil. For those of you who don't know, my two favorite soups are tomato basil and French onion and I am very particular about both. The soup came out and it's looked so good. It looked so good I forgot to take a picture! I know- blasphemy! It was nice and thick and really rich. It was almost more like a stew and I ate all of it and almost asked for seconds.  For my entree I got the redfish topped with shrimp. Not only was the fish delicious, but it was topped with an amazing sauce and the shrimp were fat and full of flavor. It also came with a nice side of roasted potatoes and green beans, which complimented the fish nicely. This dish was one of the more expensive on the menu, but it was more than worth it.  I'll be honest, when I saw some of the reviews of this place I almost skipped it, but I decided to give it a shot and I'm glad I did. Our service was excellent and the food was fantastic and my out of town visitor was quite happy with my selection. I would definitely return to The Flaming Torch, especially on a Monday.

Shoe-nami never disappoints, especially when you are in a pinch.  I needed some shoes for a ball, and since I was in Metairie today, I stopped in here. I have been shopping at this store for at least 15 years and I have bought countless shoes here. Right now the store is 90% boots, but I lucked out and found the perfect pair of sparkly pumps for my special night.  They always have items on sale and they even have a "buy one get one half off" deal going on pretty regularly. The shoes are on the cheaper side, but I like that. I really tend to beat up my shoes, so I'm not interested in spending more than $40 anyway.

I don't know what has come over me, but I have been LOVING Forever 21 lately.  It seems that the styles are a lot different than they used to be, and the stuff isn't geared just towards teens and the early 20s set these days.  They have been stocking really cute print dresses and tops.  I am a sucker for polka dots (they remind me of a vintagey kind of look) and Forever 21 has had a lot of polka dots the last few times I have been in there.  If you haven't checked out Forever 21 in a while, stop in and see if you see something that appeals to you.    This store is especially good because it is HUGE and packed with stuff.  You can easily spend a lot of time shopping around and checking everything out.

This place isn't really anything super special, but it's a great place to check out if you are heading out for a night out in the warehouse district.  They have really good pizza and the place has a nice "party" atmosphere on weekends and even has a dj.  It's open pretty late, especially on game days and during special events, so if you get hungry after a night of celebrating, then it's a good place to check out.

I really wasn't going to do it. I wasn't going to be "that person" who gives a place 5 stars on the first visit, even though every one else who has reviewed it has given it 5 stars. I'm really picky about my sushi and there's no way this place deserves 5 stars already...except that it does.  I stopped in for a late lunch and I was immediately greeted and told to sit anywhere. The man who greeted me came right over and took my drink order. My usual M.O.is to order a couple of special rolls, that way I get a good taste of what the restaurant has to offer.  I decided to get the Okinawa roll and the DeGaulle roll. With spicy tuna, shrimp tempura, tuna, salmon, avocado and mango, the Okinawa has a little bit of everything, so I knew it was a "must". The DeGaulle had salmon, spicy tuna, snowcrab, topped with their house sauce.  The first thing I noticed about these rolls- they are HUGE. At $13 each, they are well worth the money, especially if you are dining with a friend. Of the two rolls that I ordered, I would say that I preferred the DeGaulle. Both of the rolls were delicious, but the DeGaulle roll was a little lighter. The Okianwa was tasty but had A LOT going on. That's not a complaint; it was really good and I would order it again. I was pleased because I had plenty of leftovers, so I finished the rest of my order for dinner.  The service here is really impeccable. The waiter was extremely attentive and checked on me regularly and was quick to refill my iced tea. He even brought me an iced tea "to go", after I paid my check, and I thought that was a really nice gesture.  I would absolutely return to Oishii. I will have to go back and get some of their sashimi, so that I can compare it to my other favorite Westbank sushi place: Tennou. I am sure if you give this place a try, you won't leave disappointed.

Only 3 stars??  What?!  I love this place!  Whenever I go I always get the Oyster platter that comes with fries and hush puppies and cole slaw.  The inside of the place has a "nautical" theme, so you are made to feel like you are eating in a fisherman's cabin.  They have an oyster bar, so if you are in the mood for raw oysters this is a great place to go.  This is also a good place for all kinds of seafood.  I have never had anything here that I didn't really enjoy.  The food here tends to be a little on the spicy side, so if you are a person who likes their food on the bland side, you might want to avoid this one.  The restaurant is a little on the expensive side, at least for the Westbank, so if you are on a budget you may want to go somewhere else.

So, I finally made it to Willa Jean and I met John Besh. Review #1300- let's do this.  Let me start by saying I have wanted to go to Willa Jean since it opened, but I only just made it over there which is a travesty. I had hyped this place up in my head and put it on a fancy brunch pedestal for so long, that I was sure that I was just setting myself up for disappointment. Oooh baby, I was wrong.  I want say that I have been tempted to drop in and just get a pastry to go, but  I wanted to do Willa Jean the right way: I came for brunch and had a sit down meal. I know they have yummy pastries but I am savory over sweet all day, so I need some substance.  We started off with some iced coffee and I looked over the brunch menu. Everything sounded delicious and while, "One of everything, good sir!" was tempting, I opted for the egg, sausage and pimento cheese biscuit with a side of cheese grits, because that's how I get down. This biscuit was crazy and it was packed with a gooey fried egg and thick sausage. The yolk of the egg did that runny thing when you pressed it and the biscuit soaked it all up. Are you following me so far? The pimento cheese was PERFECT and blended everything together flawlessly. This was not a hand sandwich. This was a full on knife and fork undertaking.  As for the cheese grits- what can I say? Cheddar cheese and grits mixed together is like a bowl of love that warms the soul. This was a hug in a bowl: warm, comforting and cozy. I wanted to curl up with these cheese grits and take a nap.   Did I mention that I met John Besh? As if the food itself wasn't worth the wait, John Besh was here working the room and talking to folks. He went from table to table shaking hands, introducing himself and making small talk. When he came to us I could barely contain myself. I shook his hand, told him my name and tried to keep myself from fangirling in the middle of the place. It's not every day you get to meet one of your food idols. John was so sweet and nice and made small talk with us, asked what we had ordered and thanked us for coming in. We commented to him about the large crowd and he said, "And to think, when I opened my first restaurant I said I would never open another one!" Yeah, it's easy to see why he is such a success and why New Orleans loves this man. Oh and for a little lagniappe, none other than Alon Shaya dropped in for an iced coffee- as ya do. The guy sitting next to us made the comment that if Drew Brees comes in next, it will be the perfect brunch.  This was an all around stellar experience for me. Will I be back? Absolutely. I want to go back during dinner hours to see what they have to offer the night crowd. Fantastic service, delectable food and well priced- you can't beat it.  Here's a bonus for reading to the end: John Besh reads a bad Yelp review (really funny). Here's hoping he reads the good ones as well! ;) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a3vw2u1CrMA

As soon as I walked in and saw the big screens playing pop music videos, I knew I would love this place.  This bar is SO FUN! David and I came here to try Fauboirg Bistro, but ended up hanging out after we ate and watched a bit of the LSU game.They have an amazing happy hour special on Saturdays- 2 for 1 doubles and $3 draft beer (and it's good beer!). They are very generous with the pours and they also have wine on tap, if that's what your into.  There's a definite party vibe in here and I can see this place being a lot of fun as the evening wears on. Everyone i met was so sweet and friendly and happy to chat. I'll review the food in another post, but if you are coming for drinks you are going to have a great time.

Are you ever in the mood for a really big, messy burrito? I recently had that kind of craving, so David and I headed over to El Gato Negro, home of one of my favorite burritos.  We were here somewhat early (7 ish) on a Friday night and the crowd was non-existent, but we were greeted with a friendly "hello" and shown to our table right away. Joseph was our waiter and he was great- super friendly and attentive and full of personality. We started with an order of queso and I got my carnitas burrito smothered in their delicious tomato sauce. As always, the burrito was perfect and packed with goodies. I was pretty pleased. I also had a tasty frozen margarita that was a great "cool down" on a warm summer night.  The atmosphere of this place is pretty laid back and I imagine that they do a good lunch crowd and I'm sure that business picks up when there is a show at Howlin Wolf or Republic, so plan accordingly. I will definitely go back for more of their deliciousness.

Did you know that this is outside? Like, in nature and stuff? I know! I was shocked too!  I am not what you would call an "outdoorsy" person. A guy that I am seeing was recently shocked when I told him that I occasionally do venture outdoors and have even been known to enjoy an outdoor festival.  Anyway, I hadn't been here for years when a photographer suggested that we explore this place for a photo shoot. Okay, I'm down. The part of the preserve we ventured into was basically a mud trail next to a swamp. I could tell that it was pretty well traveled as it was pretty worn down and there was some trash (coke cans) left behind. Unfortunately, on the day we went it was muggy and hot and the bugs were everywhere. If I had brought bug spray, I would have actually loved exploring this area.  I'm giving it 5 stars because it is well taken care of and patrolled regularly, so I felt pretty safe. I will probably return when it cools down a little and the insects head South for the winter.

I am SO glad that I waited for Origami to get settled in before I tried it.  On the night that we went it wasn't crowded at all and the service was great! We were seated at a booth and after looking over the menu, we decided to order the salmon sashimi, the tiger roll and the margarita roll.  The salmon sashimi was really fresh and cut thick. This might sound silly, but I liked that it was cut into an even number of pieces so that each person gets their fair share. The margarita roll was excellent was reminiscent of the margarita rolls I had had at other sushi places. By far the star of the meal was the tiger roll. I can't find a menu, so I can't find the exact ingredients, but it was SO GOOD.  Like... so good I might order two the next time I go. I could have eaten the entire thing on my own!  Origami is a little more expensive than other sushi places, but the atmosphere and service was great and the food was excellent. I will definitely be back!

I've waited a long time to review the Roosevelt. While I have never stayed here, I have been here many times for various reasons. I have made it my yearly Christmas tradition to stop in here at least once and admire the gorgeous decorations and lights. There is just something magical about this place. I almost feel as if I'm in New York city and seeking sanctuary from the cold city snow in this hotel's lobby.  When you walk in, you are embraced by gorgeous chandeliers and classic decor. You feel as if you are stepping back in time to the 50's, when ladies wore fancy dresses and men wore hats. You can stop into the Sazerac bar for a cocktail with someone special and sit at the bar and people watch. Having a drink at the Sazerac is a giddy affair that someone must do at least once (or twice) when visiting New Orleans.  Even if you don't end up staying here, admiring this lovely hotel will be an experience in itself.

I have always had no problem finding whatever I need here. I usually just get stuff that will keep my car clean and shiny. I have known a few people who have gotten car maintenance done here with no real issue. The staff here is knowledgeable and friendly and should be able to help you with whatever you may need.

My 500th review!  After passing Guy's time and time again and hearing how great it is, I finally got to stop in and experience the deliciousness for myself.  I went in around 3 in the afternoon on a Saturday. It wasn't packed at all and I was able to quickly order and find a seat. They have an extensive menu, but unfortunately they don't have oyster po boys. Oh well. I decided on a fried shrimp, dressed, instead.  After about 10 minutes, I had my sandwich. I have to say that Guy's was well worth the wait. It was amazing. The bread was fresh and perfect and it was overflowing with shrimp. I ordered a regular size and couldn't even finish it all (of course I did, later). My friend got a roast beef po boy and that looked incredible too! When I go back (and I will be back), I will absolutely have to try it.

Although considered kind of "touristy" this is my favorite place to see live jazz.  I've seen Charmaine Neville play here multiple times, as well as some of the Marsalis'.  If you go early, you can enjoy dinner or drinks before the show.  They used to have free shows on Friday nights at Midnight, but I'm not sure if they still do.  The food is a little pricey, but I like it a lot.  When I went, I had a filet with fried calamari for an appetizer.  Yum!

It is completely unacceptable that it has taken me this long review this New Orleans music institution and for that I apologize.  Tipitina's is world known.  You know that.  The famous, the not so famous and the infamous have played here.  If they were worth listening to, they probably played here at some point.  I'm not telling you anything you don't already know.  The venue is huge and legendary.  Most times it will cost you a few bucks to get in the door, but it is always worth it.  Stories have been told here and history has been made here. If you are looking for good music, this place is a must, end of story.    What's one the best parts?  It's smoke free!

So, a little back story: I usually never go out to eat on Christmas day, but I am currently remodeling my kitchen so I really had no choice.  We made reservations here for 2 on Christmas afternoon. We figured that would be a good time to get a table and get some decent service. We got her at about 1:50 and checked in. Even though we had reservations, we weren't seated until 3. Seriously, we stood there waiting for over an hour. So, that put a bad taste in my mouth right away, but I am willing to give them a bit of wiggle room since it's Christmas Day.  We were seated in one of the downstairs rooms (maybe the only downstairs room) and it was pretty loud, but I was happy that someone came over and gave us menus and took our drink order right away. It was a prix fixe menu, so we knew what we were basically going to get before we arrived.   Our first course was a green salad with a vinaigrette that was quite good. The second course was artichoke and oyster soup. It was really tasty and had a lot of flavor and left me wanting more. For my entree, I had the redfish and it was just okay and didn't make much of an impression on me. It came with a side of broccoli and fresh mashed potatoes, which I really enjoyed. I was tempted to get the filet for my entree, until someone at a neighboring table told us to avoid it because it was practically raw and not good at all. The dessert was bread pudding with a bourbon sauce that was nice, but not good enough for me to finish.   I have to mention our waitress Katie. She was so nice and pleasant on what, I am sure, was a hectic day for her. She was extremely friendly, checked on our food when she saw it was taking a while and made our entire dining experience great. She was one of the highlights of the entire day.  I would say my visit here was probably a 3.5 and I'm rounding down a bit. I know it's hard to properly judge a place on a busy holiday, so I would probably come back for another try.

I recently attended a fundraiser here and this is such a gorgeous place!  Houses like this are what make New Orleans so unique. The entire house is decorated like any mansion should be decorated that was built in 1865- gorgeous antique furniture and art is everywhere and the wide open space makes it perfect for hosting a party.  The house and all of it's furnishings and art was actually donated to the Opera Guild in 1965.   The event I attended here was lovely. The Opera Guild staff did a good job of keeping everyone fed and entertained. I like that the house has a lot of space, so if there is a big crowd there is good flow and no one feels bunched up.  They are actually giving tours of the home every Monday until May 16th, 2016 so you don't have to wait for a fancy event to see the house for yourself.

Talk about a fantastic gift shop! I am redoing my kitchen- trust me you will be hearing more about this. Anyway, I stopped in here to find some kitchen goods and I seriously hit the jackpot. Not only did I find some fantastic shellacked oysters, but I found a really cool bottle opener that mounts on a wall. Give me all the things!  I know they have actual cooking classes, so I think I am going to come back and check that out.

This is a cool spot. There are a lot of nice and friendly people here and it was easy to find space at the bar.  The reason for this review is the awesome juke box. I was in the mood to play an "old fashioned" juke box (that means not an internet jukebox) and a friend suggested this place. The juke is pretty inexpensive and has a lot of good songs on it. I chose to play a lot of Louis Prima because it was just that kind of night.  A regular here mentioned to me that this is the place to be for Saints games, so I will have to come back and check the place out when the season starts.

Whoa. I don't understand all of the low reviews for this TJ Maxx!  This is a fairly new store- I think they built this new one at the same time that they built the new TJ Maxx on the Westbank. I stopped in here with a friend who was looking for some luggage that wouldn't break the bank. She ended up finding a nice piece of luggage that was perfect and well priced.  I browsed the women's clothing and housewares, but didn't find anything that I absolutely needed, but I found that they had a nice selection of seasonal clothing and a lot of good deals. We went in the middle of a weekday, so there weren't a lot of people in the store and the check out was easy. The cashiers were nice and we had no issues.  I'd return if I found myself in the area and in the need of a deal.

Lee Circle monument to Robert E. Lee, the Confederate General and is one of those classic New Orleans landmarks that locals probably pass all the time and don't even think about.  I didn't even realize you could review it! I have been looking up at this monument since I was a kid and there's just something about it that makes me proud to live in this city.  I don't know if there is much to say about it, other than that it's there and it's worth checking out, if you are visiting.

Well, I would tell you how this place is, but I have no idea.  We stopped in hoping to get a drink and a bite to eat (it's attached to New York pizza). There was no bartender and when someone came in from the connected restaurant to make a drink, he explained that he wasn't the bartender and couldn't serve us. Uh...ok.  We waited and waited and nothing happened, so we left. Swing and a miss. Maybe next time, but I doubt there will be a next time.

I like Best Buy. I really like Best Buy when they are having a huge sale.   They have a large selection of cell phones and other electronics, but what I usually get here are CDs and DVDs. Yes, I still listen to CDs. Does that mean I'm old? Whatever. They have sales all the time on CDs and DVDs and if you know what to look for, you can get some pretty cool deals.  I also like that during the holiday season, they have all of their holiday CDs and DVDs right in the front where you can find them.

So, it's a college bar. At least that's what the bartender told us. She said that most of the college kids were studying for finals (don't miss that) so that's why there weren't a lot of college kids when we stopped in.  I really dig this place. Nice little beer selection and a good crowd. Not too divey but not too fancy either. We stopped in here because my date had been bragging about his skee ball skills and this place has one of those old school skee ball games, which you can play for free. Not to brag, but I totally dominated at this game. Yep, all those years of training at Chuck E. Cheese (I went when it was called Showbiz Pizza) really paid off.  I'll be back for the skee ball alone. No smoking, which is always a win in this gal's book.

This is, by far, one of my favorite parades!  Fantastic throws and gorgeous floats.  I have collected so many of the little  Krewe D'Etat light up skulls over the years.  One of my favorite parts of Carnival.

What's not to love about Dollar Tree? As the name suggests- everything here is a dollar. I shop here a lot. I have purchased candy, cards, snacks, holiday decorations, arts and crafts, small gifts, fake flowers, gardening supplies, wrapping paper, not-so-great lotion, wine glasses and much more at this very store. What I like most about this store is the fact that most of the time all of the cash registers are open and the staff is fast and friendly about getting people through the lines. Also, there are always staff members walking around making sure that everything is neat, especially during the busy holiday season.  Pro tip: if possible, go in the middle of the day on a weekday because that's when the store is pretty much dead and you can get in and out in less than 10 minutes, if you know what you're looking for.

I really like this place! Checked out the Brassaholics here and although it was crowded, it was a lot of fun.  There was no cover or anything to get in. This place gets packed, so if you are going to see a band, you might want to go early.

It's been three years since I first tried HiVolt Coffee. As I was doing some Black Friday shopping in the area, I stumbled upon HiVolt Bakery- same coffee and this spot serves breakfast sandwiches and other noms.  I gotta say- my experience here was a lot better than my last at the other location. I stopped in to grab an iced coffee to go. The woman working was very nice and completed my order quickly. This shop is a bit small, but I like the ambiance and it doesn't feel as "sterile" as the other location.  The coffee was pretty good and I liked that I didn't have to add anything to it and I could just enjoy the coffee flavor minus the milk. I didn't get anything to eat this time, but HiVolt is now on my radar as a cute place for coffee and lunch.

This a such a cute shop! It's the perfect place to pick up a casual summer outfit and I found a nice long dress that was flowy and cool enough for summer.   When I was here, I met the owner Meghan and was impressed by everything this place has to offer. I love the long flowy skirts and the crop tops! I would say that the clothes here are great for a more relaxed look, when you don't want to wear jeans. They also have a nice collection of swimsuits with knitting on them, which I really liked. This is a great addition to this newly developed area in the city.

Pretty good PJ's with nice booths and free WiFi if you have work to do. I stopped in here to get my usual iced coffee and it was the usual good PJ's coffee that I really like.   My one complaint about the place is they wouldn't honor a coupon I had. They explained that the coupon could only be honored at certain locations, but there was nothing on the coupon that said that- it just said I could use it at any PJ's location. Anyway, I went to my regular PJ's a few days later and they not only honored the coupon, but they told me that it can be honored at any PJ's and the folks at this place screwed up. Long story short: the staff here didn't know what was going on. Other than that, the place is okay.

After reading Shercole's glowing review, I bookmarked this spot and made immediate plans to have lunch here.  I stopped in here on a late Sunday afternoon after doing some Metairie shopping. There was really no one here, but I was greeted with a smile and told that I could sit anywhere. Looking over the menu, I saw typical Greek food, but they also have other offerings such a lasagna and ravioli.   I decided to start with the Mediterranean hummus which came topped with olives, sun dried tomatoes and olives and a side of warm pita The serving was huge and it was really tasty. I liked that it wasn't doused with olive oil and the hummus was allowed to stand on it's own. For my entree I got the gyro wrap, which was a huge wrap that was packed with beef, lamb, lettuce, tomato, grilled peppers and onions. This wrap was delicious! I'm not a person who seeks out lamb, but I enjoy it when the opportunity presents itself and I really enjoyed it here. For my side I got the pasta and marinara, which was okay, but nothing spectacular.  Be aware that the Lebanese tea is nearly $4, which is a little pricier than other places. They did offer the 4 course lunch special on the day I was here, but it wasn't really Mediterranean food, so I decided to skip it. I would go back just for the hummus alone. I could have ordered that and another app and called it a day.

Third stop on the Metry bar crawl. Pretty cool place. Super friendly patrons.  The music was...interesting. Elvis mashed up with Eminem. Amy Winehouse mashed up with Queen. I gotta say, I didn't quite "get it", but eventually the horrible mash up music stopped and karaoke started. Everyone in our group had a really good time cheering on Joel, Dann, and John. They had some regulars who took the mic and they were really good. I could tell that the people here are all friends, which is awesome.  This was my final stop on the Metry bar crawl, and I would probably come back to this place if I were in the area.

Hey, do you ever go to a car dealership just to look around and end up buying a brand new car? Just me? Cool.  Well. that's exactly what happened when I went to Bohn Buick just to see what I had to see. My car was 11 years old and I'd been thinking about an upgrade. All I knew is that I didn't want another car- nope, I wanted to cruise around town in a sweet SUV. I found one I liked and the salesman, Wayne, let me take it for a test drive and gave me an overview of all the features. We did a little more talking and before I knew it, I had a brand new car in my possession. SCORE. "Hey, I deserve it.", I told myself.  Wayne was a fantastic salesman and worked with me to get the best deal possible. Scott also worked his magic to get me a deal and Ivan, the finance manager, made everything quick and painless as far as all of the paperwork was concerned.  My new car is super fancy-pants with wifi, a million radio stations and all this other cool stuff and Wayne showed me how all of it works and he was patient as he walked me through it and made sure that I understood everything. I love my new car and I love the experience that I had at Bohn Buick. My experiences with them have always been great and this time was no different.

I like this place a lot! I have seen more than one band here and have danced quite a few times upstairs to the DJ that plays.  The people here are always nice and friendly and it's a good crowd. One of the better music clubs on Frenchmen St.

I came here for lunch and I was pleasantly surprised by the entire experience.  We decided to get an order of shrimp and pork spring rolls and I got a vermicelli bowl with pork, since it was too warm for Pho. The spring rolls were tasty and got us off to a good start. My vermicelli bowl was PACKED- this is one of those places that is really generous with their bowls. The bowl was really good and the pork was cooked perfectly and had a lot of flavor.  We were in and out in about 30 minutes or so, so this is a really good place for a quick lunch.

This is a perfect little gift shop that I must have missed on past Magazine St. excursions.  Pop City offers a little bit of everything from NOLA inspired shirts to jewelry, sunglasses and other collectibles. I treated myself to a pair of earrings during my visit here that I can't wait to wear on an upcoming vacation. In the back, they have a nice selection of art for sale that was done by a local artist. The shop is very quaint and the woman working was quite nice and helped me explore the shop and find exactly what I was looking for.

Oh, Danny and Clydes, how I miss thee.  They FINALLY rebuilt in this spot, last year, after Hurricane Katrina killed the other gas station/convenience store that was here.  I love how shiny and new it is and the gas pumps actually work!  The gas is super cheap, because they are competing with the Race Trac on Lafayette (they are always the same price or 1 cent less).  The inside is nice, clean and big and they have a great selection of beer and snacks.  A good crowd goes in here, too.  I actually feel safe going here at night to fill up.  I admit that, yes, I have gotten chicken from Brothers.  It's cheap and good.  No, it's not Popeyes, and it can't compare to what Danny and Clydes once offered, but I'll take what I can get.    Thank you for rebuilding in this spot!!

Such a cute shop with a super friendly staff!  I was wandering Magazine when I came across this adorable stationary/card/all things paper store. The woman working explained to me that all of the designs are done by the owner and they are all so adorable. If you're looking for a Christmas or birthday card that's a little different or some stationary or thank you cards that have a little kick, than this is the place for you.  Everything is organized beautifully and it's all easy to find. They even have not so fancy necessities like sketch pads and graph paper and things of that nature. The woman working (I wish I had gotten her name, she was so friendly) told me that they will also have designed wrapping paper for the holidays, so I will be going back soon to see what they have and pick some up.  I felt so welcome when I was here and I will be purchasing some things from them soon. If you're stuck trying to figure out what to get someone for Christmas, head over here because you are bound to find something that will inspire you.

Only one other review that's over 3 years old? Uncalled for!  This is such a cute little jewelry shop. They carry all kinds of handmade jewelry like bracelet cuffs and necklaces.  The stuff they carry is extremely unique and I could see how a lot of this stuff would make great gifts.  Jen L. was right when she said that there is something for everyone here. They have cute little post earrings that would be perfect for a little girl who just got her ears pierced. They also have pretty little rings that any girl would love.
Flashing Gargoyles are always awesome.  The skulls didn't disappoint, either.  Another very generous crewe.  Catch of the night:  flashing gargoyles

This is a pretty basic sushi and Chinese place that serves it's purpose.  The decor is really no frills and is mainly set up as a take out joint, but that's fine. I grabbed a booth and picked a couple of rolls. I got the Naruto roll which was raw fish wrapped in cucumber and the New Orleans roll which was tuna, salmon and cream cheese topped with crab. The rolls were okay, but nothing spectacular. I was kind of annoyed because they kept falling apart has soon as I picked them up with my chopsticks- they weren't rolled tightly at all. The staff was super sweet and they were good about taking my order and getting the food out to me in a timely manner.  I'd probably order take out/delivery from here if I lived closer, but it's not worth a special trip.

I've never eaten here, but I did go here with friends to watch a Saints game and we had a pretty good time. They have a nice beer selection and although I didn't eat, the food does look pretty amazing. The place gets PACKED during Saints games with a good crowd that likes to have a good time. Because it is technically a restaurant, there is no smoking, so that's enough to make me want to hang out to watch Saints games while having a beer.  This isn't an authentic New Orleans experience, but it isn't bad for what it is.

Considering how close I live to Gattuso's, I have rarely made it here. In fact, up until last week I had only eaten here once and I barely remember that experience.  I stopped in here for lunch around 12:30 and the crowd wasn't bad at all. I think it must start thinning out around that time, since this is the "go to" for people coming from the court house and other businesses in the area.  For a starter, I got one of my favorites: fried pickles. They were really good, as I think it's probably hard to screw up something like that. For my entree I decided on the hamburger after my boy told me that it was really good here. While I probably wouldn't say that it was the best burger I have ever had, it didn't disappoint. I got it topped with cheddar cheese and it came with fries. It was huge and I was able to take half of it home to enjoy later and that's always a plus.  I really like how bright the dining room is here, during the day. Although all you get it a lovely view of the parking lot, it's still nice that there are a lot of big windows to let the light in.  On the weekends, Gattuso's has live music and they also have nightly drink specials including ladies night on Wednesday and pint night on Thursday.

It had been years since I had been here when I ended up here the other night.  Not much has changed, except on this particular night the place had a bit of a "club" vibe. I think the ownership has changed because what used to be a hole in the wall where you could grab a cheap burger is now a dark dance club type place. It is DEFINITELY different from the bar that Eddie described.  On this particular night, me and a friend were just in the mood to hang out somewhere and have a beer. The staff here is friendly and the bar is pretty nice. There are pool tables and a nice area with sofas if you aren't in the mood to hang at the bar. The crowd seems a bit younger than a typical Westbank place and the beer selection is decent.

Yes! I have been wanting to try this spot for the longest time and I finally made it in!  I have been making an effort to drink something green every day- my fridge is filled with green juice. I got the Amazing Greens smoothie, which is packed with greens, bananas, peaches and a whole lot of other goodies. It came out a really rich and bright green color and it tasted delightful. It had a bit of a tart flavor, but I could definitely taste the sweet of the fruits more than the veggies. I got a medium, but when I return, I will definitely get a small because it takes a while to sip and it warmed up because I was taking my time with it. There was a lot stuffed into this cup and it constituted a meal for me.  The store itself is really nice with a comfy seating area in the back with chairs and sofas. They made my smoothie quickly with barely a wait at all. I'm really glad I don't live close to this Jamba, because I would surely be broke within a month.

Sush-i-ri-tto! *clap clap clap clap clap* Sush-i-ri-tto! *clap clap clap clap clap*  When I heard that New Orleans was getting another poke restaurant I was pretty happy about it. For those of you who don't know what poke is: it's sushi's sexy cousin. It's a bowl of raw fish, veggies and other goodies. It's basically sushi salad or deconstructed sushi roll. I was excited to try Poke-Chan and then someone mentioned that you can build your own sushiritto here. A sushiritto is a big sushi roll packed with raw fish, rice and other yums and wrapped, burrito style, in seaweed and you eat it with your hands. As far as I know, Poke-Chan is one of the first, if not the only, place to offer it in New Orleans.  Needless to say, when I visited Poke-Chan I had sushiritto on the brain.
