It has taken me well over a week to write this review because that's how long it took me to wrap my head around how amazing this meal was. For a long time, Boucherie was on my short list of MUST try places in the city and I finally got to check this place out.  We made reservations ahead of time, and when we first walked in I was somewhat taken aback at how small the place is. We waited for our table by the door and a waiter was kind enough to get us a drink from the bar as we did so.  Once we were seated, we looked over the menu. Everything sounded incredible, but I had head really good things about the parmesan garlic fries so we HAD to start with that. Well, they definitely lived up to the hype they were cooked perfectly and covered in cheese. I think I am going to have to try to make them at home.  For my entree, I decided on the pulled pork cake with cabbage. It was AMAZING. The cake isn't super dense, so you will enjoy it without feeling as if you are stuffing yourself. The cabbage was a perfect compliment to the dish.   Because we decided to live dangerously, we got two desserts and split them both. We decided on the chocolate cake and the Krispy Kreme bread pudding. The chocolate cake was light and came topped with a huge dollop of whipped cream. The bread pudding was simply epic. Just when you think Krispy Kreme can't get any more delicious, they decide to make bread pudding with it. It was definitely decadent and not something I could do every day, but it was delicious.  Boucherie lived up to the hype and I will definitely be back.

I have been here a couple of times and have had a really good time here.  This is a neighborhood place and while it's not in the best area, if you are familiar with your surroundings or if you visit here with friends, you should be fine. I was here this past weekend for a dance party. The crowd was small, but it was still a lot of fun.    The bar is cash only and pretty basic when it comes to beer. A really chill place to hang out and unwind after a long day.

Everybody knows the main story behind the Make it Right project: Brad Pitt and a lot of other awesome people put their time and money into making sure the people of the lower 9th ward got the good hurricane proof housing that they deserve for an affordable price.  I recently was able to pass through and see for myself the work that has been done here. It's amazing. The houses are beautifully made and the lower 9th ward is more gorgeous than ever. The houses almost look like works of art. The houses are raised up and most of them have an area under the house for parking cars. A lot of the houses have solar panels on the roof in an effort to keep everything as "green" as possible.  I think that Make it Right is an amazing foundation and the work that they have done is to be admired. The people who took the time and money to do this for this community should be commended. It is my hope that other flood prone communities follow the lead of Make it Right and work to provide safe housing for their residents.

Today is the 10 year anniversary of Katrina, so I decided to spend the day doing happy New Orleans things.  One of the things on my list was to have a poboy at Domilise's. I had been wanting to try this place forever, and I figured today was as good a day as any, and I am always happy to support a small local place.  I stopped in around 2, figuring I would beat the lunch rush. I was very wrong. The long line told me that I wasn't the only one who had the idea of eating here today. I saw a free spot at the bar, ordered a drink and the bartender told me to take a number by the door and wait to be called. After waiting a few minutes, my number was called and I ordered a small dressed shrimp poboy. I sat at the bar and waited, and after about 10 minutes my number was called again, I got my food, the lady asked how many drinks would be on my tab (2), I paid and went back to the bar to eat. With me so far? Great.  The "small" poboy was indeed small, but it was packed with shrimp on really fresh bread and dressed to perfection. I was really hungry, so it didn't take me long to polish this thing off. While I wouldn't say it was the best shrimp poboy I have ever had, it was quite tasty and the shrimp were fried to crispy perfection.  A couple of notes: yes, the place is a no frills dive. The bar is packed with people who live in the neighborhood, there are pictures of regulars on the wall, and other "knick knacks". It's not fancy by any means, but when the food is good that doesn't matter. The prices are a little steep. I completely understand that this is a family business, and they have to keep the lights on, but $12 for a small shrimp po boy? Whoa! My entire lunch cost $20 before tip. I didn't mind paying that today, but that's not something I would do on the regular. The staff is extremely nice and the bartender was attentive and checked on me every few minutes to make sure that I had everything that I needed. All of the ladies cooking were nice as well and super patient with the crowd.  I liked it here. The people are nice and the food is good. I probably wouldn't trip over myself to return, but if someone suggested this place for lunch, I would definitely not fight them on it.

My dad and I stopped in here for lunch after I saw a few favorable posts about this restaurant. Truth be told, the thing that got me to make the long drive into "deep Marrero" was the promise of shrimp and grits. Someone posted that they had it on the menu here, and after confirming this for myself, we hit the road.  Like I said, we came for lunch and I'm not sure, but I think maybe the shrimp and grits is only a breakfast item. I was disappointed to see that the menu at the restaurant was completely different from the menu online. On the day I was here, the menu was just sandwiches and there was no shrimp and grits to be had. Dang.  I decided to get the grilled chicken sandwich which comes topped with bacon, lettuce and tomato and a side of fries. The sandwich was pretty good, although fairly small for the price. The chicken was juicy and it was nicely dressed and it made for a good lunch.  The atmosphere here is great. The bar area is big, the place has been beautifully renovated and I can tell that this is probably a nice spot to come for dinner or just have a glass of wine on a relaxing evening. I would give Cafe Bella another shot, just because I think they are still trying to figure out exactly what type of restaurant they want to be.

It's finally here!  So, for those that don't know, Que Rico! had long been touted as easily one of the best Cuban restaurants in the area. At the time, it was located in Slidell, and as badly as I wanted to dine there, I just never had the opportunity to make it out that way. This was a major bummer as all of the reviews and photos made Que Rico! sound like heaven.  Cut to a few months ago. Que Rico! was forced to close their Slidell location and it was rumored that they were considering opening a new location in New Orleans. Could this be a dream? If I could have easy access to the amazing food that I've heard raves about, I'd be on cloud nine. Then I got the word from a real estate friend of mine that the owner of Que Rico! had signed a lease to open on Magazine St. I had to keep the secret until they were ready to announce the big news, meanwhile my anticipation was at an all time high. They went to work restoring a space that was once a BBQ joint and I started stalking their Instagram and Facebook waiting on an announcement that they were ready to open for business.  The word finally came this week, and some friends and I made immediate plans to eat here as soon as possible. I was the only one who hadn't experienced Que Rico! for myself, so I was going in totally blind. When we got there the first thing I noticed was that the restaurant has been completely renovated. The inside is gorgeous and, although it's a smaller space, it doesn't feel cramped. Since it was my first time I was eager to try a few things.   Tostones a la Cubana: We started with this and I had never had it before. It's green plantains topped with roasted pork, cheese and olives. My description doesn't do it justice. It's delicious and a perfect starter.   Fried sweet plantains: These are always a favorite and I try to get them whenever I go to a Cuban restaurant. It's a simple dish, but so tasty. The version here is perfection.  Cubano: You know that if I came to a legit Cuban restaurant that I had to get a Cubano. I'm not exaggerating when I say that I think that this is the best one I have ever had. This was a huge sandwich with delicious pork cheese and pickles pressed into fresh bread. The cheese with melted into the meat perfectly and the sandwich was full of flavor. The pork was tender and juicy.   Cuban coffee: Finally, at the end of the meal, I had a Cuban coffee. This strong shot was the perfect end to my lunch. It was just sweet enough and had just enough of a caffeine punch to make me happy.  Service was excellent and Don made sure that we had everything that we needed. Everything was delicious and I can't wait to go back and try all that they have to offer.  New Orleans has definitely welcomed Que Rico! with open arms. We got there right when they opened for lunch and the small space quickly filled up. My hope is that anyone who enjoyed this restaurant in Slidell will visit their New Orleans location- it's worth the trip.

Come on.  What's not to love about Mardi Gras?  It's the greatest free party on earth and there are so many different levels to it!  You could play the role of the tourist: head on down to Bourbon St. and get crazy.  Fight the crowds, pay too much for drinks, do questionable things to get beads and you won't remember any of it until you get your credit card bill.  Awesome!!  You could play the role of the local (my choice): hit the Uptown parades such as Muses, Krewe d'Etat and Bacchus.  Hang out with your friends on the neutral ground.  Catch beads, picnic with friends, and have the best weekend you will have all year.  You could play the role of the family type: pack up the car and bring the kiddos to the suburbs (Westbank or Metairie) for a variety of family friendly parades that roll down the Westbank Expressway or Veterans!  A good time will be had by all as you catch beads and dance along with the dance teams and bands that march in the parades.  Sure there is traffic.  Sure there are crowds.  Sure some people get stupid.  But hey, it's only two weeks out of the whole year and it's part of the culture that makes New Orleans great.  DEAL WITH IT.  :)

Full disclosure: although I'm an adventurous eater, I'm not super familiar with Middle Eastern food. In fact, I have only been to Lebanon's Cafe once and Byblos a few times. So, when the boyfriend/man I'm seeing suggested Cleopatra's, I was down. He goes here a lot and tells me how good it is, so I figured it was worth a shot.  We went on a weeknight and walking in, I was kind of nervous. There was hardly anyone here for dinner, but then again, it is the Westbank on a Wednesday. For my drink I decided to try the Lebanese iced tea. It was pretty good and I would liken it to fruit punch more than tea, but I enjoyed it. For my entree I decided on the beef (it might be called 'gourmet') shwarma. It came with a side of rice, hummus and salad. It was all really good. I found the meat tender and full of flavor. The hummus was super good as was the salad. The rice was a little bland, but it wasn't terrible.  I would definitely go back! Because there wasn't a crowd, we were served fairly quickly and we didn't feel rushed.

I stopped in here with a minor issue on my new (to me) road bike and the staff was super nice and helpful and fixed the issue quickly. I had been in here before when I had issues with another bike and their advice was always solid and "did the trick".  Atmosphere is comfortable and the place isn't run by "bike snobs".

The Westbank has an Ulta! Fantastic!   Michelle was the first person to tell me that Ulta was coming to Oakwood, and I couldn't have been more excited. I got word that it finally opened, so I was eager to check it out.   For those of you not in the "know", Ulta is basically a huge beauty supply store. They have everything from drugstore brands to more upscale stuff. I saw on their website that they carry by favorite facial moisturizer so I headed down to check it out. They have EVERYTHING here. Not only did they have my moisturizer, but I also found some OPI nail polish that I really liked. They also carry designer perfume, hair styling stuff and pretty much anything else you could need beauty wise. I get the feeling I will be spending a lot of time and money here.

I was pretty excited when I heard that the Westbank was getting a We Dat's. I had heard raves about the chicken here and I was ready to dig in when David and I passed through for dinner on a Saturday night.  As soon as we walked in we were greeted with a cheerful, "Welcome to We Dat's!", which I loved. There were a good number of people here, but the line moved pretty fast. This is one of those "order at the counter" places and the food is served in "go boxes", so you can choose to stay and eat, or you can take your food and head out. We chose to eat here.  I got an order of the sweet heat chicken and it came with a pretty large order of fries. The drink options are soda fountain or bottled drinks and unfortunately there's no tap water. The bottled water is $2, so if you don't feel like paying that, you might want to get your food to go.  The chicken was great! It came covered in their delicious sweet heat sauce and it was cooked to perfection and nice and juicy. The sweet heat wasn't too spicy at all and it had good flavor, rather than just heat for heat's sake. The fries come with some sort of seasoning on them and I thought it was Tony's, but David thought it was something more than that. Whatever it was, I liked them a lot and the serving was plenty enough for two to share.  The food here was great and I'd definitely be back. Next time, I'll probably get my chicken to go just because I think that would probably be a little easier and I won't have to pay for water.

Since most of the reviews of this place are from out of towners, I urge you to ignore them. OK, I don't completely mean that, but I kinda do.  This is a fantastic restaurant. Me and the boyfriend had a date night here and the atmosphere was perfect and the staff was friendly. I decided on the red fish almondine, which came with potatoes and some kind of merliton dish. I'm not sure exactly what it was, but it was amazing. I think that MAYBE it was mixed with crab, but I'm not totally sure.  Yeah, no pictures because I was starving AND I was on a fantastic date and taking a picture was the last thing on my mind, so just trust me when I tell you that it was delicious and memorable. Oh! And it came with a choice of soup of the day or salad. I chose the salad, which is basically a garden salad, with the dressing of your choice.  Another touch I liked was fresh French bread and whipped butter right on the table. You can't go wrong with carbs and...hmm...whipped butter. All I know is that I was a happy camper when the bread came out.  Perfect date place. Fantastic and attentive waiter. Nice atmosphere. Minus one star because playing 80's pop music, in a place like this, just seems wrong. I will definitely be back.

Such a cute little pastry shop!  I didn't even know this place was here, until I was driving down Terry Parkway and noticed the sign. I made note of the name and did some research. I liked what I saw, so I decided to pop in and check it out for myself.  Upon entering, I was greeted immediately by the owner. It was a little later in the day, so a lot of the goodies had been snatched up, but there was a chocolate strawberry cake that caught my eye. After I got it home, I was delighted at how tasty and fresh it was. Yes, the strawberries were super fresh and the cake was light and melted in my mouth.  They have a nice selection of pastries here and, when I go back, I'm going to have to try some of their macaroons. I also saw some posts about a doberge cake that looks really good, so I'm eager to try that as well.  They serve different coffees, if you want some coffee with your dessert and, for the summer, they are also serving flavored teas. It sounds like the perfect way to beat the heat!

This is such a great little spot! While it isn't the fanciest place in the world, it's a really nice place to stop in, listen to some music and have a drink or two.  The place was pretty dead when we stopped in on Friday night, but the bartender was friendly and the band was good. The setup of the place is very odd- the band is located right next to the door, there is a small seating area across the from the band and then there's the bar. Everything is kind of squeezed in, but for what it is, it's a pretty good place.  This bar does serve Lucid "absinthe" and a few basic beers like High Life and stuff like that. There's a weird, dark seating area in the back that is kind of away from everything. I think vampires have their meetings back there or something.  All in all this place is a good time, and while it's not as "hopping" as some other music venues, it's worth checking out if you are in the neighborhood.

R&O is pretty legendary among the old NOLA crowd, yet I had never been. When my dad told me he was taking me here for lunch, of course I read over some reviews to get an idea of what I should get.  Okay, so I'll be the first to admit that I am not the biggest roast beef po boy fan. I like roast beef po boys enough, but I'll take a shrimp or oyster po boy over any other kind all day. In fact, I was raised to believe that the only *true* po boys are seafood po boys.  Anyway, we stopped in a little after the regular lunch hour and the place wasn't packed at all. There were a few people at tables, but it wasn't crazy. Walking in, this spot definitely feels like old New Orleans. I can't really describe what that means- it could be the old, aging tables and chairs or the out-of-date feel to the place. Whatever it was, I immediately liked it!  One of Yelp NOLA's roast beef po boy connoisseurs had mentioned in his review to get the cheese and gravy fries and a roast beef poboy, so that's exactly what I did. When the cheese and gravy fries came out, I was really beside myself. They really don't hold back on the good stuff around here- a nice pile of fries topped with cheddar cheese and gravy with big chunks of roast beef on top. I could have easily made this my meal and forgot all about the po boy, but alas there was more eating to do.   The roast beef po boy looked delicious and the photo I took doesn't do it justice at all. It was a fully dressed roast beef poboy soaked with brown gravy all on fresh French bread. I already knew that this was going to be a messy experience, so I just dove right in. The flavors in this sandwich are incredible. This isn't just some roast beef that someone threw in a pot for a few hours- it's been seasoned to perfection and tastes just like homemade. The gravy is generous and yes, you will make a mess, but it's so worth it. I will likely never get another roast beef poboy anywhere else, because I'm sure that it can't be as good as the one here. I will drive my "the only true po boy is a seafood po boy" self to R&O just to get the roast beef po boy here.  R&O didn't disappoint at all and although the service could have been a little better (our waiter did a lot of chit chatting when we needed drink refills and the check), I will be returning to this New Orleans institution soon.

I have passed this place so many times over the past few years and I finally decided that it was time to stop in and see what it was all about. Although I have had Caribbean food before, I'll admit that I'm not as "schooled" in it as I am other cuisines. I went into Island Paradise with an open mind and excited to try a few things that I hadn't had before and sample some old familiar favorites.  For my lunch, I knew immediately that I wanted to start with Traditional Trini Doubles- which is made with two pieces of flat fried dough filled with curried chickpeas, peppers and chutneys. This is one of the foods I had never had before, so I was going in blind.  also ordered the Paradise jerk chicken with a side of Dhalpouri roti and I also indulged in some cornbread and sweet plantains.  All of the food here is made to order, but my patience definitely paid off when an incredible spread of food was laid out in front of me. The first thing that I tried was the Trini Doubles and it was fantastic! I loved that the baras (fried dough) was nice and light and the filling was tasty with a lot of flavor. In this version, you can get it with or without peppers. I got it with peppers and I found it to be the perfect combination of savory and spicy. It was my first experience, and I liked it so much that I am already planning to order it again on my next visit. Next, I dug into the jerk chicken and Dhalpouri roti. I love jerk chicken and the version here didn't disappoint. Island Paradise serves up a large piece of juicy and flavorful chicken topped with a sauce that was sweet and complimented the dish well. The Dhalpouri roti was traditional flatbread served with Island Paradise's Trinidadian potato curry. This was a dish that had some really good spice to it and I loved it! I feel like a lot of restaurants are afraid to really serve well-spiced dishes, but I'm happy to report that Island Paradise doesn't cut any corners when it comes to flavors. The cornbread went wonderfully with everything and the sweet plantains were perfection. Fun fact about me: sweet plantains is one of my all-time favorite foods and I order it whenever I see it on a menu.  A line on Island Paradise's menu reads, "Where the island meets the mainland." and my experience here reflected that mantra perfectly. If you're looking for traditional Caribbean food in a bright atmosphere served by friendly people, then this is the spot for you.

I had heard some raves about this place, but I was skeptical because $14 for a catfish platter just seemed like a lot to me. Well, I'm here to eat my words...and some delicious catfish.  I stopped in here for lunch and we were told to sit anywhere. The place is large and gorgeous and made to handle big crowds. Lucky for me, I came for a late lunch, so the place was pretty empty. After hearing all of the "oohs and aahs" about the catfish platter, I decided to go for it. My two sides were the veggie of the day, green beans, and I also had some red beans and rice because it was a Monday and those are the rules. We also started with some nice spinach dip and some complimentary corn bread was brought out to the table.  The spinach dip was great! It was a generous serving, served super hot with really salty chips, exactly how it's supposed to be served. The catfish platter came out and I was impressed. There were four nice-size pieces of catfish piled up in between my sides. The catfish was nicely battered, but the batter didn't compromise the flavor of the fish. The fish was thick cut and juicy and it was really fresh with a lot of flavor. The green beans were good and the red beans and rice were delicious. They were perfectly spiced (even though I added come Crystal sauce, because I always do) and the tasty cornbread went nicely with the entire meal.  Staff was friendly, even though the food took a while because it's all cooked to order. I didn't mind waiting a little longer for fresh cooked food, so that wasn't an issue. I am definitely going to have to get back over there and try the chicken, because I've also heard that their chicken is beyond good.

I was going to start off this review with a spiffy quote from Romeo and Juliet, but I think I'm going to save that for my Montague review.  I was in the area and it was well past lunchtime when I realized I was starving. A quick search revealed this place and, although I had heard something about it, I didn't know much when I decided to have lunch here.  As I said it was late, so the huge space was mostly empty except for a few people enjoying some drinks at the bar. This is a "walk up and order" type of place, so after looking over the menu, I decided on a chicken salad sandwich. This spot mostly has sandwiches and I think that they also have a few breakfast items.  The sandwich was great! There was a super generous serving of chicken on it, to the point where it was falling off, so that's always a plus with me. It wasn't "mayo heavy" like other chicken salad tends to be and the bread was perfect- I think it was buttered before it was toasted. The chicken itself was tender and juicy with a lot of flavor and I thought that the craisins were a really nice touch. I always love additions that you might never think to add, but turn out to be perfect.  Capulet is mainly an event space, so they are closed by 3 every day and they are completely closed on weekends. It's basically the perfect spot to grab breakfast and lunch on a work day. If I lived in the neighborhood I know that I would probably be here all the time.

The Commissary got a unique start. Managed by Geordie Brower, Sarah Brennan, Richard Brennan III and Matthew Pettus, the space opened in the midst of the coronavirus pandemic, at the end of April. The original plan was to open as a market and dining space where the public could enjoy Dickie Brennan and Co. signature dishes easily. That plan was temporarily put on hold so that The Commissary could offer free family meals to front-line workers and to those out of work and in need.  New Orleans is currently in phase 2; eating at restaurants is allowed, but with capacity restrictions. Your best bet is to get Dickie Brennan and Co,'s delectable dishes to-go. The Commissary is offering a daily lunch menu for dine-in or takeout, as well as an array of prepared Dickie Brennan and Co. classics that can be easily reheated and served at home.  The eatery menu includes such selections as Green Goddess Salad ($13), Gator on a Stick ($11), Smash Patty Burger ($10), Smoked Catfish Dip ($7) and Pimento Cheese with crackers ($7).  One of the things that I'm most excited about is the market menu. Turtle soup and gumbo are both available by the pint ($7) or quart ($13). If you have ever had the family's famous turtle soup or gumbo, you know how special it is to have this on hand for a special occasion or just a quick warm-up dinner.  For my visit, I ordered the Creole Cuban sandwich, mac and cheese and fried Brussels sprouts.  Creole Cuban Sandwich ($12)- The menu describes this as tasso, pork debris, mayo, creole mustard, house pickles, bolilo, but I would just describe it as amazingly good! This isn't what I would call a "classic" Cuban, but I love the flakey bread and the generous pork- tender, soft and well marinated. The sandwich itself is very soft, but sturdy, and doesn't fall apart with each bite. Of course, it was perfectly pressed and it came with kettle chips, which were a nice crunchy addition.  Mac and Cheese ($5)- I'm a huge mac and cheese person and I like to try the concoction whenever it's offered. The Commissary's version is made with penne noodles and thick, rich cheese sauce. It has that fantastic "gooey" texture that you expect from really good mac and cheese. Because it's a cheese sauce, every noodle is perfectly coated inside and out, making for a decadent experience that you are going to want to share.  Fried Brussels Sprouts ($4) - If you aren't usually a sprouts fan, I'd encourage you to give these a try. They're lightly fried in a Crystal honey sauce and they are full of flavor with just enough spice. The outside leaves have that nice fried "crisp" to them, which makes for a solid bite, while the inside is still tender.  Decadent Dickie Brennan and Co. food available to-go is a real dream come true. If you do decide to dine in, The Commissary is taking full safety precautions and has spaced out seating inside and outside of the restaurant, and all of those working were masked.  *Portions of this review was originally written, by me, for Very Local New Orleans. Read the full story here: https://nola.verylocal.com/now-you-can-get-the-brennans-experience-to-go-at-uptowns-new-commissary-eatery/156903/

I was pretty shocked that the cemetery had zero reviews. It's pretty nice, located in the middle of a neighborhood. I stopped in here to take a few photos from my personal use. I was astonished at how many of the graves were older, some of the last burials in them took place in the 30s and 40s.   For the most part, the graves are well kempt in the number one cemetery, but in the number two cemetery, it's a different story. In the number two cemetery, graves are falling into disrepair, just because a lot of time has passed and the families have likely died off. That's not to say anything bad about New Orleans Catholic cemeteries, which maintains the properties. I enjoyed walking through both spaces, and I enjoyed the quiet of all of it.

Cavan is a new addition to the Magazine restaurant scene and after hearing raves, I couldn't wait to try it.  We made reservations a few days before and we were only able to get in at 9:30, so make your reservations early. When we arrived we were immediately seated at a lovely table in the downstairs area. The restaurant is in a house that has been renovated and I like that it still has the feel of being in an old house. You sit in lovely chairs with an antique feel and there are even a couple of sofas with tables where you can eat. The upholstery is a rich red and the decor of the rest of the space makes for a romantic feel.  As for the food, we started with the fried oysters and the raw oysters. The fried oysters came lightly fried on a nice toast. They had a lot of flavor and I enjoyed them. The raw oysters were amazing. I don't know what it is, but these are the most unique raw oysters I have ever had. They weren't as salty or big as some other oysters I've had, but they were extremely juicy and the cocktail sauce they were served with complimented them perfectly.  For my entree, I had the seared gulf fish that came with shaved fennel and white bean salad. The portion was nice and the fish was perfectly cooked, but not so much that it lost the flavor. It was a little cool in the middle, which I liked. The white bean salad was served cold and provided a crisp balance to the entire dish.  For dessert we decided to get a couple of Irish coffees, which was some of the best Irish coffee I have ever had in my life. It was real Irish coffee and not some overly sweet concoction that some bars might serve. It was a great end to the meal.  I loved my experience here and I would absolutely return. The wait staff was attentive and kept our drinks poured and made sure that we had everything that we needed and that we were satisfied.

After waiting MONTHS to come here, I finally make it and I'm faced with disappointment. Come on, man!  First, I LOVED the small diner feel of the place. I loved that it felt very old New Orleans. The waitress was SUPER sweet. All of that was great. The food...um. I started with the seafood gumbo. Question: have y'all ever had seafood gumbo before? Because the gumbo here sucks. Seriously. It contained exactly two (2) shrimp, had NO rice and no flavor.  None. I had to add a TON of Crystal sauce to it to get any kind of flavor out of it. I would go so far as to say that if you think the gumbo here is good, you have never had good seafood gumbo in your life. Never. Ever. Period. End of story. I could make better and baby, I am no cook. The place has 4 Yelp stars total, so maybe it was an off night.  For my entree, I got the oyster dinner which came with garlic parmesean fries. The fries were decent but the oysters were nothing special. I've seriously had better oysters on a random oyster poboy in the Quarter. I'm not trying to be difficult. I really wanted to like this place. You really have no idea (I brought someone here that I was trying to impress with my restaurant picking skills and failed miserably. He was completely underwhelmed with his shrimp.). I've been waiting to go here for months and I am beyond disappointed that I wasn't more impressed with this place. Thank God I had Brocato's after to save the night.  In short: staff was nice, atmosphere was nice, food is sub par.

It's time for an update and I am declaring Cleopatra the best lunch spot in town!  I know those are some big words, but I stand by them. Cleopatra consistently offers delicious, fresh and fast lunch at a price that's almost criminal. They have an entire lunch menu of options, but I usually get the beef shawarma plate which comes with hummus, rice, pita, a good size salad and pickled vegetables, all for $10 before tip. This sounds like a lot of food, because it is. These are generous "dinner sized" portions of delicious, fresh food and you can't beat the price.  I also like this spot because they know that if you're here for lunch on a weekday, you have to get back to work, so you get the food fast. You'd think quality would suffer, but it doesn't at all. It comes out hot and delicious.   This is a family owned place and service is always excellent and the owners take pride in their restaurant and it shows. I love the food here and I really need to make of eating here more often.

This is a gorgeous fancy shop for people who still hand write letters and appreciate the finer things.  We stopped in here just to look around and WOW- they have gorgeous things here. I loved the ink pens that you have to actually fill with ink. They have ink wells containing inks of all different colors: different shades of blue, greens and coppers really blew me away.  They also sell a large assortment of fancy magnifying glasses with beautiful silver handles and gorgeous wrapping paper and stationary. If you are looking for a unique gift for a writer in your life, Papier Plume should be your first and last stop.  The store owner was extremely welcoming and asked where we were from and if we needed help with anything. I also heard her telling other people to "enjoy the city", which I love from any store proprietor, especially one in the French Quarter.

Can't really say much about this place because I popped in and out so quickly that I didn't even have a chance to order a drink.  So, why am I bothering to review it? Well, we stopped in to see what's what and pretty much use the restroom. Although we weren't paying for anything the staff was super friendly and nice and the people hanging out here seemed nice too.  I'm sure I'll be back at some point.

This is SUCH a cool store.  More Fun is a must visit for any comic book fan or collector.  They have anything you could want and they take subscriptions, if you want your comics to arrive in perfect condition.  They carry everything from DVDs to action figures and everything in between.  If it's something comic book or collectable you are looking for, then this should definitely be your first (and probably only) stop.    Bonus points from me because I was able to find really cool books about pinups here!

I'm updating this review mainly because I MUST remember to stop coming here when Wok to Go is closed. I don't know what has happened, but the food is just awful- it has no flavor and the only good thing about it is that it's cheap. I used to get take out from this spot all the time, but the last few times I did, I couldn't even finish what I was eating.  Tonight I got the Moo Goo Gai Pan and I took a few bites and I was done. It comes with shrimp fried rice and an egg roll- both of those were decent, but the rest of the dish was inedible. I can usually power through something, even if it's not that good, but I didn't even want to bother wasting the calories by eating it all. I had some of the rice and the egg roll and that was that.  I get that it's a hole in the wall place and most, if not all, of their food comes from a bag, but this was just bad. Never again.

Owner Jason Tournillon has created a perfect spot at The Backyard, a place that truly does live up to its name with a big backyard area that's perfect for drinking beer and relaxing on a nice day.  As far as the food goes, The Backyard keeps it simple with that summer barbecue vibe. You'll find sandwiches like brisket, pulled pork, turkey, chicken and sausage, as well as a burger and hot dog on the menu. Sides are simple but classic with fries, tater tots, potato salad and slaw.  While most barbecue places have a platter option, The Backyard is all about the sandwiches. I went with the pulled pork sandwich ($10), which comes topped with The Backyard's chimmi-slaw. I like to get two sides in these situations, so I opted for the tater tots ($3) and the Muffuletta Deviled Eggs ($6), which are technically an appetizer but I wanted to mix it up.  The sandwich was great and The Backyard's famed "not sweet" BBQ sauce was a perfect touch. The portion of pork was generous and the slaw did a good job of adding a crisp bite to the sandwich. The deviled eggs were so unique! Made with olive salad and topped with crisp genoa salami, I think this is a "must try" appetizer.  This place was made for summer. Who wouldn't want to munch down on a tasty sandwich while enjoying a beer in someone else's backyard? Let the folks here handle the grill, you just relax.  I made a list of best hidden BBQ for Very Local New Orleans and this l restaurant was on it! Read it here:https://nola.verylocal.com/bbq-new-orleans/228292/

I seriously don't want to let the cat out of the bag about this spot, because I kind of like that only a few select people seem to know about it, but I want to let y'all know about this awesome place.  One of my biggest complaints about Westbank bars is 1) They all seem to be stuck in the 70's and 80's as far as decor and clientele. 2) They are so smoky that going to one means you'll have to take two showers as soon as you leave. Bad Wolf has solved both of these problems.  They dub themselves a "nerd bar" and that's because they have nightly events where you can come and play in video and board game tournaments. You can also rent board games for a few dollars (they have a huge selection), they have pinball and the whole place is decked out as a "everything nerdy" person's dream.   Even though I'm not cool enough to dub myself a nerd, I liked this place a lot because it's smoke free, the staff is really friendly and the vibe is laid back. David and I were here around 10 on a Saturday night and there were only a few people here. PERFECT. We sat at the bar and chatted and took in the scene. As someone else mentioned, they have a list of specialty cocktails and they have a pretty awesome beer selection, which made me happy since I'm a beer drinker. So, we have a smoke free bar with awesome people AND good beer. Yeah, you know I'll be back.  We didn't rent any games to play this time, but we'll definitely be doing that in the future and I know that David wants to get his hands on their pinball machines, so we're going to bring quarters next time we decide to stop in.

Long Chim is a cozy little Thai cafe, currently offering weekend takeout from their Uptown location.  Looking over the menu, I saw a couple of familiar classics such as dumplings and Tom Yum soup, but other dishes, such as the Unicorn Noodles, intrigued me. I was curious and ready to dig in.  I started with some Butterfly Pea Tea, which is a bright purple tea made with butterfly pea flowers. Popular in Thailand, the flowers are edible and are believed to have antioxidant properties. It was crisp and refreshing and had a subtle flavor that I enjoyed.  For my appetizer, I had an order of the pork and shrimp dumplings that put Long Chim on the map. These four, handmade dumplings were tender and soft served in a nice wrap with pork and tasty shrimp. The dumplings also come packed with shitake, water chestnut, carrot and are topped with scallions and ginger garlic soy sauce. The dumplings are full of savory flavor and the scallions add a nice little crunch.  For my entrée, I just knew I had to try the Yum Woon Sen, also known as Unicorn Noodles with pork and shrimp. This dish has earned its unique name, because owner May Mananya soaks glass noodles in butterfly tea overnight, dying the noodles a purple color. The dish also contains shallots, Chinese celery, cherry tomatoes, chili, garlic and soy lime dressing. The noodles are gluten-free and vegan if you choose to get them with mushrooms in lieu of meat.  I ordered the noodles with medium spice, and this was the perfect level for me. The purple noodles are certainly eye-catching, but the taste is what stands out here. The pork and shrimp are juicy and tender and I like that the soy lime dressing adds an interesting salty kick.  Finally, for dessert, I was eager to try the mango sticky rice. This is the most popular dessert in Thailand. The rice in Long Chim's version is soaked in butterfly tea, and a coconut cream sauce, leaving the rice an intriguing bright blue, gooey and very soft and sweet. It was the perfect end to the meal.  This was originally part of an article written by me for Very Local New Orleans. Click here to read more: https://nola.verylocal.com/long-chim-brings-a-taste-of-thailands-street-food-to-the-crescent-city/162986/

I've been to the Convention Center many times over the years. It's a great space: large enough to accommodate a full Mardi Gras parade and it's revelers, if that gives you any idea.  Most recently I attended NOLA Christmas Fest here and I just loved the way it was all laid out, even though we parked in the lot way at the other end and had to walk to where we were going. The staff at the Convention Center is always helpful and they're good at telling you where you need to be and when.   My only complaint is that I wish there was more parking around the convention center. You have a few choices: park in the big lot by the Riverwalk or park across Tchoupitoulas in the lot they have over there. It can't be helped, but that's the only drawback of this otherwise great space.

I'm updating because if you are going to go here, you are gonna want to get the speciality rolls.  Now I know.  I've had the playboy roll, Buddha belly roll and the St Charles roll.  All three were fantastic and about $15 each, but they are really big and enough for two people.  So, yeah this place is pretty awesome.

I hit the drive thru today to grab a strawberry margarita. I got the Big Kahuna 44oz for $8.  You can't beat it- pour what you want in a cup and freeze the rest.   We're in Covid-mode and the drive thru window had a safety screen and the woman who served me put on fresh gloves to do so. I was impressed.   Drink was great and just what I was in the mood for. Great spot!

Being an Entergy customer is like being in an abusive relationship.  Entergy totally mistreats you.  The power will go out for no reason and for 5 hours at a time.    I'm sorry, Entergy.  Is it something I said?  I won't make you mad again.  I promise.  But you can't leave Entergy because there's no one else out there.  So, you settle and decide that this is life now.  Losing power willy nilly and for no reason.  Just go limp and accept it.  One star because Entergy is a step up from candlelight and another star because I'm typing this on a computer powered by electricity that Entergy is providing.

There are probably some "pros" to parking in this lot, but I'm at a loss.  So, they got rid of the parking lot workers, but also raised the prices. In other words, you have to pay MORE to use a machine to park. I hate using a machine to park because that means my time in the lot is limited. I would rather just park and come back and pay a human for however long I was in there. With that being said- I parked for 3 hours and came back after 3 hours and wasn't ticketed or bothered. I guess I win.

I don't know if I could anything about this place that hasn't already been said.  It's not such a bad place, but it seems a little out of place on Bourbon St. I feel as if it's trying to be a little more upscale, and that's hard to pull off when you are surrounded by strip clubs and souvenir shops.   I think that the first thing I noticed about S&S is that the inside of it looks like a brothel. There's red velvet everywhere and it has a "peep show" kind of feel. Oddly enough, I kind of got the feeling that they modeled some of the decor after One Eyed Jack's, but maybe I'm insane. There wasn't anything overly great about the service, but the staff was really friendly, nice and accomodating and went above in beyond in making us feel welcome.  I might go back if I were in the area, but that's not really likely.

This place is fantastic and the staff is amazing at what they do! They have 40+ reviews and a solid 5 stars for a reason!  I was sent here by Morgan to get my hair done all 40's style for a photo shoot to promote the upcoming Fly Away With Yelp party at the World War II museum. I love everything 40's and 50's, so I was excited to see what the staff would come up with.  When you think 40's hair, your first instinct is to go for the Victory Rolls (and I love them, too) but Nicole and the rest of the staff at Maison De Cheveux had something a little different in mind. They decided on a dry set where they curled all of my hair with a curling iron and worked it into a gorgeous 40's wave updo. I loved it!  Considering how complicated the style was, they got it done pretty quickly (a little over an hour) and the results lasted throughout the photo shoot and for the rest of the day! They had me wishing that I had a fancy place to go and show off my pretty hairstyle after the shoot.  The crew here definitely knows what they are doing when it comes to hair and I would recommend Maison De Cheveux to anyone who wants to have their hair done all fancy for a party, special occasion or night out on the town.

The sculpture garden at the New Orleans Museum of Art is one of New Orleans' hidden treasures.  Located behind the museum, near City Park, the garden is free to visit and the sculptures are ever changing and when you visit you almost feel as if you are in another world.  There is a body of water that goes through the garden and you can actually go on a gondola ride!  This is a great place to just come and relax and reflect and enjoy the scenery.  It's very quiet and peaceful and I think it would be fantastic to come here after a long day and just walk around or even on a date.  I have been to a few events in the Sculpture Garden over the years and it's a lovely place to have a party. A few years ago I was fortunate enough to see a live production of "A Midsummer Night's Dream" and the garden provided the perfect back drop for this particular production. Because this spot is free, it's a great place to enjoy a nice afternoon and just relax.

This is a review of the beer/bar area and not the food.  We stopped in here on Mardi Gras, just to check it out and try out the beer. The downstairs area was pretty crowded, so we headed upstairs and snagged a seat at the bar. I would say that Crescent City Brewhouse is more of a restaurant than a brewhouse- they only offer four beers, but nonetheless, i was eager to try what they had. I decided to try the Red Stallion and the Imperial Pilsner. Both were pretty good. They didn't knock my socks off, but they were enjoyable.  The bartender was really nice and worked fast to take our order. The menu looked good, so I might try the food if I make it back.

Cucos is a chain, and when you go with a chain you are gonna get chain food.  Nothing here is overly spectacular.  When I go, I get the chicken nachos which aren't too bad.  The chips and salsa are also pretty good, but when it's free, it's hard to rate a restaurant on that.  I've also gotten the taco salad here which was underwhelming.  I don't know.  I guess I'm a snob when it comes to Mexican food.  I like it to be more on the authentic side.    If you want run of the mill "Mexican" food, then this is your place.  If you are looking for something a little more authentic, check out La Fiesta on Stumpf.

It was the end of a long day of French Quarter Festing when we decided that the sun and the walking had gotten to be a little too much and we needed some serious food. This was more hunger than a sample from a fest booth could handle, so we wandered over to Port of Call, since I had never been and my PIC insisted that I try it.  We got here around 5 and, of course, there was a line. However, we decided to just wait for a spot at the bar to open up because I actually like sitting at the bar, and who wants to wait an hour for dinner? Sure enough, after waiting about 20 minutes, we were happily seated at the bar and ordering our food.  I got the cheeseburger topped with everything, including a nice pile of cheese and I got the baked potato topped with everything including bacon bits. The cheeseburger was delicious! Granted, I am speaking from the vantage point of someone who was starving, but I found it very fresh, cooked perfectly and "hype" worthy. The baked potato was good as well, but I think next time I won't get bacon bits only because they didn't really "do it" for me.  The staff here is super friendly and cool and, considering the crowd they are dealing with, they get to you really fast- we didn't have to wait to order once we were ready. Although Company Burger still holds onto it's spot for "Marielle's favorite NOLA burger",  I will definitely be back to Port of Call. I have yet to try one of those monsoons- once I made it here after FQF I was no longer in the mood for sugary drinks. Next time.

40 Arpent is a fantastic little brewery quickly adding to the landscape of the Louisiana beer scene.  Set in Arabi,  this family owned brewery has really taken off in the last few months. It's still a small operation, compared to other breweries, but I can see them going places. I think my two favorite beers from 40 Arpent are the Creole Red Bean and Rice Ale, which tastes a lot better than it sounds and the Copasaw Wheat which is packs a lot of flavor.    I'm really excited to see what 40 Arpent does next.

Such a nice theater! We ended up seeing a sketch comedy show here in which the players performed a short skit about all 50 states. It was great! I am a huge comedy fan and I absolutely love improv and sketch comedy, so I know that I will make more of a point to see shows here.  The space itself is pretty small, but I actually like the intimate feel and there was plenty of seating and space for everyone. A man working mentioned that they are adding a bar area soon, so I'm sure that will be a draw for some people. I look forward to seeing more shows at TNM and having a good laugh.

Phillips is definitely one of the nicer places on Maple St.  When you go in, you feel as if you are in a high end place.  I have never been in here when it has been packed and it isn't packed with college kids like the other places.  There is a nice older crowd here and although the drinks are a little more expensive, it's worth it if you don't have to deal with a huge crowd.  Phillips also has pool tables and nice seating areas for groups, if you don't want to sit at the bar.  The lighting is dim and cozy and the music isn't super loud, so you can have a conversation.

I had heard a little about Echo's when I ended up close enough to stop in for lunch.  The place is pretty basic: you walk in, sit anywhere and then get up and order once you've figured out what you're in the mood for. I got an order of fried zucchini and the margherita pizza with pepperoni added.  The fried zucchini was different, but good. It was lightly battered but it still retained the zucchini flavor, if that makes sense. The margherita was pretty good, even if it didn't knock my socks off. The pizza is "brick oven/thin crust" kind and it came topped with tomato sauce, mozzarella, basil and grana for $9.50. The pepperoni was another $3. Sadly, part of the bottom of the pizza was burnt and one slice was nearly inedible (I didn't discover this until I brought my pizza leftovers home). Honestly, the rest of the pizza was fine, but I'm not sure it was worth the price. I'm used to pizza places that give you a little bang for your buck and I didn't find that here. Also, while I usually like just ordering at the counter, I found that inconvenient here and I wonder if it's because it was lunch and the place was pretty much empty and they didn't want to be bothered with coming to me to take my order.  The pizza will likely satisfy a craving, but I think prices are a little steep for what you get and for the quality of the pie.

Besides the fact that it's my dream to one day be married here, St Louis Cathedral is one of the most recognized landmarks in the City of New Orleans.  This gorgeous church is located near Jackson Square, and is a symbol and the center, of New Orleans' predominantly Catholic faith.  No matter your religion, you should have no trouble recognizing the beauty of this iconic structure.  Who could forget the poignant moment, after Hurricane Katrina, when President George W. Bush addressed our nation in front of the Cathedral?  The hands on the church's clock face were frozen in place at the very time the city lost power and the lives of it's people were forever changed.  That is one of the moments that I don't think I will ever forget.  Whether you are Catholic or not, a local or a visitor, next time you are in the area, stop into the Cathedral and light a candle.  Maybe say a prayer.  You might be a little better for it.

I'm not sure how long this shop has been here, but since I'm always in the market to shop at new (to me) lingerie shops, I was happy to discover this spot on a recent outing.  Basics is anything but basic- they have a lovely selection of "every day" bras and underwear as well as things that are a little fancier for the times when you want to mix it up. I happened to be in the market for a strapless bra, and Basics had a lot of options. The staff was helpful and friendly, and although I haven't purchased anything yet, I will be back when I am ready to make my move.  In the adjoining room they have a fantastic selection of swim and workout wear that is sure to make anyone feel fancy on their next trip to the gym. One thing that I especially liked about this shop is the attention to personal details- they had lotions and body sprays along with clothing and I like that for times when you want to pamper yourself all the way.

A new pho place popped up on my radar, so you know I had to check it out.  Pho Kang is located in the same building that used to house Pho Orchid. Someone said that they thought it was the same place, with a different name, but I'm not sure. I stopped in for lunch and there was no one else in here. I started with an order of grilled pork spring rolls and Vietnamese coffee and I got a regular bowl of rare beef and brisket pho for my entree.  The spring rolls were excellent- packed with fresh ingredients and the pork didn't have a weird grill after taste that I've noticed that it has elsewhere. The pho was great! The regular bowl was small and the perfect size for lunch and the meat was generous and the broth was flavorful. I really enjoyed it and it's one of the better "new" bowls that I have tried lately.  Service is fast and friendly, making this a great lunch stop.

I've been sitting on this review for a week and I think that I am going to go with 3.25 stars.  I really like this place. It has a cool atmosphere and the staff is super attentive and friendly. I went in and I was told to just seat myself. It's an "informal" kind of atmosphere; the menus are in a bucket on the table along with the forks and knives, which was oddly off putting..   I wasn't super hungry, so I just decided on a bowl of mac and cheese which was $5. It was really good, and if I go back that is probably what I will get. Looking over the menu, the sandwiches just seem kind of expensive to me., I caught a glimpse of other people's and they didn't look like anything overly special. I know I have to actually try one for myself. Maybe I am really missing out, but I was happy with my mac and cheese and that was that.

I went to Tchoup Yard last night to check out, what I envision will be, the hottest new bar of the summer.  One thing I liked as soon as I got here was the parking- there's a huge lot right next to the place, so you don't have to worry about stumbling around in the dark looking for your car in heels- perfect. As soon as we walked in, we immediately noticed that the crowd was a young college crowd and we were probably some of the oldest people in the place by at least 8 years. I'm not sure if this is going to be a regular thing; I think once word gets out about the place there will be a good mix of different types of folks here. The bar was nicely packed at 9 on a Saturday and we were happy to find a table somewhat close to the bar. I can tell they are still working out the "kinks" of the place, but I like that the drinks are served in frozen goblets, they have a good beer selection, they have frozen margaritas on tap (and they are actually good!), and the bartenders are fast.  Even though we started at a table, we moved and sat at the bar as soon as there was space. It was a pretty warm night, and although they have some ceiling fans at the bar itself, it was still hot. I can't imagine how this place is going to feel once summer really kicks in. I would suggest maybe a few industrial fans out in the "garden" part of the bar, in order to keep the air moving.  One thing you should realize going in: the entire bar is outside. The bar itself is covered and then there is a huge patio with tables and chairs and I think they are going to have food trucks nightly. I can see Tchoup Yard being a lot of fun once the cooler weather kicks in- I look forward to enjoying a beer here on a crisp fall evening.

It seems like we have gotten to the point where a new brewery opens in New Orleans every month. Trust me, I'm not complaining- I love supporting local beer endeavors.  We stopped in here during their grand opening weekend and the place was hopping. I decided to start with their Express Yourself IPA. Hoppy and good, it was everything I like in an IPA, but still light enough to enjoy a few of them. The other beer I really enjoyed was their stout, The Lucy. For a stout, it wasn't heavy at all and while I was wishing that it was a little bit more on the "rich" side, I found it quite tasty. David isn't much of a beer drinker, so upon the suggestion of the bartender he got a Rooibos Alt, which is a tea infused beer. He really enjoyed it and I sneaked a sip and found it really good and light and pretty much the perfect summer beer.  They are going to have food trucks regularly serving food, they have a great patio, they are going to have guest beers and they are literally just a few steps away from The Joint, so I am sure that Parleaux is going to be a summer destination for many a local beer lover. I like the friendly, laid back vibe of the place and it's the perfect spot to pass a good time. I'll be back.

Yay! This place is so cool. I love the whole setup of it. The bar itself does turn and that's a little weird, but it turns slowly and you get used to it after a few minutes. There is a huge sitting area where you can watch a live band. I think that there was a jazz singer the night that I went.  The bartenders are super fast and work really well with the moving bar. I guess they have to in order to work there. I had a "fancy" drink, which was a Ramos gin fizz. It was really good and kind of tasted like cake. I'm usually not big on drinks with hard liquor in them, but this one impressed me.  I wish I could have stayed longer, but it's a hotel bar and it's not open super late. I will definitely go earlier next time so that I can get a more extensive experience.

I love a fancy house that has been converted into a hotel! There is just something so cozy about a place like that and when you step into the Cornstalk you feel as if you are stepping into a castle in a far away land.  We occupied a room downstairs and it was small, but gorgeous. The room was complete with gorgeous wall paper, an antique style phone and old books. The decor of the entire hotel is just lovely and has a beautiful antique feel. We were bouncing around the entire hotel taking pictures and exploring, and the staff was really nice and accommodating. My only complaint is that there was some kind of construction being done right outside the window of our room and it was a little loud.  My favorite spot in the entire place was upstairs. There is a nice balcony space where you can step out and look over the garden area and it's just lovely. I would recommend anyone on vacation (or stay-cation) give this place a shot.

I'm always a fan of art that's a little different and Frenchy fits that category in the best way.  I had the opportunity to stop in here and meet the artist and I was blown away by all of his different types of art work. Full of color and open to interpretation, I like that his work is in a different style than a "typical" New Orleans artist and you can tell that he pulls his inspiration from the city, but it's art that anyone can relate to, no matter where they are from. His gallery itself has a warehouse feel but is splashed with paintings from the more abstract to gorgeous portraits of NOLA musicians Dr John, Allen Toussaint and James Booker. I like that his portraits swirl with color and that Frenchy is not afraid to "paint outside the lines".  Frenchy himself was very friendly and open and happy to talk about his art. Maybe someday I will own an original.

Meh.  This used to be a cute little low key hang out, but during the school year it's a full blown college bar packed with college kids (of course).  They do have drink specials, but the drinks shrink with the specials.  For $2.50 you will get a little more than a thimble full of beer.  I really wish I had taken a picture.  It's a joke.  There are way better places on Maple St.  Go there.

Elizabeth is an amazing photographer and so fun to work with! She brings her professionalism and her dedication to every shoot. She works with you to create a vision that you will cherish for years to come. I love how her photos have an "retro" feel to them and a little bit of edge. The images she and I created looked as if they were straight out of the 50's. You won't be disappointed.

I finally made it to this New Orleans institution and I couldn't be more pleased with my experience.  We went at around 1 and by then the lunch crowd had died down, so we were quickly seated. Everything on the menu looked so good and you can get an assortment of things like poboys, seafood platters and spaghetti.  I decided to start with the turtle soup. While it wasn't bad, it's not on the level of a place like Commander's Palace. It had good flavor, but they kind of went easy on the turtle, if that makes any kind of sense. For my entree, I got the fried oyster platter and that came with fries. I LOVE fried oysters and any place that offers a fried oyster platter is good in my book. The oysters were AMAZING. I actually loved that they were a little smaller, which allowed me to eat the whole thing in one bite and not cut it in half.  I will definitely return to Mandina's and will be adding it to my list of recommended places to visit when living in/visiting New Orleans.

Okay, so when I told a friend of mine I had never been to Phil's Grill he looked at me like I was insane and then he dragged me here (in the best way possible), so that I could taste the delicious that Phil had on his grill.  I liked this place immediately because there is table service. Somewhere along the line going to a burger place starting meaning you were going to be placing your order at the counter, so it was nice to be able to sit and chill whilst I decided what I wanted. The process is cool and I won't bore you with the deets, but you mark on the paper what type of burger you want, how you want it cooked and what you want on it.  I ordered the gator burger with cheddar cheese, lettuce, tomatoes and pickles and I got fried pickles on the side. I LOVE gator anything and I was excited to find out what Phil's gator tasted like. Well, it was perfect. I liked that it wasn't too gamey, but it was still tasty and juicy. The burger itself was pretty big, but not so big that you can't finish it in one sitting. My toppings were a nice addition and I like that you can "build your own" burger with as little or as much as you want. The fried pickles were okay, but a little mushy.   I have to go back for one reason: the bison burger. My date had the bison and all of my friends told me that I have to get the bison burger next time, so I guess that's what I'm getting. Mob rules.

This place has a little bit of everything. It feels like you are sorting through someone's garage with the way things are organized, but I like that there is a lot to look at and it's well priced. You'll find a little bit of everything here: candlesticks, lamps, old salt and pepper shakers, furniture, clocks, art, etc. Anything you can imagine when you hear the word "knick knack" is for sale at this place. I was happy to see that the prices are reasonable, compared to other shops.   The basic idea of this store is to come and get things that you can maybe repurpose into something you can use. Don't come expecting the items to be in "perfect" condition, although I did find the furniture to be in great shape.

Finally got to try this place after my boyfriend had been raving about it.  Talk about fantastic!  The place is small, but it has an upscale "diner" feel.  I ordered the "Cubano", which was their take on a Cuban sandwich.  My boyfriend got a pastrami sandwich that looked delicious!  We had table service, which my boyfriend told me was new.  We went kind of late (around 10) and the place only had a few people in it, as it closes at 11.  We will definitely be going back!

Yessss! Why did it take so long for New Orleans to get a fancy milkshake shop?  As soon as I saw the delicious photos from this new spot, I knew I had to check it out. David and I popped in to see what was shakin'. I really love the concept: you pick your ice cream "base" from a lot of different choices, you pick what goes on the outside of your cup (peanuts, sprinkles, candy, etc.), you pick your drizzle for inside the cup, then you pick your toppings.  I chose butter pecan ice cream as my base, with caramel drizzle inside, peanuts on the cup and pretzel sticks and gummy worms as my topping. Yes, I basically made myself a dang sundae in a cup, but I wanted to "ease into" the process. I loved my concoction and it was enough for me and David to share. It was A LOT of sugar and I think if I had one all to myself I'd probably pass out or something.  I went pretty conservative on my milkshake making, but you can add pop tarts and cookies to your dessert, if that's your thing. When I go back, I might try to go a little crazier, but I was pleased with what I came up with. The milkshake is a little pricey at $11, but it's a nice "once in a while" type of treat.

Wow.  I had no idea that I ate so much Mexican food, but this is my like my fifth Mexican restaurant review.  Anyway...La Fiesta isn't a place that looks like much from the outside.  Ok, it doesn't look like much inside, either.  I'm pretty sure that this is a house that has been converted to a restaurant.  But, don't let looks fool you.    The food here is awesome.  I would brand this as close to "authentic" Mexican food as it gets (correct me if I'm wrong).  My favorite is either a burrito or a chorta (I think...the thing with the cheese and meat sauce).  Everything I have eaten here has been awesome and prices are reasonable.    A definite "must try" if you find yourself on the Westbank.

This store is okay, but a lot of the clothing seems like it's a "throwback" to about 8 years ago when Affliction and short shorts were all the rage.  The women's clothing selection at this store is pretty thin, especially for summer. As I said, short shorts seem to be the big thing. They also have tank tops and a small swimsuit selection. The men's selection isn't much better with a wide selection of Affliction shirts and other dated "graphic" tees. On the day that we were here they had some men's jeans on sale and the styles are nice and this is pretty much the only thing I would consider purchasing here.

Did you know that Trashy Diva is known worldwide for their clothing and that people from all over the country covet Trashy Diva dresses? Did you know that we are super lucky to have Trashy Diva RIGHT HERE in New Orleans?  I love Trashy Diva! Why? Because I am a big fan of the whole retro style in general. I love dressing up and being fancy for no reason and having people wonder why I am wearing such a fancy dress. I love feeling pretty and girly. If you are like me, then Trashy Diva is a must.  So many gorgeous dresses that look like they were pulled straight out of the 40's and 50's. It's basically vintage clothing without the mothball smell. Whether you need a gorgeous dress for a night out or something more casual for work, this is going to be your one stop shop.  Oh! And Trashy Diva just added a nice lingerie add on to their store, so you can pick up fancy bras, panties, stockings and other sexy accessories at the same time you are picking out a gorgeous dress.  Check out the website to get an idea of what the store has to offer!

What can I say? It's a Starbucks and if you've been to one, you've been to them all.  My "go to's" for Starbucks are always the peppermint mocha frappucino or the pumpkin spice frapp, when it's in season. I stop in here when I am looking for a dessert type of drink and I don't think I have ever actually had real coffee here, now that I think about it.  This is a nice location that usually has people coming and going all day, since it's located on a busy part of Manhattan.

El Libre has been on my "must try" list ever since they opened and man oh man, this place did not disappoint.  The restaurant is completely no frills: order at the counter and sit upstairs or downstairs to eat. I decided to get the Cubano (obviously) with a side of avocado salad. The Cubano is out of this world. I really think I have finally found the best Cuban sandwich in NOLA and I am not exaggerating. I know I'm not an expert, but I just loved that the sandwich was nicely pressed and the bread was tasty and flaky. It was really a "melt in your mouth" experience for me.  The avocado salad is BEYOND good. Fresh avocado, cilantro and corn mixed up into a bowl of yum! It was the perfect side and I am stealing this simple idea for a salad and I'm going to start making it at home. It was basically guacamole before it's "mole'd" and I couldn't get enough of it.  I also got a Cuban coffee, which was a small shot of tasty coffee that was strong without leaving me jittery. It had a lot of flavor and I didn't need to add anything to it to make it enjoyable.  The staff here was super friendly and chatty, even though they were having a busy day. I will absolutely return!   Note to El Libre owners: PLEASE open one on the Westbank or Uptown!

I couldn't wait to review this exquisite gallery.  We were wandering on Royal when the beautiful art in the window caught our eye. We walked in and were greeted by a delightful woman who was more than happy to chat with us and show us around. The art here is beautiful, and is mostly French artists.  One of the exceptions is an artist named Matthew Peck. David and I were taken aback by his unique style and his paintings that look like photographs and that actually glow when the lights are dimmed. His work is spectacular, and just the fact that we were able to discover this artist is enough for me to give this gallery 5 stars. Obtaining a print of his work has jumped to the top of our "to do" list.  There are gorgeous works by many artists in this gallery, so if you're in the area don't hesitate to stop in.

It's a Burger King.  How do you review a Burger King?  They are all the same.    Well, it's number 3 for a reason.  The food is "meh", even when it's the best it's ever been.  Whoppers aren't big anymore and the fries can't compare to McD's.  They do a good breakfast and I do come here to get my favorite: a croissanwich with the little bite size hash browns.

I think I've decided to dub 2014 "the year of the re-review". I haven't been too good about posting re reviews and now that I am in my 4th year of Yelp-dom, I think it's only appropriate that I make it a point to re-review places that I haven't been to in a while or that have changed ratings. This review falls into both categories.  I hadn't been to Mikimoto in years when I decided to stop in for dinner. We were immediately seated and looking over the menu and there was a lot that sounded really good. I've made it a point to try the special rolls at sushi places, because I feel that this is where the restaurant and the sushi chef are really allowed to shine.  I decided on the Deluxe roll, the Crescent City roll and a California roll, just for good measure. I think the Deluxe roll was my favorite. It was a really big roll with cream cheese, snow crab, tuna, salmon, avocado and eel sauce on top. You really get a lot of flavor here, as well as a good "bang" for your buck. The Crescent City Roll- snow crab, spicy crawfish, tempura, avocado, green onion and shrimp was good, but it was definitely out shined by the Deluxe roll. The Cali roll was pretty typical and made for a nice small treat in between the big rolls.  Once again, the staff was really nice and friendly and the food was really good (no warm rolls this time). I will return and try more of the many rolls that they have to offer.

Out of all of the AMC theaters, this one is probably my favorite.  First of all, I love that it's located in a mall, so that you can go window shopping, if you are waiting for your showtime to come up.  Also, the upstairs (where the theaters are) is huge.  They have a huge concession area where you can sit and talk and eat your snacks before or after the movie.  The seats themselves are the most comfortable of all three AMC theaters (the AMC on the Westbank has the worst ones, in my opinion).  The theaters always seem clean and they manage crowds well (if you are going to a popular movie, they put you in a line while you wait for seating to start.  I've found that this prevents chaos.

I miss the Saenger so much and can't wait for it to reopen!  I have seen so many different shows here since I was a child.  They used to have a ballet every year that I can remember going to see on  field trips.  I also saw "Grease" here (starring Frankie Avalon, himself) when it was traveling around the country.  I think that my favorite show was, by far, when Alanis Morissette acoustic show I saw here about 2 months before Katrina.  She was touring her "Jagged Little Pill" acoustic album.  The show was really nice, because only the bottom part of the theatre was filled.  This was done on purpose so that the show had a more intimate feel.   The theatre itself is lovely, and from what I have heard will be absolutely gorgeous after the renovations are complete.  I can't wait to once again enjoy a show at the Saenger.

I'm usually against re reviewing unless my experience has changed drastically, but I'm updating anyway. This place has been a solid "meh" for the 3 years since my last review.  Look, here's the deal, when I am in the mood for cheap Mexican that ISN'T Taco Bell, I usually just go here. Seeing as how it's the 4th of July and America is a melting pot, I decided to check this place out today for lunch. I ordered the flauta combo with the beans and rice. It's all microwaved. All of it. They know it. I know it. Let's not pretend this is in any way authentic or fresh but hey, my lunch was $8 before tax and tip, so maybe I decided to look the other way and just enjoy it for what it is.  Long story short: don't go here for authentic Mexican. Go here because it's better than Taco Bell and still has the same decor it's had since it opened in 1981.

I might as well add my review of this New Orleans staple to the pile.  Pat O's is the place that every tourist wants to go because they have heard about the legendary hurricane, how strong it is, and how it goes down easy.  You already know that.  Easily, my favorite part of Pat O's isn't the hurricanes, it's actually the people.  Yeah, like you!  Whenever I go here I always make a bee line for the piano bar.  Two players banging out requests as the crowd sings along with them. Oh, the hurricanes might bring 'em in, but the piano bar will bring 'em back.  I don't think I have ever seen them stumped.  You could probably request a Lil Wayne song and they'd play it by ear for you.    The Christmas party that happens every Christmas night is legendary.  Everyone is there.  You better dress to impress, because you are guaranteed to run into old friends (and enemies, and exes) that you haven't thought about in years.  The bartenders are the best in the biz and they are always friendly.  After all, they get to work at one of the most famous bars in the country.  Years ago (right after Katrina), I briefly dated a bartender at Pat O's.  He explained to me that working there was a privilege and you can understand what he meant as soon as you walk in the door.

Here's another sushi place that I wouldn't go out of my way to go to, but the food wasn't too bad.  I've kind of made it my mission to try a new sushi place whenever I can.  When I went to this place, what immediately leaped out to me was how friendly the staff was.  We went kind of late, and they were about 30 minutes from closing, but they didn't shoot us away or rush us.  The food was good...typical sushi.  The one thing that kind of gave me pause...I ordered a roll that is normally served kind of cool.  Well, they had just finished making the rice for it, so when I popped it into my mouth it was warm...and I was expecting it to be cold.  I don't know, I just remember that as being as jarring experience.  LOL.    I'd definitely go back.

This is my definite favorite, when it comes to Uptown Mexican food.  There are a few reasons to like this restaurant:  1) Location.  It's located Uptown.  That means less traffic then downtown.  This Felipe's has it's own parking lot, so, depending on the time of day, you don't have to worry about street parking.  2) Good food.  The food here is consistently fresh, good, and of course, made to order.  I have never ordered anything here that I wasn't satisfied with.  3) Price.  It's cheap!  I had a burrito tonight, and it was 5 bucks!  With prices like that, you can mix and match.  Get a burrito, a couple of tacos, and a margarita and you will pay less than $20.  My date and I each got a burrito and two drinks each, last night.  The total bill was $35!  You can't beat that deal with a stick!  4) Service.  If you want to avoid the line, sit at the bar, get a drink, and order your meal from the bartender.  Just be sure to tip him or her well at the end of the night.  I always forget about this Felipe's and it's convenience, but I'm going to be sure to visit more in the future.

When this place fell off the planet a few years ago, I was really bummed.
