There used to be one right by my house and I loved going there when I was in the mood for inexpensive pasta that wasn't the Olive Garden.  When I heard that there was one at Clearview Mall, I couldn't wait to check it out.  Of course, you know when I went, I just had to get my favorite which is the muffaletta pasta.  Yummy penne pasta with strips of ham and salami topped with olive salad, mozzarella, and olive oil.  Sure, it's not the healthiest thing on the menu, but it is definitely my favorite.  After Katrina, they had taken it off of their menu, for whatever reason, and I was so bummed.  Well, it was fabulous and it was just as I had remembered.  The chicken quesadilla pasta is also really good, if you are in the mood for something a little spicier.  Sure, it's a mall restaurant, but give it a chance.  The food is good, not too expensive and the service is great!  I will definitely be going back!

I spent the better part of the Saints 2009 season in this place watching the Saints on the road to the Super Bowl.  This is a great neighborhood bar full of awesome locals.  It's a fabulous place to watch games because they have a huge projector screen and the place gets PACKED for not only football games, but futbol games as well!  Also, I LOVE how "into it" the fans here get.   On Saints game days, you can bring a dish in the theme of whoever the Saints are playing (ie: Saints vs Falcons="dirty bird" stew).  They also serve traditional Irish faire (the owners are Irish...as in FROM Ireland) and they have game nights.  It's just a great place all around, and whether you are local or a tourist, you will definitely be made to feel welcome here.  Fun fact: on the facebook page for this place, they let you know that it's time to come watch the game with the simple phrase, "the biscuits are in the oven!"

This is a review coming from someone who doesn't smoke or vape. I basically stopped in because we were sight seeing along Canal Street and I always wondered what this shop was about.  Well, mystery solved: it's a head shop. Here you can find a wide selection of pretty glass pipes, vape stuff, incense, and other things you can inhale/inhale things out of. The pipes they sell are actually really pretty and I got a nice picture of some of the ones they had in the display case.  Along with all of that, they sell long flowy flower and tie dye dresses, t shirts, hats, bags and other accessories. Even though I am sure me and my boyfriend looked like a couple of square fish out of water, the woman working greeted us with a smile and told us to let her know if we needed anything.  If you are into clothing that is tie dyed or a little different or if you are in the need of vape/tobacco products, this is the place for you.

It was my first time here and it wasn't even for something Saints related! I actually went to the free REO Speedwagon show here and I had a great time. Oh, I'm gonna keep on lovin' you!  This is a great spot. For this concert, it wasn't super packed so we got to get pretty close to the stage. I like that the area is nicely paved, and for this particular show, they had an assortment of food trucks as well as trucks that were selling beer and daiquiris. The drinks are a little pricey, but that's not a big deal when you are here for an event. Security was out in force, so we felt safe and we had a really good time. Oh, and bonus points for super nice restrooms!  I definitely want to go back and get the full experience right before a Saints game. I imagine that that's a lot of fun.

You know, it's strange.  Pizza is the one thing that I never think to get at a sit down place.  Whenever I do go for pizza, I usually pick Rotolo's because that's the place I'm most familiar with.  When a friend mentioned this place for lunch, I was eager to give it a try.  The first thing that impressed me was the size of the place.  It's really big, so if you have a large group they can easily accommodate you.  The have an extensive menu of all kinds of pizzas from pepperoni to cheese to chicken.  They also have sandwiches, if you are in the mood for something non pizza related.  My friend and I got some cheese sticks (they were actually more like cheese boats- split sticks with cheese in them) that were really good.  We got the "Hawaii Five O" pizza, which comes topped with ham and pineapple.  I had never had pizza with pineapple, but it was actually really good!  The pineapple cooks down, so it's not super sweet or overpowering.  I would love to head back to this place and check out one of the sandwiches.

It was a cold and rainy night, but since I love Mardi Gras and parades, I braved the weather and David and I headed out to my first Nyx parade.  I was excited- I have been wanting to see Nyx since it's inception, but for whatever reason I had never made it. This was the night! The crowd wasn't crazy at all because, you know, all of the rain, but the parade was gorgeous and the throws were generous. As for the best part: I caught a Nyx purse! Purses are their signature throw that are decorated by krewe members. Mission: accomplished. I was so excited to get one on my first try and it now sits among the rest of my Mardi Gras treasures from years gone by.  I'll definitely be making this parade a yearly "must", I just hope the weather is a little nicer next year.

Another New Orleans classic, I can remember when this place first opened.  I went to the Aquarium a few months ago for the 10 year anniversary celebration.  I hadn't been in a really long time, and I somehow remembered it being bigger.  No bother.  It was a lot of fun.    I think my favorite was probably the HUGE tank full of sharks and the big school of fish swimming around and around.  There are a lot of fun attractions for kids and they have a really cute gift shop, if you want to buy yourself a memory.

I don't get out to nearly enough pizza places, so when I had an opportunity to try Pizza Domenica, I jumped at it.  Walking in, the setup at PD is a little odd. You order your first "course" at the counter and then take a number, sit at your table and wait for it to be delivered. Then you can order more at your table, if you like.  We started with the garlic knots, because that seemed to be a favorite of past reviewers. They came with an interesting cheese dip on the side that was deceivingly light. It was almost like super light cottage cheese (but not as clumpy). It was good, but like another reviewer said, I would have been just as pleased with some marinara on the side. The cheese didn't have as much flavor as I was expecting.    For our pizza we got the Tutto Carne, which came topped with salami and sausage. I liked it a lot. Because the pies are made in a wood oven, the crust has a nice smoky flavor to it. I also like that the pizza is thin crust, so you can eat a bit of it and not feel gross when you're done.  They have a nice beer list, although I didn't partake and their cocktail menu seems to be quite large as well.  All in all I enjoyed my experience here. It might not be my very first choice for pizza, but I was not left disappointed in the least.

We met some friends for some drinks at this nice little cocktail bar. I like the loungey area and it's a good spot for mingling and we were here llater in the evening, so it wasn't busy at all. I wasn't in much of a cocktail mood on the night I was here, so I decided to get some local beer, of which they had a nice selection.  I would love to go back and actually try some cocktails, because the ones that my friends were enjoying looked really good. Although, I always like finding "fancy" type places that aren't afraid to serve beer (and local beer at that!).

I'm always on the search for good, semi-authentic and inexpensive Mexican food.  This place came close on 2 out of three of those points.  The atmosphere is very "bare bones".  It's basically just a little Mexican diner with "family" style seating in one large, brightly lit room.  They have a wide variety of breakfast, lunch, and dinner choices, which include your basic Mexican faire of burritos, tacos, flautas, etc.  The chips and salsa are complimentary, but the chips aren't served warm (I don't know why they couldn't pop them in a hot oven for 3 or 4 minutes) and the salsas were really watery.  I decided to get a burrito with pork.  It was really big, but it was also really greasy.  I don't know if that's just because the pork was greasy, but the tortilla was so soaked with grease, that it was falling apart.  It wasn't bad, but it wasn't the best I've ever had, either and honestly, I didn't finish it because it was so greasy.  The person I was with had three tacos with black beans and rice.  That looked really good, and if I go back, I think I'll try that.  I would probably go back for lunch or something, but I doubt I would make this a dinner destination, again.

I was in the area, so I stopped in here and picked up a few things. This isn't the cleanest Family Dollar, and when I was here they were out of a few basic items and some of the things weren't clearly priced. As with other Family Dollars, they have typical household basics but I was confused as to why only one line was open in the middle of a busy day. This place is good in a pinch, but not worth the trip if you're looking for something specific.

I love seeing a show at the House of Blues.  I have seen a few bands here, but what I have mainly seen here are burlesque shows.  The House of Blues has a "house" Burlesque troupe called Bustout Burlesque, that performs once a month.  Every year, the House also plays host to the New Orleans Burlesque festival and welcomes performers from all over the country.  It's a weekend packed with fantastic shows by some of the most beautiful and talented women in the world.  Last summer, Dita Von Teese, arguably the biggest name in Burlesque today, performed 2 sold out shows to an intimate audience.

This is a really nice store in the Quarter, that actually reminded me a little of Trashy Diva.  They have long and short fashion dresses as well as nice boutique items. I would say that a lot of the stuff here is perfect for a night out on the town or just any day when you feel like dressing up and feeling pretty.  They also carry fashionable lingerie and shoes.

The snow ball stand exploration continues! This time we decided to check out an old Algiers favorite: Van's. Van's is probably the oldest snowball stand on the Westbank. They have been serving the sweet stuff since the 70's, they have every flavor under the sun and they have extra goodies like nachos and hot dogs.  I got my usual rainbow (I know that sounds boring, but every stand has a different version) and David got Dream Cream (ehh...). Mine was great! It had a lot of flavor without being overly sweet and I finished more than half of my medium/$2.50 snowball. David liked the Dream Cream, so we both left satisfied. The ice isn't the finest I have ever had, but it held the syrup well. I like that there's a picnic table in a shaded area on the property, so you can enjoy your treat on site. The hours on here say they close at 7, but I think they serve snowballs as long as they have customers, and last week they had customers well past 7:30.

I finally made it back to the Saenger since the reopen, so it's time for a re-review.  I was so excited to see all of the renovations when we decided to go see Bill Burr here last week. We were fortunate enough to get "club" tickets, so it was fancy pants all the way. In the club area lounge there was a nice setup of finger sandwiches, a cheese plate, meatballs and cookies. The club area also offers discounted drinks and a lovely area for sitting and relaxing before and during the show. The club lounge is open throughout the show and the show on stage is broadcast on a tv in the lounge, so that you don't miss any of the action.  The venue itself is gorgeous. There are plenty of concession areas and everything has been beautifully refurbished from top to bottom. I love that there is staff everywhere you turn just to help you in case you get lost or need help finding something.  The performance area is gorgeous. You would never believe that the Saenger was completely destoyed by Hurricane Katrina and has been completely redone. I love the carpet that has "Saenger" on it, I even took a picture!  I would suggest you get to the Saenger theater as soon as you can. It is an amazing, gorgeous theater and I am so glad it's back. I can't wait to see more shows here.

My friend Scott and I decided to stop here on our way to some Uptown parades.  I had never been here before, so I was excited to try it.  The first thing that impressed me was the fantastic selection of different sandwiches and wraps.  They have everything from chicken to tuna to vegetarian options.  They also have salads.     I'm not sure what Scott ordered, but he decided to go with a "small"  (6 inch) pressed sandwich.  I decided on a "small" chicken caesar wrap.  I really liked mine, and Scott and I both agreed that it was a good snack.  If I were to go back, I would definitely get a "large", because the small is good for a little munch, but if you are looking for an actual meal, then you are going to want a little bit more.    It's a good healthy option, if you are in the mood for a sandwich that isn't a po boy.

Yum! So, just a FYI: this truck if more for snacks than an actual meal. They offer a few egg rolls and a few dumplings of different types. I didn't snap a picture of the menu, mainly because it changes all the time, so you are going to have to track them down and see it for yourself.  I got a Reuben egg roll and some steamed pork dumplings. The egg roll was really good and I enjoyed it. The dumplings (3) were perfect and came with a nice sauce for dipping. I kind of wish that two egg rolls came to an order, but I'll just order more next time. I caught up with this truck at Courtyard Brewery and it's hot salty goodness was the perfect snack to go with a cold beer.  I do wish that they were a little bit cheaper. One egg roll is $4 and an order of 3 dumplings is $6, but I'm still giving 4 stars because they are upfront about their prices and the food is good, especially when you are starving.

This was a neat little restaurant on the lake that we just happened to stumble upon for lunch.  We stopped in, and although it was lunch time, the place wasn't packed at all and we were immediately seated in the "Al Hirt" booth (apparently Al was a regular at this place, so he gets his own booth complete with plaque!).  Everything looked amazing, but I decided on the catfish amadine which came with corn bread, corn grits and creamed spinach. It was amazing! The fish was fried to a nice crispy brown, the spinach was delicious and the corn grits were buttery and full of flavor. I could have probably eaten another serving of them!  Our waitress was extremely nice and friendly and made sure that we had everything that we needed. I would definitely return.

After enjoying a really rich dinner at N7, my boyfriend and I decided to stop here for a little dessert.  Bittersweet Confections is one of the stands located in the St. Roch Market. It's perfect to "pop in" and just grab something sweet, because it's right inside when you walk in and conveniently located next to Coast Roast coffee. We decided to get a couple of the strawberry cupcakes. Not only were they fresh, but they were DELICIOUS. I'm usually disappointed by strawberry cupcakes, because they usually only give you a little hint of strawberry, but this cupcake delivered with it's strawberry filling! Oh yeah, it was filled and I had no idea until I bit into it. It was a pretty fantastic surprise.  BC offers all kinds of goodies and I will definitely come back and try some more. This is the perfect addition to the market.

I really liked this store with their nice selection and reasonable prices. I will agree that there was no acknowledgement when I walked in, but that's not a big deal.  I was impressed at the prices at some of the really nice items. They had a black sequin dress, that would be perfect for a fancy night out on the town, and it was only $70. They had other cute dresses and skirts that were in the $30 range. I didn't see anything that appealed to me on this visit, but Mirabella is on my radar and I'll be visiting them again.

I don't usually make a point of reviewing disposal companies, but this company deserves extra props.  I was at a big, major event this weekend and River Parish provided the "port o pottys". This weren't your typical port o pottys, they were basically trailers with a full bathroom setup complete with stalls and sinks for washing hands. The reason I felt the need to review is because they stayed on top of everything for the entire event. There was plenty of toilet paper, the stalls were CLEAN, and everything was wiped down. It really felt cleaner than a lot of regular bathrooms I've been in in this city. I always stress when I go to outdoor events because I loathe port o pottys (I know. I'm weird. I just really hate them.), so when I saw this little setup I was happy.  Hire these people for your next big event and you won't be disappointed.

Rivertown had a lot of potential. In a lot of ways, it still does.  When you walk/drive through Rivertown, you feel like you are in a small town. You pass museums, a nice theater, houses and shops. I think that the main problem is it is located at the end of the world. Of course, when I say that, I mean that it is so far outside the New Orleans city limits that no one really thinks about it and those that do really aren't interested in making that long drive.  I did enjoy it when Oktoberfest was in Rivertown. There was a lot of room and it didn't feel as cramped as it had at the old location, but sadly that is the only good thing I can say about the area. I think that if the powers that be made a concerted effort to draw people out to Rivertown (maybe a festival other than Oktoberfest or a concert series of some sort) than people would be a lot more willing to give this area a try.

I finally made it over this way to try Truburger.  With that said, I wasn't left overly impressed. You go in and place your order. I decided on the single with bacon and cheese. My friend got a double with cheese and bacon and we split an order of onion rings. We ordered, we sat down and we waited. The place wasn't overly busy for a Sunday afternoon, so we had our order in about 5 minutes.  The burger wasn't bad at all, but it wasn't anything really special. I found it kind of small and the flavor was nice, but it wasn't super amazing. I did like that the bacon on it was nice and thick and full of flavor. The onion rings were tasty and made a nice little addition to the meal.  I didn't get to try one of their milkshakes, but I did get an icy cold Barq's in the bottle which is one of my favorite treats, so that was nice.  All in all, I would probably go back, if I was craving a burger and found myself in this area, but I would probably end up choosing another burger place or getting some other food all together. Good not great. A solid three stars.

I went to a showing of the silent film "Metropolis" here, last summer.  I had never been before.  You can get a membership, so that you can be key up to date for different events.  Although I have never had the opportunity to attend, I know that the Brown! improv comedy troupe also performs here frequently.    They have books for sale about local art and films.  This is a great little art space and I look forward to going back.

I've come to the conclusion that beef shwarma might be one of my favorite foods. I find myself craving it on a regular basis and I am forced to hunt it out, no matter where I am. When the craving recently hit, Pyramids Cafe was the closest place I could get my fix, so here we are.  It was a pretty slow afternoon when I was here and I was the only customer in the place. I was pretty hungry, so I started with an order of grape leaves stuffed with meat. These were really good! They gave me a lot, and they were stuffed very nicely with a sauce on the side for dipping. For my entree, I got the beef shwarma- my favorite. It came with meat, salad and hummus. This was fantastic! The meat was seasoned perfectly and the hummus was nice and creamy smooth. The salad was fresh and I enjoyed it.  The atmosphere here is pretty casual and "no frills", but it was the perfect spot for lunch. Service was fast and friendly and I left satisfied with the entire experience.

As big and gorgeous as this VS is, I really wish that I could give it more stars.  I think that this is the biggest and most complete VS in the area. They have the most things that I have ever seen that are also featured in the catalog and on the runway. I really do have to concur with Sarah; the renovations here are gorgeous and I love how nicely everything is organized.  I stopped in on a weekday during what I thought would be a pretty slow hour. I was here after New Year's not expecting to find a big crowd. I was very wrong and the place was packed. They were having their semi-annual sale, and apparently everyone had gotten the memo. I had a coupon and their body spray was 65% off already, so I grabbed one and headed towards checkout- this is where I encountered the issue. What I found was a line that was wrapped around the store and one register was open. Keep in mind, there are many registers throughout the store and there were many employees working on this particular day- they just weren't on the registers.   I decided to hop in line and just deal with it. Well, the employee working the register took about 5 minutes with each customer. At one point one woman realized she had gotten the wrong size of an item and the checkout girl held up the line while this woman went and searched for the item in her size. That was the point that I decided to cut my losses and hope that the Oakwood VS had what I was looking for (it did and there was no line).  It's a bummer to give this store only three stars because of this one issue, but I found it all a little ridiculous. I would return, but only if there was no crowd.

I just want to start by saying that I went to this bar on a pretty "dead" night. Despite being born and raised here and going to college here, I had never been to the infamous "Boot". Yeah, I had heard the stories and avoided it at all costs. I had heard rumors about old men and drunken frat boys scheming on under age girls. Yeah, I wanted no part of The Boot.  However, when a friend and I just happened to be driving past it one night and saw that it was pretty much dead, I decided that this was as good a time as any to see what the inside of this place looks like. I mean... I had to go in at least once.  Well, I'm happy to report that I survived my experience. The few people that were in here were distracted by a football game and had no interest in me at all. The place is HUGE and is actually a really nice space. I can see it being a cool place to go see a band or something, but I doubt the owners plan on bringing The Boot in that direction. The bartender seemed friendly enough I have been in places that are worse.  Would I go back? Well, no, it's not my kind of place, but it isn't bad for what it is.

We came here to see a band on a Sunday afternoon. I wasn't expecting much, especially since smoking still flys in Jefferson Parish, but my experience here was good. They had all of the doors and windows open so that the smoke was barely noticeable, they had a good band playing, and the bartenders worked fast.  This spot is a typical "pool hall" type place and they also serve food like burgers and other bar stuff like that. I wouldn't rush over again, but I had a good time.

This is a really new Mexican place on the Westbank, and as far as Westbank Mexican places (there are a bunch) this one measures up nicely, but I wasn't blown away.  I stopped in here for lunch. First of all, I love the open air space and there are tons of seating. I can see how this would probably be a cool hangout for Cinco de Mayo and a good spot to eat dinner if you have a big group of people.  The menu is packed with everything you could want including Mexican inspired pasta dishes and hamburgers. I decided to keep it pretty simple with a chicken quesadilla that came with a side of re-fried beans and rice. The quesadilla was good. The chicken was grilled nicely and was spiced for flavor. The same couldn't be said for the rice and beans. They were just super bland and I would have liked it if they had had a little more "kick" to them. All in all the meal wasn't earth stopping, but it was pretty good for a lunch.  Our waitress was really nice and attentive and was good at making sure that we were happy and had everything that we needed. Would I go back? Sure, but there are better choices for Mexican on the Westbank. I'll probably return in a few months after they have hit their stride.

Sorry, Charlie. I had high hopes for this spot after reading some reviews, but my experience here was a disappointment.  We got here after the lunch rush and while there weren't a lot of people here, the main dining room was full, so my dad and I were seated in a small back room. I usually hate sitting in the small back rooms, but I wasn't going to start complaining.  Our waiter came right over, told us the specials and then gave us time to look over the menu. He gave us like 15 minutes, which seemed like a long time, but maybe he was swamped. We decided to start with an order of onion rings and they were fantastic and didn't disappoint. You get a HUGE pile of onion rings that are pretty impossible to finish. They were fried to perfection and great.  For my entree, I got the soft shell crab platter which came with a side salad and jambalaya grits. I was happy that two large crabs came on the platter, and while it wasn't the greatest crab I'd ever had, I enjoyed it. The salad was a salad and I was happy it was fresh. The grits were awful. They came with sausage and shrimp in them, but they were really dry. I am usually happy with any type of grits I can get my hands on, but these missed the mark for me. My dad got the stuffed crab and he didn't like it all and said that there was barely any crab and the whole dish was mostly breading.  Service was pretty terrible. We were the only people sitting in this small room and it was obvious that our waiter completely forgot about us at times. He dropped off our food and vanished. When he finally returned, we asked for the check and vanished again for a good 15 minutes.  Finally, my dad goes to track the guy down and he says he'll be "right there" with the check. Another 5 minutes goes by and he is standing around talking to another waiter while we are STILL WAITING. Um...hello?? We don't have all day. We're pretty patient people, but our patience was wearing thin. Finally he comes with the check and we just handed him a card lest there be another 20 minute wait. All in total we were there for an hour and a half which is insane for lunch. I was just happy that I wasn't in a huge rush to get somewhere, otherwise I would have been out of luck.  I wouldn't eat here again. There are places in this city with way better food and way better service.

After two years and numerous visits, it's time for an update.  Magasin is now my "go to" for Pho when I am uptown, mainly because it's close to wherever I usually find myself and it's amazingly good. I have tried all different types of Pho at this point and I would have to say that the Filet Mignon and the brisket are a couple of my favorites. Another new discovery is the avocado spring roll which is fresh and crisp and delicious, especially if you aren't in the mood for a seafood roll. The staff is always super friendly and there has been no issue with any wait the last few times I've been.  I have taken to eating outside, when it's ncie, since there are tables and although you are just on the sidewalk, it's nice to watch the world go by. The cucumber green tea is still one of my favorites and is the best flavored tea that they have.

After munching down on some sushi, I spotted this shop's sidewalk sale as I was walking back to my car.  I popped in and decided to look around and I found a cute little boutique with a lot to offer. The clothes here really appealed to me. They had comfy looking cloth shorts and nice sundresses that are perfect for summer. The prices are pretty reasonable too. I was eyeing a really cute sundress that clocked in at about $19.  Oddly enough, I didn't notice any people working the shop, so maybe they were in the back for the few minutes that I was inside. Although I didn't buy anything this time, I can definitely see myself stopping here in the future. Great casual wear at a great price is a hard deal to pass up.

Fantastic on a lot of different levels. I'm always in the market for new shoes, so whilst in Metairie, I ducked into the mall and popped in here so see what I could find.  Lucky for me, they had some nice pumps on sale, so I picked up a pair. This store also has a really nice selection of men's shoes for that special guy in your life. The staff is friendly and helpful and will sit down with you and help you figure out exactly what would work best for you and their selection is vast but not overwhelming.

Whiskey Blue is a nice little "fancy pants" hotel bar.  I would say it's a good place to start the night.  When you walk in, it's very dark and the only real light is the blue lights coming from behind the bar and the dim lights in the seating areas.  It feels more like a "mini club" than a bar.  The reason I say that it is probably best to start a night here is because it does tend to get pretty packed and the last time I was here, the music the DJ was playing was ridiculously loud (hey you kids, get off my lawn!).  The drinks aren't all that expensive, but they probably cost a little more than they would at an average bar.  A nice place to get started, but I would recommend continuing your evening elsewhere.

I am so excited right now! I just spent the afternoon bowling at the brand new Westbank bowling alley and it was a lot of fun!  This is a big deal. The Westbank hasn't had a bowling alley in years. Sometimes you just want to bowl and you don't want to drive all the way downtown, you know? Anyway, I had heard rumors months ago about this place opening and I've been following the progress on Facebook. They finally opened two weeks ago and this spot is just gorgeous! Everything is brand new (obviously), they have comfy seats to sit on in the bowling area, they have 20 lanes of bowling fun, they have a cafe area that serves drinks and food, and they have another bar off to the side.  I bowled today and had a lot of fun, even though I was a bit rusty and probably need some more practice before I enter any leagues. There is staff everywhere making sure that everyone is having a good time. The lanes are really nice and the screens are really fancy. At night they are going to have light shows while people bowl and on weekends they have DJ's.  While we were there we decided to get some lunch. I got a dressed burger which came with potato salad. The food was okay- I don't know if anyone will be coming here just for the food, but it's better than typical bar food and it hit the spot while we were in the middle of a heated match.  I can't wait to become a regular at Westside Lanes. I am really a huge fan of bowling, but I don't go as much as I'd like, because the Westbank didn't have any lanes. Now that we have an alley again, this is going to be something really fun to do on the weekends.   Also, can you say "bowling party"? A big group was having one there today!

Ya see, now THIS is a bridge!  In my opinion, this is the only way to travel from the Eastbank to the Westbank and vice versa.  I'll go the "long" way to Jefferson, if it means I don't have to risk my life (slight over dramatization) on the Huey P. Long.  When heading to the East from the West, it costs a dollar.  Who do you think you are, New Orleans?  You are not a fancy pants club, and I shouldn't have to pay a cover!  Lucky for me, I have a nifty toll tag that not only means I have to pay a few cents to cross, but usually means I won't have to sit in traffic in order to do so.  A few tips: stay out of the toll tag lane, if you don't have a toll tag!  This is an excellent way to get rear ended, or at the very least, honked at!  And PLEASE don't slow down when you are approaching the "scanner".  You can go at a decent speed and it will get your tag.  That's what it's made for.  I promise.  I have tested this theory many times over.     I mean, mind the traffic around you, but keep up with it as well.

What a fantastic little spot! Fellow Yelper Jeff C. suggested that we try this place and since I had heard a lot of good things about it, I was down.  This cozy little restaurant on Tchoupitoulas is the perfect spot for a date night or a celebration. We made reservations for 8, and although we were a few minutes late, we were seated immediately upon arrival. We were given our menus and we ordered some wine. Looking over the menu, I immediately knew what I wanted. I have been on quite the grits kick lately, so when I saw that they offered catfish and grits, I knew that was the dish for me.  As a starter we decided to get the scallops, which were pan seared with butter, lemon, croutons and capers. I'm normally not a HUGE fan of scallops (it's a texture thing), but I am always willing to try food that I haven't liked before prepared in a different way. My experiment paid off because these scallops were delicious. They were flavorful and I really liked them a lot. The capers and butter created a nice sauce for them and I didn't think about the texture once!  Next came the catfish and grits. Check out my picture- this dish was just beautiful. The catfish was crispy and fried to perfection and the grits were nice and firm and not watery at all. The smoothness of the grits was a perfect compliment to the fish and I was sure to get a little bit of both in every bite. I really can't say enough about this part of the meal and I was beside myself happy.  Finally, we really decided to indulge and we treated ourselves to the chocolate mousse. This delicious concoction of whipped light chocolate came in a small chocolate shell bowl. The mousse was delectable and light and was the perfect conclusion to the meal. I also liked the presentation. I posted a picture- it really is a work of art.  The staff was very attentive the entire time and was quick to refill the wine glasses and clear the plates when necessary. I was really very pleased with the entire experience and I think that Tomas Bistro might be one of my new favorite dinner spots in the city.  I would absolutely go back and I am now hungry for more catfish and grits.

This is the main branch of the Jefferson Parish SPCA.  It's a larger facility than the one on the Westbank. This facility serves the Eastbank and is also where animals are shipped when the Westbank location gets full. As a result, this place is pretty packed. The conditions are nice, but there are so many cats that the cages are packed with them. This isn't bad- they are BIG cages, but coming here just drives home the point that pet over population is a HUGE problem. You really have no idea until you go into a place like this and see big cage after big cage packed with kittens.  While I was here, there was one cat who was "longest resident". I was immediately tempted to take her when I saw that she had been there since February. I'm not sure what the adoption/euthanization policy is here. I know that they do keep some cats for as long as they are adoptable, but I'm not sure how the whole system works.  Just as I said in my review of the Westbank location, please be sure to go in and look around, if you are looking for a dog or cat. There are tons here that need and want a good home and it just seems silly to go to a breeder as long as the shelters are packed with strays.  And I agree with Larissa that the shelter is a little tricky to find: it's basically off a service road. Thank goodness for GPS!

This is a review of the bar area only.  David and I were here on a much needed date night. I'm a beer loved and I had heard good things about this place, so I was excited to belly up to the bar and see what they had to offer. I was excited that they had a great tap selection of all types of beer and I especially enjoyed the stout that they had on tap. David isn't much of a beer drinker, but he does like lighter beer and he was easily able to find something that he liked. I wish I had gotten the bartender's name. He was really nice and knew his stuff. He was very kind and let us sample some beers before committing to a pint, which is always appreciated.  The food sounds amazing, so I know I will be back to try some of their menu.

This quiet little shop is the perfect place to grab coffee on the go. On the day I was here, there was a woman sitting outside selling king cake by the slice. The place is small inside, but there are some tables if you want to hang out and do some reading or just relax. I ordered the iced coffee (my favorite) and I was delighted by the flavor of it. It was rich and "sippable" without being too overwhelming or leaving me jittery. I'm not in this area a lot, but I wouldn't hesitate to return here for more of their coffee.

I shop here a lot. Probably more than I'm willing to admit. Don't look at me like that! You know I love a deal. That has definitely been established. I usually get little things here like birthday and holiday cards. They also have cute little toys and knick knacks for kids. Bring them here next time you want to give them a reward for something. They also have little home decorations items and decorations for different holidays.   I bought bubbles here today. Yes, bubbles. Don't judge me.

This Rouses is pretty close to my house and it's been open for about a year. I have no excuses for being so late to check this it out.  I stopped in here because I was looking for a specific beer. While I didn't find the brew that I was on a quest for, they do have a nice selection of craft beer from all over ("all over" being a technical term). I found a yummy IPA from Stone and, pleased with my selection, I decided to browse the rest of the store.  Holy moly freshness, Batman! I love the deli section here! There's a lot of hustle and bustle- the bakery has cakes made fresh, the sushi section had a nice line because sushi is made fresh to order (and also comes pre-packaged, if you're in a rush), there is a salad bar full of delicious goodies and a hot bar with tasty treats. I am definitely going to have to stop in here to get some good stuff for lunch. As I mentioned in my review of the Rouses on Belle Chasse Highway, there is a big gourmet cheese case. So in one section you have all of your bakery, salad, sushi and cheese needs met. There is also a nice little section dedicated to fresh flowers, for that special someone (even if that special someone is you).  This Rouses is fantastic. The lines move quickly and they have multiple registers open in order to get people in and out quickly. One complaint: the parking lot could be a little easier to navigate, but that's not the end of the world.

Here's another one of those "blink and you'll miss it" restaurants that's tucked away into a strip mall on the Westbank.  I was having a craving for Mexican food and I had bookmarked this spot a while ago after a friend mentioned it to me. I stopped in during lunch and...there was no one else here. I am starting to sense a trend: is there any other part of the city where you can go to a restaurant in the middle of a lunch hour and not encounter another customer?  Anyway, I looked over the menu and everything sounded like it was really authentic. I decided to get a chicken taco salad. Even though there was literally no one else here the salad took a while, but I was happy that it was being cooked to order, so I didn't mind the wait. When it came out it looked great! The chicken was fresh and the rest of it looked delicious. The flavors were all there and I was pretty pleased. The only things I found strange were: 1) there was no guacamole, even though it was listed as being included in the salad on the menu 2) the sour cream was on the side and not actually in the salad and 3) they didn't have queso aka melted cheese. Yes, I have mentioned before that I am unsophisticated and I like to dip my taco shell in queso. Well, this place doesn't have it and the waitress thought I was nuts for asking for it.  All in all, the meal was okay and the staff was friendly. It wasn't the best Mexican food I've had in the area, but I would eat here again.

I debated on whether or not to review this store, considering that it's closing in about a month, but I figured someone might be interested in hearing about the different sales they have going on.  So, yeah the place is closing so that means there are deals to be had. Right now it's only 20% to 30% off of items, but I'm sure that will change as the end date gets closer. I snagged a couple of "casual" tops and a wallet for a few bucks less that I would have paid at the Metairie location. Of course, so it goes, they have way better deals for men and they even have Ralph Lauren suits on sale, so head over if you're in the market for something like that.

Not a bad place. Kind of one of those holes in the wall where you go in and just order a Miller High Life.  Really good local crowd. I got the feeling that most of the patrons are people who live/work in the area and walked here. I really liked the jukebox and it offered a nice mix of music from the 50's to the 80's. Bartender was nice but could have been a bit more attentive.  I won't go out of my way to return, but not a bad place if you feel like getting a drink after having a sandwich at Cochon Butcher.

Rock 'n Bowl is a New Orleans institution that I should visit more often.  I love seeing bands here and I always have a good time rocking the night away. Yes, there is actual bowling but I have only ever been to see the bands and hang out and have a drink. There is live music every night and lots of space to dance, if that's your thing. If you get hungry, they have typical bar food like burgers and fries and things like that. Staff has always been fast and friendly whenever I've been here and the sound system is actually pretty good.

I think I have another parade to add to my list of favorites!  Sure, they have the silliest throws (is it weird that I got excited when I caught a mini plunger?) but it's a lot of fun and a good time.  I also got some cool "medallion" beads with Friar Tuck on them and the kids next to me caught a mini toilet.

I have fond memories of sitting in the backseat on family trips and listening to WTIX with my parents.  Ok, I'm going to be completely honest. At the age of 11, I lacked the appreciation for the type of music my parents enjoyed. While they were in the front seat enjoying the stylings of Dion and the Belmonts and The Contours I was in the backseat going nuts and not particularly enjoying myself. But over time, my tastes matured and while I'll probably never have Mickey & Sylvia on my iPod, I will say that WTIX is the best oldies station in New Orleans. Honestly, I think that it is now the only oldies station in New Orleans, which it should consider a point of pride.  And their jingle is catchy as all get out.

Cute little coffee cafe. Stopped in here for an iced coffee and it was good and inexpensive. Kind of odd that they serve coffee in styrofoam cups, though. They also serve food and they seem to have a pretty extensive menu of breakfast items as well as sandwiches. While I didn't order food, I noticed that the man sitting next to me waited at least 15 minutes for his breakfast, which was eggs and grits. Odd that something so simple would take that long, especially since there were two other people in there.  Cute local art on the wall for sale. Wouldn't go out of my way to stop here, but if you are in the area it gets the job done.

I finally got around to trying Morning Call, since i found myself at the park with cash (They don't accept cards. In 2014. At a tourist hot spot. Uh...yeah.) and I was in the mood for a frozen cafe au lait.  I walked in and sat down and ordered from a waitress. The cafe au lait seemed a little steep at $5, but I suppose you are paying for the ambiance of being in the park and most people who come here are probably tourists who are paying just to be in New Orleans.   The cafe au lait was okay, but it tasted like it came from a mix or something. It tasted kind of "syrupy", if that makes sense. I much prefer the one from Cafe du Monde.  Morning Call also serves beignets, of course, as well as typical New Orleans food like red beans and rice and jambalaya, which is over priced. But again...paying for ambiance.  I might stop in for a regular coffee, but I would pass on everything else.

Oooh wee.  I love trying new places, so when a friend suggested Megasin tonight, I was all about it.  Where do I start?  Well, I guess I will start with the wait.  Yes, there is one.  The place just opened and you know how those New Orleans folks go mad for their Vietnamese food.  My friend and I waited for about 30 minutes.  Once we were seated, I ordered the cucumber green tea and an order of shrimp spring rolls (I would have gotten beef, but it's Lent and it's a Friday).  The spring rolls were amazing and delicous.  I don't partake in peanut sauce (aka fancy peanut butter, stop kidding yourself), so I ate them dry and loved them.  For my entree, I wanted the wonton soup, but they were out, so I got the seafood pho.  It was amazing and it had shrimp, fish balls and scallops in it.  It was really good.  Am I a nerd because I was happy that they gave me a fork at the beginning of the meal?  A lot of times you go to these places and you feel weird if you ask for a fork because you aren't being "authentic".  Well, I used a fork for my noodles in my pho soup and I didn't feel weird about it.  While this place isn't as good as maybe a Pho Tau Bay, it is definitely worth at least trying.  I mean... I'm not a huge Pho fan and I liked it!

When you first pass this place, you have no idea what to expect, but the reality is that it is really good.  I have eaten here twice now and the food is really good. They serve boiled and fried seafood and po boys. The first thing I got here was fried cracklins which were amazing. Sure, it's not health food, but every once in a while I like to go "food slummin'". The second time I went, some friends and I got some crabs and crawfish that were fresh and amazing. It's the perfect thing to pick up when you are getting a group of friends together for a football game or something.  I will definitely be back. I have yet to try one of their po boys, so that is definitely on the "to do" list.

I was wandering downtown (with purpose) a few weeks ago when I first stumbled upon the Museum of Death. I was in a hurry, so I didn't have time to investigate further, but I was intrigued.  After a quick Google search, I discovered that the Museum of Death is EXACTLY what it sounds like and the original is in Los Angeles. Not only that, but the New Orleans museum is brand new! I've always had a curiosity about the macabre and other oddities, so after enlisting my friend to join me, I decided to check it out.  Going in I was a little nervous. What is one to expect from a place like this? Would it be educational or scary or gross? I was eager to find out (in the non creepiest way possible).  We stopped in on a Thursday afternoon and it was quiet. Good. I don't want any witnesses if I happen to pass out. Apparently, passing out happens sometimes, at least according to the owner of the museum. He asked us if we had weak stomachs and if we were easily grossed out. He flashed us a pretty gruesome picture, and since we passed his test, he let us in. He explained that there is no photography allowed, so sorry guys no sneak peeks from me. It's better if it's all a surprise anyway, right?  Walking in, the tour is self guided and they start you off pretty slowly with a few bones and things like that. Things then progress into artwork by serial killers and letters written by serial killers (some really gross and creepy) and quickly escalate into pictures. The pictures aren't for the faint of heart but it's nothing horribly jarring (at least they weren't to me). You can get a "sense" of what's in the pictures before fully approaching them, so if you glance and think that they aren't for you, just skip it. I managed to look at them without being scarred for life (as far as I can tell).  There are interesting articles about serial killers throughout. I wish some of them were labeled a little better, but considering they just opened, this isn't a big deal. In the very back, there is a video on a large screen of deaths playing, which was the toughest for me. However, the room is brightly lit and you don't have to watch it if you don't want to (I watched a few seconds and decided to pass on the video). Also, on the walls in the back are newspaper articles about deaths of celebrities such as Elvis, Huey P. Long, Kennedy and other politicians. It was really interesting to read about historical events as they were happening.  All in all, the Museum of Death is more interesting than scary. I enjoyed it and I think I'll return. The owner said they will be rotating things from the L.A. museum every 6 months or so, so that will be cool to check out. I hope they update their Facebook with that info. The tour was $13 (usually $15) and it took about a half hour, just because we didn't decide to read every single thing in there.   This museum is one of the cool little "quirks" that New Orleans offers. It's worth at least one visit. I would love to see some more local stories added (I can think of a few). Hopefully that is planned for the future.

This is one of my favorite locations in the city!  The decor is lovely and has a "retro, 50's, old New Orleans feel".  This would be the ultimate place to hold a wedding and/or reception because it has that Southern charm that you want in a New Orleans wedding.  The house has three different floors and a separate quarters, so that guests can stay on the premises.  It has all the amenities of home and the courtyard is lovely with a nice pool.  I was fortunate enough to be photographed for New Orleans Weddings Magazine in this house and you can't ask for better ambiance for an "old fashioned" type of wedding or party.

Typical garden district bar.  Nothing really special going for it.  Really smoky, but a nice bar to frequent if you live in the neighborhood.  It's probably not a place I would go out of my way to visit, but it was a nice little place nonetheless.

Man, this place didn't live up to my expectations at all.  I usually find fantastic food at little "holes in the wall". Some of the best food I have ever had has been at divey little places. Unfortunately, that theory didn't pan out this time.  We came during lunch and there wasn't too much of a crowd. The waitress was super attentive at first. I was going to get my usual fried oyster platter, but I decided to switch it up, and since I saw fried soft shell crab on the menu, I got that. I also decided to start with a bowl of corn and crab bisque, a favorite.  The corn and crab bisque came out and it was pretty good. Honestly, I kind of get the feeling that it was from a can, but once I added a little hot sauce to it, it was passable. The soft shell crab platter came with a nice side salad that I enjoyed, and was probably the best part of the meal.  The crab platter came out and I was immediately underwhelmed. First of all, it was only one medium sized crab on a huge pile of fries. Once I dug into the crab, the claws were tasty, but the body was under cooked and mushy in the middle. I didn't even finish it. It was completely unappetizing.  When the check came, they actually tried to charge us for two soft shell crab platters (correct) and two soft shell crab poboys (incorrect)! It's a good thing we were paying attention, otherwise they would have made off with a good bit of extra money.  Salvo's is right down the road and a million times better, save yourself the time and heartache and just go there.

This is a near little bar and theatre located in the Marigny.  I haven't been in a while, but I've seen bands and other shows here.  They have two rooms  The main room has a stage, a bar and tables and chairs for viewing whatever happens to be going on on any certain night.  It fills up fast, so get there early if there's a show you want to see and want to have a good seat.  The back room is more of the "theatre" area.  It has a bigger stage and way more seating and seeing shows in this room has always been a more enjoyable experience for me.    This isn't a place I would go to unless something I was really interested in seeing was happening (honestly, I haven't been here in well over a year or so), but it's a decent little hang out spot.  It's not in the best neighborhood, so if you're a girl, go with a group.

This was the second bar on the Metry bar crawl. Very dated and VERY smokey with a couple of pool tables and a separate area with dart boards, tables and chairs. There was a DJ playing dated country and rock songs, but the people here seemed to like it. I kind of felt like I was in someone's basement with all of the beer sign decor that was around.  A couple of cons: bartenders are super slow and kind of clueless. They talk to people on one side of their bar while people on the other side are waiting to be served. John L H ordered a beer from the bartender who heard him and proceeded to mix a drink for someone else. I finally had to flag him down and order his beer myself. I was doing "mocktails" and they didn't have ginger ale for my cranberry drink, so I settled for Sprite. Meh. At least it was free. Since Steve said the owners are new, I chalk all of this up to "growing pains".

Giving this one a "divey five".  A dive five.  What it has: Miller High Life for $2 served to you out of an ice chest... just like your grandpa used to give you. Low ceilings A pretty cool jukebox A pool table A diverse cast of characters Bright lighting  What it doesn't have: A dance floor A tolerance for foolishness Uppity beer like Stella Artois Big screen tvs: Are you here for drinking or are you here for tv watching? Credit card machines A "close" time

This 3 stars is pretty much 3.75, so consider that as you read this.  I will start my saying that Salu is pretty much a vegetarian paradise. I think I had one "meat" dish the entire time I was here. If I was a vegetarian, this would definitely be one of my "go to" restaurants.  I started with my own Caesar salad. It was really good and I liked that the croutons and dressing were obviously house made. It was a substantial start to the meal. From there our group (4 of us) decided to split different small plates. We ordered the Calamari, the Crispy Artichoke Hearts, the Ceviche, the Patatas Bravas and the Medjool Dates. I'll review each in the order of my enjoyment.  Calamari- generous portion. Really crispy and good with a nice flavor. Would definitely order again.  Crispy Artichoke Hearts- tasty and different. Frying the hearts made for a unique texture.  Medjool dates- Definitely a table favorite. Dates wrapped in bacon and then cooked. The dates almost had a sweet potato taste and texture.  Ceviche- Good and refreshing, served with tortilla style chips. Contained scallops, which I'm not a huge fan of (it's a texture thing). Solid 5/10 rating for me.  Patatas Bravas- Just okay. Potatoes grilled with some kind of sauce on them. Generous serving, but honestly I only had a few bites.  Our waiter was amazingly attentive and we didn't have any of the wait issues that other reviewers seemed to have. All of the small plates came out in a nice rotation so that we got to enjoy them one at a time. As I said, it's a 3.75 in my book and I would most definitely go back and try their other offerings.

I've been wanting to go to Wicked for ages, since I had heard they carry a lot of "retro" kind of styles. During French Quarter Fest, I finally got my chance.  For starters, I will say that I found the staff to be extremely friendly and helpful and I liked that Wicked had a wide selection of clothing for men and women. There were a lot of recognizable dresses with name brands and I even ended up getting one.  My main complaint is this: I don't know if I came on an "off" day after everything had been picked over, but I was disappointed to find that most of the dresses were only available in larger sizes. For the most part smalls, mediums, and even larges were gone. All that remained were XL sizes. Now, I assume that the smaller sizes are fast to go when new orders come in, but I would have liked to have had more choices in my size.  I will definitely be back because there really is a huge selection of dresses to choose from and they are very well priced. I just hope that, in the future, they have more smaller sizes so that I have a wider selection of things to choose from when shopping.

I was so pleasantly surprised by this shop.  When I first walked in, I saw really nice clothes and the first thing I thought is, "Great. Nothing is going to be really affordable." As I started looking around at the prices I was shocked. Everything was under $100 and looked like it cost way more than that! All of the clothes were really nice, and although they weren't really MY style, it's nice to see a shop on Magazine that is geared toward those of us that really can't afford to drop tons of money on a shopping trip.  I can't wait to stop back in and see what they add to the shop as the seasons change.

Is there anything this place doesn't have?  We were here looking for bed stuff and candles and this store delivered. I like that everything is organized neatly and the store itself is clean and the merchandise is easy to find. I am in the process of renovating my kitchen from ceiling to floor, so once that is complete I am going to be coming back to stock up on all new appliances like a coffee maker, a toaster oven and a fancy electric can opener, as well as other organization goodies. They have good prices for nice products and there are frequently coupons in the paper, so you are sure to find a deal.

I brought my fancy comforter here for a good wash because it's way too good for my home washer. Actually, it's way too big for my home washer, but you get what I'm saying.  The woman working here is super friendly and helpful. My load took 30 minutes and about another 15-20 minutes to dry. My comforter came out clean and in good shape. It wasn't misshapen or beaten up or anything like that. The machines only take quarters and they have a change machine, if you need it. The last wash is at 7:30 and the place closes at 9.

I'm not exactly sure how long The Skeleton House has been haunting St. Charles Avenue, but I believe it's the better part of five years.  This is one of those things that makes New Orleans unique- some folks decided to decorate the outside of their home and lawn with "punny" skeletons- and nothing is more scary than a good pun. I've visited the house in past years and it just gets bigger every year. I think my favorite this year was their take on Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump and I got a kick out of "Skully Skullenberger".  You aren't allowed on the property itself, so you have to be satisfied with checking everything out through their gate. You really can't be shocked, as there are A LOT of skeletons the owners don't want disturbed. Put this on your "must visit" while celebrating Halloween in New Orleans.

This a cool little place to see a band.  The crowd is older, but that doesn't matter.  It's a small place, but a nice hang out spot when a good band is there.  The staff is always really nice and there are pool tables, if you want to just go and hang out with friends and play a game of pool.  My main complaint is that the place is really smoky and it's hard to handle after a little while.

Continuing on my mission of eating at all of the restaurants on the NOLA Eater "38 Essential New Orleans Restaurants, January 2015"(http://nola.eater.com/maps/the-38-essential-new-orleans-restaurants-january-2015), for my next place to try, I chose Mariza.  This is a restaurant I had not only never been to, but I hadn't even heard of it. Reading the reviews here on Yelp, made the place sound very promising, so I was excited to check it out.  We stopped in pretty early- about 7, on a Saturday, and there was a 20 minute wait. No problem at all, as we weren't in any rush, so we decided to take a seat at the bar. I decided to sip on a nice glass of wine as I looked over the menu.  First of all, I like that the menu isn't overwhelming. You get a nice selection of food without feeling inundated with choices. After we were seated, we decided to start with the cheese plate. This came with three delicious cheeses with some bread and some blueberry sauce, which was a nice touch. The cheese was delicious and not too rich (does that make sense?).  For my entree, I decided to try the black linguine. I had always heard how fancy and fantastic black linguine is, so I felt quite posh ordering this dish. The linguine came topped with a yummy sauce and crawfish and shrimp. I decided to get the large bowl, because apparently, there is no shame in my game. The dish was amazing! It had a lot of flavor and was unique and unlike anything I had had before. I couldn't get  over how much I loved it. The shrimp were nice and plump and the crawfish were juicy and cooked perfectly.  I have to mention the atmosphere of this place. It's cozy, but not loud. It's pretty dark, which would make it an excellent spot for a romantic evening. I loved the whole vibe of the place and it felt more like a New York restaurant, than a New Orleans eatery.  All in all, I loved it here and I would definitely return.

I gotta say- I have some beef...er, chicken with all of the Westbank folks who have been keeping this spot a secret since it opened in February. Y'all know I love fried chicken and tasty waffles, so I should have been the first person informed that this place existed pretty much in my own backyard.  Now, when it comes to Westbank breakfast food I usually hit up Waffle House. However, my biggest complaint about "The House" is- for a place that has dubbed themselves a "Waffle House", their waffle options are lacking. You get plain, pecan, chocolate chip, peanut butter or blueberry (but only once a year). I want more options! Well, Freddie's has you covered with their blueberry, strawberry and seasonal options and the waffles are super fluffy and fresh and, of course, you can pair them with fried chicken, bacon, sausage, or steak for just a few extra bucks!  So, I stopped in here with my chicken and waffles craving and, I'll admit it, my eyes were bigger than my stomach, so I also got the $3 side of grits. The amount of food you get for the price is incredible! For $11 you get 4 big pieces of juicy, flavorful, fried to golden perfection chicken and 4 fluffy waffle wedges that have blueberry taste, but aren't overwhelming. The serving of grits was also quite large and the savory grits and chicken balanced the sweet waffles well. There was also syrup for dipping and I dipped the chicken and the waffles- don't judge me. It was all delicious!  They have a wide variety of other breakfast items here such as omelets and eggs benedict as well as lunch offerings like poboys, salads, red beans and rice, seafood and grits and a fried shrimp platter. The staff was super nice and attentive and the owner and the cook even came over to make sure that everything was to my liking. I loved this spot and I can't wait to go back!

Woot! I finally made it over to Avery's and the experience didn't disappoint.  I am never in this part of town, so when I found myself over this way around lunchtime, I made a point of treating myself to a po boy. I wasn't in a seafood mood, so I decided on a 6 inch hot sausage po boy. First of all, the prices here are insanely fair. A 6 inch hot sausage came to a little over $5. In fact, the most expensive po boy I saw was maybe $10 for an oyster (6 inch). I feel like so many shops take advantage of our love of that certain sub and hit us with crazy up charges, because they know that we will pay it. Not so at Avery's.  The sandwich was amazing. It was crispy and thick with delicious meat. It also had some kind of sauce on it (I think). Now that I think of it, it may have just been the condiments mixing in with the sausage grease, but hey, it worked for me. Avery's has table service, but I decided to get my sandwich to go. I was in a bit of a rush, and Christy (one of the owners) was super cool about speeding things along so that I wouldn't miss an appointment.  I will definitely be back to Avery's. I get the feeling that with the revitalization of Tulane, Avery's is going to blow up even more than it already has. I better enjoy the lack of a line while I can get it!

I really don't know what to think about Siberia. It's obviously a neighborhood dive bar. I went here with some friends to see a band. It was a pretty good time. I liked that it wasn't super packed and there were benches for sitting. The place is really dingy and on the night I went the bathroom was pretty gross like it hadn't been cleaned in a while.   The bartender was nice enough, but the patrons weren't overly friendly. I'm used to people who at least return a smile, but these folks weren't having it. It almost seemed like they were in their own little "regulars" clique and I was the new kid they didn't know or want to acknowledge.  I'd probably go back if there was a band or something, but I wouldn't go out of my way.

My dad and I stopped in here for his birthday and I was pretty glad that I thought ahead to make reservations, because it was packed at lunch on a Wednesday!  We were seated right away and I decided to start with the baked potato soup and for my entree I got the Cuban sandwich with a side of black beans and rice. The baked potato soup was excellent! I know I say this a lot- but I really could have had just this and left satisfied. It was very rich and filling and I enjoyed it.  My Cuban sandwich was pretty good and, while I don't know how authentic it was, it was packed with meat and cheese and nicely pressed, so I didn't have any complaints. The rice and beans were a nice touch and I was happy that that was a side option.  Service was a bit slow, but that was understandable considering how packed the restaurant was. I don't think there was one empty table the entire time I was there. I would definitely be back, but only if I made reservations ahead of time.

You know on my first ever trip to St. Roch Market I just had to try the Mexican place they have here.  La Mezcla has a nice selection of goodies such as tacos and enchiladas. but today I was in the mood for a taco salad with pork. I went up and ordered, gave the guy my name and waited as he made my food fresh. The salad was packed with pork, cheese, lettuce, tomato and onions all in a crispy shell with jalapeño dressing on the side . I couldn't wait to dig in.  The ingredients of this bowl are resh and crispy, and the pork is so juicy that I really didn't even need the dressing and only ended up using a little of it. My only tiny complaint was that there wasn't much flavor to the shell (I'm a shell muncher), but that is not a big deal at all.  I will definitely be back to try more of what La Mezcla has to offer. The man who ordered before me got the tacos and they looked amazing. Service is fast and the food is good- perfect.

Awesome!  I got so many throws from this parade I didn't know what to do with myself!  Very generous and a great crew.  I got some cool blinky beads and three cups.  Total winner!  Everyone who I went to the parade with came away happy.  A great opening act for Muses!!  Catch of the night: Blinking medallions

I love this place! Between the souvenir shops and the strip clubs you might not realize there is actually a pretty decent little jazz club on Bourbon Street.   I had heard about Fritzel's cozy atmosphere and I was anxious to check it out. My experience didn't disappoint. First of all, I like the place because not only do they have awesome live music, but they have good beer. It's a total win.  The night we went there was a really good little jazz band playing. I like that the place is small because that adds to the intimacy of the experience. I will definitely be back. This is one of those places that you almost wish wasn't on Bourbon Street so that you could go more often.

The worst! You go and order and ask them specifically to not include certain condiments- they don't listen. Then they tell you there is going be a wait for you to get your food. They ask you to back up your car, because there is a pressure plate at the drive thru window that is timing how fast they get the food to you. When you back up, it resets. Apparently the manager doesn't like them to take longer than a minute on each customer, so their solution is to cheat the system by telling customers to roll off of the pressure plate.  Also, their highway sign is never on and lit up and I complained about it to HQ months ago . I think the employees leave it off because they don't want to be bothered with serving customers at night. It's easier to make people think you're closed.  Shady sneaks who don't deserve your business.

For years I have wanted to do a fancy New Orleans Jazz Sunday brunch, and after attending a Yelp event at Broussard's, I knew this was the place.  For birthday meal #3, I booked Sunday brunch here through Open Table. We arrived right on time for our 11 am reservation and we were seated immediately. We were given the choice of the dining room or the courtyard, and we chose the courtyard because the weather was perfect for sitting outside.  I started with some $12 bottomless mimosas as I looked over the menu. If you're a fan of mimosas, you must get the bottomless. They bring you a cute little carafe of OJ, mix a mimosa for you at the table and then keep the champagne flowing until you leave. Really- they were on top of the whole "keeping the glass full" thing.  I decided to get an order of the crab benedict, which is two crab cakes topped with eggs benedict. I also got a side of the stone ground grits because, well, I love grits. David got the chicken and waffles that we had sampled at the Yelp event we attended.  The crab benedict came out looking delectable. Eggs cooked to perfection sat atop tasty, rich crab cakes. Don't let my picture fool you, it wasn't served to be with a broken egg, I poked it to check the consistency. Of course, it was perfectly cooked. This dish was so rich that it bordered on over-the-top decadent and I loved the way the the egg soaked into the crab cake as I ate it. I was actually pretty happy that I got an order of grits on the side, because I think it paired well with my eggs. The grits tasted like homemade and were creamy and good. It was also nice that it was a serving that could have easily been shared. David's chicken and waffles looked just incredible and came with syrup served on the side- I'll try them next time.  After our meal, we sat and enjoyed the morning and that's when the jazz band started. A three piece band walked from table to table taking requests. When they got to me, I mentioned it was my birthday and they sang "Happy Birthday" to me. It was a delight and definitely a great memory.  To my surprise, at the very end of the meal, our waiter brought out complimentary crème brûlée, with a candle, for my birthday. Someone saw the note about my birthday on my Open Table reservation! See, this is how it's done. The dessert was delicious and I was so happy that I had chosen this spot for my first ever jazz brunch; special touches like this will keep me coming back again and again.  From start to finish my experience here was top notch. The staff was friendly and everything flowed beautifully. I never had to ask for a drink refill, orders were taken promptly and dishes were cleared quickly. It's the little touches like that the make the customer feel as if they are getting the full experience when dining at a place like this.  I will definitely be back to Broussard's and I want to experience dinner here as well. If you're looking to celebrate a special occasion, this is the place.

David and I popped in here, as I had always heard raves about this classic Italian spot.  I hadn't made reservations when we were here early on a Saturday. I would definitely recommend reservations, because although we were seated immediately, if we had been here an hour later, there would have been a wait. We were seated at a cozy corner table and looking over the menu, I knew what I wanted immediately.  We started with an order of mozzarella sticks that came with tasty marinara sauce for dipping. For my entree, I got the chicken supreme- fried chicken topped with a rich crawfish sauce. This dish was incredible- it was very rich and flavorful and, while it was probably odd to order something like this at an Italian restaurant, it was prepared beautifully. It also came with a side of pasta a red sauce, which I thought was a nice touch.  David had the lasagna and enjoyed that as well, so that might be a good pick if you're looking for something more authentically Italian.

We were here on a Saturday night and the place was pretty dead. I already had an idea of what I was going to order, so we were seated and ordered right away.  For a starter we got the Voodoo shrimp, which is sautéed jumbo shrimp, simmered in an amber beer reduction on top of housemade jalapeño cornbread. This app was so good! I honestly probably could have made a meal out of it. The cornbread was tasty and soft and soaked up the sauce nicely. The shrimp were tail-on and were big and perfectly cooked. The entire dish was fantastic and my favorite part of the meal.  For my entree, I got the shrimp and grits which is tail-on jumbo shrimp simmered in chipotle garlic cream sauce, layered over a housemade crispy fried grit cake and served with sweet teardrop tomatoes. Keep in mind, this dish is served with a grit cake and not typical grits. I loved the way the grits were cooked and they went wonderfully with the fat shrimp.  I gotta say though, I think I blew it on this one. My date got the lobster mac and cheese and after tasting a few bites, I decided that THIS is the dish to get. The macaroni is perfectly cooked, the lobster is generous and there is cheese for days. As good as my shrimp and grits was, I think I will be getting the lobster mac and cheese when I go back. It was so good that it tasted like homemade- incredible.  Service here was decent and the atmosphere is okay. Keep in mind most people eat here before going to a show at House of Blues, so the service is a bit rushed. All in all I liked my experience here and I'll be back.

A friend of mine was visiting from out of town, and being the huge coffee fiend that he is, he had compiled a list of different coffee places to try. One of the places on the list was Cherry Coffee, and since we had just had lunch a block away, we decided to check it out.  Cherry Coffee isn't even a coffee shop, but a stand located inside of Stein's Deli and Market. I walked up and ordered and iced coffee and it was really good with a lot of flavor and just enough "kick". Admittedly, Cherry has their work cut out for them; District Donuts is right next door and their coffee is really good as well, but this little stand seems to be holding it's own.   I would love to know if the owner has any plans to open a "brick and mortar" coffee shop in a different location. From what I could tell, she is doing just fine here. Cherry probably wouldn't be my first choice for coffee in the city, but it does a good job in a java heavy landscape.

What brought us all the way to Kenner, was the promise of cheap crawfish. I had been doing my due diligence in researching what places had the cheapest crawfish in town and at $2.99/lb, this place was the big winner. I had also had it on my list because I wanted to try one of their Crabby Mary's.  We were here on a Saturday night and there was a good size crowd at 7. We decided to start with some fried pickles, just because we both like them and we wanted something to munch on. We then got the boiled crawfish with sausage and potatoes and I got my Crabby Mary.  The crawfish was pretty close to perfect: they were a good size (bigger than I had had at a previous spot) and while they could have been a tad spicier, they had a good flavor. The sausage also could have been spicier, but I enjoyed it as well. My Crabby Mary was pretty good. What it is is a bloody Mary topped with a fried soft shell crab, two fried shrimp and two hush puppies, all for $20. Honestly, as good as it was, I probably wouldn't rush to get it again. My suggestion would be- order this for lunch with a side and call it a day. I'm not sure if it was worth the $20.  Our waitress was extremely nice and went above and beyond, especially when we thought we had a "sausage emergency" (we thought they had forgotten the sausage, so our waitress brought us more). I would love to go back and see what else they have to offer and I will probably be back for some more crawfish before the end of the season.

FINALLY!  I'm sorry, I'm giving this Chick Fil A 5 stars for convenience alone.  Metairie has had a mall-less Chick Fil A for years and the Westbank has finally caught up.  I love the Chick Fil A chicken salad sandwich, I will definitely be frequenting this location, so that I don't have to worry about parking at the mall and waiting in what seems to be a never ending line.

This is a great little PJ's located close to City Park and the cemeteries, if you want to get some caffeine before enjoying a day of grave hopping (it's a thing).  This location is pretty big compared to other PJ's locations, and there was a nice crowd when I was here at 9 am, on a Saturday, before a photo shoot at the park. They have a variety of snacks, as the other PJ's do and there is plenty of seating, including booths and nice sofas. There's even some seating outside, if you're in the mood to hang out on a nice day.  The staff was friendly and the coffee was as consistent as it is with other PJ's location, making this spot a complete win.

First of all, the best part about this bar is that no smoking is allowed. David and I stopped in here to see a band, and although the place is small it's full of really good people. I wish they had a better beer selection, but I was pretty happy with my purple haze.  Because of the band, they got a good little crowd but the bartenders handled it well. This was the first venture since everyone has been vaccinated, so nobody was wearing a mask. I feel comfortable and everything was handled well.  The bar is located in a strip mall, but don't be put off. It's a fun little time and the drinks and people make it worth it.

You might be wondering why I am reviewing a store that's going to close in a few weeks. Well, I wanted to mention all of the awesome sales they are having right now.
