I was happy to find myself in the area because I did know that this K Mart was closing and I was eager to snag some good deals on some things that I need. I really lucked out, mainly in the beauty department. I'm not a big fan of drug store makeup, except when it comes to my foundation, concealer and powder: Cover Girl has my pale self covered. They had all Cover Girl products on sale, so I stocked up. I also picked up a few eye shadows for ridiculously cheap. The entire store is on sale, so if you are looking for something, it might be worth checking here first.  It's too bad that this K Mart is closing, because it does serve a purpose. I really hope they do something about the parking lot before the new tenant moves in- the parking lot now is a mess and you have to go in a certain way and out a certain way and the design is just weird.

This has been my post office forever and I really have no huge complaints about the place.  The people are always really friendly and the lines move pretty fast.  I think the only negative thing I would say about it is that the tellers really do take their sweet time.  That's awesome when they are taking their sweet time with you, but when you are in a rush it can be frustrating.  Oh well.  During the holiday season, they are really good about adding more staff to accommodate the crowd, which is always nice.

I could have sworn I reviewed the Crescent City Connection aka the CCC aka C³, but I guess I didn't.  Now, you would think that I would give the CCC 5 big ones since I drive this thing almost every day and there's no more tolls. Ha, nope! Why am I only giving up 3 stars for this bridge? Um, a few reasons.  #1) The toll booths are still up. It's time to tear those bad boys down. They make the bridge visually unappealing and they cause traffic.  #2) Coming from the Westbank, on the right there are two or three lanes closed for NO REASON. NONE. There is zero reason for those lanes to be closed. I want to drive in those lanes. Why are they closed?? Oh wait, I don't care. Open them.  #3) Come 4:00, drivers going from the Westbank to the Eastbank go full retard on this thing (Tropic Thunder style). There is no reason for traffic to be backed all the way up at 4:00. Maybe 5 or 6, not 4. I don't know what's going on or why it happens, but when I have to leave my house at 4:30 for a 5:30 appointment, that's not cool. Oh and the traffic starts getting bad at 3 on Fridays. Awesome.  I'm giving a star because I have to drive on this thing all the time and I'm giving one more because there's no more tolls.
Definitely worth the drive out to Belle Chasse!  Fantastic Catfish and generous servings.  Small place, but that is part of the charm.  Easily my favorite place for Catfish in the area.

El Paso was pretty good, but I wasn't blown away.  I came here for lunch and the place was dead except for me and my dining companion. The waitress was super nice, even though she seemed a bit more wrapped up in watching a talk show than taking our order, but that wasn't a huge deal. Once she came over, she dropped off some really good chips and salsa and we looked over the menu.  I got the carnitas quesadilla which came with a side of sour cream and tomatoes. The quesadilla was pretty good, but I found the carnitas a bit dry. Other than that, it had good flavor and it made for a decent lunch. My friend got a burrito that looked outstanding and I think that I will get that next time.  Service was a bit slow, but I would probably stop in for lunch again or to get a "to go" order. Just a note: they will give you water that isn't bottled if you specify and just tell them you want ice water.

I was craving chocolate and I was in the area, so I stopped into Vega Tapas for chocolate cake. Yes, just chocolate cake and red wine.  For starters, I LOVE the atmosphere! The bar area makes you feel as if you have stepped into another world. There are some sofas in a cozy part of the bar, right next to the window, that are decked out with pillows and candlelight. The actual bar is painted red and there is nice Spanish-style music playing in the background. It's just a lovely feel.  Anyway, chocolate cake- I'm here for the cake. Well, I was told it was fantastic and they weren't lying. The cake was nice and dense and a little bit fudgey- we are talking about PURE chocolate here. I think it's a flourless type of cake because it was really rich and really good. I paired it with a glass of cabernet and the combination of the flavor of the wine and the cake was perfection.  I didn't get any "real food" this time, so I will come back and dine in.

Deborah and I stopped in for lunch and I was excited because I pass this place all the time and I've been eager to try it.  The crowd was pretty thin at around noon on a weekday, so the service was excellent and the waiter was fast and attentive. I decided to get the Seed Club which is a club sandwich made with lettuce, tomato, and avocado. No meat, of course, since the place is vegan. The sandwich was pretty good and came with a little salad on the side. I found that it was well worth the $10 and I was happy that it was vegan without being anything "out the box" (I'm still not sure what vegan cheese is made of).  The portions here are pretty small, so I think it's probably better to get lunch here, rather than dinner, unless you plan on going all out and getting a few things from the menu. I enjoyed it and I'll return.

I used to shop at Express all the time in my younger days, so I decided to pop in here and see what they had to offer.  They have the usual "casual, but not too casual" type of clothes that they've always offered and they had a nice selection of dresses, tops and sweaters that I was happy to look through. On the day I was here, I was in the market for some new jeans, so I snagged a pair for a pretty good price.  The thing about is Express is that this store is only really worth checking out if they're having a sale. Otherwise, I do find them a little pricey for the quality of goods you're getting. With that being said, I have always liked their jeans and I do think that they are actually worth the price tag.

I've been to this place a few times.  It's not terrible and it's definitely one of the better bars on Bourbon, although that isn't saying much.  I do like the fact that they have a nice patio area, but I found the upstairs really tight and cramped for what they are trying to achieve.  The area isn't really big enough for a huge bar, dance floor and separate VIP area. It takes forever to get a drink and the space is really small for the super loud music that they play.  If I were to go back, I would definitely just hang out downstairs.

I stopped in here last night to see Little Freddie King and I'm bumping them up a star.  The beer selection here is pretty solid, they have food in the back and the patrons were a lot friendlier this time around. A nice group of people even asked us to join them, because they knew the band. We had a really good time watching the band, I had no problem finding a good seat and bars like this is why the smoking ban is a good thing. This bar is really small, so if smoking was still allowed it would be a "no go" for me. Now I can add this cool spot into the regular rotation! Oh, and if you are just in the mood to stop in for food, there are booths in the back so you can sit and eat.  Luke, one of the owners, was super friendly, as he was working behind the bar, and was really attentive and made sure everyone had what they needed, drink wise. I had a good time and I'll return.

This is just a review of the coffee, since I had just eaten across the street when I stopped in here.  This spot used to be the Reservoir Cafe, and that place was nice enough, but they have certainly done more with it since Deville moved in. I got a large iced coffee that I really enjoyed. The coffee wasn't anything overly special, but it had a lot of flavor and I liked it.  The decor here is really nice- they have nice spots where you can sit and take advantage of the wifi while doing some work and cozy tables are nice if you want to sit and enjoy some crepes. While I didn't have any crepes I did notice that they have all types varying from sweet to more of a meal. I will definitely have to come back and try them.

Not bad, if you know what you are getting into.  Hurricane's hosts a lot of cover bands, and that's usually how I find myself here. If you are lucky, you will get a spot by the bar, during the busier shows. If you aren't lucky, you will have to wade through a crowd of people to get one beer. It's Metairie, so there's smoking but their filter system is pretty decent. The beer selection is pretty good- they had Lagunitas on tap the last time I was here. Staff is always friendly and there are pool tables in the back, if you're into that type of thing.

I didn't want to do it. I really didn't want to be one of those people that actually likes Hobby Lobby. Politics aside, from the outside Hobby Lobby just seemed like one of those places that was a little too perfect. "Of course we have a pecan and pumpkin scented candle with pine undertones! YOU'RE AT HOBBY LOBBY!" Full disclosure: this place is kind of awesome and it made me miss the days that I used to spend wandering the aisles of the long shuttered Gordon's of Gretna.  Naturally, it's August, so the first thing that you see as soon as you walk in are Halloween and Thanksgiving decorations. In fact, they have an entire wall of Thanksgiving decorations. Napkins, plates, candles, cornucopias of varying sizes; they have it. They also have Christmas everything. I'm not sure if this is year round, or only because we have entered the second half of the year, but today the employees were putting up a massive nativity in the middle of aisles decked with stockings, trees and other holiday goodies.  Moving on, I noticed that this place has home decor on lock. Everything you could need for kids and adults alike is here. Your kid is into sports? They have every base covered (heh) from signs to vintage sports memorabilia. Comic books more your kid's thing? Check out all of the Superman, Batman and Spiderman posters, lights, drawer pulls, emblems, logos and knick knacks. Need to decorate a man cave? Great. What does he drive? Here's some vintage signs that he can hang on the wall. Redecorating the house? How about a huge decorative wall clock? Is a massive cross more your thing? Maybe some trendy (but not too trendy) wall art. Or let's just keep it simple with a couple of frames.  Do you like to sew? Boom, fabric and everything else you need to make your dreams come true! Art and crafts- do you like gluing stuff to other stuff and throwing glitter on it? Yes, right over here in the craft aisle! Do you like to draw? Here's some fancy paper! No matter what your hobby, Hobby Lobby does indeed have you covered. I'm not even a crafter, but God help me I wanted to buy some felt and start scrap booking.  Oh Hobby Lobby, I didn't want to like you but I do and I can actually see myself getting some decorations here for Christmas or Valentines or Easter or President's Day or Arbor Day, because I know you have something for every holiday on the calendar. I hate myself.

I really wanted to go with four stars on this one, but I gotta go with three.  I stopped in here on Endymion Saturday having not gone to the parade. I had, however, sat in about 45 minutes of traffic, so I decided to reward myself with some beer and some barbecue. The menu was a bit limited on this night, but that's not a big deal. I ordered the pulled pork sandwich and a side of mac and cheese.  After a brief wait, the food was ready and I was excited to dig in. The pulled pork was topped with coleslaw on a pretty thin bun. It was decent, but not earth shattering. I guess I could have added some sauce, but I'm one of those people that believes that good barbecue doesn't need sauce. The mac and cheese was a huge let down. It was pretty bland, I had to add salt and my friend had to add barbecue sauce to his to improve it. I don't know how 4 cheese mac and cheese comes out bland, but that was the case here.  I'm going to chalk all of this up to an "off" night due to parades and I will definitely return and try the food again. They had a burger that sounded really good that I am eager to try, so that will be my next pick.

Hi Do is a much needed local bakery in an area where local bakeries are lacking... on the Westbank.  Don't go in here expecting to find cupcakes and petit fours.  Croissants are the star of the show in this little gem located in the heart of Terrytown.  You can get them stuffed with fruit or cream cheese (my favorite).  They are made fresh, are absolutely delicious and at $2, the price can't be beat.  They also have bear claws and turnovers.  Another thing that is unique about Hi Do is the fact that you can order one of their specialty king cakes all year long, even during the "off" season.  That could make a great treat if you need something to hold you over until parade season comes around again.  My only complaint: they are cash and check only.  No credit cards accepted.  Understandable, because the place is a small family owned business, but still annoying if you find yourself here without cash in hand.

Oh Lord. Ok, well I had a photo shoot here.  When me and the photographer arrived at the hotel and checked in, he immediately realized that the room that he had asked for was not the room he was given. He had asked for a suite and they put him in a small room (cell) with one bed, a brick wall and zero ambiance. He called the front desk and they explained that they had double booked the suite that he had asked for. Keep in mind, this was October so it wasn't super busy.  They put us in another room, and it was a little better but not much. The room was seriously so small that if I had to stay there for an extended period of time, I would probably go crazy. I guess most people who stay here are out on the town, but you still hope that you will come back to a nice room.  The light in the bathroom was ridiculously dim and I felt as if I was getting myself together in some kind of weird haze. Also, the bathroom didn't look all that clean.  Don't let the name fool you, you probably won't feel like a Queen if you stay here.

Lucky me! I'm never in the East, but I had to take a work trip out here, so of course I knew that I just had to have lunch at Dong Phuong.  I was seated right away at around 1:30 and I looked over the menu with anticipation.  I love my pho, and I had heard raves about this place, so I knew that I was getting #44- Pho Tai. And, as long as I'm here, I might as well treat myself to some delicious egg rolls.  The egg rolls came first and I was delighted that the four of them were a good size and so good! The crust was nice and flaky and the inside was delicious and I loved soaking up the sauce that it came with. Next came the pho and for $8.00 you get their "one size" bowl, which is really big and packed to the brim with deliciousness. The broth was perfect and the meat was plentiful. I can see why so many people rave about the food here- it some of the best pho that I've had in my few, but varied, adventures around town.  Along with the fantastic food, the staff just couldn't be any nicer. My waitress was super sweet and asked if it was my first time and asked how I had heard about the place. I just think it was a nice touch for her to make small talk like that, considering how busy she was.  I'm so happy that I get to check one more New Orleans institution off of my list and I will absolutely be back.

Brigsten's is always a dream come true. Delicious food in a cozy, homey atmosphere.  David and I stopped in here for a little date night and it was fantastic, as always. I had been here before, but it was David's first time. He got the steak and I had the bass.  My bass was perfection! It came with delicious, creamy mashed potatoes and all of the flavors were just perfect. For dessert, we enjoyed pecan pie and bread pudding that was out of this world. David thought it was some of the best bread pudding he has ever had.  Brigsten's is easily one of the best restaurants in town and we will be back!

I'm leaving three stars so there is room to grow.  I was here for opening day and, as a craft beer "person", I'm always excited to welcome a new local brewery to the scene. I had read Emily's review, so I did know what to expect. The place is very small inside. It's so small, that I don't know what they're going to do on really busy nights, especially if the weather is inclement. There's just something about the bar area that feels very tight. The patio isn't too bad. I would recommend adding some patio umbrellas for when the hot summer days start to kick in. Seating is "family style" with tables and benches, so go ready to mingle.  As for the beer, I enjoyed it. I came late in the day, so a lot of the offerings were tapped out but I did have the Falcon Warrior IPA, which was tasty and the Weisses and Virtues Weizenbock, which was even better. I would probably go back just to have more of the Weizzenbock- it had a decent abv while remaining smooth. I have to go back to try the porter and cream ale that Emily mentioned- I love thick beer.  Brieux Carré will likely do very well in this spot, even though it's small. I imagine that if/when they start distributing I will probably avoid the space and enjoy their beer elsewhere.

This was a pretty good PJ's and I feel like it deserves points just for being out in the middle of no where. I mean, do you know how many areas of the city are more populated and don't have a proper PJ's?  It took a minute for me to find this location, because I have no clue where anything is in Chalmette, but once I got here the service was fast and friendly. I got a large iced coffee with 2% milk and they were a little stingy on the milk, but other than that, it was okay. If I had one complaint it would be the fact that there is no milk and cream out for the public to use. Well, they do have that Carnation imitation cream, but not the real stuff. Sometimes I like adding my own because I know exactly how much I like.

I'm so excited that Rizzuto's decided to open a casual dining spot on my side of the river!  This place is fantastic! Not only do they have amazing pizza, but their pasta dishes are out of this world. On my latest visit, I had the baked ziti which was phenomenal. It was a huge portion with a thick layer of cheese and covered in meat sauce. You really can't get any better than that.   The place is small, so they do a lot of takeout and they have a good size menu with a lot of options. If pasta is your thing, they have plenty of choices, as well as salads. On the appetizer menu, they have a huge meatball topped with ricotta cheese that is a must-try. I have eaten here a few times now, and I have never been disappointed.

I was so excited to try this new spot for lunch today.  I am a really big fan of Mediterranean food, and I definitely have my favorites around town, so Shawarma on the Run had a lot to live up to. Ordering is simple: you go up to the counter and tell them what you want and you sit and wait and either eat there or take your food to go. The man working the counter was very nice and helped me figure out exactly what I wanted. I got the beef shawarma platter which came with a small salad, hummus, pita bread and rice. I also got a Lebanese tea.  The food was good. The meat had a lot of flavor, the rice and salad were good and the hummus was nice and smooth. My platter and my drink came to $16.44 which was a bit pricey for lunch, especially considering there are other places where you can get the same thing for a $10 lunch special. My tea was $3, so take that into consideration. I guess it all evens out and the extra few dollars won't keep me away.  I want to return and I want to try one of their wraps that look so good. Everyone here was really friendly and it was a nice atmosphere for dining. I am a fan!

I really liked this place. It's a neat little hole in the wall off of Bourbon St. and a nice place to check out if you are trying to get away from the touristy crowd. It isn't anything fancy, but you can see that it's a nice neighborhood bar with a good group of regulars.

What do you do when your house has windows that are over 40 years old and summer is coming and you have decided that this is going to be the year that you get them all replaced and save some cash on your energy bills? You start by doing a lot of research, sitting through a lot of sales pitches and finally going with your gut. My gut told me to go with Allstate windows. Nope, I didn't just type "new windows" into google and go with the first result; I did my research and I couldn't be more pleased with my choice.  Getting windows is a process. First, the sales person will come out to your home, look over your old funky windows, discuss what you are interested in and talk prices to figure out what works best for you. Then another person comes out and measures for the windows and after a few weeks your shiny new windows are ready to be installed.  I didn't need a lot done. I wanted a total of 5 new windows. I was told that a few installation guys would come out and work their magic and the whole process, from start to finish, would take a day. I was pretty excited that it was going to happen so quickly. The installers showed up right on time and got right to work. They had the process down to a tee: they cut out the old windows, popped in the new windows, sealed them, worked the rest of their magic and were done!  The new windows are GORGEOUS and I couldn't be more pleased. They are double pained and I am already spoiled at how easy they are to just slide open on a nice days. I know that we haven't had a lot of warm days yet, but I can already feel the difference in the house and the windows are doing a great job of keeping all of the heat outside where it belongs.  After the windows were installed, I had a few minor issues with some sealing and one of the installers came right back out and took care of it with no issues. It's been over a month and I couldn't be more pleased with the entire process.

Whoa. I stopped in here on Mardi Gras and BINGO! we have a winner.  For starters, I was so delighted that this place decided to stay open for Mardi Gras. We stopped in for a very late lunch (after 3) and the place was packed, Lucky for us, there was an empty spot so we were immediately seated.  We were STARVING, so we knew that we were going to order a few things. We started with the crawfish and tasso cheesecake and the duck waffles. Oh yeah. The cheesecake came with some bread rounds on the side, so that you could spread it and WOW was it good. There was a nice size serving and it was buttery and rich and full of flavor. The duck waffles were amazing. Delicious flaked duck came topped on thick waffles which were then topped with syrup. It was a like a delightful breakfast treat in the afternoon.  For my entree I got the chicken salad sandwich with a side of smoky mac and cheese. I thought I was just going to get a run of the mill chicken salad sandwich, but I was totally wrong. What I got was a PILE of chicken salad on delicious bread. The chicken salad was nice and cold and I just loved it. It came with a little fruit salad on the side as well as some thinly cut pomme frites.  The mac and cheese was on point! After a less than stellar mac and cheese experience at McClure's, I was craving some good mac and cheese and Red Dog delivered! It had a ton of flavor and a ton of cheese. I was a happy camper.  My date got the lamb and brussels sprouts. He was kind enough to let me grab a bite and that dish was delicious as well. He was so excited that I suggested this place and I was so excited that I found this spot on Yelp.  I will absolutely return to Red Dog Diner: the restaurant that is so much more than a diner.

This store is a MUST for anyone who takes their costuming seriously or just wants to let their inner drag queen out with the perfect wig.  Oh yes. Fifi's has a lot of different accessories and things to make you feel glamorous, but it is definitely all about the wigs. Whether you are looking for something crazy and different or you just want something for those days when you just don't feel like doing your hair, this is you one stop shop.  I didn't get to try any wigs on this time, but I will definitely be back. I want to treat myself for the days when I just want to be someone else.

David and I were here for the Christmas lights and it was okay. The line to get in is insanely long- we waited at least 30 minutes and I feel like it could have been better organized. It's $5 to see the Christmas lights during the holiday season. They have a nice little setup of different characters and things like that. It's not quite as "extravagant" as Celebration in the Oaks, but it's a nice little thing to do for the holidays.  You can get out and walk around or you can just drive through. We drove through and it goes pretty fast if you drive. You might want to walk if you're looking to make an evening of it.

Alright. I'm ready to let you all in on an awesome secret. This place is one of the hidden gems in the New Orleans area.  Yes, The Jefferson Orleans North is a reception hall. Yes, you can have a Sweet 16 or a wedding here. But there's something else. Something I just discovered myself. On Sunday nights, from 7-10, The Jefferson Orleans North hosts The Pat Barberot Orchestra, which is a real big band. Not only that, but you can actually dance. Like...real dancing. Like the type of dancing that they did in the 40's and 50's where you actually hold someone close and move around the dance floor.  I understand that the Jefferson Orleans has been holding these weekly dances since the 70's. My grandmother used to come here in the 80's. Also, and I just have to be honest, most of the people who actually go to dance are in their 70's, 80's and even 90's. And they are the most delightful people in the world and quickly make you realize that you are never too old for a spin around the dance floor.   So, why do I like it here? Because when you are on the huge dance floor and listening to a real big band, you are transported to a different time. You're transported to a time when life was a bit simpler and the music was really good.  Maybe you are thinking, "Well, that sounds good and all, but I don't know how to dance." Okay, well neither do I. I know the basic box step and a few small swing steps and that's about it. I'm not going to be winning any dancing contests any time soon. But I still have so much fun and all of the people who actually do know how to dance are always encouraging.  The dancers at the Jefferson Orleans are so excited when younger people come in and I promised them that I would do my best to bring in new faces. So, that's where you come in. Put on your best dress or suit (yes, it's that type of vibe) and join us on a Sunday night at 6:30. If you want, feel free to shoot me a message and I will let you know when I will be there, so that you will see a familiar face. I guarantee that you will have a good time.

As a self proclaimed "lover of all things glamorous", I couldn't wait to visit the Sazerac bar in the Roosevelt, when it reopened.  I went about a year ago before the first annual N.O. Burlesque fest.  I was dressed all "pinuppy" and I felt like I fit right in.  The bartenders were wonderful and the atmosphere was fantastic.  I felt like I was stepping back into a different time.    The Roosevelt itself is gorgeous and has a very "classic" feel.  I dressed up to go, but it's not necessary.    Great date place, because the atmosphere is cozy.  You can sit at a bar and they also have tables and a little sofa area.

This event was super fun and a little bit unexpected.  John told me about this event and asked me if I would want to tag along, so I was definitely down, even though I don't smoke cigars or usually drink whiskey. I figured that this would be a good opportunity to try something new.  We got to the place and I was immediately impressed that Yelp had the entire back room. There was plenty of space for everyone to sit and mingle it all started with a good vibe. To start we were all given a complimentary old fashioned and the owner of Cuban Creations, Kevin, told us a little about this place and what it's all about. It turns out, it's the only business in the French Quarter where you can still smoke and they offer cigars and whiskey of all times.  Kevin passed out the cigars and explained the basics of smoking. I'm not a smoker at all, but the cigar I tried was very light and easy to puff on. It didn't make me cough or anything, so it was perfect for a beginner like me. We also sampled a few whiskeys and, since I'm not a big whiskey drinker, I appreciated that it was only a small taste. The whiskeys were good sippers with no "burn", so I enjoyed them.  As always, it was great seeing my fellow Yelpers and I had a really great time being out of my comfort zone and trying something a little different. Thank you Tomas for organizing this awesome event and thank you Kevin for having us!

Bridge city, chick. Bridge bridge city, chick.  So, what happens when the Gretna Waffle House and the Harvey Waffle House are both packed to the gills with hungry parade goers? You find yourself in Bridge City, apparently.  We walked in and this place was packed, but most people were waiting on their "go" order, so we sat at a booth. It took a minute for the waitress to acknowledge us, but we ordered our All Stars and I got extra hash browns because I was super hungry after hitting parades. My food came out pretty timely, but I got sausage instead of bacon, so the waitress comped that and gave me my bacon and my waffle was late, so she comped my extra hash browns. It's Waffle House mathl no complaints here. Extra meats and free hash browns makes this kid super happy.  She was pretty timely with my coffee refills and the food came out fast and hot, even though the place was packed. We wouldn't come here again, unless it was absolutely necessary, but the food was good and our waitress was great.  If you're in Bridge City, get your breakfast fix here.

By the beard of Rex, this parade was generous! So, this was my first ever Rex parade. I may have attended another, but I was probably a kid so who the heck knows? We planted ourselves outside Avenue Pub (my idea, cough cough) and it turned out to be the perfect spot. There was nice cover by the balcony, thin drink and bathroom lines and we stood underneath the balcony happily catching throws.  Oh hey, did you know that each float in Rex throws their own unique throw? I didn't! But you better believe I was doing my best to collect signature throws from every float. Some floats were better than others- some stalled and some zipped by. I know that Rex is the King of Carnival, but who cares? I'm here for the throws.   We had a good time catching beads and this krewe was throwing and having a good time, so I was pleased. Also, I got to see the St. Aug Marching 100, which is always a treat. I'm excited I caught it maybe for the first...or second time.

Can you believe that I have lived in New Orleans my entire life (9th generation, if you want the facts) and I have never had a Plum Street snowball? I know! It's almost embarrassing, especially considering the fact that Plum Street is one of the more famous stands in town.  David and I headed over and it was a little later (around 7), but lucky for us, they were still serving up the sugar. The stand is tucked into the middle of a neighborhood, so you'll miss it if you don't know what you're looking for.  I got the strawberry shortcake snowball in a cup and watching them make it was something to behold. They DOUSE this thing in syrup, y'all. They don't hold back on the juice at all! The flavor I chose was super sweet and creamy and I love how fine the ice is. For those of you who are new to snowballs: it's all about the ice. Chunky ice can totally ruin the snowball experience.  The snowball I had here was so good that I wanted to go back the next day. It was probably the best "classic" snowball I have had in a long time. Needless to say, this spot is a "must".

Bub's NOLA is a tasty addition to the New Orleans burger scene.  I love that their burgers are smashed, so that they are nice and crispy and delicious. You can get them dressed or with bacon and, of course, a side of cheese fries.  My one teeny complaint was, on the day that I went, it was super hot and they didn't have air conditioning (this might have changed in a month or so since I visited), so eating inside was pretty brutal. They do have outdoor seating, if you want to enjoy some sidewalk life. They are also right next door to Banks St. Bar, so you can pop over and get a beer.

I had been to Koz's once before, but there was a pretty insane line at lunch, so I ended up leaving. The second time I tried Koz's I got to completely skip the line, because I ordered via the Waitr app and they brought the food to me. Obviously, this is a review of just the food and not the service.  I decided to get a muffaletta half and a large potato salad. I think my total was $11, which wasn't bad at all. The muffaletta was perfect! The bread was soft- which I like, there was plenty of meat and olive salad and it was doused in olive oil. Also, a "half" muffaletta is still pretty big and plenty enough for lunch all on it's own. The potato salad was a white potato salad and it was just okay. I'll admit that I am kind of picky when it comes to potato salad and this one was lacking something and it didn't have much flavor. I ended up packing it up and taking it home where I added salt and pepper, and that was an improvement, but I probably wouldn't order it again.  All in all, I enjoyed my lunch and since Koz's has one of the best muffalettas I've tried, I'll probably be back.

While I can't give the Super Bowl this year 5 stars (the Saints weren't in it!) I have to say that I am really proud of New Orleans right now. Not only did we host the Super Bowl, but we showed the world that New Orleans is able to host a huge event (almost) without a hitch.  Yeah yeah, so the lights when out for about 30 minutes. Big deal. You know how NOLA works; we will do anything in our power to keep the party going for as long as possible.  All in all I had a great time enjoying Super Bowl festivities and I was glad to see a lot of locals out and about having a blast with our visitors.

This post office has slipped down hill in the past few years. I'm in a line 6 deep with one person working and this is all the time. Why not hire more people? This woman is ringing everyone up and fetching packages. This isn't just today- it's all the time. Very frustrating when you have things to get done. I don't blame the one person working, I blame the entire system.   I won't even mention the days my mail goes completely undelivered.

I went to a wedding here and I really enjoyed the place. It's probably not the fanciest venue to hold a party or a wedding, but it gets the job done. I remember that the wedding I attended here was outside in the courtyard at night and it was really nicely lit and cozy.  Fun fact: my 10 year high school reunion was held here. I didn't attend.

I love Mid City for a few reasons. First of all, it has really come a long way since Katrina. It's expanding and getting better every year. New businesses are opening all the time, there is a good vibe wherever you go, and it seems that every time I turn around someone else I know is moving here.  I love Bayou St. John and the fact that you can go kayaking on the water. It's such a quaint atmosphere and has such a nice "homey" type of feel.  Favorite restaurants: Felipe's,Toups, Theo's, Dooky Chase and Angelo Brocato (of course). Favorite bar: Bayou Beer Garden because of the extensive amount of beers they have as well as the nice patio that sometimes hosts live music. Also, City Park is in Mid City and I love City Park.

David and I decided to stop in here on St Patrick's day, of all days, to try something a little different and get a bite to eat. First of all, I love the layout of the space. Plenty of light and I can see myself sitting on the gorgeous patio outside on a nice spring day.  David and I both got the hamburger and we got an order of the mac and cheese to share. The hamburgers were fantastic! I think David complained that his had a little too much onion on it, but that's an easy fix. The mac and cheese was out of this world. Very creamy and I like the big noodles they used.  I saw someone at another table yet a amazing looking bowl of French onion soup, so that's definitely on my list to try next time.

A Korean restaurant might not be your first thought when you think of barbecue, but You should definitely pay this spot a visit. Little Korea BBQ has a menu with barbecue faves like BBQ chicken, pork belly and beef short ribs. They even have the option of grilling your own food at your table, if you feel like having a culinary adventure. If you'd rather let the kitchen do the cooking, that's an option as well.  I had the Garlic Samgyupsal ($17) - Garlic pork belly that was delicious and tender and served with white rice and sautéed vegetables. I also got a side of the Baked Corn Cheese ($8) which is sweet corn covered in a thick layer of mozzarella cheese and baked; it comes out sizzling and it's a combination that you wouldn't expect to work, but totally does!  I made a list of best hidden BBQ for Very Local New Orleans and this l restaurant was on it! Read it here: https://nola.verylocal.com/bbq-new-orleans/228292/

I have been passing this place for a couple of years now and I finally decided to stop in and grab an iced coffee. I had no idea how teeny tiny it is on the inside- they share a space with the Herb Import Company. The shop itself is basically a stand but there is a patio area outside where you can hang out, if you want.  The iced coffee is priced well and I really liked it. It was full body and had good flavor without having so much caffeine that I wanted to run a marathon right after drinking it- perfect. The woman working at the counter was very nice and friendly and greeted everyone with a smile.  While this wouldn't be my first stop for iced coffee, I have no complaints about the brew I had here.

This is a nice market, if you're in the area. I recently had lunch across the street and took the opportunity to pick up a few things since it was close by. It's one of the "newer" Rouses, so everything is really nice and the layout is excellent with lots of space and the "New Orleans theme" that Rouses is known for.  I was in and out of here pretty quickly with no problems. Tip: don't park in the lot unless you're shopping here. There's a security guard patrolling who called out someone who parked in the lot and tried to head across the street. I think they will even tow you if they notice that your car has been parked there for an extended period of time.

Robert is fantastic! I almost feel that it's similar to Whole Foods, minus the attitude, if that makes sense.  I happened to be in the neighborhood and I had to pick up some supplies for a co-worker's birthday and Robert had just the stuff. I found some catering trays that were ready to go and a doberge cake that I was able to pick up, without having to order ahead.  While this store is fairly small, they have a nice variety of things to choose from and the prices are reasonable.

Sit back and grab a snack, because this is gonna be a long one.  I've heard about Pêche forever. I've heard it's great. I've heard it's a must. I got funny looks when I told people I had never been. I even recommended it to folks visiting, just because I had heard how great it is, but I had never been there myself.  When I decided that I wanted my birthday to be a food extravaganza, Pêche was at the top of my list. I came here with my dad and, just in time, Pêche had just been named one of the top New Orleans restaurants of 2017. I made reservations more than a month out. I was prepared. I'm glad because when we got here at 7 on a Thursday it wasn't just packed, it was PACKED. Every table was full- wall to wall full.  Happily, we were seated immediately at a table right along the wall. Perfect! When I told the members of a food group that I'm a part of that I was going to Pêche they had many suggestions. Fried bread! Shrimp toast! Whole fish! I said "yes" to all of it. It's my birthday, I DO WHAT I WANT!  Fried bread: Uh, bread that's fried. Yes. Topped with salt makes it perfection. A nice crust on the outside and soft, tender bread on the inside made this appetizer a delight.  Shrimp toast: It was flaky and delicious. WOW. This was delectable and packed with flavor. I had pretty much starved myself for the whole day to experience this and it was worth it. All the way.  Whole fish: Everyone told me to get the whole fish when I go to Pêche, so I got the whole fish. I had two choices: one was big enough for two people to share and yes, I was very tempted to get this $50 fish all for myself, but instead I went with the trout that is made for one person to enjoy. The fish came just as God made it (head and tail attached) and battered and fried to perfection. This was a nice size fish, but I had no problem finishing it with the quickness. The meat was tender and it came right off of the bone easily. I've had a whole fish at other places and there are always those tiny bones to contend with, but at Pêche I was able to easily remove them. The waiter who cleared my plate commented, "That's how you eat!" and I felt pretty proud of myself for eating it all. It was also topped with some greens, but they honestly came second to the fish.  Drum: My dad got this dish and he loved it. In fact, not only did my father finish this dish (which never happens), but he raved about how good it was. For those of you who don't know my dad, that is a ringing endorsement. Trust me, people.  Because I wasn't done eating, for dessert I got the salted peanut pie, which came topped with ice cream. It was delicious and is a must for any peanut butter lover. It was all topped with a chocolate sauce drizzle and they made me feel special when they put a birthday candle on the plate.  I LOVED my experience at Pêche and I will absolutely return. Everything was perfect from start to finish and it's easy to see why Pêche is considered one of the top restaurants in New Orleans. It's restaurants like this that make me thankful for my fast metabolism.

This is where we started the Metry bar crawl. I had never been here before, so of course I got a little lost, but once I found the place it was all good.  This is a nice little bar. They have a pool table and a section with dart boards. There's a lot of room so that you don't feel cramped. Not super bright, which I liked. The music was pretty current and nothing overly dated played.  Friendly staff. I was doing "mocktails", so I ordered a cranberry and ginger ale, which I was given free of charge.
This was a beautiful parade with a lot of great throws.  Really generous to kids and a really good time.

As someone who knows pretty much nothing about how to make pho, but everything about how to eat it and what I like, I give TD Pho House a big 5 stars.  I saw that this place was opening and I didn't think much of it. The Westbank seems to have a lot of these hole-in-the-wall pho places and most of them are decent, but nothing spectacular and they usually don't stick around for very long. I started seeing raves about the newly opened TD Seafood Pho House and I was intrigued, so I recommended it for a work dinner.  The inside has been completely renovated from when it was another Vietnamese restaurant. It's bright, modern and welcoming with a big sparkly bar, booths and TVs on the wall showing football. I got an order of Pho Tai Gau and we also got some egg rolls and pork spring rolls. The egg rolls were good, and although they were likely from a bag, I enjoyed them. The spring rolls were great! They were nice and big and the pork was really good and had a lot of flavor.  The Pho Tai Gau is when things got crazy- I think this might be one of the best bowls of pho I have ever had and I'm not exaggerating. It was packed with flavor, the meat was beyond generous and tender and the broth was super tasty. Like I said, I'm not a pho expert, and I'm not a pho snob like some people, but I know what I like and I really liked this. My "go to" bowl of pho is Pho Bang, also on Manhattan, and I want to say that the bowl here knocks Pho Bang out of the water. I would absolutely return for another bowl of this stuff, again and again.  As the name says, they also have seafood here and you can get crab, shrimp and crawfish, if you're in the mood. The food came out fast and the staff was friendly. I'll be back!

I was SO excited about a Fresh Market opening Uptown!  I had heard so many good things about the location on the Northshore and I knew a Fresh Market would fit in great here.  So, what is Fresh Market?  Well, it's like Whole Foods, but not as snobby.  Located in the former Borders bookstore location, this brand new store is beautifully clean and organized.  There's a beautiful selection of assorted flowers and an entire wall of produce.  You can buy ready to eat meals, such as chicken dinners and they even have fresh sushi here!  I was blown away by the fresh baked goods, and although I didn't purchase any this time, I will definitely be back to try one of the gorgeous cakes they had on display.  I also have to add that the candy and coffee selection in this place is insane.  There is a whole wall of jellybelly jelly beans!  You can buy individual boxes or fill your own bag!  Upstairs (yes, there is an upstairs) is where a huge selection of wine is located.  There is even a nice little section with tables and chairs where you can sit and sip coffee and chat with friends.  The whole store is wonderfully decorated and has a very "homey" feel.  You almost feel as if you are in someone's really fancy (and stocked!) kitchen.  While some of the items are a little more pricey than your local Winn Dixie, there is more selection of "unusual" items (such as a fancy selection of assorted juices!) that you will enjoy.  Next time you are uptown, be sure to check this place out.  There's bound to be something here that you will like.

I couldn't wait to review this spot after I was here for lunch yesterday!  A friend and I both like trying new places, so as soon as we heard about 14 Parishes and their Caribbean food, we immediately made plans for lunch. I was here about 10 minutes before they opened (they open at 2) and the co-owner was nice enough to let me in so that I could sit down and look over the menu while I waited for my friend.  It was hard deciding what to get because everything sounded fantastic, but I settled on the Portland which is a plate of jerk chicken served with cabbage and two choices of sides. For my sides I got the plantains and the mac and cheese. The food came out and WOW- this is a lot of food for $10! Check out my picture!   First of all, I loved the chicken- it was juicy and tender and had a lot of flavor without overwhelming the meat or making it too spicy. I sometimes hesitate to order chicken at restaurants, because some places tend to overcook it, but 14 Parishes cooked theirs perfectly. The mac and cheese was just like homemade and you could tell that it was made from a family recipe. The plantains were out of this world- sweet and soft and a perfect compliment to the rest of the meal (I should mention there was a whole bowl of plantains that I didn't get a picture of- super generous.). The cabbage was also a nice touch and it combined well with the chicken.  I don't usually mention drinks, but I had a mango and carrot juice that was quite tasty and they also serve ginger beer, if that's your thing. The co-owner is the one who waited on us and she was so sweet and friendly and made sure that we were happy and had everything we needed. This might be one of the best lunch deals in town, so be sure to add 14 Parishes to your "must visit" list if you are in the mood for something different.

This parade has really slipped. This is the parade right before Orpheus and they're going to have to kick it up a notch, if they want to be a proper lead in to such a big parade.  Proteus had a few disadvantages this year: it was cold and it rolled while it was still light out, making their "blinky" beads pretty useless. Also, they seem to throw the same stuff every year and that just gets boring. The people riding always seems nice enough, so this isn't a personal attack; I just wish that there was a little more variety from year to year.

I was having a "college bar" adventure with a friend when we ended up at Bruno's. I have been to Bruno's a lot over the years and it's pretty much one of those "it is what it is" type of places. It's a good space with plenty of room, pool tables, video poker and typical bar fun like that.  Honestly, it's a typical college bar and if you aren't a college kid you'll probably feel weird hanging out here. Or maybe that's just me. ha. I will say that they have a pretty decent beer selection and the bartenders are always fast, even when the place is crowded.

This is a cute shop with nice clothes and an awesome staff.  I was in here looking for some vacation clothes, and even though they sell things that are a little nicer than what I need, the woman working was really great in helping me find some pieces that might work for me. They sell a little bit of everything here from crop tops to skirts to dresses. The prices are reasonable for the quality and I loved that there is such a variety of different colors, especially pastels. I didn't find exactly what I needed here, but the friendly staff and variety of items guarantees my return.

It's a Starbucks like any other Starbucks.  Overpriced coffee drinks served by people who don't have any idea what they are doing (how hard is it to remember that I want SKIM milk in my iced coffee or no whip on my frap??).  This particular Starbucks is a former bank that has been converted (it's the Westbank way!).  The parking lot is a nightmare.  On one side you can't get out of the place without playing an odd game of "musical chairs" with whoever is in the drive through.  On the other side, they squeezed parking spots in by the drive through area.  Good luck getting out of your spot if the drive through has a line.  It's not happening.  I usually only go to this Starbucks when I'm in a hurry and would rather use the drive through than have to park, order and wait.

I have adopted quite a few cats from the SPCA in my life.  This is a great organization that does it's part to help the animal community. They do free/discount neuters, spays, chips and vet care for any animal that needs it. They care for strays around town by putting out food and doing the trap and neuter routine. Basically everything they do is in the best interest of animals. I don't think I could add anything to what Jane S. has already said. She covers it all!

Uhhh... how have I never reviewed Dino's??  I have never been here where the service wasn't top notch. I sat at the bar tonight and we were treated like freakin' royalty! Do I want a lime in that cocktail? Why, yes I do and thanks for asking! It's dark and cozy here and they have Lagunitas, so I'm happy. Full disclosure: David and I were winding down our evening when we ended up here, so we weren't here very long, but so what? We came. We drank. We conquered.

I went to this place a few weeks ago, but I'm only writing a review now, because I was trying to figure out how to put it's greatness into words.  I had only heard of this place in passing when a friend of mine and I decided to check it out.  I was immediately impressed as soon as I walked into the door.  We were there for an early dinner on a weeknight, so it wasn't crowded.  There was a guitarist playing light background music in the dining room, which just made it an even more lovely experience.  As soon as we sat down, the waitress was extremely helpful about everything from wine selection to which dishes she recommended.  We started with an appetizer of blue crab beignets, which were amazing!  They were these light, fluffy pastries stuffed with delicious crab and then drizzled with a tasty sauce.  We both agreed that they were fantastic. (Sorry Scott S, maybe you were there on an "off" night.  These DEFINITELY tasted like crab to me!)  For our entree' we got the fish of the day (I think it was black fish, but don't quote me) that was cooked to perfection, and also covered with a delicious cream sauce.  Needless to say, I finished all of it.  No doggie bags, here!  I wish I had had room for dessert.  The waitress described a pecan pie with Bourbon sauce and Vanilla ice cream, which I am sure I would have adored.  I LOVE pecan pie.  I may go back one evening and sit down and try it sometime soon!  I would absolutely go back here. Between the atmosphere and the food, this is a fantastic place to start an evening.

I'm usually not one to update a review with the same rating, but I wanted to do it in this case, because not only have I not had an issue with Chase at all, but the staff here is fantastic.  I recently had a banking issue that I needed handled and banker Emad Jabbar went above and beyond to help me sort it out. He called a bunch of people and worked his bank magic and assured me that all would be fixed- and it was! Emad is now going to my first call for any of my banking needs. He definitely knows what he's doing and he keeps you informed throughout the entire process.

Man, I hate to do it but the 5 star rating I gave this place a few years ago is just embarrassing now.  I was here last night and I got a steak burger with cheese and steak fries. I ordered the burger cooked medium and it was way over-cooked. There wasn't even a hint of pink in it at all. AT BEST it was cooked medium-well and that's being generous. My boyfriend's burger was overcooked as well, though not to the extent that mine was. Service was slow and it took forever to get our check at the end of the meal. I can't totally blame the waitress, because she is working the entire dining room alone, but please hire another waitress to get things moving along a bit. Also, this place is dark- really dimly lit. I feel like I'm eating dinner in an old bar room.   I don't know, I really liked them the first time I went after the reopen, the second time I was underwhelmed but chalked it up to an off night, but last night was the night that I finally had to put my foot down and say "enough is enough".

My Tennou review is definitely due for an update.  First of all, they are doing a lot to fix the place up and it is looking really nice these days.  I now have a few "usuals" whenever I go. I always get the noodle.salad. Granted I haven't been to every sushi place in NOLA, but besides Hana or Mikimoto, this is one of the few places that I have found that has noodle salad. Please correct me if I'm wrong, because I love the stuff! You get a huge order for $3.50 and it's so good. Another fave is the salmon sashimi, which you get 7 pieces of and is still cut really thick. The Philly roll and the tuna rolls are awesome and every once in a while I'll treat myself to the salmon roe or the rainbow roll.   The food is always super fresh and the service is fast and friendly. They are always adding different special rolls, so be sure to ask about them.

*this is a review of the bar area*  We stopped in here because there was a bit of a wait at 1000 figs, so we thought a glass of wine would be nice to pass the time.  I should start by explaining that I'm not really a wine person. Sadly, I can't really tell the difference between an "okay" bottle of wine and an "excellent" bottle of wine. All I know is that I like red wine, so there it is.  This little shop has a wide selection of everything you could need and has a nice selection of bottles. I decided just to get a glass of red wine to sip on as I waited. The atmosphere here for drinking is pretty stark. There are a few tables and stools in the middle of the store. There's no real fancy sitting area or anything like that (at least none that i saw). It basically is what it is, if you are in the mood for a no frills glass of wine.  I will definitely have to go back and actually buy a bottle of wine, so that i can review again having had the "shop" experience. I get the feeling that this place does lean more towards the "buy a bottle" crowd than the "have a glass here" crowd.

Do you want cheap Mexican food and yummy margaritas??  Look no further than this gem.  Located in the Quarter, this place is fantastic and wonderfully priced!  I usually get the Taco Salad with chicken and they also have great burritos.  I introduced my boyfriend to this place, and he liked it, too.  The frozen margaritas are the best.  A great place to just sit and watch the world go by, as you eat dinner.  It's nice if you want to eat downtown, but you don't want to be in the "thick" of the whole tourist thing.

I LOVE Hana!  Whenever I go there, I feel like I'm in an exclusive Sushi cafe.  I always get a booth and the wait staff is always attentive. It does help if you go in already familiar with sushi, because their menu can be a little confusing.  My favorite is the salmon sashimi and tuna rolls.  Food is very well priced and the atmosphere is great.  My favorite sushi place in the city!

Jeff has been doing my hair here for 9 years now.  I would never go anywhere else and will probably go here until Jeff retires.  I only get my hair cut (I don't color anymore), but I am always satisfied.  The staff will work with you to give you the look you want.  I have also gotten my make up done here in the past and I am always satisfied. A+!

Rendezvous is my second favorite Magazine St. bar.  They have a great beer selection and a great crowd and atmosphere.  The place is kind of dark, which makes for a good kind of "underground" vibe.  They have booths, if you don't want to sit at the bar and they have pool tables, if you are in the mood to shoot pool.  They have a fantastic internet jukebox, and video poker, if that's your thing.  In my opinion, this place is everything that The Balcony Bar used to be.

I was here and I needed some new shoes for an event, so naturally I was going to get some Jessica Simpson heels. I love the selection of shoes here because they are well priced and the staff is knowledgeable. I ended up finding the perfect pair of (really high) black pumps that I was happy to wear to a Yelp event.  Along with shoes, this store has a nice selection of handbags and fragrances. I'm not sure if this Dillard's is bigger than the Westbank location- it seems like it, but I could be wrong. This location does seem to have a wider selection of whatever I happen to be looking for, so I would come back if I was in the area.

I know I have been reviewing a lot of pet places lately, but I guess I have been making the rounds for one reason for another.  PetSmart is a cool store. They sell animal toys and food and accessories and things of that nature. They also have quite the selection of small animals such as guinea pigs, rats and birds and they also sell fish. My favorite part is (of course) the cats that they have up for adoption. I like that the cats they have are adults. It seems that you can find kittens anywhere. Also, the facility they have for all of the animals is very nice.  They also do grooming, but I've never had anything that needed grooming, so I don't have any experience with that.

I came here looking for some wall art for an upcoming house "redecorating" and while the selection was good, I just couldn't get past a few things.  First of all, this Kirkland's was really cluttered. There were so many things for sale that there are actually things on the floor because there is no space for them anywhere else. There was limited organization which made navigation difficult.  Also, I came here ready to spend some time really looking for things, but their AC was broken and the place was sweltering hot. On a 90 degree day you really have to get someone out ASAP to fix the air situation. It was stifling and when I started to sweat in the store, I was forced to call it a day. I felt bad for the poor girl working in her long pants because she looked miserable.   I'll return, but maybe in the cooler months.

This a nice gift shop that shares a space with Parish Ink.  They have a wide selection of tshirts, home decor, Louisiana-centric items and other little conversation pieces and gifts. One interesting thing that I saw here were Mississippi River (I think) maps, that would make a good gift for a traveler or anyone who likes geology or something a little different.   On the day I stopped in, I was in a bit of a hurry and looking for a "different" type of engagement gift for a friend. I ended up getting him a leather travel wallet, which I think he will like. When I bought it, the woman was extremely nice and chatty. I'd love to return.

What can you really say about Aunt Tiki's?  It's the diveiest of all the dive bars on lower Decatur. We popped in here on New Year's Eve, of all times, because the crowd was starting to build outside and we needed an escape. This place is pretty no frills: Miller High Life in a bottle, a dirty sofa that you probably don't want to sit on and packed with locals. I had been here before and in my memory it was a lot more dim, but it was nice and bright on the evening that I returned. The crowd here is pretty chill and not as crazy as maybe some other places throughout the Quarter.  Just don't forget that you are on lower Decatur, and keep your wits about you, and you'll be fine.

This is a review of the bar area only, I didn't eat.  We found ourselves here late-ish (11 or so) one night and we were the only people in the place. We sat at the nice bar and chatted for a little while- I had a beer and my date had a cocktail. The atmosphere here is interesting, but I found it a bit cold. The lights were really bright and I guess since we were the only people here we felt a bit out of place. The staff couldn't have been nicer and they didn't rush us out the door, even though there was no one else there. It just felt like I was having a drink after the party had ended and everyone else had gone home.  I think I am going to try to go back again earlier in the evening and get some food there and see if that changes my opinion of the place.

The pizza here is huge, cheap, and delicious.  Order one slice or maybe two, because that is all you will need.  A whole pizza is gigantic and definitely needs a group to be finished.  Highly recommended, if you want to make the trek to the 'wego.

This is a really cute shop, especially if you are a collector of New Orleans themed jewelry. All of the jewelry is nicely organized and the shop owner greeted me when I came in. Some of my favorites were the Rosenberg's necklace, and the necklaces with the K&B and Schwegmann's logos. I love things like that because not only are they unique to the city, but no one else will "get it" unless they are from here. I also loved their selection of bracelets and rings with St. Louis Cathedral etched into them.  Honestly, some of the prices are a little high, but on the day that we stopped in they had a 50% off sale on the entire store. However, I can tell the quality of the jewelry is very good, and it's unique, so I think it's worth the money. This is your one stop shop for any New Orleans lover or collector in your life.

Pelham was a nice hotel and while it wasn't a Pontchartrain-level experience, I enjoyed it here.   The room was fairly small, but reasonable. This is definitely the type of hotel you stay in if you are going to be out and about in the city all day and you just need a place to sleep/change/shower. It's no frills, but the room was clean and the staff was friendly.  24 hour parking is right across the street for $36/day. Do the smart thing and park your ride and Uber around the city- you will end up saving money in the long run. Also, the hotel is located close enough to the Quarter that you can even walk to and from during the day, if the weather is nice.

Ding! Bumping up to five stars because I stopped in today for sunscreen because I don't want to burn. #palelife  I grabbed the CVS brand SPF 50 for $8. Works for me! There was a dude who was shopping with me who got the $24 sunscreen. Lah. Dee. Dah. The line moved fast in the middle of Mardi Gras madness and I left feeling not ripped off. A win all around. I would shop here again.

If Hana is my favorite sushi place, then Tennou is a close second.  Great salmon sashimi (the pieces are always THICK) and nice sized Philly rolls. I usually go for lunch or an early dinner.  I always leave full and satisfied.  Great atmosphere and wait staff.

This is a really cool bar, even if it is a little out of the way.  First of all, I don't know if I would refer to this bar as a "dive" bar. To me, a dive bar is a different animal entirely, but maybe that's just me.  This is a nice little neighborhood bar full of friendly people and personable staff. When I first stopped in here, I was surprised to see how big it is on the inside. It's pretty roomy with plenty of tables and chairs and I can see it being a really good place to watch the game.

Why did it take me SO long to get to The Joint?  Me and a friend came here for lunch after I told him that I had never experienced the magic of The Joint. It was a Monday, at around 1, so the place was fairly empty and there was no line. I walked up to the counter and decided to get the pulled pork sandwich topped with cole slaw and mac and cheese. This is my usual "go to" barbecue place meal and I think a pretty good way to judge how good a barbecue restaurant is.  My order came out super fast and I was so excited to dig in. Check out the picture of me at The Joint under my profile pics- all smiles. Well, DANG! This pulled pork was juicy and flavorful and didn't need a bit of sauce, y'all. The cole slaw added the perfect amount of crispiness to it and it tasted beyond fresh. The mac and cheese was out of this world. It was super cheesy with a little hint of smoke to it.  I would never call myself any type of barbecue expert, but I think this place is pretty awesome. I love the "down home" atmosphere, the family style seating and the amazing food. I can see why so many people are in love with this place and I am now a member of that club.

I really like this place and I've been coming here for years.  I don't know if I would call this a "legitimate" Irish pub, but if you are in the mood for Harp or Guinness, they have it. While it isn't the cleanest bar in the world, it does attract a good crowd and they have bands playing almost nightly.  I like that you can sit at the bar and get a French Quarter vibe without going deep into the Quarter or dealing with tourists. That's another thing; this isn't an overly touristy spot, so if you are looking to escape that type of crowd, look no further than the Kerry.  Point of interest: all of the dollar bills stapled to the ceiling above and around the bar. I don't know what they story is there, but it's pretty cool. Check out my picture.  Bonus points: plenty of available outlets for a quick phone charge while you drink your beer.
I love Ruby Red's!  I usually get the steak burger with cheese and fries.  Family owned place and the staff is really nice.  Great for lunch!

I liked this Michael's, but my biggest complaint was that I couldn't find what I was looking for and locating staff was nearly impossible.  I was here looking for some specific arts and crafts type materials, that someone had told me to purchase here for a project I'm working on. I don't know enough about Michael's stores to just be able to locate exactly what I need in a big store, so naturally I looked for some staff to help. The only staff I could find was checking people out- there was no one on the floor. I wandered around for probably 15 minutes before I finally just gave up and resigned myself to trying my regular Michael's on the Westbank. I would have made a bigger point of trying to wave someone off of a register, but since I had just stopped into this store because I was in the area, I decided not to bother.

Amazing.  I've passed this place hundreds of times, but had never tried it until recently!  The food here was great.  For a starter, I got a "mini" French onion soup.  It came served in what was basically a coffee cup and was a perfect appetizer.  The soup wasn't anything fancy, but it was hot and cheesy and I really liked it.  My friend and I decided to split an entree.  We got the manicotti, which came with a salad and cheese bread.  It was delicious.  Splitting the entree was a really good idea, because coupled with the bread, it was the perfect amount of food, since we were going somewhere and didn't want to have to deal with leftovers.  They had an assorted sandwich menu and I really want to go back and try some of the other food they have.  Their menu is well priced and you definitely get your money's worth, when you get dinner here.

All the credit goes to David for discovering this place through Instagram. After seeing all of the delicious pictures of various things coated in a thick layer of cheese, as well as mac and cheese piled high on top of things, I knew we had to see this place for ourselves.  First of all, Faubourg Bistro is located in the back of a bar, but it's a really fun bar, so don't let that stop you from visiting. We went at around 6 on a Saturday and it was a pretty chill crowd. We had already scoped out the menu online and while they didn't have one thing we wanted (no crawfish grilled cheese, since it isn't crawfish season), they did have the skillet pizza mac and cheese that we had our eye on. We each got an order.   After a brief wait we were presented with a personal skillet of mac and cheese layered with tomato sauce and topped with pepperoni. As soon as I dug in the cheese oozed and mixed with the sauce and made the macaroni nice and ooey gooey. THIS MIGHT BE ONE OF MY NEW FAVORITE THINGS! The dish was so rich and I couldn't get enough. It also came with garlic bread on the side, in case you want to spread your carbs on top of more carbs (and of course you do!).  Needless to say, I got through about half of this thing and took the rest home for later. I am happy to report that it is just as good upon reheating! Truth me told, David and I could have easily split this dish and left happy. We have a plan for next time: we are going to order a cheeseburger and a skillet pizza mac and split it. There is so much yum on the menu that we are bound to be back a few times over.

I think you might need a special card or membership to shop here. Fortunately, I have some friends who are in the process of opening a business, so when they go here they let me tag along.  This place is basically Costco on steroids. Everything is in HUGE portions, because it's meant to be used in restaurants and business stuff like that. The deals here are amazing, if you have a place to store the stuff. This is basically your one stop shop if a huge hurricane is pending and you need to stock up on goods.  On the day we went, my friends were stocking up on produce which was super fresh and well priced.  I would love to come back here during crawfish season, to get some mudbugs for a boil. The store is cold, so bring a sweater. If you have the means, I highly suggest shopping here.

This place is pretty genius. I imagine the first conversation that ultimately lead to this place existing went like this, "Hey, what do people love?" "Cheap drinks and patios!" "Perfect! Let's tap some wine and offer delicious cheese plates and other goodies to go with it." "Done and done!"  I was excited to finally check this place out on Saturday night. Pretty much everyone I know who has been here has raved about it, so I figured I would enjoy it. I've been a fan of Bayou Beer Garden for obvious reasons, so taking that same premise and applying it to wine is just plain brilliant.  We got here around 10 and the place was packed. First we tried to find a spot on the patio, but since that proved to be impossible, we headed inside. Lucky for us, there was plenty of seating at the bar. They have a pretty big menu of a lot of different wines, including a nice selection of wine on tap. Because I'm not a wine expert, I went for a few cheap reds which I really enjoyed.  I was able to glance at the food menu and if I hadn't just completely stuffed myself at dinner, I would have gotten a yummy cheese plate or one of the other food items they offered. The entire menu sounded amazing and I am going to have to go back and sample a few things.  I love the atmosphere here and I imagine that the place is only going to grow in popularity as the months pass. The patio is huge and I am going to make a point of getting here on the earlier side next time, so I can sit outside and take advantage of the nice weather. The bartenders work really fast and are great at keeping up with the crowd. We didn't have to wait longer than just a minute or two to be served between drinks.

Macy's is my kind of store. It's a big, fancy department store that isn't afraid of a sale.  I decided to stop in here after Christmas to check out their "after Christmas" sales. They had a lot marked down, and although I was in the market for fancy shoes that I wasn't able to locate, I was still impressed by everything that they had to offer. The store itself is huge and has everything from clothing to higher end makeup, just like any department store. You are more likely to find "name brands" here than any other place. There is staff everywhere and I noticed that none of the checkout lines were super long, even though there were a good number of people in the place. They seem to be on top of things.  One thing that I don't really like about this store is the parking garage. It's just oddly built and a little convoluted for the purpose it's trying to serve. I mean, I guess that it's convenient, because it's connected right to the store, but I would prefer a regular parking lot. I get it, they need a lot of levels for a store of that size.   I'll be back, if I need something and I'm in the area.

I was having a sushi craving that demanded satisfaction, so I headed over to the newest sushi place on Poydras.  I popped in during a busy lunch hour and I was seated at the sushi bar- right in the middle of the excitement! The sushi chefs greeted me and I looked over the menu and tried to decide exactly what I wanted.  After ordering a few rolls, I was given a complimentary clear soup that made for a delightful start to the meal. Because I went during the busiest time of the day, the food took a little while but I knew that it would be worth the wait.   This is what I got: Miami Roll- This is their version of a Philly roll with salmon in place of tuna. It was perfect, fresh and good.  Angel Roll- This is a roll with crab inside and avocado and salmon wrapped on the outside. I really enjoyed this because it was light but still packed a lot of flavor.  Sashimi Roll- This was my favorite! This was a HUGE roll with crab, avocado, crab stick, tuna, salmon and white fish with cucumber on the outside. It was out-of-this-world good, really fresh and flavorful and I would order this roll again.  The sushi chef who was making my rolls mentioned that it was his first day and he did a great job! I was honored to be one of his first customers. The staff is very friendly and attentive, even if you're sitting at the sushi bar. I usually hate sitting at the sushi bar because I think the wait staff tends to forget about people over there, but Osaka was great.  I can see this place becoming one of the "must try" sushi places in the area and I will be back.

The first thing I would tell anyone headed to this place is to not expect this to be a quick trip.  First of all, the place is small and every inch of it is packed with dresses and garments.  It's wall to wall.  A lot of them are bagged in plastic, so you have to really search through the stuff if you are looking for something specific.  They do have great deals and the staff is really helpful.  You will definitely find a treasure, if you take the time to look.    Be sure to head to the back for some vintage, but more expensive finds.  Definitely worth the trip.

I was brought here for the first time last week.  I don't have any experience with Pho, so trying this kind of food is always an adventure for me.  I ended up ordering the pho with glass noodles and wontons in it and it was really good.  We also had spring rolls, which were different, but weren't too bad  The staff was really nice.  I'm giving this place only 3 stars because the place is super small and cramped, and I felt like I was eating in my school cafeteria.  It wouldn't be my first choice, but I wouldn't balk if someone brought me.

This is an adorable shop, if you are or someone you know tends to gravitate towards gifts that are a little "different".  I stopped in here on black Friday weekend to do some early Christmas shopping, when I came across this place. I would say that this place is like Claire's for adults. They have so many cute little things such as snowball and Hubigs pie magnets, unicorn horn headbands, earrings, other jewelry and kitschy candles. Many of the products are made locally and have a "New Orleans lean" to them, so this is a good place to shop if you are looking for some NOLA souvenirs but you don't want to venture into one of the French Quarter shops.  I picked up a few cool jewelry pieces while I was here and I will definitely return to see what else they have to offer.

This is a really cool place with a really cool vibe.  It's a neighborhood bar located in the heart of Algiers, and most people who go here either live in the neighborhood, or live on the other side of the river within biking distance of the ferry.  On the day that I went, it was nice out and all of the doors were open.  The people here were friendly and the atmosphere made you forget that you were on the Westbank.  Also, the bar is dog friendly, so feel free to bring you furry friend with you, if you are in the mood for a drink.  This is a great place if you want to just catch up with friends and hang out for a few hours.

Dat Dog. Dat Doooog. On Magazine St. is a little Dat Dog!   Get it? Like Cat Dog! I think of that every time I hear "Dat Dog", but I digress.  Stopped in here the other night for a munch and I actually tried something other than my usual gator dog! I'll get to that in a minute.   Whoa! This place is pretty huge! And with a full bar, it seems like a really cool place to hang out with friends and get a good bite to eat.  I ended up getting the hot sausage topped with cheese and onions. It was pretty good. The hot sausage could have been hotter. It could have been WAY hotter. I actually added some Crystal sauce to it in order to give it a little kick, but all in all it was pretty good. I think that I am going to stick to my gator dog when I go back though.  The staff was super friendly and talkative and asking about my night, so that was nice. I like feeling welcome at places like this.
