I probably won't be back. Next time I am in the mood for El Mesquite, I will just go and get the real thing.

I barely even know where to start about my experience here. I went with someone who is a sort of sushi expert, so I didn't get any of my "not really sushi" things like Philly rolls and crunchy rolls. We were going authentic here (for the most part).  When I told a friend of mine I had never eaten here, he was shocked. He knows that I like the raw stuff and he insisted that we go and get dinner here. Fine, twist my arm. I let him order and I only knew for sure that I wanted one thing: the tuna sandwich. I'll get to that in a bit.  We started with the Ankimo, which is steamed monkfish liver and the assorted pickles. I'm a pretty big fan of liver of all types, so the Ankimo was right up my alley and I really enjoyed it. The assorted pickles were yummy and were a nice start to the meal.   Next we ordered the tuna sandwich, an Ume roll, a spicy tuna roll and a yummy fatty fish that I can't remember the name of. The tuna sandwich was really good. It was blue crab that was sandwiched between two pieces of tuna sashimi. It was a total mayonnaise bomb, but I liked it a lot and it was a yummy guilty treat. Next was the Ume which was pickled plum in rice and seaweed. This was incredible! I wasn't expecting to like something that was this simple, but it was really good and it was packed with flavor. The fatty fish sushi and the spicy tuna roll were both perfect and I would order both again.  For dessert we had Tamago, which is a delicious egg custard served over rice in the same style that sushi is served. Apparently, you need special training in order to be able to make Tamago and only a few places in NOLA actually serve it. I liked it a lot, and while it was odd having rice with something sweet, somehow it worked.  I knew that this place was "legit" when a large party of Japanese men came in, didn't speak a word of English and ordered a TON of food that all looked incredible. Seriously, I wanted to be invited to that party.  I finally see why this sushi spot makes every "top restaurants in NOLA" list that ever comes out. I will absolutely return next time I'm in the mood for sushi in Metairie.

How can you go wrong with a place with huge pictures of "old time" movie stars on the wall?  An offshoot of the World War 2 museum, my boyfriend and I ate here before going to the Ogden (it's right across the street).  We didn't have a lot of time, so we decided to just get an app.  We ended up splitting the mini cheeseburgers and they were DELICIOUS.  I mean, the place IS a John Besh restaurant, so it's only the best.  We were also given flavored pickle spears, which sounds odd, but they were really good.  I could definitely see going back to this place for a night out with friends.  They also have a nightly show called the "Stage Door Canteen" that is set in the time of the 40's, during the war.  I haven't seen it yet, but it is definitely on my "to do" list!

There's a reason why this is called the "best" of all the Popeyes in the city and why Eastbankers will travel all the way to the Westside, in order to come to this one.  The chicken here is always consistently fresh and hot.  I wouldn't say that it's cooked to order, but it's darn close.  The chicken just seems crispier here, than at other Popeyes.

90.7 FM on the dial!  Definitely my favorite radio station for really good old (and new) music.  I love the variety of music that they play from jazz to blues to funk.  This is the station that introduced me to Rebirth Brass Band years ago!  They play some old music on vinyl records, which I really enjoy.  This station is a "must" for any local or visitor trying to get into the "spirit" of the city.  Also a great listen for those who miss WBYU.  Not quite the same, but the closest thing to it on air in the city.

I ended up here on my quest for live music. I actually found it here but dang, why is y'all's ac not pumping in the middle of a New Orleans August?  We were loving the music and loving the cocktails, but we couldn't hang out for very long because I was starting to puddle and that's not a good look. It was HOT. I love the layout of this spot- it's obviously an old house that has been converted and I love that the front room has a nice bar and the performer(s) while the back rooms are more relaxed and social.   Four stars because the atmosphere won me over and I can see myself coming back when the weather is a little cooler.

We were strolling down Frenchmen, when we heard music coming out of here and saw a crowd, so we decided to check it out.  It has been a while since I have been to Frenchmen, but I think that this place is pretty new- at least, it feels new. You walk in and the stage is right next to the front door, there are tables and chairs throughout and a nice long bar. One of the best parts of the downstairs are the huge screens so that you can see the band, even if there's a crowd.  We headed upstairs, just to see what was going on and it's more "club mode" up there. We arrived early in the evening, so there weren't a ton of people, but there was a huge dance floor and another nice bar. The cool thing about the upstairs is that they have a balcony, so a lot of people were taking advantage of that and enjoying the nice evening.  This place is a lot better than a lot of other music clubs on the street that get jam packed quickly and are uncomfortable to the point that you can barely move. The band that was playing was solid and everyone was having a good time. I'd return.

Clever clever...  The idea of this place is that they will put all of this cool stuff up for sale right next to bars and other tourist traps so you will definitely want to buy something. Here you can find special candles and incense and books. I swear, I was thisclose to buying some candles. I doubt any of the things sold here are legit voodoo things, but it's a cool place for someone to stop in for the novelty and fun of it.

After passing this place over and over, I finally decided to stop in for lunch.  First of all, although the restaurant is pretty new, I knew I was in a good place for Pho when there were multiple older Vietnamese people sitting around eating when I walked in. I mean, you gotta figure these are the folks who know their Pho. They grew up on it. They make it themselves. I knew that I was in for a treat.  Looking over my menu I saw that I had a lot of choices. I liked that they "broke it down" for those of us who aren't familiar with Vietnamese or what is in certain types of Pho. For my meal, I decided on the pork Spring rolls and the beef brisket with rice noodles. The order of Spring rolls came two to an order, but they were a pretty good size. I was even unable to finish mine, because I munched on it as I ate my Pho. The beef brisket Pho was amazing. The broth was flavorful and there were big pieces of beef in it. It was super good and I wasn't able to finish it all, even though I got the "small" bowl. I really liked the noodles. At Pho Tau Bay (my usual go to) I usually get the glass noodles because I'm not crazy about rice noodles. Here they were fantastic.   Also, big props to me for not using the FORKS they brought out for the white folks (me and my friend) at the Pho restaurant! All chopsticks for me, baby!  Dare I say it? This place MIGHT almost edge Pho Tau Bay out of the top spot for my favorite Pho place. Maybe I was super hungry today or maybe I'm giving extra points because it was cold out. I'll have to (gladly) return in order to make a final decision.  All in all the meal was fantastic and I will definitely be back.

This is the type of bar I think of when I think of divey New Orleans bars- it's dark and secluded and has a good crowd.  We stopped in here after dinner one night and even though it was semi early in the evening, the night was already well under way for a lot of folks. I like that the bar is a bit cozy and mysterious and they are generous with the pours. My friend was really digging the video poker machines in the back, and they seemed to be paying well on this particular night.  We had fun picking out songs on the jukebox and sitting at the bar and chatting with our fellow patrons as we let the night drift by. The bartender was friendly and welcoming and we had a great time.

You can keep Port of Call.  In my opinion, this is the best burger place in the city.  They serve a lot of other things, including hot dogs, but if you want good food order a burger with everything, including cheese and onions.  It's my favorite.  I usually get a huge root beer and fries on the side.  Definitely not health food, but if you are a looking for a good local burger, this is the place to be.

Whenever someone asks if we can go to Lucy's, I always ask if we can go across the street to Tommy's instead.  This is one of the nicest and coziest spots in the city.  I have memories of coming here on Friday's in the late afternoon.  Me and some friends would look at the wine list and pick something that we had never heard of before.  Then we would just hang out and talk and catch up.  Day would turn into night and a woman would start singing with piano accompaniment, as the after dinner crowd started to file in.  Older men in untied ties would sit at the bar and have a glass or two and discuss their day.  There's just something amazingly "old school" about it.  You feel a little out of place, but not in a bad way.     I would suggest Tommy's to anyone who is looking for a different bar experience.  Anyone who is looking for something a little more classic that your average watering hole.

I don't know if you can really call this a legitimate mall. It has a Target, an AMC theater and a few shops here and there, but it's really nothing spectacular. I don't even think that anyone would go out of their way to go to this mall. It's more of a nice place to walk around while you are waiting for your movie to start. Sorry for all of the "hate", but there are a lot of other way better malls out there. Lakeside is  minutes away.

I love the Lakefront. I first started coming here back in high school on weekends. My friends and I would gather and hang out by the car listening to music with a bunch of other high school students who were doing the same thing. I don't really remember cops patrolling in those days. I guess they didn't care about high school students potentially falling into Lake Pontchartrain.  Alas, Katrina hit, we all grew up and everything changed. The Lakefront is still really nice and it's a cool place to hang out on "Sunday Funday" after a Saints game or whenever the weather is nice.   The reason for the three stars is because the cops are INSANE out there. They will pull you over if you don't look like you work or live in the area and if you are going so much as 3 miles over the limit, you will get a ticket. Trust me, I went to UNO, so I am quite familiar with the "rules" of the Lakefront. Lucky for me, I have never been in any kind of trouble, but I see people getting pulled over all the time. I mean I get it, it's a residential area, but they do not mess around so be careful.

My 700th review!  You know that I had to come back to an old favorite. There is finally a Felipe's in the booming Mid City area and I couldn't be happier. I don't make it to Mid City often, but I am so happy to see this area developing.  So, what about the restaurant? I came on opening night because I am a huge Felipe's nerd and I wanted to show my support. I was happy that I was seated at the bar pretty quickly. Yes, service took a while, but it's the first night so I didn't expect it to be super speedy. Lord, I was feeling sorry for some of the bartenders because some of the folks coming in where just plain RUDE. Complaining about the wait when they could plainly see that A LOT of people were waiting. Come on. Don't be THAT guy.  I ordered an al pastor taco salad with a side of queso. It took a while, but when I finally got my food, it was so good. All of the ingredients were nice and fresh and I had no complaints.  I will definitely be back to this Felipe's location. One of the things that this location seems to have over the other two is the parking. There is plenty of it in a well lit lot, so that may make the difference between me coming to this location or the S. Miro one (that lot is SO small). The staff was super nice. PJ was my bartender/waiter and he was putting up with A LOT of rude people and handling it all with a smile. They still have a few kinks to work out, but I definitely enjoyed my meal here.

After exploring Brunch Fest, we decided that we wanted actual real brunch that involved sitting and eating and not waiting in a long line.  We found ourselves at Cafe B and I am so excited that we did. This is a somewhat fancy kind of brunch place, so put on your Sunday best if you are heading this way. We sat at the bar for fast service and enjoyed bottomless mimosas and complimentary blueberry muffins as we looked over the menu. Of course, I saw grits on the menu, so I went with that. The grits were served with veal, which I'm not usually a fan of (it's a consistency thing), but I decided to give it a try anyway.  The veal and grits came out and it looked amazing. The grits were nice and creamy and they were topped with veal, a yummy sauce and a poached egg. I am still not a HUGE fan of veal, but I did find the dish really good and I enjoyed it immensely. I didn't even think of putting a poached egg in with the grits, so I'm going to have to try this trick at home.  I loved the fancy brunch here and I would definitely return. The menu is packed with other things I am eager to try.

Like Columbus, I've discovered something that others have discovered before me. Yes, like the New World, Three Happiness is pretty awesome.  I am always open to trying new places, especially if they happen to have Vietnamese food on the menu. I had passed this place bunches of times throughout my life on the Westbank and I always wondered about it. I finally decided to stop in.  First of all, don't be intimidated that this place is located in a super sketchy strip mall. Yes, there was a weird guy lurking outside of the place when I went. No, he didn't bother me. Just walk with purpose and you'll be fiiiiiine.  The atmosphere of this place is great. I love that it's wide open and you can even rent it out for parties! I went shortly after normal lunch hours, so it was empty when I got here. I seated myself and looked over the extensive menu.   You should know that this place has a lot of choices- both Chinese and Vietnamese. They have everything from classic Chinese dishes such as lo mein to Vietnamese yums like pho, vermicelli and banh mi. I already knew that I wanted some cold spring rolls and pho with rare beef, so that's what I had.  I love that the spring rolls come 4 to an order. It works out for sharing and guarantees that everyone gets their fill. The pho was great! I got the small bowl, which turned out to be perfect for lunch. The broth had a lot of flavor and there was a nice, generous serving of meat, which made it perfect.  I loved this place and I will definitely be back. They are closed Mondays, so be aware of that. I like that they have a huge menu, so they are sure to have something good that everyone would like.

Hmm...I guess I'll write a review, since I checked in here.  They have a nice selection of beer and snacks and their gas is always pretty cheap.  I've actually gotten sandwiches from here before, and they are pretty good!  They also sell Yellow Tail wine, which is a classic.  The staff is really nice and when I went in on my birthday, the guy who checked out my items wished me "Happy Birthday".  Did I just admit to spending my birthday at Race Trac?  You bet your sweet bow tie I did.  I hear the iced coffee is good and cheap, but I can't speak to that.  They do, however, have different colored frozen drinks, which is probably the sugary equivalent to the "squishee" on The Simpsons.

I am so excited that there is finally a yummy cupcake shop on the Westbank!  I have only had one cupcake from here, because I wanted to test the place out.  I got the "Wedding cake" cupcake (one of my favorite flavors) and it was delicous!  It was soft and well made and topped with a mound of delicious icing.  At $3.23, these specialty cupcakes are reasonably priced.  Gigi's has a lot of cupcake choices from red velvet to chocolate.  I could definitely see stopping in here and picking up a dozen for a birthday party or special occasion.  I will be going back and trying their other flavors very soon.
Just had to update and mention that WWOZ has an iphone/android app with the channel streaming, so if you aren't in town, you can still listen to awesome music.  Yes, I just discovered this.

Pretty much one of the best places to get all of the "fixin's" for a crawfish boil or cookout.  They have all of the fresh seafood that you could ever want or need. Yes, they only do take out, but keep in mind the fact that post people who frequent this place live in the area and are usually picking up stuff for crawfish/crab boils and things like that. The staff is really friendly and will be more than happy to help you with whatever you need.  They also have sausages and things like that, but I have never gotten that stuff here.

I like Bar Redux. I really like Bar Redux.  This place makes you feel like you are hanging out in a friend's basement. I said that same thing about Dos Jefes, but the difference here is that the basement belongs to a cool friend and not your parents. The bar is on the divier side, but the staff is friendly and eager to please. It's definitely a neighborhood place and that patrons are more than happy to make a bit of chit chat.  On this particular night the patio was closed, because there was no band, so I didn't really get to get a feel of that part of the place. It was also really hot out, so I wasn't complaining. I've also heard that they have amazing food, so I will have to see what the kitchen has to offer when I return.

Quaint hotel that gets the job done. The biggest selling point of this hotel is probably the location. It's perfectly located right in the middle of the Lower Garden District and downtown. You can walk to the WWII museum from here, Tivoli and Lee is a really good restaurant that is attached to the hotel, Bellocq is a fancy cocktail bar that is close, it's right on the streetcar line and there are always cabs driving through the roundabout. Oh, and Circle Bar is also within walking distance, if you are in the mood for live music.  The rooms are SUPER small and very "cell" like, but you are on vacation, and you probably won't be spending that much time in the hotel room anyway. The lobby is really nice for hanging out, if you don't feel like going out but you don't want to stay in the room.  I had to laugh at the "mini bar" in the room. $9 for what is basically the equivalent of a shot of Jack Daniel's when there is a mini mart right across the way where you can buy a fifth for a little more than that. You gotta love them for trying.
Awwesome parade with a lot to give.  Very generous krewe.  Catch of the night: tons of doubloons and blinky medallions.

This store is okay. The place had just possibly been robbed when we got here (lots of cops and confused workers), so maybe I'm leaning a little more towards the negative.   Honestly, we just stopped in here for a wine and liquor run, so this review is going to be short and sweet. They were having a sale on Barefoot wine, so we got that and it turned out to be pretty good. They have a pretty good beer selection- nothing too crafty, but the more "mainstream" stuff is well stocked and there are a lot of choices. Aisles are wide to prevent crowding, which is awesome and we checked out with ease. We even saved $4 for using a Winn Dixie card.

Things it is: a dive a cool place to see a band a place to get two types of 40 Arpent beer on tap a place to get tamales a cool local hangout  Things it isn't: an uppity hang out a smoke free bar a place that you will probably want to spend a lot of time smoke free a place with an extensive beer list a place with signage   Old Arabi Bar is a straight up dive if ever there was one. I had a good time here watching a band that I had never heard of and enjoying a local beer. The tamales were exceptional and although there was no sign, you shouldn't be scared of this bar that is basically a hole in the middle of a neighborhood.

One of the great things about French Quarter Fest is that you end up wandering into places you might not have stumbled into otherwise. Enter Naghi's.  What drew me in were the life size sculptures, which I assume are meant for a gorgeous mansion or yard. These things are beautiful and one day, when I have my dream home, I will own many of them. They also had a golden Buddha statue just hanging out on the counter that cost $3000 and a huge portrait of Prince. Yeah, this shop was randomly awesome. They had a display case full of gorgeous jewelry and the man who was working was very nice and greeted me and told me to let him know if I need any help.  I'm not sure if I will ever have the financial means, but when the day comes and I have a mid-life crisis, I'm skipping the sports car and getting that Buddha.

I've been to this place a few times now and it's more than a bar, it's a really nice place to relax with friends.  Sure, it's an older crowd, but on Fridays they have Phil Melancon on the piano and you can't resist having a good time as he sings classics from Nat King Cole and others from that classic era.  The hotel and the bar have an old Hollywood history.  Celebrities such as Tennessee Williams, Frank Sinatra, Walt Disney, Truman Capote and many others have stayed (and drank) here when they were in New Orleans.  The Bayou Bar definitely has an old, classic feel and it's one of those New Orleans bars that makes you appreciate what the city has to offer.

I love this new little consignment shop on Magazine! I think they just opened, because they were in the process of hiring someone when I went in.  They have a great variety of things here. If you are looking for something super fancy and want to pay a little more, they have what you need. If you aren't looking to spend a lot, they have something that will suit your style at a reasonable price. This shop is really cute and my dinky little pictures don't do it justice.  They have everything from skirt and tops to dresses to vintage style purses and jewelry. I will definitely be back when I am looking for something with a little flair.

Oh, Dat Dog.  I had only heard rumors of your awesomeness.  Then I got to experience it for myself.  Dat Dog isn't your daddy's hot dog.  Leave those franks at the ball park.  With such options as bratwaurst and crawfish sausage, you can't miss.  You can get your hot dog topped with your choice of toppings from onions to cheese and much much more.  They also serve fries that you can get topped with chilli and cheese.    I had a fantastic alligator sausage hot dog with cheese and mustard on it (I'm a purist).  It was WONDERFUL (see my pic)!  Also, there is something about the buns that just makes the whole experience great.  Warm, soft and a little bit...sweet?  I will definitely be going back and I'm eager to try all of the sausages that they offer.  Yum!

Super generous Krewe. The gentlemen love the Mar. I got beads, blinky beads, a blinky bracelet and a blinky headband. Was I blinkyed out? Negatory. Hermes proved, once again, that they are the most generous of the Thursday night krewes.

Four stars for the atmosphere. Four stars for the food. Three stars for the price.  The atmosphere of this place is great. It has that "50's diner" type of feel that I really liked. The menu is on the wall, you decide what you want, you go up and order, they take your name and you wait to be called.  They have a whole selection of things to choose from such as poboys, salads and all day breakfast. They also have daily lunch specials such as red beans and rice and meatloaf, depending on the day. I decided to get what they are known for- the burger. I got the Lot-O-Burger with cheddar cheese, fries and the Frostop root beer.  The burger was good and had a lot of flavor and was nicely dressed with lettuce, tomato and cheese and I liked that the fries were sprinkled with salt and a spicy flavoring that gave them a little kick. The root beer was delicious, and free refills are always nice.  My only complaint is the price. For my burger, fries and drink, the total was $9.30. That's not a lot of money at all, but that just seems like a little more than I would like to pay for a quick lunch, especially considering I ordered at a counter and picked it up myself. That's a small little thing and I will definitely be back as I did enjoy my meal (and off the record, I completely cleaned my little basket).

This must be one of those places that you have to visit a few times to enjoy. I really wasn't impressed. The patrons didn't seem friendly and they had a dj for some reason. Keep in mind, there were about 6 people in this place when we went.   It's a 24 hour bar. I can only imagine the type of people that hit this place up at 8,9, or 10 in the morning. Good God. I guess it's more of a neighborhood hangout, but I just don't get it.

After a Yelp event, I was craving some iced coffee, so I popped in here because it was close and it looked like they had what I needed.  I kept my order simple and just got an iced coffee, even though all of their sweet treats looked amazing! My coffee was okay- I could tell that it was "no frills" coffee (that's okay, they aren't really a coffee shop) that had some ice added to it. Also, I didn't ask for cream and sugar, but for whatever reason they just decided to add it- not a huge deal, but that's worth noting if you have dietary concerns.  Decent coffee if you're in a pinch, if you're looking for the "good stuff", go elsewhere.

I tried this place a while ago, after so many people had raved about it.  This was during the time that Oak St. was being worked on, so it was kind of a challenge getting there in the first place.  Anyway, I went and I wasn't really blown away by the food here.  I got my usual: salmon sashimi and a couple of rolls.  They were good, but not good enough for me to go out of my way to get here.    I will, however, comend them on their atmosphere.  The place is quite large, well lit, and I liked the modern feel.  Also, for dessert I got some green tea ice cream and I was blown away at how yummy and refreshing it was.

I have been back here a bunch of times since my first review and I feel as if I have gotten a feel for the place.  When I go, I usually get the "daily", which is the cocktail of the day (you can sample it, before you order) or I just let the bartender mix me up something that he thinks I will like. I also really like the wine selection that they have. Although there are sofas in the back and tables, I usually sit at the bar and chat with other patrons.  The place never really gets overly packed.  It's one of those places where people stop in for a drink or two and move on, so there is good crowd flow.

I really liked Two Sisters 'N Da East when I went, so when I heard they were opening a Westbank version of that restaurant right in my own backyard, I was really excited.  I stopped in here for lunch on a Monday. I had already heard that the place is small, with just a few tables, and it gets packed for lunch so we decided to go around one, after the big crowd had moved on. While there was still a good amount of people here, we found a table right away. This restaurant is a bit different than the one in the East- here you walk up to the counter and order and they bring your food out to you. They have daily specials, so just pick something that is available that day and you're good to go.  I decided to get the fried catfish platter which came with two nice pieces of catfish, green beans, sweet potato rice and my choice of side- mac and cheese. This was A LOT of food and it only cost $10! The catfish was really yummy and after I added a touch of hot sauce, it was perfect. The sweet potato rice was different and a nice surprise. The mac and cheese was outstanding, and clearly a family recipe and the green beans were good with bits of bacon in them. My friend got the red beans and rice with sausage and that looked so good as well. They sell a variety of things that you can get on the side, and I was kicking myself that I didn't think to get some cornbread because I remember the cornbread at the other location was great.  The food here is delicious and well worth the price. They seem to do a big "take out" business, so next time I might just order ahead and pick up my food to go. They have a wide variety of offerings from smothered okra to fried chicken, so I'm sure I will be slowly working my way through the menu to see what I like best.   The staff here is super friendly and nice, it's cash only for now and the only drinks available are bottled. Judging by the crowd, this place is going to do really well and I'm excited that there's a restaurant like this in our area, with good Southern cooking. I can't wait to go back.

I am so excited about the first CC's on the Westbank AND the fact that it's 3 minutes away from my house.  They have only been open since Monday, so the staff is still working out the kinks, but I have been here twice and both times my experience was pretty good. The first time I went through the drive through and ordered a large iced coffee. They clearly gave me a medium, but they charged (what I thought) was the medium price so I just took it and went on my way. Like I said, they just opened, so I'm not gonna give anyone a hard time over such a small slip up. Today I went inside and ordered a large iced coffee. This one actually was large and it was the same price as what I had been charged for a medium (just over $2). I'm not sure which was the mistake, but if a large iced coffee really is only $2.50 or so, then I will be back all the time.  The space inside the store is nice with plenty of seating and they have a nice selection of pastries, if you are in the mood for something sweet. I am giving 4 stars on convenience alone and the coffee is really good.

This is such a welcoming place! We were having Sunday Funday in the Quarter when we passed this spot. The doors were wide open and the musicians told us to "come in!", so we did.  This is a small bar, but I found it cozy. It was packed with what seemed like neighborhood regulars and everyone was enjoying themselves. As the name of the bar promises, there was a jazz band holding court in the corner playing some classic tunes. I can't vouch for the food, but the drinks are well priced especially considering you are in the middle of a "touristy" area.

I used to be such a fan of this bar.  It had an awesome crowd and was always a good time.  My friends and I even hung out here after last year's Saints super bowl win and had some pizza.  Lately, though, whenever I have gone, I have just felt out of place.  The bar always seems way too crowded (which is great for the owners) and the kind of people that go there are just... different.  It seems like more of a crowd that would hang out at Monkey Hill.  That's not a horrible thing, but if I want to hang out with college kids, I'll go to a college bar.  Also, they removed the pool tables.  I guess they are trying to attract a different crowd, but the friends I would go with would go specifically to shoot pool and have a beer or two.  I have no idea why they would get rid of the pool tables.  Weren't they making the place money?  Also, in place of the pool tables, they have just scattered small tables and chairs and added a few booths.  It all just seems so out of place, now.  I would be glad to go back in the warmer months and hang out on the balcony upstairs, as I have in the past, but for now this is just a "one drink and go" type of place for me.

Tutti Frutti  offers delicious frozen yogurt at reasonable price. The way it is done here is you go in and you are given a cup. You then fill the cup with as much yogurt and toppings as you would like, your cup is then weighed and you are charged according to how much your cup weighs. Really simple, especially on those days that you aren't in the mood for a lot or you are in the mood for a little more. Tutti Frutti offers a nice selection of flavors including pecan praline, raspberry pomegranate, death by chocolate and almond. Keep in mind that you can mix and match flavors, so the possibilities are endless.   The best part about Tutti Frutti is the toppings. Not only do they offer fruit toppings such as fresh strawberries and kiwi, but they also have a nice selection of nuts and candies, for those days that you are in the mood to really indulge. Also, don't worry if you aren't sure what flavors suit your tastes;   Tutti Frutti is more than happy to let you sample all that they have to offer.

This is a decent space. Me and some friends came here to see some music and we had a pretty good time. The area we were in was pretty small and dark. I'm not sure if the entire place is like this, but once the space started filling up it was pretty tight. Cover wasn't horrible- $10 at the door, and the bar had a decent beer selection.  Parts of the show sounded like it was a bit too loud for the space. I don't even know if this is a legitimate complaint, or maybe I'm just old. It's a nice enough place that I would return for future events, but it would have to be something that I really want to see.

Monkey Hill is one of those bars that you want to check out during the week, and avoid like the plague on the weekends.  Definitely a more upscale bar, Monkey Hill is located by river road.  It's a good size place with a nice bar area and a nice sitting area with sofas and chairs, where you can sit with a big group or get to know new people.  My only complaint is, on the weekends, this place gets packed with college age regulars who are dressed like they are going to watch a tennis match.  That's not necessarily a bad thing, but I have always preferred to go during the week.    Worth checking out, if you are looking for a nicer uptown experience.

Color me SHOCKED.  When you think of food at the zoo, what do you think of? I usually think of hot dogs, burgers and nachos. David and I were having a zoo day and we got a bite to eat here because it was right in the middle of things. There was a pretty good crowd for a Saturday, but the line was moving fast. They have a lot of food options here, but still, I wasn't expecting much. I got the chicken strips with fries and David got a shrimp po boy with cheese fries.  Let me tell you- I couldn't have been more pleased with how good the food was here. First of all, you order and they have it ready to go for you right away. Second of all, my chicken strips were HUGE. The batter was nice and the chicken was tender and juicy. David's po boy was PACKED with shrimp, to the point that they were falling off of the bread. Here's the kicker: my chicken strips basket was $7.50 and David's sandwich was $8.50. That's a good deal, any way you want to look at it. As far as drinks go, they have all of the basic soft drinks and water and they have beer and daiquiris, if you've had enough of the kids and want to get liquored up. No judgement. If you want a souvenir cup, it's $6; again, not a bad price at all.  On my next trip to the zoo, I won't even hesitate to eat here. The food is good and the service is fast. You can't ask for more than that.

I've been here a few times, but I have yet to eat here.  Some friends and I usually just hang out in the bar area, because we don't feel like dealing with the smoke at another place.  The staff is always super friendly and eager to please.  So, why three stars you ask?  Well, I guess it's because this place isn't anything overly special and the drinks are over priced.  I know, you're going to call me cheap, but I think $5.75 for a Stella is a little steep.  It's not a bad price if you're on a date and having a fancy night, but just for a random night out, it can add up.  I would go back if I had a reason to, but I wouldn't go out of my way to spend an evening here.  I do want to try the food though!  Ok, I'll go back and try the food and re-review.  Deal?

Whoa! This PetSmart is really huge and way bigger than the one on the Westbank.  My cat has been having stomach issues, so I stopped in here to talk to a pro about maybe switching up her food. He pointed me in the direction of some "nature based" food that is more plants than meat because apparently meat can irritate older cats stomachs. It's a whole thing! While I didn't purchase the food, the guy I talked to was quite knowledgeable and he definitely knew what he was talking about.  This store has a great selection of toys, food and all the other good pet stuff you could want. They have cats up for adoption in the front, and in the back they have fish, reptiles and small furry creatures. There was one bearded dragon who kept eye contact with me the entire time and I think he wanted me to take him home. Fun fact: I used to have a pet iguana and I would love to have a bearded dragon, but today was not the day.  Anyway, I love the new and nice store. I am thankful for the helpful staff and cat food education.

It's late night. I can't sleep. I'm reviewing a Taco Bell. What has happened to my life?  Okay, so actually this Taco Bell is pretty decent as far as Taco Bells go. They have never messed my order up and they are generous when I ask for extra sauce. My problem with this location is the line is often way too long and they are slow getting people through and I have been told, more than once, that they are in the middle of a shift change when I think that they just don't feel like being bothered with taking and preparing an order because the store is dead in the middle of the afternoon.  I know fast food is pretty limited in this area, so I guess you can just take what you can get.

Whoo hoo!  I got to try Barrel Proof and I loved it! Did you know that our very own Elite yelper Davis J., LIVES at this bar? Ok not really, but he is here a lot and when someone has a bunch of check ins to a place, in a short period of time, I bookmark it and file it under "must try".  I finally found myself at Barrel Proof and it didn't disappoint. Formerly Bridge Lounge, Barrel Proof is a fancy cocktail bar without the pretension of a fancy cocktail bar. The staff is friendly, the crowd is rowdy and the drinks are good. You can't ask for more than that. They have totally redone the inside of the place and the only thing that remains of Bridge Lounge is the cozy, dark atmosphere (minus the dogs and loud music). The bartenders are happy to mix you up a fancy cocktail or just pour you a beer, if that's more your speed.  I will definitely be back to make more memories and have some more good times.

I love Celebration in the Oaks!  This is always fun, because the whole family can do it.  On paper it seems so simple: Christmas lights in a bunch of trees,  but it's so much more than that.  The park is transformed into a twinkling magical Christmas land.  I know some people might not be into that type of thing, but I always enjoy it.  This is always a popular place to bring the kids, a good place for teens to hang out for a little while and the perfect place to propose during the holiday season (ok, I'll admit, I think that a proposal here is a little cheeseball.  I mean, I'm not the type of girl who wants to get engaged among screaming kids, but hey, judge not lest ye be, right?).  There's a train that you can bring the kids on and a carousel and other fun little things for kids to do.  Popcorn, hot chocolate and other little snacks are provided.

This is a lovely little sushi spot located in the heart of Lakeview.  A friend and i were here for lunch and I was immediately impressed by the atmosphere of the place. The restaurant seems to be a converted house, the decor is modern and sophisticated and we were seated in a nice booth as we looked over our menus.  We started with an order of edamame and I got an order of the noodle salad. The edamame was perfect but the noodle salad was a bit of a mess. Their version had a TON of mayo in it. There was so much mayo that after a few bites I had to stop eating it because it was making my stomach hurt. Every other noodle salad I have had usually had a very light coating of mayo, but this place went way overboard.  For my entree I got a Philly roll and I got the Tiger special roll. The Tiger roll was packed with tuna, salmon and avocado and wrapped in salmon. I really liked it and I liked that it was good and filling without being overly heavy. The Philly roll was as good as the Philly roll that I have had at other places. One thing that really struck me is how fresh the rice was. Sometimes you get rice that is a little stiff, but the rice here was cooked perfectly and the food overall was very fresh.  I would go back and get a repeat of everything I ordered here, except the noodle salad.

Talk about a blast from the past! Do y'all (30+ folks) remember actual music stores? When I was a kid, my favorite was Musicland at Oakwood Mall. I remember on one side of the store they had a selection of records, through the middle of the store they had CD's and along the wall they had cassettes. I used to LOVE spending time in there looking over the music to see what I wanted to treat myself to, with what little money I had. Peaches Records brought all of those memories flooding back.  I happened to be in the area, so I popped in here just to see what it was all about. There were no other customers, but the woman working gave me a friendly greeting. I think that this store could have everything you could possibly want: new and old records, used CDs, tshirts, cassettes- you name it. It's as old school as you can possibly get. If you are any kind of record collector, and you are looking for something specific, this should be your first stop. I loved that along the side wall they have headphone kiosks where you can listen to music. I remember that from back in the day too!   I didn't find anything I wanted to buy on this trip (although I was tempted to buy an old Dolly Parton record), but I will definitely be making a habit of checking this place out, on the regular, just to see what they have to offer. I like that their used music CDs are well priced and they have a good selection of new stuff.  Note: I love that the space is an old Woolworth's complete with diner-area. I wish it was operational!

I finally have the time to properly describe my entire Marcello's experience. Here it is, probably in too much detail.  First of all, I had heard how fantastic Marcello's was going to be before it even opened. My friend, Liam had just been hired as a bartender and created their cocktail menu and Liam is an amazing craftsman of fancy cocktails, so I knew that this place was already off to a fantastic start.  For my second birthday dinner night out, I picked Marcello's because I had been dying to try it after hearing about the old world charm of the place. We placed reservations ahead of time- a must.  The restaurant itself is not overly small, but still has a quaint feel. There's is a lot going on, and it's busy, but you never feel like you are being ignored. We arrived a bit early, and after a short wait, we were lead to our seat. Immediately we were offered fresh bread, which I found delightful.  First things first- the wine menu. Looking it over, you feel a bit overwhelmed. This place knows it's wine. In the dining room, racks of wine are everywhere and it's all fantastic, good wine. I let my dining companion choose, as he is better at than type of thing that I am and he picked a delicious red that was light and bit tart that I enjoyed.  The menu is extensive and they give you a lot of choices. For one of our starters, we decided to just let the kitchen whip something up for us. What came to our table was thinly sliced lamb belly on a bed of pasta. The lamb melted in my mouth and I was in heaven. Next, we ordered some fried calamari, which came out hot out of the fryer. It came with two dipping sauces- a marinara sauce and a caper aioli that was addicting.  For my entree, I decided on the Tritoni, which was a tough call, because I also had my eye on the fettuccine and fried oysters. The Tritoni is lobster, shrimp, crab, and spinach covered in a sherry cream sauce and served over fettuccine. It was incredible. All of the flavors of the dish came together to produce a light, but delectable experience. I liked that it wasn't too heavy but it still filled me.  The staff was incredibly nice and accommodating, constantly checking to make sure that we had everything that we needed and that everything was to our satisfaction. After dinner, we moved over to the bar to enjoy another glass of wine and some coffee.  This is a family business, and it absolutely shows with all of the care that they put into every step of the dining experience. It is the PERFECT place for a date or a "dressy" night out.  I will absolutely return to Marcello's and hopefully I will return sooner rather than later. I am excited to explore more of the menu and make this delightful restaurant one of my regular stops for dinner.

*This is a review of the consignment part of the store*  With all of the stuff we had to clear and get rid of during a recent "clean out" we knew that trying to sell things on our own wouldn't be out only option. After doing some research, Heirloom Furnishings seemed like a good place to sell some things that we had no need for.  I personally sold jewelry here. The owner went through every piece and picked out what she thought would sell, priced it and before I knew it it had been sold and she had a check for me. While some pieces took a few months to sell, others sold pretty quickly and I was pleased with the way that she decided to price things. Of course, because it's consignment, the owner does take a percentage, but it's a small price to pay considering it would take longer for you to sell the stuff on your own.

3 stars with some room for improvement.  This place literally just opened about two weeks ago, so I appreciate that they are still trying to figure things out. I stopped in here for an iced coffee, after seeing some mumbles about this place online. The shop itself is really cute, if not easy to miss. Yes, I walked past it twice because I'm not super familiar with the area and it kind of blends in with the rest of the buildings.  The atmosphere is nothing to speak of- there are a few tables and chairs that don't really do much for me (my table was wobbly and I almost spilled my drink when I sat down) and a "family style" table on the side with a lot of seating. The staff is really friendly and welcomed me when I walked in, but I have two major complaints. First of all, before I even walked in I could hear the music blaring from inside. Once inside, there was loud rock music playing- not what I was expecting and I didn't like that at all. I go to coffee shops to relax and I just couldn't  relax with that music playing. My other complaint is the heat. I was here in the mid-afternoon and, because there are a lot of windows, the shop is quite warm. It was so warm that I eventually had to leave because the warmth of the shop coupled with the music was making me uncomfortable.  I wish they had more pastries or even sandwiches. The coffee was good, so I would probably stop in for some iced coffee to go, but I wouldn't stick around.

I am ALMOST hesitant to post this review, because apparently this is one of the better kept secrets on the Westbank.  A little backstory: every now and then, a foodie friend of mine will check in here on Facebook. He raved about how amazing it is, and being a fan of poboys, I knew I had to try it. First of all, trying to find any info about this place online is pretty much impossible. No menu to speak of, not a lot of reviews, nothing. So, I made it a point to get some good snaps of the menu, because Jake's has A LOT to offer.  Ok, so this place is just a stand on the side of the road. It is located right across the street from the Plaquemines Parish Sheriff's office and right next to the ferry launch, so I am assuming that's where they get a lot of their business. And when I say it's a stand, I mean it is a little bigger than a snowball stand.  You walk up and order what you want. You can get a half or a large and you can get it on a bun or French bread. I got a large shrimp which was just under $10 and I had half for lunch and saved the other half, so it all evened out. My friend who goes regularly says that they have fantastic hamburgers and the best roast beef he has ever had, so I will have to go back and check that out. Also, they have oyster poboys when oysters are in season.  The shrimp poboy was AMAZING! I loved it and I liked that it was packed with shrimp and perfectly dressed. The bread was just crispy and flaky enough to make the whole sandwich really come together.  They have some metal tables outside, if you want to eat there, but I just got mine to go. The staff is super friendly. I am definitely going to go back and try the roast beef, and I'll probably add on to this review when I do so.  Cash only! Check the photo for their hours! Check the menu pictures for all that they offer including hot dogs and broccoli bites and sides!

I had MoPho for dinner and I am honestly a little torn.  First of all, I loved the atmosphere of the whole place. Cool and casual, it's a great place to enjoy a meal or a cocktail with friends after work.  There isn't a whole lot to the menu, but what they do offer sounded amazing. The first thing we decided to try were the Spring rolls. We decided to get half shrimp and half pork shoulder. The shrimp was...weird. It was fried, which I wasn't expecting or really in the mood for. If I had known the shrimp was fried (the menu makes no mention of this), I would have just gotten both of them with pork shoulder. The pork shoulder rolls were delicious and had a lot of flavor. Half of one almost seemed like a tease and left me wanting more. I will say this- for two Spring rolls, $8 seems a little steep. Just my opinion.  For my main meal, I decided to get the beef pho with flank, pork belly and head cheese. You can pick three proteins, and they have interesting choices from ox tail to cock's comb. I wasn't really in much of an experimental mood, so I stuck to pretty basic choices. The pho had a lot of flavor and came in a really large serving. One thing that struck me as odd was that the noodle was flat and not round (see photo). It's not a huge deal, just different. I prefer a round noodle, but whatever.  This is a good place to check out if you are in the mood for Vietnamese fusion. There's nothing really "traditional" about it, but it's still good. While I wouldn't necessarily go out of my way to eat here again, I would definitely stop in for lunch or dinner, without hesitation, if I were in the area.

So, full disclosure time: I'm not the biggest fan of Thai food. I've tried it in the past and for whatever reason it just didn't do it for me. That all changed when I stopped into Banana Blossom. Banana Blossom was on the January edition list of "38 Essential New Orleans Restaurants" (http://nola.eater.com/maps/the-38-essential-new-orleans-restaurants-january-2015), so I decided to give Thai food another try.  The restaurant is very simple, but nice. We sat down and I decided to ease into this Thai experience by sticking to food that I know I like. We started with the fried calamari which was just excellent. It was nice and fresh and right out of the fryer. The pieces were small and came with a nice sauce for dipping.  For my entree I got the coconut ginger shrimp. which was 4 large shrimp that were battered and served over rice. I had the option of getting the dish "mild", "hot", or "very hot" and I decided to go with "hot" because I enjoy a little spice. The food was so good! The rice had a lot of flavor and the shrimp were fried perfectly. There were also some vegetable mixed in the rice, which made it great. I found the food spicy, but not so spicy that it took away from the flavor of the food. The portions are quite large and I boxed up half of me meal and took it home.  I loved my food experience here and I will now definitely return, since there is some Thai food I really like in my area.

At the end of a long night out in Da Metry's, you might find yourself hungry. In which case, make your way over to City Diner to get something good before you head home.  We stopped in here after a pretty long night. It's all a bit fuzzy, but I do know that a delicious breakfast with eggs, grits and bacon was involved. The classic breakfast wasn't the star of the show. This place is known for their HUGE pancakes, so of course we had to try them. I'll admit it- by the time the pancakes came out I was pretty full. I cut myself a slice of the pancakes (like it was cake) and I do remember it being delicious.   City Diner is one of the better choices for a late night meal in this area. I'm not a huge IHOP person these days, so I'm happy to support this spot and I'll return.

This is a nice spot off the "beaten path" for those of us who don't want to go deep into the heart of the French Quarter, but still want to hang out downtown for a little while.  The people here have always been really nice and the drinks are well priced. The place is kind of small, but I actually do like the fact that there aren't any tvs here (or if there are, I didn't notice because they weren't on), so that there aren't any distractions if you are trying to have a conversation.

Great food, but good Lord what a boring dinner.  David and I wanted a date night, so I picked this spot, as it had been on my radar for a while. I made a reservation, but when I arrived it was clear that wasn't necessary, as there were only 4 other occupied tables in the huge space on a Saturday night. After some confusion as to what party we were, we were seated on a side of the restaurant away from all of the other diners. We were in no-man's land, y'all.  After looking over the menu, I decided to get the braised pork and smashed potatoes and David got the shrimp and grits. The pork was GREAT! It tasted like a home cooked meal and had a gravy sauce on top and the potatoes were fantastic. David liked his shrimp and grits, but be aware that the shrimp in the dish come with the tails on.  I enjoyed the food, but I was expecting more from this spot. Our waitress seemed pre-occupied and there was little to no interaction with us. She stopped by once to take our order, once to drop off the food and once to refill my drink and ask how it all was. It almost felt as if we were being hustled through our dinner as quickly as possible. The place itself feels like a warehouse and the atmosphere isn't super welcoming. Also, being seated away from the main part of the restaurant made me feel like we were an afterthought the whole time we were there.  If I go back, I'd probably just eat at the bar and have a few cocktails. I didn't drink, so maybe that was the problem- this place might be a lot more fun if you're drunk. I hear that they have a good happy hour, so if you're looking for that, this might be the spot for you.

This place is fantastic. They serve delicious daiquiris and food if you are looking for something to munch.  We stopped in a little later on a Saturday night and I was tired of drinking beer, so I got a margarita daiquiri. It was really good and actually tasted closer to a margarita than other shops that just taste like a mix. I know that this was from a mix too, but it had more flavor than other spots. The bartender was friendly and made us feel welcome. I'm sure smoking is allowed since it's JP, but I didn't notice a smokey smell in the place, which puts it at the top of my "cool" list.

I love this store because there aren't a lot of places to get an assorted choice of cheeses or beer on the Westbank and this Rouse's has a wide selection of both.  First of all, the cheese case is a thing of beauty. This ain't your mama's cheese case! They have so many different assorted and exotic types of cheeses. When you go here you better be prepared to take your time and come with some willpower, because whenever I go, it's all I can do to keep from filling my basket with different assortments of brie, gouda and munster. Seriously. If you can't get to a proper cheese shop, the Rouse's cheese case will hold you.  Also, their beer selection is awesome. They have big bottles of Rogue, Magic Hat #9 and Runination ale. If you are in the mood to try something really different, they have something called "Vampire Blood". I've never tried it. It's a pale ale. I don't know.  Rouse's also makes sushi rolls in store, which really aren't that bad. They are made fresh daily, and while they aren't as good at something you would get at a legitimate sushi restaurant, it gets the job done if you want to pick something up for a quick lunch.

Yes, I'm reviewing Arby's.  Why?  Because Arby's is awesome.  Yeah, you got me, it's not the type of roast beef you will find at Mother's or Parkway, but it's FAST FOOD.  Those 4 stars up there are fast food stars.  If I were to compare it to Parkway...well, I wouldn't.  That would be silly.  Arby's is one of those places that I wish was on the Westbank, but I'm glad it's not on the Westbank, because I would be there all the time.  The roast beef is always fantastic and I could probably finish one of their regular sandwiches in three minutes.  You get your choice of fries...curly or straight.  THEY GIVE YOU A CHOICE!  What's not to love about that (and who get's straight when they can get curly??).  They also have jalapeno bites, potato cake bites, and mozzarella sticks.  They have an extensive menu of "toasted" stuff (and a chicken sandwich?!  Get outta here!), but I usually just stick with a plain old roast beef and I put some horsey sauce on there and call it a meal.  I'm easy, like that.  The service at this location is always fast and I always stop in for a treat when I find myself in Metairie.

Wow. Domenica had been on my list of places to try for years and I am so excited I finally got to check it out.  My boyfriend and I were here for a pre-Valentine's Day/post Krewe du Vieux dinner. I had made reservations a month ahead of time and I'm glad I did, because spots fill up fast. We were a little late for the reservation, due to traffic, but I gave them a call and they were understanding and we were seated immediately upon arriving.  Everything on the menu sounded amazing. We decided to start with some bread that came with butter and a molasses spread. It was warm and fresh and a perfect start to the meal. I had done a little bit of research and I knew that I wanted to get the squid ink tagoltini. I have been a fan of squid ink pasta, that I have tried elsewhere, and I was eager to try their version. I was worried that it might not be enough (other reviews had mentioned that the portion is small), but my concerns were alleviated as soon as the food was brought out. This was delicious pasta wound nicely onto the plate with big chunks of crab meat on top. It was decadent, without being too heavy. I love the sauce that the pasta was topped with and it brought a lot of flavor to the dish. I absolutely enjoyed this and I would get it again upon returning.  My boyfriend got the lasagna and I must say- I was a little bit jealous. The portion of the lasagna was huge and it was topped with a think layer of cheese that was melted and baked to perfection. It looked like homemade lasagna and he loved it.  Although they were super busy, the wait staff was attentive and quick about taking the order and getting our drinks. I love the atmosphere of the place with the dimly lit dining room that gives the entire experience a cozy and romantic feel. This was one of the best dining experiences and I will be happy to return.

Salvo's is AMAZING. Don't be put off that it is "all the way" in Belle Chasse. It is most definitely worth the trip.  This is a pretty basic restaurant. You walk in and order whatever you want at the counter and then you sit at one of the picnic style tables. It's no frills, but the food is delicious. I always get the oyster po boy and I am never disappointed. The oysters are always fat and juicy and really good.  Other than po boys, Salvo's has other fried seafood, platters and boiled seafood. The staff is super nice and will make you feel right at home.

I don't know if Spanish Plaza (Plaza de España) has been restored or renovated since some of the previous reviews, but I found it to be lovely. David and I wandered over here after we were done with Fried Chicken Fest and after a quick stroll through the Riverwalk Mall. The fountain was on and it was nice and clear water flowing through. The fountain and the surrounding structures are in good shape and it was lovely enjoying the afternoon next to this iconic New Orleans landmark.  As Nicole said, the restaurants in the Plaza are few and far between. I don't know what a "Crazy Lobster" is, but they got one.   I guess there's not much to say that hasn't previously been said about the Spanish Plaza. It's not necessarily worth seeking out if you visiting from out of town, but it's worth a look if you find yourself in the area.  Spanish Plaza aka Plaza de España, I like you.

This cute little shop was unexpected on our walk down Decatur during French Quarter Fest.  We stepped in and we were delighted to see all kinds of tasty treats for sale from unusual candies to just about every soda and soda flavored product you could think of. We picked up some salt water taffy, because I had never had any and my friend insisted I try it. Yep, it was a total win and I loved the melt-in-your mouth goodness of the treat.  This is the perfect shop if you are looking for something a bit different to give the kids (or someone else you love) for a fun occasion such as Easter or Christmas.

I'll be the first to admit that I am not the biggest fan of king cake. I mean, I like it, but I have been known to go an entire Carnival season without having a single slice.  After seeing a lot of people posting photos of their delicious cakes online, I decided to go out and get one of my own. After a bit of research, I found myself at Antoine's. For $18, you get a really large king cake. I opted for the plain, just so I could make a fair judgement on the taste. Well, it was out of this world delicious. I like that it was soft and sweet without being overwhelmingly sweet. Some king cakes overdo it on the sugar and it's too much to handle, but Antoine's did theirs right.  The staff was friendly, and they had king cakes galore into the late afternoon, so I didn't have to worry about rushing in to get one early in the morning.

Yet another one of the delicious gems located inside St. Roch Market.  I stopped in for lunch and I already knew what I was getting. I had seen pictures of The Munch on the internets and I knew that I had to make this pulled pork and mac and cheese sandwich mine. My hopes were pretty high, but they were definitely met as soon as I was presented with this plate of goodness. The combination of pulled pork and mac and cheese sounds decadent, because it is. I only ate half of the sandwich and took the rest to go, I swear!  My friend got a crepe, which looked fantastic and I will be trying one of those next time. I like that Dirty Dishes has a nice selection of different things that are sure to suit any mood you're in. The fact that this is a family owned business makes coming here even better. I will be back.

It's a restaurant!  It's a nightclub!  It's a bar!  This is one of those places that you have to go into ready for an experience and if you go to The Bombay Club, with that attitude, you won't leave disappointed.    The Bombay serves signature cocktails and also has dinner.  A friend and I went to see a singer here and we ended up getting an appetizer to enjoy, while we watched the show.  It was fabulous.  My suggestion: get there earlier in the evening, as the place gets pretty packed.  Honesty time.  Is this place cheap?  No.  Even a beer will run you about $8, but when you go here, you aren't just paying for dinner and drinks, you are paying for an experience.  Most of the time there is live music, or at the very least, someone on the piano.  It's not a place you would necessarily go to every weekend, but for those special nights, when you want to dress up and you aren't afraid to spend a few extra bucks, it's perfect.  The atmosphere is wonderful, and if you are doing an "old school" night, then this is definitely one of the places you are going to want to visit.  It has an extremely high class feel.  Although I was wearing jeans, and I felt comfortable, I would have felt a little more "authentic" had I been wearing a nice dress with my hair all done up.  Maybe that's just me.  Since I have only had the opportunity to go here once, I look forward to returning.  This would be a great place for a romantic date or just a night out with friends.

After all of my Middle Eastern food reviews I have been writing lately, a few people told me that I had to check out Lebanon's Cafe. Okay, twist my arm.  I met a friend here and it was a pretty busy night, but he was able to grab a table outside. Normally I'm not a big fan of eating outside, but it was a nice evening so I went with it, We decided to start with some hummus as we looked over the menu. The hummus was perfect. It was creamy and whipped to perfection. I notice that a lot of places leave some lumps in it, but the hummus here was nice and smooth.  For my entree I got the beef shawarma. I know it's what I always get at these places, but I know what I like. The shawarma came with a side salad and hummus. What I like about the beef here is that there is a big serving of it and it comes with big pieces of onions and tomato in it. It was delicious! Fortunately I was starving, so I really enjoyed all of it.  Our service was excellent. Even though we were sitting outside, our waitress was attentive and quickly took our order, refilled our drinks and cleared our plates. We really couldn't have been any happier with the entire experience and I will return.

Yay!  I was so excited to try this place, when I saw the sign go up,  I love Mexican food and I am always looking for good Mexican places on the Westbank.  It seems like I am always looking for good food on the Westbank.  A lot of times, it's hard to come by.  I went here today for lunch with a friend of mine.  The restaurant wasn't packed at all (it was us and 2 other people).  It was really nice on the inside.  It used to be an old Pizza Hut, but it has been completely redone with nice tables and chairs and a nice bar/kitchen area.  The first thing that struck me was how inexpensive everything was.  It was really well priced and you get a lot for what you order.  Chips, salsa and green sauce are complementary, but I found the salsa a little watery.  I would have liked it if it was more actual salsa and less salsa juice.  Looking over the menu, it struck me that this is authentic Mexican food.  They even serve tongue.  Bobby B, I know you like it, but I wasn't brave enough to give it a try this time, but maybe next time.  I decided to get the burrito plate with came with a taco, beans, rice, lettuce, tomato, guacamole and sour cream.  It was SO MUCH food that I had leftovers.  My lunch only cost $8, which I thought was fantastic for a dish that I basically got two meals out of!   My friend ordered the devil shrimp.  The waitress warned my friend that the dish was super spicy, which I thought was really cool of her.  I will definitely be going back to Jalisco and recommending it to people.  It's really good Mexican food for a really good price, so be sure to check it out.  See some of the pics I posted for an idea of the menu.

My boyfriend and I got lunch here a few months ago, after a trip to the zoo, and we were both majorly underwhelmed.  First of all, I ordered a ham and cheese sandwich with a side of mac and cheese.  When I got it, there was no cheese on my ham and cheese.  I probably should have complained, but I was super hungry, so I just decided to eat it.  It wasn't anything special.  It was pretty much a ham sandwich that I could have made at home, yet it was 8 bucks.  My mac and cheese was watery and flavorless.  I can't remember what my boyfriend got, but he wasn't overly impressed, either.  I had never been there before, but he had and said that the quality of food had gone down considerably.

I just happened to come across this place while leaving Winn Dixie one day, so I added it to my list and suggested it the next time we were looking for a place to have work lunch. I always feel so cool when I'm one of the first on Yelp to discover a new Westbank restaurant like this. Ha.  This spot used to be another Thai restaurant, Banana Blossom, and the inside still has the same charm that it always had. It's small, but comfortable and there's a good amount of seating for the space. Now, I'm not as versed in Thai food as I am in other cuisine, but I know what I like. And what I like is pretty basic.  We started with an order of the spring rolls, which is lettuce, carrots and noodle in a wrap. It's really good and really light. For my entree, I got the pineapple fried rice. It came out STEAMING hot and there was well enough of it for two people. It comes with chicken and shrimp and the pineapple adds a tart sweetness to the dish that I really enjoyed. This dish was SO good and I plan on adding this to my "take out" rotation, since this restaurant is right by my house. I should also mention that they bring out a cute and free little lettuce and tomato salad, when you order, so I think that was a nice touch.  This was a great place for lunch and I love how obviously fresh everything is and how it's all cooked to order. It took a little while for the food to come out, but that didn't bother me because it was all so good. The waitress (whom I believe was the owner) was super sweet and made sure that we had everything that we needed and told us that "spice-level" can be adjusted according to our taste, so that was a nice addition. I will definitely be back.

The more I eat Vietnamese, the more I realize my palette probably leans more towards the "Americanized" version of things, so keep that in mind as you read my review.  I stopped in here for lunch, as this place had been on my list for a long time. I rarely make it into the "deep Westbank", so I was happy to find myself over this way for work in the early afternoon. Walking in, the place is really dark and dimly lit save for a tv playing Judge Judy (loudly) and some lights at the bar. I took a seat and looked over the menu.  Since it's around 90 degrees in the shade these days, I skipped the pho (mistake?) and got a pork vermicelli bowl instead. The bowl was very "no frills" and contained thick chunks of pork, vermicelli, lettuce, some cucumber and peanuts. The vermicelli was great and I liked the sauce they served on the side to add to it. The pork was okay but seemed...off. It wasn't off in a "this pork has turned" sort of way, I just don't think I liked the way they prepared it. It was kind of mushy and didn't have a ton of flavor. I also got an iced coffee, which I enjoyed.  I am glad I checked this place out, but I'm not in a hurry to rush back. I know that they are mostly known for their pho, so I guess I made a mistake when I didn't just get the pho for my lunch, but live and learn.

What's better than a thrift store? A thrift store that's for a good cause!  I was in the area today and I decided to stop in here and have a look around. I love how big the store is and I love how it's organized: by style and price. Blouses are $5, dresses are $10, etc. They also have a "boutique" section of individually priced items that cost a little more. I found a few things in that section to be a bit overpriced, but I was willing to forgive that since proceeds go to a good cause.  They also have men's clothing and housewares, although the housewares section is pretty limited and they didn't have much to offer in that department. I found a cute top for $5, so I considered the trip a success. I also like that this thrift store has dressing rooms. It seems that so many of them are "buy at your own risk" and you don't get a chance to try the items on.  The woman working told me that a few times a year that have a bag sale where you pay $10 for a trash bag and you can fill it up with as many items as you can fit. They have one this Saturday and she said that by Monday they will have an entire store full of new items, so I know that I'm going to be back.

This hotel is one of the best kept secrets in the Garden District.  Prytania Park is in a perfect location- within walking distance of a lot of cool bars and restaurants. It's in a safe area, check in is easy, there's a nice big lot so you don't have to park on the street, downtown NOLA is just an Uber away and the rates are pretty reasonable.  With my experience here the rooms have always been clean and everything has been well looked after. The rooms on the actual inside of the building are quiet and safe and far enough away from the street that I don't have to worry about noisy foot traffic. The tvs are small, so if you plan on watching a lot of tv (for some reason), be aware of that.

I love barbeque. This is a recent development within the last few years. I wasn't properly schooled on how good barbeque should taste, so as a result I ate a lot of bad barbeque and then started avoiding it all together. I now know how good barbeque should taste, or at the very least I know what I like. I like La 23 BBQ.  Look, I have no excuse why it took me so long to get here. None. I lived less than ten minutes away from this place for years and yet last week was the first time I tried it. After hearing raves from fellow foodies, I knew that I had made a mistake waiting so long to get my hands on this delicious food.  From the outside, La 23 looks pretty basic: it's a roadside stand with tables and chairs on a big covered patio. You walk up to the window, tell them what you want and they bring it out to you in a "go box" and you can go on your way or you can eat on site.  I decided to get the two meat half and half platter with two sides for $16. I figured this was a pretty good deal for this kind of lunch. I got the brisket and the jalapeño sausage with mac and cheese and cole slaw.  Brisket- delicious, juicy and cooked to perfection with a lot of flavor. One bite of this goodness left me wishing I had just gotten two big portions of this meat and called it a day. It had the perfect amount of smoke and I enjoyed it.  Sausage- pretty good. It didn't blow me away, but I was really in the mood for sausage so I enjoyed it. I would get it again, but I wouldn't get this as my only meat. I think it's a good compliment to any other meat you might get.  Mac and cheese- WHOA! Some of the best mac and cheese I have ever had. Really gooey and cheesy with great flavor. I now understand why some people's pictures of this place show them with two servings of this stuff. It's phenomenal.  Cole slaw- if you aren't a fan of cole slaw with mayo, this is the cole slaw for you. More like a light salad, I don't think there was any mayo in it at all and maybe it was made with some vinegar? I'm not sure, but it was good.  La 23 definitely lived up to the hype and I would go back. This is probably one of the better barbeque places in the area and I hope that they stick around and stay on the Westbank and just let people drive out and make the trip. I wish they had another "green" side like sprouts or something like that but, other than that, I have no complaints about this spot. Right now they mainly hold lunch hours, but I wish they were open for dinner every night- I think that might be the plan in the future.

Ahh! Finally! I feel like I've been waiting forever for this location to open, especially since David and I are such a fan of the French Quarter location.  We stopped in tonight for a quick bite and this spot didn't disappoint. They don't have a full menu yet, but we got an order of the 5 cheese mac and cheese and it was WONDERFUL. We loved the atmosphere of the place, there is a full bar with music videos playing, and the bartender just couldn't have been nicer. They have a whole selection of burgers and I will definitely be back to get an order of their pizza mac and cheese, which is one of my faves.  This is going to be a hot late night spot among the local college crowd and I'm so happy to have a place like this uptown without having to fight quarter traffic.

I recently had the privilege and honor of spending three glorious days, well into the evening, at this court house serving jury duty.  Before Monday, I had been called for jury duty (JD) one other time and we were dismissed due to lack of cases. I was not so lucky this time. Some basics: when you get your summons, you will have a number that you are assigned. This will be your number throughout the process, so don't forget it. Check the JP website the night before to see if you have to report.  Parking: the parking garage is convenient and easy and your parking will be validated, so park there for easy access. I suggest getting there a little early to avoid the line going in, especially on busier days.  Once you get there you will check in and then you just sit and wait for your name to be called. If you're lucky, you'll be called fast or dismissed. I was called immediately and I headed upstairs. The first trial I was a going to be a possible juror for was a criminal trial. After about two hours of group questioning, I was dismissed and sent back downstairs to wait to be called again. The jury I was actually picked for was a civil trial that lasted two solid days. Lucky me. More on that in a minute.  On the day I was waiting to find out if I was going to be chosen, we were given 15 minutes to get something at the snack bar, eat it and get back to the jury pool room. Apparently, it was a busy day at the JP courthouse. The snack bar has a few sandwiches and other snacks, but if you can bring your own food, that will be even better.  The actual serving of jury duty was okay. My judge was super cool and gave us lots of breaks, brought in breakfast and lunch and our jury "lounge" was packed with candy, coffee, soft drinks, water, chips, fruit, cookies and other goodies. The bailiffs really did the best they could to make the experience as comfortable as possible for us and constantly checked in to make sure that we had everything that we needed. There's WiFi in the jury room and you can have your phone as long as you aren't in the courtroom or deliberating on a verdict (this might have been just because I had a civil case, though. I'm not sure how criminal cases work with internet access).  If you get picked, expect some long days. I didn't get out until after 7 on all three days that I was there. The worst part of the entire experience was the constant sitting around and not really moving.
