I also got a side of potato salad, because during my sampling I loved it!  The shrimp and grits came and they looked so good! There was a good amount of shrimp served on top of yummy, creamy grits. I added a little hot sauce and this just put the entire dish over the top. It was amazing! My potato salad was delicious, of course. The potato salad here is diced potatoes with a nice dressing mixed into it, so it isn't heavy at all.  The menu does tend to change a bit, but I found that it's eclectic enough that anyone is sure to find something that they will enjoy and there is even a kid's menu, so be sure to bring them along as well. Lunch is served at the restaurant, Tuesday through Friday from 11am to 2pm. There is also dinner on Fridays from 6 to 9.  I will absolutely return to Cafe Hope and support this amazing restaurant. A meal here is one you can really feel good about.

To look at this place you would never guess that it actually has really good food!  I stopped in here with a friend of mine because we were in the mood for hamburgers.  I got the 8oz dressed burger which came with a cheesy potato.  I ordered it medium, but it was closer to well done.  It was still really good and juicy.  I was surprised as I would never expect good food from a little dive such as this.  We didn't stay for longer than we had time to eat, but from the sports paraphernalia on the walls, I can tell that it's a good place to catch a game and hang out with friends.  I will definitely be going back here to hang out with friends and try some of the other food they have to offer.

BZZZ  Someone told me that this coffee shop has some of the strongest coffee in the city. I either love a challenge or I'm a masochist, because upon hearing this I thought to myself, "We'll see about that!"  I stopped in and I could immediately tell that this was the kind of place where everyone knows each other. The woman in front of me was super chatty with the barista and upon ordering the last fruit tart, was nice enough to turn around and make sure that I didn't want it. I didn't, but I thought it was super sweet of her to ask. There is a huge space in the back with tables and chairs if you need to study or do some work. All in all, a really cozy place.  Upon ordering a large iced coffee with 2% milk, the barista warned me, "Sip this ssssslowly. If you drink it fast, it will be bad." Well, jeez. I've never had coffee come with a warning before. Now I'm kind of nervous. I took that first sip and...yeah...that definitely has some serious kick to it. Here is where I mention that I drink coffee every day. And I drink (what I thought was) fairly strong coffee every day. Oh, what a fool I was.  I drank some of it. I ate a huge lunch. I drank some more of it. After about drinking half of it, I was electric. I could have painted a house. I could have swam the Mississippi river. I could have jogged around the city...twice. In short, this coffee is no joke. Maybe I'm a caffeine lightweight. Maybe I just can't hang. I don't know. What I do know is that after drinking half of a large iced coffee, I threw the rest out for my own sake. Don't get me wrong; it was good coffee, but I was afraid that if I had any more my heart would explode, is all. Next time I will get a small and make sure that half of it is milk. Whole milk even. Oof.  My name is Marielle and I can't handle super strong coffee.  In short: good coffee. Very strong. Small for me next time. Woosh.

You know I had to be one of the first to check out the first Dairy Queen on the Westbank.  I had been looking forward to checking this place out, since since I had heard that DQ was finally coming to my area.  I went expecting a crowd, and I wasn't disappointed.   I mean, they had to have the JPSO out there directing traffic!  Despite the crowd, it was all very organized and the drive thru line moved quickly.  And I must say that the staff was super nice, even though they were swamped.  I ordered a turkey club sandwich, which came on a panini type of bread and, of course, a strawberry cheesequake blizzard.  Both were so good.  The sandwich was excellent and deli style, even though it was just fast food.  The blizzard was wonderful and left me wanting to try all of them.  Needless to say, I will definitely go back.  There is so much I want to try!

Ok, I'll admit it. I'm not the healthiest person in the world but I do try. I eat fairly good food and try to take care of myself.  One thing that has always eluded me is juicing. You know- that thing where you go to the market, collect all of the healthiest fresh fruits and veggies you can find and take them home and pack them into your juicer. Well, I don't have the patience for that and I don't have a juicer. But I still want juice. Now what? Well, that's where Raw Republic comes in. They do all the work for you. Just stop in, pick out a bottle of what you are in the mood for, and just like that you are drinking down 3lbs of juiced fruits and veggies. Cool, huh?  I stopped in and headed over to the juice case. I picked out the greenest thing I could find (a kale, cucumber, parsley, apple and pineapple concoction) and quickly checked out. I should note that the owner was super nice. The juice was actually really good. Sure, it's an acquired taste since I'm not a regular juicer, but it made me feel healthier with every sip.  Raw Republic also sells vegan cosmetics and healthy cereal servings. Next week they will be offering raw dips. I'll definitely be back to check it all out.

Me and the man were craving meat, and when our first option didn't pan out, we found ourselves here.  We came on a weeknight and there were a few people here, but it wasn't packed or anything. The first thing that struck me was that the inside looked as if it hadn't been updated since the place was built in the 80's, but that's no big deal. Pretty typical.   We decided on the burger with cheddar and that came with fries. The burger was cooked to perfection, but the only complaint was that it was a bit greasy. Like, to the point that the grease was coating my mouth. I feel like this is an easy fix, but about halfway through the burger, it got to be a little off putting. Other than that, it was really good, which sounds weird after the "grease" complaint, but here we are. The fries were super good and I did like the kind of "down home" feel of the whole place.  I would probably go back, mainly because the Westbank doesn't have a lot of other burger options, so I'll take what I can get.

Mmm..home cookin', when you don't feel like cookin'!  I have never been disappointed when getting food from here.  My favorite is the fried catfish, although that is pretty hard to screw up.  They have a lot of menu items from chicken to pork chops and the prices aren't too bad.  We mostly get take out, but the one time we ate there, the staff was great.  Good size portions and yummy sides (try the cole slaw!).

In my quest to try different restaurants all over town, a friend and I ended up here.  To be honest, I would probably give this place 3.75 stars, but since this isn't Star Search, we'll just go with 4 stars.  I really liked the ambiance of this place. It's small, but nice and the lay out is perfect for the space. For our starters we got the Foie Sheaux. It was delicious foie gras topped with greens. It was very rich and very good. I'm not usually a huge fan a foie gras, but this was amazing.  For my entree' I decided on the Lamb Osso Bucco. This really was an experimental kind of night, because I usually don't go for lamb at all. I guess if you are going to have something that's out of your comfort zone, this is a good place to do so. It wasn't bad. The lamb was tender and it came on a bed of fettuccine.  The sauce had a lot of flavor and complimented the lamb well. I am still not really a lamb fan, but this dish was well prepared and succulent.  As for dessert, we ordered the pumpkin ice cream. It came topped on a ginger snap. It was good because it was really light and refreshing and was a good way to end the meal.  I might go back and try some other dishes, but Apolline probably won't be on the top of my list of "go to" restaurants.

This is a divey little neighborhood bar, but it hosts a good crowd. On the night that we were here a few streets in the area were without power, so there were a good number of people enjoying the ac and having a few drinks.  The drinks are cheap and thankfully there is a smoking ban in place, so I was able to enjoy my cocktails without worrying about reeking of cigarettes. The bartender was a real character, had a lot of personality and loved to chat. I want to go back and play some tunes on the jukebox- there was a line when I was here and I am anxious to see the kind of music selection they have.

What a cool spot!  I had passed this place a few times on my way to Delachaise and always wondered what it was like. It looked small and cozy, so I was eager to check it out.  I walked in and I felt welcome immediately. The bar was filled with local "regulars", and although the place is pretty small, I had no issues finding a seat on the side away from the bar itself. They have a few beers on tap and I'm sure more in bottles. I just stuck to getting Bass on tap.  My only real complaint was that the place was a bit smoky, because it's small, but if you stay a little while it really isn't that bad.

I was pretty bummed when TJ Maxx moved from it's previous location near my house, alllll the way to Algiers. It takes me 10 whole minutes to get there!  Since I found myself in the area, I decided to stop in and check out the fancy new digs. The store is located in an entirely new complex and everything is fresh, new and organized perfectly. The store is HUGE, so I can't really blame them for the location change. TJ Maxx has everything from clothing to purses, jewelry and housewares. Since it was nearing the end of October when I stopped in, naturally all of the Christmas stuff was on full display- from wrapping paper to holiday scented candles.  I've always liked TJ Maxx because the items here are well priced and actually nice and not of cheap quality. The staff was also super friendly and were sure to ask if I needed help, which was extremely appreciated. Although I didn't buy anything, the check out lines weren't too long and all registers were open.

Whenever I think of this place, I think of the phrase "A great place to visit, but I wouldn't want to live there."  Twelve Mile Limit is a cozy little cocktail bar, but I have to agree with Tiff D when she said that it is a dive. It's pretty much a dive bar that tries to fancy itself up by serving cocktails. It's not in the greatest of neighborhoods (because of this, I have only been here once) and I think it's more of a neighborhood place than a place that someone would seek out. There are so many nice cocktail bars in the city. Going out of your way to come here for a drink seems like a waste.

I discovered this place 2 years ago, just by chance.  What a lucky find!  My favorite is the fettucine alfredo with chicken and a Peroni on the side.  Their breadsticks are fabulous and so is the olive plate.  I've also gotten pizza and it was fantastic!  Great atmosphere inside and great outside sitting right on Esplanade avenue.  The trees on the street on a nice day make you feel New Orleans, if that makes sense.  A definite "must try".

This is the "original" NOLA area Macy's and it's not that great.    Like others have said, it is extremely lacking. I was in the area and decided to stop in and check out the handbags and the selection was just pathetic. Things are disorganized and out of place and there are no employees around to help. It's sad because I came ready to spend my money and left empty handed.  I passed through the shoe department on my way out, and it looked as if it had been hit by a tornado. Shoes thrown everywhere and some not matching and I couldn't even begin to find something that I would want to purchase. You would think that the manager would take more pride in his/her store. I think I'll stick to the Lakeside location.

Since it's the New Year, and I have been here several times since my last review, I've decided to raise them one star.  I usually go and get a large black iced coffee in the drive through. I get what I pay for and the service is prompt. I can't give them more than three stars, because their food leaves a lot to be desired and when I order food they are always slow. There's a Dunkin on Terry Parkway now, so I'll probably just go to that one when the construction in that area is complete.

For those of you who don't know, David and I have recently discovered the deliciousness that is Waffle House. When I heard that the former Honey's pool hall was going to be magically transformed into a Waffle House, the irony wasn't lost on me. Naturally, we made a point to come here as soon as it opened.  This Waffle House isn't quite as big as others I've been in but I love the setup. There are booths, of course, and there's a nice bar area where you can sit and enjoy your food.   We were here on a busy night and I was impressed that the staff was really on top of things. The manager Josh was great at keeping all of his employees organized and getting orders out fast. I got my usual All Star meal which is bacon, grits, eggs, toast and a waffle and I got a side of hash browns, just for good measure. The food came out cooked perfectly and my eggs were just how I like them. Josh even checked in with us to make sure everything was cooked correctly and I thought that was really nice of him.  The staff is new, so the food took a little longer but that wasn't a big deal at all. Everything was as good as we've had at other Waffle Houses and the friendly service ensures that we'll be back to this location.

I really like this cute little shop!  Located on Freret, this place has two things that I really like: good coffee and quiet. It seems that the new trend is to blast obnoxious music in coffee shops. There's none of that here.  I got an iced coffee and it was really good. It didn't taste like the "same old" that you find at other shops. In the front, there is a nice seating area with big chairs and there are tables and chairs in the back, Local art adorns the walls, giving the place a nice, quaint feel. Also, it's a huge plus that the coffee isn't SO strong that it makes me want to run 25 miles without stopping. Sometimes I think that some of these places are in a competition to see whose coffee can make someone drop dead, first.   Anyway... I like this place and I shall return.

The thing about the French Quarter (it's not French QuarterS. If you add an "S", so help me God..) is this: there are parts of it that are amazing and gorgeous and historical and there are parts of it that are touristy and a complete money suck. You have to know where to go.  For starters, avoid Bourbon St. It's nothing but t shirt shops, tourists (the obnoxious kind), overpriced drinks that are watered down and general grossness. I really like Decatur (Molly's in particular) and Toulouse. If you are looking for antiques, look no further than Royal Street.  As far as food goes, what are you in the mood for?  Bayona is a fave of mine and is located on Dauphine. If you are in the mood for something a little more casual try Coops or Fiorella's on Decatur. If you would like to see live music, Preservation Hall is legendary. I'll save the review for the business listing, but if you find yourself there you won't be left disappointed. I won't even go into all of the cute little boutiques that are all over the place down there. Take a walk and don't be afraid to explore.  Yeah, it's true. Parking down in the Quarter is no fun, especially if you are "parallel parking impaired". I usually just park my car in a lot. I know that if you are local you are probably shaking your head. Parking in a lot beats driving around for 30 minutes looking for a spot, finding one and parking, only to later discover that you parked under a sign that says, "No Parking on Saturday night from 9-11 when the moon is full and it's humid" and you now have a ticket to pay. Ain't nobody got time for that.  Oh and please be patient with the pedicabs and buggies down there. Riding their bumper will not make them go faster and bumping your horn will spook the donkeys. Don't be a jerk.

I was here for the Summer of Sustainability dinner that I was lucky enough to get tickets to through Yelp.  The space itself is lovely. The clubhouse has a Southern mansion type feel from the light fixtures to the bar area. When you walk out on the back deck, you are surrounded by large trees that canopy the green space that leads out onto the golf course. I would really just enjoy sitting out here on a nice day, sipping a cocktail.  For the dinner I attended, everything was organized beautifully. There were 6 courses total and each course had it's own fork set in place, as well as it's own wine glass. The staff here was great about refilling drinks in a timely manner, clearing plates as I was finished and the courses came out quickly. The bartender here is extremely knowledgeable, and when I first got here, he helped me pick a wine that I would like since I'm not really that much of a wine drinker.  Now that they are open to the public for lunch and dinner, I will be returning to get the full clubhouse experience soon.

While not one of the more extraordinary cemeteries in New Orleans, Lafayette Cemetery #1 is worth a walk through, if you're in the area. I happened to be in the neighborhood and I realized I hadn't been here in a while, so I decided to take a few minutes and duck in. The cemetery was pretty quiet except for a tour guide telling a few folks about the space.   One thing I find a bit off putting about this cemetery is: although there are a few entrances, they are all locked off except for the main entrance. In other words, you are kind of trapped if you walk all the way to the back and decide to want to make a quick exit. Also, there are a lot of rows of graves that are ill-kempt and there is a lot of mud and muck in certain places. On my way out someone approached me from behind to ask me for money- he was a homeless veteran. I was glad I was with my coworker, because he scared the hell out of me. Security in here would be nice, at least at the entrance.

The National World War II Museum is a "must visit" when you come to New Orleans.  I have been here 3 times and it's always the first place I suggest to anyone who is visiting from out of town.  This place is full of all of the History of the war and really cool artifacts and interviews with people who went to war, as well as those who stayed behind.  I haven't been able to get back to see the film "Beyond all Boundaries", but I hope to soon, as I have heard that it's excellent.  Be sure to set aside an entire afternoon for the museum, because it is quite large and there is a lot to see and read.  You want to be able to take your time, so that you can get the full experience.

Such a great little place! After seeing a few folks check in here, we decided to head over and see what it was all about. I just love tiki bars- fruity drinks in fun cups and glasses with a tropic atmosphere. What's not to love?  This bar is tucked into the middle of a neighborhood, so it might be a bit hard to find at first. Fortunately, it's positioned nicely under a street light, so it's not too hard to miss. I decided to get their house punch, which was fruity, really good and served in a cute tiki cup complete with umbrella and mermaid. If tiki drinks aren't your thing, they have a full bar and a nice selection of local beers. They also serve food, if you're hungry. I only tried one drink on the day I was here, but I'm eager to stop back in and try more. They have a nice stage area, so I think that they might be planning on hosting bands in the future. I can't wait to go back!

I've been back to Oak a few times since my previous review and I think it's only appropriate that I bump them up a star.  Maybe when I first came here, I came on an "off" night, but the times I have been here since have been delightful.  The venue wasn't packed at all and not everyone was dressed up (dressing up isn't bad, mind you, the last time I think I had caught the place when they were having an after party for a Christmas thing).    This actually is a great place to see live jazz and I love that a place like this exists uptown.  I love seeing live shows, but don't always want to deal with the hassle of driving to and parking somewhere on Frenchmen.  Oak is in a really nice and safe area and street parking is plentiful close to the venue.    The staff is extremely nice and helpful and attentive.  I will definitely be going back a few times over and keeping my eye on their music calendar.

This cool little snowball stand not only serves snowballs, they serve a whole menu of poboys and fries. Since I am on a Westbank snowball adventure, I just got a snowball.  I decided to get a rainbow flavor (a new favorite). You walk up to the window, ring the bell and let them know what you are interested in ordering. One thing about this place is they give you a choice of "coned" or "flattened" at the top. Well, why wouldn't you get the cone?  The ice was okay, but not really as fine as I like and the juice was definitely lacking. The flavors they used blended together decently, but after a while the whole thing just tasted like a lime snowball. One plus about this stand is that they do have tables and chairs, if you want to sit outside. The stand isn't in the best neighborhood, and you are eating on a highway, but the only other option is eating in your car.  Good for what it is, but I won't be back.

My boyfriend (I start a lot of reviews like this, but we go out to eat a lot, ok? ;)) and I were both in the mood for a cheeseburger when we went here.  For some reason, I thought a New Orleans hamburger and seafood co. was located here, but I digress.  Anyway, we went in and ordered our burgers medium.  Well, they ended up coming well done, but they weren't bad, and we didn't bother to waste time complaining.    The service was good and the food came fast.  The only complaint my b/f had was that they calculated a 15% gratuity into the check, for a party of only two people.  It seemed odd, because he had planned on tipping a little bit more than that.  Of course, I explained that for every person who tips 18%, there is that person who doesn't tip at all.  They have obviously had some kind of issue in the past, so they felt the need to do that.  I would go back, but I would stress that I would like my burger medium and not well done.

I love having a drink on the porch of this gorgeous house turned hotel and pretend I am sipping a mint julep in the old South.  This is one of my favorite spots to hang Uptown and definitely a great place whether you want to get a drink on date, or with a group of friends.  If the weather is a little too hot for your liking, you can always sit inside, just be aware that it fills up fast.  Also, they do have wait service, but most of the time you are better off getting your own drink at the bar, if you are in any kind of hurry.  Also, I was actually lucky enough to know someone who was staying here years ago, so I got to take a look at one of the rooms.  It was huge and gorgeous and had a real "old" New Orleans feel.  I do some modeling and I would love to do a shoot there someday, but I digress.  This would be a great place to stay if you are traveling to the city on your honeymoon or just on a vacation.

Picture it: New Orleans. End of June. Probably around 90-something degrees and dense humidity, even though it's the evening. After seeing a show in the Quarter I had the BRILLIANT idea to actually "go out" somewhere down there. Meanwhile I'm in heels. So dumb.  Where am I going with this? Well, here it is. I was walking in the heels and the heat and the humidity when I decided I needed AC and ASAP. The cool air was flowing out of this place and we immediately went in, not even knowing what it was. Well, it turns out that it is a really cool place that sells a TON of beer and wine. They had beer that I didn't even know was sold down here! I was impressed.  Although I personally didn't buy anything, they are getting five stars because of what my friend did and how they handled it. Well, he had a huge bottle of beer ($14) that he was going to buy when gravity fought back and he dropped it. Bottle smashed, beer e'rrywhere, some got on my shoe. It was a mess. The guy working there immediately rushed over, cleaned it up and when my friend insisted on paying for the broken bottle (as well as a new one) he was told not to worry about it. He just charged my friend for the unbroken bottle, told us to tell people about the place and sent us on our way. He was so nice. You know as many drunk people as that guy sees in a night, he could have been SUPER ornery about the whole thing but he wasn't. So five stars it is. And I will be back.

Something about this restaurant just screams "old world 50's glamour". The decor is modern, yet has a retro feel, the atmosphere is upscale and the vibe is hip.  We were here with a group of 8 for dinner on a Friday night at 8:30. Reservations had been made, so once the entire party had arrived we were seated pretty quickly. I had already glanced at reviews of this spot, so I already had in mind what I was going to order.  We started with an order of meatballs and for my entree I decided to get the Pompano, after reading raves about it. It came with an assorted greens salad on the side. I also got a side of fries. The meatballs were really good- they had a lot of flavor, even though I only had one. I could have definitely eaten all of them if I didn't have a lot of food coming. The Pompano was excellent- it was light with a lot of flavor. I think that the sauce it came with was made from pumpkin and it was just delicious. The side salad was okay, but nothing overly special. The fries were excellent and came with aioli on the side for dipping.  My one small complaint was I wish that the waitress had been a little more attentive to our side of the table. She seemed to be mainly focusing on the other side and it was hard to hear her over the noise in the restaurant. She became more mindful of our little group after we said something, but it took her a minute to get us drinks and fill us in on the menu.  I really liked everything here and this is a great place for celebrating a special occasion or just having a nice date. The proximity to the bar at the Ace Hotel also makes it a really cool place to eat and get drinks.

I love pizza and when I saw that this place had Chicago deep dish, I was in. I had never had deep dish before, but the pictures had me sold.  We stopped in on a late Saturday afternoon and lucky us, it was happy hour. Happy hour means $3 draft beer and half off of apps. Sweet! They have a nice selection of local beers and we got an order of mozzarella sticks, just to start us off.  Now, the deep dish pizza takes 45 minutes to cook, so keep that in mind when you are visiting. We got the supreme deep dish which is pepperoni, sausage, green peppers, onions, and black olives all layered into cheesy goodness. I can't even describe how good this was. There was cheese galore and layer after layer of meat and sauce. The crust was perfection and the whole thing was unlike anything I had ever had. We got the 7" pie and that was more than enough for two people and we even had leftovers.  The food was good and service was friendly. and I will definitely be back, especially for happy hour.

This is another one of those bridges that freaks me out. I don't usually like driving across this one because, like the Judge Seeber bridge, this bridge seems like it's going to collapse any minute.  The few times I've crossed the bridge it has been up maybe half the time. I can't really complain about that because the Belle Chasse Bridge is just as bad. Anyway, this bridge is narrow and rickety. I'm not a fan and I prefer to avoid it, if possible.

This place is great! Not only can you go in and get your makeup done by a pro for a special occasion (or just a night out) but they sell makeup here too. The entire staff is really knowledgeable and can help you figure out what works for you (and what doesn't).  They also do spray tanning and you and your friends can have a makeup party for a birthday or bachelorette party. It's a really cool idea for something different.

Thanks to Yelp, I had gotten vouchers for a free breakfast here and since I am never one to turn down free food, we headed over to happily spend the $30 gift card.  The place was pretty dead for Sunday brunch at 11am. That might be worth noting if you like Sunday brunch, but hate a wait. We were seated immediately and looked over the menu. As soon as I saw that they offered shrimp and grits, my decision was made. My boyfriend got a traditional breakfast of bacon, eggs and toast. I also got one of their nitro iced coffees.  The coffee was excellent. The shrimp and grits, on the other hand, was lacking something. First of all, there were only 4 tail-on shrimp in the entire dish. Second of all, it was kind of bland. I had to add salt to it to get any type of flavor out of it, and I usually never have to do that. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't on par with other versions of shrimp and grits in the city, so I wouldn't order it again. My boyfriend's traditional breakfast looked delicious and he mentioned that the bacon was nice and crispy.  Service was excellent and our waitress was nice and attentive. Maybe brunch just isn't their "thing" and I would love to try the place again at lunch time.

This a nice little neighborhood bar. The bartender was really friendly and they have good beer like Fat Tire and LA 31. It was pretty slow on the night that we came, so we chatted with the bartender and the one other patron that was in the place. I can see how this is probably a popular hang out earlier in the evening. I got the vibe that it's a "pre game" type of bar. I'd love to come back on a night where there are more people. Like others have said the place is cash only.

This shop is incredible! First of all, they have a lot of cute clothing and the owner was awesome. Second of all, it's all really well priced stuff! On the day I was here everything was $19! That's almost unheard of for a store on Magazine St.  Here you'll find a nice selection of casual-style dresses and other outfits. They also have a nice selection of accessories. I wished I had come to this store first because I had just left another store where I splurged and bought a few things and I think my money would have been a tad better spent here. I'm definitely going to be coming back to do some post-Christmas shopping and I can't wait to stock up on nice, inexpensive clothes.

I really need to rave about this place for a minute.  I love how cozy the house itself is- there are rooms in the back area and there is a nice colorful patio. We were in one of the back rooms that is right off of the street and it was nice and quiet and we weren't bothered at all. The room is small, but if you are looking for a great "crash pad" during Mardi Gras, or any other time that you are visiting, this is the place for you.  I love this neighborhood, and there are a lot of bars and restaurants in the area that are walkable and the streetcar is just a few blocks over. The staff is as nice as can be- the first time I dealt with a man and the second time I dealt with a woman. I think they are both owners and they were helpful in getting us cabs so that we could zip around town.  Creole Gardens has a complimentary breakfast for customers- one at 7am and one at 9am. You order at the kitchen and they bring your food to you in the dining room.

I don't know why I bother with fast food at all, especially Sonic.  The service at this Sonic is always super slow, more than once the food has been...let's just say "not really hot" and I always seem to leave unimpressed. The only saving grace is the happy hour, where you can get discount drinks, but even those are pretty disappointing.   There are better choices for fast food. Avoid this place.

Review #800 (and review #346 for the year. BOOM.)  For this momentous occasion, what better place to review than where I spent my birthday? I had wanted to try this place FOREVER, so when my birthday rolled around, I knew that this would be the perfect place to celebrate.  The actually take reservations, so we made some and were immediately seated when we arrived. We got a nice, small table in the back, which was perfect for me. Looking over the menu, everything sounded amazing. We decided to start with the Sautéed Herb Gnocchi with Pancetta, Parmesan and English Peas and the Pâté with Pickled Vegetables and Roasted Pine Nuts. The gnocchi was okay, but the pâté was AMAZING. They bring you a huge serving of it, and two people didn't even get through it all. It was fantastic.  For my entree, I decided on the Cochon de Lait with Stone Ground Grits,  Pork Cracklin' and Sweet & Sour Red Cabbage. Although my entree was pretty slow to arrive (at one point I wondered if the order had been sent to the kitchen late) once it did I was thrilled. The pork was tender and perfectly cooked. The meat's gravy soaked into the grits resulting in a delicious mix and grits and juice that was just a delight. I was impressed that it was a good serving of food and I couldn't finish it all. I seriously want to go back and get this dish again. It was that good.  Friendly staff and a great atmosphere make this the perfect place for any date night or celebration. I will most definitely return to One.

I don't have much occasion to frequent Office Depot, but whenever I have been here I have had no issue finding what I needed. They have all of the basic office supplies that you would expect to need and find and they even have fancy office furniture!  About a year ago I bought a box of envelopes (for some reason). I used two of them before I realized that I didn't need a whole box. I brought them back and explained the situation and they took them back and gave me a refund with no issue.

Kind of sketch-ville. Of course I was passing through Algiers when my "low fuel" light came on. Naturally, I started freaking out (inside) and hit up my smart phone to find the nearest gas station and this is where it lead me. There were random men just lurking outside with no real purpose. There were people giving me weird looks as I was filling up. Yep, this gas station had it all! With that said, the gas wasn't too pricey at $2.05/gallon. I wouldn't seek this place out, but it got the job done so mission accomplished.

Café Adelaide was on my list as soon as the Coolinary list dropped, so I was excited to try it.  We made reservations, and it's a good thing we did because lunch time on a Friday gets packed at this lovely hotel restaurant. Since Café Adelaide is Brennan owned, I went in with naturally high expectations.  I had looked over the Coolinary menu before we got here, so I knew exactly what I was getting. I started off with a bowl of the Commander's turtle soup. I think that Commander's has some of the best turtle soup in town and, since this is the same recipe, this bowl didn't disappoint. The broth was delicious and there was a generous amount of meat. Even though it was a "special" menu, the serving was quite generous.  For my entree, I got the BBQ shrimp and grits. Tasty tail-on BBQ shrimp over chilis, pork belly, and grits with a sweet BBQ glaze. I liked that this was different from typical shrimp and grits in that it was a little bit sweeter because of the glaze. The shrimp were nice and fat and everything blended together perfectly.  For lunch, they have 25 cent martinis, if that's your thing (limit three). The Coolinary menu really can't be beat- the turtle soup and shrimp and grits lunch cost $20. Staff was friendly but was clearly a bit overwhelmed by the crowd. I loved the "dressy casual" atmosphere of the place and large windows let in a lot of natural light and make for a nice experience. I will return.

Wow.  I had completely forgotten about this place and I haven't been in about a year!  First of all, believe it or not, I have never gotten the pizza here.  Yeah, I know.  My favorite is the Pasta Jambalaya and I get it everytime I go.  It's basically jambalaya served over penne pasta...delicious!  Now just a fair warning, all of the LA pizza kitchens are independently owned and they all have different menus.  When I went to the uptown location, not only was I surprised to see that they didn't carry my favorite, but the dish I ordered (I can't even remember what it was) wasn't good at all.

I don't review fast food places on here unless the food/service is exceptionally good or exceptionally bad.  This review is because this Bell is the latter.  I went here when it first opened a few months ago.  The service was super slow and the food was sub par.  I ordered a grilled stuft burrito and it was missing things that I remember being in it.  Sure, it was the first one I had had in ages, but they wouldn't just remove things from it, right?  Last weekend, it was late, so my boyfriend suggested we get Taco Bell.  First, for him to even suggest we get food from here is earth stopping, as he hates the place.  But I digress...  I ordered the Nachos Bell Grande and he got some sort of melt and a burrito.  My Nachos were DISGUSTING.  They had no "meat" (see the latest news about this place) on them and they were SOAKED in their cheese sauce stuff.  It was like someone emptied the cheese gun on it and threw in some beans.  I couldn't even finish it.  Gross!  My boyfriend took one bite of his burrito and said that it tasted awful and couldn't eat it.  I've never had any issue with any other Taco Bell.  I would chalk it up to the place just opening, and them still getting their "stride", but it's been a few months and how hard is it to make nachos??  I think I'll just go to the one on Manhattan, as I usually do.

I just loved this unique gallery!  I was lucky enough to be able to pass through here on Dirty Linen night and I was delighted by the type of art that Chris Roberts-Antieau has created here. The art here is really unique because the "paintings" are really all hand stitched. It's like someone created different art work quilts that tell a story and convey a mood. It's very unique and very interesting.  Some of the art stands alone, and some of it tells a whole story like a quilted comic strip, of sorts. It's such an interesting way of creating art that the process itself must be fascinating.

Well, good job Dunkin on Manhattan. You managed to screw yourself out of a five star review from me after one bad experience.  Let me start by saying, I like this place. Well, I did like this place. This was my third visit, as I am an avid fan of iced coffee and it's cheap and good here. It's nice to know I can go somewhere to get iced coffee that won't cost $6.   I went in this morning and one other person was in there who had already ordered. I walked up, ordered a large iced coffee and decided on some hash brown bites as a snack (6 pieces).  The man in front of me got his order as I continued to wait and wait and wait. Finally, a girl asks what I ordered and I tell her. She starts prepping my iced coffee and asks if I want cream. I reply, "Just a splash" Y'all, it came out the color of white milk. Seriously. "Just a splash" does not mean "fill half the container with cream". Yep, this is why I always get black coffee wherever I go.  But that's not all, I still need my (6) hash browns. So, I'm standing there sucking down my coffee flavored milk drink thing when FINALLY someone comes and asks if I'm waiting on something. "Hash browns", I reply. She acknowledges that and goes back to her business. I guess she just wanted to check in. Then another girl asks who also then goes back to what she was doing immediately after. It should be noted, that while I was waiting, the girls who weren't busy loading donuts were laughing and joking with each other and taking pictures on their cell phones.  FINALLY the young man preparing the food sees me and asks if I need something. Once again I say, "Hash browns. I've told two people already." He says that no one told him (I believe it) and they would be right out. Shortly thereafter, there they were; my 20 minute hash browns. Admittedly, I snatched the bag from the guy and just left because I was irritated. Now, since I waited so long it maybe would have been a nice gesture to maybe make it a double order of a whopping 12 hash browns, but whatever. I'm not the manager (where WAS the manager, anyway?).  I get that this place is new, but come on. No one was in there and there was one person in the drive thru. There's no excuse. I might go back for iced coffee (black) but NOTHING else. If hash browns take 20 minutes, what happens when someone gets a breakfast combo? Does the place just shut down?

I think I have found my new Uptown coffee house hang out.  Ever since Rue De La Course on Magazine closed, I have been searching for a new Uptown coffee place to call home. Sometimes you just want to go somewhere and sip coffee and take it all in. I think I have finally found my new place.  Reservoir Cafe is really neat. In a lot of ways, it reminds me of that other LGD fave Mojo. Not only is the coffee really good, but there is plenty of seating (they even have booths!) and the place is small enough to feel cozy and nice. They serve sandwiches for breakfast and lunch and have all of the other basic things that you would expect from a coffee place. I like that they have a big window in the front, so that you can watch the world go by. There is plenty of outside seating, too for the nice days that you want to get some fresh air.

Here's a fun fact about me: when I was a kid, my parents made me study a lot. Now, I don't say this in a bad way, in fact it benefited me greatly. You see, I went to private school and my parents encouraging me to study was their way of getting the most bang for their buck. Growing up, Educator and I were very familiar with each other. Way more familiar than one kid should ever be with a place like this.  I recently decided to stop in here, mainly because I hadn't set foot in here since I was probably 11 or so and I was curious as to what it was like to view this place through the eyes of someone with a driver's license. I remember coming in here with my dad and picking up workbooks that would help reinforce my well priced education. When I stepped in, all of the memories came back. The place has not changed one bit in 18 years.   Everything you could possibly need is here, whether you are a teacher or a parent looking for educational tools. They have educational posters, workbooks, flashcards, bulletin board supplies, maps, educational puzzles, games, learning aides, etc. They have everything. This place is like heaven for teachers. It's pretty incredible.  When I went in, the place was completely dead and there were three people working. This kind of baffled me. I guess they have to be prepared in the event that a horde of teachers rushes in and needs flashcards and workbooks STAT! No time to waste!  Anyway, whether you are a teacher or just someone who wants to brush up on their fifth grade math, this is the place for you. Just a note: I noticed that most of the workbooks and educational things are geared towards elementary school, so if you are in high school or college, you might want to look elsewhere for study aides.

Oh my gosh! This is SUCH a cute shop!!  I never even knew this place existed, until I happened to be driving down Magazine St. one day and it caught my eye.  This place is amazing and carries every type of umbrella you could ever imagine. I love that they have unique, pretty umbrellas, and in a rainy city like New Orleans, it almost makes you wonder why there aren't more umbrella shops in town.  I didn't buy anything this time, but I have my eye on a gorgeous red lace parasol. They have umbrellas for second lines for weddings as well, so if you are looking for that type of thing, be sure to check this place out. They even have umbrellas that are perfect for kids!  I will say that the umbrellas are not on the cheap side at all, but for as unique as they are, I think that they are absolutely worth the money.

Ha. We actually ended up here accidentally. We had just finished dinner at Gautreau's when I had the idea to see some live music. I knew that a band was probably playing at Les Bon Temps on Magazine, so we hopped into a cab and told the cabbie that's where we wanted to go.  Well, he misunderstood and we weren't paying attention (too much chatting) and next thing you know, he pulls up in front of Bon Ton Cafe. Deciding to make the best of an unplanned situation, we decided to hop out and check the place out.  Well, it's a full on restaurant, but they do have a bar, so we sat and enjoyed some beer for a little while. The staff seemed happy to have us and enjoyed our little story about going down the wrong path.  After hanging out for a while, they called us a cab and we eventually ended up at the correct Les Bon Temp. Naturally, this is the one day a week that a band wasn't playing. You win some, you lose some.  I'll be back at Bon Ton soon to actually eat.

This coffee was a lifesaver when I stopped in here after checking out during my Pontchartrain stay. The cafe itself is pretty small with basic tables and chairs and you let them know if you are dining in or getting something to go, as soon as you walk in. The staff is super nice and although I didn't eat here, I can say that the iced coffee is particularly good and while it's not the *best* coffee I have ever had, I found it flavorful and enjoyable.

This isn't one of the biggest or fanciest parades, but it's a good little kick off to the Mardi Gras parade season.  They don't have any really special throws, but I did get a cup to add to my "collection".  Suzanne pretty much hit the nail on the head with this one.

Bellocq is one of the fancy cocktail bars the New Orleans is known for. I am not really a huge cocktail person, but I can appreciate a well crafted drink.  Bellocq has an extensive menu of drinks that they can make for you, that are sure to appeal to all tastes.  Oddly enough, I think that the best thing about this place is the atmosphere. It's really dimly lit, which I love. I really dig cozy places like this. It also has a lot of sofas and benches for group sitting, which adds to the tranquility of the entire place.   If you are in the mood for a little something to eat, they have a small menu of little tapas that you can munch on.  I knocked off a two stars because the staff seemed overwhelmed by the large crowd and there was limited seating at 9 pm.

It's time for a re-review because I have been here many times in the 4+ years since my last review and I am always happy with the food and service.  We were here today before the first game of the NFL season. We were pretty hungry and the place had a good number of folks waiting for a table, so we gave them our number and they said they would text us when a table was ready. We wandered around a bit and after about 25 minutes we got a text and we were seated.  Our waitress was super friendly and fast and we didn't have to wait long for her to take our order. We started with the onion strings, which was a pile of thin cut onion rings fried to perfection. We loved them. For our entree, we both decided to get the crawfish etouffee and I got a side of corn grits. Well, at first there was a bit of confusion- they brought out the corn grits and two small bowls of the crawfish etouffee. Considering this dish is $12, we were hoping there was a mistake There was, it turned out they had accidentally sent out app portions. They let us keep the app portions and sent out our crawfish etouffee entree.  The crawfish etouffee was delicious! It was a large portion, the crawfish were both fried and sauteed and it was served in a delicious sauce over rice. I like that the sauce was spiced nicely and I didn't have to add any hot sauce to it. The corn grits were perfection and if you have had corn grits at a place like Zea's, they are on the same level as their version.  We didn't have to wait a long time for food or drinks and the staff was really good at keeping up with the crowd. This is a solid stop for food, especially before a game.

Okay hotel located in what I would call "sketch ville".  A friend of mine was staying here on his visit to the city. The room wasn't too bad. It had an area for sleeping with a good size tv and there was an attached "sitting" room with a seating area and a desk and a view of Canal Street. One thing that would get really old is the ridiculously small bathroom. You have to squeeze yourself against the wall in order to get the door to close!  The thing that struck me about this place was the lobby. There seemed to be people who weren't staying here milling about and the staff seemed pretty indifferent. Even though my friend was just a few blocks from Bourbon, I encouraged him to get a cab and not walk because the area isn't good at all.

This is a pretty "okay" gas station. I always like to get gas at Brothers because it's definitely cheaper than other stations. Inside they have some food offerings like fried chicken, fish, po boys, fries and things like that. The store seems pretty clean and I've never had an issue with service here. The one or two times I've gotten food here, it's been pretty good even though this isn't my usual go to Brothers.  This spot can get a little sketchy at night, so keep your wits about you.

This is an interesting little hole in the wall where the selling point is cheap drinks. You will also see some unique characters here. Cheap drinks or not, this isn't really my type of place and I would never go out of my way to come here. With that said, it serves a purpose and the "regulars" seem to like it.

This is for a review of the pool/bar area.  I was here for a private party. I really liked the pool area. I didn't get to swim, but I can see how during the summer this would be a cool hang out spot for those of us who don't have a pool or want to sneak into a hotel pool to swim (ha). The pool is a good size and there is a nice outdoor bar and seating area/cabana area. Really nice for a party or something.  The inside bar area is nice too. There is a pretty decent beer selection and the bartender was friendly and nice. The seating is somewhat uncomfortable and left a little something to be desired, but besides that I really enjoyed it here.  I would love to go back and actually try the food and get the full experience.

Really fun spot that always has a cool band on stage and a lot of people dancing.  Cafe Negril isn't as big as some of the other music venues on Frenchmen St, but it's still really cool. It gets full pretty quick, so a lot of the time you just end up dancing with a bunch of strangers and it's a lot of fun. They have a lot of reggae bands that play here. I don't think that's all that plays here, but it's what has been on stage the last few times I have been here.  I'd go back. Worth checking out, but probably not worth going out of your way.

Coolinary, y'all! I had to re-review and fill you in!  So, Coolinary is one of my favorite times of year. You get to dine at places you might not normally dine and try different menu items. As soon as I saw the Coolinary lunch menu for Audubon Clubhouse, I knew it had to go to the top of my list.  We sat on the porch, on a nice cloudy day and it wasn't too warm at all. The view is gorgeous- you get to look out at the beautiful park and majestic trees and the golf course in the distance makes for a nice "rich" feel. It's the perfect place to catch up with friends. Enough about the view- it's all about the food.  When I saw the Coolinary menu here, I thought it was too good to be true. Considering the price is only $20, I assumed that the portions would be super small. I was so wrong. I started with an order of the hummus. Out came a generous portion of yummy, perfectly spiced, creamy hummus with a side a crackers for dipping. It was light and a perfect kick-off to the meal. For my entree, I got the fried catfish poboy. I had assumed this would be a small poboy, but it was a full-sized poboy served with a large pile of fries! WHAT?! You go to any other poboy joint in town and pay nearly $20 for just this dish. The catfish was thick and juicy and fried perfectly. The sandwich itself was nicely dressed and the fries were crispy, just how I like them. I happily cut the sandwich in half and boxed the rest up for later. For dessert, I had to go with the bread pudding topped with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Their bread pudding is yummy with a nice drizzle of sauce on top. It was rich and decadent and a delightful way to end the meal.  This was a perfect afternoon lunch and, I would bet, one of the best Coolinary lunch deals going right now. It was so good that I think I am going to try to go back at least one more time before the end of the month. The staff was great and you just can't beat the level of class at a place like this. This is one of the secret places in New Orleans that makes our city great.

I've been coming to this Baskin Robbins forever. I really like that it is a little smaller than other BRs. To me that adds something to it.  I came here the other day for a strawberry and banana smoothie and it was so good! I had never tried any of the smoothies here, but now that I know how tasty they are, I will definitely be getting them more often.
Awesome glass beads, bracelets, and luggage tags this year!  Another all star performance!

With a name like "Who Dat" it's gotta be good, right?  This is a neat little Marigny coffee shop and cafe. When I pulled up to this place, I didn't expect much. It looked SUPER small and nothing really special on the outside. When I went inside, I was pleasantly surprised to find a super cozy set up. First of all, it was a rainy day, so that added to the cozy atmosphere. Second of all, I liked that there were small tables and a little "dining" area in the back and on the other side there was a room complete with sofas. It felt like I was at someone's house.  I ordered an ice coffee, which was delicious and I decided to sit outside with a friend and talk and watch the rain. Really nice. I didn't get to try the food but looking over the menu, they offer what sounds like super yummy sandwiches that I will definitely have to go back and try. I also want to try their breakfast selections.  Extra points for super easy street parking. I got a spot right in front and there were plenty to spare!

I am pretty excited for this car wash. Usually, I have to travel all the way to Marrero to get my car cleaned the way I like, but this spot is closer to home so I thought I would give it a shot.  I just did the drive thru wash on the day I came. Like Eddie said, it is a "touch" car wash, so there are brushes and stuff scrubbing the dirt off. They don't have a "pre wash", which is usually a guy with a soapy brush who loosens up the dirt on your car before your drive into the wash. It had been a while since I had my car washed, and while this car wash did get a lot of dirt off, there was still a lot of dirt left on my car after I was done- a bummer to say the least.  I'm not complaining- the wash I chose was only $5 and I know that if I had done a "pre scrub" like Eddie suggests, it would have done the job. I'll probably be back.

I am updating this because I first wrote my review when I was just a baby yelper and I didn't know that a review had to be more that two sentences.  I like Breaux Mart. It gets major points because it's so close to my house and super convenient. I don't think I have ever picked up actual full grown groceries here, in the true sense of the word. The only thing I usually get here is beer, wine and ice cream. I know. I usually stop here when I am on my way to a frat party or something, or so it would seem. With that being said, they don't have a huge beer selection. If you are looking for specialty brews, you are going to be left disappointed. They have the basics: bud, coors, abita, NOLA, etc. but that's about it.  As for the ice cream selection (yeah, I'm going there) they don't have any of the Ben and Jerry's I really like (Late Night Snack, Americone Dream) and that can get annoying.   However, they do have a great bakery and do always have super fresh French bread and other pastries. I'll also stop in for produce every now and then, as it is always fresh.

I have been here once and I will probably never be back. The place isn't bad and the staff is super nice, but I HATE bars where I have to get buzzed in.   I know it's supposed to make me feel safe, but the buzzer has the opposite effect on me. I get buzzed in and then the questions start popping into my head. "Why do they need a buzzer?" "What happened that the manager finally said 'We need to start buzzing people in'"? "What is the criteria for NOT buzzing someone in?" "THAT dude looks a little suspicious. How did HE get in?"  It's just a whole lot in my head when I am trying to just relax with friends. No thanks. There are too many nice bars in the city. Ok, now I'm sounding like a snob. In conclusion, good place that would be better if I wasn't worried about the buzzer.

I have been passing by this little Italian restaurant for years, but I had never had the opportunity to go in.  Just the outside looked nice.  Sort of small and dimly lit.  I always imagined what it was like inside.  A friend and I finally went here for dinner and I was immediately blown away, before any food was even served.  The staff is very friendly and greated us when we walked in.  The place was kind of packed, and we hadn't made reservations, so we sat at the bar and chatted, while we waited on a table.    We waited about 20 minutes and when we were finally seated, we were given complimentary bread sticks that were served with the most delicious garlic butter I think I have ever had.  I ordered the fettucini alfredo.  That's pretty standard whenever I go to a new Italian place, but they have a huge menu with every kind of veal you could want to stuffed chicken and seafood dishes.  My dinner came with some kind of Italian chicken soup with veggies and a salad, and it was fantastic.  The alfredo was beyond amazing and the sauce was so decadent and rich, that I had no choice but to take a lot of it home.  It was SO fantastic and good!  The atmosphere of this restaurant is amazing.  It's really small and cozy.  It has dim lighting (not too dim, but just enough for a romantic feel).  There was Louis Prima playing in the background, as well as other "big band" tunes.  It was right up my alley.  This would be a FABULOUS place for a date!  The staff is super friendly and eager to please.    Go here expecting an experience.  From the time we walked in, to the time we left, it took about 2 hours.  If we had made reservations, it would have gone a little faster, but that's not a big deal.  This is such a nice place, you won't want to rush your time here.  This is the quintessential date place.

I had completely forgotten that we had gotten take out from here!  I got an alligator poboy from this place that was out of this world delicious!  I tend to be a pretty adventurous eater, so if you are too, then you have to try it.  I've only gotten take out and I haven't been to the actual place, so I can't really review the atmosphere or anything.  I'll be sure to update when I go back!

Oh. My. Godddddd.  Ok. First of all, let me start by saying that I am not a GIANT burger fan. I like hamburgers, but I'm not a person who seeks out the best burger and is always "on the hunt" for the perfect burger. With that said, if I WAS that type of person, my search would end here.  Stopped in here for lunch on a Sunday during a Saints game. The crowd was non existent. Perfect. I was immediately welcomed when I walked in and after looking over the menu, and taking the advice of the man behind the counter, I decided on The Company Burger with sweet potato fries on the side.  I sat and waited and my food came quickly. Like others have said, the burger doesn't come with lettuce and tomato. The one I ordered came with cheese and pickles. They have a "mayo" bar with different mayos and sauces. I decided to try the chipotle mayo and the "special sauce". The special sauce was okay, but the chipotle mayo was so good that I put it on my burger and went back for more so that I could dip my fries in it. Super healthy that way.  The burger was out of this world. It was cooked to perfection (medium) and super juicy and delicious. The fries were amazing and for $2.50 you get a TON. My fry basket was overflowing and I wasn't able to finish them all. I really liked that the Saints game was on a big tv so that I could sit and watch the game as I ate. It made for the perfect scenario since it wasn't super packed. They have beer and soft drinks if you want something to drink, but I just had water.  I agree with John L.H. about the parking. It was super easy with the lot, but I can see how it can probably get packed during peak hours, so keep that in mind. I can't wait to go back and try some other burgers!   And for all of the people who gave low reviews because they don't eat beef: You serious, Clark? The word "burger" is in the name. What did you expect?

Really fun and we had a perfect spot right near Canal Place!  This is a pretty short parade, and as long as you aren't going into it expecting a big Mardi Gras style parade, you are going to have a good time. I liked the themed floats that had a local flavor (Pat O'Brien's, PJ's coffee) and the highlight was definitely the bands and the marching groups.  I wish that there had been a few more "spooky" throws, but I was happy that I got a whole bunch of Krewe of Boo cups, a Pat O's hat, PJ's coffee and Aunt Sally's pralines. Whenever food is involved, I'm a happy camper- if only I had gotten my hands on a bag of Chee Wees! I do wish they would throw beads with Halloween themes such a skeletons and pumpkins and things like that and maybe a signature Krewe of Boo bead- the regular plain Mardi Gras beads seemed like a waste and lot of people didn't even bother trying to catch them.  All in all I had a good time and I'll attend in the future.

I had heard about this taco truck from a few people on twitter, but I had never found myself at Dos Jefes, so that I could try it.  When I first heard of this place, I was a little hesitant.  I mean...it's a taco truck.  How good could it be, right?    Well, after a Yelp event, my friend Scott and I decided (well, he decided and I went along with it) to finally give taceaux loceaux a try.  We get there, and I was blown away at how many people were waiting in line for this food.  We were kind of late, so they had already run out of a lot of food, but they still had a nice selection of things to choose from.  For the life of me, I can't remember what I got (all of the menu items have super creative names) **edit: Taceaux Loceaux (@TLNola) just tweeted me and reminded me that I got the "Messin with Texas" which is a slow roasted Brisket Taceaux.**  but it was fantastic.  It was a taco with brisket topped with cabbage and all kind of other goodness.  It was delicious.  I couldn't believe that such good food could come from a truck!    I will definitely be going back in order to try some of their other stuff!

After passing Rag Doll over and over when it was closed, I finally made it here during business hours. I was not left disappointed.  First of all, they have all kinds of cute dresses that are great for everyday wear or a special occasion. My favorite was probably the rack of handmade dresses using vintage patterns. Super cute idea! New vintage! They also have an assortment of vintage clothing and jewelry, which is really reasonably priced (less than $30).  With so many "vintage" shops on Magazine street, I found that this is one of the best of the bunch, as far as prices go. You can step in here and choose from a lot of cute things for well under $100. My kind of place! I will definitely be back.

I was a huge fan of the Little Tokyo location that used to be here and it seems like Ikura is just as good, if not a little bit better.  I stopped in for a really early dinner and, even though I was eating alone, I wasn't forced to sit at the sushi bar- already a win. I decided to keep it simple with my usual Philly Roll and Tuna Roll and I got their Big 'n Easy roll which had all kinds of yummy raw stuff in it. The Philly and Tuna rolls were perfection. The Big 'n Easy roll was great, the fish was fresh and it was really big and well worth the price. Of course, I had leftovers that I was happy to box up and enjoy later.  One thing that blew me away was how fast the service was here. There was a decent crowd and I had my food within 10 minutes of ordering and I was really pleased with that. My one tiny complaint was that it was a nice, sunny, early evening and the waiter closed all the blinds in the middle of dinner, making the restaurant almost completely dark. Hey, I like to see the sun when it stays light out a little later and eating in near darkness at 5pm was odd. Despite that one hiccup, I will definitely go back.

I can't believe I forgot to review this place!  I went here when some friends and I went to a Saints game a few weeks ago.  This is a great place to hang out before or after a  Saints game, mainly because it's really close to the Superdome and they serve beer and food.  When we went the bar was extremely packed (of course), but in spite of that, we were able to order food and we were served pretty quickly.  We sat at the bar, since it was the only "free" spot, so I didn't get to try out the fancy beer taps that are on the tables.  This is a wonderful place to go if you are tailgating for a Saints game, or if you just find yourself in the area and want something a little different.  I will definitely go back, next time I find myself in that neck of the woods.

For birthday meal #2 I chose Rizzuto's because I had heard good things about the place and famed Tony Angelo's had been here and I was a bit curious with what changes they had made to the inside.  I made reservations on Open Table and we were seated as soon as we arrived. We were seated in a small, back room with some pretty noisy people, but I understand that it's a festive time of year, so I just let it go. I had heard how rich the food was, so we decided to skip appetizers and go right for the main course.  I got the tortellacci, which was stuffed with short ribs and topped with  marinara, pecorino romano with pork & red gravy. It was quite tasty. I had never had an Italian dish with rib meat included, and I really enjoyed it. What I heard was right: the dish was really rich. I had no complaints and I would order this again. David had the lobster fra diavolo which looked AMAZING. This was a huge portion of pasta and David thought that it was really good.  As for the not so great: we were brought bread and olive oil, which we enjoyed, but I thought it was odd that it was dropped on our table about 2 minutes before we got our entrees. Maybe this is policy and they want to make sure you are actually ordering food before they give you bread, I'm not sure. Also, right before we got our food they dimmed the lights and I just don't like eating in the near-dark.  Since it was my birthday dinner, we ordered the cheesecake, which was great. It wasn't too sweet, in fact it was almost more savory than sweet, and we really enjoyed it.   It kind of bothered me that they didn't put a candle on my dessert plate or even wish me "Happy Birthday", especially since I made a note of it on Open Table when I made my reservation. Right now you might be rolling your eyes or saying "give me a break, princess", and I get that, but it would have been nice to hear a mention of it. I don't need a song and dance, just a little acknowledgement. It's not a big earth-shattering deal, but worth a mentioning for anyone else planning a celebration here.  All in all the atmosphere of the place was great, the food was good and our waitress was on top of everything. If I go back, I'll request a table in the main dining room and not the small back room and I wouldn't go for another celebration-type event.

Um. No. I don't like parades where the Krewe is more concerned with getting drunk than throwing beads. Tonight we encountered float after float of people literally just waving to the crowd and not doing anything else. It was sad. There were pretty much zero throws from this parade and the riders were obviously only there to drink and throw stuff to their friends. Skip it.

I think that I am becoming somewhat obsessed with all of the rooftop bars that New Orleans has to offer. At this time last year, we didn't even have one and now we have three! I am hoping that this trend continues.  Monkey Board is located at the top of the new Troubador hotel and talk about fancy! Not only do you get a gorgeous view of the city, but there is a lot of space for lounging, fancy sofas and chairs, an outdoor bar area and food! I will say that while the roof top bar at The Pontchartrain will always have my heart, Monkey Board is probably the perfect spot for those of you who enjoy day drinking with a view. There's no fighting for space and there's no having to go in and out for drinks. Everything is at your fingertips.  On the night we were here we enjoyed a couple of cocktails but we didn't end up staying very long because New Orleans weather is weird- warm one minute, cool the next. Alas, the chilly breeze got the best of us after a while and we had to call it a night. I am definitely making plans to go back when it's a bit warmer and maybe even try some of the food. I would call this one of the more romantic spots in the city and look forward to having many a date night here with the man.

Man oh man. I don't even know where to START with this review, son! So many flavors and so much good stuff. I will try to go my best to describe my experience.  First things first- we stopped in here at around 7 on a Thursday night and there was a 30 minute wait. No worries- just duck next door into Swirl, have a glass of Pinot and they will text you when your table is ready.  This place is small, y'all! There aren't that many tables and it's pretty cozy. I like it like that, but I know a lot of people might not. The menu is pretty extensive will all kinds of Mediterranean goodies to choose from.  We started with the lamb hearts (don't get nervous) and the Brussels sprouts. The lamb hearts were SO GOOD! Does it make me weird that this was one of my favorite parts of the meal? Those Brussels sprouts, though. What do they do to them?! They aren't fried or grilled. I don't know, but it's some kind of magic- mine never taste like that.  For our main course, it was pretty difficult, but we decided to go with the falafel platter and one of the specials of the day which was boar. Pretty wild stuff. The falafel platter was incredible and was plenty enough for two people. It came packed with hummus, slaw, house salad, flatbread, and a few other goodies. I took a picture; check it out. My favorite on this platter was definitely the hummus- it might not be the very best I have ever had, but it was creamy smooth with a lot of flavor. The boar was also tasty. I don't think I have ever had it before and i found it a little gamey without being too overwhelming.  My experience here was amazing and I would LOVE to return. The waitress was extremely attentive, even though it looked like she was in charge of almost every table and the food was memorable.

I'm kind of worried about this place. It just opened (they have grand opening signs everywhere) and yet, the place was totally dead when I stopped in.  I had received some "incentive" coupons in the mail from this Dunkin' Donuts, in order to encourage new customers. I needed no real encouragement, as this DD is pretty close to my house and I am a sucker for cheap, not so great, but it has caffeine in it, coffee.  I stopped in to get a discount iced coffee with my magic coupon and the place was pretty dead. The girl behind the counter was super nice and accommodating and I felt bad that I wasn't more in the mood for a donut or something, but I was kind of in a rush and needed an iced coffee STAT.  I've pretty much made it my personal mission to keep this place open. This spot has been cursed ever since the Pizza Hut closed, so I'm gonna stop in a couple times a week for coffee and a sandwich or something.

This Sun Ray is a weird mix of cooked plates and sushi.  They have things you would probably expect from a place like this such as chicken and shrimp and even nachos and quesadillas.  Oddly, I have never had any of that.  The two times I have been here, I had the sushi.  Now, this isn't what you think of when you think of a typical sushi place.  I got a few rolls and the sashimi, and the fact is, it was just ok.  It's definitely a good place to get sushi, if you are in the mood for it while you are with people who don't eat the stuff, or are in the mood for cooked food.  Would I seek this place out for just sushi?  No.  Sun Ray wouldn't even make it into my top 5 for that, but it's not terrible.

Some friends and I checked Oak out for a bite to eat at a place that's a little different.  It wasn't great, but it wasn't terrible either.  First, I definitely have to agree with people who say that this place is loud.  It's really loud, and although they have live music, I don't think that this place was built for that kind of thing.  If you want to see a band here, don't expect to have any kind of conversation.  Also, Oak is really brightly lit and I wish that there were more places to sit.  It was pretty packed and seats were at a premium.  Heads up: if you go here, dress up, because everyone does.  My friends and I were in jeans and we felt a bit out of place.  Not a bad place to start your night, but once it gets packed, it's no fun.

Du Mois was kind enough to host the first Yelp Elite event of 2011.  I had heard about the opening of this gallery, but hadn't had the chance to check it out, before I attended the event.  I was really impressed.    The place itself is small, but nice with three main rooms and a large room in the back.  I was surprised to see some photographs of an old acquaintance of mine on the walls.  I knew she was a photographer, but I had no idea she was so accomplished.  I like that the gallery is brightly lit with a lot of open space.  A great addition to uptown.

I feel like this is one of those places when you want to feel like one of the "special" people.  The place is definitely fancy and the atmosphere fits well into it's Uptown location.  The thing about this place is I never really leave FULL.  You know how other sushi places leave you feeling like you won't have to eat for a week?  This place makes me feel like I'm just "munching".  Maybe I'm not ordering enough or just eating with too large a group.  Ha.  The food is good, but nothing spectacular.  I would call it overpriced, only because you can get the same thing somewhere else for a lot less.  But, as in a lot of these cases, you are paying for not only the food, but the experience.  My boyfriend's friend just started working here, so maybe I will make it back.  I'll be sure to update, if my opinion changes.

I'm always on the hunt for yummy Italian food, especially on the Westbank.  I will definitely be adding DiBlasi's to that list.  When I first walked in, I was struck by the cozy atmosphere.  Sure, it had a bit of an "80's" feel to it, but at the same time it felt quite charming.  The restaurant is HUGE and can definitely cater to large groups with no issues.  Before we ordered, the waiter brought out delicious, warm bread with butter and olive oil.  It was the perfect thing to munch on as we looked over the menu.  For our appetizer, we started with the artichoke and creamy spinach.  It came warm and cheesy with bread to spread it on.  It was fantastic.  For my entree', I got the Fettuccine ala DiBlasi, which was pasta with a cream sauce.  I got the smaller size and it was perfect for me.  It was really good and I really enjoyed it.  The person with whom I was dining got the lasagna.  I was able to try it, and as much as I liked my entree', when I go back I will be getting the lasagna.  It was rich and meaty and perfect.  Our waiter (Tony?) was EXTREMELY attentive and helpful and was really good about getting drink refills and helping with menu suggestions.  My experience here was great and I am really excited to go back, try other menu items and remember to save room for dessert.

This is every mother's dream, especially if you are a mother who is looking to go the "natural" parenting route. No, I'm not a mother, but I stopped in here with a friend who was looking to pick up some things for her future niece or nephew.   Not only will you find baby toys and furniture here, but you will find a vast array of natural products such as baby washes and even cloth diapers. And if you have no idea where to begin with cloth diapers, the staff is expert at it and will tell you everything you need to know from what kind of diapers you need to how many times to change them and how to wash them.  Mom isn't left out, Zuka offers a wide variety of nursing bras, maternity fashion, skin products, breast pumps and nursing pillows. Basically, everything you need to care for your little one before and after he/she has arrived.

Admittedly, I am not what you think of when you think "country", but for the past few years I have been on the hunt for red cowboy (girl) boots. Why? Well, because I think they are pretty cool and an all purpose kind of shoe. And red is just snazzy.   I had looked online, but I hadn't ever had the chance to look for boots in an actual store. I was super excited when I saw that not only did Cavender's have the boots that I sought, but they were priced well! I didn't buy them yet, but I will probably be back to get them after a little more shopping around.  If boots aren't your thing, Cavender's also has a nice selection of "country" inspired clothing and jewelry. A lot of the clothes are overly "stereotypical" of what you think of when you think of Western wear, so don't be afraid to stop in and look around. You might find something that suits you.

Me and the boyfriend were heading to a show at Southport Hall and decided to stop in here for a quick bite to eat.  This is a divey, no frills kind of restaurant- the menu is basically any fried seafood you can imagine. We started simple with some fried pickles and I decided to get the oyster platter which came with fries and a salad.  The pickles were okay. They really went heavy on the batter, but I was happy that the batter actually stayed on the pickles and didn't fall off as soon as I picked them up. The side salad was good, but I REALLY should have asked for the dressing on the side. Good Lord, they must have poured it on with a ladle- there was so much dressing. I need to just stop getting dressing all together, most of the time I don't even like it. I'm gonna be honest- the rest of the food was pretty disappointing.
