The oysters were small, flavorless and way over battered. On top of that, the batter really didn't have any flavor so it was like I was eating fried balls of nothing. The fries were okay, but you aren't going to go here just for the fries.  All in all I was expecting way better from a place that has been around for a while. There are a lot of other places that serve tastier oysters, so do some research before settling with this spot.

I'm kind of on a new mission to try all of the Vietnamese restaurants in the area. That is what brought me to Pho Danh.  First of all, Pho Danh is located right inside the Hong Kong market, so if you are looking for it, that's where it is.  I stopped in around lunchtime and I was surprised that there was no one in here. Seriously. It was me and the staff. The place was completely dead except for that. I'm thinking that maybe they get more of a dinner rush after people have done their grocery shopping after work or something.  Anyway, after looking over the menu, I decided on a small bowl of brisket and tendon pho. It came out quickly and I was excited that there was a lot of meat in it. The broth was okay, but really nothing spectacular. It had a decent flavor, but if I were to compare it to a place like Tan Dinh, there would be no comparison but for what it was, it was okay and got the job done. The price of the small bowl was a tidy $6.50 or so and made for a good lunch.  I wouldn't go out of my way to get Pho here, but if you are looking for a bowl before doing some shopping at the Hong Kong market, then Pho Danh is a viable option.

I want to start this review by saying that I visited this place when we had just come off of a Saints loss in the playoffs. My spirits were down, so when my friend suggested this sushi place, I thought that would be the perfect thing to make me feel better.   We went and were seated immediately, even though it was a Saturday. They have so many yummy sounding things on the menu. Unfortunately, I don't remember exactly what was in the rolls we ordered and the roll descriptions aren't on the online menu, so I'll do my best to relay what we had.  The waitress brought out a complimentary clear soup while we looked over the menu, which is always a nice touch. We decided to order a bunch of special rolls and some sashimi. We got the escalar sashimi, which I had never had before but was really good. We also ordered the lettuce wrap roll. This refreshing roll and zero rice but instead was crab meat with lettuce wrapped around it. It was really good and refreshing. I don't remember what all was in the Niki roll, but I do remember that it was fried with shrimp and then topped with a delicious sauce. It was huge and I loved it. Finally, the Coco roll contained coconut shrimp and cream cheese, which sounds like a weird combo, but was fantastic. Ooh! And as a small bite we got a salmon roe roll that was delicious. It was a lot of food, but fortunately we had brought our appetites and we were able to finish pretty much everything.  I would definitely go back to Taste of Tokyo. I loved everything I had and I am eager to try other menu items.

I am pretty torn about this place. I came for breakfast and got two eggs over easy, grits, bacon and toast. The eggs were VERY under cooked to the point that I couldn't finish them, a few pieces of bacon were pretty much burnt and the grits were...odd. The grits were almost soupy because I think they put too much cream in them or something- I could barely eat them with a fork.  The staff here was nice and I do like the atmosphere of the place. I didn't partake, but they have a "build your own" Bloody Mary bar for Sunday brunch. Maybe this was an off day, so I would probably give them another shot.

Muses is one of the parades that I (and many others) look forward to every year.  The entire crew is made up of women.  They floats are fantastic, huge, and wonderfully lit (since it's a night parade).  I think that my favorite float of theirs is probably their big shoe float.  Shoes are definitely the ongoing "theme" of this crew.  Shoe beads, shoe bracelets, and even custom decorated shoes are just some of their awesome throws.  In past years I have also caught fluffy zebra print spears, scarves,and light up necklaces.  Marchers with the group include the Camel toe lady steppers and the Muff-a-Lottas.  This is a definite "must" on the Uptown parade route.  Catch of the night: decorated shoes.  Anything with a shoe on it (not hard to come by!).

Ugh.  First of all, has anyone ever given a mall a gleaming review?  "I love fighting wayward teens with nothing better to do than wander around a mall on a Wednesday afternoon and angry moms wrangling their screaming brood in order to buy an overpriced pair of Nikes."  These are the same folks who obviously haven't heard of the new fangled thing called the internet and zappos.  But I digress.  Yes, every now and then I find myself with the need to go to the mall.  First of all, Oakwood was once pretty good.  It had some nice restaurants and great stores and kiosks.  Those days are gone.  The stores in this mall are "low budge".  What I mean by that is; little rinky dink no name shoe stores, a weird purse store full of cheap trash (go to Dillard's and get something good), pathetic kiosks dedicated to wigs, "blinged" out chains, cell phone covers and lash (yes, eyelash) decorations.  Oh, and I almost forgot the tooth whitening station and massage "nook", because if I want white teeth and a rub down, I head to Oakwood.  Look, I grew up on Oakwood.  I loved what it was before the storm.  Sure, it was a little "Westbank", but I was a teenager and didn't know any better.  And the Neon Pretzel that they used to have was the BOMB!  I will say this...the saving graces of this mall are the Victoria's Secret (I think I'm gonna review that place separately because I can't make it from entrance to register without being asked if I wear the right size bra at least once), the Cafe du Monde (because I loves my frozen Cafe au Lait), and the Bath and Body works.  All the rest of the stores are geared towards younguns (Forever 21, Charlotte Russe, etc.).    If you MUST go to a mall, go to Lakeside...but have fun parking!  You know what?  Don't even go there.  Just shop online.  Seriously.  Ebay it.  Gently used is better than "mallin" it.

If White Linen is snooty and pretentious, then I would call Dirty Linen it's more fun cousin. The cousin you want to hang out with because she knows all the cool people and all of the cool places to go and she'll sneak you beer before you hit 21.  Dirty Linen is so much better than White Linen. Yes, it's still hot, but it's not nearly as "uppity". Most of the crowd seems a bit younger than White Linen and the whole atmosphere is more laid back and relaxed. The galleries on Royal are fantastic and everyone just goes and has a good time and seems to be in a good mood.

This is a review of a lunch on a weekday.  We stopped in here for lunch after hearing that Rivershack was opening a Westbank location. I enjoy the food at the other Rivershack, so I came here knowing what to expect.  We started with an order of fried pickles and they came with a mustard for dipping. I don't know what it was about them but they really had no flavor. I don't know if the batter wasn't seasoned or what, but they didn't have any "kick", even with the mustard.  For my entree, I decided to keep it simple and get a chicken Caesar salad. It wasn't bad and I enjoyed it and it was big, so I had plenty to take home. The salad wasn't anything overly special, but it was a better alternative to a burger on this particular day.  The venue itself is really big and is perfect for live music. I think that they have bands every weekend. They have a lot of beer on tap and everything is fresh and new. The venue is completely smoke free, so it'll be a nice "fresh air" place to hang out, especially since smoking isn't banned in bars in Jefferson Parish and every other Westbank bar is a smoke pit.

Once I heard that lame Pho Danh had moved out of the Hong Kong Market and a new Pho restaurant had taken it's place, I knew that I had to try it. I had no idea what was even here, so I kind of wandered in blindly.  Walking in, I was a bit nervous. Everything is the exact same as Pho Danh was. I thought for a second that maybe this was just Pho Danh by another name. I sat down and looked over the menu. Everything sounded awesome, but I decided on the P3: Eye round steak and brisket in a large bowl. It came out quickly and fortunately for me, I was starving. I was delighted that they definitely didn't hold back on the meat AT ALL. The bowl was packed. The broth itself had a nice spice on the nose and the meat added a nice flavor to it. For $7.50, I had a really good lunch and enjoyed every bite. All in all it was really delicious and I wasn't disappointed at all.  I found the staff courteous and helpful to the many people that were here for lunch. I will be adding Pho Hu Tieu to my regular rotation of Pho stops.

When a friend was visiting from out of town and said he wanted to eat somewhere nice, the first place that came to mind was Balise. Although new, I had heard nothing but good about this restaurant and I was eager to try it. Lucky for me, he felt the same way.  First of all the restaurant itself is more than meets the eye. They have a main dining room downstairs and then a larger dining room upstairs. There is even a small balcony outside that you can dine on, if the weather is nice.  For our starter, we were feeling a bit adventurous so we started with the venison tartar. It came topped with horseradish and a high recommendation from our waiter. I have never really had anything "tartar" before, so I was excited to try it. It was very interesting. It's served cool with dill mayonnaise. The horseradish added a nice little kick to it and the venison itself had a lot of flavor and wasn't intimidating in the slightest. It was a nice light start to the meal.  For my entree, I decided to get the soft shell crab which came served with a medley of vegetables. Talk about incredible! The crab was very lightly fried and nice and crispy. The portion was huge but somehow I managed to finish it all. I couldn't have been happier with this dish.  A few complaints: the place is pretty loud. They are going to have to figure out a way to buffer that. There weren't a lot of people the room in which we were dining and I could barely hear my own conversation. Also, someone had a screaming one year old, which didn't help matters.   Overall, I really liked it here and I am eager to return.

I have passed this flag shop probably a million times, with it's colorful flags and banners hung outside the building and all over the sidewalk.  I was recently in the market for a garden flag for my front yard, so I decided to start here. Talk about overwhelming!! There are flags, windsocks, windmills and other myriad garden decoration everywhere! There are all along the walls and they are hung from the ceiling. You literally have to weave your way through them all to get to where you're going.  When I finally tracked down the garden flags I was faced with a lot of choices. Every kind of flag that you could possibly imagine of varying size, prices and themes. When I was here I was looking for a pretty simple "every day", non-seasonal flag, but all of the ones I seemed to find were spring/Easter themed. I did find one Obama flag where he looks about 20, so I assume it dates back to '08.   I would have asked for help, but on the day I was here the woman working was on the phone having a fairly loud argument with someone about internet connection, so I thought it best to not bother her. I'll be back, but I will need some guidance next time.

A few weeks ago, around lunch time, I had a hankering for some brunch for lunch. Ruby Slipper had been on my radar for a while, so I decided to head over and treat myself to some eggs 'n stuff.  This was my first time here and the location is just gorgeous. I love the huge space with plenty of natural light- I'm sure it gets packed on Sunday mornings. Looking over the menu, everything sounded amazing. I kept it conservative and got an order of Chicken St. Charles with a side of grits and a side of bacon. I also got iced coffee and hot coffee, just to get my mind right.  The Chicken St. Charles is poached eggs on a piece of fried chicken atop a biscuit. If it sounds like I just described a piece of heaven, you aren't wrong. There's just something special about breaking a poached egg and the yolk drips all over a piece of fried chicken and onto a biscuit. There must be a word for it, but I'm not sure what it is. Let's just go with deliciousity. This deliciousity was off the charts and I had no idea how rich it was going to be- and that's not a complaint.  The side of grits and bacon were a perfect round off to the meal. The grits were delicious and the bacon might be some of the best bacon I've ever had at a sit down restaurant. The iced coffee was okay but, surprisingly, I actually preferred the hot coffee. They serve it in a huge mug and it's just great.  The waitress was really nice and got everything taken care of in record time. I love the vibe here and the food is out of this world, so I'll be back.

This is a great place to see a band.  The place is really big and has great accoustics.  I saw the Molly Ringwalds here about a year ago and had a really great time.  The venue has three separate bars, so you're covered if you need a drink.  The best part is probably the parking lot, so you don't have to worry about street parking.  I would recommend checking the website before going to a show, because depending on who's playing, the cover can be kind of high.

I just stopped in for iced coffee, so this review is going to be short and sweet.  I was in the area and had heard this place was pretty good, so I decided to check it out. To my delight, they have a drive thru BUT it is an extremely sharp turn around the building and a little tight, so be careful if you are driving a big body type of vehicle.  The coffee itself was good. I was happy to see that their version of "large" is actually a really good size. The coffee had a lot of flavor and I enjoyed it.

Now, I rarely eat fast food anymore, but I just had to get over to the new Westbank Arby's as soon as it opened. I feel like in the grand scheme of fast food world, Arby's is one of the better choices. Their classic roast beef only has 360 calories, which isn't terrible for dinner. I've been waiting for years for the Westbank to get an Arby's and the day is finally here.  Anyway, this Arby's used to be a Dairy Queen, so it's pretty small and the lot is tight. There was a pretty long drive through line, so I just went in. Service was fast and I had my classic roast beef in hand in no time. Considering that they only opened last week, service was great and everything went off without a hitch.  I got the sandwich home and I enjoyed it, as I always have, because Arby's classic roast beef is perfection on a bun. Add a little mustard and you're in business. My dad got some fries and I tried a few and they were spicy, curly perfection. I'm still not big on fast food, but I'm glad this place in the area and while it's not going to be the best sandwiches you've ever had, it's satisfies the need for a quick lunch.

Royal Street is to the Quarter what Magazine Street is to the Garden District- you can find it all on Royal Street.  Royal Street is my favorite street in the Quarter for a few reasons: it's not packed with bars like other streets, there are a lot of gorgeous galleries to pop into and take in the lovely art, antique stores don't get any better than on Royal and the street performers and buskers add a certain charm that you would be hard pressed to find anywhere else. There is nothing better than walking down Royal Street on a nice afternoon and taking in the vibe of the city and maybe stopping into some shops along the way to do some browsing.  Royal seems to be in the center of it all, and when you find yourself here you can guarantee that you aren't too far from a good time. If you spend enough time on this street, you will absolutely be able to catch a second line or two.

I'm bumping them down a star. While Muses is still an awesome parade, I think that they could be a little more generous with the throws and, yes, that includes the shoes. I have been going to this parade for years and years and I have never caught a shoe on my own. Shoes not withstanding, I feel that if you are in the middle of the parade route, you just aren't going to get a lot. We were standing with a big group of kids who had trouble getting throws, so it wasn't just because I'm a grown woman. I was pretty pleased with what I did catch this year: my rubber ducky light up pen and the silver block letter Muses necklace are two of my favorites. There were plenty of bands and dance groups, which is always fun and the ladies seemed to be having a good time.  While I think that this parade is still a "don't miss", some improvements can be made as far as consistency goes.

Storyville is such a cool place for locals and tourists alike to go and pick up some really cute New Orleans themed tshirts and favors.  This is the place where I got my infamous "Brad Pitt for Mayor" tshirt that always seems to get a chuckle whenever I wear it.  Storyville is located right across the street from another New Orleans tshirt shop: Fleurty Girl, so between both stores you should be covered for anything you may need.

For my 100th Yelp review for the Yelp 100 challenge, I decided to review Joan of Arc.  I absolutely love this statue. One of the many nods to France in our great city. She sits majestically on her horse on Decatur St.. She has become such a fixture in our city, that it's hard to believe she has only been here since 1959 when Charles de Gaulle came here and presented her to New Orleans on a state visit.   I know it's probably a little hokey, but I like then there is a big Saints game and someone takes the liberty of attaching a Saints flag to her pole.

I stopped in for a quick lunch on a rushed afternoon.  I liked that the green tea I ordered came bottled and not from a mix. I don't really mind the mix I get at other places, but the bottle is always better in my opinion. I got a Godzilla roll (special roll), which came packed with snow crab, salmon, tuna, yellowtail, avocado, asparagus, cucumber and cream cheese and wrapped in green soy paper. It was a huge roll and well worth the $15. I usually don't pay this much for a special roll, but this is the only one on the menu that appealed to me and I really liked it. I also got the two roll special of a tuna roll and a Philly roll. The two roll special came with a pretty basic salad that was okay, but nothing really incredible. The tuna and Philly rolls were good.  Akira is good, but a little more expensive than I'm used to. I can usually get a tuna roll for about $3 and it was $5 here. All of the food was fresh and I enjoyed it.

It's been a long time since I've eaten here. They closed for renovations a while ago and I never returned. That all changed today when my dad and I stopped in here for lunch.  First of all, we came in around 12:15 and the place was slam packed and there was a wait. Every table was full and the staff was hustling. We really hoped that this was a good sign.  We were seated and started looking over the menu. The last time I was here (2011), I had a burger, but the definite emphasis of the menu these days is seafood. They have an oyster bar so you can get raw or char grilled oysters. As tempted as I was to knock out some raw oysters, I decided to go with the pecan crusted catfish that was on the lunch menu. Amanda, the waitress, was wonderful and enthusiastic excitedly telling us that the pecan crusted catfish is one of the best things on the menu.  First came a nice little side salad. It was delicious and I loved that it had spinach in it. I love spinach! When the pecan crusted catfish came out I was blown away. It was hot, right out of the pan and HUGE! This was an incredible piece of fish. The fish was topped with a meuniere sauce and was delicious! The pecans added a delicious flavor to it and overall I really enjoyed it. The dish also came with some new potatoes and a piece of French bread. Needless to say I took about half of my meal home and will be enjoying it later. I should mention that this amazing meal was on $12!  All in all my meal was amazing and I will definitely return. Next time I go I think that I am going to arrive around one, as I noticed that's when the crowd starts to thin.

I had heard raves about this spot, so I was excited to stop in for lunch on a busy Saturday a few weeks ago.  There was a thin crowd in the early afternoon, but I was seated immediately and although I had to wait on someone to take my drink order, that wasn't an issue. I decided to start with the oysters Gentilly and I got shrimp and grits and a side of onion rings, because it's the freakin' weekend and calories don't count on Saturdays.  The oysters Gentily was great! These were lightly fried oysters topped with a yummy sauce and it was a great start to the meal. The shrimp and grits was INSANELY good. This isn't a dish you're going to want if you're on any kind of diet. It's super rich and creamy and the tail-on shrimp are cooked perfectly. I don't know what is in that sauce they put on it (I'm guessing A LOT of butter), but it was addicting. The onion rings were also really good and I liked that they were lightly battered and fried and still retained the onion taste.  I enjoyed my lunch and I had plenty of leftovers, so I was a happy camper  when I left. I will definitely be back for those shrimp and grits.

We've parked here twice while we went to Broussard's and we didn't have an issue either time. The only times we have used this lot have been during the day, so I can't speak to what it's like at night, but in the daylight hours it feels pretty safe. Prices are pretty typical, although maybe not quite as expensive as some of the bigger lots.
Well, I drove up and ordered and they gave me the food in a timely manner. It doesn't get much better than that, right?

I love the peristyle! Not only is it probably one of the most well known landmarks at City Park, but there is always something going on.  Most recently, the peristyle hosted "Swingin' in the Oaks", which featured an orchestra playing all kinds of classic songs. The thing that I like most about the peristyle is the wide open space where you can just go and sit and relax on a nice day. One of my favorite things to do is get an iced coffee from Morning Call, and sit on the steps next to the lion statues and just relax and watch the goings on in the rest of the park.  Weddings and other fancy events are held in the peristyle as well and I have done my fair share of photo shoots in between the gorgeous pillars.

It's hard to find anything negative to say about this historic park and preserve. Okay, maybe one negative thing- during the summer it gets really hot and humid and the bug situation is insane, since you are in a swamp and all.  This park has some great man made trails, so that you can walk through and observe nature from the safety of some slightly raised wood. I wasn't exaggerating when I said that you are completely surrounded by swamp when you're here and although I have never seen a gator myself, I'm sure they are wandering around. Like, I doubt they say to themselves, "Hey, those people are trying to enjoy a nice nature walk, let's not spook them with our little eyes that float just above the water."  You are going to see spiders and other crawlies but you will also see gorgeous plants and flowers and you will hear birds chirping and get to experience the glory of nature first hand. This is a nice quiet place if you want to relax and a great place to spend some time during the cooler months.

Nice, quaint hotel.  Super easy to find and plenty of available street parking is always a plus with me. The rooms itself was nice. It had a nice sleep area with a small attached sitting area. There was a bar right by the door complete with a sink so that you could mix drinks and entertain if you want to stay in the room. I like that the hotel is far enough away from the madness of the French Quarter so that you can still walk around the area and not feel too much like a tourist.  I had a photo shoot here and the photographer mentioned that he got a really good deal on the room through one of those hotel discount sites, so be on the lookout for that kind of thing.

I have been a fan of Dirty Coast for the better part of 10 years or so. I wear their t shirts all the time and I love that they offer New Orleans themed goodies that aren't cheesy.  When I stopped in here I was on a mission: I was looking for pins. They offer the cutest New Orleans pins and I just had to stock up on a few. I got four and they were having a sale, so they came to $30 total. I got a gumbo with french bread, an oyster poboy, a snowball and a bloody Mary. I am SO excited to add these cute pins to my collection. I will definitely be back to get some more to give as Christmas gifts.

Although I didn't buy a mattress set from this place, they are getting 4 stars because of their huge selection and helpful employee.  I stopped in here the day before the 4th of July to check out what sales they had going on. I'm in the market for a new mattress set, and I decided to start my search here. The man working was extremely helpful and friendly and helped me decipher what kind of mattress I wanted, since there are so many choices these days (firm, plush, soft, pillow top, gel foam, etc.).  I won't say that they have the best deals in town, but they did have a lot of mattresses on clearance for around $300 and $400. While they really didn't fit what I was looking for, this would be a good place to start if you are looking for a discounted mattress for a college kid, a first apartment or a guest room.

Believe it or not, I had never set foot in Joey K's until recently, although I feel like I've eaten at every other restaurant on Magazine, at one point or another.  We decided to go right when they opened, in order to beat the lunch rush. I love the decor with a room full of Simon's artwork- it all felt very New Orleans. We started with an order of onion rings and I decided to get the 4 piece chicken meal which apparently comes with two sides.  The onion rings were great! They were battered nicely and the batter actually stays on when you dip them into ketchup. That had a good "bite" to them and they were sturdy and good. The chicken- wow. So, with the four piece order you get two wings and two breasts. I made it through a breast before I was calling for a box, so that I could snack on the rest later. The chicken is juicy, falls off the bone and I like that the batter has a good crunch to it. Green beans is their "given" side and the other side I chose was mashed potatoes. The green beans were tasty and I could tell that the mashed potatoes were homemade. Excellent!  The food here was wonderful and I'm eager to return. If I decide on the fried chicken next time, I might skip the onion rings, just so I have space for more than just a breast!

This is going to be a two tiered review, so strap in.  Tier one: Parking- Hey, what is UNO doing with the money they charge to park in their mud/grass lot? I know what they aren't doing. They aren't putting down concrete, so that I don't have to walk in wet grass and across a shell lot in nice heels.   I was here for the Harry Connick Jr. show, and naturally, I "brought it". When I "bring it", this usually includes a nice dress and high heels. After waiting in an INSANE and poorly directed line to get into the lot, we were instructed to park in damp, muddy grass. The great irony in all of this is the painstaking lengths I go to to avoid muddy grass in my everyday life. I will walk half a mile around something, even if cutting through muddy grass is a short cut. Then I had to walk across this uneven shell lot, that was probably put down in 1983, and has barely been maintained since. I won't even get into having to walk up a windy ramp in heels, because then I'll just sound like a complainer.  Seriously, take some of that $10 per car y'all charge to park and lay down some cement. The high heels of the world will thank you.  Tier two: The show itself- After we got in and found our seats, the show was really good. I was impressed with the entire space, the sound quality was great and, although the seating area was a bit cramped, it was tolerable for a few hours. I had a good view of the stage from my seat and we had a good time. The only misstep I could find was when Harry gave a shout out to his 92 year old father in the audience, and the spotlight guy couldn't find him, even though he was standing and waving. Jeesh.  I know that UNO Lakefront Arena is mainly a setting for sports and graduations, and I'm not completely sure I'd attend a concert here again. If I do, I'm getting there stupid early so that I don't have to teeter across shells in heels.

This is pretty much the perfect gift shop for the "girly girl" in your life.  Not only does this shop have adorable clothing, but they have gifts that are perfect for a new bride (they have a cat themed glass that says "I'm getting Meowied"), anyone graduating, or pretty much anyone who likes wine. Their "I don't give a sip" glasses are pretty cute. I love the dainty jewelry they have here and I can never come here without buying at least one bracelet.  On my last trip in, I got myself a necklace, a bracelet and a cute top because they happened to be having an end of season sale. The better sale items are always on the back wall and the ladies working are always helpful in finding whatever you may be looking for. While this store isn't quite as big as the one at Oakwood, it's packed with a lot of good stuff.

This is a review of their king cake.  I'm always on the hunt for really good king cake. I'm not a huge king cake connoisseur, but I know what I like: traditional, "plain" with a nice icing/sugar combo.  I had heard the king cake here at Coffee & was good, so I picked one up. First of all, the cake here is HUGE and costs $15- well worth the money in my opinion. It was nice and soft and had that nice cinnamon taste that I enjoy in a king cake. The icing/sugar combo was perfect and overall I enjoyed it and would purchase another one.  In addition to king cake, this diner has traditional donuts and diner food, including $6 shrimp and grits. I'm tempted to try it, but I'm also scared. I think I'll just stick to the king cake.

Bacchus is one of my favorite parades. This Super Krewe is made up of huge, gorgeous floats and is always generous with the throws. I usually like to catch it on St. Charles Avenue, because I can't be bothered with barricades on the downtown part of the route.

Hey kids!  Do you want your teeth vibrated out of your head by music that is super loud?  Do you want to dance in near darkness with sweaty strangers on drugs to repetitive, pulsating beats?  Do you want to over pay for a weak vodka drink?  Do you want to be hit on by a 50-something year old man who is just too cool to stay out of the club on a Saturday night (he is SO HIP!)?  Do you just have nothing else to do come 4 in the morning and you want to make one more bad decision?  Then Ampersand or "Amps" is the place for you!  Ugh.  Seriously.  It's New Orleans.  Why are you in a horrible nightclub that wishes it was in Las Vegas?  Go see some jazz, for goodness sake.  I haven't been here in over two years.  I will never go back.  You can't make me.

Mardi Gras fountain is a landmark that I didn't even know was check in-able! I think it was built to honor all of New Orleans' Mardi Gras krewes. It really is a gorgeous landmark, now that it's been redone, albeit a bit out of the way.

David and I were having a seafood craving and I had been wanting to try this place, so off we went.  We were here on a Saturday night for dinner and the crowd was decent and we were seated immediately. It's an older crowd- I think we were the youngest people in the place by at least 20 years, but that's not an issue at all. I had already glanced at the menu before we came and I knew exactly what I wanted- the catfish with grits topped with crawfish etouffee.  We started with an order of onion rings, since we both love onion rings and we are always on the hunt for really good ones. The rings here were okay. I liked that they were thin cut and lightly battered and fried. My only complaint was there was no salt on them, but that's easy enough to fix and I get that not everyone might like onion rings coated in salt.  By the time my catfish came out I was ready for it- it looked beautiful and the picture I took doesn't do it justice at all. This was a HUGE piece of thick catfish topped with etouffee on a generous bed of grits. The catfish was fried to perfection and very tasty, the etouffee was out of this world, but the star of the show was the grits. The Creole tomato and smoked gouda grits complimented the fish perfectly and added pizzazz to the entire meal. I could have had more grits. Always more grits. The dish also came with a side of vegetables that were good, but forgettable.  Service here was great and the waitress was good about checking on us and refilling our drinks in a timely manner. This is definitely going on the list of place we love and we will be back.

This spot just opened, so I was jazzed to find myself in the area around lunch.  Those of you might remember when O'Henry's was in this location, so it's nice that another good lunch spot has moved in here. We sat upstairs and the place wasn't packed at all around noon.They have a little bit of everything here including sandwiches (which you can also get as a wrap) and a nice selection of entrees.  We started with the calamari and I got the grilled chicken sandwich with no ranch. All sandwiches come with fries. The calamari was great! It was lightly battered and nice and crispy. When my sandwich came out, I was disappointed that my chicken was fried instead of grilled. They've only been open a week, so I wasn't going to make an issue over it and the sandwich looked good, so I rolled with it. It turned out to be a happy mistake because the fried chicken was great! It was super flavorful and juicy in the middle. After tasting it, I didn't even mind that they messed up my order a little.  I'm not sure of our waiter's name, but he was really nice and attentive and made sure that we had everything we needed and kept our drinks refilled. I loved eating on the balcony and I hope that they plan on adding some fans once we are in the dog days of summer. It's nice to have a spot like this back on Carrollton and I'd return for lunch.

I'm going to start off with a really basic assessment: World of Beer is great for those of you who live in Metairie, want some decent beer and maybe have yet to discover Lager's.  Maybe I went at the wrong time. I went on a Saturday night and there was the usual crowd of people in there who were looking for a party. My friend and I sat at the bar and looked over the menu. Nothing really jumped out at me and everything you can find here you can find at Avenue Pub.  The vibe here is just weird. It's a beer bar and we were sitting at the bar and the bartender was non stop with making mixed drinks. Who comes to a beer bar and gets mixed drinks? And then there was a singer there that just felt unnecessary, out of place and odd.  If you want food they have such faire as the "beer pretzel". God only knows what that is. I'm sure it's a pretzel with a beer sauce or something.  There are way better places for beer all over the city. I won't be returning to WoB.

This place isn't as terrible as some other clubs (*cough* Amps *cough*), but it's still not really my scene. It is a big space with three different bars downstairs and the staff does seem to do pretty well in handling a big crowd. The music is horrible and way too loud. Yeah, I know, it's a nightclub. I guess I'm old. Whatever. When my teeth are vibrating in my head, I'm not having fun.  They have different theme parties that they go all out for. I haven't been to one in years, but I remember them being a pretty good time.

This is a review of a special event in the Penthouse Ballroom.  What can I say? Windsor Court seriously knows what they are doing when they host a special event. I recently attended the Southern Rep Gala here and I was blown away by everything. When I first walked in, there was a main room where everyone could mingle while drinking their drinks and enjoying the yummy appetizers that were being passed around by the professional staff. I think my favorite part of this first area was the patio and the balcony. It was a lovely evening, and you had a great view of the river and the bridge. There was plenty of seating on the patio area so that you could sit and talk and enjoy the sunset. It really felt as if I was at someone's home.  After cocktail hour, we were lead into the main ballroom. At our assigned table we were served an amazing salad that seemed to have a house made dressing. For our entree' we enjoyed a filet that was cooked to perfection, served with asparagus and mashed potatoes. This steak was so perfectly cooked that I was able to cut it with a butter knife. Everyone at our table raved about how fantastic it was. Dessert was a delicious slice of cheesecake that came with a side of strawberries. The entire meal was out of this world and easily one of the best I have had this year.  The entire evening came off without a hitch. We were able to watch the scheduled performances as we ate and everything began and ended exactly when it was supposed to. Everything flowed beautifully.  If it is within your means, I highly suggest the Windsor Court Ballroom for any event. Whatever it costs, it is worth it for the memory you and your guests will enjoy for days after the event has ended.

I have always been a fan of this little corner on Maple. I used to eat here when it was Vera Cruz! So, when I heard that the nasty bar that had replaced Vera Cruz was closing and a fancy sushi place was opening here, I was excited. I'm a pretty big sushi fan and I'm always open to trying new places.  We stopped in here on a Saturday night around 8 or so. There was a nice crowd and we were seated immediately. Upon our Yelp check in, we got a free decanter (small) of sake each (one for each of our check ins). The waitress was super nice about it and she was super helpful.  The atmosphere of Kakkoii is really nice. It's kind of dark, but really cozy. They did a great job decorating the place with an modern Asian kind of feel.  We decided on the salmon sashimi, the LSU roll and the Hawaii 5-0 roll. Both rolls were really good and the Hawaii 5-0 roll was especially unique because it had mango around it. Normally I am weary of the fruit/rice/fish combo, but it seemed to work and I really liked it. The only real complaint I had was that the rolls could have been a smidge bigger for the price.  I would definitely go back and work my way down the roll menu. Ha.

I think I may have new favorite Quarter bar!  This is a really cozy spot, I love the atmosphere and the whole place just feels "old New Orleans/Europe" to me. On the night we were here we sat at the bar and had some champagne. The vibe here is very laid back and relaxed, and on this particular night, it was a thin crowd and Patrick was walking around talking to customers and having a good time.  There's an outside patio area that I am eager to check out when the weather gets a little cooler. The best part about the place is that it's close to Bourbon for those who want to be near the "action", but not in it, but it has yet to be over run with obnoxious tourists (I love tourists, but not the ones who only come to New Orleans to get wasted).  I can't wait to go back.

I have passed this place probably a hundred times and I finally decided to get some dinner here.  Walking in, you feel as if you are walking into a friend's house. The atmosphere is very welcoming, I like the dimmer lights and it's an overall cozy and welcoming feel. We were seated in the back, which made me happy because that meant we were away from the main crowd of the restaurant.  Rebecca was our waitress and she was really friendly and told us the specials as we looked over the menu. I decided to start with the Gulf oysters, which is kind of salad served with oysters, fennel, spinach and croutons. It was a delicious and refreshing start to the meal.  For my entree, I got their version of shrimp and grits which was tail-on shrimp in lemon, basil & garlic beurre blanc with goat cheese grits, roasted mirliton wrapped in prosciutto. Talk about delicious! The goat cheese grits were a little "muskier" than what I am normally used to, but the mirliton balanced it out nicely. I have to say that "wrapped in prosciutto" is a little misleading, only because in the version that I had there was the mirliton with the prosciutto on the side. I had no complaints, and you can easily "wrap" it yourself if that's what you would prefer. I really like the way this entire dish came together.  Finally, for desert, I had the house made chocolate ice cream which was a special of the evening. I enjoyed it with coffee and it was as delicious as chocolate ice cream usually is and it made for a nice end to the experience.  I loved Bistro Daisy and I will have to return and try more of what they have to offer, although it will be difficult not getting the shrimp and grits again.

I've been sitting on this review for a while, mainly because I'm not sure how I feel about Mimi's and my experiences here have varied so much, that I feel as if I can't form a solid opinion.  What I do know: I really like the downstairs and the people that frequent this place are really cool.  It's pretty much a neighborhood bar, so a lot of people here live just a few blocks away and call this their "go to" joint.  What I'm on the fence about: upstairs and the food.  I really like that the upstairs area has the "DJ Soul Sister dance party" thing every Saturday. What I'm not crazy about is how packed the upstairs gets and along with that, how hot it gets.  Also, the people who frequent the upstairs tend to be a lot more drunk and when they are dancing don't care who and what they bump into, as long as they are having a good time.  Jeez...that last sentence made me sound like a grandmother, but it's true!  I've only had the food here once.  A friend of mine ordered the "lamb pops" and they weren't too bad.  I know... lamb in a bar.  Trust me; I wouldn't have "gone there" had my friend not ordered something for me to try, but I was pleasantly surprised.  So yeah, like I said I'm middle of the road when it comes to Mimi's.  I'd probably go back and stay downstairs where the people seem a lot more laid back and not so much  "on a mission" to get wasted and slam dance.

Three cheers for Gator 1! We got to ride this around town for the Brews Cruise and our lovely CM Morgan gave us special permission to review this one of a kind party transport system.  As others have described, the Gator 1 is a party bus that has been magically transformed from a fire truck. If that's not cool enough, you are in a covered but open vehicle where you are standing (and holding onto the safety bar) as you are driven from spot to spot (complete with sirens and honking).   Don (the captain of Gator 1) was awesome and kept the tunes pumping and he helped us maneuver getting in and out of the truck safely. This is probably the most fun party bus type thing that I have ever been on. Don is a very safe driver and drives slowly so that everyone is safe on the ride.  I had such a great time and I wouldn't hesitate to hire Don and Gator 1 for any type of party or bar crawl.

As much as I like the Blue Dog, I feel like I don't have a love affair with that mutt that some people do.  I stopped in here to look around at other pieces of Rodrigue's work. Other than Blue Dog, Rodrigue painted quite the collection of tombs. Yes, the above ground tombs that New Orleans is known for- Rodrigue apparently painted quite a few of them and I found these pieces just lovely. I feel like they tell a story with which we can all identify. Of course, some of the tomb paintings do have that sneaky dog in them, but the ones in the swamps with trees covered in moss are the ones I like the most.  The woman working in the gallery on the day that we stopped in gave us a bit of history of the Blue Dog, as well as a few of Rodrigue's other works. Of course, all of the art here is a bit hefty in price, so owning one is probably a dream that will never be realized (for myself). Still, it was nice to stop in and look around.    At the gallery, you can buy a book that features many of Rodrigue's work, so that makes a good souvenir just in case the art is a bit out of your price range.

This is a review of the bar only.  We stopped in here for some post-event cocktails and I immediately loved the laid back vibe of the place; it was really cozy and hip. The bartenders were really sweet and I was impressed with Revel's beer selection.   I'm always looking for nice bars that cater to the "chat and drink" crowd more than the "party" crowd and Revel definitely fits the bill. They seem to have quite the selection of cocktails that I will have to try the next time I'm in the area.

I want to go back! I want a do over! I want to get queso!  We came here for taco Tuesday- you really can't beat $1 per taco, even if they are pretty small. Even though it was nicely packed, we were seated quickly and I started with a medium frozen margarita as I looked over the menu. I already knew I was getting tacos and I was debating on whether or not to get queso, but I decided against it because I figured the $5 price was too much for what you would get.  The margarita came and it was okay. It tasted more like a margarita daiquiri and it was neon green which just screamed, "this is from a mix!" Oh well. I got 4 tacos- two of the barbacoa and two of the al pastor. The barbacoa was okay, but I did find it a little dry. The al pastor was PERFECT- full of flavor and delicious!. When I go back, I am going all al pastor. I wasn't sure if 4 small tacos would be enough, but they filled me up perfectly. My friend got the fajitas which looked and smelled amazing.  Now for my one regret: we were getting our check when the waitress brought the table next to us a HUGE piping hot bowl of queso. Wait, what? Is that really the queso? That's why it's $5, because it comes in a HUGE bowl?! So much regret. So much want. So much going back to maybe just get queso and chips and call it a day (don't judge me).  This place is pretty awesome. They have everything you could want and expect from a Tex-Mex style place and they even have burgers and other sandwiches, if you are dining with someone who isn't in the mood for Mexican. I am definitely going back.

5 years later and I just bought a mattress from here, so I'm re-reviewing!  I actually bought the mattress a few months ago, but I wanted time to "break it in" to make sure I liked it. I ended up getting a nice new Sealy at a fair price. My advice: always wait for sales to purchase a mattress- they happen multiple times a year and you will save a ton.  Anyway, the staff was very helpful when I stopped in to look at mattresses and I ended up finding a foam mattress that I love! It's been a few months and I have no complaints. The delivery folks took my old mattress when they delivered the new one, so the process couldn't have been any easier.

Kind of a weird way to describe it, but I would almost label this place "Vietnamese fast food".  It's a small place located right inside the Hong Kong market. There's a counter where you can order and a couple of tables and chairs.  I stopped in because I heard through the grape vine that they have an avocado smoothie here and avocado smoothies are my new obsession. Went right in and ordered. I like that you have the option of getting your drink without the tapioca balls (my choice). The smoothie was a really good size for $4.75 and full of flavor. You could tell that it was really fresh. Pro tip: I noticed that as the drink warmed to room temperature the avocado taste was a lot more rich, so don't be so quick to gulp it all down in the first few minutes.  They also serve small banh mi sandwiches, which are a steal at $3 each. That's why I labeled it "fast food", because you can get a quick little bite for cheap.  I'll definitely be back and I'll probably get some sandwiches when I return.

This is a lovely photo gallery located right in the heart of Jackson Square.  The work of Louis Sahuc is featured throughout the gallery, Louis has been a photographer since 1972, and here you can buy originals and prints of his work in all sizes. His lovely art varies from pictures of New Orleans during a hard rainstorm, to St. Louis Cathedral in the fog and the people of New Orleans.  What I like about Louis Sahuc's work is that it isn't typical New Orleans photography. Yes, there are pictures of the architecture of the city, but his work seems to contain more heart than some of the other work I've seen. I feel like his pictures are meant not only to appeal to tourists, but to find homes with locals as well.  If you are in the area, be sure to stop in and check it out.

Crazy good!  We stopped in here for dinner one night and even though it was a Friday, it wasn't crowded at all. I had never been here before, but I knew what I was in the mood for so ordering was a breeze. I started with a frozen margarita with salt and chips and queso. The margarita was perfect, and although it was probably from a mix, I liked it. The chips and queso were a perfect start- the chips were nice and thin and not too salty.  For my entree I got the pork burrito and I got an order of rice and beans on the side. This burrito was HUGE! I loved that it was topped with sour cream and taco sauce and it was jam packed with huge pieces of pork, rice, beans, sour cream, cheese and guacamole. This would have been easily split between two people. The rice and beans were okay, but I found the rice to be a bit dry.  Service was spot on our waitress didn't leave us waiting for the check or the box. I will return.

I'm always on the hunt for really good lunch places, here on the Westbank, and my search recently brought me to this locally owned restaurant.  Walking in, I love the feel of the place. The space is very big with a lot of room for big parties. There are TVs on the walls, so you aren't going to miss the big game if you decide to stop in for lunch or dinner. The menu is eclectic, with a heavy leaning towards seafood and pasta.   When I was here for lunch, I took the opportunity to try their version of shrimp and grits. For only $9 I knew that I couldn't go wrong, and I'm always looking for tasty shrimp and grits on the Westbank. Fire Food and Spirits' version of this classic Southern dish didn't disappoint at all. I was thrilled at the large serving for the price and it was seasoned perfectly. The tail-on shrimp were large and the grits were creamy and perfect and were served topped with a delectable, spicy sauce that added just enough kick, without being overpowering.  I definitely get the feeling that Fire Food and Spirits is built for a celebration. Whether you're watching sports with some friends over a few appetizers or celebrating a birthday, graduation, or other special occasion, Fire Food and Spirits will give you a dining experience that you won't soon forget.  I've heard their wings are a must try, so I'm going to come back and try them soon.

I want to start by saying the salesman was great and I have zero issues with him.  I stopped in here while getting some prices for a new mattress. Believe it or not, it's been 5 years since I bought a new mattress and it was already sagging, but that's another story. I found a mattress that I really liked at another store, so I was shopping around trying to find the best price. Well, first of all, spoiler alert- Mattress Direct has some of the highest prices I encountered, despite their catchy, "The best rest for less" slogan. Also, the mattress I was interested in was the only one that didn't have a box spring and was basically sitting on the machinery that was used to move it into the store, so if this had been my first stop, I wouldn't have even bothered trying the mattress I really wanted.  The salesman did his best to explain pricing and everything, but at the end of the day, it was "no" from me. There are better prices out there, so shop around before you buy from here.

If you're looking for a cute spot for a reasonably priced dessert, look no further than The Cupcake Collection. Here you will find the sweetest treats at the best prices. Flavors like chocolate, vanilla, strawberry, and they're famed sweet potato are must try.   Everyone who works here is always so sweet and welcoming and the cupcakes are simple, but delicious. They are still taking covid precautions, so for best service, I would suggest ordering your cupcakes ahead of time on their website. But, if you just drop in, they'll take care of you.  I wrote about the history of this spot for Big Easy Magazine. Check it out here: https://www.bigeasymagazine.com/2021/06/23/1new-orleans-native-mignon-francois-discusses-the-origin-of-the-cupcake-collective-and-how-she-built-the-wildly-successful-empire-from-scratch/

Why review a tunnel?  The same reason you climb Mt. Everest: because it's there.  There aren't a lot of reasons to travel to the Westbank.  Not that the Harvey Tunnel is a reason, I was just saying.  It is definitely a faster route than the expressway and if you want you can hold your breath when you go in and see if you can hold it the entire time until you drive out of it.  Only do that if you are a passenger, though.  I don't know what your breath holding capacity is and I don't want to be blamed for someone passing out and wrecking their car.  Umm... I guess that's about it.  Oh yeah, I kinda wanna see this tunnel and the Belle Chasse tunnel fight it out for "official tunnel of the Metro New Orleans" area.

I just had one of the best burritos ever and I had to share!  So, El Patron has really taken off since my last review. Whenever I pass this spot around dinner time it's packed. I know what you're thinking: it's because of that lovely view of Lapalco you get when you sit on the patio outside. While that may be true, I truly think that El Patron has some of the best food around.  I was here for lunch today and I was in a burrito mood. I decided to get their El Burrito Mexicano, which comes with your choice of chicken or beef with rice, onions, corn and other goodies inside. Then, it's topped with cheese and ranchero sauce, all for $12.   When the burrito was delivered to me, not only was it HUGE (it took up the entire plate!), but it was packed with properly grilled and sliced chicken. This was not shredded chicken like you will find at so many places. This is BIG CHUNKS of chicken that you can see. And the chicken/filling ratio is perfect. Sometimes you get burritos that are more filling than meat, but that wasn't the case here. This was plenty big enough for me to split into two meals. The only equivalent that I've been able to find elsewhere is at Juan's and it's $14 if you get it "wet" and not as big. My new favorite burrito is right here on the Westbank. This is like discovering oil in my backyard.  I will be making this place a bi-monthly stop, for sure.

I had been trying to decide what review #2200 would be and I had a spot in mind, but decided that it should be Ruby Slipper instead.  This is the last place I dined before the "stay at home" order from the mayor due to the covid-19 panic. We were already on edge when we ate here, but the bartender was AMAZING. He was funny and light-hearted and kept us laughing throughout our visit. He really took our minds of our worries, all while sanitizing everything and handling multiple customers at once with kindness. I'm kicking myself for not getting his name, but he had brown hair and a beard. He was wonderful.  For my meal I got my regular- Chicken St. Charles, which is a fried chicken Benedict on top of a biscuit. I also got a side of grits and bacon. It was all delicious and, considering the circumstances, it was perfectly cooked and served with a smile.  This experience is one of the reasons I love Ruby Slipper and I'll always return. They really make you feel like family. Please give that bartender a raise- he went above and beyond.

Water ice is a tasty dessert that's big in the east, especially in Philadelphia. The finely granulated concoction is blended with flavor throughout and scoops and eats like ice cream. It melts slowly and makes for the perfect treat on a hot day.   There are 20 flavors to try including blueberry, lemon, strawberry lemonade, cotton candy and cherry.  I tried the cherry flavor and, as someone who had never had anything like this before, I was immediately hooked. It's so much different than a New Orleans snowball. The flavor is evenly blended throughout the dessert and the taste is refreshing- I was a fan after my first bite. I like that it doesn't melt quickly and get all soupy, like some other ice desserts.  If you want something other than dessert, Tapeh's provides lunch items such as chicken and waffles, sandwiches, nachos, fries and Philly cheesesteak.  I wrote about this spot for Very Local New Orleans, read the whole article here: https://nola.verylocal.com/tapehs-water-ice-brings-a-tasty-east-coast-treat-to-algiers/161674/

Let me start off with a few positives. I LOVE the fact that 5 Guys is giving the Westbank a shot- none of these burger places ever open a restaurant in my neck of the woods. Ordering online is super convenient; I was able to order and pay on the site and pick it up at the store with no problem. They let you put a ton of stuff on your burger and the staff is working fast to get everyone's orders out in a timely manner.  I ordered the cheeseburger and I topped it with a ton of stuff: lettuce, tomatoes, pickles, grilled onions, mustard and ketchup. The cheeseburger is a double patty and they are extremely generous with the toppings (there were two thick slices of tomato on my burger and I was pretty pleased). Burgers are cooked well done and are substantial- I ate half of mine and I was full. The taste was okay- better than a place like Burger King, but don't compare it to a place like Company Burger.  I also got an order of "little" cajun fries, which was a super generous portion, and more than I could get through. I did, however, have a few complaints: the fries were SUPER spicy. I like spicy food, but the spice was overwhelming to the point that I couldn't even taste the fry itself. Also, the fries were a bit soggy. I'm not sure if this is because I got a "to go" order and they sat in the bag on the drive home, but they were a little softer than I like.  I'm giving three stars with some room for improvement. The food is a little pricier than your average fast food place, but I think it's worth the money considering what you get. When I go back I will probably get the "little" cheeseburger and the un-spiced fries just to compare.  Allergy note: peanuts are served in bulk and are everywhere, and fries are fried in peanut oil.

Walking into the unassuming building that houses the Backstreet Cultural Museum, you can immediately tell that you're in a place of importance. From the moment you enter, photographs and memorabilia adorn the walls, telling stories about New Orleans culture that, while acknowledged, is rarely appreciated by those on the outside looking in.  The mission of the museum is to preserve and perpetuate the unique cultures and traditions of the New Orleans African American society through collections, publications, exhibitions, programs and performances. The museum recognizes that the preservation of culture is a part of community development and presenting these exhibitions is a way of strengthening traditions and enhancing economic prosperity in the community.  In addition to the permanent collection, the Backstreet Cultural Museum regularly provides exhibitions at the New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival and Essence Festival. Pieces of collections from the museum have also been featured at the Ogden Museum as well as the New Orleans Museum of Art.  For $10, Mr. Francis, or his daughter Dominique, will take you on a guided tour throughout the museum and give you a history of the collection and the groups represented here. Every corner of the building is packed with memorabilia and history.  The Backstreet Cultural Museum is a must-visit for any local who is interested in learning more about African American club culture and what makes Mardi Gras traditions so special. It's thanks to Mr. Francis' hard work that these treasures are preserved for generations to come.  *Portions of this review was originally written, by me, for Very Local New Orleans. Read the full story here: https://nola.verylocal.com/know-your-nola-backstreet-cultural-museums-collection-highlights-black-new-orleans-traditions/157174/

Whenever David and I have something special to celebrate, we like to pick someplace special. It was David's birthday, so I knew that we had to make the dinner count. David loves a good steak and Mr. John's had been on my list for a while, so I made reservations for a celebratory dinner.  We were here on a Saturday night and the place was rightfully packed with people having a great time. We were seated immediately and given menus. Boris was our waiter and he was incredible. Not only was he full of personality, but he had suggestions on what we should try and what he thought we would like. Before we had a chance to order, out came some complimentary meatballs. They were delicious and I was happy that David got an extra one (with a candle in it) for his birthday.  I already had an idea of what I wanted and I had my eye on the filet. I got mine medium-rare and I got Freddie mac and cheese on the side. You might be wondering what Freddie mac and cheese is. It's mac and cheese with crawfish and andouille sausage mixed in. David got a New York strip and a baked potato.  My steak came out cooked perfectly. It was still pink on the inside and nice and juicy, which is just how I like it. The Freddie mac and cheese is to die for. I don't know who in their right mind would get the regular mac and cheese when you can get mac and cheese with freakin' sausage in it! David loved his steak and said that the baked potato is one of the best he has ever had.   When it was time for dessert, I didn't even have to say anything. I had mentioned in my reservation that we were celebrating a birthday and out came a complimentary tiramisu with a candle in it. Perfect! I LOVE when restaurants go the extra mile to make the customer feel special. The dessert was tasty and perfect and an excellent way to end the meal.  A few points: 1) The place is loud. There was a huge party behind us and David and I could barely hear each other talk. If we go back, I think we might go on a weekday when it's a little calmer. 2) The restaurant is dark, so if you struggle with that, you might want to go when it's a little brighter outside.  Neither of these "issues" warrant knocking the restaurant down a star, but I wanted to mention them.  Boris was wonderful and always made sure that my wine glass stayed full and that everything was prepared to our satisfaction. We loved Mr. John's and we both think that this was one of the best steaks that we have ever had. We are already talking about going back next time we have a craving for something a little more high-end.

I hadn't eaten in over 12 hours and I was starving when the photographer I had just worked with suggested this spot. Ooh, I had heard all about it and I had been looking for an excuse to go- nearly starved to death is as good of a reason as any.  The place is pretty basic: you go up to a counter and order off of a board. There's some seating inside, but it was a nice day so we sat on one of the tables outside. I got The Delicate Lady, which is a chicken salad sandwich with blueberry bbq sauce and the boudin egg rolls and potato salad to share. I also got iced tea, which came with no straw, because that's how these places roll these days. Remind me to get a reusable straw because I hate when ice touches my teeth.   ANYWAY, The Delicate Lady came out and it was gorgeous. Chicken piled up topped with delicious sauce and finished off with lettuce for a good crunch. I liked that the chicken salad wasn't super heavy on the mayo and instead relied on the chicken itself to really bring the flavor. The blueberry sauce was a nice touch and added a sweetness to the sandwich.  The boudin egg rolls were crazy good. I had heard that these are a "must" and that's accurate. It's boudin in a typical egg roll wrap and there's cheese in there too! It's probably not any kind of healthy, but oh man is it good. The potato salad was solid as well. I thought it was a lot like German potato salad, which is made with vinegar. It was super tasty and it all balanced well.  While we were eating, one of the owners came out and asked how we liked everything. I thought that was nice because, you know, she didn't have to do that. I like when the owner or manager checks in with customers. Everything was great and I'm definitely going to be back.

Grit's isn't as bad as it's next door neighbor, F&M's. The crowd tends to be a little bit older and the music is more tolerable.  I stopped in on a week night for drinks with a few friends and I realized that it's actually a decent establishment. The drinks are well priced and the bar is a "hang out" for friendly neighborhood folks who are happy to make conversation. I remember this place before the smoking ban, and I can only imagine that the ban worked in Grit's favor. The bartender was friendly and was happy to make small talk and I would return on another week night.

Really big PJ's and open pretty late (we stopped in around 9 after we had sushi next door), so that's pretty cool.  Lot's of tables and free WiFi for anyone who wants to do some work. Definitely one of the "sit and stay" PJ's, rather than a "order and go" store. The iced coffee I ordered was really good and priced the same as other PJ's.  I'll be back when I find myself in the area.

I live pretty close to the Westbank Pho Bang, so I have been a fan for years. I think Pho Bang is some of the best pho in the city and, while other people like to worship at the altar of Tan Dinh, I regularly go to Pho Bang for my #14 large and spring rolls.  I was out in Metairie, around lunch, when I saw that a Pho Bang had opened on Vets. Now, that every location is owned by a member of the same family, so the menu is pretty much the same.  I stopped in here and ordered my large pho tai gau (eye-round steak, flank, and brisket), egg rolls and spring rolls.  As expected, my pho tai gau was as good as ever. There's just something about the pho here that's just amazing- it's a real cure all. If you feel sick, this stuff will cure you. The egg rolls were crunchy perfection and the pork spring rolls were excellent.  The service here is always fast, so it's perfect for lunch and this location has a little bit of an edge on my regular pho bang, because this one has banh mih.   This is a great spot for lunch or dinner- you won't be disappointed.

The food here is a reflection on what you would find in any Colombian kitchen; the servings are large and the dishes don't hold back on the flavor. The experience feels as if you are eating in a friend's home rather than a restaurant.  Some of the menu's specialties are Empandas ($2.50), a traditional corn patty filled with beef or chicken; Bandeja Paisa ($22), white rice, red beans, grilled steak, pork belly fried egg, avocado, sweet plantain, Colombian chorizo and arepa; Patacón Gloria ($18-$22), fried green plantain with lettuce and cheese with choice of pork, steak and chicken, or shrimp; and Pescado Frito ($25), a grilled stuffed fish served with rice, vegetables, fried green plantains and salad.  Everything was fantastic and the owners are so nice. They now have outdoor seating which is perfect for nice days.  I wrote about this spot for Uptown Messenger. Check it out here: https://uptownmessenger.com/2021/05/golden-gate-bistro/

On the day I was here it was pouring rain, which normally wouldn't be an issue but there is VERY limited parking at this location, so I actually had to park across the street and trudge through puddles to get here. Hey, I had a craving for fried chicken and I was willing to do anything necessary to satisfy it.  This place is pretty basic: order at the counter, get your number and they'll bring you your food. I was lucky that I beat the lunch crowd (seriously, the line was out the door about 5 minutes after I ordered) and I was able to order at the counter immediately upon walking in. I got a two piece white meat fried chicken with the veggie of the day (creole corn) and fries. I also got a lemon meringue pie to go because I earned it.  Considering there weren't very many people here when I ordered, there was a good 20-25 minute wait, but I guess you can't complain when the food is cooked to order. Now, I'm gonna be honest. When the food came out I was a little underwhelmed. The wing they gave me was super small and the breast didn't have as much meat on it was I would have liked. With that said, the chicken was really good, crispy and juicy. Is it the best fried chicken I've ever had in my life? No, but it satisfied my fried chicken craving and I enjoyed the meal. The fries were good and the creole corn was basically corn with some Tony's in it, but I don't have any complaints about that.  Later that evening I had my lemon meringue pie and I think it might be some of the best lemon meringue pie I've ever had in my life. It was really sweet and light and made for a perfect late night dessert.  While Fiorella's wouldn't be my first stop for fried chicken, I would come back simply to try other menu items and for the friendly, family atmosphere. I wouldn't come on a rainy day, though.

Yep. Considering David and I stop in here once a month and it's one of our favorite places to grab a bite to eat, I figured it was time for a re-review.  This place is the best, y'all- on so many levels. First of all: they have the best burger in town. I'm not lying. I have tried burgers elsewhere and nothing can compare to Company Burger. I don't know what it is- maybe it's the bread, maybe it's the meat, maybe it's the speed in which they deliver it to my table, but it's pretty perfect. I have never been disappointed by my single with cheese- not even once.  And then there's the onion rings. Forget the fries and the tater tots- onion rings is where it's at. Purple onions sliced and fried to a golden brown. And they always give you a lot- the little baggie they come in is always overflowing with oniony goodness. I like to get the chipotle mayo from the mayo bar and put the stuff on my burger AND dip my onion rings in it. Yep, I'm not ashamed. Add a draft beer to the order and you have pretty much the perfect meal. They consistently have great beers on draft and, if that isn't your thing, treat yourself to a milkshake or cold drink.   The Company Burger has become my happy place and I am always so excited when we have plans to eat here- kind of like how a dog gets excited to go to the dog park. I can't wait to go back over and over again.

We wandered into Brick Oven, one night, after Gendusa's was packed. This was right after the election, so I assume people were just happy to be out of the house and eating cheap.  We got here and the place was pretty dead and we were seated quickly.  For our appetizer we got cheese bread and for my entree I got shrimp and crawfish pasta and I got a meatball on top, for funsies. The cheese bread was delicious- it's super hard to mess that up. The shrimp and crawfish pasta was excellent, as well. The meatball was a little over cooked, but that's not the end of the world.  I used to go to Brick Oven more often than I do now, but I think I'm going to add it to the rotation.

It's hard to even wrap my mind about the deliciousness that I experienced here. I had been wanting to try Clancy's for a while and when my dad offered to take me here for a Friday lunch, I jumped at the chance.  For starters, make reservations. It's old school: you're going to have to actually call and talk to a person, but reservations are a must. The place was packed when I went, but thanks to reservations, we were seated immediately. This place is very old time New Orleans- the menu changes daily and the service is top notch. I'm talking "switch out utensils between each course" top notch.  For my appetizer, I decided to get the seafood gumbo. The serving was generous and it was packed with shrimp, crab and oysters. I'm not talking small scraps of seafood- these were good size shrimp and oysters. Please note that the gumbo contains okra. I love okra, but I know that it's not some people's thing. For my entree, I got the soft shell crab. I think the menu said that it was roasted, but it seemed fried. Either way it was delicious. The batter was nice and light and it had a lot of flavor. It was paired with a vegetable medley that complimented the crab perfectly.  I normally don't do desert at lunch, but look, if you come to a place like this, you have to. What's that? They're known for their bread pudding in whiskey sauce? Well, if you insist. Yeah, this might have been the highlight of the entire meal. Holy sugar! This serving is huge and it's well worth the $10, although my dad and I were wishing we had just split one, rather than each getting our own, but oh well. The bread pudding is rich and decadent and the sauce they serve with it is incredibly good. I really want to just go back and get this and a cup of coffee and call it a day. I'm not even a huge fan of bread pudding, but I would eat this every day if it was socially acceptable.   Clancy's was perfect in every way. The service was outstanding and the staff was on top of everything. I felt very "classic New Orleans" as I was eating here, imagining all of the different people who have enjoyed meals in this place. You should know that nothing about this restaurant is inexpensive, so bring your spending pants. For example, coffee is $5 a cup, but it's all worth it for such an amazing and memorable experience.

I'm not gonna lie- when I heard that Master P was opening a burger place, I had my doubts. I thought it was all a gimmick, so I had to head over and check it out for myself.  After much anticipation, I headed to Big Poppa's for lunch. I was on a mission to discover if the burgers here were indeed, "Bout It Bout It". Walking in, I immediately loved the vibe of the place; it's like an old diner with a modern feel and I was given a friendly greeting by the smiling staff. The combination of counter and table service here is like many burger joints. You order your food at the counter, the staff gives you a number brings your order right to your table.  I thought I knew for sure what I was getting, but then, I saw it: They have a fried chicken sandwich! Of course they have a fried chicken sandwich. Why wouldn't they?  The thought crossed my mind, "Do I dare? Do I order a burger AND a fried chicken sandwich? I can't come to a burger place and not get a burger, but chicken sandwiches are hot right now. Should I get both?" My heart answered, "Absolutely!" and my stomach agreed, so I got the fried chicken sandwich meal, which came with fries and a drink, and I got a Big Poppa Bacon Burger as a nice little side. Hey, this is all for research purposes.  I first looked at the chicken sandwich and saw two big fried chicken breasts dressed to the nines with tasty fries on the side. Truth be told, the fries here are more like potato wedges, but that's no complaint. I bit into the massive sandwich and I was delighted to be confronted with something different for once; the batter here is actually a little sweet, which set off the salty, juicy flavor of the chicken. The taste level was off the charts; if you're a chicken sandwich fan, you're going to want to add this one to your list.  I was halfway through the chicken sandwich when I remembered I still had a burger to eat. It's a super thick patty grilled to perfection, dressed with lettuce and tomato and then topped with a generous pile of grilled onions, Big Poppa sauce and battered-and-fried bacon. Yes, the bacon is battered and fried. I put the whole thing together and dove right in. As soon as I took the first bite, I could tell that this burger was something special- maybe one of the best burgers I've had, and I'm pretty picky when it comes to burgers. It reminded me of the kind of burger you have at backyard family barbecues that just translates into good, old-fashioned comfort food.  I raved about this spot so much that my dad came over and grabbed one of the burgers for himself and LOVED it. If that's not a solid endorsement, I don't know what is. I will definitely be back!

David and I were here on my birthday because it was the only bar that wasn't crazy packed, because there was a big event going on downtown.  I like this place- the vibe is relaxed and the big selling point is their awesome beer selection. You don't expect to find a good craft beer bar in the middle of Bourbon St., but this spot fit the bill nicely, so I was happy that we just happened to find this spot. They had a band when we first got there, but they were on their last song as soon as we sat down.   This is a place worth checking out, if you're trying to get away from the crowds.

Honestly, I'm not a SUPER huge fan of Indian food. I'm a firm believer that within every type of food there is something that a person can at least tolerate but I find it difficult to find something tolerable about food with curry.  When I came here, a friend of mine and I split an order of chicken tikka masala. It was basically chicken in a cream sauce served with rice. It wasn't bad, but it's probably not something I would go out of my way to order again.  I really don't know if I'll be back. I try to stay open minded, but this type of food just really doesn't ring my bells.

Considering all of the lots in the Quarter are now "pay ahead", the garages are really becoming the only option, if you don't want to pay for more time than you need.  This is a pretty typical parking garage. You pull in, hand your keys over to the valet and you pay and get your car when you return. This is a good place to pay and park if you're going out in the Bourbon area and you want to be close and get there and back quickly. We parked here when we were going to Mr. B's and when we returned we handed over our ticket with no problem. There was a little oddness while we were waiting for our car. Turns out the person we handed our ticket to didn't pass it off to a valet, so we waited longer than we had to.  All in all, this was a pretty good experience and definitely beats parking in one of those drafty lots, especially when the weather is cool.

I'll tell you what. I was here on a Saturday morning for a quick coffee and this place was BUSTLING!
