I have always been impressed with the way they do things here- they are extremely good at getting people through the line and to their seats and everything is well organized. For the show, we were seated upstairs which has it's own bar space and bathrooms. If you can get a seat upstairs for any show, go for it; it is absolutely worth the few extra dollars. From where we were sitting (Row C) we had a fantastic view of the stage, sound was perfect and the seats were comfortable. We really couldn't have asked for a better experience.

I have been going here for years and I love this car wash for one reason and one reason only: it's NOT touchless!  This car wash actually uses the "snakes" and gentle brushes to wash your car properly.  You can go and pay good money and get more than just high pressured water and soap cleaning your car.  Don't get me wrong, the wash is extremely gentle and won't scratch your paint job, but if you need to get bugs and gunk off of your car, this is the wash you have to go with.  There are three washes you can choose, depending on how "detailed" you want it to be.  The cheapest is $4, I get the $8 one and there's one for $12 that gives you the tire shine stuff and I think a wax of some sort.  Also, they have FREE vacuums, so once you get the outside of your car all clean and shiny, you can take care of the inside.

This PJ's is located inside the Doubletree Hotel on Canal. On the day that I was working an event at the hotel, this PJ's was a lifesaver. The store itself is small, but has a few tables and chairs. The coffee was good and the staff was fast and friendly. I was here at 10am and, for some reason, they were in the middle of a staff change and could only accept cards. That wasn't a big deal, but I've never experienced that at other locations.  A large iced coffee came to about $3.47, which is a bit cheaper than my regular PJ's, so I was happy.

I just had to check this place out a year ago.  I don't have a fear of "creepy crawlers", so there was no hesitation on my part.  I liked it here.  The place is large and there is a lot to see and do.  The staff is extremely polite, and they are quick to step in with a bottle of windex in order to quickly clean fingerprints off of the tanks containing the insects.  I would definitely say that this place is best for kids.  I liked it, because it was a definite learning experience, but I can see how most adults would probably find it boring.  My favorite part was the butterfly exhibit with every species of butterfly on display, as well as the butterfly garden that was full of live butterflies.

This is a fabulous day long celebration of St. Patrick's Day.  Pretty much every bar and business on the block participates and it's a huge party.  The parade is really cool and is a nice follow up to Mardi Gras.  It's a small parade, but it's a really good time and draws a fun crowd.

Since the Uptown Nacho Mama's closed, this is the only remaining location anywhere near the city.  I would like it if it was a little more convenient to get to.  Being located all the way in Elmwood makes getting here a real trek.  I usually like to travel to Uptown and sometimes downtown, and that's it.  But I digress.  This isn't a bad location.  It's a nice place to stop into, especially if you have plans to go to the movies, which is located nearby.  I usually sit at the bar and have found that service is way faster when I do so.  Not a bad place, but I probably wouldn't go out of my way to go here.  There are way better Mexican places around.

Dmac's is quite the establishment. I walked in hungry and I left starving. Allow me to explain.  I was first turned on to Dmac's after the Yelp March elite event that left us sampling brunch favorites. I was fortunate enough to not only score a coupon for 50% off a burger, but I was able to nab a gift certificate for $25. This pretty much guaranteed my return.  So, we stopped in and ordered and I flashed my certificate like a big shot. It definitely worked it's magic, because not only was my meal discounted, but Mr. DMac himself came over to say that he had never even seen such a certificate. I "fiddle dee dee'd" and explained to him the Yelp promotion and he was delighted that I had returned to his establishment to try his faire.  I ordered the burger medium rare with cheddar cheese, bacon and grilled onions. It came fully dressed and cooked to perfection. The concoction was so perfectly prepared that I had no problem polishing off the entire thing. Normally I would have felt guilty, but I very rarely eat red meat and since I knew I was going to have a "full" dinner, I treated myself to a "slim" lunch. No morsel was spared and I devoured the burger with no shame. I like that when I said "medium rare" the kitchen wasn't shy about leaving my burger pink and juicy. I couldn't have asked for a better burger experience. As far as New Orleans burgers go, this is the burger to beat.  Now onto the music. We were treated to the sounds of the Jeff Davis Project. What a delight! This is a band that starts you off with some Tracey Chapman, throws in some Janis and finishes you off with Prince's "Purple Rain" and some "House of the Rising Sun" for good measure. Good Lord did I have a great time listening to this music! Oh and they have a full fledged blues night on Mondays, so be sure to stop in if that's your thing.  All in all I had a fantastic time at DMac's. DMac himself came up to us at the end of the night to ask how our food was and to make sure that we were having a good time. In my book, it doesn't get any better than that. I love when a business owner takes care to make sure that his customers are happy. That alone ensured that I will return.  DMac's is fantastic and I will definitely return. Juicy burgers and good music. How can you resist? So why did I leave starving? I left hungry for more of the musical perfection that this establishment offers. Thirsty for more art- which is the calling card of any stage. I can't wait to experience more.

I have been here two different times now and I MUST recommend this quaint bed and breakfast to anyone visiting New Orleans.  This is a cozy house located in the Bywater and super close to the Quarter. The rooms feel very French and you feel as if you are in a cozy European bungalow. The neighborhood is very nice and there is plenty of available street parking and the house is surrounded by a lot of other nice houses. My favorite part of the place is the backyard. There is a full pool and then there is a lounging area that is shrouded by banana trees. You feel as if you are in a completely different world. I like that the house isn't super huge and it's quiet. You feel as if you are staying with friends.  Not only is this the perfect spot for people visiting from out of town, but it is fantastic if you are a local and want a change of scenery and surroundings for the weekend.

One of my favorite places to eat in the quarter.  They have delicious food.  From sandwiches to pizza.  My absolute favorite is the Mystic pizza.  Oh my gah!  It is so good. I seem to remember gettng a pasta salad here once.  I love how big the servings are here and the place is perfect for groups. Also, this place is open late, so it's a great place to stop if you need some dinner after a long night.    Try not to be put off by the paintings on the wall that seem to resemble Angelina Jolie.  Fun fact: a friend of mine lives in the apartment directly above this place and his pad smells like pizza 24/7...a little cool and a little weird, eh?

It is what it is: a cigar bar.  Really small and smoky inside, so if you are easily bothered by smoke, you might want to skip this one.   Great local music by a live band inside.  Great patio area outside, if you want to get away from the smoke and the crowds.  I agree with K.W.'s review about the inside needing an update.  It definitely feels as if you are hanging out in someone's basement during prohibition.    I would love this place if I were a cigar aficionado.  I would like it a little more, if it were a little bigger and less crowded, but what are you gonna do?

I'm going to start off by saying that I am not a HUGE fan of barbecue. I usually go for anything else before I say "let's get barbecue", but I was out with a friend and he wanted some, so we ended up here.  Boo Koo is located in the back of Finn McCool's bar. There's no separate entrance, so you are going to have to fight the crowd in order to get to the back and place your order. Once you order, you can either get your food to go, or sit in one of the limited seats inside or outside.  I decided on the Cajun Cuban, which is Boo Koo's version of the traditional Cuban sandwich. I don't know what makes it "Cajun", but it was really good. It tasted like a typical Cuban to me. It might not be the best I have ever had, but I would order it again. I also really liked how crispy the fries were that came with it.  I would give this place three stars for dining in and four stars for take out. Why? Because of the smoking. I just can't enjoy my meal while smelling cigarettes and it was cold and rainy the night we were here, so sitting outside was out. Also, they have a video golf game located right in the small dining area and the guys playing it were SUPER loud (screaming and high fiving- typical frat behavior) and chain smoking. I would suggest ditching the game entirely, or moving it away from where people are trying to eat.

Oooh I feel so fancy! I finally got over to Poke Loa for lunch, but unfortunately I forgot my yoga pants at home.  Since Kyoto closed, this town has certainly been missing a good poke bowl and I think that Poke Loa does a good job of filling that void. The process is easy enough: walk in, hop in line and tell them what you want. You can build your own bowl or you can choose a pre-made bowl from their menu. I decided to get the King Loa bowl, because the pictures looked great and it looked like you got a lot of bang for your buck. The King Loa bowl included four scoops of fish (salmon and tuna), three types of roe, rice, lettuce, onions, edamame, and a few other goodies all topped with a yummy sauce. I also got a Big Easy Bucha drink from the case and just like that I had the perfect lunch.  As others have said, the food is super fresh and they are bringing fresh fish out constantly. I loved my bowl and it was SO MUCH food for the money. Seriously, those who complained that it wasn't a lot of food didn't do their research- I even had leftovers. I love that you can mix  the bowl up yourself once it's "built" so that you can combine flavors. There were a lot of people on the day I came, but the staff had the line moving quickly.  I have to mention that the plastic bowls made my heart hurt. All of that plastic is going to be piled into landfills and it will never break down. I was actually glad that I had leftovers so that I could recycle the bowl after. I would love it if they added a recycling bin. It would be as easy as dumping the leftover food out of the bowl and tossing the bowl into the bin- something worth thinking about. NOTE: The owner just contacted me and informed me that the bowls are eco friendly and biodegradable! This makes me so happy!  All in all I loved it here and I would return in a heartbeat. This is a great little lunch spot and a great addition to the area.

I've only been here once, and it was for a pick up order, so I can't really speak to the service, just the food.  I ordered a super felony with pork carnitas and all the usual "fixins".  I agree with Jen that it's a little ridiculous that they charge $1.49 for guac.  I mean, I can see charging fifty cents or something, but more than that just seems greedy to me.  The biggest thing that I like about this place (and apparently other Izzo's) is you can place your order online, give them your cell phone number and they will text you when your food is ready. After I ordered my food online, I popped in and I was in and out in probably 30 seconds.  Super convenient.  And honestly, what would stop you from ordering online and then dining in, skipping the line completely?  Nothing, as far as I can tell.  VIP treatment FTW!

Sure, it's a divey bar, and honestly there's really no reason to go here considering all of your other options, but this place has two redeeming qualities.  The first thing that saves this place is the karaoke.  Sure, the sound system kind of sucks, but it's something to do when you are in the mood for something a little different.  The second thing is, on Thursdays, you can get a huge steak and mashed potatoes and corn for $10.  You can't beat that!  They also offer chicken, salmon, and tuna, if red meat isn't your thang.  Oh!  And the bathrooms are always clean.  Huzzah!

This building is the space that Christian's and Redemption formerly occupied. I didn't have the opportunity to go to either on of those restaurants, so actually eating dinner in what was a former church was a whole new experience for me.  From top to bottom, this place is just divine. I love the fact that the restaurant is situated in a "reworked" church, and still has the feel with the stained glass windows and high ceilings. The atmosphere is cozy, yet elegant and everything is just beautiful. The staff here might be the friendliest staff in town. I know that some of you might say it's because the place is so new, but I was greeted by multiple people when I arrived, a few staff members stopped by during dinner to inquire about the meal and I got a friendly goodbye on my way out the door.  I started off with the #gooddecisions cocktail as I looked over the menu. Everything here sounds so amazing, and I like that they have a nice selection of options from seafood and pork to chicken and vegetable dishes. For my appetizers I got the 3 cheese plate which came with the chef's choice of cheeses as well as the rabbit rillette, which is basically a pâté, The cheese was delicious- I wish I could remember exactly what the cheeses were, but I really enjoyed them. The rabbit rillette was out of this world. It was full of flavor and a biscuit came on the side so it could be spread. It was really rich, and if I was just getting a drink and an appetizer here, this is exactly what I would order.  For my entree, I got the whole smoked fish, charred eggplant, house yogurt, eggplant & black sesame seed purée. The fish is indeed a whole fish which comes with the bones in and head on. It was delicious! The fish had enough meat on it that the bones being in it wasn't a problem at all and they were fairly easy to "pick out". The fish had a smoky flavor that was good without being overwhelming. The eggplant was perfectly roasted and the yogurt was a nice touch and mellowed out the flavor of the fish a bit- it was a nice balance of flavors.  I loved my experience here and I am excited to return. On the night I was here the crowd was pretty thin, but I am sure that this place will definitely "take off" once word gets out about how good it is.

I was really on the fence with this one, but I think I'm going to go with three stars and leave some room for improvement.  We were here for a quick snack before a show downstairs at the casino. We decided to sit at the bar, and we hoped this would mean service would be a bit faster. Right away we could tell something was up because the bartender was running around like crazy and took a while to get our drink order. It turns out she was completely on her own- she was taking care of drinks for basically everyone in the place by herself. Okay, the delay can be forgiven.  We ordered some onion rings to munch on. Well, first we ordered the nachos, but the awesome bartender basically told us that they are not very good and not worth the money, so THEN we ordered onion rings. I really like the rings here- they are the thin "steak house" kind that come in a big pile and there was jalapeño sauce on the side for dipping. It was all really tasty.  At one point, I ordered another beer, and because the bartender was so busy, she forgot about me for a while. She did comp that beer, so that was nice of her. I don't blame her at all for being on her own, she did the best she could and she never stopped.  This is a pretty casual type place, so I might stop back in if I find myself in the casino again. I also notice that they show the UFC fights at the bar, so take note if that's your thing.

Wow. I had no idea this place even existed until a friend suggested that we go here for lunch.  This is a small Vietnamese cafe disguised as a coffee shop! When you walk in you are struck by how super small the place is, but the menu is extensive. They have all kinds of different types of Pho and other Viet treats, as well as bubble tea.  When you walk in, you order at the counter and then pick a seat and wait for your meal. I ordered the wonton soup. It was so good and was very generous with the wontons and pieces of beef. The broth was tasty and I got so much that I couldn't even finish it all! It was the perfect lunch.  If I am ever in Metairie and craving Pho, I will definitely return to Frosty's.

Winston's has always been a favorite of mine. I don't know what it is. I really think that it's the atmosphere. The all wood interior really does make you feel as if you are in an English pub and the people here are always nice and friendly. I really like the fact that it doesn't get too crowded in here and most of the people are just stopping in to get a drink before going out or just to sit and chat with friends,  I think that my favorite part has to be the leather couches that are off to the side. That little nook is so cozy and it feels like you are in a cabin somewhere. I really wish that they still had the jukebox with the Frank Sinatra albums on there, but oh well.  They are currently renovating the patio, and when that is complete the bar will be completely smoke free inside.

Oxalis has been on my "gotta try" list for a while now. I had it bookmarked for ages, but never had the opportunity to stop in until recently.  We were here early evening on a Saturday. We didn't have reservations, so we sat at the bar- perfect for us. Looking over the menu, everything just sounded incredible, so we decided to sample a few things.  First, we started with the bone marrow, pomme frites, and the pork rillettes. The bone marrow was rich and tender and spread perfectly on the toasted bread that it came with. The pomme frittes were out of this world and came with two decadent dipping sauces, which added to the "yum" factor. My personal favorite was the pork rillettes. This was basically a pork pâté spread that we enjoyed on bread rounds. OMG it was so incredible! Honestly, we could have just eaten appetizers all afternoon, but we decided to continue exploring the menu.  For my entree, I got the burger with blue cheese on it. The burger was small, but I thought it was the perfect size for me and the blue cheese added a nice tart kick to it. Blue cheese on a burger is so simple. but really brilliant and the meat was cooked perfectly and nice and juicy.  Finally, because we like to do things right we got dessert in the form of a delicious Three Milks and a Barrel cake. This was cake soaked in condensed milk and vanilla bourbon. I mean, come on, it doesn't get much better than that. The cake was perfect and soft and gooey. Amazing.  I loved Oxalis for a few reasons: the atmosphere is great, the food is delicious and affordable and the place is just all in all really romantic. I can't wait to go back.

Really impressed with this place.  So, after listening to my friends rave about what an amazing place this is, I couldn't wait to check it out. I stopped in for lunch, because I was craving pho and spring rolls.  I decided on a small bowl of pho with brisket and eye round steak and some pork spring rolls.  The rolls were super good. They were big, with a lot of flavor. The sauce on the side was not your typical peanut sauce. it was almost like a spicy barbeque sauce. It's hard to describe, but it was delicious. The pho was great and packed a lot of flavor. I would have liked it if there were more noodles, but that's not a huge deal.  Everything was pretty typically priced and the restaurant itself was simple, like most Vietnamese restaurants. The staff was super attentive and was always sure to check and make sure everything was okay.  I've heard the Thai food here is amazing, so when I go back, I plan to try that.

This is a pretty typical shopping mall, but I like it. They have a good selection of stores, plenty of parking and there are convenient food places nearby. My "musts" in this strip mall are Bath and Body Works and Sally's. I think that this complex is a nice addition to the area and they seem to have a store that appeals to everyone.

I ate here last night and I couldn't wait to write a review! Don't be fooled by the fact that the restaurant is basically in a convenience store- they serve fantastic food!  We started with the stuffed grape leaves and the falafel and both dishes were exceptionally good! I loved the grape leaves because they were cooked well and had a lot of flavor. For my entree, I got my go to- the beef shawarma which came with salad and hummus. I know that I get this as every Mediterranean restaurant, but it's my favorite and it's how i know if I like a place. Cleo's version didn't disappoint. The beef was nice and tender, the salad was good and the hummus was perfect. I like when the hummus is finely whipped and that's how it was here. I loved it!  I like that they let you pick any drink you want out of the store and they are extremely attentive and make sure that you have everything that you need. This spot is open 24/7, so you really have no excuse to not check it out, especially on those late nights. This restaurant was a real life saver for us and we will be back again.

I love art.  What a gorgeous and unique gallery.  I like that there was a lot of stuff to buy that wasn't exclusively "art".  The gallery not only offered prints, but they offered really cool souveniers in the form of unique voodoo doll key chains and prints.

Gretna is actually a cool little city with a lot going for it.   Old Gretna is probably my favorite. Years ago, I was able to become acquainted with the ins and outs of Old Gretna. It really has a small town feel about it. The houses here are pretty cozy and the neighborhoods are pretty nice and well kept.   Some of my favorite things about Gretna are the farmers market every Saturday. Here you can get fresh produce that is grown by "small town" farmers. Gretna also has a festival that has music acts, craft booths and really good food. The fest always gets packed and draws a really good crowd. A few weeks after the fest wraps up, there is a weekly riverfront concert, on Fridays, right on the river. It's always a good time, free and a lot of fun.  There are a lot of great places to eat in Gretna and you can't beat the convenience of the ferry that brings you to Gretna from Canal street and back. There is no excuse why everyone shouldn't visit!

When I first walked into Blue Tomato, my first thought was "Great, a dive."  It was kind of warm, small and the place was hazy from food being cooked.  My friend and I sat down and looked over the menu.    I decided on the pork burrito which came topped with cheese and sauce and came with a side of beans and rice.  My expectations weren't high AT ALL, but I was blown away.  The burrito may have been one of the best I have ever had.  I am not exaggerating!  It was amazing and tasted like it was home cooked.  I also had a margarita which was also really good.  If you aren't in the mood for Mexican, don't worry.  Blue Tomato has all kinds of menu items from hamburgers to pasta!  I think that their specialty is Mexican food, but there is pretty much something here for everyone.  I will absolutely be going back and I can't wait to try some other items on the menu.  Just a note: when I left the place I did smell a lot like food because the dining room and the kitchen are right next to each other and the kitchen is "open" style, so the smell goes everywhere.

This is a cool place.  A friend and I were in the area, so we decided to stop in and take a look at Manning's, since we had heard so much about it.  We sat in the bar area, just so we could take it all in.  It's a sports bar and there is a HUGE screen in the front of the place with recliners in the first few rows.  This seems like it would be the perfect bar to watch the game, as long as you get here early and are lucky enough to grab one of the recliners.  I would love to come back and try the food.  Honestly, this isn't the type of place I would judge based on the cuisine.  It's a sports bar.  Go there to watch a game and hang out with friends.  The food should probably be a second thought.  Anyway, I will definitely be back and I hope to check out a few Saints games here, next season.

Yay! I always love when a new Italian place opens up close to home.  I went to Buca for lunch today. I was immediately struck by the decor. There are pictures everywhere, from everything to religious figures to Italian movie stars and singers. There are 2500 pictures total and each room has a different theme. There is a "poster room", a "Sinatra room" and a "Cardinal room" just to name a few. A waitress was kind enough to give us a tour of the place, since it's new and it wasn't too packed. There is even a "Pope" table. A table that is surrounded by pictures of different Popes and a covered statue of the Pope in the middle of the table. Kind of creepy... kind of cool.  You can even call ahead and request the special table that is located in the kitchen! All in all, the concept of all of this is pretty neat.  We were seated in the Cardinal room. The wait staff was extremely attentive and asked if we were celebrating anything. We weren't, but asking us was a nice touch. They were really good about checking on us to make sure that we had everything we needed.  For my lunch, I ordered the baked rigatoni, because my first choice, lasagna, was already sold out for the day. It came covered in cheese and had sausage in it. The sauce was good and rich and had a lot of flavor. I really enjoyed it. It was a lot of food, so I took half of it home to enjoy later. I wished that I had room for dessert, because they had cannolis that I really wanted to try, but maybe next time.  All in all I had a good experience. The atmosphere was really cozy and nice and I would definitely go back.

I saw Russell Brand at The Civic! Ok, now to review the venue and not Russell. Let me think. Got it!  First and foremost, one thing I immediately loved is the fact that parking is a cinch. There is a parking lot right across the street, so parking is painless and there wasn't a long walk so I felt super safe. I got in line before the doors opened, and although there was a bit of wait, everything was handled pretty quickly and we were in in no time.   The bar is there immediately when you walk in and the bartenders did a good job of keeping up with the crowd. Drinks are a little steep, but you are there to see a show really, so that's not a huge deal. Once in the theater, I was overtaken by how beautiful the whole venue was. It was wonderfully redone and everything was nice and new and fresh. I was fortunate enough to be seated on the floor and it was the perfect spot to see the comedy show.  The staff was super nice and friendly and were more than happy to help people find their seats. Everything went really smoothly considering this was only the second show at the redone Civic.  I can't wait to see future shows here. The place is gorgeous and is going to be fantastic for plays and concerts.

This shop is a real vintage treasure. First of all, a lot of what they have here is from different estate sales, they carry varying style from different eras and they have a lot of things that are extremely affordable.  I actually ducked in here on a rainy day to escape a storm, and to my delight, this was a shop that was right up my stylish glamorous alley! As Jen stated, they carry everything from shoes and dresses to jewelry. I found a GORGEOUS lace dress that had been marked down considerably from it's original price. I was so excited, because even though it's vintage, it is in perfect condition. I was even more excited when it fit, because a lot of vintage stores only carry dresses that are on the much smaller side.  The woman working here was very helpful and pointed out exactly what was on sale and mentioned that they even carry vintage designer items! Score! I had my eye on a necklace, but it was a bit out of my price range for the day.  From casual to fancy, if you need a dress for something special, this is the place.

This is a great organization.  I adopted a cat from this group about two years ago.  Volunteers provide foster homes to some pets until they can be placed in forever homes.  The organization is non profit, so upon adoption, they ask for a donation.  I found my future kitty on Craig's list.  I contacted her foster parent and we set up a meeting, so that I could meet the cat.  I got to meet her in her own foster environment, so she was comfortable.  There was no pressure to adopt.  I am so happy that I adopted through ARNO.  Whenever you are looking for a new pet, please look at groups like ARNO and LASPCA first.  There are so many animals out there that needs good homes.

This is a review of the bar.  This place was a real life saver during Endymion in that it was a good place to grab drinks and use the restroom. The bar itself is pretty much as divey as it gets, but the drinks are priced well and the bartenders were pretty friendly. If you're in the mood for food, there is a fully functioning diner in the back complete with all day breakfast and places to sit. I'm not going to lie- the food smelled and looked amazing and if I hadn't been at a parade I would have taken the time to sit down and have something to eat. I will definitely return and try the food.

Man oh man.  I had been wanting to try this place for so long.  I mean, I love cheese and the word "cheese" is in the name of the place, so how could it be anything but awesome?  I was so excited, in fact, that I went on the website ahead of time and decided what I wanted to order when I got there.  Don't judge me!  I decided on a sandwich called "Hook's Cheddar" (formerly the Beecher's).  It's a delicious turkey sandwich topped with lettuce, tomato, avocado (!) and a white cheddar cheese on ciabatta bread.  It was FANTASTIC!  First of all, it was so big that I couldn't finish it in one sitting.  There was a generous portion of turkey and a nice thick piece of cheese on it.  I was not left disappointed.  It came with a choice of side salad or kettle chips and I decided to go with the side salad.  The whole meal was amazing.  The atmosphere of the place is interesting.  You walk in, and you are immediately struck by how small the inside is.  There is a huge case full of cheese that you can buy, the register where you order and a few tables to sit.  There are more tables outside, if you want to have more of a picnic feel.  Once you order, you are given a number and they bring you your food.  I chose to sit inside, because it's summer in New Orleans and I'm not a masochist.  I definitely want to go back and try their other sandwiches and salads.  I saw one of their salads and it was huge and looked delicious.

I  had the thin sliced brisket with the blue cheese cole slaw on New Years Eve (see picture) and it was delicious. I like that you can just order it and they will deliver it right to you at Courtyard Brewery. A bunch of us ordered BBQ and it really put our little New Years Eve party over the top. Damien says that he slow cooks the meat and you can definitely tell. It's melt in your mouth delicious with a lot of flavor and not chewy at all.  Right now, Black Label is only a popup inside of Barrel Proof, but I am hoping that they have an actual store front soon.

There seem to be a thousand or so souvenir shops in this town, but this is one of the better ones.  Toulouse Royale sells things that are a little more unique and different from just your typical bead and t shirt places. Sure, this spot has beads and t shirts, but they also carry mixes, magnets, spices and other things of that nature. As a local, I don't really shop in places like this- only because I pretty much have every type of thing that they carry, but it's a good store to pick up some keepsakes if you are visiting.

It had been ages since I had set foot into Dragon's Den and it was pretty much just as I remember- except they serve food now and they seem to have working ac.  I used to hang out here pretty regularly back in 2009 when Dragon's Den was one of the few places in the city where you could see a burlesque show. Back in those days, there was no ac upstairs and it was hot and stuffy and you just had to deal with it. A lot has changed since then- there is a really nice bar downstairs that leads into a patio area. Upstairs is still small and a little stuffy, but it's not nearly as hot and the bartenders are really fast in getting the drinks poured and served.  The dance floor is small, so if you are the kind of person who isn't a fan of smaller spaces, you might just want to hang out downstairs. When I go back, my plan is probably going to be just spending time on the downstairs patio.

What a lovely and amazing cozy little spot!  We were wandering around deciding where to eat when Martinque Bistro was suggested. We called 10 minutes before we arrived to make our reservation and were told that was no issue at all. We showed up and were seated immediately.  Martinique feels very European to me. No, I have never been to Europe, but it seems like one of the little cafes where you would go after admiring classic art at The Louvre. Seating is very close, which may be off putting to some, but I didn't mind at all. It was so close, in fact, that if I had been so inclined I could have held hands with the older gentleman seated to my left, but then that would be just weird.  For my appetizer, I decided on the "special" which was a cold watermelon soup. I know it sounds super strange, but it was actually really good. It was a cold soup with different vegetables and spices in it and in the middle was frozen watermelon ice that made the entire thing delicious and refreshing. It was definitely different, and probably not for everyone, but I enjoyed it.  For my entree, I decided on the shrimp and lobster which was served over some kind of pasta (super technical terms here). It was light and delicious. The shrimp were nice and big and juicy. I know I am weird, but lobster doesn't really ring my bell. I don't dislike lobster, but I prefer shrimp, so that was the highlight of the meal for me.  This is a great spot for a romantic dinner. I will definitely be back!

This is a really nice hotel located at the end of Esplanade.  I met someone for a modeling gig here and I was really impressed with the place. It has a nice sized lobby right off of Esplanade. The room itself was open to a huge patio, which I thought was lovely. In the room there was a seating area complete with a sofa, chairs and tv. There was a kitchenette with a small fridge, sink, coffee maker and microwave and the bedroom in the back, although small, was nice for what it was. The bathroom was also pretty small, but it wasn't terrible.  Friendly staff and pretty easy to park. I think that they even have valet.

I like this Chase branch!  I stopped in here today just to do some good old fashioned banking and the woman I dealt with was really nice and helpful. The line moved quickly and there was a teller at every window. My usual Chase branch has everything automated now, so it was nice to actually talk to someone one on one and get done what I needed to get done.

Damian is back! I got to enjoy some delicious Brügger's Barbecüe at their popup at Side Bar. As always, the food was beyond delicious. I got the brisket and sausage platter which came piled high with brisket, spicy sausage, regular sausage, potatoes and cole slaw. The platter cost $16, I shared it with another person and it was more than enough food for me.  The best thing about Brügger's Barbecüe is the fact that the brisket doesn't need sauce. It's nice and tender and cooked to perfection with a smoky flavor and juicy enough so that it doesn't need anything added to it. Of course, if you are in the mood for sauce, they are more than happy to give you what you want.  Brügger's Barbecüe is going to be popping up all over, so be sure to keep an eye out and getcha pull!

The peanut butter bacon cake I was able to try at Toups was INCREDIBLE. It was soft and delicious and so good. The girl at Toups told me that because Debbie delivers cake to them that if I place an order with DDD, they would be happy to deliver whatever cake I order to them so that I can pick it up. Talk about super convenient! I think my next birthday cake will definitely be from Debbie Does Doberge!

This is a really cute cafe in Old Metairie.  Although I just stopped in here for an iced coffee, this place is so much more than a coffee shop. First of all, the iced coffee I got was amazing. It had a lot of flavor, without being overpowering.  I was really impressed by the menu here. They serve everything from pastries, salads and wraps to specialty sandwiches. I was tempted to try some food, but I was in a bit of a rush.  The shop itself has very good atmosphere and a lot of space. As Jen L. said, there are plenty of tables where you can eat and, of course, there is free WifI, if you need to get some work done.

Long story short: it's a mall. Since Yelp requires me to expound a little more on that sentiment, here we go.  I agree with other reviewers who say that this is a good place for tourists, but not worth going out of your way. I would, however, go out of my way if I was in the market for something specific. One thing they have here is a fudge shop. I love fudge, so that was worth the trip for me. They had quite a few stores that were having "season change" sales, so it was nice to browse around and check out the deals. There is a store that sells Michael Kors purses, another that sells kitchen ware and other various clothing outlets. The food court is okay- there are some pretty basic chains like Cane's and Izzo's. The one burger place they had had the longest line of any of the food options. There's a daiquiri shop as well as a nice little bar in the middle of the food court, if you are making a day of it and feel like drinking.  The main selling point of the Riverwalk is the view of the river. I really love any spot in the city where you can hang out on a nice day and watch the water. I just have different memories of the Riverwalk from when I was a kid. I remember more local places and less chains, but I could be imagining things.  It's good for what it is, but nothing overly special.

This is really a 3.5 star review. When is Yelp going to provide half stars?  Stopped in here to fulfill my mission of trying every Vietnamese place in the New Orleans area. First of all, don't get freaked out by the appearance of this place. It is, quite literally, a hole in the wall. You walk in and there are pictures of the food on the menu taped to the wall, which a very nice lady instructed me to point to when I was ready to order. I decided to get some rice noodle beef soup to go. I should emphasize that I got soup and NOT Pho. Yes, there is a difference.  I liked that they gave me my entire order "not put together" for lack of a better term. I got a container of soup broth and then a styrofoam container of beef, noodles, sauces and "fixins" (onions, peppers, lime, sriacha, and sprouts). It was nice to be able to put it together myself so that the noodles didn't get mushy and soak up all of the broth on the way home.  The soup itself was okay, but I had to add some hot sauce to the broth to give it any kind of flavor. I also found it really oily, for some reason. The noodles and beef were good and the onions added a nice kick to the mix. The meal cost $8 and I just think that this is kind of overpriced for what you get, especially since I can tell this is mainly a take out place (there aren't public restrooms).   I will probably return just to see what else they have to offer, but next time I'm in the mood for noodle soup, I'm going to go elsewhere.

Although the clothing here doesn't fit my particular style, I have to give them 5 stars because of the fantastic selection and great customer service.  As soon as I entered the shop I was greeted and asked if I needed help finding anything. Although I was just browsing, it was nice that they were attentive to the potential customer.   There is a great selection of day dresses and cute tops and they have a huge selection of jewelry. I feel like their stuff is more on the "fancy casual" side but it's really nice stuff.

Whenever someone ask where they can go to get cute New Orleans themed gifts, I usually tell them to look no further than Fleurty Girl.    FG started as an online tshirt shop and exploded into a full blown New Orleans chain that sells everything from local themed tshirts to fleur de lis rain boots and pretty much anything else you could want.  This is a great place to go if you want to pick up a little treat for yourself, or if you are looking for a gift for your favorite nola-phile.  One of my favorite things that I have ever gotten here is my fleur de lis stainless steel coffee scoop.  It is so cute and I use it every single day!

This is a neat little neighborhood bar. The staff was friendly and the patrons seemed cool, too. I really like that this place allows dogs. I always find dog friendly places extra welcoming. It's worth stopping in if you are in the area and you want a drink.

Whenever I have to get my license renewed, I always go here. There is never really a line and I am always in and out in no time. People have always been friendly and it seems a lot more relaxed than your average DMV. The last time I renewed my license, I was in and out in 30 minutes. Boom! I would never go anywhere else.

While on the Metry bar crawl, me and some other folks decided that it would be a good idea to eat. Steve and Michelle suggested we check out Taqueria Sanchez, which was a few feet away from Colby's cocktails,.Since I am fairly familiar with the Sanchez, due to their Westbank location, I decided this was as good a day as any to die of food poisoning.  TS is located in what is basically a converted trailer. It is super duper small with a few tables inside and small bar area where you can order or eat. We all walked in and looked over the menu. I wasn't really hungry, so I decided on a small pork quesadilla which cost 4 whole dollars. Everyone else ordered and we all waited. The food came pretty quickly considering there were about 5 or 6 of us. Once food was acquired, we headed back over to Colby's to eat.  I opened my plate and was pleasantly surprised. This looked really good. My quesadilla came with a small side salad and green sauce. The green sauce was spicy but delicious and added flavor to the meal. Well, my quesadilla was PACKED with pork and was actually super good. I will say that I was surprised, but pleased. Steve ordered a torta that looked AMAZING and I will definitely be heading to the Westbank location soon in order to try one of those.  TS is good, but I wouldn't go out of my way. Perfect if you are in the area bar hopping or staying at a nearby hotel, though.

This place is a Tex-Mex lovers dream!  I want to start by saying that this place is listed as a buffet, but the food is served cafeteria style, so it doesn't come into contact with the public. This place is clean and buffets are freaking disgusting.  With that being said, David had heard that this place is owned by the same people who used to own the famed Pancho's in Metairie. Basically, it's an all you can eat Mexican food extravaganza. For $12, you can stuff yourself silly with everything from tacos, tostadas, flautas, taquitos, tamales, enchiladas, rice, beans and MUCH more. The best part is that once you have hit the line, you can turn the light on on your table and the waiter or waitress will come by and you can let them know if you want more, and they will get it for you.  I got a chicken taco, two tamales, a flauta and rice and beans. The food was excellent and I'm thrilled to report that it was all super fresh. When I was in line, I was impressed when they replaced the container of refried beans, that was only half empty, with a new full container of fresh beans.  I loved everything here and I might have overdone it a little bit. And yes, they have the sopapillas with the honey. My only regret is that I didn't discover this place sooner, as I can already tell we're probably going to be dropping in here at least once a month for the good stuff.

OH MY GAH!  This place is girl heaven.  Everything sparkly as far as the eye can see.  Rhinestone covered rings, bracelets, earrings, necklaces and headbands!  They have so much unique stuff.  One thing that caught my eye was a rhinestone covered snake bracelet.  It was the most unusual thing I had ever seen, and if I had any idea of where I could wear it, I would have bought it on the spot.  They have really unique necklaces with pendants from musical instruments to owls to frogs to turtles.  They have a HUGE selection of earrings.  I took a pic of the earring wall.  Check it out, because right after I took it, the owner told me that was a "no no".  I will definitely be going back, ready to spend some money.  I was so caught off guard by this fantastic shop mixed in with bars and crappy souvenir shops that I was not ready to shop.  LOL.

I was in the neighborhood, so I decided to pop my head in here and see what it was all about.  The first thing that struck me was how friendly everyone was. I was greeted as soon as I walked in and one of the men working came right over and very kindly asked me if I was looking for anything specific or if he could help me with anything. This is a really nice grocery store and, although it's small, they have a nice selection of things. They have fresh fruit and vegetables, and extensive dessert case, sandwiches, a hot food bar and much more. They even have an oyster bar, but I don't think that it was operational on the day that I was here. Prices are fair for the area and the products are "good" brands (does that make sense?).   I really like that the market has a big parking lot (in the back) which makes access to and from the market a breeze. As I said before, the staff was beyond friendly and welcoming- more than any other grocery store I've ever been to. This is a nice addition to the neighborhood and worth checking out.

When it comes to coffee shops and stands, I'm usually not much of a Starbucks type of person. It's nothing personal. The coffee is decent, but I just prefer to support local coffee shops.  On a recent mall outing, I was in the mood for some iced coffee and my choices were a long line at Cafe du Monde or no line at Starbucks. I guess I'm an easy mark: no line wins over line every time, no matter what. This isn't a full on Starbucks shop, although they offer everything you would find at a regular Starbucks. It's pretty much a coffee stand in the middle of the mall. The man working was really friendly and the iced coffee I got was good and decently priced. I'm sure an iced coffee with 2% milk was the most "normal" order he had heard all day.  The cool thing about this stand is there are plenty of sofas and chairs, in case you want to lounge around and enjoy your coffee and take a break from the rest of the mall madness.

I first visited The Grill Room for my 21st birthday. I don't remember much about that experience, as I wasn't the food/restaurant lover that I am now. I was excited to return for a Coolinary lunch.  Everything about The Grill Room is elegant: people dressing up for lunch, the white table cloths, the view, the wait staff- perfect. They opened their doors right at 11:30 and since we had a reservation we were seated immediately. Make a reservation because when we called, 11:30 was the only reservation left, which was fine by us.  We were seated by a window that was facing the city on a cozy rainy afternoon. We started with cocktails as we decided what we wanted. Jason was our waiter and he was on top of everything and so friendly! His expertise added to the entire experience.  I got the grilled redfish almondine, roasted brussels sprouts, roasted tomato soup and mac and cheese.  Grilled redfish almondine- so tasty! It was a small portion, but it had a lot of flavor and I loved that they left the skin on in order to keep it juicy.  Roasted brussels sprouts- I love brussels sprouts and they way they were done here was perfection. I have to figure out how they make the outside crispy, but keep the inside nice and tender. I think some sort of butter sauce was involved as well. It was out of this world.  Roasted tomato soup- This was my favorite!! Yes, I loved this more than the mac and cheese, believe it or not. Delicious without being too rich or heavy and full of fresh flavors- this is a must.  Mac and cheese- Aahh! Tons of cheese mixed in with penne pasta! Sign me up. This dish was super rich and I was only a few bites in before I had to ask for a box. They didn't hold back on the cheese at all- it was melted all over and then baked on top.  For dessert we had the sorbet. How can I describe this? Refreshing, cool, light and the perfect end to a wonderful lunch.  I have to agree with Charles when he said that this is probably one of the best lunch deals in town. Even when it isn't Coolinary, you can get this deal with the Windsor Court Plate lunch Monday through Saturday. You must go if you have yet to experience The Grill Room.

A theatre attached to the well known Royal Sonesta hotel,  Friday's the Jazz Playhouse hosts free Burlesque shows at midnight with an accompanying live band.  Organized by local Burlesque star, Trixie Minx, the venue features what I would call "old school" Burlesque.  Local burlesque stars dancing to a live jazz band.  The cozy atmosphere provides an especially intimate experience.  The drinks aren't the cheapest, but they are reasonable by Bourbon Street standards.  A great place to escape into another time.

I had no idea what to expect from Green Goddess when a friend told me that we had to try this place. After a decent walk through the quarter and after being led down an alley, we were here. Oh...we're sitting outside? Great. I'll admit, I'm a complete priss who doesn't like to be hot, so when I saw that all of the seating was outside and it was the middle of July, my heart leaped into my throat. The good news is- there was a nice breeze and after a while I didn't notice the heat. I swear I'm not lying.  There are so many goodies on the menu, we just decided to order a bunch of things and munch. First we got the pate that came with toast rounds. The pate was wonderful! It was nice and rich, of course, but what I liked most about it was that it was whipped and this made it really easy to spread on the rounds.  Next we got the boudin and duck sausage plate. This was served with pickles, bread and mustard. The boudin was so good. It was tender and juicy with a lot of flavor. The duck sausage was quite tasty, especially when it was dipped in the mustard. Then we got the shredded duck which came on a bed of greens with potatoes and bacon wrapped dates. I think this was my favorite of the whole meal. I really could have eaten an entire plate of those dates and the potatoes were cooked perfectly. The duck was really good as well and I liked that it was served on top of a little salad.  Finally, it was time for dessert and we ordered the praline bacon ice cream sundae that came topped with black sea salt. WOW. The flavors on this thing were out of this world. The bacon and salt added the perfect compliment to the sweet of the ice cream. It was a delicious combination, and definitely enough to make me want to go back and get this again.  All in all, I liked my meal here. I'd love to go back, but I will probably wait for autumn to do so.

This is my first ever time at any Hooters, so bear with me!  Not a bad place, if you are craving junk food.  Nothing here is good for you and most of it is fried.  It like the boobs: all filler and nothing of substance.  Ha.  But I digress.  The fried pickles are pretty good.  Although, they come with a weird sauce which is unidentifiable and mysterious and I suspect it's a weird combo of mayo and ketchup.  Instead, I asked for ranch on the side and it cost me 65 cents.  Um... really?  We're charging for ranch?  The waitress was super nice and attentive.  I guess I would go back... for the pickles, but that's about it.

I rarely eat Wendy's and I rarely review fast food places, because if you've been to one you've been to them all, however, this one needed a review.  This is the one Wendy's where I can go where they don't mess up my order, they are fast and the staff is friendly.  I always do drive thru and I never have to wait more than just a few minutes for my food.  Even during lunch they aren't packed.  Awesome.

This is a really nice store with a good selection of tops and dresses that i liked. I'm on the hunt for vacation clothes and I was able to find a nice top that is just perfect for my needs. The staff was above and beyond friendly and helpful and I was in and out in no time. I only wish that I had discovered this shop sooner.  Note: the sizing differs between different items, so be sure to try on anything before you by it. Don't just go by size.

It's pretty embarrassing that I have lived in New Orleans my entire life and I only just managed to make it over to the Prytania Theatre. Just keep that little detail between us, okay?  This is such a fantastic theater. It's been around forever so it has that really nice "old school" kind of feel. It's a single screen theater, so be sure to check the website for movie times and don't show up just expecting to see the latest releases whenever you want.  I really like that they show a lot of old movies here. I just got to see "Purple Rain" on the big screen. Not only is this one of my favorite movies of all time (how can you not love how 80's this movie is? Prince wore lace gloves and half of the audience watching The Revolution perform had feathered hair.), but because everyone in the theater had already seen the movie, people were encouraged to sing along and interject their (hilarious) commentary. It was a fantastic time. Oh! And you can BYOB for the weekend shows (and maybe during the week, but I'm not positive)! How cool is that?  The theater is really nice and it even has a balcony, if you want a different kind of experience. The concession stand sells all of the usual popcorn and candy treats and all summer they will be showing kids movies in the mornings.   Keep an eye on the schedule and get down to the Prytania asap for an awesome time!

Everybody knows that it can be scary when a pet is sick.  Recently, my cat was having serious stomach issues. He wasn't eating and he was losing weight. I took him into Dr. Addison and she was quick to pinpoint the problem. First she gave me some medicine to give to him and when that didn't work she came up with another solution that helped my cat immediately.  Dr. Addison specializes in feline care and because of this she is quite knowledgeable about anything that might be bothering your cat. She is also good about follow ups. I brought my cat back in for a follow up checkup and she even called me to make sure that he was feeling better.  I wouldn't hesitate to bring any of my cats back to Aurora.

Although I am still a huge fan of the muffulettas here, I just had to update after getting the shrimp platter this past Friday. It's kind of a cosmic joke here in New Orleans: during Lent, we Catholics aren't allowed to eat meat, so we have to "settle" for delicious fried seafood. We came here for that very reason.   My boyfriend had told me how great the fish and shrimp platters are, so I was down to see what it was all about. I got the shrimp platter (butterfly) with two sides- french fries and red beans. The platter was about $14 and I thought that price was decent- and then the food came out. WOW. The butterfly shrimp are HUGE and plentiful! They were perfectly fried and very tasty. I loved the fries- they had the perfect amount of "crisp" to them and the red beans were out of this world good. I only had to add a little bit of hot sauce to give it that "kick" that i like.  The shrimp platter was well worth the price (especially since you get your choice of two sides), and I would get it again.

It was one of those nights where Mimi's started to get crowded, so we headed across the street to this place. I had never been before, and there weren't many people here when the bartender introduced himself- I think his name was Steve.  We chatted briefly with a nice couple that was sitting at the bar. They explained that they were neighborhood regulars and raved about what a great place it was. I had to agree- they had good music on the speakers and everyone was having a good time.  There wasn't much else going on this particular night. We all just sat around and talked and had a good time. I'd return.

This is the way a shoe store is supposed to be! Everything is neatly organized and the staff asks if you need help as soon as you walk in.  Although I didn't find the exact kind of shoes I was looking for, they were having a big sale on the day I was here, so I picked up some cute pumps at a good price. Prices are pretty moderate and are a little more expensive than Payless or other "discount" shoe stores, but not as expensive as some department store name brands. The shoes are organized by style and are easy to find and navigate.

I'm not gonna lie. The first time I went to this place, it looked like sketch ville USA. I was a little weary of this little Magazine St. market, but my friend told me that the food is really good, so I decided to give it the benefit of the doubt.  They have a lot of "take out" type of food and I decided that the hot sausage po boy was as good as anything to try. For just under $10, it was a real deal for the size. After I got it home, I was blown away at how good it was! It was packed with sausage and had a lot of flavor. It ALMOST tasted as if I had ordered it from a real po boy place.  I highly recommend this weird little convenience store that makes good sandwiches.

This is one of the better antique/vintage style stores in the Quarter. I really like this place, because they have a little bit of everything.  When I stopped in here I was able to pick up a few costume pieces for a friend's party. The staff is really nice and helpful, especially if you are looking for something specific. As others have said there really isn't much organization to the place, so take your time and work your way through the store. Being here feels a little like being in your grandma's attic, so nothing is organized.  The vintage clothes that they have here do tend to be a little dingy at times, but I find you can clean them up with a good wash. The dress I bought was a little musty, but it was much better once I threw it in the washer and was well worth the less than $20 I paid for it.  Le Garage also has a nice selection of lamps, furniture, knick knacks and other things you can use to decorate your space. This place is a dream for anyone who wants to be a little more creative with their decor.

Since I usually go to the *other* Surrey's and it's usually packed, I decided to check this one out instead. Although there was a wait, we didn't wait for nearly as long and the "half hour" estimate they gave us turned out to be only 10 minutes.  We were seated inside and we were waited on and served pretty quickly, because they are eager to get people in and out on a busy Sunday. Of course, I got my favorite- shrimp and grits. I am not lying when I say that the shrimp and grits here might be my favorite in the city. They are just so perfectly creamy and good, and the croutons and bacon that the dish comes with are a perfect touch. I finished the entire bowl of this delicious goodness and I am excited to go back for more. I think I would eat this for breakfast every day, if I could. Let's just say it's good that I don't live closer to Surrey's.  Just a note: they didn't have the AC on when we went, so it was quite warm. Just be aware of that if you decide to eat here during the summer.

Ummmmm am I missing something?  My dad and I stopped in here today for lunch. I was expecting fireworks but instead I got a big disappointment. We got here at around 1 and the place had a good crowd. At first we were seated inside, but had to move to the outdoor patio because it was freezing cold inside- not a huge deal. We both ordered the soup of the day to start and my dad got the stuffed crab dinner and I got the fried oyster dinner.  The soup of the day was brie and shrimp soup which was excellent. My entree came with a salad that was basically just lettuce and tomato, but it was okay. My oysters were really puny and there weren't very many of them. The fries were pretty good, but for $23 I was expecting  A LOT better. My dad was underwhelmed with his stuffed crab and said that it was more breading than crab.  The Galley would have been a 4 star experience if the prices weren't so out of this world. I just think a fried oyster platter with a few small oysters just isn't worth $23. I understand the idea of "market price", but I left lunch feeling as if I had been ripped off and I really don't like that feeling.  Maybe I should have just gotten some boiled seafood or the soft shell crab poboy they are famous for, but next time want a fried oyster plate I will skip this spot and just go to Fury's.

I don't even know what a "hipster haven" is, so when someone mentioned that this is what Saturn Bar is, I was pretty clueless. I'm still not even sure what the definition of a hipster is, but I digress.  I have been here a few times for the dance parties that they have. They are always a lot of fun and DJ Matty has really good taste in songs and always plays stuff that gets the crowd excited. This is just one of those places I don't frequent very often, because I will only go with a group of people and never by myself and it's hard to find people who want to come here and just dance.  The bathrooms are pretty rough, but the dance floor is spacious and the upstairs area is neat for getting a little space to yourself and just observing the crowd. The staff here is always friendly and the people who hang out here are pretty cool.

This might be one of the best lunch specials in town, if you are willing to make the drive.  My dad and I stopped in here for a Friday lunch, after I had heard raves about it. The cafe itself is kind of hidden in the back of the terminal, but once we found it we were seated immediately. The first thing I really liked about the place was the amazing view of the tarmac (?) where all of the planes were coming and going. I'm just going to pretend I own a private plane and I was just grabbing lunch before jetting off to somewhere exotic in one of those adorable puddle jumpers.  On Fridays, the blue plate special is catfish served with cole slaw and french fries, so I decided to go with that. I also got a side of mac and cheese, because I have to test the mac and cheese wherever it happens to be available. The food came and I was blown away by how much they gave me- two big pieces of catfish, cole slaw and lots of fries all for $10. The catfish was really good and crispy, just how I like it. The cole slaw was excellent and the fries, more like potato circles, were crispy and yummy as well. The mac and cheese was just okay. It was penne pasta with cheese on it and, while I could tell it was made fresh, I wasn't blown away by it.  They have lunch specials every day Tuesday through Friday and they are all $10 and range from pork chops to meatloaf. Like I said, I am pretty sure this is one of the best lunch deals in town and I'd love to go back and try another one of their specials.

This isn't the most sophisticated store and yes, a lot of the clothing is geared for a crowd that is a bit younger than myself, but there is a time and a place for some of the things sold here.  The best thing about Rue 21 is that the clothes are cute and they are affordable. I don't go here and buy mini-dresses or anything like that, but today they were having a sale so I scooped up some "thin" t shirts to wear now that the heat is out in full force.   Rue 21 is pretty much a rip off of Forever 21 which itself is a rip off of H&M and they sell the same type of clothes that you probably shouldn't expect to last a lifetime. If you need a cute outfit or top for a cheap price, this is the place.

I was leaving a meeting at the Zeitgeist when this cute little shop caught my eye with their items on the sidewalk. I love a thrift store so, of course, I stopped in.  I was immediately greeted by a man working here, whom I believe was the shop owner. He was really friendly and made me feel welcome and I couldn't wait to start exploring. The shop is small, but they have a nice selection of items here for both men and women, both casual and a little "fancy". I was also impressed by their wide selection of shoes that look as if they have barely been worn. Everything is fairly priced and very affordable.  I didn't get anything on this day, because I was in a bit of a rush and didn't take the time to search the racks properly, but this shop is definitely on my radar and I'll be back soon.

I was actually on my way to grab lunch somewhere else when Mona's caught my eye like a beacon in the night. I quickly turned around and found myself here in a fairly empty restaurant at around 2 pm on a weekday.  I sat down and the waiter (owner?) came over quickly to take care of me. I knew exactly what I wanted, so I got the beef shawarma which came with salad and hummus. I have been to Mona's other location before and I always enjoy their beef shawarma plate. The hummus is always delicious and the salad is nice and fresh- this location was no different. I also enjoyed a mint tea with my meal, which was quite tasty. Because I was one of only two customers here, service was fast and efficient. I did notice that they tend to do a big take out business, so keep that in mind if you live or work in the area.  I enjoyed my experience here and I will return.

SO. MUCH. COLOR!  Walking into Terrance Osborne's gallery is like walking in to the middle of a Technicolor movie right out of the 1940's! All the color is why I have been a fan of Terrance's for years and I was so excited when I found out that he was opening a gallery on Magazine Street. When you walk in, you are surrounded by Terrance's unique works and life size paintings. My favorite thing about Terrance's art is how well he captures the culture of New Orleans and Louisiana in his work. Terrance and his wife Stephanie completely renovated the space and the light, art and details of the architecture come together perfectly in the space. The gallery is a "must see" for any art lover, and if you have the funds, you can purchase one of the paintings that would look good on any wall.

Considering how close I live to this place, you would think I went more often. Alas, this was my first visit.  I brought a coat in here to get cleaned and they did a good job. It was ready in a few days and as good as new. At $16 they are a little more expensive than other cleaners but considering I got the coat back fairly quickly, and didn't have any issues, I would say it's worth it.  Next time I will bring something here to be altered and I will re-review.

Swap is one of my favorite consignment shops in town. They have a fabulous selection of designer (and not so designer) clothing and accessories and prices are wide ranging. A lot of what they have here is practically new and super affordable. I have been on the hunt for the "perfect" light summer dress and I found it here. Not only was the dress like new, but it was fairly inexpensive. even though it was a "name" brand. The staff is friendly and will help you find anything you need and there is a nice selection of shoes and hand bags as well, to complete the outfit.

I'm gonna start by saying that Cowbell has beer now, and will have liquor soon, because they just got their license.  Those of you of were all up in arms about your lack of booze, can relax.  I swear, it was mentioned in so many reviews of this place!  Anyway, after a night of driving around, and finding that every place had a 2 hour (or more) wait, we decided to give Cowbell a try.  The first thing I noticed was the interesting decor.  It's set up in a "family" style kind of way, long tables and chairs.  Kinda like Bud's Broiler.  As an app, a girl we were with ordered the mac and cheese, so that we could all try it.  Let me tell you, it was delicious.  It was made with a white cheese and it was nice and creamy.  We all agreed that it was fantastic.  I decided to order a burger with cheddar cheese, which comes with hand cut fries.  I was really wishing that I could sub the fries out for some of that mac and cheese, but alas, substitutions aren't allowed.  The burger was delicious and cooked to "medium" perfection, just the way I like it.  Usually, I order a burger "medium" and just assume that I will get it "medium well".  I've learned to live with this.  Here, the burger was perfect and exactly how I wanted it.  I was impressed.  At the end of the meal, we decided to try out the two desserts they have: the "chocolate city" and the apple pie.  Both were fantastic, but the pie is probably the best I have ever had in a restaurant.  I would definitely go back, probably for lunch.  The place wasn't crowded at all, which was great.

Stopped in here after Krewe De Vieux, and it was packed, of course.  The bar itself is really dark, but the people seemed pretty friendly and accommodating. They have comedy shows here on a pretty regular basis. I have yet to go to one, but I would love to check it out on a night like that when the place isn't as crowded with parade goers.

On a visit here, I took it upon myself to duck in here and see what this neat little exhibit was all about. It's basically a lot of the Mardi Gras gowns that a Mardi Gras queen wore over thirty years. You can tell that a lot of care has been taken to preserve these artifacts and seeing them up close was a real treat.

Sometimes a girl just has a craving for a massive amount of pasta, and when that craving hit, I found myself at Oak Oven eating some of the best pasta I have ever had.  I knew I would be in the area, and a friend of mine lives nearby, so we made plans to grab an early-ish dinner here. Since the website suggests reservations, I made reservations about two hours before we arrived. We were seated without a hitch (and I'm glad I called ahead because the small place filled up fast).  This is a cozy little restaurant, off the beaten path and the atmosphere feels as if you are dining at a family home. Everything on the menu sounded incredible, but I had to go with the Penne Diavola which is penne and gulf shrimp, blue crab, and a spicy red sauce. I won't lie- I got the large and ate every bite with no problem. The pasta was cooked perfectly, the shrimp were nice and plump (and plentiful!) and the crab added the perfect touch. The sauce was a bit spicy-sweet and after adding parmesan, it was the perfect dinner. I coupled it with a glass of delicious red wine which put the meal over the top. Because you only live once, I also decided to get the creme brulee for dessert. Delicious custard was topped with a yummy sugary shell and it was a splendid end to the meal.  I agree with Kelley's assessment that Oak Oven is a hidden gem, and I will be going out of my way to dine here again.

I guess a lot of people are probably put off of Redfish Grill, because of it's proximity to Bourbon Street and the fact that it caters to mostly tourists, but we had heard good things about it, so we decided to have a romantic dinner here.  David made reservations, we arrived on time and waited a little bit in the bar area for our number to be called. Once we were seated, we looked over the menu- everything sounded amazing. We decided to start with an order of alligator boudin balls, which were delicious. They were packed nicely with meat and came drizzled with a pepper sauce that was really good.  For my entree I got the shrimp and grits. This is tail-off shrimp and grits mixed with a cream sauce and topped with bacon popcorn. Yes...actual popcorn. The dish was okay. It lacked spice and I should have asked for hot sauce, but I didn't. The popcorn on top was kind of weird and completely unnecessary in my opinion. Like...it was bacon popcorn but it just tasted like popcorn to me. Why was it there? The dish all in all had decent flavor, but it wasn't the best shrimp and grits I have ever had.  David had the catfish and crawfish etouffee. It looked amazing! His only complaint was that the etouffee was a little sweet. I tasted it, and he was right- it was sweet and tasted a little odd. It was still good though and if I go back, this is what I'm getting.  My experience here was pretty good and I'll return. Even though the restaurant was PACKED the food came quickly and our waitress was very attentive, which is the main reason for 4 stars.

I am so excited!! Finally a cute cafe, on the Westbank, that isn't a chain!  Someone posted about this place a week or so on facebook and after looking at the photos, I knew I had to make my way to this adorable Italian cafe. Walking in, you feel as if you are walking into a cafe that you would find in a storybook- the outside is decorated for Christmas with a large wreath on the window, a nutcracker and garland wrapped around a light pole. Inside, there is a large Christmas tree and Harry Connick Jr's Christmas album playing in the background. There are tables by the windows so that you can look out as your enjoy your treats and free wifi is available, if you have some work to do.   They offer all kinds of delicious pastries, different types of coffees and gelato! Do you know how happy I am that there is a place for gelato in Gretna? I think they might be the only place on the Westbank where you can get real gelato. Today I got a frappe and a chantilly lace cupcake. Both were delicious and I can't wait until Amore starts serving breakfast and lunch.  As I was enjoying my treat, a lot of lawyers were in and out getting coffee and shaking hands (the courthouse is right across the street). I can tell that this little spot is going to be the place to see and be seen in old Gretna. I loved my experience here and I will return.

One star??  One stinking star??  Ouch.  I mean, this place wasn't earth shatteringly great, but it was a little better than one star.  I went in and I sat in the bar area, which always means immediate service.  I decided on the chicken quesadillas.  They weren't anything special, but they were pretty good.   I mean, Chili's is a typical chain place with typical chain food.  You can't go in here expecting to have the greatest meal of your life, but it was okay for what it was.  I will say this- I was reading other reviews about slow service.  I didn't have an issue with  this because I sat at the bar, but I did notice that the bartender made a frozen margarita for someone at a table.  He placed it on the bar for the waitress to pick up, and it took about 5 minutes for her to grab it.  Half the drink was melted by the time the waitress brought it to the table.  If that drink were for me, I would have sent it back.  Just something that I noticed.

I'm gonna start this off by saying there are certain foods I consider myself some sort of an "expert" on.   I know my sushi.  I know my Mexican food.  For the most part, I know my Italian food.  One thing I am definitely not an expert on is Vietnamese food.  However, a friend of mine insisted we go here and told me that it was good, so I decided to give it a shot.  The atmosphere of the place is really nice and has a really nice "upscale" kind of feel.  For an appetizer we got some beef spring rolls.  They were really good.  I've found that spring rolls at other places don't have a ton of flavor, but the ones here were really good and I finished both of mine.  For my meal I got the wonton soup.  It came with wontons, chunks of crab and meat and those crunchy things that you put in the soup came on the side.  It was really good and the broth didn't taste as "earthy" as some other broths sometimes do.  It wasn't huge, but I think it was the perfect size for lunch.

Anyone who knows me that I love a thrift store. When I heard that a fancy Goodwill was opening in Metairie, I knew I had to check it out.  This Goodwill is nice and it pretty much does all of the work of finding the *nice* donation stuff for you, but the prices are still reasonable. I wasn't looking for anything specific, so I just checked out the dresses. I was really impressed- A LOT of the clothes still have their original tags and I saw some dresses originally marked over $50 with a Goodwill tag for under $10. Score! Some of the clothes lean more towards the "trendy" side of things, so if you are looking for something that is going to last a few years, you might have a hard time.   They have a nice assortment of dresses, tops, skirt, men's fashion, shoes and even a few household items. The selection isn't huge, but they have only been open a month, so I'm sure that will change over time. If you are looking for an outfit for a special occasion, put this on your list of places to check out.

La Nuit is a cool little venue that could be awesome with a little work.  The theatre itself is pretty old and gets hot during the summer.  The sound isn't all that great, but that's not a huge deal, as the room is really small, so I've never had trouble hearing anything.  Also, in order to get to the bar, you have to go outside into the box office area.  It makes you feel weird when you have to get up in the middle of someone's set in order to go get another drink.  I understand that there's nothing they can really do about that, but it would be nice if they had a drink area in the actual theatre or maybe a cocktail waitress, as Jess suggested.  The box office has a nice little "lounge" area that you can hang out in before the show, if you don't feel like standing outside.  This is definitely a place I will return to, especially for the right performer.  I'm glad that New Orleans has a comedy scene and there is a venue for new comics to polish their act.

I always feel weird reviewing different locations of the same chain, because I almost feel as if they are all the same.  This is good PJ's to check out if you find yourself in "da Metrys" and you want some good local coffee.

Some friends and I stopped by this place a few days ago before the Saints/Falcons game.  It's located within walking distance of the dome, so it's a big game day bar.  The place has a bar area, if you want to actually sit at the bar.  They also have tables and booths, if you want to sit there and order from the waitresses that walk around.
