Although, the place was PACKED when we went in, the drink order came really fast when we ordered and the waitress was really attentive and checked on us often.  This is a definite "must go to" place if you are heading to the game, or just looking for a fun place to hang out with fellow Saints fans.

Drive thru daiquiri shops are what makes New Orleans so unique. Nothing like getting behind the wheel and driving through a liquor shop and heading out to a party or a parade with a cup full of booze. As long as the straw isn't in it and you aren't sippin' and driving, it's completely on the "up and up" according to the law.  This particular shop used to be a bank or a loan center or something like that. David and I were heading home from a parade and I had decided I wanted a sweet treat, so we hit the drive thru. I got my usual medium Crawgator and it was perfect- just enough sweetness with just enough liquor and for only about $6. Service was fast and friendly and I enjoyed sipping my drink at home for the rest of the evening.  I find these shops are always better if you're just "passing through", rather than a place to hang out. I'd be back.

Really cool fest with good food and beer, even if one of my friends, who is actually from Germany, calls the food "Americanized German food".  This fest is always a good time with bands playing and people dancing to polka music. My favorite has to be the chicken hat that I obtained a few years ago. When you press it's foot, it plays the chicken dance. Fun for the whole family!  The beer is a little overpriced, but you get a discount if you buy a souvenir cup. I wish the fest wasn't all the way out in Rivertown, but I think that it's going to be moved back to New Orleans next year.

I happened to find myself here after stopping at Chateau Sew and Sew in search for an embroidable gift (is that a word? A gift that is able to be embroidered).   Anyway, I stopped in since this place is right next door and they have a little bit of everything here. I stopped in on Black Friday and they were having a nice little sidewalk sale with a few dresses discounted. It was mainly day dresses and casual things, nothing fancy, so that was right up my alley, I stepped in and found a really cute little shop. I was taken aback by all of the nice travel bags that they had for sale- they had a nice assortment.  One of the best finds in the whole store is the assortment of vintage records they have! First of all, the collection is HUGE and covers all genres. I'll be the first to admit that I am not really a record person, but I will be definitely directing my music loving record collecting friends to this secret music spot.  The owner of the store was really nice and friendly and she even offered me champagne while I shopped. I really liked this cute little shop and I loved that everything is made locally. I will definitely be adding this place to my list when trying to figure out what types of Christmas presents to get friends this year.

A generous three stars MAINLY because it's their first year and you gotta start somewhere. When I first heard that New Orleans was adding a Fried Chicken Festival to their already packed fest lineup I was very excited. When I heard it was going to be held at Lafayette Square I thought to myself, "Uh oh". It was then that I concocted a plan: I'll get there early, hit a bunch of booths and get out. Well, you know what they say about best laid plans.  As it turns out, a lot of people like fried chicken. Like...a lot of people. There were a lot of vendors and every line had at least a 30 minute wait by 11:30. The Willie Mae's line wrapped around the entire fest, had well over an hour wait, and had me asking, "Y'all know you can just go get the same stuff at one of their two locations, right?" Since this was the first year, it was clear they were unprepared for the crowd. I don't blame the vendors, they were just working with whatever info they were given, but some of them looked downright panicked at the lines and crowd and I wouldn't be surprised if some run out of food before the fest closes.  The lines were all long with no organization at all. Most vendors didn't have enough people working (again, not their fault really) and they seemed overwhelmed with all the people. The picture I posted of the crowd is MAYBE 20% of all the people that were there.   I was able to try two booths one served chicken tenders, boudin balls and fries for $8.50 and another served two piece chicken with mac and cheese for $7. Most booths had chicken dishes between $7 and $9 dollars. My boyfriend waited in the drink line for about 25 minutes for cold drinks and when he got to the front the drinks weren't cold because they had just put them on ice...so there's that.  This is most likely going to be a yearly event, so I have a few suggestions:  1) Have something to separate the lines. There was a lot of confusion as to who was in what line and going where.  2) Add more workers to the vendors booths. You need to have a few people frying and a few people taking orders. One booth had one person frying and one person taking/preparing orders.  3) Make separate booths for mixed drinks and soft drinks/water. The reason my boyfriend had to wait in such a long drink line was because they were mixing up boozy drinks for other people and all he wanted was water.  4) Move it a bigger area. Maybe somewhere at City Park because it was getting pretty tight at the square and I have a feeling next year there will be even more people.  From what I heard of the bands, they were good. I think I heard one band as I chomped down on my chicken. The food I did have was yummy and I just wish I had been able to try more food. I might go back next year if they change the location.

This is a neat little place if you are looking for something a little different.  I stopped in here to look for a gift for a friend who is a collector of more macabre types of things. They have a nice little collection of jewelry- necklaces, rings, bracelets and the like. Not everything is made from animal products, so if that isn't your thing, you might find something else that you like. The jewelry here is definitely more on the "artsy" side, but they did have a wide selection of items.  Aside from jewelry, there is a nice little collection of artwork and postcards, which would make perfect gifts for the friend who is into things that are a little different.

Incredibly good!  I stopped in here for a quick dinner after a photo shoot a few weeks ago, and I was excited to try this spot, as I had heard raves about how good it is. Lucky me there was no line or crowd, so I ordered the sweet plantains and the smothered Haitian greens.  The plantains were plentiful, cooked perfectly and delicious! They were so good that I almost got another order to take home to snack on later. The Haitian greens bowl was wonderful. It was tender greens served with red rice and pork shoulder. It all melded together perfectly and it was so good! For $9 it was a tasty and affordable dinner.  The woman working (the owner?) couldn't have been nicer and got my food to me fast. I would eat here again!

I don't get over to this place nearly enough, but when I do, it's always awesome.  There is just something about Igor's that is just more quaint than your average bar and grill. I like the cozy atmosphere, I like that the grill is in a corner behind the bar, I like the laundromat in the back and I love the bloody Marys and hamburgers.   Here you will find people from all walks of life and everyone is friendly and welcoming. A New Orleans classic.

I had some banking to do, and I was in the area, so I decided to kill two birds with one stone.  I was happy that there was pretty much no crowd at 2 in the afternoon and I was able to walk right up to a window, take care of what I needed to take care of and go on my way. The staff was friendly and the parking was ample. My whole experience here was as easy as a bank experience can be, so I left a satisfied customer.

Flamingo A-Go-Go is very new and I think they are still trying to figure out what they want to be. Are they a restaurant? Are they a bar? Are they a place to watch the game? Are they a funky late night hangout spot? The answer to all of these questions is, "Yes".  David and I stopped in here after Krewe du Vieux for some post-parade eats, at my insisting because I had heard good things about the place. It was a Saturday night, at around 9 or 10, and the place was pretty dead. We took a seat at the bar and looked over their beer and "flock-tail" selection. I got a beer and David got a king cake daiquri.  The first thing you're going to notice about this spot is how bright it is: the pastel colors and vivid lighting screams "1980's California" (not that I was there) and I like that they are going for a fun, chill atmosphere. The food is eclectic- they have seafood dishes, sandwiches, burgers and snacks. They had shrimp and grits on the menu, so I got that and David got a burger. The shrimp and grits was okay, if not a little bland. I added a good dousing of Crystal sauce to it to give it a little "kick". Flamingo is located close to the WW2 museum, so they might hold off on the spice so as not to offend the palate of any touristy customers, so I can appreciate that. David thought his burger was pretty good, but not the best he had ever had.  The staff is friendly and the food came out fast. They have a nice patio space that I'm sure will be a big hangout once it starts to warm up a little. Another plus is that they are open and serving food until 2am, so it's a good place to check out if you've been out late drinking and you need a bite to eat before you Uber it home.  I'll be eager to see what they have to offer once they find their legs and hit their stride. This will be a fun place to pass a good time and have a beer or a fancy drink, so I'll be sure to come back.

When I heard that Chef Alon Shaya was opening a new restaurant, named Saba (Hebrew for grandfather), I couldn't wait to try it out. I had been a big fan of Chef's other Middle Eastern restaurant, the super-popular and multiple award winning Shaya, but had shied away from it due to recent controversies involving challenges over the name and John Besh's involvement. I couldn't wait to enjoy lunch at Saba on their opening day and lend Chef Shaya all of the support.  Upon entering, Saba feels different right away. The space has been beautifully done, portraits of Alon and Emily Shaya's respective grandfathers greet you at the front door and the restaurant has a very homey and welcoming feel. When I walked in, I really felt as if I was in someone's living room. Instead of booths, there's a lounge area with tables next to a lovely bar area, more tables- big and small, in the dining room, and a private "cafe" with a table that seats 14. Huge windows let in plenty of natural light, so you don't feel as if you're "stuck" inside while enjoying lunch. There's a lovely patio area outside, that's going to be perfect for sitting and watching the world go by, on really nice days.  As far as the food goes, the menu does feel very familiar. If you have eaten at Shaya, you'll immediately recognize Saba's "mix and match" tapas plates (3 for $15 and 5 for $25) and the selection of hummus including tahini and lamb. One thing that's new, and worth being noted, is the addition of blue crab hummus served with snap peas, lemon and mint. If you have taste that's a bit more expensive, you can dig into the caviar menu which includes Ossetra, Paddlefish, and Salmon caviar. There are other offerings such as lamb kabob, octopus, Matzo Ball soup and falafel.  The food I enjoyed:  Pita and olive oil: This came complimentary to the table after we ordered. Warm, fresh, fluffy pita that melted in my mouth served with smooth olive oil. This was the perfect munch while we waited for our meal.  Brussels sprouts hummus: perfectly roasted Brussels sprouts in delicious whipped creamy hummus served with fresh out-of-the-oven pita that was still warm. The sprouts were packed with flavor and a perfect start to the meal. Honestly, I could have easily stopped here. This was a meal in itself.   Safta's fried egg plant sandwich: WHOA. Fried eggplant nestled into a pocket of pita bread. The eggplant was lightly fried and it was bathed in a delicious sauce that put it over the top. Big enough to share.   Fried oyster schnitzel sandwich: Saba's version of an oyster "po boy". Lightly fried, salty oysters packed into warm pita bread dressed with cucumber. This sandwich is a must and it's shareable!  Moroccan carrot salad: This tasty side is generous and cooked to perfection. I think there's a yogurt and feta sauce with it. Fresh, of course, and memorable, especially for a veggie dish.   Saba is open all day, and in between lunch and dinner, they have a menu full of delicious goodies to munch on, making this spot the perfect place to pop in after work to grab a drink and a quick bite at the bar. Saba will have a sister restaurant, Safta (Hebrew for grandmother), that is opening in Denver, so if you're over that way, and you like delicious Middle Eastern food, be sure to check it out.  I would absolutely dine here again. Chef Shaya greeted us when we walked in and welcomed us, and his lovely wife Emily stopped by our table, after our meal to make sure that we enjoyed everything. Service was impeccable and the staff moved like a well-oiled machine.   Understandably, immediate reservations are a bit hard to come by at the moment, but Saba is definitely worth the wait. I'll definitely be back.

Mona Lisa is a great place, if you want good Italian food in the quarter, but you want to be kind of out of the "thick" of things.  The place is small, but don't let that put you off.  The food is delicious.  I usually get the linguine alfredo (a favorite) with a glass of wine.  The staff is extremely helpful and the cozy decor makes it great for dates.  The tables are kind of small, but I like that and think it adds to the intimacy of the whole experience.  I can't wait to go back!

I am super fortunate that I haven't had to depend on cabs very often, but whenever my friends and I have used a cab we have always chosen United.   UC definitely has the best reputation of all of the cab companies in the city and they don't balk when you get in and tell them that you need to go to the Westbank. It has been years and years since I have needed a cab, but I keep United programmed in my phone at all times, just in case of an emergency.

This place is fantastic for any Mardi Gras throws and supplies that you may need.  A friend of mine was riding in a few parades this year, so we went to check this place out in order to get huge bags of beads and throws to whip at people at parades. Once you get over the heavy plastic smell that hangs in the air, this place is actually really neat.  Aside from throws, they do sell Mardi Gras decorations, as well as a few costume accessories. While I wouldn't go so far as to call this a costume store, if you are looking for one of those Mardi Gras foil wigs that people like to wear, this is the place to pick that up.

This is a new addition to an area that I've dubbed "restaurant row" in Lakeview. This is a fantastic little spot in the building that used to house Mondo and I just love the feel and atmosphere.  My dad and I stopped in here for lunch and I immediately loved the vibe: relaxed lunch with an upscale feel. I decided to start with an order of the She Crab Bisque because I do make a habit of indulging whenever I see it on a menu. It was fabulous! Tasty and rich- a great start to the meal.  For my entree I had the Shrimp Lucci, which came highly recommended by the waitress. This was shrimp tossed with mushrooms and pasta with a light buttery sauce. This was AMAZING! I loved how light it was, but it still satisfied my craving for pasta. It was the perfect lunch dish and I would order it again.  For dessert, I dug into the Tiramisu which was flavorful and decadent, without being too over the top. It made an already great lunch even better.  Everything here was fantastic and I will absolutely be back!

Finally something has moved into this space at the American Can! It has sat empty for years and I'm so happy that this little cafe has moved in.  This spot just opened, and I wanted to check it out, so I stopped in for a quick lunch on a slow afternoon. It's primarily a coffee shop that also serves some breakfast and lunch style bites and I decided to get the empanada and the chorizo egg biscuit. I also got an iced green tea.  You order at the counter and everything comes out ready to be taken out, but you can get some plates and utensils if you let them know that you're eating in.  Empanda- this was a great start. The crust was nice and flaky and the meat inside was tender. It also came with this spicy green sauce (it has a name, but I'm drawing a blank) that was the perfect touch.  Chorizo egg biscuit- WOW. This thing is HUGE and dense. The biscuit is super thick and the egg is cooked to gooey perfection. There was so much of this that ordering both this and the empanada was too much, so I took half of this sandwich home. It came warm and cooked to order. It was delicious and I think that this is the "must try" item on the menu.  They also have a wide variety of other bites such as yogurt, plain biscuits and cookies. The space is very open with plenty of seating indoors and outdoors and it all feels very new and modern. I'm sure this coffee shop will be a definite hot spot once word gets out that it's here.

I was here for an easy lunch and the place was empty except for one other table. We decided to sit in the bar area, so that we had "full service".  I was keeping it a bit light so I got the fish almondine that came with a side of steamed veggies and rice. The dish was okay. It wasn't full of flavor and it could have used a little salt, but the fish was cooked well. The veggies were great and perfectly steamed and I probably could have had a whole meal of just that. The rice was okay, but again, lacked flavor. I guess they think that if you're here and not ordering fried food then you must be on some sort of restricted diet.  The staff was nice, but the restaurant itself just lacks personality and, honestly, it's a little depressing. It's pretty dark and there weren't a lot of people around so it felt like we were all on our own. I probably wouldn't come back unless I was at the mall, starving and craving seafood.

I wasn't really familiar with this cute little Lakefront spot, but when my dad told me that he wanted to try a new seafood place for his birthday, the good reviews guided me to Sala.  It was around noon when we were here for lunch, and the place was empty except for one other table. The first thing I noticed is how big the restaurant is- it seems like a nice place to celebrate a special occasion and there's a nice "living room" area in the middle where you can just sit and enjoy happy hour drinks.  I decided to start with an order of the calamari. The serving here is huge and it's plenty enough for two people, and it comes atop a mixed salad concoction with a yummy sauce. The batter is light and not overwhelming at all, so you still get the flavor of the dish.  For the entree, my dad and I both got the drum almondine, which is lightly fried and topped with a lemon butter sauce and toasted almonds and is served with a side of brabant potatoes. This dish was outstanding! The fish was full of flavor and perfectly fried and the lemon butter sauce was out-of-this-world decadent. In fact, my dad RAVED about how good it was (he's a pretty hard sell) and said that it's one of the best dishes that he's had in years. I have to agree- you get two big pieces of fish, with a generous serving of potatoes for $23 and it's all cooked to perfection. This dish is a MUST, if you visit.  Our waitress was so sweet and I wish I had gotten her name. She was attentive and knowledgeable of the menu and made sure that we had everything that we needed. Sala is a hidden gem and I'll be back.

No small market seems to define its neighborhood more than Hank's Supermarket in the Bywater. While you might not find it listed in any tourism brochures, Hank's is a place of legend; from the locals who darken the door, to the fried chicken and daily food specials. It's served as a place of comfort for many New Orleanians for about 50 years.  Walking into Hank's, you can immediately tell it's a bit different from other corner stores. Not only is there a 24/7/365 hidden treasure of an extensive craft beer and wine selection, but you can get a hot meal whenever you want it.  New Orleans is known as a food town and the corner stores are no different. Everyone seems to have that one thing they are known for- for Hank's, it's fried chicken. My original intention was to enjoy this delicacy at home, but the smell of the 4-piece dark meat was so enticing, that I had to throw caution to the wind and sneak a few test bites in the car. The flaky crust and tender meat made for a delicious surprise, and for about $3.50 for four pieces, this might be one of the best fried chicken deals in town.  Even if it's your first time visiting Hank's, there's something about the place that feels familiar and welcoming, kind of like New Orleans itself. More than a market, it's a home away from home that has a little bit of everything you need -- whether you realize it or not.  *Portions of this review was originally written, by me, for Very Local New Orleans. Read the full story here: https://nola.verylocal.com/inspiring-songs-massive-instagram-following-delicious-chicken-hanks-supermarket-is-the-quirky-corner-store-of-the-bywater-thats-all-heart/158370/
Cute shop for a coffee fix in the Quarter. Reasonably priced with a friendly staff. The only drawback is they close mid-afternoon, but that might just be because of Covid and Ida staffing issues.

It was my first time really venturing out into *the world* when I decided to stop into St. Roch Market for lunch. I was relieved to see that they were asking customers to "mask up", so I put on my cute homemade mask and decided to see what I was in the mood for.  Selection was limited, but I was delighted to see Laksa NOLA was open serving tasty Burmese food. Looking over the menu, I knew I wanted noodles and spring rolls.  I got the Laksa Bowl with chicken and it was basically a ramen-like bowl packed with an egg, tofu, bean sprouts all swirling around in delicious broth. They also give you a special sauce on the side, if you're looking for some kick.   The spring rolls are shrimp spring rolls and they are very light and served with Laksa's special sauce. They were delicious!  The staff here was beyond friendly and did everything they could to make me feel comfortable throughout the entire process. The food was amazing and I couldn't have been happier with my experience.

Rosedale has been on my list for a while and my dad and I finally got over here for lunch after a busy afternoon of cemetery visits.  We were here around 1 on a Friday, and the place was dead except for a couple of people seated right next to us. I was immediately drawn to the cute, kitschy salt and pepper shakers and I kept trading off until I had the cutest ones for my table- things get wild when there's really no one else in the place.  Looking at the menu, I thought I knew what I was going to get: they have shrimp and grits, so I'm getting shrimp and grits. But then I looked at the ladies sitting next to me- one had the shrimp and grits and the other had the fried chicken thighs. Holy moly, those thighs looked good! It turns out the thighs come with greens and mac and cheese. That sealed the deal and I got the thighs.  When the food came out it looked amazing and I'm glad I was hungry because this was quite the lunch. The thighs were tender and crispy, the batter was perfect and the serving was generous. The greens were obviously fresh and the mac and cheese tasted like homemade. This isn't "out the box" mac and cheese, this is the real deal. All of my food was great and I will be ordering this again. My dad got the turtle soup and he enjoyed it, but he found it really spicy.  Service was impeccable from start to finish and Rosedale certainly lived up to the "hype". I'll be back.

Park Island Brew is great! I love the cozy vibe of the inside and I love that there's nice seating on the boulevard outside, under the trees. When I stopped in, I just got a regular iced coffee, but I know that they do all kinds of specialty drinks including milkshakes. The staff is super friendly and everyone is being Covid safe, so I felt good about spending a little time here. If you're looking for a neighborhood coffee joint, this is the spot.  I wrote about this spot for Mid-City Messenger! Read that article here: https://midcitymessenger.com/2021/01/27/park-island-brew-opens-during-pandemic-because-people-needed-a-place-to-go/

This was such an amazing experience on so many levels!  I had been wanting to try this place out when I finally made it here on a date. I was excited to dress up and have a nice night trying something new. The decor here is lovely and, because we made reservations, we were seated immediately.  We knew that we were going to start with the raw oysters as soon as we spotted them on the menu. They were so good- big, juicy and delicious. Next we tried the crispy grits which was topped with country ham. This was SO GOOD! It was unique in that it was a grit cake and it was just fantastic. It had a lot of flavor and it was definitely something unique and perfect for a starter.  For my entree, I got the smoked trout. This was delicious flaky trout that was topped with an assortment of fresh greens. It was a good size serving and I really enjoyed the dish. It was tasty and light and perfect for a spring evening.  Kenton's was fantastic and I can't wait to go back. The staff is attentive and I would say that this is a perfect place for a date and/or a nice evening out.

Krewe of Chaos, you suck.  Seriously.  You are the meat in the sandwich of two awesome parades... Babylon and Muses, and you can't manage to throw anything good?  Come on!  In Babylon, I was so weighed down with throws, I had to drop them off in my car before the next parade.  Out of all of your floats, I got 5 pairs of beads.  FIVE!  Talk about lame.  Members of your crew seemed more intent with drinking than with throwing and when the float would stop, they would just stand there drinking their Bud Light and not throwing anything.  What gives?  PLEASE fix this before next year!  Uptown people want throws and you are the opening act for MUSES!  Act like it!

I was in Metairie, when a craving for shawarma hit, so I stopped in here for lunch.  First of all, be aware that the parking lot is a tight fit and construction in the area is a mess.  I was seated right away and decided to start off with the "Hummus and more" hummus, which came loaded with garlic, and all kinds of other goodies. It was fantastic! My entree was beef shawarma with more hummus and rice. The meat was tender and the food was good.  My one complaint is service was slow, even though there was really no one there. Not a big deal, but this might not be the best place to visit, if you're in a rush.

Know by most locals simply as "13" this is a place for late night food.  When I went, it was after a long night of showing friends of friends around town.  The staff is questionable, at best and the food, for my taste, wasn't anything special.  I think I had a burger.  I know that locals rave about this place, and for bar food it isn't bad, but I would have to be talked into going here again.

Not sure why there's so much hate for this Domino's.  This is a newer location and I like it because pickup is super convenient. You order on the app and they have a drive-thru where you can just go and get it. No getting out of the car or anything.  This was the first time I had Domino's in a really long time and I was pretty impressed with it. Sure, it's not as good as restaurant pizza, but it's better than other fast food pizzas and it satisfies the craving.

I know.  I know.  Reviewing a fast food place.  How boring.  Well, this Taco Bell has replaced the one on Manhattan as my "go to".  I had abandoned it after years of patronage, because there was always a line that lead to a 20+ minute wait for just a few tacos and frankly, it was hardly worth it.    The last few times I went there was actually no line (I guess bad news for them, but whatevs) and the service was really nice and friendly.  My order is always right and I always leave with a bag full of yum.  I think that that people caught on to the one on Manhattan never having a line, and started crowding over at that one, leaving this one empty.  Fine by me!

After hearing all kinds of raves about Cosimo's, I figured it was time to check it out.  This is a nice little neighborhood bar that is far away from the hustle and bustle of the quarter. It's a friendly place where everyone seems to know everyone. We didn't stay a really long time, but I was able to try a bloody Mary and it was just as good as Joi had described.  I like that it's a little darker here. I have an appreciation for darker, cozier bars.

What a friendly staff! This review is actually long overdue because they took care of a framing need of mine over a year ago.  I had a print that I needed matted and framed. After shopping around and deciding exactly what I wanted I needed, I ended up here. It wasn't really a difficult frame job: I needed an 8 x 10 photo matted into a 11 x 14 frame. After picking the exact frame and matting that I needed, the staff was quick in helping me put it all together. I actually think that you can just buy the frame and mat and do it yourself, but I like to leave this kind of thing to professionals. The result was a perfectly framed picture that I now have hanging on my wall.    Sterling also sells a wide variety of unique prints, especially "Louisiana themed" prints such as pictures of birds, swamps and water scenes. Any of the lovely prints sold here would make a great gift.

I had been wanting to try Rum House for a while, and tonight I had the chance.  When I walked in, I was shocked at how packed the place was.  This was obviously a secret I was last to find out about.  I sat at the bar and I started with a margarita.  It was so good and perfect with salt.  I then ordeedr a cuban sandwich for my meal.  Now, I'm super picky when it comes to Cubans, but this one was delicious.  Fantastic ham and cheese pressed into bread.  It was so good.  It came with sweet potato chips (which I have never had) and that were so good. On top of that, my dinner was only $10!   I was so happy with my whole meal, and I ended up taking half of it home. See picture!  I can't wait to go back to Rum House with some friends.  It's so good, there is bound to be something for everyone here.

Update! Update!  Okay, so if you read my previous review for the Fried Chicken Festival, you know that it was a real mess last year. This year was SO MUCH BETTER! Barely any lines, lots of space and yummy chicken made for a great time!   The fest was moved to Woldenberg Park and what a difference it made! It wasn't cramped and there was plenty of space to wander around and we got to enjoy our chicken while sitting by the river. Vendors were on top of their game this year and lines moved fast. I was so excited to see some new booths out there and more space meant there were more stages and even food trucks!  If you're considering hitting up this fest, DO IT.

I went to this Zea's today for lunch,  Because my last two experiences weren't that great, I was kind of nervous.  Although the place was crowded, I was seated quickly.  I got the catfish strips with hush puppies.  It came with a choice of two sides, so I got broccoli and corn grits.  The food came quickly, which was impressive, because literally every table in the place was full.  The catfish was great.  It was very lightly battered and the strips were a great size.  The portions were big, which is always a good thing, when you are spending $11 for lunch.  The place wasn't noisy at all and the waiter was very attentive, even though he was swamped with tables.  This was a MUCH better experience than the last two times I was at Zea's.  I would definitely return to this location.

Far away from the majesty that is some of the "nicer" places of rest in New Orleans, lies Holt Cemetery.  A bit of history: Holt is where the poor of the city were (and in some cases still are) buried.  There aren't many (if any) above ground tombs and Holt remains one of the exclusively "in ground" burial sites in the city.    Walking through the grounds, you are immediately overwhelmed with sadness, mainly because the graves themselves are mostly handmade, falling apart and old.  You get a  personal and intimate feeling when you are looking at them.  Dates are handwritten and headstones are made out of various household materials such as plywood and even plastic.  It's a real testament to all the types of people that live within our city.  The fact that you can walk a few blocks and see some of the most gorgeous places of rest you will ever see and then come here and see the opposite, really speaks to you.

Hi Ho is okay. It's one of the "dirtier" bars/clubs on a street that is already pretty filthy.  I've been in here a few times over the years, but most recently I was here for DJ Soul Sister's  dance party, that once used to reside at Mimi's. If you remember how packed the upstairs of Mimi's used to get, multiply that by about 20 and you'll get an idea of what we are dealing with here.   First of all, on this particular night, the entire place was dark except for the bar. That in and off itself, made me a little nervous. The place was absolutely packed, which I wouldn't have had an issue with, but when people start drinking, they tend to not watch where they are stepping. I hung out by the bar for as long as a could and then finally decided to bail.  I should also mention, that the ladies room was out of order and only one bathroom was working. Needless to say, I decided against using the men's room.   In the past, I have seen bands and burlesque shows here that were a lot less hectic, so I might go back for something like that.

For years I have heard people rave about August. I even had some friends invite me to lunch here a few times. I always declined- I knew that if I was going to do August it would have to be dinner and a lunch just wouldn't cut it. I was determined to dine at August the right way- dinner with all of the bells and whistles.  I finally got my opportunity this year for my birthday. First of all, I goofed because I waited until two weeks before to make reservations leaving my only dining options for 6pm or 9pm. I chose the 6pm slot, and it worked out, but don't be like me- plan ahead.  I love that there is FREE parking across the street which probably means I will be dining here more often, if only for the parking convenience. We were greeted when we walked in and seated immediately at a small cozy table in a side room. As we were looking over the menu we were presented with a small amuse bouche in an egg. I won't bore you with the details, but it was quite enjoyable.  Because I had done my research, I decided to start with the potato crusted oysters. I am happy to report that they completely lived up to the hype. Lightly battered and fried oysters that had so much flavor. I couldn't get over how juicy they were, even though they were fried and I think that this dish completely ruined other fried oysters for me. I really could have gotten two plates of this and left happy. However, that might be frowned upon.  For my entree, I got the flounder which was also lightly fried and topped with shrimp and crab. It also had a lovely sauce that was very light and delicious. The flounder itself was nice and flaky and full of flavor. I love how the shrimp and crab complimented the flavor of the fish making for a delectable, but not too heavy, entree.  For my dessert, I chose to get the cheese plate. I know this might sound strange for a dessert choice, but I am a cheese person and I just couldn't pass up a plate of assorted cheeses served with marmalade and flat bread. Who could possibly say no to that? The cheeses were amazing and, while I am not enough of a foodie to tell you what the cheeses were exactly, I will say that I enjoyed all of them and I was more than happy with my decision to get this plate.  Because it was my birthday, and August is all about making you feel special, they brought out some candies at the end of the meal on a plate that read "Happy Birthday". It was a nice touch that sure did bring a smile to my face on such a memorable day.  I know I am echoing what others have said, but Restaurant August is a must for locals and visitors alike. Not only is it one of the nicest restaurants in New Orleans, but the food is delicious, the staff is very friendly, and the atmosphere can't be beat. Whether you are out for a romantic evening or you just want to get a nice dinner with friends or family, August should be at the top of any list.

I hadn't been here in years when a friend brought me here the other night to hang out with his pals.  This was not the Bourbon Pub that I remember. It was WAY better. I used to hang out here before Katrina. Back in those days, it was a rarity to see women here on a Saturday night and a lot of times they were given dirty looks by the regulars. I totally get it. This is a legit hang out for a lot of people and a bunch of straight women who see it as a novelty to dance with men who have no interest in them romantically can get annoying.  These days the Pub seems totally different. Not only are there a bunch of people of all types here, but everyone is super nice and friendly. Downstairs is a mingling area with a main bar and tables. Upstairs has a huge dance floor, a bar and a balcony. I noticed that there were a bunch of straight women and straight couples here. It was nice to be in a place where everyone is welcome and everyone can have a good time. Drinks are a little expensive, but that is to be expected in the quarter.  Note: $15 minimum on all tabs (which is equal to 2 beers and a tip).

I've been to this bar a few times. It isn't too bad, considering it's a quarter bar. It's full of neighborhood locals who have clearly grown tired of the French Quarter tourists and their foolishness (who can blame them?) but are friendly nonetheless.  I have to agree with Lindsay and say that the music here is really good and I did really have a pretty good time. I probably wouldn't go out of my way to visit this place, but if I were to find myself in the area, and I don't feel like venturing into a tourist bar, I will probably stop in here.

I am so glad that Bayou Bar is back!!  This is my type of place: a nice cocktail bar where you can enjoy a good vibe and listen to good music. We were here on Saturday night and the place was jumping! This is a perfect date spot because it had a really romantic "old school" vibe. On the night we were here there was a gentleman on the piano playing requests (a lot of Elvis, Sinatra and other classics like that). Being in this bar is like stepping back in time- I was all dressed up and I felt like I was in a music bar in the 50's. It was perfect.

While not as nice as City Park, this isn't a bad little place.  It's located close to the zoo, so you can go for a stroll when the weather is nice.  There is a super fancy golf course, if that's your thing.  I probably wouldn't go out of my way to visit, but I would definitely love it if Audubon Park was in my neighborhood.  While there, I saw a nice family having a picnic and it seems like the perfect place for something like that.

This is an adorable shop that is perfect for the NOLA lover in your life.  I was here getting some Christmas gift ideas (8 weeks, y'all) and I found a lot of options. Not only do they have brightly colored ties and belts, for the man in your life, but they have cute necklaces that are stamped with NOLA neighborhoods, so you can represent where you're from. They also have glassware that is etched with streetcars, for a subtle nod to the city without being obnoxious. They also carry locally made makeup bags and other New Orleans themed gifts.  The woman working was extremely friendly and filled me in about all of the items I was looking at and I will be sure to return when I officially start my holiday shopping.

Whoa. Okay, I just ate here for lunch today and I couldn't wait- I had to review ASAP.  So, I had tried Blue Oak ages and ages ago when it was at Chickie Wah Wah. This was in my baby Yelp days and I wasn't even sure of the name of the place that produced this delicious BBQ (at the time). Fast forward to today when I was determined to get back to Blue Oak and try it again.  We stopped in a little before 2 and there was still a good lunch crowd and a line, so we hopped in and looked over the menu. Super bummer: they were out of brisket, but yay, there's a meatloaf sandwich on the menu today, so my buddy got that. I got the pulled pork sandwich and garlic mac and cheese because I am predictable. After a short wait, the food arrived and the waitress told my friend that the meat loaf sandwich he got is the best thing on the menu. No comment was made about my pulled pork. haha  ANYWAY, the pulled pork sandwich comes topped with pickles and cole slaw. I don't want to go telling any tales, but I think I might prefer Blue Oak's pulled pork over The Joint's- it was smokey and so full of flavor. I added a touch of sauce and it really made it pop. And the mac and cheese...um...GOOD LORD. This is some of the best mac and cheese I have ever had- it was garlicky and gooey and perfect. The entire meal was mind blowing and it made for the perfect lunch.  I would be interested in hearing what other fans of The Joint think about the food here. I think it is REALLY close to being better, y'all. I will have to try it again to make a final decision and then again just to be on the safe side...for research.

I stopped in here for a quick cup of iced coffee, since I happened to be in the area. The shop is small and very quaint and the woman working was nice and welcoming and happy to make chit chat with the customers.  I love the atmosphere here. You almost feel as if you are in someone's house and the weather was nice on the day I was here, so the door was open. My iced coffee was delicious and potent. I like that you can add you own milk or cream, as I like to gauge how much I want in my coffee on a particular day. The "large" iced coffee is on the smaller side, as compared to other shops, but it's nice and strong without being overbearing or making me jittery. In other words- it was pretty perfect.

I love Cafe Degas.  A cozy little French cafe' located on Esplanade Ave.  Start with the cheese plate and go from there.  Wonderful French food.  If you like to eat rich, you can't go wrong here.  The tables are tiny and cozy and perfect for dates.  This was the first place that I ever had escargot (liked it!).  I always leave full and happy.

I love Ulta so much and this one is fantastic!  First of all, Ulta is awesome because they have everything under the sun- beauty wise. If you are a girly girl, like me, this place is heaven. This particular store is not in a mall, so it's really big and everything is nice and spread out and easy to find.  I dropped in here looking for my favorite moisturizer combo: Olay Regenerist serum and Neutrogena moisturizer with retinol. If you want a couple of my beauty secrets, there they are- I use them both together. ANYWAY, I am always sure to buy these particular two products here because they usually have a "buy one, get one half off" deal on at least one of them. You just have to make sure you stop in at the right time. Sure enough, I was able to grab them for a great price. Yeah, it's only a few dollars cheaper than a drug store, but that kind of thing adds up.  They also have a really extensive perfume section and you can sample all of the perfumes before you buy them. This is a big deal, especially for someone like me who is obsessed with body sprays and perfumes (it must be the French in me).  If you are able, skip the Westbank Ulta and get to this one ASAP, for all of your beauty needs. They are sure to have something you can use.

Honestly, I NEVER think of Rally's when I am in a fast food mood. With that said, I stopped in here a while ago. I got a pretty basic cheeseburger and fries. It wasn't too bad. The fries are always good and I think I like Rally's fries better than any other place's, but that's not enough for me to go out of my way.  Service was pretty good. They have two different drive thru lines for quick service.

Ale is a pretty cool beer spot. While I wouldn't go and call it the BEST beer bar in the city, they do a good job of representing some of the best craft beer out there.  We stopped in semi-late (11 or so) on a Saturday night and the place was slam packed. We were able to find a spot at the bar and looked over the beer menu. I got a couple of IPA's which I enjoyed. As I said, this place has a pretty good selection.  I have a few complaints: the bar is really loud- don't expect to have a conversation of any sort, if the place is at full capacity. Service is slow- this is understandable considering the crowd, but just a heads up if you are out one night and in the mood for a "quick" drink. There are a lot of tvs- like almost too many for the size of the space. I get that they want to have tvs to show games and stuff, but if there is no game on there is really no need to have a different tv movie playing on every television. I doubt anyone here was paying attention, so just turn the tvs off and let people chat.  There is seating outside, but on the night we came it was pretty cold, so we decided to just stick it out indoors. I actually plan to return on maybe a week night when it won't be so crowded to see if my experience is different. If it is, I will definitely re-review. I would also love to be able to sit out on the patio on a night when it isn't 40-something degrees.

My favorite uptown coffee spot.  They have great iced coffee, internet, and yummy (though kind of pricey) "munchies".  Great place to stop in and rest your feet during a long day of shopping on magazine.

If the fact that I scarfed a medium rainbow snowball down in about 10 minutes is any indication, this might be my favorite snowball stand on the Westbank- so far.  Located in the far back of a parking lot, Buck's serves a little bit of everything: ice cream, malts, nachos and, of course, snowballs. I decided to get my usual rainbow and the first thing I liked is that it was an actual rainbow and not just a pile of different colors that eventually turned brown. The ice was made with one of those snow wizard machines, so it was really velvety and fine. They were generous with the syrup and this was the perfect treat for a warm evening.  They have a few benches outside for sitting and the whole operation is under and over hang, so you won't get too hot.

Oh man. Now THIS is a thrift store!  After raving about the Westbank Red, White and Blue store, I was determined to check out the original the next time I found myself in Harahan. The day finally came and WHOA- this place makes the Westbank store look like a little baby thrift store. This store is huge and packed from wall to wall with all types of goodies. They are two aisles of dresses! Electronics as far as they eye can see! There were two big working telescopes for sale. Dolls! Books! Knick knacks! House wares! Cool!  I knew that this place was big, but I had no idea what I was getting into. I couldn't even shop in all of the sections I wanted to shop in because there was just too much to sort through. I did score a really pretty dress for $10, so I was pretty pleased with that purchase. Bonus points: there was a long line, but the checkout people got us all through really quickly.  This place was awesome and I can't wait to come back. I might have to start making a monthly pilgrimage out to this spot.

Dickie Brennan's...a review that I have been putting off, because how do you describe one of the best dining experiences of your life?  This place is class from beginning to end. We started with some wine in the front bar while we waited for our reservation to become available. The vibe here is very old school 50's with the bartender attending to everyone's needs without hesitation and people enjoying their happy hour cocktails and good conversation throughout the bar.  We moved on to the dining room, which is set in the "basement" part of the building. We were seated, given menus and our drink orders were taken. We started with a crab cake that came with creamed corn on the side. The crab cake was basically just crab and it was delicious- tender and tasty. The creamed corn was a perfect compliment to this dish.  Next we had a tomato and bleu cheese salad- fresh tomato and lettuce topped with crumbles of bleu cheese and a crustini of bread. I am a huge bleu cheese fan and this was a great start to my amazing experience here.   My medium-rare filet came out perfectly cooked. The meat was tender, juicy and full of flavor and every bite melted in my mouth. As sides, we split potatoes au gratin and creamed spinach. Both were prepared perfectly- the potatoes had a nice crust on top and the spinach was creamy and rich with an almost buttery flavor. The steak and sides combined together exquisitely. Last but not least, we had a soft shell crab because we just *had* to try it. The crab was fried to perfection leaving just enough "crunch" to make it enjoyable.  The Maitre D checked on us regularly throughout the meal to make sure that we were enjoying everything. He made small talk with us and he explained how Dickie's had to be completely renovated after Hurricane Katrina.  If you are a steak lover, Dickie Brennan's is a "must". This is one of the best meals I have probably ever had in New Orleans, and I have had a lot! Everything from beginning to end was an experience I will never forget and I will not only return, but I will be suggesting this place to my friends- local and tourist alike.

The Bulldog is one of my favorite places in the city and I have been going here for years.  As a girl who likes good beer, The Bulldog has a fantastic selection of both bottle and draft.  If you can think it up, it is pretty much a guarantee that this place has it.  I prefer this location over the one on Canal because it's smaller and has a more intimate feel.  I know that this might put some people off, but I love it.  It makes mingling a lot easier, and you meet new friends when you share a table with someone.  The bartenders are always attentive and go out of their way to accommodate me, even if they are busy.  Don't hesitate to ask for a sample of a new draft before you pay $5 for a pint.  They are also quick to give a good recommendation on something you might like, if you tell them what your "regular" is, and you are in the mood to experiment.  Big screens above the bar make it great for game days.  Get here early for Saints games or major sports events, because the place gets packed!  The food is good and cooked to order.  My fave is the Abita burger.   What I think I love most is that the patio is heated during cold months, so if you are one of those people who is more comfortable sitting outside, you can still have a good time.  Oh, and dogs are welcome on the patio!

I love our local PBS station.   Every once in a while I'll be bored and flipping around on the tv and I'll stumble upon a show about local New Orleans culture on PBS. They have all kinds of documentary style shows (most made in the 80s) about things like "Easter in New Orleans", "Food in New Orleans" and "The New Orleans that was" just to name a few. In fact, I think that I was watching one of these shows a few years back when I learned that Gold Brick Eggs are local (I'm a little dim, sometimes).  On Mardi Gras day I was watching a show about the history of New Orleans Mardi Gras and I was really enjoying it. Then sometime in the show they mentioned that it was originally airing in 1980! 33 years and it still held up and was fantastic! You can't beat that.  Of course, WYES also brings you national programming like kids shows and your precious Downton Abbey and Nature.

No. Just...no. Heat. Crowds of pretentious people. I just can't do it.  At one point, White Linen Night was considered the biggest social event of the summer. Somewhere along the line it became bad. Very bad. Hoards of people (many of whom know nothing about art and are just there to simply "be seen") packed onto a street sweating onto each other while drinking wine. Glamorous? I don't think so. White Linen Night has now become po boy fest minus the awesome food and fun spirit  I used to think I could do it. I used to think I could go down there and have a good time. I have never had a good time at White Linen Night. Not even once. If you are into art, that's awesome. I get that the main purpose of the night is to visit galleries that you wouldn't normally visit and maybe buy some art, but I would rather take my own day and visit said galleries when I am not fighting through a crowd of hundreds of people and sweating my makeup off.

This is a really fun spot!   My boyfriend and I were here on a Saturday afternoon just to have some fun on a lazy day. This spot is basically a bar with a driving range in the back. We hadn't eaten, so we decided to grab some lunch here before we started chipping balls (is that the term? IDK). I had a side salad and a chicken quesadilla. For a bar, the food was really good. The side salad cost about a dollar and it was basically a bowl of lettuce and tomato but, for the price, I enjoyed it. The chicken quesadilla was PACKED with big pieces of chicken and cheese and came with sour cream and red sauce on the side, in case you wanted to add it. My boyfriend had a fried shrimp poboy that was packed with shrimp and he enjoyed it. I was pretty impressed that such good food came out of a bar kitchen.  After we ate, we bought a bucket of golf balls and headed out to the driving range. It's what I imagine any other driving range to be like: you stand in the box, hit the balls and there are markers that tell you how far you hit it. Well, I have never played golf before so I was pretty terrible, but I still had a good time learning the technique and practicing my swing. I was just happy to get some air on a few swings.  This place is open until 11pm on weekends, so I imagine it is probably a lot of fun to come here with friends, have a few drinks and hit some balls out into the night. I will definitely come back.

I stopped in here to try their Blood Mary for the "Yelp's Battle of the Bloody Mary". Wow, what a cool place! This is a review of the bar area, even though they also serve food.  It was Friday night and the bar was fairly packed. I love the entire vibe of this bar: it's fancy without feeling snooty and it almost has an "old Hollywood" vibe about the place. The bartenders were super friendly and excited that we were there to try their entry in the Bloody Mary contest. Considering how busy the bartenders were, they were happy to make small talk when we ordered.  Even though we sat at the bar, I like that there is another area with tables and chairs, just in case you want to be seated away from the rest of the crowd in the bar area. I would definitely return.

Say what you want about Chick-Fil-A, at least it's consistent.  I have never been left disappointed with this place.  The staff is friendly and nice and the food is always good.  I don't get the typical "chick" sandwich.  I usually get the way unhealthier (because it's loaded with mayo) chicken salad sandwich.  It is the best chicken salad sandwich you will ever get at a fast food joint, I can guarantee you that!  Their waffle fries are also a fave, but I'm usually left wishing that they were a tad crispier.  I like to bring them home and pop them in the oven, for a bit, in order to get them the way I like them.  Minus one star for sometimes putting the cole slaw in the bag, on it's side, causing leakage.  Closed on Sundays, but I'm sure you knew that.

I always like my "milestone" reviews to be something a little special. For #1200 what better place to review than the restaurant where I spent my 33rd birthday?  For my yearly birthday dinner, I knew that I wanted to eat somewhere special. After hearing raves about GW Fins and even recommending it to people and telling them that I had HEARD it was really good, I finally got to try it for myself.  For starters- make reservations. Yes, they take walk-ins but we had a 10 minute wait even with reservations, and while we waited we heard walk-ins being told that the wait was 45 minutes to an hour. This is a very popular restaurant that gets very crowded, so just open table this thing.  We were seated in the large dining room, and our waiter Morgan came over and took our drink order and explained the specials. I had done my research, so I already knew that I was going to be starting with the shrimp and grits appetizer. This appetizer came with fully peeled shrimp, sautéed and covered in an amazing sauce. An appetizer size serving of grits was under the shrimp and sauce and mixed into the dish perfectly. This appetizer was out of this world incredible and was a perfect start to the entire experience.  For my entrée, I got the pan crusted Sheepshead. It came topped with jumbo lump crab meat and included asparagus and capers. This dish was simply amazing. The fish itself was lightly fried and it was perfectly flaky. The capers added a nice little salty touch to the dish and the asparagus was a perfect accompaniment. It was all topped with brown butter which added a richness to the food without making it too filling.  Of course, I had to get dessert. I decided on the Salty Malty ice cream pie. This was delicious salted ice cream that came on a salty pretzel crust which was then topped with caramel, whipped cream and chocolate covered pretzels. The cake was huge and I loved the mix of salty and sweet. This is a dessert that is definitely made for sharing.  My experience here was excellent. Not only was the food perfection, but the staff was amazing. Our waiter, Morgan, did a fantastic job and the entire staff here just never stops. Once your meal is completed, your dish and utensils are whisked away. Water is refilled regularly and the cocktails never stop flowing. No matter what you are celebrating, GW Fins should definitely be at the top of your list. I am so excited that I finally got to try this New Orleans institution and I can't wait until I am able to dine here again.

Dot's is a really cool place. A diner with an "old timey" 50's kind of feel complete with kitsch adorning the walls.  We walked in and decided to sit in a booth. The waitress was very friendly and told us to take our time as we decided what we wanted to order. They have pretty much everything here from breakfast combos to sandwiches and when you are as hungry as I was, everything sounds amazing. I was feeling adventurous, so I decided to get the Big Dot breakfast. This comes with two pancakes, two sausage patties, two pieces of bacon, grits, two eggs and hash browns. Yeah, it's a lot of food. It came quickly and while I didn't finish ALL of the food, I made a pretty good dent in it and only left the pancakes and toast. I guess that I wasn't in much of a "carb" mood. The food was okay, but nothing spectacular. All of the food here is made to order, so it's fresh and you can actually see the woman cooking the stuff on the griddle.  Honestly, this is a good breakfast spot if you are in the area, but it's not worth going out of your way or anything like that. I would say that it is only slightly better than IHOP. Dot's is open 24/7, so it's perfect if you need a late night meal.  If I were to go back, I think I would probably try the club sandwich because I'm a sucker for a club.

Ok, I'll admit it.  I am now totally biased into thinking that the Half Moon is an awesome place, because I fell for my boyfriend over a game of Scrabble on the patio.  Personal life aside, this is a nifty little dive.  Granted, it's not the best place for a girl to go by herself, but if you are with a group or a guy, then don't hesitate.  They have a juke box full of great music, you can play different board games here and the bartenders are really nice.

Welcome to Feelings Cafe, home of the tiniest servings in the world. Okay, not quite, but the servings were pretty small.  We got here on a Friday night and didn't have a reservation. The place was pretty packed, but we were lead upstairs and told the wait would be 30 minutes. We were seated before the bartender even had a chance to give us our drinks, so that was great.  The upstairs area is pretty dark. I would call it "cozy" if I wasn't trying to read a menu by a tiny candle, like this is the olden days. We decided to start with the chicken liver mousse, because that sounded just divine. A really generous portion came with some bread rounds. It wasn't long before the rounds were gone and I was going after the remaining mousses with my fork. Hey, all's fair in love and liver.  For my entree I decided to get the drum, which came on a bed of spinach. The food came pretty quickly, and I'm not gonna lie y'all: this was a little baby portion of drum and spinach. I KNOW that it was probably what most people would call a "fair" amount of food, but I'm HUNGRY! I like to eat! And for $17 you better give me more than just 4 or 5 (yes, I counted) bites of delicious drum! That's another thing: the food was really good! So good that I wanted more of it!  "But Marielle, the picture you posted looks like a reasonable portion." "Lay off me, I'm starving!"  I should have read the reviews; more than one person mentioned the small portions. Oh well, I guess you live and learn. I would probably go back, but I would go in knowing what to expect and I would probably stop at apps and drinks.

This is a pretty typical Michael's: they have arts and crafty things of all types. I usually buy colored markers and educational toys for kids, whenever I find myself invited to a kid's party. The games and craft things that they have for kids are not just fun, but educational as well and you are sure to find something for a child of any age.  On this particular trip I stopped in because I am currently shopping around for a Fujifilm Instax Mini 8 camera (say that 5 times fast), which is an instant film camera- basically a Polaroid camera (everything old is new again). I had heard that they carry them here, so when I found myself in the area, I decided to stop in. Well, they do have them, but they are a bit more expensive than I was seeing online elsewhere, so I decided to pass. They do also have the film for the Fujifilm Instax cameras, and a photographer friend mentioned that they frequently have film sales, so if/when I get my hands on one, no doubt this will be the place I stop for film.  Now that the holidays are here, this is a good place to stop for all of your Christmas gift decorating as they have all kinds of little fun bows, stickers and baubles you can attach to your presents to make them a bit more interesting.

This isn't a bad little hangout. If I lived in the area, I would definitely give it more stars, but since it's a little out of the way and not really worth the drive time, 3 stars it is.  This dimly lit bar caters mostly to neighborhood folks. The bar is a good size and the crowd is lively and fun. When I went, I didn't stay very long but I see that there is a nice group of regulars that hang out here. The bar was pretty smoky, but since the smoking ban kicks in on April 22nd, that's not a huge issue.  I'd come back if I were in the area, but I would go out of my way.

When I found out that Cherry coffee was getting it's very own store front I was very excited. I LOVE the Cherry located inside Stein's Deli and not only is that location still there, but this lovely location is situated right in the middle of a quaint neighborhood with plenty of convenient parking.  I stopped in today and grabbed a large iced coffee. I had some time on my hands, so I decided to sit for a while and take in the scenery. Past reviewers have done a great job of describing the fantastic atmosphere of the place. There are big windows that let in plenty of light and the space itself is large so that tables and chairs aren't squished into each other so you feel cramped.  The coffee was delicious as always. Cherry has some of the best iced coffee in New Orleans, as far as I'm concerned and I can never quite get my fill of it. This is a great addition to this quiet neighborhood and I am excited to make Cherry Espresso a regular stop whenever I find myself in the area.

Chug that coffee and wake the kids, because this is awesome Mediterranean food.  I always get the hummus for an app and I know I'm not the first to tell you that it is awesome!  Then I get the chicken or beef schwarma (sp?) and yum!  It's fantastic!  I know some people wouldn't call it "authentic", but maybe that's why I like it.  Look, I'm never going to be able to eat goat.  I just can't go there (I'm looking at you, Lebanon Cafe').  The place has a great atmosphere and is a fantastic date place.  Belly dancing on Thursdays...I think.  That might be worth looking up.  I just realized that I am long overdue for a visit back to good 'ol Byblos.  Now I'm hungry.  But not for goat.

I've been here a few times for a few different reasons.    This is basically a huge business building in the middle of the CBD. I really like the building itself, but parking is a HUGE pain. It doesn't matter how early you get down there, there is going to be zero street parking and you'll have to pay an arm and a leg to park in a lot.  The building itself is really nice. There are two levels and the second level has a nice food court and although I haven't eaten there, they seem to have a lot of food options. The place is a huge, so be sure to check the guide at the front entrance, in order to figure out where you want to go.  I've been to the hair salon that is in this building, as well as the bank. Both open out onto the street, which is convenient if you can get parking close to where you want to go.

I have passed this park so many times and I had no idea it existed until Andi reviewed it, so here we are.  This is an okay little park. There is some decent playground equipment where kids can play and have a good time. I like that some of the playground stuff has mats around it, so the little angels won't hurt themselves. It's right next to Morning Call, so it's the perfect place if you want to let your kids entertain themselves while you get a cup of coffee or a snack. With that being said, a few things could probably be improved such as the big dirt patches that have no grass on them. Also, the space is pretty small and, being to close to a busy area with cars can be dangerous. I'm not just thinking about kids running into the street, but anyone could drive up and just walk into that park with no explanation. On second thought, maybe don't leave your kids here while you get coffee at Morning Call.  It's a good play space, just keep your wits about you.

I was lucky enough be able to check out this venue for a fancy event.  The space here is lovely. This large piece of property is surrounded by lovely trees and gardens that make any event picturesque. Outside there is a seating area with a fireplace where you can take in the view. Inside there is a bar in the front and then a big room where the party happens and then there is a connected room with great light and views. On the night I was here, the entire "outside" room was illuminated and the yard area was beautifully lit. I like that the space is large enough so that you don't feel stuffed into the space.  The staff was attentive and cleared everything as needed and the bartenders were fast about keeping up with the crowd. I didn't eat much, but the food I did have was good.

While the name is unappealing, the shop itself is delightful.  Like Katie, I was drawn into this shop by the $2 record bin. Surprisingly, there were a lot of good picks here. I'm not a record collector (I have my mom's old records, but alas no player), but I have quite a few friends who are. Along with a nifty selection of $2 records, inside there is a whole box dedicated to New Orleans artists. I found some goodies from Pete Fountain, Allen Toussaint and others. They also have a nice selection of cassette tapes.  They carry a few pieces of clothing- there are some vintage concert and band shirts for sale, but the clothing is more of an afterthought to the record collection.

Wasabi is a cozy little place to eat sushi just outside of the quarter.  I didn't go and order anything out of this world, but I won't bore you.  I will say that the staff was nice and that the romantic atmosphere makes for a great date place.  You are going to pay a few extra bucks, because it's close to the quarter, and they can do that, but it's a good place to pass through, every once in a while

I really like that the Westbank has some good sushi choices: Tennou, Daiwa and I can now add Fuji Hana to the list.  The atmosphere of this place is a little "fancier" than a typical sushi place and this restaurant is extra cool because it also has a hibachi.  I didn't get the hibachi, but from what I could tell, they put on quite the show and I think that I'm going to check it out next time.  All I got when I was here was the Philly roll and the tuna roll and both were really good.  I was going to get sashimi, but it's only 3 pieces for a $6 order and I honestly didn't think that it was really worth it.  They did have an extensive list of special rolls to try, and they were the same price as a special roll that you would get at any other place.  The waitress was really attentive, friendly and helpful and even boxed my leftovers for me when I was ready to pay.  While I probably wouldn't make Fuji Hana my "go to" for Westbank sushi, it is definitely a place worth checking out.

I own a Pontiac Grand Prix, and from time to time I need to bring it here for body work.    I was recently in a fender bender and I had to bring my car in to get fixed.  I had a dented front fender, a passenger side door that wouldn't open, and paint damage.  I brought my car in on a Monday afternoon and by Friday morning it was fully repaired and ready to go.  My car is now in show room condition thanks to the great work by the guys over at Don Bohn.    I have been here many times, and I will be back if I ever need damage repair again (here's hoping I won't).

So, full disclosure: as far as local coffee goes, I think I like CC's a bit more than PJ's. Why aren't there more CC's locations?  I stopped in here for an iced coffee fix, there was no line and the cashier was really friendly and nice. My large iced coffee was tasty and I like that "large" actually means large here and you get a lot of bang for your buck. I think I paid a little over $3 for 24 ounces of iced coffee which really is a deal, especially considering you're paying the same thing at PJ's for 16 ounces. I like the coffee and service and I would return.

My quest for the most amazing hamburger in New Orleans brought me to High Hat.  I did my research, and many have called the "High Hat" burger one of the best in the city, so I had to see for myself.   I stopped in here, and I immediately liked the "retro" kind of feel of the place. There was even Motown playing over the loudspeakers. We sat down, and the friendly waitress came over to take our order. I decided to start with the chicken and andouille gumbo. It was okay, but even after I added a TON of Crystal sauce, it was lacking some flavor. Also, there was a good sized chicken bone in my gumbo. I'm glad that I'm not the type to scarf soup down, or else that could have ended badly (and this amazing review may have never been written!).  I ordered the High Hat burger with the pimento cheese on the side, as instructed by a few of my fellow reviewers. The burger was cooked perfectly "medium" as per my instructions, and topped with lettuce, tomato and house made pickles. There was a huge cup of cheese on the side (it comes melted, not sliced) and I can only imagine how much of that would have been poured all over my burger. If that's your thing, go for it. I just spread a generous amount on my burger and I found that to be perfect. The burger was juicy and had a lot of flavor and the cheese added a nice touch and an extra kick.  While I thought High Hat's burger was REALLY good, The Company Burger is still at the top of my list for "favorite" New Orleans burger, so far. I would definitely go back to High Hat and get the burger again or maybe try another one of their yummy sounding sandwiches.

I lunched with a friend here whilst finishing my Christmas shopping on Christmas Eve.  There was actually a nice little lunch crowd in the place at about 12:30, but my friend and I were able to grab table and assess the menu. We started with the pork spring rolls, and since the day was unseasonably warm, I decided to skip the pho and got the pork bún (vermicelli bowl) with egg roll instead.  The pork spring rolls were excellent. They were packed with pork, lettuce and vermicelli and really delicious. Of course, there was peanut sauce for dipping- perfect.  The pork bún did not disappoint at all. This bowl came PACKED to the brim with huge pieces of pork, lettuce, peanuts, carrots and vermicelli noodles and an egg roll on the side and there was fish sauce to mix into the dish. The pork was perfectly cooked and I loved how generous the portion was. It was perfect for lunch and definitely hit the spot. I also got a Vietnamese iced coffee and, even though it was a bit sweet, it was really good.  Just a note about some people complaining about the wait. Yes, there was a wait. It was about an hour from the time I sat down to the time i was walking out the door. I will say this: there was one woman waiting on every table in the place and clearing tables as people left. She never stopped and she was even running from table to table to make sure everyone was happy. I'd be willing to bet there was only one person in the kitchen cooking, as well. This is a small operation and they are really working hard here to keep everyone happy. If there is a bit of a wait, just be patient. I went in with open eyes, having read past reviews, so the wait wasn't an issue for me. More time to chat, I say!  I loved my experience here. The food was excellent and the staff was polite and friendly. While I won't say that it's the very best Vietnamese food New Orleans has to offer, I was left happy with my food and I would return.

This is a nifty little neighborhood bar with friendly staff, cool customers and a pretty good draft beer selection.  A friend of mine lives right across the street from this place, so we have found ourselves here a couple of times. Don't be fooled by the outside- once you are inside the bar space is really big, complete with a long bar and booths and tables against the wall.  As I said, there is a nice little draft beer selection- they have brews from Lagunitas, Great Raft and Gnarly Barley on tap, so you won't be stuck drinking just Miller High Life all night. They have a wide section for the pool tables, if that's your thing and the few times I have been here, the music has been pretty good and has ranged from jazz to rock, depending on the night.

I stopped in here for a late lunch and the place was understandably dead. It was fine with me- I don't care if I'm the only person in a restaurant at any given time.  I was seated, and as I looked over the menu free chips and salsa were dropped off. Have you noticed that fewer and fewer places bring you free chips and salsa? I can understand charging for queso, but I like having the chips to munch on while I'm deciding what to eat. I decided to keep it simple and go for the burrito dinner which comes with a ground beef burrito, beans and rice.   The food came out within 5 minutes, which immediately made me go "hmmm". I like fast service, but when food comes out that fast I wonder how fresh it is. The burrito was okay, but nothing special at all. It was literally ground meat in a tortilla. I'm not even sure you can call that a burrito. The beans and rice were decent, but forgettable.  I might have to go back and try something a little more complex. The food hit the spot, mainly because I was starving, but if I had been expecting really good Mexican food, I would have been left disappointed. Also, service was okay, but my waiter was handling a beer delivery at the same time that he was waiting on me, so I had to flag him down a few times and remind him I was there.

Despite having an awful name (really, it's terrible. The original name: "Dis & Dat" wasn't any better.) this restaurant offers some pretty amazing burgers. We stopped in on a Saturday afternoon, because I was craving a burger something fierce, and although I had heard raves about this spot, I had yet to try it.  Dis and Dem is a no frills type of place. There's a large bar area with some tables and chairs off to the side and you place your order at the bar. My friend and I both decided to get a cheeseburger and we split some seasoned fries. This burger was HUGE! Seriously, I had to cut it in half and take half of it home because I was super stuffed and I couldn't finish it. The fries were really tasty- I think they were dusted with a Creole seasoning type of thing and I liked them a lot.  Reading some older reviews for this place, it seems like they have made some real improvements in the "quality" department. I would encourage anyone who went when they first opened to give them another shot. They just do burgers now (I think they did hot dogs when they first opened, as well) and I really think they nail it. For me, this burger was as good as Company Burger and that's my "top tier" burger pick.  They also do breakfast, but I'm not sure if that's everyday or just on Sundays. I would love to return to Dis and Dem. Now I'm hungry.

I love this lovely little spot at Audubon Park. As Jen said, the tree is beautiful and majestic and it's the perfect spot to spend an afternoon. I had never even heard this tree called the Tree of Life, until last year when I was trying to meet up with a group of people, and I had no idea what tree they were talking about.  A definite landmark in our wonderful city, it's a must see if you find yourself in the area.

A friend and I stopped in here for lunch on a Saturday afternoon and we were surprised to find that it wasn't packed at all. Aside from us, there were only a few people sitting at the sushi bar.  Everything on the menu sounded great, and I decided to start with the squid salad. The best part of this salad is that it's nice and cold and the squid is thinly sliced, so that it's not too chewy. I've found that some places have big hunks of squid and it can be difficult to chew. File under: squid fanatic problems.  We decided to get the rainbow roll and the Fantastic roll. The rainbow roll was pretty typical. The fish was really fresh and I enjoyed it. The star was definitely the Fantastic roll.
