This is tuna, salmon, yellowtail, masago, cucumber, avocado and scallion wrapped in a special seaweed that is almost similar to lettuce. I really enjoyed it because it was light and it had a really good flavor.  If you happen to be dining with someone who isn't into the raw stuff, they have a pretty extensive selection of noodles, rice and other cooked dishes like that.  All in all my experience here was fantastic and I will definitely be back.

They have an open mic comedy show every Wednesday night and occasionally have comedy shows on Saturday.  Comedy is really the only thing I have ever seen here.  They also host bands, but the place seems a little small for that.  I mean, it gets pretty packed for a comedy show, so I can only imagine the crowd that comes to see a band.    Cool little dive to get a drink.

I like this place for live music, but as far as the whole "laundromat" thing, well...I can't speak to that. I'm with Jen L.; the idea of washing my clothes in a smoky bar doesn't appeal to me at all and kind of defeats the purpose of doing laundry in the first place, in my opinion.  I haven't been here often, but the few times I have been here have been a lot of fun. The bands are always pretty good and I have found that there is rarely any kind of cover.

I wanted to give this place a better rating. I really did. I went to Elizabeth's and I think that I did it wrong.  So, we went and were seated upstairs at the bar. It was an interesting vibe up there. I probably would have preferred a table, but you live and you learn. I ordered the eggs florentine which is two poached eggs with sliced up potatoes and fried oysters topped with creamed spinach. I liked the eggs and I liked the oysters, but I felt like the "center" of the meal was the potatoes when it should have been the eggs. When it's 10am, I don't really have the strength in me to eat a pound or two of potatoes.  All in all the food wasn't bad, but I have honestly had better at St. Charles Tavern. I know. You are probably wondering what is wrong with me. I think it's because I so rarely do breakfast at a sit down place, that when I do I just want the basics: eggs over easy, toast, hash browns, maybe some grits and bacon. Maybe it's the "country" in me, I don't know.  I was able to try some of the praline bacon which was as amazing as bacon topped with sugar can probably be.  I will definitely go back, but when I do I will probably order the grits or something a little more my speed.

Ignatius is one of the things that makes the city of New Orleans fantastic and unique.  A Confederacy of Dunces holds a special place in my heart and is one of my favorite books. Set in New Orleans, it has been called one of the defining novels set in New Orleans. Ignatius is the main character, and at the beginning of the novel he is described as waiting under the clock at D.H. Holmes for his mother. That's where he stands to this day.  Philadelphia has LOVE, New Orleans has Ignatius.

This is pretty much the exact type of shop I picture when I think of the Bywater: a small place packed with neighborhood locals, a little sketchy and no ac.  I like it here, for the most part. They don't have ac, or at least it wasn't on the evening I stopped in, so I do wonder what happens in the summer. There is a nice little crowd of locals sitting outside, and even a few shop kitties walking around and sleeping on chairs at the tables.  Not only is Flora a coffee shop, but it's a juice bar. I wasn't in the mood for java when I stopped in, so I decided to get a nice carrot juice. There is a large seating area in the back, so we were able to sit back there and chat while some other customers played a board game in the front.  I really did like this place. It has a "hipster" kind of atmosphere, but it's a good group of folks and I could see myself stopping in if I lived in the area.

This is a pretty average Sally's store. You might not always find what you are looking for here, so if you really need something, you might want to save some time and go online. I came in looking for a hot air brush that I saw was on sale. Well, I went to another Sally's and it was on sale there, but sold out. I came here to look for it, and they had it, but it wasn't marked as a sale item. Kind of odd, considering it on sale online AND at another store. Oh well. I wasn't concerned enough to ask about it.  I would go back if I was in the area and really needed something, but I'll probably stick to purchasing online.

If you are into tools, hardware, or home improvement of any kind, then this is the place for you.  First of all, I don't know any handyman (or handwoman...er, handylady?)  that can walk into this place and not leave with something.  They are always having sales on their already ridiculously cheap merchandise and they carry anything that you may need in the hardware line.  They even have coupons in the paper for free things, like mini flashlights!  Really...do you know what a pancake air compressor is??  Yeah, well I didn't until a few months ago, but this place has 'em!  I'm not into tools, but even I was blown away by how cheap things here are.  Check it out!

This place is pretty fantastic and super yummy, especially considering that it's a chain.  We stopped in for lunch and ordering was pretty easy. We started with a Greek salad, which we split. All of the ingredients were super fresh and I loved that there was a generous serving of cheese on the salad. It had a lot of flavor and it was a perfect start to the meal.  The pizza we ordered was the Kosmic Karma. This is a pizza with feta cheese, spinach, tomatoes and pesto. Not only did I feel like I was eating (kind of) healthy, but it was really good.  Our service was okay, but kind of slow. The waitress was super apologetic about our wait time and her nice personality made up for our wait. I will definitely return to Mellow Mushroom.

Bad.  Touristy and bad.  Sure, they have drink specials, but keep in mind that the place gets PACKED and the music comes in the form of two people on stage singing along with a song.    I went here a while back with a friend of mine.  The conversation with the bartender went as follows:  "I'd just like a water, please." "$4" "Oh no, just ice water.  Tap water." "We only serve bottled water." "I can't just have tap water?" "No, sorry."  At this point, I grabbed a plastic cup, walked to the bathroom and filled the cup under the tap.  The bathroom attendant told me that everyone does that because no one likes paying for bottled water.  You'd think the owners of the place would have gotten that memo by now.  Now, I get it.  You're a business.  You want to make a few bucks.  But come on, forcing people to pay for water is ridiculous.  If you want to make more money, maybe have less "3 for 1" deals so that people can get free water.

Oh my gosh!! This whole store is where you would shop if you had plans to attend a party at Jay Gatsby's mansion. Really, that is the only way I can describe it.  This shop is perfectly perfect in every way and it makes me want to throw a big shindig, just so I will have a excuse to spend all of my money here. There are so many charming things: sparkly dresses, pastel dresses, beautiful costume jewelry, furs, hats, feather wigs and a tiara, just to name a few. Setting foot here was like visiting your great aunt's house, provided she has lots of style.  I couldn't quite tell if this shop was a consignment shop or not because all of the items are "one of a kind", in the sense that there is only one of each thing offered. For example, I found a beautiful dress that would be perfect for New Years Eve, but it wasn't in my size. Despite that, I love the feeling that you are in a fabulous closet packed with vintage inspired treats.  I didn't buy anything to do, but I do intend to pick up some sparkly hair accessories as the end of the year approaches.

I love these little "hole in the wall" galleries that you can find throughout New Orleans. I must have passed this place tens of times and I had no idea it even existed until I attended an event here last week.  The gallery is small, but the art is well done and poignant and reflects the culture of New Orleans and the struggle of many of the citizens therein. There were some interesting mediums here: photographs printed on glass and thin pieces of cloth, hands and fingers molded out of plaster, and pieces of art set in repurposed window panes and other found items. I liked that all of the art here told a story and conjured up emotion.  The event I attended was a "meeting of the courts" Mardi Gras/Alexander the Great party. It was a lot of fun, and although there were a lot of people here, the space was used well and it didn't feel over crowded. This was a very New Orleans type of night with all types of people coming together to have a good time and usher in the Carnival season.  If you can make it to New Orleans Art Center, it's definitely worth checking out.

This is a decent daiquiri shop. We were here on a Saturday night because we had an hour to burn before a movie. I like that the space is wide open and it was a nice evening, so they had the doors open. They have lots of TVs, if you want to watch a game and the bartender was fast at taking orders and making everyone happy. They do have a drive thru, as well, in case you aren't in the mood to drink at the place. They have daily specials and they serve basic food like pizza (probably frozen) and other snacks along those lines.

Wow. It's been over 6 years since my last review and my, how this place has changed.  I don't know if there are new owners, but Bulldog is now a full fledged "craft beer" bar. Gone are the days of Budweiser and Coors light on tap. Almost every tap has a local or other craft beer and I couldn't be happier about the change. The entire beer system has been replaced and is shiny and new. There's an extensive menu of draft and bottled craft beer and the beer menu is displayed on one of the tv screens at all times. Bulldog has partnered with Untappd, so you can link your beers to the bar and keep track of what you've tried.  I guess because of all of these changes, the vibe here is just different. It doesn't have as much of a college feel as it once had, I think probably because all of their beers are a little pricier than they used to be and most college kids don't have much interest in craft beer. On the night we were here the crowd was definitely a little older than I've seen in the past. I'm not sure if it's always like this, but I get the feeling it is.   They still have the kitchen serving the same bar grub that they always had. And much of the decor of the bar is the same, although I did notice that all of the "fake" celeb autograph pics that used to be all over the place are now gone.  I like the change, but there's something I'll always miss about the "grittier" Bulldog. This used to be my hang out when I was in my 20's and there was just something about it. That old feeling is gone, but I'm excited that they have gone more into the craft direction and are now a "legit" New Orleans beer bar. I was excited that they had Jucifer on tap, so that made for a happy birthday when I was here celebrating.

Pretty decent, but not overly fantastic.  I got the brisket Pho in a "regular" size bowl that was $6.50. It was okay, but for $1.25 more at Tan Dinh you get a lot more "bang" for your buck and a better tasting broth. It wasn't terrible, but it was missing something. I feel like they are afraid to make it taste too "authentic" for fear of alienating some of their less experienced customers.  Oh well. It made for an okay lunch, but I probably wouldn't return.

This is such a fancy pants PJs!  It makes me wish I lived uptown.  First of all, the place is huge and there is plenty of room, if you need to study or do work.  They have a seating area with couches, a tv, and board games, if you want to go and just hang out with some friends.  They have a diverse food selection with everything from stuffed croissants and muffins, as well as other little snacks.  For some reason, a large iced coffee is 30 cents cheaper here, than at other PJs.  I have no idea why, but iced coffee that costs less than 3 bucks is always a win.

Dang 'wego! How long have you been hiding this place?  I feel like I am always on the hunt for new lunch places and my recent trek brought me out to Westwego after a meeting. I was in the mood for some seafood and after checking Yelp, I found this place. Walking in, there isn't much to see: a few tables and chairs and you order at the counter. That's okay, I'm not here for the ambiance.  Mostly everything is fried and they have a wide selection of fried seafood. The fried fish plate sounded good, so I went with that. You get a choice of how many piece of fish you want (up to 8) and I went with three because it was only about $8 and I figured the pieces were going to be small. Well, I was very wrong. Out came a plate with three HUGE pieces of fried catfish, fries and a small "salad". The fish was excellent- sliced thin, but not too thin and perfectly fried. I was able to get through one piece of fish before I decided I should just take the other two home. The fries were pretty good and the "salad" was just lettuce, tomatoes, and pickles, so I didn't bother with it.   Like I said, this is a pretty basic place and you can tell they are mostly a "to go" business, but the food is well priced and worth the trip, if you are anywhere near Westwego around lunch or dinner time.

I usually don't make it out to Wednesday-before-Mardi-Gras parades, so this was my first experience with Druids. After seeing past posts online and reading a few reviews here, I was expecting the worst. However, I was pleasantly surprised.   The Krewe was celebrating their 20th year and I didn't notice that any of the floats were overly scandalous or offensive. Of course, it was raining and I was trying my best to stay dry, so maybe I missed something. While they weren't throwing as generously as the bigger Krewes do, I caught a few things and everyone seemed to have a good time.

We stopped in here, during French Quarter Fest, to get the lay of the land and to see the friend of a friend.  First of all, the place was pretty empty, so I got to see how big it really is. There's a front bar area with a stage and a huge dance floor. In the back, there is a wide open space with another bar. It wasn't functioning on the night we stopped in, but I can imagine that on packed nights both bars are put to work.  The man performing on stage was really good, especially considering we were in here on a Thursday afternoon and the place was pretty dead. I appreciated that he was putting on a show, even though the place wasn't full and he was competing with street performers.  It's not the best Bourbon bar, but it's far from the worst.

Not the worst spot in the world, but it's small and get's really crowded. If you can grab a spot by the bar, you're golden. Really cool place to see some live music and it wouldn't be my first choice for live music, but it's definitely not at the bottom of the list. People are reasonably friendly, considering how crowded it gets.  Not a bad spot, but I wouldn't go out of my way.

I feel like I describe every bar I visit as a "neighborhood place", but that's exactly what J&J's is.  I think I had been here before- the bar area looked familiar, but I'm not sure.  There was a game on the night we stopped in and a lot of the regulars were sitting and enjoying it. They serve basic drinks here and they also have Schlitz in a can, which is pretty unusual and random. Pool tables in the back and nice bartenders make it a good place to hang out.

This is a nice little place packed with folk art.  Upon walking in, at first I didn't know what to think. The art here is definitely a little bit different to what I am used to seeing. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to talk to the gallery owner, so I'm not sure of the complete history of the pieces, however I really did enjoy them and think they were nice.  The subject of the art is African Americans, mainly children and the art has a nice Southern feel to it. I would call the art here "simple, but quaint", if that makes any kind of sense. I do think that the pieces are interestingly done, and while it isn't my taste, I can appreciate the work put into them by the artist.

We were going to see a show across the street, so we stopped in here for a "quick" bite. I ordered a small pizza and my friend ordered chicken wings. The wings came out pretty quickly, but my pizza was no where to be seen. I am a patient person so I waited. I waited for 30 minutes. I finally decide to step up to the counter and say something and they are shocked that I haven't gotten my food yet. Then the guy tells me that they didn't put the order in. Um...really? So after over 40 minutes of waiting I got my pizza. I was so hungry at that point that I just scarfed the food down, so I can't even tell you if it was good or not.   I won't be back.

I like this place. It's a nice little restaurant in the Fulton area.  Now, to be totally honest, I have never actually eaten here. I usually find myself here hanging out with friends and having a good time. I really like that (because it's a restaurant) it's completely smoke free. I find myself more and more drawn to smoke free places as of late. I have really begun hating reeking of cigarette smoke at the end of the night.   Anyway, this is a nice alternative to some of the other places in this area like Lucy's or Red Eye. I have never seen it overly crowded and the staff is nice.

Ashley's isn't a bad addition to the Westbank Vietnamese scene, but some improvements could definitely be made.  On the bright side, Ashley's has an extensive menu of pho, banh mi, fried rice and Chinese combination plates. They also have spring rolls and Vermicilli noodle bowls and other food you would expect to find at this type of establishment. The interesting thing is that Ashley's also has an assortment of po boys. I didn't try any but if you are not in the mood for Asian food, they have shrimp, ham and cheese, hot sausage and roast beef po boys.  When I stopped in here, I decided to get a bowl of the eye of round steak in beef broth. Honestly, it wasn't too bad, but I've had better. The broth had a nice enough flavor, but something was off and I couldn't quite put my finger on it.  As far as improvements go the biggest would have to be the table cloths. The tables are covered in white plastic table cloths, which is fine, but they are obviously not changed or even wiped down between customers. The table where I was sitting had a table cloth on it that was dirty and stained with old food. It also had tears in it where it looked like someone (probably a child) had poked at it in many places with a fork. It was just off putting. Another complaint was that I ordered iced tea and the woman working explained to me that they didn't have straws. Who runs out of straws? I didn't necessarily feel like putting my mouth all over the cup I was drinking out of, but I was left with no choice.  I think that Ashley's is probably good if you are in the mood for takeout, but I would be loath to dine in again.

I've been sitting on this review for a while, mainly because it's hard to properly put my experience at Restaurant R'evolution into words.  We stopped in here for a late dinner at 10, because we waited until earlier that day to make reservations. When we arrived at 10, we were immediately seated.  It felt really fancy when they handed us the drink menu on an iPad. Definitely a different touch that I thought was neat. After looking over the menu, I decided on a garden salad and the Crawfish-stuffed Redfish Napoleon. The salad was, well...a salad, but the stuffed redfish was amazing. It was delicious and rich and came topped with an amazing sauce. The person I dined with had the scallops, and although I'm not usually a fan of scallops, I found them pretty tasty.  For dessert, I decided on the Turbodog stout chocolate cake. It came with a little bit of ice cream, too. It was small, but it was the perfect end to the meal. As a treat, we also asked to explore the "chocolate jewelry box". This is a multi-level box that comes with a different chocolate sample on each level. If you are a chocolate fan, like I am, this is a "must".   Dining here was a fantastic experience. Definitely a first class fine dining experience with a great and attentive staff and people who were eager to make sure that we had a memorable time.  Pro tip: after your meal, ask to see where they keep all the wine. So much wine!

This is such a great little spot for lunch! A friend and I decided to eat here, as I had passed this place many times and really didn't know anything about it, other than it is a Vietnamese restaurant.  I got here around 1 and the place was empty, except for one guy sitting alone and eating a bowl of Pho. The menu sounded so good! They have a HUGE selection of spring rolls of all types. I could definitely see myself just making a meal out of 3 spring roll orders, but today I just decided to try the spicy salmon spring roll. I also got a pork noodle bowl salad, because I was trying to keep it a little bit light.  The spicy salmon spring roll was so good! It was unique in the sense that I don't think I have ever had anything like it. It's raw salmon and vermicelli wrapped with some sriracha. It had a lot of kick and was really good after I added a bit of soy sauce to it. The noodle bowl was large and delicious. There were large slices of pork on top of a generous amount of noodles, lettuce and cucumber. It was the perfect meal for a warm September day.  I really enjoyed my lunch here. Like I said, I could have easily made a meal out of the spring rolls- they have the largest spring roll selection that I have seen, so if that's your thing, check it out.  I'll be back!

Accidentally stopped in here with a friend when we were looking for another bar in the same area. Really cool space with friendly people. They were offering free mac and cheese when we came, and although we didn't partake, I thought that was nice. There weren't a lot of people and they had a little jazz band playing in the back. Ordered one Abita Strawberry and was pleasantly surprised when it was only $3, considering some other places charge as much as $5 for the same thing.  I'll be back if I'm in the neighborhood, but I think it would be a better spot if it were smoke free.

I went to a wedding here, so this is a review of a wedding experience.  First off all, the Hilton Riverside is HUGE! It almost seems never ending and there are a ton of meeting rooms and halls. For the wedding I went to, we all went into one big room for the actual ceremony and then we were lead across the way to a bigger room for the reception.  Now, this is mainly going to be a review of the food, because is there really any other reason to go to a wedding? Seriously. So, this wedding had a lot of awesome food that was all provided by the Hilton chef's (or whoever is in charge of that type of thing). There was oysters Rockefeller that were delicious, but I think that my favorite was the fish and cheese spread. I know it sounds odd to serve fish at a wedding, but it was super fresh and delicious. Long story short: the food was on point.  The room where the reception was wasn't the biggest room I have ever been in for a reception, but it got the job done and everyone seemed to have a good time.

It had been a long day and I was starving with a capital "S" when we decided to check out the new Company Burger.  Now, I'm a long time fan of the original Company Burger, so to say that I had high expectations of this place is probably an understatement. This location definitely has a lot to offer- the restaurant is big and is clearly meant for game crowds, they have an extensive menu and the staff is fast.  I decided to get my usual single cheeseburger and I also got a side of fries and a side of pork rinds. Yes, they have pork rinds on the menu! The food came really quickly, and I don't know if it's because I was so hungry, but it was one of the best burgers I have probably ever tasted. Of course, the fries were cooked and seasoned perfectly and there was a very generous portion of pork rinds with my order. Pork rinds might seem like something random to eat with a cheeseburger, but they were actually perfect. The Freret St. location needs to add them to the menu and then we'll be golden. Just like the other location, this Company has a nice selection of beers on tap and they also have milk shakes. Unlike the other location, this Company has a wide variety of sides.  The only reason I am rating it four stars is because the parking is a pain and I can imagine it's a huge pain during peak hours. Besides that, don't hesitate to stop in for a little bit of amazing.

When it comes to cool streets with lots going on, this one is at the top of the list.  One of the main selling points of Frenchmen is that it's a good hangout for tourists and locals alike, and it's not Bourbon St.  The places on the street feel a little more "authentic" New Orleans, because you can go here and actually see live local acts.  Jazz, blues, swing and more can all be found over the course of just a few blocks.  I know that Frenchmen isn't in the safest area, so whenever I go, I'm always sure to go with a big group, and I always end up having a lot of fun.  Also, every year on Halloween, Frenchmen hosts a huge block party, which ends up being the "place to be seen" for grown ups who want to have as much fun as the kids.  It seems that anything you want can be found here.  Check out jazz at Snug Harbor, a local blues act at DBA, do some salsa dancing at Blue Nile, hit the club at Maison, or get something to eat at 13.    Frenchmen is a definite "must" for anyone who is looking for the heart of New Orleans.

There's a new craze hitting the New Orleans food scene: fancy grilled cheese sandwiches. Needless to say, I totally approve.  Stacks might not be the "big cheese" when it comes to grilled cheese places in this town, but they have some really good stuff that left me satisfied. Stacks is located in the bar area of the Embassy Suites on Julia. It's the hotel restaurant, which is enough to make me stay at Embassy Suites every weekend for the rest of my life.  We sat down at a table and the bartender came over with menus. I decided to get the Turkey and figs which is a sandwich that leans toward the sweeter side with turkey, fig jam, bacon, cheddar and gouda. My friend got the Drew Bries which came packed with apple, bacon, praline and brie. We decided to do the "split" so we could each try a half of a sandwich.  I loved mine! It was the perfect combo of savory and sweet and I could easily enjoy this as a yummy breakfast sandwich. The Drew Bries was okay, but I found it to be a little too cheese heavy for my taste. I think it need a more substantial meat than bacon to even it out. Both sandwiches came with shoestring fries and the whole meal was delightful. Overall I liked both sandwiches, but when I go back I am definitely getting my Turkey and figs again.

Oh hey, I had a completely painless experience here.  You can bring something here and have them pack it, or you can bring something already packed and ready to ship. I suggest the latter because I was able to be in and out within just a few minutes. I went online first and printed out the shipping label I needed and got everything ready to ship, so it was just a matter of handing over my package and getting a receipt. They also sell an assortment of packing materials and boxes, in case you want to stop in and do your own packing and boxing.

This isn't a bad place, but I wouldn't go out of my way to visit.  I came here for the first time to watch the premiere of a friend's film project.  There's a bar area and then a separate area for a private party.  The clientele here is... interesting.  There was one guy in there who was drinking out of a huge "Walk Ons" jug and cursing up a storm.  I got the impression that he worked there, but I could be wrong.  I did like that 12 bar had sofas.  My friend and I hung out and people watched for a while, as we waited for the show to start.  There are pool tables and tvs, if you are in the mood to watch a game.  If you are looking for something, in the same area but a little more upscale, check out Ernst Cafe next door.

Meh. I don't like chains. Call me a snob. I just don't.  A friend of mine was having a good bye dinner here so we stopped in and I brought my open mind. We sat at the bar and it was what it was. The good thing about sitting at the bar is that the beers are a plenty.  For an appetizer we ordered the buffalo chicken dip which came with chips and celery (???). It was pretty good and had some good flavor. I got an order of mac and cheese because pasta and cheese is always a win. This was the highlight of the night. Seriously, the mac and cheese was amazing.  As an entree I got the Outback burger, medium-rare with cheddar cheese. It was decent, but I have definitely had a better burger elsewhere. I don't want to sound snooty- I liked it, but I've had better. The burger was cooked medium, which isn't a huge deal, but when I order medium-rare, I want medium-rare. Also, I think my big complaint with the burger was that the bun overwhelmed the meat. The bun was a little too fluffy and bready. When I have a burger, I want the burger to be the star of the show. I took home half of the burger, and after taking it off of the bun, I could really appreciate that the burger was at least juicy.  I will say that the bar staff was on point. They were extremely attentive and quick to get us our order.

Wow.  I really wasn't a fan of this place, but after seeing all of these reviews, I think I'm going to give it another try.  I went and I got the (a?) pupusa.  I had never tried it before and it wasn't bad.  It was really exotic.  It wasn't bad, but it's not what I'm used to.  I'm pretty adventurous, but this was different even for me.  I ordered on the recommendation of someone else, so if I went back I think I would take a little more time to look over the menu and figure out what I wanted for myself.  I have heard that they have an excellent breakfast/brunch, so I am eager to try that.  They don't serve alcohol, just a heads up.  They do have really good tea, though.

Would you believe that I live a hop and a skip from this place and I have never been? What have I been doing with myself?  I stopped in here for a breakfast meeting because the person I was meeting is a regular here and were both close enough to make this a good meet up spot. The restaurant is pretty basic: you order at the counter and the waitress will bring your food out to you when it's ready. Because I was here for breakfast, I got the traditional breakfast (#1), which was 2 eggs, bacon, toast and grits and coffee. The grand total was around $9, which is a little more expensive than other breakfast spots, but not a huge issue.  The food was great and I loved that my eggs were cooked perfectly (over easy) and the bacon was nice and crispy. The staff here is super sweet and are quick to warm up your coffee when you need a refill. All of the patrons seem to know each other and whenever someone walked in the door, other customers would immediately greet them with a pat on the back or a handshake. This is the regular breakfast joint for a lot of local folks.  They also serve lunch and they are open until 6, if you are in the mood for an early dinner. Lunch items on the menu include po boys, sandwiches, salads, platters and other things along that line. I probably wouldn't lunch here, but I will definitely be back for that delicious breakfast.

The Westbank trying to be Eastbank.  I used to go here a lot, because a guy a dated a few years back loved it, but I always found it WAY overpriced and the food wasn't that great.  The staff was ok, but it looked like they couldn't deal with the amount of people who would come into the place.  If you want a more upscale dining feel, don't waste your time on this place.  Drive the 6 minutes is takes to get uptown and pick a place on Magazine St.  Trust me.

A fantastic open air market where you can get everything from veggies to (on the Second Saturday of the month) arts and crafts.  This has become a sort of Satuday morning tradition.   The vegetables are home grown by local farmers, fresh and delicious.  You can also get farm fresh eggs and corn meal.  They have dried okra, if you are in the mood for a crunchy snack.  They also have homemade honey and hot dishes such as crawfish bread.  A local performer provides musical entertainment while you shop around and all of the vendors are extremely friendly.

New on Magazine Fresh raw fish and hibachi Will go back for more  This place is new on Magazine (it just opened last month) and I'm already a fan. I stopped in for lunch last week with a friend, There was barely anyone here, so we were seated quickly. I knew exactly what I was in the mood for.  First of all, my friend wasn't in the mood for sushi (weirdo), so he decided to get a hibachi steak that came with a side of rice and vegetables. I, on the other hand, was all about the fish. I got an order of salmon sashimi, a Philly roll, and a spicy crunchy roll. The salmon sashimi was fantastic and yummy and fresh. You get 6 pieces for about $9, and while the pieces aren't as big as some other restaurants, that's a pretty good deal and I was happy with  it. The Philly roll was really good and a good size. The spicy crunchy roll was okay, but instead of putting the sriracha in the roll, they just put a dab of it on a regular crunchy roll. I kind of wondered if they forgot to put the spice in it, so they just decided a little dab would be okay. Who knows. It wasn't bad, just different,  They don't have iced green tea on the menu, but they will make it for you if you ask. It's real green tea and not the powdered mix! SCORE!  All in all I liked this place a lot and I wouldn't definitely return and try some special rolls.

After some friends raved about this place, we decided to check out Wingstop. I'm not usually a fan of getting wings "out" at places, but I figured I would give Wingstop a shot.  It's easy enough to order here: you walk up, pick how many wings you want, pick your flavor, pick your dip and pick your side (fries or veggie sticks- side note: who is ordering veggie sticks??). I decided to get 3 boneless lemon pepper wings and 3 boneless Louisiana spice wings with fries and blue cheese dip. There weren't a lot of people in the place, and the order took a while, but the wait wasn't too bad.  The flavor of both if the wings that I got was good. The Louisiana spice could have used a little more "kick", but all in all it was okay. My big complaint is that a couple of the wings were SUPER small with more batter than chicken. Also they were very greasy. So greasy that I probably should have "blotted" them before eating them. So greasy that they left a pool of grease at the bottom of the basket they were resting in. I know it's fast food and "you get what you pay for", so I guess I shouldn't be complaining since my meal cost $9, but still. Next time I'm just gonna throw those bad boys on a paper towel. My boyfriend got the Louisiana spice and the BBQ wings and didn't care for the BBQ wings at all. They do give you plenty of fries that are pretty good and the blue cheese dip was surprisingly tasty.  Another small complaint: my boyfriend went to get a Coke and the machine was out of Coke. We told them and they said they would fix it. They never did- meh. I will give props for this: the lady who made the wings told us to combine orders next time and save a few dollars. That was a cool "pro tip".  I would probably go back now that I know exactly what I am getting. The food is good for what it is- fast food chicken. As long as you aren't expecting Popeyes quality, you won't be disappointed.

This is a fantastic outdoor food court that is located on the Oretha Castle Haley corridor (is that a thing?) and is a great spot for lunch. There aren't a TON of places to choose from in here, but I like that there is a nice selection of different types of food such as Spanish, Jamaican and Asian inspired food. They also have a snowball/juice stand that serves up goodies that will cool you down on a hot day.  I think the best part of this food court is all of the amazing seating under an over hang, so you won't overheat. I was here for lunch and I didn't notice the heat at all and there are plenty of seats and tables for groups. It's worth checking out, if you are in the area.

Marc is a great photographer. Not only is he professional, he is super patient and has a great artistic vision. He's very open to discuss anything you might need and is open to working with you to make sure that you have a satisfying experience. I highly recommend him for any photography need that you may have.

Cool! A neat new cocktail bar in the downtown area.  We were walking down Decatur when I saw that this long rumored place had finally opened. I walk in and I was taken aback. This is NOT Pravda in any way shape or form. The entire place has been gutted of it's Russian absinthe bar charm, and in it's place is now a drinking establishment that has yet to really build a personality. The marble bar is pretty nice though, so I will give them that.  We sat at the bar and I decided to try the "Red Wedding". Yes, it is named after that infamous episode of Game of Thrones (I asked). It contained rum, but it also contained A LOT of other stuff that made it taste really bitter to me. It was definitely a "sipper", which I am fine with. The bartender saw that I wasn't really into what I had ordered, so he was kind enough to make me a French 75 (his suggestion) and that was much better on my palate. My friend ordered the Valeira Gorge and it was so good that he asked the bartender for the recipe (and the bartender obliged!). I took a sip and it was super good and refreshing. When I go back, I will probably get that.  We went kind of late, so I think that the kitchen was closed. I would love to go back and try the food. All in all, I would say 3.75 stars with a little room left for improvement.

We randomly stopped in here on a Saturday night and we were seated in the bar, since we hadn't made reservations- no problem at all.  For starters, the restaurant is really dark, I mean so dark I could barely see the menu. After looking it over, and consulting the waitress about her recommendations, we decided to start with the octopus appetizer. This dish is grilled octopus and potatoes served with an interesting reduction of beets and lemon. The dish was okay, but the potatoes were a little overwhelming and there were more potatoes than octopus. All in all, the octopus itself was enjoyable.  Next I had the hangar steak, cooked medium rare and served with pomme frites. This dish was delicious and the steak was perfectly cooked, juicy and flavorful. The pomme frites were tasty as well and they came with a side of aioli for dipping. It was all so good.  For the most part, I liked my meal here. I think next time i will actually make reservations so I don't have to sit in the bar area.

While some friends and I were hanging Uptown for parades, someone suggested that they were in the mood for seafood.  Although I had never been here, this was the first place that came to mind (mainly because it was a two minute drive from where we were).  I had passed the brightly lit building a few times, and since I like trying new places, I was eager to check it out.  When we walked in, we expected the place to be crowded.  While there were a few post parade "stragglers", we were seated quickly in a booth in the bar area.  They had a limited Mardi Gras menu, but that was okay since we were just in the mood for some kind of seafood.  As we munched on our complimentary bread and butter, the first thing that we started with were the char broiled oysters (they offer them raw, too).  They came to the table while they were still sizzling and they were really good.  The oysters were big and juicy and the butter sauce on them was fantastic.  For my entree, I wasn't super hungry, so I decided to get a bowl of corn and crab bisque.  It was delicious and there was so much of it that I couldn't finish it all!  One of my friends got the special, which was the redfish topped with some kind of sauce.  I was able to try it, and that was amazing too.  By the end of the meal, I was receiving "kudos" for my suggestion of trying this place out.  I also must mention that our server was amazing.  I wish I could remember her name, but she was super cheerful, even though she had mentioned she had been working all day and she had to be back at work first thing in the morning.  She was super attentive and was asking about our Mardi Gras and about the different parades we had seen.  She really made all of us feel welcome.  I would definitely go back to Superior seafood.  I would love to see what their full menu has to offer.

Wow. Cool. You can seriously review this unique little area?  This is where all of the artists hang out. There is usually a neat little art market on the weekends where you can buy whatever the artists are selling from paintings to sculptures and other little unique artifacts. They also sell handblown glass pipes, if that is your thing. Hookahs, too!  Frenchmen street has really expanded beyond just the awesome music scene and is now a place for artists to congregate and sell their wares. A definite "must" for any tourist or local.

I really loved the Endymion parade this year, due to it's switch to the Uptown route following Bacchus.  Endymion is a parade that I rarely get a chance to check out, because when it comes to Mardi Gras, I am a complete uptown girl.  When it was rerouted, due to weather, I was excited.  The throws were great and the Krewe seemed excited to be rolling after Bacchus, one of the biggest Uptown parades.  The floats were gorgeous, as usual, and it was a good crowd.  I had a lot of fun.  Catch of the night: a light up spinning "wand" and HUGE black and gold beads with a giant Fleur de Lis on them.

Walking into Trader Joe's felt a bit "culty". People were glazed over with excitement over the fresh produce. One young woman was gathering multiple bouquets of flowers in her arms with the excitement of a child in a toy store. I was able to resist the urge to check out TJ's for about two weeks. After reading the raves and seeing people lose their minds on Facebook, I decided to finally check out the place when I found myself in Metairie. I didn't really know what to expect: it's just a grocery store right?  Now that I have done some shopping here, I get it- kind of. They do have a lot of organic food and other goodies that is all reasonably priced because it's their own brand. Oh yeah- 98% of everything here is Trader Joe's brand. This is likely common knowledge, but I didn't know before stopping in. I glanced around and found myself at the cheese case (naturally). They have a nice selection of well priced cheeses, so that was a win. I then made my way past the cookie butter tower to the liquor area (as you do) and I picked up two big beers and a bottle of wine for a grand total of a little over $8. Not bad, but how is the stuff? Well, after getting the beer and wine home, I can safely say that "it is what it is". The beer didn't blow me away, although it was tasty. The "2 buck Chuck", as it's come to be called, is just fine if, like me, you aren't much a wine expert. All I know about wine is that I don't want it to be bitter. This wine wasn't bitter, so I'll consider it a win. One weird thing: when I finished it I noticed it had stained my wine glass purple. It was fine after I washed it, but that probably happened because it's cheap wine. Who knows.  The location of this store is convenient, parking was easy as pie and the folks checking people out got everyone through the line with the quickness. I will most likely return.

The other night I was having a pasta craving and after enjoying the spicy cajun trio pasta at the Marrero location, I decided to get the same thing here in "take out" form.  First of all, it was really convenient to be able to place my order online. My food was ready in about 15 minutes and I was able to pick it up as soon as I got there. When I got the food home and started to eat it, something was off. It wasn't spicy AT ALL. Did they forget to add "spice" to the spicy cajun trio? Also, there wasn't nearly as much cheese as there was on the previous version I had, which was disappointing. Other than that, the dish was pretty good and there was plenty enough for two people (not that I was sharing. ha).  I'll probably go back here and just chalk up the lack of spice and cheese to some kind of fluke.

We found that this was the perfect place to grab a bite to eat right before a movie. We skipped the wait and sat at the bar where Kat (Cat?) took care of us.  We started with the duck empanadas, which were delicious! The shell was flaky on the outside with a nice meat in the middle. They were served with a yummy sauce that complimented the dish perfectly. For my entree, I had the shrimp and grits. The shrimp were tail-off in a creamy sauce complete with sausage. This dish was also really good, but it wasn't the BEST shrimp and grits I've had and I almost could have done without the sausage, even though I am a sausage person. However, the grits were nice and smooth and perfectly prepared, so there was no complaint there.  Service was excellent and sitting at the bar was a great choice because it was quiet and we didn't feel rushed.

I attended the "A Dark and Stormy Night" event here, so I don't know if I had a typical experience (I assume this place mainly hosts wedding receptions), but I think I got a good feel of the venue.  For starters, I did have a bit of trouble finding the place. It's kind of hidden and GPS offered me zero help. When I finally found it, it was in a pretty obscure area of the park. Keep in mind, it was dark, so I was working at a disadvantage.  When I finally arrived, I was greeted by a large room of people having a good time. The venue itself it quite big and for this particular event, everything was spaced out nicely with art and auctions in the middle of the floor and drinks and food on the outer edges.   As far as food goes- it was kind of strange. There were people walking around the room with hors d'oeuvres and then there was a table of snacks. The food was pretty no frills: it was a couple of cheese balls and some chips and dip. Hey, I love a good cheese ball, so this girl wasn't complaining; the only thing I found odd is that the chips were just dumped on the table and not in a bowl or something. Eh, not a huge deal. Outside is, of course, Popp Fountain and it looked lovely as it was lit up and nicely illuminated for the evening.  I had a great time here and I would love to return for another event.

With it's comfy patio, tasty treats and light beers, I can already tell that Port Orleans is going to be a summer hot spot.  We were here opening weekend and the crowd was big, but the staff managed it well. I tried most of the beer and the one that stood out to me the most was the Storyville IPA. I love the hoppy goodness of an IPA and this one is light and crisp enough to have a few at a time and not feel weighed down. This is a perfect summer sipper, if you are looking for something with a little kick. The other beer I liked a lot was the John Law Pilsner, which was also light with a little bit of hop to it. I will be back for Storyville and John Law again and again.  David, who is not much of a beer drinker, really liked the Tea Pale Ale. I tried a sip of it and found it refreshing and smooth. It's not quite a lawnmower beer, but light enough to enjoy a few of them.  Port Orleans also serves food and it all looks really good, so I will have to go back and try some of the bites that they have to offer. I love the laid back vibe of the entire place, the staff knows their beer and there is plenty of space for relaxing. Port Orleans is likely going to be my "go to" brewery, at least for the time being.

I was already quite familiar with the goodness of Orleans Coffee, when I popped in here after a meeting. I got my usual iced coffee and it was as delicious as usual with a rich, tasty flavor. This review will be more about the space.   Located in the Zeitgeist, this Orleans location might be a bit difficult to find, if you don't know what you're looking for. Once inside, the stand is right in the front with plenty of seating in an open area. It's not a typical coffee shop type feel, but I love the big windows so that you can see out onto the street.  I didn't get anything to eat while I was here, but they seem to have a nice lunch selection and service was swift, as well. This location is probably a bit more convenient than the Prytania location, only because parking is a bit easier, so I will probably return.

My tank was on the low side and I found myself in...Kenner, so I stopped in here just to get enough gas to send me back on my way safely.  The gas is cheap, but the credit card machine was having an issue, so I had to go inside. After going inside, the guy working there assured me that the issue was resolved. I went out and tried again. NOPE; the pump still isn't working. Finally, he let me pay inside and I gassed up and went on my way.  Sketchy looking station in the middle of nowhere. I wouldn't go back.

First and foremost, the thing that "makes" this place is definitely the view and the location. There is just something really nice about eating lunch on the Lakefront, even if you are eating at a chain.  This is a former Joe's Crab Shack and I hadn't eaten in this building in probably 10 years. I came for lunch and there was a pretty decent crowd, but we were seated quickly.   Looking over the menu, I decided that the red beans and rice sounded good, so I got that. It came with a nice serving of beans and rice with andouille sausage and fried fish on the side. It was a lot of food for a lunch. The beans and rice were nothing overly special, but the sausage and the fish were really good. I think that if I go back, I will just cut out the "middle man" and get the fish right away.  All in all, it was a good meal at a good place. I would go back if I were in the area.

This is a quaint little coffee shop located in the middle of a quiet neighborhood. This is more of a review of the atmosphere than the coffee, since I didn't try any of the coffee.  I stopped in here to check out a friend's band on a Tuesday night. Neutral Ground hosts small music shows in a nice corner of their shop. I like this idea, because the shows are early and fairly short and the perfect thing for "night out" during the week. The coffee shop itself has a living room type of feel with assorted tables and sofas. They seem to offer all of the basics: coffee, tea and milk and a small assortment of snacks, especially pastries.  Cash only.

Miyako was pretty good and I would probably rate it 3.5 stars, but I can't so it gets three stars. Me and a friend popped into this place when they were 15 minutes away from closing. Even though we came in late, the hostess happily seated us and we ordered.  We decided on the salmon sashimi, a rainbow roll and a Philly roll. Only two pieces of sashimi come to an order, so we got three orders which came to about $10. The rainbow roll was a special roll and it was good, but I would have liked if it was a bit bigger for the price.  It was nice that I didn't feel rushed even though they were on the verge of closing when we arrived. I would probably go back, but it wouldn't be my first pick for sushi in the city.

I don't know why there are so many negative reviews of this place. No, Cafe Maspero isn't one of the finer dining establishments in the city, but it gets the job done when it's late and you are looking for something good to eat.  Dustin and I stopped in here on his suggestion. I had never been before, but I had passed this place a few times and it always looked casual and inviting. Looking over the menu, they pretty much have everything that you could want. From red beans to sandwiches, Maspero's seems to have it covered.   We decided on a cup of French onion soup and the club sandwich and fries and shared it. The French onion soup was amazing! It was probably some of the best that I have ever had. The club sandwich was just okay. Honestly, when I think "club sandwich", I think of a sandwich with layers. This was just basically ham, turkey, bacon and cheese all piled together. It wasn't bad at all, it just wasn't what I was expecting. I hear that the muffaletta is really good, so when I go back, I'm going to try that.  Four stars because of really good soup, super fast seating and fast and friendly service.

Lola's is located on what I have dubbed "restaurant row" on Esplanade; that little nook of cool, exotic dining spots that also includes Santa Fe, Cafe Degas and Nonna Mia. I had no idea that a yummy little Spanish cafe was right across the street. This was an amazing discovery.  Lola's is a pretty small place, so when you go, be ready for a little wait. Fortunately, the turn around is pretty quick, so we didn't have to wait long before we were seated.   Looking over the menu, I was a bit overwhelmed. There was a lot going on here and everything sounded amazing. For the appetizer, we decided on the Crabmeat Tropical. This was crabmeat mixed with homemade alioli served on an avocado half. Yes, you read that right: crabmeat on top of an avocado! It tasted as amazing as it sounded. I seriously could have eaten an entire one by myself and not even felt bad about it.  For our entree', we decided to get the medium meat paella (which is made for 2 people to share) and split it. I had never had paella before, but it is basically a cousin of my beloved jambalaya, so I was immediately on board. I really liked that there was chicken, pork and sausage in it, but there wasn't an overwhelming amount of meat and it the flavors were balanced nicely. The meat mixed well with the rice/veggie mixture of the dish and made for a really nice meal.  I loved Lola's atmosphere and our waitress was very nice and attentive. I will definitely be back here again.

This is a great little neighborhood coffee shop.  They serve coffee, donuts, breakfast and the usual coffee house faire.  The place is family owned by an awesome guy named Phil Songy and the staff is really nice and personable.  If you come in, you will be made to feel like a part of the team.  My favorites are the jelly donut holes and the apple fritter.

Really small bar, but a really cool place to see a band.  I spent Saturday evening here for the first time since the whole renovation. We were there to see a band and it was a good crowd. Circle Bar is extremely small, so we were sure to get there early so that we had a good spot at the bar to sit and enjoy the evening. It filled up fast, but the crowd wasn't too bad. The band performed in a small area in a corner and everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves.  The staff was super friendly and attentive and all and all it was a great time.

Hmm...I guess I'll review it, since I go here a lot.  If you have been to one Walgreens, you have been to all of them.  Most of their stuff is a little overpriced, but they do good business because you don't want to drive all the way to Target to get a fresh tube of Maybelline.  They have cute stuff for the holidays and lots of Saints trinkets, if you are looking for a last minute gift,  Really good ice cream selection (Blue Bell) and they carry the new flavors.  They have a decent, yet overpriced "grocery" aisle, but really, who goes to Walgreens for that stuff, anyway?   The one department that is always a "win" is the photo section.  Great priced and high quality one hour prints.

I ate here last week and I am just now getting around to writing a review for this place, mainly because my experience here was pretty forgettable.  The food here is a solid three stars: not overly great, not bad at all, really just "meh".  I got the chicken flautas which came with a side of rice and beans.  It wasn't bad.  Halfway through the meal, I was wishing that I had added a little spice to the rice and beans, as it was really kind of bland.  The prices weren't bad and I would say that it's a good place for a fast hot lunch.  I will say that "Amigos" does have an extensive menu and even the pickiest eaters are sure to find something that they will enjoy.  Unfortunately, the Westbank doesn't have as diverse of a selection of Mexican faire as other parts of the city, but my Westbank "go to" is still El Mesquite Grill.

This is a lovely bit of green space right in the middle of Carrollton Avenue.  This spot is ideal for parents because there's a jungle gym for the kids. I sometimes have meetings here, especially when the weather is nice. The park is small, but it's well kempt. There's a walking trail to get some exercise in, when it isn't too hot. I especially like the occasional art market that they have here. I used to go all the time a few years ago and I remember that it used to be packed with different booths filled with artful offerings.   Palmer isn't as visually stunning as Audubon Park, right down the street, but it's a nice part of New Orleans.

Really conveniently located and has a quaint little convenient store attached. Gas was $3.41 when I filled up here back in June. Not too bad. I felt safe in the area and didn't feel the need to constantly look over my shoulder. Card machine worked fine and I was in and out in no time.

The Saints may not have made it to the Super Bowl this year, but they get to be my 300th yelp review, so that's something!  Since I was born and raised in New Orleans I am, of course, a life long Saints fan.  I was lucky enough to go to my first ever (can you believe it?!) Saints game this year, and I had such an amazing time.  The energy in the dome was indescribable and you could feel something magic in the air.  Even when I don't have tickets to a game, I watch every Sunday with friends and cheer them on no matter what.  Saints fans are some of the best in the world.  Win or lose, Saints fans will go down to the airport and welcome players home from their away games.  I don't have to talk about how amazing the Super Bowl win was and what it did for the people of the city.  You already know all that.  You already know all about the victory parade that stopped the city and the fact that there wasn't one report of violence that evening.  The Saints definitely do something magical for New Orleans, and for that we will always be grateful.

I just adored this place and I adore it enough to give it 5 stars.  They have a huge beer selection here and the bartender, Todd, was really good at helping me find a beer that I would like. The bar itself it small, but I dig that because it makes for a cozy atmosphere. Although it's small, it's good for groups because they have 3 "picnic style" tables inside and a bunch of them outside, so don't be afraid to bring some friends along.  Although the beers are imports, and some of them are on the more expensive side, most of them are super well priced and $5 or less in many cases. That's awesome because you can try a bunch of different beers without breaking the bank.  Bonus points because they are smoke free and will be serving food soon!  I will definitely be back and I can't wait to tell people about this awesome new addition to the uptown area.

Who doesn't love Roman Candy?  For those of you who have no idea what it is, it's basically taffy. It is SO good. If you can get to it when it's still warm, then you will be in heaven. Every New Orleans kid grew up on the stuff. I didn't know they had a mobile cart and the only time I ever had it was at the zoo. I remember I used to get my parents to buy me a bunch so that I could take some home and have it later. Amazing.

Wow. I am so glad there is a place like this on the Westbank!  So, this building used to be a Twin Peaks. I don't know anything about Twin Peaks other than it's a Hooters rip off. Grand opening, grand closing. When I heard that a Legacy Kitchen franchise was taking it's place I was excited. When I heard it was going to be a steak house, I immediately bookmarked it. The Westbank doesn't have enough good steak places (okay, we have Outback), so this was a fine welcome to the neighborhood.  I stopped in for lunch with a coworker and the menu looked amazing. I knew that I wanted to start with the onion rings because I'm an onion ring freak and the Westbank doesn't have good onion rings anywhere and I'm here to judge everything. I also got a cheeseburger with bacon on it because I make excellent decisions. "Well, why didn't you get a steak?" Because it was a work lunch and I didn't have time to nap. Anyway, the onion rings came out in a tower type thing and they were out of this world! You have to get the onion rings. I might go back just for the onion rings. They are perfectly fried and light and so good! My burger, which I ordered cooked medium rare (yeah, you heard me), came out PERFECTLY cooked. I usually order burgers medium rare, because if I say medium it comes out well done, but this burger was excellent. Thick, juicy and perfectly cooked. The bacon on top was crisped to perfection. It might be the best burger on the Westbank -we have a best onion ring/best burger thing going on here, people. For serious.  On top of the excellent food, the waitress was great and, although she was a tad slow with getting drink refills and an extra plate, she made up for it with her sweet temperament. Will I go back? Uh...duh. Lucky me, I have an excuse in that my boyfriend loves onion rings too and I will be bringing him here so he can try them.

5 stars for a BK?? Whaaaaaat?? Before y'all go chasing me off of Yelp for finally posting one too many 5 star reviews, hear me out. First of all, those are 5 "fast food" stars. Second, this place earned it for a few reasons: they actually got my order right on the first try and they included napkins. It doesn't take much, huh? Considering I am now officially done with the Westbank Burger King because of their foolishness of not being able to successfully complete a simple "cheeseburger and fries" order without there being some issue that causes me to exit my car and actually go into the building, the bar is set pretty low.  I went through the drive thru and I got a cheeseburger and fries and a small coke. I was almost embarrassed to even be seen here because MoPho is next door and I REALLY wanted pho, but I was in a rush. Anyway, they got my order right and it was hot and tasted like food. So...five stars.

This is definitely my "go to" when it comes to milk. It's always fresh and delicious and the turnover from cow to milk jug is pretty speedy. Seriously, their milk is that fresh!  As Eileen mentioned, their seasonal Egg Nog can't be beat and makes for a delicious holiday treat. I am also a really big fan of Brown's chocolate milk because it has a lot of flavor of doesn't just have a "hint" of chocolate in it.  Whenever Brown's is an option in the dairy case, it is always my first choice.

I was only here for coffee, and not snacks, but I couldn't have had a better experience.  I was in the area and starting to feel drained when I noticed this spot, so I popped in. They were actually decently busy with a lunch crowd and I was just getting iced coffee to go. The coffee was really good and rich and packed a nice punch and I'd come back for more. The menu looks tasty, so I might have to try the lunch one of these days.

A nice little PJ's located on Tchoupitoulas in a strip mall.  It's quaint and the atmosphere is nice and they do nice business, since they are right next to a grocery store.  It's nothing overly special, but it's a nice location close to the Uptown neighborhoods.

This place is insane.  Ugly secondhand clothes marked "vintage" that cost $50.  Yeah, okay.  When I shop at a thrift store (and that is exactly what this place is, don't let the high prices and the fancy word "consignment' trick you) I am doing so because I'm interested in saving money.  I'm sorry, but you can't just slap a sticker that says "vintage from the 80's" on something and use that as an excuse to overcharge people.  I guess they are targeting tourists and I'm sure some pay the prices, but if you are local, you are way better off just heading on over to the red, white and blue and searching the racks.  I just don't understand where Funky Monkey gets off charging these prices when Buffalo Exchange has way better stuff, a bigger selection, is way cheaper and is located a block up.

Someone reviewed this place and called it "a place for tourists", and while this is true, locals shouldn't be afraid to check this place out.  First of all, if you go for breakfast, be prepared to wait in a line.  This is an extremely popular breakfast place.  Whenever I go, it's usually for a late (after 9) dinner.  I like the hamburgers.  They are prepared on the griddle, right in front of you and they actually toast the hamburger buns in the burger grease.  Yeah, it's not the healthiest, but, wow, is it good!  This is also the only place that I will actually consume a milkshake.  I am sure they are probably 1,000 cals a serving, but it's nice to treat yourself every once in a while.

Oh Dijon, I have been sitting on this review for over a week trying to decide in which direction to take it.  I'll start at the beginning.  We came here early on a Saturday night and we were seated immediately.  Maybe because we had reservations, but really because there was no one else there.  Not a soul, besides the people working there.  The first thing that came out was the amuse bouche.  It was good.  Some sort of crab thing.  My only complaint was that the crab tasted, well, fishy.  Same goes for our appetizer, which was crab meat inside some kind of weird dough shell thing.  It tasted overly fishy.  Like, I wondered whether or not it was fresh or if it had been sitting out all day.  For my entree, I got the rabbit stew.  It was ok, but it was really "meat dense" (I would have loved it over rice, instead of a few strands of fettucine) and the rabbit didn't have a ton of flavor.  Honestly, I've had better at Cochon.  Way better.  My friend had steak which also kind of sucked.  Sorry, just being honest here (it's how we learn).  Kurt, the owner, came over to inquire how our meal was (I guess when you are the only customers in the place on a Saturday, the owner gets friendly).  We were honest with him about our meal and he was understanding, although I was a little put off when he asked me "have you even ever had rabbit before?", as if it was MY issue that the food didn't blow me away.  Sorry, I know what I like.    Honestly, the best part of the whole experience here was our server Nicole, who was really friendly and seemed happy to be there, even though we were the only people in the entire place.  I'm willing to go back (for lunch) and give the place another try, but they need to make some menu changes.  I would definitely suggest more seafood options.  It is New Orleans, after all.

This is a Metairie institution that my great aunt and uncle used to love.  I stopped in here with my dad for lunch at around noon on a Tuesday. Considering the time, the place wasn't super packed and we were seated quickly. Looking over the menu, it's all local New Orleans kind of food.  For a starter, I decided on a cup of turtle soup. It came with some sherry to mix into it, and while I have had better turtle soup elsewhere, it was good and it definitely hit the spot. For my entree I got the fried oyster platter that came with fries and a side salad. The platter was perfect. It was huge and packed with large oysters that were juicy and lightly fried. I liked that the platter came with both tartar sauce and cocktail sauce for dipping. There was so much food that I was more than happy to be able to take some of it home for later.  My dad got the lump crabmeat au gratin. It looked amazing and it was covered with cheese, which made me definitely want to try it the next time I am here.  My experience here was great. Heather was our waitress and she was super nice and attentive and made sure that we had everything that we needed. I will definitely return to Mr. Ed's.

Okay, so technically I went to the Bayou Market Express which is right next to the buffet, but I don't think it's a whole separate business. It's all in the same family, so let's just go with it. Review go here.  I passed through here on my way to Boomers because I am Westbank to the core. I needed a snack and this place had food: sold. I decided to get a chicken salad sandwich. Super brave, right? A mayonnaise based sandwich made sometime earlier in the day, just waiting for me in a refrigerator that I am putting way too much faith in. You order at the counter, tell them what you got and pay for it. Pretty easy. They have all sorts of things fresh made like poboys, fried chicken, fries and things like that- snack foods. The chicken salad sandwich was $7.  The sandwich was decent. It didn't knock my socks off, but I was hungry so I enjoyed it for what it was. It's on poboy type bread which kind of overwhelms the chicken salad, so I just ate the chicken salad and ditched the bread. Don't judge me.  I didn't get violently ill or die: three stars!

Ok, y'all. This motel really isn't THAT bad.  I've been here a few times for photo shoots and this is a pretty basic motel set up. For $59 a night, you get what I would basically call a "crash pad". This isn't where you stay if you want fancy accommodations, it's where you stay if you want a place to sleep after hanging out in the city all day. It was perfect for my "retro motel" photo shoot, so I really liked the fact that everything was a bit out of date.   The room itself is a little dated. The TV is old and the comforter and curtains look like they were purchased in the late 70's. The bathroom leaves a lot to be desired and probably isn't cleaned regularly.  There's an ice machine and a cold drink machine outside. I will say that the room itself looked to be clean. The bed was clean and nothing out of the ordinary or disgusting jumped out at me.  It's probably one of the better "cheap" Westbank motels, if you just need a place to sleep. The area seems pretty safe and I didn't see anyone questionable lurking around.

Full disclosure: I'm not a buffet person and I find the entire idea of a buffet pretty gross. However, I was outvoted so I found myself here hoping for the best.  This is a pretty typical Asian buffet- they have all of the traditional Chinese-American foods and they also have sushi rolls and boiled seafood like crawfish and shrimp. Buffets make me pretty nervous, so I kept my choices pretty basic. I got a couple of the veggie sushi rolls, crab rangoons, egg rolls and pot stickers. I basically stuck to stuff that I know came out of a package and had the least amount of human contact possible. Nothing stood out, but everything was good. One thing actually did like was the lobster au gratin which is basically lobster and a lot of cheese. I rolled the dice on that one, and lucky for me I survived the experience.  This place "is what it is". Don't come here expecting anything spectacular, but come here expecting to stuff your face for about $17.

I'm kind of torn about The Point.  This is a neat little lunch place in Harvey. They only serve lunch and close at 4. I met Dustin for lunch here, on his suggestion. They serve all kind of things from sandwiches and burgers to hot plates. It's cafeteria style, so you walk up and tell them what you want and they put it on a plate and you pay at the register and seat yourself. Not a bad setup for lunch.  I decided to get a club sandwich with sweet potato fries and Dustin got one of the specials, which was fried chicken with salad, corn and mac and cheese. My sandwich was okay. It was nothing overly special, but I enjoyed it. The sweet potato fries were a nice touch. I was able to try some of Dustin's chicken and mac and cheese. It was super good and for a lunch, you really get your money's worth.  I like the atmosphere of the whole place. The walls are decorated with Louisiana knick knacks and signs and the whole restaurant has a "50's diner" kind of feel. The staff was super nice and friendly.  I think that I would go back and maybe try one of the hot meals that they offer. They also have burgers, so I might check that out too.

Ohhhh yes. Panera Bread has finally landed on the Westbank and oh my gosh was it worth the wait.  When I saw that a Panera Bread was coming to Manhattan, I was pretty excited. I had never been to the Panera in Metairie, but I had heard how great this place is and I am a sucker for a soup and sandwich combo. I'm usually not a huge chain person, but the Westbank is sorely lacking in good deli places, so I am going to take what I can get.  Today was only the second day the this Panera was open, so I was pretty surprised that there wasn't more of a crowd at lunch. I guess word hasn't gotten out about the place yet- perfect.  I walked up to the register and decided to do the "You pick 2" soup and sandwich combo. I got a half of a bacon turkey bravo sandwich and a cup of the broccoli and cheddar soup. I also got an iced tea. Once you order they give you a buzzer, and when your order is ready, you go and pick it up at the window.  The food came out fast and it looked amazing. The sandwich half was a good size with fresh turkey, bacon, lettuce and tomato. Everything tasted really fresh and I loved it! The broccoli and cheese soup was a dream come true. This is one of my favorite all time soups and the Panera version didn't disappoint. I was a little nervous that the soup was going to be out of a can, but it tasted really good and I loved it. Bonus: they give you a baguette with your soup order, in case you want to dip!  This Panera is new so, of course, there are a few "bugs" to work out, but I loved the food and I will absolutely return. I am also really excited that they have a drive through, for those days where I don't feel like dining in.

I was so excited that David and I actually made it down early enough to catch a good part of Zulu.  I had never been to Zulu before and I knew that it was one of those parades that I just had to see. Everyone is familiar with the style of Zulu and, along with Rex, it's one of the big parades to roll through New Orleans on Mardi Gras day. The crowd was thick and the riders were having a great time and throwing generously. Of course, the "goal" was to catch a Zulu coconut, which I noticed that they were throwing copious amounts of, so I figured our chances were pretty good. We were in the back of a huge crowd when David put his hand up and a rider tossed him one and he caught it like a pro! It's so awesome that this was our first Zulu experience and we were able to get a signature throw.  The crowds are always a lot more mellow during parades on actual Mardi Gras day, so I enjoyed the parade and the big crowd was tolerable. I definitely want to make this a yearly tradition.

I visited this church, for the first time, to view their St. Joseph's Altar. I had heard that their altar is spectacular, and it definitely didn't disappoint.  The altar here is huge and gorgeous and decorated with everything from cakes and cookies to seafood and candles. I can see why people come from all over Louisiana come to see this altar. I tried to take some good pictures, but there was no way I could capture the majesty of this thing in one single frame. Needless, to say, the line was out the door.  One thing I like about the way they do things here: they have two lines. The super long line is for people who not only want to view the altar, but also eat some of the food and there is another entrance for people who want to see the altar, but don't want to eat. There are also people selling prayer cards, candles, holy water, rosaries and other religious items, if that is something that might interest you.  The outside of the church itself is amazing and lovely and is a beautiful addition to this quiet Gretna neighborhood. The grounds of the church courtyard are extremely spacious, and I liked that there is a nice area with benches, if you want to relax and say some prayers while enjoying the nice weather.

This restaurant has certainly made a name for itself in the year or so that it's been open. It seems that every time there's a "Best New Restaurants" list, Heard Dat Kitchen is on it. Up until recently, the place was only take-out so as soon as the opening a dining room section, I made it a point to stop by.  Heard Dat is located smack dab in the middle of a neighborhood and the only reason I knew which building it was is because of Yelp. I parked easily and popped in. I told the woman behind the counter I was there to eat in and she lead be around the building and down an alley to a room on the side where the dining room was.  Everything sounded so good, but I decided to go with the shrimp and grits. The shrimp were tail-off and the grits were creamy and tasty. There was also corn in it, which was pretty different, but I liked it. I liked that the portion wasn't too big, it was perfect for lunch and it was only $10. In fact, most of their dishes are around the $10-$14 range, which is pretty great considering what you get.  I have to go back and get the red beans and rice with fried chicken. Some other folks got that and it looked SO GOOD that I almost got an order of it to go.

Tried this place last night for the first time.  In one sentence: great food. awful singing.  In more than one sentence:  I was blown away by the unique selection of "goodies" on the menu.  Not only did they have traditional sushi, but they also had treats such as fried zucchini, fried spring rolls, mozarella sticks and more.  We got the fried zucchini and spring rolls to start.  They were so good.  I had my usual, (which, if you read my reviews, you know is the salmon sashimi, tuna roll, and philly roll).  We also got one other roll, called an uptown roll.  I was blown away at how well priced the food was.  The salmon sashimi was only $7!  At other places it is usually $10, at least.  Pretty awesome.   With everything we ordered, the bill was $39 and we were more than full at the end of it.    I didn't get any of it, but they have an extended menu of ramen.  I have never seen ramen outside of a college dorm (read: I'm no expert), but they have all types with beef and pork in it.  Definitely check this place out, if that's your thing.  The place also has karaoke.  Really bad (in a good way) karaoke.  To some, this is the main draw.  I would have to go back to experience this to the fullest.

Wow. So I didn't know this place had a yelp listing, hence the lack of check in. I didn't know it even existed.  A friend of mine, who lives in this neighborhood, actually brought me here after telling me about it and pretty much blowing my mind. I have passed this park probably a thousand times and never realized that it was a real park. I guess I just thought it was a lot or something. But it has benches and a pretty fountain and a really nice green space. If I lived nearby I would probably be here all the time on nicer days.
