This is a favorite of my friends in Nashville from the teen daughter to the professional father. And I can see why. Clothing, art, jewelry, toys, musical instruments! Wow I wish this store was in NOLA.  From the street it doesn't look that large, but it just keeps going and going. There is a small parking lot behind the shop with maybe a 2 or 3 spots. And the shop has both a back parking lot door and a front door on the street.   The staff was great, even getting a giant ladder so I could have just the flying cat that I wanted. I found several great Christmas gifts here and I only wish I had the $ to actually buy myself a bunch of clothes. Next time!

After moving a few times last year, I think this Gallery has settled in at the 600 block of Royal. It's a great space with lots of exposed brick and high ceilings...the better to showcase and hang art!  Beth helped me with my newest Barkus poster, as well as another from a couple of years ago that I skipped. She was great to work with and was very patient with my indecision.   The gallery still features a variety of artists who find their inspiration from our companion animals. They sell everything from original paintings to notecards so there is a price point for everyone.   Love the fanciful spirit of the art.

Lakeside was one of the first 2 malls in the GNO area.  And sometimes you can see it's 70s roots, but mostly the decor and the cleanliness of the mall is right on time.  My biggest gripe is that as the most successful mall in the GNO area it is almost always crowded.

First time over the new expanded bridge today! Wow! It's so nice. Gone are the memories of the super narrow scary bridge where a breakdown (or even slow truck) could ruin a whole trip.   I do still need to get accustomed to the on and off ramps since I was so familiar with the old ways but small price to pay to sail across.

TMI review...I'm not a big waxer. I've had allergic reactions to wax and I also have a big old scar on my leg that's pretty sensitive. But every now and then I break down and decide to bite the bullet.  The good:  I called and made an appointment about 30 minutes out.  They're open on Mondays. Space is nice and inviting. Yelp deal with check in 10% off.  The meh: Though the price was still high for lower leg only.  Wax wasn't fully cleaned up on one leg.  Good news is that I didn't break out into a rash and she worked quickly enough that my scar wasn't too irritated.

I was running errands on Magazine a couple of weekends ago and discovered that a store I was aiming for had shut down (disappointing!) but then I noticed a few doors down this new salad spot (intriguing!)  So it was time for lunch.  The set up was a bit confusing to me since I hadn't been to one of these yet  (because it feels like a franchise, right?)  Anyway, my salad was tasty and full of premium ingredients. No skimping here.  The ingredients were all really fresh (hey! it's in the name!) and tasty.  And I liked that you could completely customize your salad to your own particular taste buds.  Things I didn't like: I was dining in so I would have liked less disposable (and wasteful) options, like a non-plastic fork.  I also would have liked a better drink selection, although the water with lemon in a free dispenser was a nice touch.  Their ice tea did not seem fresh brewed to me, so I'd probably stick with water here in the future.  Or I would just take out since that's what it seems like you're supposed to do.  Which is some ways is too bad, since the day I went was gorgeous and all the french doors were open to both Magazine and Webster.

I've had fine meals at Katie's and I've had mediocre meals here too.  It is a fun neighborhood spot and the menu is diverse...and maybe too big. How can you make all those various items well?  However the variety is part of the selling point, in that if you're with a group then there is something for everyone.  I would probably give this 4 stars but on my last visit both entrees came with items that were not mentioned on the menu and we both would have opted to NOT have had we known.  There drinks are good.  The A/C can be spotty...like lots of old buildings.

I was here for a birthday party on a Friday evening WITH the bubbles happy hour drinks! I had the Wycliff (too sweet for me) and the Charles Roux (weirdly heavy) but you can't go wrong with the Ruffino Prosecco. At some point I switched to the HH Mule's which were tasty and not too tart.   The birthday girl had reserved space for her gathering and I was able to sample some of the cheese from the cheese & charcuterie bar. Tasty. And I ordered a bianca flatbread which was good but a bit bland. I didn't get much roasted garlic at all.  The space is large with plenty of bar seats. They were jumping on a random Friday night in November. Definitely will be back for HH pricing and bites.

While I normally choose a local shop, I was in the neighborhood & hadn't been to a Baskin Robbins in a while.   The sales clerk was a little done...but we were there near closing and I was insisting on tasting the weird colored ice cream (like acid green and bright purple). Those flavors mostly tasted like really artificial candy.  So I went with Mississippi Mud.  It's a little less expensive then CC but the product is definitely inferior. Still not a bad choice if you're in the neighborhood.

I want to be comfortable in this space and it is gorgeous and the happy hours that I've been here, it's been hit or miss with the bartenders, like everywhere. But I just can't.   I am frustrated that this beautiful space was a bit of a political boondoggle and that it was renovated with money that was intended for New Orleans Public Libraries. This is not the fault of the current management or staff but it leaves a bad taste.   I wish them well.

Great used book store in the quarter.  It's just the sort of place that you think all the shelves will fall over on you...and I mean that in a good way.    I've always thought that many quarterites go here to sell their books when they move, so usually a good selection fancy cookbooks and art books.

This shop was actually not part of my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom because she was not interested in hitting clothing stores. BUT I had stopped in the day before Thanksgiving with friends and got distracted and somehow left the store with the wrong dress.    I ran in while my Mom was in a different shop (that I had also been to 2 days before) and we switched out super easy and very gracious since the shop technically wasn't open yet.  I was even invited back for champagne in an hour. Alas, we had moved further along.  Bonus Toulouse (the bulldog) was not at the shop on Wednesday but on Friday he glued his nose to my pants to get a full whiff of my girl at home.  He made me feel extra welcome.

Oh wow. It had been quite sometime since I'd been in the Saint and probably never as early as I was this most recent time. But this where friends wanted to hang out after dinner, so there you go. Like all NOLA bars, I'm so glad they are non-smoking now. I seem to remember barely being able to see my friends through the haze.   Yes it's a dive bar but they offer a solid pour...I wouldn't order anything fancy. And the bartenders are great, until you annoy or anger one then you might as well leave. But that's the way of all dive bars. They usually have a guy on door who is appropriately terse and will check your ID, no matter your age so that's fun.  As always, entertainment value depends on who you're with and what's going on around you.

The go to place for men's suits in the city.  When my youngest brother graduated from college, I priced out buying him a good interview suit from the various places around.  Perlis ended up being a better deal than most of the department stores because of their free alterations policy.  And the alterations are for life...now if my brother had only kept the moths away from his suit, then it would have been more useful.  As for women's clothes, I know they carry a number of designer brands, and I've tried on a few things there, but have never purchased for one reason or another.  The gift section upstairs is very fun & unique.  This is not a store that you want to run into looking scruffy BTW

This is one of these events that I can believe I haven't reviewed.    I am NOT a bar professional but do love a good drink, especially when it's free! The tasting rooms are amazing and introduce you to a world of liquor or liqueur that I never knew existed.  I've taken vacation days the last two years to attend the weekday events.    There are also book signings, a gift shop, lectures, and a whole lotta schmoozing.  I still think my all time favorite tasting room was the Old New Orleans Rum mojito bar at 10 one morning.  There was fruit so that counts as breakfast, right?

Yum. Why has it been months since my last visit? Delicious tofu bun (which can be had without fish sauce) and included really tasty carmelized onions. We also had the  super spicy tofu cao. The menu isn't huge but that means that they can do a great job with the items listed.  I need to go back and try their banh mi and their pho....soon.  The owners are working hard to make sure everyone os satisfied. I only wish it was closer to my house.

Can I just say WOW! I was super impressed with almost everything I ate.  It's a buffet line and you can choose between one to all the items on the menu. I had the mac-n-cheese, okra-tomatoes-corn medley, collard greens and fried cauliflower. My friend had the white beans, jambalaya, mac-n-cheese and greens, plus a sweet potato pie. The white beans were amazing and I was jealous. The mac-n-cheese was delicious and was definitely better than versions made with chemically cheese. My two veggie sides were delicious but the cauliflower was a little greasy for me... I think I got the bottom of the pan. My friend's jambalaya had zero fake meat so it seemed like a pilaf to me but she said the flavor was good. And the pie was yummy.  This place is tiny so your best plan is to take out. We were lucky enough to grab a table as we paid so could enjoy our food there. I definitely had enough for two meals. Staff was great and friendly.  Parking is tight as there are a bunch of businesses in this building (martial arts in the garage in back, barber upstairs)... the parking lot is for the dojo so don't try to park there.

As I was traveling from point A to point B, I realized that I was starving so I decided to take a chance on this strip mall sushi joint.   The space is small and very basic. The staff was really nice and accommodating.  I ordered my rolls to go and so didn't really use table service....  The rolls were fine if basic. Everything tasted good...but I did my usual and declined the sauces on top. I hate gooey sauces on top of rolls. I think this makes me an unAmerican sushi eater.  I had a couple of rolls...and they were good so there's that. Next time I might try the sushi.  I do like that they have online ordering...not that I tried it since y'know, driving. But it doesn't seem to be the whole menu.

I went to Luke last month for lunch and really enjoyed my meal.  Even better my boss was picking up the bill; not that Luke is super expensive though.  I thought my blood orange hollandaise sauce (on shrimp farsi) was good enough to drink.  And I enjoyed a specialty cocktail but I can't remember the name, but it was light and perfect (and I was with my boss who doesn't drink, scandal!)  She had the crabmeat omelet and couldn't stop raving.  My only problem with the restaurant was that it was so loud.  It was difficult to have a conversation across a table and I'm generally considered...a high volume person.  Definitely looking forward to going back.

I had to have lunch at Il Posto today because I was craving the roasted beet & gorgonzola salad.  Amazing delish combination.  Sometimes I just need a beet fix.  Yes, I know that's odd.  I recently stopped in for breakfast with a small herd of family members and about 1/2 of us were immediately drawn to the orange cranberry scones which were fresh out of the oven.  Yum.  We may go here a little too often...I sometimes feel like Norm! as I walk through the door.

We grew up calling this the Point or the Point at the Lake. Not to be confused with Sunset Point which is evidently on the other side of the lake.  Yes, you went here to smooch your boyfriend (or girlfriend or whoever) on occasion but the real fun was driving out here when the waves are crashing and you can sit inside your nice warm, dry car and let the waves crash on you.  OK maybe this was more fun when it was my parents' car and I wasn't worried about the paintjob.  I drove out here on Saturday with my nieces so they could play along the lakefront. Most of old West End is just gone thanks to a series of hurricanes and for those of us who grew up eating Sunday lunches out this way, it's just sad. Some of the boat houses along Breakwater Drive are being rebuilt.  So while I love that this spot is still here. I was really uncomfortable letting my nieces run around because of the volume of trash on the ground. Some other families had the same notion and shared bread for them to feed the ducks that were on the marina side. The amount of rubble is considerable so flip flops were probably not the best footware.

I am not a bowler and I've mostly been here for family birthday parties, but I think it's a pretty good bowling alley. I was really impressed by the upgrades the alley has made (since the last family party...whenever that was). There are fancy digital score boards which flash images when the player gets a strike or spare. They even have a vending with socks for sale in case you forgot to bring some.  It does have a kitchen with basic fare. The pizza at my niece's party seemed to be enjoyed by all.  And I believe that there is a full service bar on site.  Again, I didn't partake of that today.  This is also the location of the Jefferson Recreation Dept's special needs bowling league. My niece loves it.

Fun atmosphere. great theme.  tasty drinks.  Since I was with my Mom who grew up during the worst of the red scare stuff, she thought the Soviet theme was pretty funny.  Yes, you can bring your aging mother to bars in the FQ and still have a good time

This place actually delivers to my work so that's a plus. And the pizza has a decent crust and the toppings were generous. Since they sell by the slice, it's nice that the slices are huge.   Now for the meh. The margeurita pizza had no basil on it and the cheese was definitely not a high quality. When a pizza only has sauce, tomatoes, basil and cheese, missing one is kind of a big deal.  The delivery person arrived on time and while one of our salads was missing; the location corrected that and delivered it within 15 minutes.

Color me surprised that this is a new review for me. I know I've eaten at this restaurant previously. And at multiple iterations of other restaurants in this space over the years...  Last night I enjoyed their delicious Coolinary menu and it did not disappoint. We had early reservations because it was packed on a Tuesday! So I was able to enjoy a HH old fashioned to start. Yum! LOVED the rolls that they dole out like gold during your meal. They are smart to not put a basket on the table; I would gobble them up like a piglet.   My first course was the tomato gazpacho with crab, watermelon and pequilo peppers; it was light and delicious. I was also able to snag a bit of the cobia ceviche and the shrimp risotto... both delicious but I made the right call for me. For my 2nd course, I had the salmon and they were kind enough to sub out the bacon vinaigrette for a saffron sauce. The corn bread pudding was delicious and the salmon was perfectly prepared. The sauce was light and airy. Delicious. If you're starving, get that pork shank... it's comically large and very tasty according to my dining companion. For dessert, I got the chocolate fudge pie, mostly because I was already too full and I knew that I was taking it home. Rich and decadent!  We also tasted their seasonal cellos which included dill, fennel, orange and lemon. I think I was the biggest fan of the fennel, but the orange was really the highlight for me.  Service was on point, like watching a well-choreographed dance, especially with the small space and so many people. The atmosphere is light and airy. And if you're dining alone, there is plenty of the room at the bar.   Excellent first Coolinary meal of the season.

A super girly vintage inspired gift shop. The staff were really helpful without being pushy and their stock was somewhat unique.  They had cute reading glasses, jewelry, and housewares. I loved the items that were arranged by color and the handmade items.  Plus free jelly beans since it was Easter weekend.

This is one of those weird spots that tries to be something for everyone. So I'm usually wary... But this is where friends wanted to go so....  We didn't have cocktails so I can't comment on that. But we ordered a variety of items. One friend got mostly items that I would associate with a Chinese restaurant and two others got mostly sushi and rolls. I got noodle soup because that's what I was craving. But you could also order a steak or pasta or chargrilled oysters. OK. Everything was fine. But the restaurant was pretty empty. I think they do beacoup take out business though.

This was my 2nd time (maybe 3rd) sampling the wares from this truck. Today it was a really delicious lobster/crab mac n cheese. Seriously amazing with an almost crab au gratin taste.  Previously I had there jicama watermelon salad which was also delicious. I will definitely need to stalk them a few more times and sample more dishes.  Prices are good & the food comes up quick AND the truck has an awning which is nice if it starts raining...

The Cellars fills an essential need to this suburban community, a place to buy wines (and liquor) that may not be available in the local grocery stores.  (Yes, grocery stores sell liquor in NOLA).    They have a good selection and sponsor tastings most Friday nights, which my uncle is a big fan of.  They have also sponsored seasonal dinners, which my parents have said were quite tasty.  A bit off the beaten path for me, but I am always willing to trek out there with various family members who live in the area.    They also have a deli counter which I really need to go try, especially since I recently heard that a cousin is managing it.  Prices are competitive.

I know folks who have had problems with other Tire Kingdoms.  But we've had great luck with this branch.  They've patched our numerous flats, ordered & installed specialty tires, and have been helpful and honest.

Bayou Tree has been taking care of the oak trees in front of my MiL's house for decades.  They cut down the 60 foot tall hackberry tree that was threatening to split our new house in 2...I mean who let's a hackberry get to be that big when it's 4 feet from the house?  They had to use a crane to take the pieces out over our roof.  Scary.  We've always found their prices reasonable and their works professional.  Besides removal & stump grinding (we've used both), they also do landscaping, planting, trimming, spraying, etc.

So much fun...the Rinard Gallery has actually been traveling around a bit. They are no longer in the 700 block of Royal, a sign redirects you to the 800 block BUT the gallery employee told me that they'll actually be moving to the 600 block as soon as their space is ready...probably April.  Once I found their great new space, I was able to acquire my 2014 Barkus poster (Dogzilla). The gallery also carries a number of other animal oriented artists. I've only ever purchased cards and Barkus posters from them but the staff has always been lovely.  If you are a pet person, checking out this gallery is a must.

It's an arena!  It's usually cold so bring a sweater.  The food is overpriced and so is the liquor...because y'know it's an arena.  But other than that it's pretty nice. The seats are comfy and everything is well marked so you can actually find where your seat is. And it is clean...including the rest rooms so yay for that.  Parking costs extra, so see if you can park on the surface streets (a couple of blocks away on Loyola is a good bet) which may only be metered until 6 pm.  PLUS last time I was with brother #4 and he knows all the best routes and we were out of there in no time and beat the crowds.
I love Target.  That said I actually prefer the Metairie location.  I think the westbank store might be larger, but I find it's layout confusing.

I've been to GI a couple of times now and it's a solid choice for a group with diverse tastes; 1 person wants raw oysters and another wants a steak.  It can get really loud but the cocktails are good and the prices aren't bad.

My Hollygrove has grown since I reviewed them almost 4(!) years ago. The boxes/bags are still great deals on local produce that is super fresh and amazingly delicious.    But, wait, there's more! Now they are open 5 days a week (closed Mondays & Fridays) AND they have dairy products (cheese curds for Jennifer B!) and eggs and locally butchered meats and jams and jellies and juices and breads...whew.  If they had toothpaste I could have finished my weekly shopping here.  They do take credit cards and there's been a 10% off Yelp checkin deal for almost 2 years.  Now to start figuring out what I'm going to make with all this yumminess.

C'mon how do you NOT love beautiful hunks of sweet fried dough? I passed by on Saturday night late on my way home from the country with my beautiful friends. And we devoured an order of 2 and they had some cafe au lait (and a gumbo) and I had my standard chocolate milk.  Honestly I do prefer Cafe du Monde whose beignets are a bit fluffier than these. But when you're hungry and you're in the Metrys these will do nicely.  Bonus points because I spotted a local acting celebrity while I was there.

I'm glad that our visiting Portlanders wanted to go to Happy Hour here and partake of those 50cent oysters. It helped erase the memory of my last meal here (see previous review). We were seated in the overflow back room which was lovely...and much quieter than the main space. (Seriously, Luke, consider some sound reinforcement; your main dining room is beyond "lively" and into painfully loud when it's busy.)  I enjoyed my 1/2 price old fashioneds and as I'm not so big on the raw oysters, I ordered a delicious beet salad. And shared fries with the group.  Our server was lovely and handled a capacity crowd on Ash Wednesday with ease and grace. Our orders came out in a timely fashion and if there was a delay (with our 2nd batch of oysters), we were given more information. And of course, the company, Merilou, Melvin, Lindsay & Vicky was outstanding.

Looking for a new 'do and I'm still shopping around for a steady stylist.    Likes:  * hours are good...open until 9 a couple of weekdays * Billy asked what I wanted & he really looked at my hair for texture, movement etc. * worked on the cut for quite a bit with a lot of care.  Dislikes:  * Billy is the salon owner & was distracted by his employees * Gave a hard sell on products (hate that)  Verdict? I'm not sure yet.  I'll have to see how the cut grows out with my very fine, very straight hair. But I would be willing to give them another chance.  Also I saw no evidence of spa services.  Maybe that's a hold over from when they were in a larger space across the street.

Banting's is a much more no frills nursery.  They usually have a number of more mature trees and also have local favorites (like banana magnolia) that other growers do not.  Since they are no frills, they are also cheaper, sometimes.

Ah, the Fly...  I spent many a drunken high school evening here...before they started shutting it down to cars at night.  Great place to play frisbee, baseball, with the dog, or just hangout with your friends.  One word of warning is that certain afternoons seem to be 'cruise' time so be prepared to be stuck in traffic or breath exhaust.  As for the name, there used to be a structure in the center of the park against the river that sort of looked like a butterfly. The roof was designed to withstand hurricane force winds.  Unfortunately, the structure could not withstand being run into by a barge and had to be torn down.  I watched a riverboat race in the 70s from underneath the building (hey, it was shady).

This the shop to go to if you need to find all the goya cookies...which sometimes I need. Don't judge me.   I like that the Breauxmarts around town cater to their neighborhood so this shop carries more hispanic foods than the one on Magazine or the one in River Ridge. Otherwise the rest of the items are as high quality and fresh as all the stores.   Definitely a good spot for local items, sales and delicious cookies.

I had gone to the Petite Rouge truck on occasion so its good to see that they are now a bricks and mortar joint.   The menu is expanded from the truck which is really good for this non-coffee drinker. There are 5 or 6 teas (but not a printed list that I saw) if you want hot. Iced, I think they offer a ginger and an herbal and a black.   I went with the hot green which was delicious and OMG HOT. Like be careful and get an extra cup band hot.   It's a great use of this under used building and VERY spacious. Bonus points for the series of popups in the back room!

This is seriously the most adorable gardening & accessories store that I've ever been too. If I lived nearby I would stock up on all the cute items...and then, of course, kill any plants that I bought.  My aspirations of gardening are always better than my execution.    Next time, I'll come in without flight looming in my future.

This place is not closed as I thought last year. The daiquiri shop is on the Marigny side and Le Booze is on the Canal St. side. Maybe I was drunker than I thought whilst walking by..or tired. That's it. I was really tired.  This is a great basic bar on Bourbon where that sort of thing is rare. The bartenders are good (although do not expect craft cocktails here) and efficient.  BIG BIG bonus is that you can use the hotel restroom (although it is at the discretion of the bartender let you) AFTER you purchase a drink.

I didn't got to Saltwater Grill with high hopes since the reviews were mostly so poor.  BUT I had received a GC as a present from last Christmas, so I couldn't let a free meal slide.  I was somewhat pleasantly surprised.  The fried onion rings were excellent, with just the right hint of grease.  The bar made a good cocktail (my cousin even braved a milk punch and said it was good).  Randomly the restaurant was out of french bread (which is insane).  But the seafood dinners were tasty and our choices of sides were good, especially the asparagus.    Normally, I would probably rate Saltwater Grill a 3 or 3 1/2, especially for the lack of french bread (poboys on buns, please).  BUT (again) it turns out we knew our server so got excellent, if somewhat silly service.  So +1 for Becky.

This shop has been at this location forever... since the early 80s? But I hadn't stopped by in forever.  If you're in need of some loose linen, this is your spot. PLUS they had a mannequin out front with a crawfish button up shirt (men's sizing) that I might need. Instead I was practical and bought a rain cape for when I don't feel like wearing one of my many raincoats.  Lots of selection. Really friendly and helpful staff. Clothes and jewelry and crafts and what not.

My friends think it's weird that I don't wear contacts or glasses or anything.  Yes, I'm over a certain age, but so far my eyes are the same as when I was in my 20s.  But y'know who wants to gamble with their eyes? So I go get the complete work up every couple of years to make sure that no hobgoblins have taken up residence in my retinas.    The staff is efficient; the tests are disturbing (but really that the nature of medical tests involving your eyeballs); and the atmosphere attempts restful...something I will probably never achieve at a medical office without drugs.  There are a couple of physicians on staff, but I see Dr. Hendricks and he's thorough and professional.  I'll see him again in 2014.

Had a delicious mango snoball today.  It's interesting that real juice does not have the same viscosity as the syrup in normal snowballs so it's more like eating a juice filled with really fine ice rather than a traditional snoball.  I was glad to see that their machine was a snow wizard which does produce a very nice fine ice w/o annoying chunks.  I will definitely be back again.  The perfect treat for a warm September day.

As I walked down this end of Magazine Street I spotted this new interesting furniture stop in a former warehouse space. AND it has parking out front. AMAZING on this stretch.  It's all consignment furniture and the longer it stays, the cheaper it gets....which is clearly marked. By the dates on the furniture, it opened sometime last week. Lots of beautiful chairs and wood furniture including a nice collection of prieu dieu if you need that. I was interested in the many many foo dogs. There were quite a few Asian accessories.   Was allowed to browse without interruption but there were staff on hand to answer questions. Nice addition to this end of Magazine.

Katie's is a solid choice for lunch when you have a bunch of people with various needs. Picky eaters, NOLA only food, vegans? Yep all covered.   The prices are good for the quality and the service is usually very personable and easy to work with (see picky eaters/vegans/etc). The space is fun, but downstairs is "lively" so not the easiest place to have a business lunch in you have a loud group near you.   They don't take reservations unless you are a large party... which can be problematic on weekends and for brunch. I'm glad they opened up the upstairs for more dining, although that's not an option if anyone in your party cannot do a flight of stairs.   I've had fish dishes and salads and pasta here. All are tasty. Maybe I should eventually try a pizza?

Another year, another great Tales. Each year it seems to get bigger and better. Everyone I met was lovely...well, I did avoid some of the stinkier people. (C'mon it's south Louisiana in July wear deodorant!)  The expansion to three hotels (and lots of bars and other venues) spread the activities and the money all around the quarter.  And as a book geek, the bookstore with tons of cocktail books, memoirs and this year bitters! was great.

How I wish Slim Goodies was still open for dinner. That's when I ate here the most (pre-K). I love that their menu is inventive and has something for everyone.  I went most recently with my youngest nieces on a chilly weekday morning. There were only a couple of other tables and the server was kind enough to help us find the warmest table. The girls were pleased with their food but not so much with their hot chocolate (maybe too much powdered mix in the cup?).   Yes, it gets ridiculously crowded on the weekends but this place will always have a place in my heart for being open and serving me plain veggie burgers in Fall 2005.

A coffee truck that actually serves iced tea? Oh yeah I'm a fan. I was intrigued as I drove by this adorable little citroen truck this morning on my way into work. So once I dropped all my stuff, I wandered back over to check them out.  My friend got an Americano which she deemed very strong but tasty. And I got an iced sencha green. I love that they specify what type of green you're getting since I'm snooty like that. This morning they offered 2 iced options (the green and an herbal) and maybe 4 hot options (including a couple of black teas).   There was also a couple of homemade cookie type items for sale. I had the raspberry granola square and it was tasty and filling.  The person working the truck was hustling through the line and definitely offered the whole service with a smile thing. Plus oh so cute truck.

Oh, Rocky's, how I once loved you.  Your delicious pizzas, your yummy salads, your interesting music choices.  But then you got sloppy; I would get a pizza with someone else's ingredients slopped over on one edge.  The service got...odd.  Then that whole Katrina thing happened, and you abbreviated your menu.  OK we all had to adjust but you never returned to your pre-K menu and you eliminated all my faves.    Yes it is decent pizza but I go to Theo's or Reginelli's instead now.

I usually abstain from reviewing National chains because my input is sort of pointless.  BUT Today, I had my choice between 4 different alcohol samples at the Clearview location.  I chose to sample 3 out of the 4.  So I've got to give some credit to a place that gives me free wine.  Great prices on wine; good selection of imported food items; interesting kitchen/gift selection

This is a solid choice in the pantheon of RS cafes around town. The menu is the same as all the others. I like that this one is a bit smaller so not so warehouse-y.   The food is solid. The drinks (if you choose to imbibe) are strong and the coffee plentiful. The staff is what brings this up to 4 stars. They were hustling and making sure everyone was taken care of.  Be aware that this corner location has a ridiculously small parking lot which has been an issue since this building replaced the old laundromat at this location. SO there are valets who park your car. I don't think you get a choice in this. Yes the valet is free but don't be that person... and give the parker a tip.

Technically this is now Perestroika at Pravda as it is transition from a vodka bar to a rum bar. And I wonder what the final product will be. The owners are the same as the folks at Cure in the Freret Corridor.  The bar is much more stripped down than it was. Gone are the little lamps on all the tables...which is probably good as they seemed a bit hazardous. Much of the wall decor is gone too, so it seems a bit bare inside.  The cocktails are top notch. An delicious old-fashioned for $6 during happy hour? Yes please.

What a great place to hear music. The musicians are top notch and the venue is beyond intimate.  And I get that during busy times waiting in line to get in is part of the fun. But sometimes you're just not up to standing that long, y'know.

The cafeteria is looking pretty good after the renovation a couple of years ago AND new management came in as of January this year.  There are usually a few choices for lunch and a basic breakfast selection (eggs, variety of meats, oatmeal, grits, and biscuits).   My big gripes are that it really depends on who you get as a server/cashier as to how much food you'll get or how much you'll pay. And nickle & diming over some crackers, margarine is just irritating.   It is convenient but it's just kind of blah. If I have a choice, I'll go find a food truck on the street instead.

Pandemic update: I was in the FQ on a lazy Saturday just wandering around and enjoying being outside and that the throngs of tourists were absent and noticed that this shop was having a sale.  When I arrived I was one of two people shopping, so it was easy to socially distance. Everyone was wearing masks and you were allowed to try on clothes.   I scored a couple of pairs of linen pants event though linen season was over.... well is it ever really over when it's mostly hot here? And a couple of dresses all for a very reasonable price.   Call if you're specifically headed down to them and it isn't Saturday. Really this is a good idea for any FQ shop. Many aren't keeping their full normal hours with so few people spending money.

I caught up with this truck at a food truck rally in Broadmoor after work one day. The chefs were hustling to keep up with the crowd. I had the mac-n-cheese and a crawfish pie. The crawfish pie was tasty and a bit small. The mac-n-cheese was rich and delicious. I appreciated that they do have vegan options since those are hard to come by with most food trucks and veggie friendly red beans n rice.   If you're trying to hunt this truck down... well good luck. It looks like he posts to his FB page once he arrives at a location, but no schedule seems to be available. And his website still lists him as being in the Northeast. I did notice that his phone number is now NOLA local, so I guess that means he's relocated back to home.

Good stuff!  Took a risk and stopped in for a sammich.  Grilled shrimp & onions on an 8 in loaf of french bread.  Very tasty and fresh.  Plus I learned that are at least 7 flavors of Mad Dog and that Boones Farm Wine is still being made (Strawberry Hill, even).

Pandemic update: Whew... A friend talked me into actually eating in a restaurant. Yipes! But Muriel's handled everything beautifully. They took his name at the door for contact tracing and the tables were distance or had curtain barriers between them (looked like a heavy waxed cloth with artwork!). The staff was all masked and handled everything beautifully.  The coolinary menu was still available over Labor Day weekend so I enjoyed the house salad (delicious manchego), the shrimp and grits (wow I gobbled this up) and the creme brulee (which was AOK but not dazzling). My friend had the gumbo, the gulf fish and the bread pudding. He said they were all tasty. No drinks for me since I had to drive myself home.  Service was on point and I really appreciated the precautions they took. Patrons must be masked as they are escorted to their table and if they need to go use the restroom.

My favorite moments from the parade this year (2019). A subkrewe had just walked past and started chanting SHARK! Then they all ran around in circles creating a Sharknado. Good times. Also the King Cake babies dancing then returning to their natural state by laying on the ground, arms and legs up. OH! And the pacman antics. All you dots are underrated! The game would be nothing without you! And everyone was having fun.  With nothing else going on this past Saturday night, the parade was the biggest I've seen and so was the crowd.   Special shout out and thanks to the krewe of trash pickup!

I've been to dinner here a couple of times and most recently to the Eatventful sponsored shindig.    The food has always been tasty and the portions appropriately sized.  The tapas portions last week were perfect for the price.  The cocktails are inventive and seasonally appropriate.    Now if I had fewer cocktails, perhaps I would be able to describe the food better...

Dorignac's is great for local items, local produce and liquor. They also have a wide selection of prepared foods AND a decent selection of items from local restaurants. Their staff is helpful and knowledgeable.  During the pandemic, mask wearing has not been 100% amongst employees and customers. One employee was only wearing a face shield which is just frustrating to me. Another took his mask off to have a long chat with a customer. And now that Jefferson Parish has lifted the mask mandate, I probably won't be back for awhile.

I do love the fancy decor of this bar...attached to Broussards Restaurant. You feel very swanky have a drink and visiting with friends.   Before the opera the other night, I stopped in for a beverage and snack. Their HH bites are $5 each and are very tasty. I had the fries and the shrimp remoulade, 2 shrimps with a bit of salad, which were perfect. I probably could have eaten a 1/2 dozen more of these. But the fries were plentiful and filled me up. I had a lovely sparkling rose for $7 HH price.   BEST of all was the friendly staff. I had recently been to another fancy FQ bar, attached to a restaurant and could barely get the attention of the staff. So that I ended up chatting with the workers about the weather, the opera, what their other jobs were... you know the usual, was great.

I've wanted to attend Chewbacchus since it's first year (I was even a kickstarter supporter), but it was always parading against Endymion which is family central for me. Not this year!  Since I had my Mom and non-driving brother with me AND they wanted to see the uptown parades first, I ended up using a parade tracker app and stalking the parade.  We ended up near St. Claude & Elysian Fields and had an excellent view of the parade and I enjoyed it immensely.  Loved the shout outs to various specific shows (Star Wars, Space Balls, Star Trek, Dr. Who, etc) and to genres (Zombie, cartoons, etc). All the costumes were awesome and my handmade throws were super-cool.  Seriously, it looked like everyone was having an excellent time, especially Peter Mayhew (AKA the real Chewbacca) and his wife.  A must see for carnival!

Review for the hotel bar only.  The building is a great retro-fit from an old office building (at least from the lobby, public area perspective). The decor and colors all feel very homey and retro.   I was waiting on friends and chose to hang out at the small hotel bar in the lobby rather than the bar at Josephine Estelle and it was happy hour (4-7 daily)! I got a discount sparkling ($5 or $6?) and some snacks... I can't find a menu online to say specifically what. My wine was tasty and the snack was good. Bartenders were friendly and helpful.   There was a DJ in the corner and he definitely added to the ambiance without being so loud that I couldn't hear my friends. PS there's a real black & white film photo booth in the back near the elevators for photo shenanigans with your friends.

After seeing a coworkers cute Saints T scored from this boutique and hearing good things from the Yelp community, I decided to take a gander.   Yes black & gold shirt stock is cute and different from other stores. Great sale rack where I scored an excellent Christmas present for one of the nieces. Sales person was sweet and helpful but not pushy and offered good customer service.  Loved the layout; I'll definitely be back to see what spring styles they will be offering. My only complaint is the usual about boutique sizing...which isn't really their fault.

Whatever you do, leave a bulky purse or jacket in the car. The paths through the stock are narrow and you may feel like you will be buried in an avalanche at any moment.  The pricing is uneven. Some items were really well priced and then others were really high. Unfortunately, the place is so jam packed that some of the stock is being ruined by the clutter.   The staff member was helpful and picked his way through the piles to get to display cases. Bring a flashlight to better see into the back of the heavily stocked and crowded cases.

What a lovely courtyard! When I stopped in at the holiday shopping market at HNOC, I realized I was starving. The HNOC cafe to the rescue!  I twas a lovely day to eat outside and I enjoyed the delacour salad. It was HUGE even without adding a protein. And with the super tasty bellegarde bread and butter a great meal. The beets and the dill dressing were perfect together.  Ordering at the counter was easy. And the service was great.

Since the Dueling Oak in City Park have been mentioned in our talk threads, I remembered that I was going to add a listing for this AMAZING old tree.  Just to the left (as you face the gates) of the Sculpture Garden in City Park, stands this magnificent tree. Even if it didn't have an interesting history, the tree itself is a beauty.  In the mid-19th century, this was the site of duels (supposedly) because it was a bit out of town and honor could be defended without others getting involved. There used to be a pair of oaks but one was destroyed in a hurricane in the 1940s.   I'm grateful that this 300 year old behemoth is still standing...  http://neworleanshistorical.org/items/show/109

LOVE their menu... LOVE. The seafood hotpot is the best dish I've eaten in New Orleans this year. SERIOUSLY OMG AMAZING... Ok I might be done with the all caps.  Other items consumed the Hamachi (delicious), spinach cavatelli which is like the fanciest mac-n-cheese in the whole world, carrots (Charles is correct about the yumminess).   For cocktails, I had the Letters of Transit which was perfect but doesn't seem to be on the menu anymore. I've also had their amazing frozen sangria. And I know a couple of friends LOVE the Adromeda.   The dining room is lively, especially when the bar area is full. Service is on point! I love the formal dining service in a more casual environment. Every member of the staff was excellent.  Honestly, I can't wait to get eat here again!!

I stopped in for what I thought would be a quick visit on Friday night. Wow. I should have stuck to my regular store. This was only my 2nd visit to this location.  The aisles are tight. Be prepared to say excuse me to other shoppers every few minutes. The aisles that aren't tight? Piled high with stock in the middle of the space so that you still have to run an obstacle course.   I found what I needed and then proceeded to check out and every line was LONG. Ok so there was an after-work rush. I attempted to use a Rouses GC that I received as a gift. Nope. The machine wouldn't take it. And my sweet cashier tried. Rather than tie up the already long line. I was directed to customer service. Where I stood and stood and stood. There were 2 people staffing the desk, but they mostly spoke to each other and then started taking people who wandered up rather than those of us in line... who couldn't maneuver because of random stock displays in the middle of the floor. I was told that it was my fault for waiting in line. OK.   I gave up. And I'll figure out the GC thing at my regular Rouse's.

I first became aware of this NOLA tshirt company when they were still doing internet sales only. Then they had a popup shop and now their own bricks and mortar! Good for them.  Good selection of shirts and fun designs. Plus some other local lines are carried in this tiny store. The tiny store means that they were trying to keep it to only a couple of people at a time which was a Sisyphean task for the poor store clerk. Masks are of course required.  When I've been in the sales staff has been great about finding sizes and generally being helpful while not pushing the hard sell.

I parked near this shop for the parade on Saturday. And thought, "bittersweet? I know them... pop up? market? who cares? CHOCOLATE!" So I stopped in. I was in desperate need of a tea and they had several choices, iced. The mango was perfect, strong but not bitter.  I also decided I deserved an orange cranberry scone and some chocolate bark. Both were super tasty and the scone was HUGE. I might have snacked on it over the course of a day. So many cranberries! The chocolate bark was tasty and nice and dark.  The location is lovely but small. There were a couple of people camped out, coffee-shop style. But there were still plenty of tables since other folks were like me and getting there goodies to go.  If this shop was near my house or work, I would be in trouble! I can't wait to go back and try their plated food.

LOVE that the old Maylie's space has a restaurant that is as beautiful as it was... OK Maylie's (which closed in the 80s was kind of run down but it was still beautiful and that wisteria vine was gorgeous in the spring). Definitely a 5 star space especially considering the last incarnation that was here.  My review is for the brunch menu only. The menu was interesting and had some variety to it. The winner was the dutch baby pancake... that lemon curd was to die for. Even my friend who isn't into sweet breakfast was swayed. One friend had the crab cakes which she said were good but was raving about the duck fat potatoes underneath. The other friend had the couchon and grits. And I had the smoked salmon and egg. So here's the thing each of our dishes had a poached egg and none of the eggs were poached properly. All the yolks were set and for one of us the yolk was set but the white was somehow undercooked. It was weird.   For my salmon dish, it was tasty and the salmon was well cooked and not overly salty, but the hollandaise (of which there was maybe a tablespoon) was only on the egg, when the salmon could have used the moisture. I think the dish could be excellent with a bit better plating and egg cookage.   Our drinks were tasty (mimosas and an old fashioned). And they were offering a Veuve special which we did not participate in. One of my friends has been to their happy hour and said it was great but they don't have any information on that on their website.   Service brings this above a 3 since our server was hustling especially after the restaurant filled up by midday. They've only been open since September so I hope they find their footing.

Went to Felix's on this past chilly/rainy Saturday with my parents. Since it was raining, I really appreciated being able to park underneath the restaurant and avoid the drizzle (there are about 4 spaces). And there's an elevator up to the restaurant (but also a couple of sets of stairs), so that was important for the parents.   We got an assortment of items. I got my standard fried shrimp plate; Mom got the fish of the day grilled; and Dad had the trio of soups. The shrimp were great...perfectly fried and a nice size, but the cole slaw that came with was meh. It was a little too sweet for me so maybe they added sugar? Mom loved her redfish and couldn't stop raving about it. Dad's soups were very small but since he ate part of our meals it was OK. He really enjoyed all three soups and Mom loved that they were served in cute demitasse cups.  As for service, the restaurant was mostly empty. But our server would disappear for long periods of time and it didn't seem like things were firing quickly from the kitchen. It was mostly just curious as to what was going on.  Also the restaurant is chilly. It was a cold day and like much of New Orleans it seems like the restaurant was designed for hot weather. My Mom got really chilled which was the only issue with delayed service.

As a non-beer drinker, I often end up at beer places because of friends. I was grateful that they offered lemonade as a non-beer option. I just wish they had something else.  My friends seemed happy with the selections on tap. And there was a food pop-up happening if you need snacks. The day I was there, a DJ was spinning so that was fun.  As it is summer, please be aware that the space does not have A/C. It does have fans and that helps but I would have dressed differently had I known.  It's kid friendly and has a variety of games and fun things to keep the kids distracted. My favorite was when a toddler ran in and stole the cornhole bean bags. His Mom was pretty mortified but the teams cheered his efforts so good sports all around.

Every doggie loves some fun romping with other pups, right? (If your dog doesn't resemble this remark, this isn't the place for him or her.)  Sienna loved running on the levee (pre-arthritis & orthopedic problems) and she loved romping with the other dogs.    This is where to go if your dog wants to play in the moshpit, if your dog gets scared or aggressive, please stay home.

I met a group for lunch earlier this month. And I do like their premise of a meat and (1, 2, or 3). And I enjoyed the seasonality of their menu. The space is lovely and lowkey...old school diner meets farmhouse meets hipster thriftstore and I mean that in a complimentary way.   My group had the fried chicken, fried catfish, sauteed shrimp and a pig ear sammich. For sides we had the sweet potatoes, cabbage, wintermelon salad. The sweet potatoes were the most versatile of the sides and went with everything. My friend did not like the cabbage which she thought contained fish sauce. The wintermelon salad was tasty but it's acidity fought with my shrimp.  Here's where it gets a bit difficult... my friend got 2 huge pieces of fried chicken (both a breast and a thigh) and I got 3 large shrimp and the price point was similar. Yes shrimp are more expensive than chicken. But the disparity in the portion size was glaring.   The food was all tasty and I would rate it more of a 3.5 because of the weird portioning. There was also a huge group in the back the day I was there and so the meal took a bit longer than I actually had for a workday lunch.

Wow!!! The special of the night was a pompano sashimi. AMAZING!  We arrived at 6:30 and the restaurant was filling up so we opted for the sushi bar. I would recommend dining with just one friend OR coming early. There was a party of 6 and a party of 5 when we arrived plus all the small tables so they were slammed.  Even so our mostly raw dinner came out quickly. Besides the amazing special, our group of three had the Snow White, the Million Dollar Baby, the Under the Sea, the Dark Forest and smashed cucumbers plus five scented edamame. My other favorites were the Dark Forest (mushrooms and tofu) which came with rice and the Million Dollar Baby.  The cucumbers and edamame sides were delicious. We also had a beer, the mojito and a senseition. I had the senseition and the ginger/lime was strong but it was tasty. My friend loved her mojito and we just wished our waiter had actually checked back at some point to see if we would have liked more drinks. Oh well.  Will definitely be back soon!

Haven't had NY Pizza in almost 20 years and I don't know why it's been so long.  Tonight we ordered the Queens: mushrooms, artichoke, feta...but not sure I had a spinach on mine.  The crust was excellent.  Love that the new location is closer to home.

After a lovely day of lounging/eating/drinking with the amazing Vicky, Lindsay & Larissa, we decided that we were hungry again and so wandered over to La Casita for some light supper on a Saturday night since tacos sounded like the thing to do.  We ended up sitting at the bar since they had reservations for a large party at all their front tables. But seriously this is a small restaurant (maybe there is a back patio in the right weather?) so don't plan on coming with a herd.  We had cocktails which were fine and well priced, although we missed happy hours by about 5 minutes. The tacos were fine too. The thing is that I don't really remember what I ate. The food was fine but not really memorable. I think I ordered 2 tacos...maybe 3 and I was full. Done.  The bartender was cool with splitting up our bills and we paid via a cube...which seemed weird in a restaurant setting but maybe it's the future.  I feel like maybe they're still working the kinks out...there was confusion about a few thinks and I would definitely give them another try.  5 stars for the company btw.

I hate to be the odd person out but 5 stars? I don't think so. Yes this restaurant is new so I guess I'm being generous with my 4th star... but really I think a 3.5 is what my rating should be.  I went with friends on a Sunday night. and the restaurant was packed. But my friend had made a reservation so cool. We were seated near the open door to the hotel lobby next door. At some point a large group of friends gathered in that space and were HOLLERING, which cool have fun, but it echoed into the restaurant and made talking with my friends nearly impossible. When I asked about closing the door they said it has to stand open while they are operating. OK. Whatever.  Service was... odd, maybe trying for quirky or fun, but mostly odd. There were no bubbles by the glass so I just decided on club soda. But my friends found a beer and a glass of wine that they wanted.   Food wise, I had the gulf fish crudo which was lovely and flavorful. I would have loved more mirliton and satsuma. And the gnocchi which was good but the ratio of gnocchi to toppings was off. I had beaucoup crispy kale and mushrooms and not enough gnocchi to go with. My friends had the gumbo, bbq shrimp and the hangar steak. They seemed to enjoy their dishes.  The prices are a bit high but it's a hotel restaurant. The space is spartan/modern and a bit loud.

Great produce selection.  Plenty of cheese, kosher items, Italian food, and seafood.  AND let's not forget the liquor prices.  + they have fabulous baked goods at excellent prices  I was there just before NYE and the little old ladies were lined up for the champagne samples!

Still my go to shipping spot. The service is always friendly and courteous. They are very willing to find the best shipping method at the best price.   The retail/gift items are still there and definitely show a local flare, so if there is a line you can shop while you wait.  They also always have snacks out, either fresh fruit or cookies which is a really generous, personal touch.

So I finally made it to the uptown location of this chain pizza joint...mostly because they mailed me a $10 off coupon and it was about to expire.  The service was sort of ridiculous. The staff seemed to be trying but they were just completely off their game. We had to ask for water refills (after rejecting my 1st 2 drinks...one because I was given an Arnold Palmer instead of an iced tea and then the iced tea because it tasted like a mix rather than brewed) and plates. They were slammed and apologized for the mis-steps.  The salads we had were yummy and the garlic knots with beer cheese were tasty. The pizza was more just meh. We had the Kosmic Karma and I was not a big fan of their pesto.   We were seated downstairs because trivia was happening upstairs (and seemed to be really popular). The downstairs is pretty loud and it was crowded on this random Wednesday night.  Our floor show was watching people be confused by the 3 different doors that this space has...although only one is in use.

Still an awesome grocery that would be my primary if it was closer to my house.   They have great liquor deals. good seafood and more antipasti supplies than anyone should ever eat. I also think they get some of the freshest produce of all the groceries. I love all the local brands they carry.    Their baked good section at the front (with a separate cash register) offers traditional petit fours (like McKenzie's used to make) and an assortment of delicious diet-busting treats.  And I am still a fan of their cheese selection.  The deli in the front has some prepared foods (others are in the back in the meat cases and near the seafood) and they have tables and chairs for folks looking for a quick lunch.  They also have butchers and actual knowledgeable employees on hand.

It had been a bad week and by Friday I deserved a massage. LOVE that they have online booking here AND that they have appointments after 5.   Checkin was very easy and I was escorted to the ladies locker room and shown how the lockers work (really I do need that sort of help). I was offered my choice of beverages; yes bubbles, please. And after changing into a robe AND some slippers (they had baby feet sizes!), I waited in a staging area, sipping my bubbles that were left for me next to my name.   I opted for a Swedish massage instead of deep tissue and it was LOVELY. I was offered the stress relief oil at an upcharge but it was so very worth it. And the massage was great. I am kicking myself that I am so terrible at names and do not remember my therapist. She was amazing and really released a lot of my stress knots out.   She escorted me back to the lounging area to continue relaxing and to have some of their spa water. Then across the hall to the dressing room.  There are a few dedicated parking spots behind the spa; parking lot is accessible from Carrollton Avenue not Canal. But otherwise there is street parking.

Re-review (7 years later) since I was here 3x in 3 weeks recently. My nieces love the chicken banh mi here and say it's juicy and delicious. The youngest niece has also recently discovered her love for the fried tofu steamed buns, which is such a filling app that it's pretty much a meal.  I love their lemongrass tofu bun (vermicelli bowl) which is huge and usually ends up being 3 meals for me.   Staff is always friendly. Food is brought out quickly and always delicious.

Pandemic review: I saw on their instagram that they were carrying some super cute Halloween t-shirts so I went on over and ended up with a great dress instead.  Staff was masked and social distancing was enforced. As always the staff was very helpful and friendly.   Definitely a great spot to find some different items... And now that I think about it, where did that shirt I bought along with the dress end up?

The food was fine, although pricey. Our service was bizarre.  Really? The food waiter won't take an order for a glass of wine, nor will he tell the drinks waiter to come back and get said order?  The atmosphere is nice....except when the staff dried to stack dishes up their arms like it was diner...and then dropped them.  Good cocktails though.  My out of town friends liked it more than I did.

I found a roll of film in my old camera... which I could not remember when the last time I used it. I knew it was likely overexposed after a decade but decided to develop it anyway.  Bennett was super easy to work with just drop off and they scanned and emailed me a dropbox link. Yes. My film was overexposed and the pics were later than I thought... probably mostly from 2006.   My only reason for the 4 stars instead of 5? Their hours. I get that photo places are not as popular as they once were but 10-4 Monday-Thursday only? It took me months to actually get over there when they were open.

Eleven years later... this has become the go to spot for some of my family to host private dinners. The upstairs rooms are great for a sit down dinner or a cocktail party. As others have said the balconies are lovely (and are no smoking so don't do it).   The food, drinks and service have always been on point. At the most recent event we were even allowed to bring in an outside birthday cake to supplement the delicious in house desserts.  HH at the bar with snacks is great... when I feel safe doing that again. It's also a great spot for a business lunch (when they bring it back) but do not think you're doing a quick lunch since this is fine dining service. Lean back and relax into it.  The menus do change seasonally and the daily specials are very good. The most recent party we had a veggie array that included some really delicious in house pickles.   Cannot beat the views of city park!

A nice addition to the proliferation of Eastbank Vietnamese places. I had the fried tofu spring rolls and the grilled shrimp vermicelli bowl. Both were good but with a couple of tweaks could have been better. The spring roll was really loose and fat which made it a bit difficult to eat. The flavor was delicious as was the peanut sauce.  The bowl had perfectly grilled delicious shrimp and maybe just too many noodles for the ratio of sauce.    I only had black iced tea (but their is an herbal option) but their bar menu looks interesting so perhaps a cocktail is in my future.  The service was very friendly and the both the bar and the counter are great options for dining alone.  The space is really clean and modern, although it's a bit odd that the only mirror is outside the bathroom...makes for public primping.

Time for an update.... The cafeteria management is definitely stepping up their game. Recently there has been a sushi chef working and you can get handmade rolls and/or a poke bowl! The Action station often has tasty salads and other customizable options. Breakfast continues to be a really good deal.   And there are now fancy drink machines so I can fulfill my lime coke needs, as well as 3 different iced tea dispensers. They are really responsive to requests and the staff is great.  I am sad that don't have the fried okra waiting for me anymore but did I really need it anyway?

Going here reminded me of eating at my Granny's when I was little, so much good food.  I went just before Christmas with a couple of coworkers.  I had a plate lunch and they did the buffet.    I liked the old school salad bar although it was limited. Folks don't come here for salad. My shrimp plate was tasty & the breading was good & shrimp were cooked well.  Coworkers both enjoyed the salad bar with the only complaint being the temperature of the fried chicken...when a fresh batch came out, they hightailed it back to the steam trays and said it was perfect.  Another highlight from the buffet were the candied sweet potatoes-delish.  Like most soul food restaurants, Lil Dizzys can be a tough place to eat if you don't eat pork. I even asked if the green beans had meat in them & was told no...foolish question, of course they did.  A great neighborhood place to get some down home cooking

Pandemic review I saw on an insta post that Roulaison was offering a chocolate rum liqueur and I had to have it!  Ordering was easy-peasy online, including options for pay it forward pricing for hand sanitizer that they will donate to a local medical organization.   Pick up was also very simple. I was emailed a time and stopped in and picked up at the door. We were both masked and it was seamless.  And the liqueur was delish too!

Choctaw was forced to abandon it's westbank roots yesterday and parade uptown. Which means I saw it for the first time since maybe the 80s. And it didn't disappoint.   The floats were fun and the beads plentiful. Yes, it's an early day parade, but the bands and marching groups were enthusiastic. Couple that with the gorgeous weather and you've got an awesome day.  I hope they enjoyed their spin on St. Charles avenue but from all reports they'll be back on the westbank next year. Good for them for staying true to their roots.

I went to the sign lighting at the Roosevelt (formerly the Fairmont and then before that the Roosevelt).  While it is clear the hotel still needs work, they are planning for a soft opening at the end of June.  The Welcome Reception for Tales of the Cocktail will be in the Sazerac on July 8th.    Keep up with their progress at their blog:  http://therooseveltneworleans.com/blog/  I can't wait.  I used to take my grandmother to the Sazerac for a cocktail before/after symphony concerts at the Orpheum across the street.  I hope (and hope and hope) that the reopening of the Roosevelt rejuvenates that entire area.

I am so not a runner... but I did walk the CCC this year as a charity walker and my team raised money for Team Gleason (http://www.teamgleason.org/). The charity arm of the CCC is great. There were 15 possible charities to work with and a ton of money was raised. So yay!  The race start was a little confusing to a novice like me. I knew you were supposed to be in your bib color start but late arrivers tried to run people over and get ahead of you. I mostly tried to keep out of the way and not get stepped on...   There were fun bands/snacks/water along the way. And it was fun to see who costumed and who was in their serious running gear. For the record, my bunny ears were fine. My bunny leggings didn't breathe so well on that muggy day.  The after party (to which you can purchase tickets) was fun but very muddy at the City Park festival grounds. We hung out for a bit and then wandered over to where we had left a 2nd car the night before. There were buses to take you back to start but the lines were long.   Great run that goes through a good swath of the city.

It's a mall.  It has national chain stores...but also a few local ones (Mignon Faget, Adler's, Jean Therapy).    It's actually really well kept up and clean.  The food court is a zoo but again it's usually pretty clean and has a good variety of foods (but it's always loud).  It's the only location left in the city with a William-Sonoma and Macy's.  So I go when I need that sort of thing.    They've actually improved the parking over the years so props for that.  Now if the Causeway construction would just finish...

I love Tujague's.  I've never had a bad meal here and I'm a sucker for the early 20th century style of serving.  You choose your entree and that's pretty much it.  Everything else is set.  The kitchen staff & the waiters have all worked their forever and it's fun to watch their interactions.  I could eat their shrimp all day every day.  I even got to tour the 2nd floor when my cousin considered them for her wedding reception.  What a great building.

This is a huge indoor/outdoor warehouse space that can be used for special events. I hadn't been inside since around when it opened and had a different name...  It's great to be able to have both indoor and outdoor sections. And that the entrance narrows (thanks to the triangular shape) so that access can be limited as you file people in.  Biggest con? That you're standing on a concrete slab in a warehouse for hours. So if it's chilly, you feel it despite the crowds.   Parking in the area is rough, especially if there are multiple events going on.

So I'm kind of fibbing when I say I got ice cream from this location, instead it was from their food truck at Centennial Park.   They had 4 flavors so, of course, piglet-y me, I got the 3 scoop sampler. Flavors were dark chocolate, pistachio-honey, and vanilla (but y'know with more words).   The sampler was perfect. The chocolate was borderline bitter and delicious so the fancy vanilla was the perfect complement. The pistachio was really nutting and had a slightly salty taste so the honey was a welcome contrast.  Seriously good ice cream. I can understand why the shop had lines each time we passed by.

Delicious soup; good fish dinner.  My friends loved the frog legs, but I just can't eat them.  We had kids with us and the wait staff was good with them too.  And, of course, they were well behaved.  Lovely specialty cocktails.

For review 1100 I've chosen the quintessential NOLA condiment. Forget your other schmeers...Blue Plate is where it's at.  I know it's not made in town anymore but that doesn't matter. If I'm buying mayo, I'm buying BP.  Bonus star for the awesome old factory at the Jeff Davis/Earhart/Washington Ave traffic snarl that is now apartments.

Brief and beautiful! I stopped in 2x last weekend since I think they'll mostly be done by next.   Tulips take a huge amount of work in South Louisiana. You have to chill the bulbs to get them to bloom and cannot leave them in the ground over the summer because the moisture will cause them to rot.  Huge thanks to City Park and its gardeners for working to have this short moment of beauty and exuberant spring into our lives.

So Yelp says I never reviewed Trinity. Except, I know I did.  I think the Yelp HQ people are messing with my mind.  Or maybe it's our local CM Jess.  Y'all need to stop it.  Trinity is a nearly 200 year old grand Episcopal church.  And while it is mostly uptown and lilywhite, it has been changing.  Female priests have been hired by the parish since the early 90s and they church does a lot of outreach. I'm a fan of the current rector, Henry.  He was wonderful at the death of a family member a few years ago, when he was brand new.  Amazingly empathetic.

First question the store owner asked us? How were we all related...um what? But it fit the kooky style of the store.   There is a really nice selection of clothing, housewares and furniture. The prices were pretty good for the selection especially in this fancying up neighborhood. The store is really full so take your time perusing. I wasn't so into the clothes, but the accessories and the furniture were really fun.   Worth a peruse if you're in the area. Might be a spot to avoid if you tend towards claustrophobic, but I've been in way tighter shops.

Oh look it's 5 years later  and it's time for an update. The owner has transitioned from father to son in the last few years, so there have actually been some changes at this venerable restaurant. The dining room looks the same, only spruced up...same for the bar. The menu has some different items on it and some of them are actually healthy. I know it's a shock.  I recently enjoyed a Tales of the Cocktail lunch at Tujague's. It was 3 courses and a Sazerac for around $25. And it was delicious. I had a lovely salad, a beautiful piece of fish and then bread pudding, of course. Oh and I almost ate an entire loaf of french bread by myself because it was warm and tasty.  The staff was great and even let me charge my phone near their station (no plugs in the antique dining room). I'm glad to see them still going strong.

Interesting space...in the front, there's some table & chairs set up (with free wifi advertised but I didn't use) and art for sale. In the back is the juice bar.   The staff lets you know what is fresh and what is frozen which I liked and the prices seem on point for fancy juice drinks. They offer both veggie & fruit juices and you can customize to your hearts content.    The counter person was polite and offered suggestions and I was in and out quickly. Good stuff.

I've had the business bookmarked for two years...ever since Anita had her spray insulation done. I walked into her house and couldn't believe what a difference it made. I thought to myself, I need to get this closed cell foam blown under my 130 year old house...and it was added to the lengthy list of home improvement projects.  Fast forward to this month. I called and spoke to Brad and we chatted about what I wanted done. He stopped by my house for measurements the next day (when I wasn't home so no time off of work). He quoted a price later that day.  The price was lower than I expected so Yay! And we set up a day for them to come blow foam. He was a good communicator throughout the whole process via email, phone and text. He answered all my questions and was really good to work with.  They arrived right on time yesterday morning (at 7:30) and were finished by 3 pm. They did say my house was pretty easy. I had long since cleared most of the junk out from under the house, although they found a crate and a garbage can (thanks old tenants). And my house has over 3 feet of clearance so no belly crawling needed.   And, wow, I can tell the difference even while I'm in my very high Victorian bed. Highly recommended.

The first time I went to Origami it had only been open a couple of weeks & the service was comical rather than bad. I watched confused waitstaff pinball off of each other in confusion over who was responsible for what. The rolls & sushi were good though, so knew I would be back.  Fast forward to my most recent couple of visits, both times we were large groups (6ish) and were seated right away (even over Mardi Gras weekend). The staffing issues seemed to have been solved.  I've now tried a good portion of their menu and I've not been wowed by anything.  The portions on some rolls are huge (which can lead to massive over ordering).  And I've gotten a couple of items that had ingredients that weren't listed on the menu which was odd (and off putting for one of my friends).    The space is lovely and the location is convenient for me. But I've not been wowed by the food, so while I won't cross it off the list, it won't be my first choice.

Y'all know I love a Sonic, so I popped in here for a quick strawberry limeade and a breakfast sandwich as I left Tennessee to head back to NOLA.   My first mistake was ordering the biscuit instead of my usual texas toast. The biscuit was hard and dry and I threw half of it away.  My second mistake was that when I ordered my medium drink; the voice on the intercom said I could get a large for the same price, so of course I did. Which meant that I had to stop and use all the welcome center bathrooms. Oh well I was happy & well hydrated.  This is a really clean spot and I do appreciate that. Probably a 3.5 experience because of my hardtack biscuit but we'll round up for pleasant personnel.

I grew up eating at the suburban location of this restaurant and while it was always busy, this location is like being on a cattle car.  Or maybe it was just because I was eating here on a Sunday afternoon when there were 40K librarians down the street at a convention.  I had the stuffed crab lunch special (which +1 star for serving in an actual crab shell, you hardly ever see that anymore) which strangely had a cream sauce on top of the stuffed crab. It was a little heavier than I expected but still tasty.  One of my friends had the shrimp poboy and the shrimp were well fried and tasty.  Plus he got the bread pudding and there were 2 different kinds on the plate. Both were good.  The 3rd person at our table ordered their only vegetarian option (besides pasta) which was a portabella and spinach poboy. While in theory this could be a good sandwich, in execution it looked disgusting and must have tasted much better judging from his reaction.  Our server was mostly attentive but we did have ask for ice tea refills.

Great place to shop for inexpensive trendy pieces. They have a lot of variety and the shop is usually sorted by color which is interesting. They had cute accessories and a variety of clothing.  Yes it's mostly inexpensively made and the prices reflect that but if you have a teen in your life (or are pretending to be a teen) and you need shorts with pompoms around the hem, then this is your spot.  The staff was really nice and very helpful. And the store was really clean. Are the clothes for me? Not really but I would definitely look here for costume pieces.

I was lucky enough to dine at Trinity for a friend's birthday a couple of weeks back and the entire staff made our table feel like VIPs! Multiple staff members greeted us and wished my friend a happy birthday. The bartender came up with a custom cocktail for her based on her clearly defined likes & dislikes. She liked it so much she had 2!  And the food OMG. The food. We started with the baked oysters trinity. And they were amazing, each flavoring complementing but so different than the one before. We then split a couple of appetizers among the 3 of us...I know one was the ricotta gnudi. So different from what I was expecting but super tasty. Then the 3 of us split the vegetarian polenta dish and the linguine seafood dish. OMG they were both simply amazing. Really really delicious.  Did I mention that the bread was simply amazing too? It's made by the inhouse pastry chef. I tried to hoard all of it but I friends made me share.   After our meal, our birthday girl had bread pudding with a candle in it... At this point I thought I might explode. So of course, we ended up concluding with small glasses of port.   The staff was on point and super helpful and patient with our birthday silliness. The renovation is gorgeous!!! I have not eaten in this space since the 90s and I cannot believe it's the same place. So light and gorgeous and yes, still an open kitchen.   Definitely a great spot for a special occasion or just because you deserve some delicious food. Now I want to stop by on a regular night for a cocktail and app...

I had to make the jaunt out to Metairie Road to seek the mythical nutella king cake. And it was as magical as everyone said.  It's a light brioche style cake with a not too sweet thread of nutella throughout.  Love! (Although in all fairness, my Mom liked the cake but has decided that nutella - her first time trying - was not really for her.)  So consider your own over/under on nutella.  The shop is cute & spacious. The counter person who helped me was really helpful, even pointing out the free samples of a different variety of king cake. Alas, it contained my nemesis, goat cheese.   While there I also got some amazing Satsuma sorbetto. So delicious!

Oh dear lord. I ordered a dozen plus cupcakes for my parents' 55th wedding anniversary. And while the cupcakes were fine, the service...  First I verified online what flavors they offer on Friday. Then I called this store...and it went to voicemail. I left a message. 2 hours later, I called again.
