And then dessert which was supposed to be an ice cream sandwich with 2 oatmeal cookies...and my ice cream was completely melted by the time it was placed in front of me.  The food was OK, really, but the vegetarian menu was not thought out. And I have no idea what I would have gotten for the scallop course if I didn't eat seafood (a 3rd salad?), but for the price ($95) per person it really wasn't worth it to me.

On our FQ gallery roam yesterday, Re & I popped into this lovely local art spot. We both recognized many of the artists who have pieces in this shop and it was great to see the shop chockfull (to the ceiling) with local artists from original pieces to reproductions.  They had many of the cat paintings by Cary Chun Lee (who also had rooster paintings and a great landscape in the shop) and glassworks by Studio Inferno and Icon fusions by Christina Miller (so I bought another piece) and the patrons saints created by the Schlaus (I already have St Jerome). And many many more.   It looks like they are affiliated with Jardin (in the alley/courtyard next door) according to their FB page. But the shops are not physically linked.  Great spot for an assortment of local arts and crafts for reasonable prices.

Dinner Lab was started in 2012 as a way to bring uncommon cuisine to New Orleans. You pay a membership fee (or receive one as a gift) and then you receive emails about upcoming meals.  Meals for April 2013 included  North Korean, Ecuadoran, Hawaiian, and Indian.  I'm attending my first dinner on Saturday so we'll see how it goes!

You know I'm a dog lover and I do love a bar where our furry friends are welcome.  The layout of this bar is a bit odd but it is very homey. I agree with John that you feel like you're in someone's fancy home bar more than at an actual commercial establishment.    It's probably a good thing that this bar is on the other side of the river or I'd treat it like my living room. Excellent call on including it on the Party Bus tour of the Wank.

For the record, I am not particularly an LSU fan.  I find the preponderance of purple & gold that already exists in my life kind of irritating.  That said, if you need an LSU themed gift for anyone, hit up this store.    I was actually looking for Saints gear (which they also carry) and while that section was much smaller, they had a nice selection of black & gold items too.  As befits a small independent store, the staff was extremely helpful.

Sometimes you need to take folks to someplace fancypants and as this is the bar at the Ritz Carlton Hotel, it fits the bill.  The sofas/chairs are mostly really comfy. The cocktails are well crafted. But, yes, it's pricey. They've got to pay for the a/c, decor & fresh flowers (which are gorgeous) somehow.  The music is good and folks do dance...sometimes.  I've never actually eaten any of the food here.  Also the ladies rooms are first rate.

I'm going to lose my librarian card. I never knew that there was a bookshop at this location. So if it's closed you'll just wander on past. But if the shutters are open, then there will usually be some sale books on the steps and you'll know you've arrived.  WOW this shop is full, full, full. The owner is very knowledgeable about this stock so can direct you to a section or author you're interested in. AND he built the shelving himself so that's pretty amazing.  I bought an autographed vintage 84 Worlds Fair book for a fair price. So I'm a happy camper.  Definitely a good spot to check out for bibliophiles.

Oh, look, another review of the Maple Leaf! Does it really need a 58th review? Probably not.  Will you get one anyway? Sure.  I've been going to the Maple Leaf since the mid80s and it really hasn't changed too much.  Sure the back patio exists and is nicer than it used to be, but much of the bar looks the same as it probably did 50 years ago...but with more outlets.  It's a great place to go see live music and be swept up in the excitement.  The only reason for the -1 star?  I am so OVER smoking in bars.

Yep. It's a bar on Bourbon, BUT it also can be a calm respite from the street.  Yes there are still frat boys and wooo girls who patronize this bar. BUT the bar is spacious the drinks are affordable (beers, straight pours and basic mixed drinks only). The staff are on the ball and amazingly patient.   I also like that the interior looks like it hasn't been renovated in decades...if you can discount the flat screen TVs that is. The bathrooms are a bit sketch. It definitely does have character.

Hadn't been in Coop's in over a decade and went with a group for lunch. Despite the crowd the service was personable & entertaining and our food was delivered promptly.  Everyone said their dishes (and cocktails) were good, even the duck quesadilla which I was REALLY skeptical about.  Be prepared to wait and the service can be harried, but the food is solid.

A little library history... this is one of only 3 Carnegie libraries (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_library) still standing in New Orleans; the others are Nix on Carrollton and the Children's Resource Center on Napoleon. This is also one of the few NOPL libraries that didn't flood in K, but was still closed for several years because of roof/structural damage.  This location is small but since the renovation (reopened 2013) it is a really efficient use of space. I love all the light that comes in through the windows. And that it is walking distance for many of the neighbors.  The location is named after a library activist (don't you love them!) who ensured that the branch wasn't closed in the 1960s. Her family still maintains a separate website (from nutrias.org) for this location: http://www.hubbelllibrary.org/  While this is definitely not the closest public library for me, I usually try to make it over in December for their Christmas tree/wreath sale that benefits the library.

One of my favorite places to have a cocktail in the quarter.  You have to love a building that survived NOLA's major fires in the 18th century.  Plus it was a money laundering operation for the privateering Lafitte brothers.  Do not order a "fancy" cocktail here, however.

Still another review for bars on Frenchman...most of which I was sure I had reviewed. I think Yelp tortures me by disappearing my reviews occasionally and no they aren't filtered. Or maybe I'm suffering from a huge hallucination...in which case I blame the sinus meds.   Spotted Cat is kind of awesome if you want to get up and close with the band. It's small (intimate) and friendly. The bartenders are spot on (see what I did there).   My confession is that sort of hate that it was featured on Treme so now it's a must stop for tourists (Sorry, Melvyn). But don't let that dissuade you. Pack yourself in and dance along with the crowd and the band. Just don't forget to hydrate!

So recently it was time to replace my old subaru... And, of course, the lightbulb went off and I thought of Yelp's own Jennifer B and that she does internet magic for the Bryan autoplex people, so I commenced to bugging her via email/gchat/in person at Yelp parties. And she was totally gracious AND mentioned that the exact car I might be looking for was on their lot and on sale...with a financing deal! The universe was telling me to pull the trigger...or at least Jennifer-Yelp-??? was pushing me along.  I met with Rex (an awesome low-key sales guy) and gave the car a test drive. We talked deal and then I went home and thought about it. A day and a half later, I am the proud owner of a new 2012 Impreza - manual 5 speed. And I'm a happy girl.  I financed through Subaru and it was a painless process; the finance guy (who is over in the Chevy building) was amiable and not a typical hard sell finance guy.    All in all a great experience and I'm loving my new girl...now to figure out a name for her.

I was super excited that this old hubcap store was finally put back into use after being empty for over a decade. I'd been watching the conversion to a gardening center while the weather was cold and dreary.   Friday I stopped in to pick up some herbs and also bought scented geraniums (the plants smell - nice to me but hopefully yucky to mosquitoes - and are supposed to be mosquito repellent).  The man who helped me was great and we chatted about the hydroponic systems they sell. This shop *edit* sells the Verti Farms hydroponic systems who grow lots of hydroponic produce locally but they aren't directly affiliated, as I was just informed. Just wanted to clarify...  It looks like they're still gearing up their stock but the space is nice although the outdoor area (where the plants are) is still a bit rubbely...why add gravel when you already have gravel, asphalt, rocks, whatever as your ground cover.  The plants I bought looked gorgeous and I'm eager to use some of the basil, thyme & mint in the kitchen. I'm definitely interested in seeing what they become.

The place was packed and I ended up smelling like the kitchen, but my sammich was well made and the selection was good.  The layout is a bit confusing and my experience with NY Delis has mostly been in the Catskills rather than in the city, but I think Stein's does compare.    Now I need to head back and peruse the groceries when it's not packed to the gills.

3 year later and I still love my car. Most of the staff (both sales & service) are aces and I like the online booking system BUT why doesn't the online booking actually email the service reps who will be working on my car???!!!!  Recently, the potholes of New Orleans took out one of my tires. I have a comprehensive service package (gold star plus) which includes tires (and roadside assistance so shout out to the guy who came out in the rain to change my tire for me). So I book my appointment on Tuesday night when I get home for the following Thursday afternoon which is my first available time to take vacation time from work to get the car fixed. It takes a while to get from downtown to the dealership thanks to construction happening everywhere so I show up and they don't have my tire in stock.   The service rep was very apologetic and made sure that I have his card so next time I can duplicate my booking in the online system by emailing him. This efficient how? But I guess that's what I'll have to do. The tire was in stock within 24 hours and I was able to get back out to the dealership and have it changed on my 2nd trip.  Also, my gold star plan covers tires...BUT the program is really setup for the dealership to be reimbursed not for customers. The service reps are nice but both times I've needed tires replaced they have been shocked that it is an actual customer calling them....(after 15 minutes on hold with Subaru to get their phone number and then another 10 minutes maneuvering through their menus). Evidently, Bryan is the only Subaru dealership in the US who makes the customer pay rather than going through the service themselves.

My only experience here was a large (40 people) private party in one of the upstairs dining rooms, so my experience may be a bit different from others. The service was gracious and not too stuffy. The food was good and the atmosphere was great.

Hadn't been to Parasol's in a while, but it's as good as ever.  We had a tasty, really fresh shrimp poboy & our friends got the roast beef and declared it super tasty.  Plus delish fries.  Plus some of the staff still had green hair from St. Patty's day.

I took a chance on this spot just off Metairie Road for lunch last week. And I think it has a bit of an identity crisis and is trying to be all things to all people. It has sushi AND is an Asian influenced Bistro AND has a burger selection AND looks like it might be a straight up bar (based on the drink menu) at night...even more so then the Sun Ray Grill location that was here previously.  Nothing on the grill menu jumped out at me so I opted for sushi for lunch. I had a couple of pieces of nigiri (tuna & salmon) and an avocado/cucumber roll, along with a miso. The miso was incredibly salty. The nigiri was well cut and beautifully presented and the avocado/cucumber roll was the perfect palate cleanser. For me, there is too much cream cheese in the roll menu, but that may be what sells in the area.  My server was hustling and the spot did have a fair amount of business for 2pm on a Thursday. Ultimately this was probably a 3.5 for me, but the service and the sunny locale upped it to a 4 star.

Fun housewares and kids stuff. This is a new shop on Magazine but it's an established business in Lafayette. They had some cute Louisiana themed dishes that they commissioned. Plus tons of cute child gifts. They also had some books, stationery, jewelry, and other unusual items.   They share the space with another Lafayette based company, Parish Ink and there are 2 staff members and 2 cash registers.  The stock in both is interesting and the staff were friendly. I'll definitely be back.

I love inari and it is hard to find at sushi restaurants in NOLA. And there it was on the menu. YUM! I also am a big fan of the passion roll which was cucumber and some fish and some stuff. (Yes, I could look it up but just trust me that it's delish.)  The service was good; the dining room was simple and the fish was fresh. What more could I want?  The dining room was not crowded on a Friday night in January so quick seating and hot sake & hot green tea were much appreciated.  Plus we got rock star parking right out front. Clearly it was meant to be.

This seafood joint belongs at the lakefront...but the lakefront "ain't there no more."  So it's a good thing they are uptown.  Excellent fried everything.  And I am partial to their iceberg lettuce salads.  The stuffed artichoke would keep vampires away, in a good way.
On the other hand the food is good & they have yummy cocktails.  And I can walk there from my house.  I guess I'm a pushover.

Dinner Lab met all my expectations...I really loved the unusual cuisine (North Korean this week) and the staff was amazing.  Water bottles on the table so you could help yourself. Free pouring wine and a pseudo-mojito made with a Korean liquor. Awesome! And then five courses of yummy food and the servers remembered that I was a problem child who received off  menu needs. (Yes, I'm special.)  I will say that your dinner companions can really make these events. The person to my right kept his back to me all night as he leaned into his large group so that was odd. But our dinner companions across from us (the seating was huge long banquet style) were lovely and we had a great time chatting with them.  (My date for the night was the lovely Anne W.)  Of course, they said we were their favorites...because why wouldn't they?  The venue will get a separate review and was really fun.  I will definitely be back for another dinner soon.  Payments for dinners are via PayPal, FYI

I just rode the carousel for the 1st time in years at my niece's birthday party last month.  It's as beautiful as ever and historic!  The carousel dates from 1906 and looks it, in a good way.  There are other small amusement park rides, bumper cars, tilt-a-whirl and the ladybug.  Plus you can take a train from here and ride all over City Park.

I've been hearing mixed reviews about this spot but I wanted a grunchy/granola type sandwich after a trying day and thought they would probably have one. And the Veggie King was exactly what I wanted. The veggies were fresh, the bread was hearty and I was a happy camper. Since I was getting take out, I decided to also get the Broken Noodle Salad (lunch & dinner in one trip) and was also really pleased with it.   The staff who assisted me were pleasant and efficient so no complaints.  I'll have to find an evening to actually dine in and sample the cocktails. Because now that I'm typing, I want that salad again.

A great place to hang out with friends...until the smoke gets too thick.  The kitchen does a tasty job and the beer (& bourbon) selection is good.  Try heading upstairs for a quieter time and access to the balcony.  The upstairs isn't always open though.  Only big negative is the weirdly configured ladies' room.  It's a huge space but the stalls are tee-niny.  Like bang your knees on the door small, and I'm short.

All I heard was ooooh H&M is opening. This is so exciting. OOOHH. I'm going to wait in line for hours....and I finally get there and, yawn.  Maybe there was just too much hype. Maybe it's because I hit up a mega-H&M in Germany in the 90s. (The US stores, that I've been to, are pretty much tiny in comparison.) But I don't get it.  I'm glad that the retail space isn't idle. I'm glad a major international retailer has come to our fair city. I'm glad that this location has housewares as well as clothing. And I'll probably stop back by when I'm downtown for other reasons but I don't see it becoming a destination shopping venue for me.

So Fleurty Girl move to the space next door to the old shop...the only reason you can tell is that both still have signs. The new shop is gorgeous with lots of artistic touches and architectural details.   Love the great selection of gift items, way beyond t-shirts AND I love how spacious this store is compared to the Magazine shop.  Not sure what other reviewers are complaining about staff-wise. All three sales clerks in the store on this busy pre-Christmas Sunday were pleasant and polite without being pushy.  (Yes, I'm feeling alliterative).  Magazine is still my go to because of proximity but I definitely will be back to this location too.  And as always, I have to comment how much I hate this strip mall's parking lot.

-1 star for being a duplicate entry to the colloquial name for this park, the fly (http://www.yelp.com/biz/the-fly-new-orleans). Notice that the common name has over 20 reviews, while the proper name only 1...OK, now 2.    This is a great spot to watch the river float by and to play on a jungle gym or to watch kids play sports (soccer, baseball, etc).   Sunday nights are cruise night so don't get caught in the traffic.  Also, I've heard reports that they may close access down for months to work on the levees.

I splurged on a facial (thanks living social deal) and a massage in the chaos before Christmas.  Rene is correct the place is very clean and quiet (except for the another annoying patron who wouldn't get off her cell phone...in the dressing room/the shower/the waiting area).    The rooms are well appointed and comfortable with fully adjustable beds; yay for a slight angle for my poor wrecked sinuses.  My massage was perfect, relaxing and worked all the knots out of my neck.  The facial was less serene.  It was good but the facialist was more rushed in her actions. It may have just been in contrast to the massage.  Either way both were lovely and my skin still feels great days later.   Negatives were the other annoying patron (obviously not the spa's fault) and the dressing room which was a spacious two stall restroom with lockers and a single shower room...which had a couple of women waiting for it.  Positives are that the spa is open 7 days a week, 363 days a year (only closed on Christmas & Thanksgiving).  The long hours and days open are reflected in the prices, I think.  Or maybe the prices are standard hotel spa rates and I'm just unaware.
Storyland is a great place for kids to see their favorite nursery rhymes brought to life.  You can climb on a fire truck , go down the dragon slide, and stand inside a whale's mouth.

When I said I needed to Christmas shop this was one of the 2 stores, my local friends suggested and it's a great eclectic store. I bought beaucoup presents here from novelty socks to housewares to a Day of the Dead figurine.   The staff varied from helpful to indifferent and the store was well laid out, although it's chockful so it makes moving around a bit tough, especially if the store is crowded like it was the day I was there.   My niece tried on a bunch of clothes and while the sizing was a bit irregular (as one would expect in a shop like this), there were some really different styles especially if you want something different than mallware.

New, vintage, antique, collectibles, junk, art...it's all here. This another space that has LOTS of  vendor booths and the quality of their wares seems particularly high.   Not interested in jewelry, next booth. How about original art inspired by Japanese calligraphy? Or maybe some antique weaponry? Or original paintings of New Orleans street scenes? Or low VOC craft paint? Or baby stuff? Eclectic right?  The place is well laid out and the staff are present but not pushy. Most of the booths are over crowded so that you can actually see the stock. And there is a nice wide center aisle (on the 1st floor) so you don't feel claustrophobic.  Definitely a spot to check back at fairly often.
Good stuff.  Everything is custom made. The bar is roomy and the servers were quick.
MMMM...drunken noodles.  Now I'm hungry.  Great vegetarian selections; not so great with the cooling down some dishes when you're out with folks who cannot handle the heat.

The service was very high end with two attentive waiters checking on us, but not so much that it was annoying. The atmosphere has changed little from when it was Byblos, maybe slightly different lighting?  I tried two of the pizzas and split a Caesar salad (which was definitely large enough to do without either of us grumbling). Bread appears on the table but ours seemed skimpy for the size of the basket. (I know it's minor but you get this nice big bread basket and you think you can pig out...and, yeah, it's 1/2 a small loaf of delicious bread, which just makes you want more.)  The Caesar was tasty as were the pizzas, roasted cauliflower and the spinach alfredo. Both were really good. And I had a couple cocktails that were watermelon based; the first was delicious, but the second was more slapdash...definitely not made with love. Oh well.  I guess I'm leaning towards a 3.5 rating. I feel like it's a little pricey but the quality is there. Probably good if you're on a date and want something a bit more upscale.

The SPCA does amazing work. Period.    As the proud Mom to a very silly rescue lab/pitt/chow/racoon mix, I really appreciate all the hard work that the LA/SPCA does.  And, yes, I put my $ where my heart is.  This location is their fancy post-K digs which are much nicer (and not destroyed) then the old Japonica street facility.  But I miss the old theme song.  So check out their online stores:  http://www.la-spca.org/shop/home.htm and give them support.

Seriously, the best toy store in NOLA. I always find something fun for the kids (or the adults who act like kids) in my life.  Recent purchases include:  coloring books (for a my teen niece recovering from surgery), a Saints ball, washable markers (for the younger nieces), NOLA music CD for kids and a pig that shoots balls out of his nose.    Yep this visit was part of my annual Magazine-Street-Black-Friday-Shopping-Extravaganza with my Mom.

I love a solid old school diner. And that's what this is.   Maybe you'll get a cranky waitperson, but I'd be cranky waiting on drunks too. Maybe your breakfast/burger/waffle will be cooked to perfection or it won't.   BUT it's a quick and affordable throwback in the French Quarter and really that's all I need to be a fan.

Brrr... the weather turned and we needed to get the child out. So we stopped for hot chocolate and a chai latte. The staff was quick and courteous. The drinks were tasty and the space was welcoming and clean.  Since we were already chilled we went hot not cold, but love that they also serve ice cream.   Quick in and out so we could get back to shopping...

My Mom loves this store. She loves that it's really affordable and that it's in a strip mall with a parking lot. AND that their custom wrapping job is to make a small gift item look like a traditional New Orleans snoball.  There are lots of random housewares and jewelry and tshirts and stuff. It was insane the Saturday before Christmas but the staff had a system and while they were rushed, they were helpful.  Definitely a place to find some random gifts for an inexpensive price.

What a great space! Yes, it's confusing to walk into the gallery space and then "find" the cafe space, but y'know it's the quirks that make things interesting.  Loved my sandwich; thanks for the recommendation, Joi! The tea was lovely and the homemade breads were delicious!    Definitely a spot to check out to just sit and chill.

A very nice upscale mall on the edge of the FQ.  OK, upscale for NOLA.    It has Saks, Pottery Barn, William Sonoma, Banana Republic, Mignon Faget, a Landmark movie theater, and Southern Repertory Theater.  Oh and Rhino!  Rhino is an artist consortium shop, great jewelry, ceramics, woodworking, etc.  The food court is small and I usually just get a cold drink...I mean I can go to Sbarro's in the 'burbs.  For folks who live in the city, it's a great alternative to fighting the suburban shopping malls.

Droopy's has been in a couple of locations on Jeff Hwy over the years.  In the 90s they used to be closer to the parish line, across from Riverdale Middle School.  Now they are further out in Harahan.    Droopy's is a family run business and they know their repeat customers.  My oldest niece doesn't even have to order; she just says hi and out comes her favorite.    What reminded me to actually write a review was that my 13 year old niece recently had them make her a pickle snowball.  I was not with them to be grossed out, and I'm not entirely certain if they used syrup and then put a pickle in snowball or if they used pickle juice.  Maybe it's better that I don't know.  But it does show the lengths that they will go to please their customers (even if they are crazy).

My disclaimer on this review is that I used Ultimate Fitness pre-Katrina.  When they re-opened after, my $ situation has changed so I wasn't able to go back.  And when I did have $ again...well I became a lazy lump.  The deal with this gym is that you work out intensively with a trainer once a week for 30 minutes.  And you (or your trainer) push yourself HARD.  I've gone away barely able to walk.  And it does build muscle quickly.  I discovered I actually had abdominal muscles, who knew? And because I had an appointment with a human being, I was much less likely to skip.  The problem for me was I have multiple joint issues and even with a trainer the intense workout would exacerbate my existing problems.  What I probably need (if I wasn't a lump) is more a straight cardiovascular routine which you could also do here as they had machines in the back that you were welcome to use on the days you didn't train.

Reasons to go to Gordon's: You need some picture frames, art supplies, a slipper chair, some artificial flowers, and a bunch of Saints accoutrement.  Honestly, they have the most random stuff.  Before the National hobby chains game to town, there was Gordon's (and used to be Eric's of whatever part of town).  Seriously, this location has the most random assortment of furniture; I was very surprised that they didn't have what I was looking for...an umbrella stand.  Lots of seasonal bric-a-brac. And I believe they have a service department that will make dried flower arrangements/wreaths/swags for you.  They also have a framing department.

Still a fan of this store...I think my last review (from 3 years ago!) was for their old larger location.  While they have a good variety of pet supplies, particularly higher end food and treats (in case your pup needs it). But they don't carry national brand people clothes anymore. I did see a few local tshirts though...which I think were for people and not dogs.  The staff is always really helpful and not pushy at all.

Sara's has an interesting history.  It was originally one of the only Indian restaurants in NOLA (old Calcutta) and then the chef got bored and changed it into a world fusion joint.   My FIL used to complain every time that some Tiki Chicken dish was no longer on the menu.  They do have a few excellent dishes.  Their coconut shrimp in curry sauce is really tasty and not too sweet.  I also love their portabello salad w/ cherry dressing.  BUT, the prices do seem high.

This is a solid Sonic location across from the Saints training facility.  It's never too crowded and the food comes out quickly and is hot.  It's kind of hidden between buildings so you have to know where it is or you'll blow by it.  If you need to get out of the lot and head back into town, then be prepared for folks on Airline trying to run you over.    Plus it has some nice landscaping in the middle of the car spots.  Check out my pic...that's a lot of palms.  Sonic is my fave fast food; love a snack of tots and a strawberry limeade when I'm out and about in the 'burbs.

First thing to know is that they are not trying to be authentic Thai food.  They are striving for a blend of NOLA & Thai.  Sometimes they are successful but sometimes they're not.  I do think the prices are a little high.

Wow! Just over a year later, I actually made it back to eat and with the same friend.  Do your self a favor and try the crabmeat & shrimp au gratin.  I am a huge fan of this dish in general and really enjoyed their take on it. It was much lighter than most versions (slightly disappointing to NOT feel my arteries being clogged but probably better for me in the long run) and sort of lemony.  My salad with housemade thousand island was fine. And my friend loved her fried green tomatoes and crawfish (maybe crab) cakes.  Cocktails were again lovely.  She had a champagne julep (both bourbon & champagne) and declared it delish. I had a mango cucumber collins and decided while it was fine, I am not a fan of mango vodka.

So since the Yelp powers decided to take down my 2008 review of Nick's (when I marked it closed...yknow since August 2005), I'll just post again. My original review linked to the demolition permit from the City...which had just been issued.   I spent a fair amount of time at Nick's maybe around Freshman/Sophomore years of college. I was never a fan of the ridiculously named shots and the big practical joke was to get a newbie to order something ludicrous like a penguin...male appendage. (Hey maybe that's why my old review got taken down. Using the anatomically correct name for the boy bits.) Of course, hilarity ensued when they found that name didn't exist.   Then I found that my Uncle would stop in at Nick's on occasion after work for a Dixie on the way home. Since the bar was located across the street from the Brewery, they had the freshest Dixie on tap. Clearly my late night visits never overlapped with him.  Fast forward to summer 2005, my cousin had a friend visiting from England and I wandered over to Nick's with them to have that fresh Dixie. It was lowkey and divey. And not the college mob scene of years before. I cherish that memory since only a month later, Nick's was no more.  With the revitalization of Tulane Avenue, I wish Nick's Bar could have been a divey oasis in the middle of everything.

I often stop at this CCs location when I'm out and about shopping and need a cool drink or a stop to sit.  For the location, there is a lot of room..unless a huge group of women are having a baby shower. Seriously, who hosts a baby shower at a coffee shop...without warning the employees. Bizarre.  There are usually lots of folks using this as an office and/or study hall, but I've never actually been shushed here so maybe the less high strung work here.  Last time I was in, I had some lemonade concoction. I should have read the description better. I thought I was getting frozen lemonade, but instead it was a lemon smoothie...or something. Lemons & milk, ick. But that might just be me. Next time I'm sticking with iced tea.  Bonus: I have accidentally stalked our new CM Morgan here. So that's fun.

I love Canine Culture.  They carry Barkology and Life is Good.  They carry dog food, toys, costumes, etc.  They offer pet grooming and sponsor SPCA adoption days.  All and all they are just good people with a fun store.

It's a WalMart and I'm not really a fan, but it's near my parents house and someone had given me a gift card and I needed cereal.  Bleh.  The best thing about going to WalMart is the people watching: I saw a child get hit with a shoe because he had lost the other one somewhere in the store. I saw 2 other children pretending to get shot and roll around in the aisles, challenging all the basket pushers. And, of course, there was the incredibly stoned couple who couldn't comprehend anything the cashier told them.  Good times.  For some reason, this store had an insane number of liquor displays this weekend.  Who knew they still made Boonesfarm Strawberry Hill (I immediately texted a friend to inform him it was still being made...good times at 14) or grape vodka.

Hey Yelp! This location is in River Ridge, not New Orleans. Yes, I know 70123 should be a city zip code but it's not. Get over it.  So with that off my chest, this is a fancypants Winn Dixie. It has a ton of prepared foods, a decent selection of fresh produce, and all the usual grocery items.  It has always seemed clean to me and the store well maintained.

La. Pizza kitchen offers solid pizzas and pastas.  They are not super expensive and they are usually tasty.  Just nothing too spectacular about the food or the atmosphere.  A good solid choice when you have a group and need to accommodate multiple issues (food allergies, vegetarian, meat-atarian, etc.)

I should hard sell Storyland to folks with kids since it turns out they kept 2 of my nieces and my nephew employed all summer. They "performed" as various characters on Saturday afternoon.  Who knew? (I know bad aunt)  Storyland is really a magical place for little kids.

I am so excited that this neighborhood branch of NOPL is re-opening on Saturday (7-13-13). This is one of the surviving Carnegie Libraries in New Orleans and was built in 1907. It's a great building with a small collection but all the amenities one could want in a neighborhood library.  This library survived Katrina with only minor roof damage and was back up and running in October 2005. Unfortunately, it was closed because of structural issues in May 2008 BUT the building was used for various tv & film projects even while closed. Hmmmm...  Having been to their temporary digs (the old carriage house for the Algiers Courthouse), I'm sure both staff and users will be happy to return home.

Sometimes a bricks & mortar book store is a necessity and when out in Metairie, local shops aren't really an option.   I stopped in just before Christmas to help my brother finish up his gift buying. We were both struck by how the number of actual books has been reduced as compared to movies, CDs and gift items.   The parking lot was a zoo and the staff was polite to curt depending on their location. They do have a great Louisiana/New Orleans section though so props to a National chain for that.

You would think that a shrimp or fish taco at a festival or arts market would be sketchy.  You would be wrong.  Woody's tacos are served at a variety of events around town.  I've had them at both the Arts Market in Palmer Park  and at the Freret Street festival.  They are always delicious and fresh.    He also serves a meat (pork today) and a vegetarian/vegan taco too.  But I've never had those.  Check out their FB page (http://www.facebook.com/pages/Woodys-Fish-Tacos/215165961864000) to see where they'll be next...  After tomorrow that is since the Arts Market in November is Saturday & Sunday, you can still try them out this weekend.

I love going to Neophobia, although I hardly ever buy.  Guess I'm just a looky-loo.  They had a padded black leather bar that I swear is the one that was in my Aunt & Uncle's house in the early 70s.  They have great mid-century modern pieces: furniture, accessories, clothing, art, housewares.  Think upscale vintage/thrift store that you don't have to dig through the junk to find the gems.  I cannot take my Mom here though.  She just exclaims over the prices for stuff she either still has in a cabinet somewhere, or that one of us broke decades ago, or that she gave away.

Driving past this former home on Jeff Davis, you would never know that it had such a lovely outdoor space. Yes, I know the name has garden in it...but it also has beer, not my favorite.  As I drove around the block to find parking, discovered the parking lot situated directly behind the building and the lovely patio which did have a decidedly jungle feel.  The alcohol selection was good and my friends were pleased with the beer selection (both tap & bottles).  Prices were good. And I didn't try the food.  The TVs all over the patio were nice since it was olympics time and the fans were welcome although insufficient on a July evening, since I showed up in my work clothes.   +1 for the butterfly flitting around under the patio cover and looking all pretty.

I liked that there were only 2 choices for washes here: basic & fancy. And you have a choice for vacuum or no vacuum (although that doesn't affect the final price). I was a little confused by the whole drive your own car system.    Wait in line; pull into the vacuum area; turn off your car & let the vacuumers do their thing; pull around into the back parking lot and swing around to the autowash area; get confusing instructions from the guys who spray stuff on your car (maybe only with the fancy option?); get out and go inside to pay; sit inside (or outside) until they finish wiping down your car.  The whole process was pretty quick for me. But there was only 1 car before me when I drove in. The cleaning job was OK and I had to touch up several spots after I left and I felt like the windows were a bit smeary.  Staff was polite and the place was clean....just confusing

Adorable shop for baby/toddler clothes, toys, etc. The salesclerk who assisted me was young and very helpful, so I didn't have Megan's experience for which I'm grateful.   I ran in to buy a last minute first communion gift and they had plenty of selection. I loved the guardian angel necklace but it was too pricey for me to buy for a 7 year old who will lose it one week. I did find some very cute and affordable (under $20) cross earrings that were age appropriate.   Definitely a spot to find cute baby items but don't expect bargain prices.

I'm still really happy with the service at the Subaru dealership. I've gone in a few times for routine maintenance and it's been easy-peasy. I love the online booking that's available. Each time they've been really good at communicating and then asking if I have enough time for them to wash my car, um...yeah.  And now that the service center is over in the Subaru building, it even has comfy chairs. So that's definitely a plus.  One year later, I'm definitely enjoying the good gas mileage and the reliability of new Subie.

And then there were 4! If you follow my reviews, you know I'm a fan of Theo's in general. I like there not too thin/not too thick crust. And I think their toppings are pretty top notch. My niece had mentioned that the March pizza of the month was a Thai Shrimp so that was percolating in the background....  I was headed out to the Metrys for a meeting and realized I was STARVING so stopped in at the new location for a quick pizza (and some bread sticks to share with the group) and got that yummy pizza of the month. So different, so delicious.  As for the location, Theo's occupies the corner unit of a strip mall and I'm pretty sure I had an old Mac fixed on this location a million years ago. But their renovation looks great with some nice homey touches. The seating seemed ample and they do serve the beer and wine with specials at different times of day/days of the week. Staff was lovely and superpatient with the herds of parents coming in with overtired children.

I've shopped at a number of the Double M stores over the years...most of them did not survive Katrina.  This store in Harahan (not NOLA) is notable for it's glorious flowers and plants outside.  That's how you can tell it's in the burbs; the plants stay out even when the store is closed because the local municipal cops are just hoping someone will try to take them.  The shop carries gardening materials and supplies, as well as pet merchandise.  Most recent purchase?  A curry brush for the horse that has adopted us, sort of.

Super cute jewelry, art, stationery shop. TLots of cute gift items and because I was there just before Christmas (maybe) the store was chockful of stock so watch that big purse. Lots of unique items and prices reflect whether a piece is handmade or mass produced.  Staff was helpful. And the parking lot out back was great (it is a paylot). There is a backdoor to the parking lot so that was useful and then you get exit out to the street too.  Great shop to find a perfect gift, a special memento or something for yourself.

Back in the 80s (what's with me & the throwback memories today-maybe the new year has made me contemplative), my friends always wanted to go to O'Henry's for the frosty schooners of beer; as a non-beer drinker, I appreciated their full bar.    The food is basic burgers, fried seafood, and plate meals and it fills a need since NOLA seriously lacks in diners.  While I've never had a great meal here, I've never had a bad one either so points for that.    Bonus, you can get a free steak on your birthday (with driver's license as proof, of course.)

I was wandering on Maple Street when I saw the signage that a new shop had opened...down the long hallway in the building where Jamila's is located.  The name Sarah Ott sounded familiar so I took a gander.  The shop is small and has only been open 2 weeks. You might be familiar with Sarah Ott's designs from other small shops...her script NOLA necklace and bracelet and other jewelry designs. This shop includes tshirts (men & women) and jewelry and scarves and other small accessories.  The store clerk was very nice and not pushy. I can't wait to see what Sarah comes up with next

The great thing about visitors is that you go out and eat special meals. This was my first trip back to la Petite Grocery (well besides for drinks) in several years. We had a fabulous meal.   My friend & I split the special soup & salad of the day. The soup was AMAZING. It was just perfect, leek & broccoli with a little bit of cream. The salad was well balanced with greens, blue cheese & pistachios.  We each had an appetizer as our main meal I had the spaghetti with blue crab. It was the perfect size and the crab was really luscious, but it was maybe a smidge over parmesaned which made it a bit salty...or maybe that's just me. This did not prevent me from gobbling it up. My friend had the octopus appetizer and said it was amazing.   So we planned to be good and stop and then I heard the special dessert was a peach gallette with strawberry ice cream. And my friend ordered the creme brulee. The gallette was lovely and huge! which did not stop me from eating it all. And my friend raved about the brulee.  The restaurant was pretty full as it was Jazz Fest weekend but service stayed on point and it wasn't too loud despite the happy crowds. I do have to mention that the flowers in the restaurant, on tables, the bar, the hostess station, etc were stunning, just really beautiful.  All and all a great meal.

My thoughts on Pascale's:    The food is good and a throwback to the menu on many NOLA restaurants in the 50s.    Don't eat the BBQ shrimp while wearing a silk blouse.  They are MESSY!  The raw oysters are supposed to be some of the best in the city; sadly I do not partake.  The wait staff can be...interesting, sometimes indifferent, sometimes super friendly.  I think it depends on the phase of the moon.

Long overdue review! I discovered this adorable local shop last Christmas and they have a great selection of stuff. Lots of artistic oriented gifts, mostly with a NOLA theme. Cute baby stuff, crafty items, jewelry and art.  I've pretty much bought something everytime I've been in. This year it was an oyster themed tea towel, a handturned wooden spoon, and art.   I was back last night for their After Hours Art Pop-Up. My gift for my Mom just wasn't working out and I found the most ridiculous perfect gift from one of the vendors. Whew. And I'm done.  Definitely a place to stop and buy great NOLA/Louisiana themed gifts... or maybe even something for yourself. Those clay cheese boards...hmmm

The other Tuesday Morning that I shop at.  This one has the advantage of being twice the size as the Airline store.  It also has a good selection of furniture and rugs.  I bought a nice Tues. Morning rug pre-K and it survived being cleaned twice (thanks to my dog) but did not survive the Katrina flood waters.  Oh well, not a bad run for a large room rug that was purchased for around $350.

So if you've been following my twitter stream, you know I'm on jury duty in Civil Court this week.  What can I say it's jury duty, you're really bored while you're waiting around the jury pool room.  The chairs are uncomfortable but they do offer free coffee and water.  The bathrooms are reasonably clean and the staff is professional and recognizes that most folks don't want to be there.    Civil court has a leg up on criminal in Orleans parish because you actually call in to see if you need to show up.  So instead of heading in on each scheduled day, you call the night before.  As of this moment, the schedule is everyday for 2 weeks.

I needed a king cake, stat! So I ran by this new outpost of Haydel's Bakery on a Saturday evening. They had beaucoup king cakes and so many other adorable items, plus coffee, hot chocolate, what not.   It's a small shop but with it's gleaming surfaces and white color scheme it's very inviting. I like that there was a clear way to queue up to order your pastries/bevs/whatever.   Service was quick and my black & gold robbed cookie was delicious, as was the king cake!

I needed a quick lunch while working in Chalmette for the day and our first choice turned out to be closed. Since my friend had been here before, we turned around and chose breakfast for lunch (although they do have poboys and yknow actual lunch food).   I got a breakfast plate with eggs, grits and a biscuit. My friend got a special of bananas foster french toast. Both were good...and my biscuit was delicious. The server was friendly and quick with the iced tea refills. Real butter in the basket of goodies too!  Normally this spot might just be a 3 star for me but let's talk about the decor which elevates it one for me. Yes, it has a weird golf theme which I don't really get, but someone in the family must be a metal worker because there are beaucoup metal pieces all around the place. From the lovely, intricate benches outside, to the weird coat of arms high above the bar area - complete with golf clubs, of course, to the metal sculpture in the ladies room...honestly it was so quirky that I would come back just for that...and that grilled biscuit.

The Rendezvous is an interesting place. Back in the day it was a neighborhood old man bar. But times change and maybe the old men aren't as plentiful in neighborhood bars?   I've been hearing lots of friends sing the RT praises. So 1st weekend of parades, I got some crawfish at Big Fisherman down the street and met up with some out of town friends to visit and chow down.  Bartender was super nice and happy hour was until 8pm on a FRIDAY. Yes please. We sat at a table and made sure to clean up after ourselves. Lots of different folks in the bar, including some dog friends.   Will definitely be back

Every once in awhile, I wander into someplace in the FQ with friends and think "why have I never been here before?" I don't know why I've never been to Touche before. It's certainly been there since before I was of drinking age. Because OMG that downstairs (basement level in NOLA?!) paneled room...it feels like hanging out in my aunt & uncle's home bar in the 70s. (Don't worry we were only pretending to drink...really.)  The evening we stopped in, the bartenders were a bit overwhelmed by the volume of people hanging out for Dirty Linen. But they were hustling and dealing with the drunks easily.   Definitely a spot that will go into my rotation for FQ crawls.This is a solid old school bar. Order a straight pour, a beer or a basic mixed drink.

I swore that I wrote a review for this company but I guess it was one of those disappearing listings....  I've used their service a couple of times for my new baby. They do a great job getting all the pollen out of the nooks and crannies. And the inside is sparkling...until y'know I trash it again. The staff is great about communicating and payment is easy on square.   I love that I can shop or wander around the FQ while they handle my car, instead of just sitting in a waiting area. I wish they offered their services on weekends, but I think it's mainly geared to the people who used the garage as work parking. They offer their services at a couple of locations in the CBD.

I was wandering on this section of Magazine yesterday during the parades. I was surprised to see this new spot. So this is a drinks only, during parades review.  The entrance to the courtyard is actually on Bordeaux not Magazine so that was first tricky bit, but there were 80 bajillion chairs and people meandering around during the parade. There was a guy selling drink (small $5 and large $8) tickets and a limited drink menu... There were separate tickets for food and about 5 items on it. So I got my large drink ticket from him, ducked into the very clean, brand new restroom, took care of business and headed to the bar. The bartender was friendly and handled my mimosa easily. And even put it in my tervis for me... although he did question me about giving it to a child. Don't judge me on my need of a sippy cup at a parade. That's how you don't spill your drink!  I was surprised to see a longer menu posted in the photos. So maybe there is indoor dining? In the little building adjacent to the courtyard? I was so confused. Maybe the dining room entrance is on Magazine but was closed because of all the people?   Opening the Friday of parades is a crazy move! I'm not sure what the place will be like once we're back to normality. It's an interesting addition to an area with a bunch of bars/restaurants but nothing quite like this.

I like this Langenstein's and used to patronize it more often when I lived closer by.  Lots of prepared foods but the produce was a bit disappointing this evening.  Great beer & wine selection too.  I decided I needed their shrimp salad for dinner  (white remoulade as the dressing).  Delish.    I will say the parking lot was designed by a drunk person.

I bought a Living Social deal here last fall and realized that it was about to expire at the end of this month.  So off to the Plant Gallery I went.    I should mention that I had a plant moratorium imposed on me awhile back.  I am a bipolar gardener.  I get all inspired and do lots and then forget to water for weeks on end. This makes for many dead plants.  Which depresses my significant other when he has to throw them all away.  Anyway, I tried to focus on smaller plants (less painful to look at once they're dead) and herbs.  I ended up with some lovely geraniums for the front porch and whole bunch of herbs for the kitchen garden (OK really it's a bunch of pots, but much of my yard is concrete thanks to previous owners).  The prices were competitive and the staff was very knowledgeable and friendly.

Stop and take a breath.  Admire the historically inaccurate statue of Andrew Jackson (rearing horses are for folks who died in battle).   Consider that this square is where early militia did maneuvers and what the city must have looked like.  Enjoy the art on the fence around the square; chat up the artists and maybe even buy something.

Long overdue review: The combo with the beer garden means that there is something for everyone at these sister establishments. The food is a bit more elevated on the wine garden side and the wines on tap or by the glass are numerous and tasty. If your companions want draft beer, then they just wander over the beer side and get that. Same for a basic burger.  On the wine side the menu is a bit fancier... and yummier in my opinion, their mac-n-cheese is tasty (currently artichoke and spinach but I've had crawfish before too) as are the stupidly addictive garlic-parm fries. The roasted cauliflower side is delicious. The only miss for me has been the fried avocado taco. But I think I'm just not a fan of that preparation. Live and learn.  The happy hour prices for wine, sangria, beer and a couple of batched cocktails are quite reasonable and run until 6:30pm. Plus when it's warm out, there's usually frose! Just like the beer garden, there are 2 bars one inside (dark and sexy) and one outside (sort of like drinking at a cabana club).   Small parking lot behind the outdoor area, but it fills up fast. The outdoor areas are dog friendly. And the private party space is available too.  Fun times and making everyone happy. I like it.

Solid neighborhood bar. I don't know about the dive thing though...maybe because I remember what this place used to be before it was renovated. Oh well.  I don't stop in often and I don't usually stay long so that sort of says it all.  Bonus points because La Cocinata is outside often.

The little nieces (one who is now taller than me) had been asking to go on a paddleboat ride since they spotted them in the spring. With that in mind I had purchased a Groupon back in April/May (maybe?), we didn't make it until I had the girls for a couple of days in July. YES, I went on a paddleboat ride in July in NOLA. Yes I am an idiot.  The service was great! They actually honored my Groupon which had just expired so I was very happy to save the money. The staff was friendly and made sure we understood how our 4 person boat worked. My 12 year old niece (the one taller than me) and I made sure to sit opposite to counterweight each other as advised, as the 9 year old is a twig.  We got there right as they opened at 10 but OMG it was already so hot. While the shop does sell water, I was glad I had brought big water bottles from home which were full of ice too.   Turns out the nieces didn't really understand how much work the paddling is AND they were scared of spiders (1 on the boat), alligators (we saw none), sticks in the water that looked like alligators...or snakes (many), going under bridges (2 & the only place to get out of the sun), the ducks and geese that started following us (OK actually I was scared of that goose...it was big).   To get us back to the dock, I started having to badger them to paddle and I thought I would pass out from the exertion and the heat. 45 minutes of fun!  Next time I'll wait for cooler weather. So don't try the paddleboats in July. The end.

So many hotel bars are soulless... just a spot to unwind after a rough day of travel. Not this one. It's so frigging cute!   It's small space but that just makes it cozy. It has vintage charm for days. Plus if the light/weather is right, the patio is perfect and lots of folks were wandering out to take selfies in front of exposed brick walls.  The bartenders were solid and the bubbles were cold. Plus there's a pop up for snacks and you can pay for that at the bar. Definitely a spot I'd pop into again.

My niece wanted to have some Halloween fun last month so we drove over to Ghost Manor and watched the fun. We watched from across Magazine as it was really crowded around 8pm the Saturday before Halloween.  It's amazing that this is just someone's fun decor! The 11 year old niece thought it was up to Disney standards. And since we are both short, across the street gave the best viewing. And when an additional character suddenly appeared, it was less scary to be far away. The songs were fun and the synchronization was great. My favorite are the animated eyeballs in the top windows. To watch the full cycle of songs took less than 30 minutes.   The music isn't too loud... which I'm sure the neighbors are appreciative of. And the scariest thing I saw was an older man who almost walked into Magazine street traffic because he forgot where he was.   Park a few blocks away and walk over. Don't stop right in front of the house and block traffic or the views of the people who are already watching. Be friendly and don't try to scare little kids!

I drop off my online shopping returns here pretty often. And the store is usually super crowded with stuff, boxes and whatnot. But the staff is great and very helpful. New policy that your dropoffs are scanned immediately and you get a receipt. When I did that this week, my return was processed immediately by the seller and my $ was refunded. So yay!  What makes this place just OK is the parking lot... yes it's a business uptown with a parking lot so that's great. BUT it's a lot that services 11 different businesses plus UPS trucks picking up/dropping off so it can be chaos. And, of course, the perpetual problem that other people don't know how to drive/park.

So when they say large, believe them the large is LARGE. I was starving middle of the day and cranky and nothing sounded tasty. And then I decided I needed pizza. AND I saw shrimp remoulade pizza on their menu.  Delicious. The shrimp are great and the remoulade made a nice addition. My Caesar salad was fine but nothing great. Wish they would have had fresh brewed tea, rather than just bottles...but they have a yummy drink menu. And if I hadn't been heading back to work, I would have tried one of their frozen daiquiris.   Decor is slightly funkier than the last pizza spot in this location. Staff was pleasant and I wish I would have had time to eat out on their deck.

Whenever someone says there's an event at Cafe Istanbul, I flash back to the 90s when it was a major club on Frenchmen Street. But no. This is a lovely theater inside the Healing Center building. And it is accessed from the back along St. Roch. There is a small parking lot that is accessed from N. Rampart.   I was there for a charitable event with a variety of musical presenters... shout out to the dance group that finished their number by holding music streaming from a phone up to a mic when the sound system cut out. Sound was pretty good but at least one band was just too much for the small space.   The bar prices were $$$ but maybe that's because the charity was getting a cut. Restrooms outside the theater were clean and spacious.

I used to go to this building... back in the day when it was a bar. So when it opened as Sucre, I could not believe how light and airy and beautiful the renovation was. Seriously. Night and Day.  If you've been to the other Sucre locations around NOLA, you know what to expect. Gorgeous pastries, luscious ice creams and delectable chocolates at a premium price. And mostly the items are worth the price. I think I've had one pastry in all these years that did not live up to the beauty.   Service can be hit or miss. Sometimes you get a super attentive really good server and sometimes you get a bored teenager. Oh well.  Love that you can just drop in and grab and go.

Not my favorite gas station...but one of the closer ones to my house that is actually name brand gas. The pump lines are tight which isn't usually an issue...until people start freaking out about an impending storm and then everyone gets super aggressive.  The prices are higher then most other uptown stations which are always higher than the 'burbs. Another cost of living in the city.

This is what passes for a shopping mall in the Garden District.  *Converted historic building - Yep *Random boutique shops - Yep *no National stores - Yep *Random other offices - Yep  There's a good coffee shop (Still Perkin'), cute kids clothing store (Mignon), a great book store (Garden District) and a couple of boutique/gift shops (Bonner & Judy) and then there is a bunch of rotating stores...I miss the kitchen store that was here pre-K. Plus real estate offices, lawyer offices, whatever.  Some Rink secrets...there is a small parking lot underneath the building that is accessed via Washington Ave. It was built as a skating rink (I guess for those new-fangled roller skates) in 1884.  Seriously the building is lovely. Stop inside and enjoy the atrium. Modern shopping centers wish they could get that ambiance.

It's been years since I had eaten at Silk Road but I had been hearing that chef Ganesh was back behind the stove... and I had loved his food years ago at Old Calcutta in the Riverbend.   I stopped in after a nearby art show with a friend. We shared the samosas and some saag paneer. I also had tikka masala and my friend had something with eggplant. Everything was good and tasty.  Service was fine and there was lovely live musician playing.

Typical NOLA food outside of work? Yep I'm trying it. The shrimp poboy was OK. The bread was too soft for me (more like a roll than french bread) and there wasn't enough lettuce/tom/pickle for me. My friend got the burger and loved it though. The fries are really good.  They tend to be near the medical campuses a couple of times per week. They don't seem to really post on their FB page or anywhere else as to where they'll be on any given day. So you just have to happen upon them I guess.  The owners are super nice.

Great selection of whiskeys! I was here on a chill Wednesday night, celebrating a friend's birthday. There were HH specials (a punch called Tiger Woods) and our bartender/owner was amazing. I got to try 2 new to me whiskies so that's exciting and the feeling is more like you're in someone's awesome home bar. Definitely seemed like most folks were getting straight pours rather than fancy cocktails.   The space is lovely with a variety of seating and a cool vibe. There is space out back to enjoy the Sticks portion of the menu and though it was rainy several of my friends enjoyed the space & the cigars while under an umbrella. The owner also moved some chairs to under the front awning.  Be prepared to be buzzed in. And there is a single bathroom which is OK because this isn't a huge space... but plan accordingly.

Pandemic Update:  Staff is masked and patrons are required to be masked (as is still the city mandate). They have hand sanitizer by the front door.  As always super cute merchandise, mostly made in Louisiana. I was specifically there for my 2nd brother's birthday present but ended up with some cute things for me too.  Staff is friendly and courteous.  Love a quick in and out! And since I walked over, I had zero issues with parking.

This market is no longer overseen by the group that does the Crescent City Farmer's Market on Saturday mornings.  The owners of the wine store in the American Can Company (the market is in the parking lot) have been working to get this one going again.  But it is so small, I don't know that I would go out of my way to check it out again.  There was only 2 produce vendors on the day I went, 1 seafood vendor and 1 dairy vendor. The other half dozen were all selling prepared foods.  Not really what I was looking for.

Pandemic update: Martin's is doing a great job. All staff is wearing masks. Outside there are clear signs that say clean baskets and used baskets for your grocery carts. They are doing in side pickup and delivery (not sure if that's just food or what). There is a big table at the front door with orders pulled for pickup.   The shelves are fully stocked with all the booze. They had a good cheese selection and they have limited catering items from the kitchen in the back. All the tables in the kitchen area are pushed together and all the chairs are stored away.   So if you're drinking your way through this insanity. Martin's has you covered.

This is one of those occasions that perhaps a new listing would have been better than a change of address. Disregarding reviews from prior to May 2016 is probably smart.   This is much smaller than the old Westbank location but it's completely suited to a quick downtown lunch. The hours are totally different too. M-F 10-5pm for dine in and then 5-7pm for takeout.  There is no longer table service, instead you queue up and place your order than find a seat.. Great bar seating plus a smattering of tables, maybe four 4tops and eight 2tops. There's also a bench for those waiting for takeout.  The menu is about the same as the old WB location. The staff is hustling! So even though it may look crowded, your food will come out quickly. Also they package to go orders carefully so no spills!  I'll definitely be back and that to go option at the end of a work day sounds great.

Another restaurant that I can't believe I haven't reviewed yet.  Pho Tau Bay has delicious Vietnamese food in a diner like setting. The prices definitely reflect the no-frills atmosphere.  And, man, is the food good.  They have a good selection of both veggie & meat dishes. And the menu does a good job of letting the diner know what she will be getting.  The ice tea is a tasty jasmine variety.  Days closed are Thursday & Sunday.

Gorgeous new location for this midcity shop. I feel like this location is even more spacious but maybe that's just the layout.  Last night was the grand opening and there were tons of people there and an art market outside for the occasion. I'm glad there will be space for special events just like the midcity location.  Lots of great local art, pottery, tshirts, jewelry and housewares for sale, from the GNO (greater New Orleans area) to Mississippi...   The staff is lovely and there's space to move about. Since this is a converted house on Magazine street (like the original location). I'm not sure that it has a ramp. So call if you need that accommodation.

Wow! The store is pretty huge and spacious for a neighborhood market. There is beaucoup parking adjacent to the store (on the lakeside) and across Peniston in a new lot.  There were plenty of staff to offer assistance and while the store was still being fully stocked (they only opened on Friday), there was plenty of interesting items to peruse.   The deli area is huge! The cases are spacious and it was definitely not crowded the day after their opening. There was a grab & go case but also plenty of seating for dining in.   I bought a sampling of single local beers for a houseguest at the end of the month and some Martins branded fruitcake for an early present for my parents. I will definitely be hitting up the deli/prepared food section in the months ahead.  Also, I moved all my photos from the Closed version of this store to the new listing. Yes after all this time, I still fail at Yelp.

Pandemic review Gabrielle's is doing low contact takeout Friday through Sunday. AND they are offering a coolinary special for the month of August (maybe into mid September). Online ordering from their website with no contact payment. And you set your pickup time. Super easy.  I picked up 2 three course coolinary dinners last night for me and mom. Not only was it delicious but there was so much food, we both have leftovers for today!  As always their crab bisque is stunning and my mom was surprised at how large the Cobb salad was. She loved the dressing.  The entrees we chose were the grilled gulf fish, with a crabcake and the BBQ shrimp pasta. Wow they were both delicious. Mom was raving about the amount of crab was in the crabcake.  Finally we had the peaches and cream and chocolate pecan pie for dessert. I thought I wasn't a fan of shortbread cookies, clearly I just had poor versions; paired with fresh peaches and Creole cream cheese, perfection! The pie was rich and decadent. Perfect end to the meal.  Pickup is easy on the side of the restaurant at what looks like a snowball stand window, just ring the doorbell. And I love that everything was packaged beautifully and that all dishes did well as takeout.

Reasons I have been to the SKC: * to go vote (2020) * to see the Police from a suite! (2007) * to see Cirque du Soleil perform (?) * to actually see a basketball game (???)  This sports arena works as a multipurpose space and I really appreciated that it was opened up for use as an early voting location for the 2020 Presidential Election.   Plenty of parking nearby. Good signage. For voting, social distancing was enforced, everyone wore masks and we were given finger cots to cast our ballot on the touch screens.  Fastest voting experience ever!

I had not been inside this spot in a very long time. VERY.  But I was taking my parents to an early dinner after a health appointment and we wanted to try a new spot AND I remember that they were already advertising crawfish at a good price so off we went.  The crawfish were really good. Small but that's to be expected this early in the season (end of January) but really good seasoning. Spicy but not too spicy. And they had potatoes and corn if we needed.  Dad got a fried oyster plate and the oysters were huge. Mom got the grilled trout platter and she said the fish was delicious. I had the shrimp remoulade salad with grilled shrimp and it was huge and OK. The remoulade was really good but I would have preferred boiled shrimp and next time I would do fried. Plus the shrimp were small, but there were plenty of them.  Service was... disorganized but sweet. There were so many people wandering around, but our crawfish came out before we got waters/tea. The entrees came out and we hadn't been given silverware. Everything was rectified but it was just weird.  Ambiance is dated and looks pretty much the same as the last time I was in there... as I said it's been a long time.  Will definitely go back if I'm in the area, especially for the crawfish.

I was surprised when I finally made it over to this lovely new bar... because the last time I was at this address, it was still a private residence. But it's a great new addition to the NOLA cocktail scene as one would expect from one of the leaders of the NOLA bar world.   The courtyard was gorgeous on a slightly cool evening, and it was a lovely respite from the bustling scene inside. So no matter your mood, there was a vibe for you. My cocktail was the Night Tripper and it was funky and perfection... much like it's name sake.   I wish their food menu had more snacky items, something shareable while you are having a drink. But I get that they are serving full dinners and not just bar food.   Service was perfect, of course.

Since it's been a few years, and I've dealt with another plumber (my general contractor subbed out a job to his go to guy), it's about time to update this review.  Richie or his guys have over the years, moved the plumbing in my bathroom, replaced fixtures, tested gas lines, removed space heaters, installed a dishwasher, checked out random leaks, and other plumbing ickiness.  He's always been up front about the costs and his workers have always been respectful and communicative about the work being done.  I'm glad some of my Yelp besties have had the same experience and it's not just that I've known him since grade school.

OMG! I was overwhelmed by the scent of chocolate as I opened the door. Is it possible to get drunk off that smell?   I bought one of each of the bonbons in the case...which the owner/chocolatier said was a little light at the moment since they're focusing on super fancy king cakes (3 types) which look amazing! Someone should totally buy me one.  My bonbons were satsuma, brandy milk bunch, tiki, chanterelle something or other, and king cake. Plus I bought some of their single source dark chocolate bark with nuts and candied kumquats. I endeavored to not gobble up all the bonbons in a fit of ravenous greed and to be all dainty and savor each one. They were all delicious, even the brandy milk punch (love the drink not a fan of white chocolate). The chanterelle (yep mushroom) had an interesting earthiness and I would totally get this one again. The satsuma was probably my favorite but then again I'm a citrus and chocolate person all the way. You could definitely taste the rum in the tiki one and it was the prettiest of the bonbons I think. The king cake one was stunning with hints of cinnamon. The bark has just enough salt and the dark chocolate is amazing.  I'll definitely be back and they tell me that they might be making dipped candied orange peel which would make me the most faithful customer ever!  LOVE the creativity of their case... zombies, tombs, Han Solo encased in carbonite/chocolate, And that gorgeous scent!

This is a review for the Mid-City Thursday market. I'm not sure why it says Metairie with an address on Vets but I've submitted updates.  I was running home from an appointment on City Park Avenue last week and I saw the CCFM signs reminding me about the Thursday market so I u-turned and headed over.   Since it's June a brief heavy cloudburst had just finished but the puddles were easy to avoid. Booths are currently very well spaced and since I was there before 5 it wasn't too crowded.   I was able to get peaches, green beans, creole tomatoes, sheepshead filets, tofu and gorgeous bread.   Yummy!  Only downside was that parking was tight. There were signs saying no street parking but people were anyway and that caused issues on the 2way street.

Oh no! You're about to drive across the Causeway and you realize you need gas because who knows what will happen on those 20+ miles. Chaos could be ahead of you. And if you're on the southshore, sure there's a gas station on the right side of the road and all BUT it's usually 10 cents (or more) more expensive then u-turning into this Exxon station.  The station is clean. The pumps work. There is a store that sells the caffeinated beverage of your choice.   Please note that this store is still more expensive then other Metairie locations but it is always way cheaper than across the street.

This spot near my work opened last week and my coworker let me snitch a couple of appetizers. Yum! Loved both the pakora and the samosa. So today we did a big group order (via an app) and got lunch for 4 of us who are in person at work today.   We picked up (and they seem to mostly be dealing with app delivery) and the space has only a couple of tables and chairs so I think they are mostly doing takeout and almost no dine in at the moment. Both staffers put on masks when we arrived.   I had palak paneer and my coworkers got a variety of dishes. All are tasty. Also they have fried bhindi aka fried okra. Yum!  They have been very grateful for our business both times we've been in. Indian can be hard to get in NOLA so super glad this place is close to work.

I called Jefferson Appliance in September to look at 3 appliances at my old double (which I'm currently renting out).  Of course, on one appliance the problem wouldn't duplicate while the repair person was there.  Figures.  Another problem turned out to be a loud motor and as the dishwasher was out of warranty, it would cost more for a new motor than to just replace the whole machine.  Satisfactory answers on both and the price of the new motor was related via a follow up call.  The final appliance was a front loader washing machine.  We were told it wasn't working because my tenant was using too much soap and they left.  But it turns out that it only worked once or twice after they tried the approved cleaning method.  So I called Jefferson Appliance back...and left a couple of messages.  No one has ever returned my phone call.  Perhaps they've gone out of business?  Or maybe they just don't want mine.

Here's my disclaimer:  I grew up with Richie so I've known him about a million years.  And he's a good guy.  He worked with me on my bathroom renovation pre-K, even advising ways to help us cut costs on things we could do ourselves.  Post-K he inspected my gas lines and got my gas turned back on and fixed the leaks that were caused by random floating stuff that slammed into my pipes.

What a parade that I haven't reviewed?! How is that possible.  I like that this parade is coed and has some really random celebrities so that you can try to remember who they are when you're already carnival-ed out and your brain is sloooowwww.   The flowers were really pretty this year. And the throws seemed to be plentiful, except that I didn't see any Leviathan stuffed animals thrown near me. Those are my favorite.  I had planned to head home after Proteus since I was tired and had an early morning planned on Mardi Gras but the parade (and my friends) was engaging enough to keep me until the firetruck rolled by.

I've been wanting to try this restaurant since it opened and it finally happened on Friday night.  Best dishes? Mixed ceviche of drum & shrimp and the shrimp tropicale. The other delicious dishes we sampled? Sangria, asparagus, the potatoes, creme brulee valencia, vanilla flan, and the bread & aioli.  Only dish I was meh on was the fried salmon nuggets...although others in my group really liked them.  Our server was sweet, but didn't know the menu too well. Luckily the other server jumped in with assistance. The location is intimate and comfortable.  Three people left very sated and the bill was only about $100. Well worth it.  If you're dining alone and prefer bar dining...they have that too.  I would go back in a heart beat.

I used to live almost across the street from this Shell and even bought bread there once in desperation.  The station is well lit and mostly clean.  The pumps usually have paper for receipts (if you care about that sort of thing).  The car wash is well maintained.  Considering the surrounding neighborhood, it's really much less sketchy than it could be...and I say that as someone who lived nearby.

Pandemic update: For whatever reason the online apps thought PTB was closed on Mondays so I had to call in my group order. I had planned to walk over to pickup so really no big deal. Masks are required. More than 1/2 the tables are marked for non-use to aid social distancing. And there's a QR code near the door if you want to scan and look at a menu on your phone rather than pickup a paper menu. One entrance in and one out. Plus markers on the floor while you're lined up to keep everyone distanced.  Since I had called in the order, my food was to the side waiting on me. So that was super easy, just had to sign the receipt and put down the tip.   I had the tofu bun and it was delicious as always. The rest of my group was very happy with their food from soup to banh mi. Pho Tau Bay does not disappoint!

Why are people reviewing this location which is currently an empty lot? This location has not been open since the federal flood in 2005.  But seriously Martin's Wine Seller people...what's the hold up with the new building? There has been a concrete base poured for a couple of years and nothing but blowing sand. I would be very unhappy with you as my neighbor at the moment.   At least the Google street view was when you were actually working on it, I think.  Annoying.  And, yes, I will mark it closed.

I've purchased a couple of pieces from Halpern's including a sofa that was supposed to be delivered the week of Aug.29, 2005.  Oh well I eventually got a replacement Jan.2006 which I consider EXCELLENT service all things considered.  Much of the wooden furniture is made by their woodworking folks, so you can customize to your hearts content.    The only reason they don't get 5 stars is that they are still filing all their orders on paper and are not computerized at all.  I know, hard to believe, but it's true.  It makes it hard to ask questions about your order as they have to find the actual paper order.
