Wow! What a wonderful meal we had! It was a random Wednesday when I finally had dinner at the reincarnated Gabrielle. We made reservations for 6:30 (phone calls only, ugh!). My friend ordered a really lovely bottle of rose bubbles (no idea what) and it complemented our meal perfectly.  I was not as hungry as I needed to be! But I still attempted 4 courses... all appetizers this time. I started with the bisque and OMG it was good, earthy and rich and full of crabmeat. Next I had the grilled shrimp salad with pistachios. Super tasty and the shrimp were perfect. For my entree I had the appetizer special of the evening which was a crawfish enchilada; the corn tortilla was an amazing complement to the crawfishes.  We had pre-ordered a blueberry pie/buckle/something, another special and it was tasty. PLUS a flourless chocolate torte with peppermint ice cream. Both were delicious and the chocolate dessert felt like you were injecting chocolate directly... in a good way.  Our service was great, offering us fresh french bread and more butter. Our water glasses were never empty and the bubbles were flowing.  I really enjoyed the space too. Simple decor with some well selected paintings. Next time I'm sampling craft cocktails!
Really they deserve 3 1/2 stars.  My color always looked great, but I was never totally happy with my cut.  And I thought the prices were a little high for the atmosphere.

While this spot has been a diner for decades... and I grew up down the street, I'd never been in. But today was the day! Mom chose this spot for a quick family lunch after hearing good things from the neighbors.  The owners/workers were super friendly and patient with our usual family nonsense. You order at the counter and most people carried out but there are some tables to dine in.  We had a fried shrimp poboy (niece enjoyed and it was huge with a good number of shrimp), chicken tender plate (3 huge tenders and a different niece said it was delish), 2 shrimp plates (shrimp on mine were super tasty but the onion rings were meh but Dad liked his mashed potatoes), and a shrimp/fish plate (Mom said it was good and I tasted the fish and it was good and she liked her cole slaw). The big hit was the fried okra. We got the large serving and we ate it all. I LOVE fried okra!  Fountain drinks or a cooler of bottled drinks were available. Mom also got a mango bubble tea which she said it was a tasty dessert.   Great addition to the neighborhood.

Pandemic update: Things are afoot at the Rink! Evidently there are new owner of this nearly 150 year old building. Yes it was built as a roller skating rink in the 1880s. Crazy fads!  There have been renovations happening and some tenants have had their spaces re-shaped and others are not staying. It will interesting to see what happens in 2021 with this space.  Masks are required and they have signs up about who is cleaning the space. As always the parking underneath the building is key to a quick visit.

What has Richie's crew done for me recently... * Installed a dishwasher. * Changed what must have been the original sink drain pipe in the kitchen (HORRIFYING). * Installed a new kitchen sink.   Just a week or so ago, they fixed terracotta pipes under my coworker's house because they were cracked. Gotta love an old house.   I've used Richie's Plumbing for over 20 years and always highly recommend.

My 130 year old house has entered the 20th century when I had central air & heat installed a couple of months ago. It was a pretty straight forward job as my attic has plenty of space and y'know a shotgun equals a straight run.   My sales person, Chase, was great and we discussed then entire job and the contract detailed every aspect. Which was great as a referral tool during the install. The price was good and I asked (and received a discount) because I had 2 systems installed (both sides of my shotgun).  The actual installers tried to be as neat as possible which was difficult considering the volume of slate debris in my attic and that my ceilings are doubled...old plaster with lathe and then a layer of gypsum board (pre-dates modern drywall). The job went as Chase had told me it would.   I've been really happy so far and my house has been nice and cool in August & September. We'll see how toasty warm I am in a month or so.

I was so confused to discover the sign that said Betty's Bar since I knew this as the 700 Club. But sure OK.   It was trivia night when we walked in and while I didn't participate they asked some legit hard questions. Plus there was a drag queen hustling the evening along.   My friends got an assortment of tacos and while I tried the mac-n-cheese taco I was way too sober to eat that carb bomb. Everyone wolfed their food down so they must be good.  Drinks were good and the place was packed with trivia teams. There's also beaucoup tvs; I'm not sure if they show sporty-sports on them as it was all music videos when I was there but that might be what happens.

Pandemic update: For much of this 2020 insanity, Piety has been offering curbside pickup at their shop on Broad. No going inside but ordering online and giving them an actual phone call to let them know you've arrived. Their bonbons have gotten me through.  Fast forward to December when they started doing a popup next to the St. James on Prytania. So while all the commercials were recommending that I give myself the gift of a new car, I instead gave myself the gift of delicious chocolate! So a box of bonbons and some of their yummy peppermint bark... oh and a cup of their hot chocolate which was like mainlining cocoa, yknow in a good way.  The popup was outside. Everyone was masked. It all went very smoothly. And I had chocolate to soothe my jangled nerves.  Eleventy-billion stars.

Oh wow it's been a minute since I've actually dine at Antoine's. And when Re suggested that we enjoy their summer lunch special, I said sure! You can't beat $20.18 for 3 courses!  To avoid parking drama, I used a rideshare into the FQ from work which worked out great both going and coming. The waiter was great and took into account that two of us had to rush back to work while the rest of the group could be more leisurely. I had the strawberry salad and the drum and the mousse as my three choices from the prix fixe. All three courses were delicious and not so huge that I felt like I was in a coma when I went back to work.  They do have a daily drink special for $2 (I think) but that day it was a screwdriver so I opted for a glass of bubbles instead which was perfect.   We sat in a corner of the large annex dining room which made it easier to see the memorabilia on the walls. The large annex is my preference over the main dining room.   Thanks to Re for getting me back over to this icon!

They get bumped up a star for their unique pastry case items.   This week I tried a couple of their savory pastries...a cruffin and a scone. I'm not sure what was really in either item. The cruffin definitely had cheese & garlic and the scone was mostly herbs. And they rotate what's in the case, so if definitely ask what's the flavor of the day to avoid stuff you're not fond of/allergic to.  I've been back several times since May and I've always been pleased with the quality, texture & taste of every pastry item.  Now if I could make it back over there for lunch...
Lucky's is a great neighborhood bar.  The staff is tolerant of your nonsense, but not to the point where you're allowed to abuse other patrons.  I like that in a bar.

Y'know just when you think you've been *everywhere* in NOLA, someone plans a birthday party at a venue and you realize you've never even been in this area.  The name indicates the theme of the bar which has beaucoup nautical flags and whatnot on the walls. The bar is suitably dark and comfortable; there is a game room out back with an assortment of entertainments and big windows that open up to the patio. The patio seemed to be newly overhauled when I was there and it's a beautiful space to host a birthday party. The theme of the party was silly hats and no one in the bar gave my grandmother's vintage beach hat a second glance...even with the brightly painted shells which are sewn onto it.  The sangria of the day was delicious and the tuna melt...was weird (tuna & cheese) but a huge portion for the price.   Definitely a chill place to hangout with friends.

I usually avoid writing reviews of national chains, but Petco sponsored an adoption by ARNO this weekend, so I guess they get some brownie points.  Our elderly piglet of a dog requires special dog food; Petco sells it at a reasonable price.  They have lots of other pet supply stuff that you might need.

If you're in the FQ and feeling fancy and not traditional (which is a problem for me since mostly it's fancy & traditional) then Vive is the place to get a cocktail. It is really pretty.  And their fancy drink menu is really tasty & fun.    I attended an event over the summer and had something with champagne (freshly opened split bottle) and violetta.  It was pretty & super yummy to the point of dangerous.  The bartenders held their own against the overpacked house my group brought in for the evening and were really good natured about the insanity.  The patio & pool are very tempting even with the heat (or cold right now).  At the Yelp event here, I chatted up some fake Canadians and they said the rooms in the accompanying hotel was really nice.  Plus it's the sort of place where you can meet fake Canadians...but, of course, I needed Canadian Jennifer to tell me they were fake.  Well, not really since even I could tell they had the wrong accents.

Since someone just asked, this is the shop that we use for basic repairs on our truck.  We've used them off and on for a number of years depending on the problem with the vehicle & which car it was.  The staff is knowledgeable and friendly to work with.  Although really, automotive stuff falls within my partner's purview as he is a carguy.

Of the suburban megaplexes, this is my favorite.  It has stadium seating and alcohol.  I don't usually buy snacks so can't really comment on the snackbar...except when it comes to the frozen Jack & coke.  C'mon you know you want to drink at the movies too.    Or maybe it's just me, see in the 80s there was a daquiri cinema within a 1/2 mile of the Elmwood Palace and it had lots of high octane drinks.  I saw everything from the first Star Trek movie (nerd alert!) to the first Die Hard (I know I am super cool) all with a potent daquiri in hand.

I was out in Elmwood when I decided that a takeout pizza was just the thing to make the rest of my evening. And since I'm a big fan of the other Theo's locations, I stopped in.  This is definitely the largest of the Theo's and if I had a big group, to dine in, then I might trek out to Elmwood instead of to my closer uptown location. The staff was courteous and professional.  The menu seems to be the same at all 3 locations (although I would guess the specials might be unique to location). I'm a big fan of their crust which is thin and crackery like.

Real wood furniture in a super cute old building in old Gretna. The staff is really helpful; the prices are good and like I said REAL WOOD.  I've previously purchased book shelves from them (stained to match existing ones) in 2008. This time I purchased the perfect kitchen table and a small writing desk. The turn around was superquick since they had both tables in stock.  I'm loving their new rocking chairs and I have my eye on another storage piece that I may order later this summer.   Seriously good folks.

Amazing brie sammich!  I stopped in on my way to Jazz Fest because I needed some breakfast items before I ate all the rich food on the grounds.  The space is bright and open and the staff were really helpful.  I got a mini cake/muffin (super yummy), a brookie (interesting concept but my niece was more enamored than I was), a chocolate covered cinnamon roll (OMG good) and the special sandwich of the day...brie, jam, spinach, walnuts on a baguette. So amazingly good.  I will have to put this spot into lunch rotation on days when I can runaway.

In my mini-shopping palooza (see my other reviews from today), I also hit Bloomin' Deals the only straight-up thrift store of the group.  The  store was arranged in a sensible functional manner.  The stock was as varied and interesting as it always is.  You do need to check your pieces carefully as this is again all donated clothing, although I did find a skirt with store tags still on it.  Unfortunately I would have needed to be an Amazon to wear it.  Plus I scored a formal length black velvet skirt for $6 for my event in 2 weeks.  Bonus don't even need to hem it.

Perfectly acceptable hotel bar at the Sheraton near the Galleria in Metry.  The space is both the restaurant and the lobby and the bar. The staff was attentive and friendly. There is a nice patio area that is sort of on the street but they do a good job of screening it with potted plants so it is a nice space. There's also a lounge area adjacent if sofas are more to your liking.  The prices for some drinks seemed a bit high, but my friends got discounted rates for drinks so woohoo for half price.

So my stylist has left her previous salon and opened up her own space even closer to my house, so of course, I chased Nicole over here.  The new salon is bright and airy. There are only 3 chairs and right now only 2 stylists so not as hustly-bustly as bigger salons. Everything is clean, new and charming.  As always, Nicole gives great cut and color. And always get compliments on my hair.  Love their online booking system!

Crazy that this place only has 1 review. Not only do they have a good selection of plants, aquatic and not, shade and sun, annuals and perennials...you get the drift, they also sell a ton of yard art. Breaks my heart that I had to tell Vicky L that we could not buy the 8 foot $3k gorilla.  Oh and did I mention fountains?  Inside is a great shop for home decor items and other gifty things with a gardening edge. AND then there's the jewelry behind the counter.  I've been able to find affordable Christmas gift items some years that were just perfect.    Bonus points for having a private lot so you don't have to hunt for off street parking.

Another dinner at the Am. Sector and another lovely cocktail.  This time we snacked on the onion rings which turned out to be heavily battered...which I normally don't like but these were still light and delicious, although I was not a fan of the sauce that came with.  My dinner companion got the chicken fried steak and said it was yummy.  While for almost the same price, I ordered the crab salad and it was tiny.  The crabmeat was fresh and rich...but not that rich, y'know?  I wish I had been warned.  I've heard that the restaurant is packed at lunch but at dinner time you still nearly have the place to yourself.

This is in the other wacky strip mall on Metairie Road near the railroad tracks (fun fact it's on the former location of a car dealership, maybe Packer, and an old drive in). Look for the CC's in the back corner away from the tracks.  The shop is spacious with lots of indoor and outdoor seating...atlhough don't sit at the tables for Zoe's or try to bring Zoe's into the CC's...maybe turf battles.  I had quick service and polite baristas. The whole place does look like it needs to be cleaned up a little but maybe that's just the Christmas rush.

The dish I ordered (a special for the LA/SPCA fundraiser) seemed a little ambitious for such a low key restaurant but it won the WWL taste contest that morning so why not? And it was delicious...my only criticism would have been that the pieces of ginger were a bit large for me.  The scallops were well cooked and the risotto was tasty.  Definitely an ambitious local joint.

It had been almost 10 years since I went to Bayona.  I just don't get to the FQ fancy restaurants that often...typical local, I know.    I had a lovely lavender cocktail while we waited for our reserved cocktail - it was made with violet, elderflower liquer and bubbly.  So yummy I had another.  My 1st course was a special of crawfish pie; while it was fine, it was nothing super special and honestly, I've had better at festivals.  My main course was amazing though; I had the pepper encrusted tuna and it was cooked perfectly and the green peppercorns elevated it above the usual.  My dinner companions had the lamb, hangar steak, and fish.  Everyone agreed that the food was great.  We also sampled three desserts: a basic, but good creme brule, the strawberry pistachio bombe which was light and airy and not at all what I expected, and one of the daily sorbets but I can't remember the flavor.

I was invited to a liquor tasting in early December at Generations Hall. (Yes, a free liquor tasting and yes, I have the best friends EVER.) The space in divided in an interesting manner...I guess so you can rent just part of it. But we were in almost the whole hall. I liked that there were elevated spaces (the balcony above the stage area) and the bar in the big room that was a few steps up. The food was all catered by Miss Linda so that was yummy (if not super veggie friendly) and, of course, there was the free flowing liquor.  The venue staff was quick to clean up spills and seemed on top of things. All in all a really good adaptable space for a variety of rental needs.

This is the much smaller sister shop to the one on Maple, and it carries similar stock. Lots of higher end mall brands with a few actual designers thrown in. The longer the stock stays in the store, the less expensive it gets.  The shop is well laid out and they keep the browsing experience comfortable. The dressing room situation is not ideal and can get pretty jammed up on a busy day. The staff tries to keep it moving and is very helpful.   The sizes are mostly small so if you're a bigger boned gal, you're out of luck mostly. They also carry jewelry, accessories, purses and shoes.  I've never sold through them only purchased.

Great bright airy space with plenty of tables, some outlets but everyone seemed well behaved with no one fussing about low chatter. Love the pretty fresh flowers at every table and the comfy sofa where I was perched for a couple of hours.  My the iced tea was perfect...strong but not overwhelming. Since I went after work the dessert case was a bit picked over but others seem to enjoy the sweet bites they chose.   Love the monkey art. Wish their menu was available online...but unfortunately their website (from their FB page) is no longer valid.

Nine years later and I had to have my house tented AGAIN.  Dry wood termites are the devil. The housecall guys were professional but if you find termites get on their schedule! I made my appointment for the tenting around 2 months in advance and that was their first availability. Communication could have been a little better, but they figured I remembered from 2004 all the rules (not so much).   Still I'm glad to have ALL the bugs killed. And I just wish my neighbors would take care of their properties so I wouldn't get re-invested.

I was a bit late getting to this event and scored one of the last succulents.   The gardens were lovely and they do have an interesting selection of plants. The chickens and bunnies were not roaming as I had feared (was worried about hoards of children chasing them about) but were penned and protected.    The various partner businesses were interesting and their spokespeople were fun to talk to. The bluegrass music was good and not blaring.  A great way to spend a gorgeous evening.

I chose Ciro's Cote Sud for my birthday dinner this year since we hadn't been in years.  The food is just as delicious as always...why do I forget how much I love the pasta fruits del mer with a curry cream sauce.  E had a pasta with shrimp & veggie dish that was also tasty with lots of garlic.  My poached pear salad was tasty although the pears were really different from how I've had them before.  We finished by splitting the profiteroles...which were perfect.  I'm not sure when it became OK to serve profiteroles the size of your fist, I still prefer the golf ball sized ones.  These were perfect.   Oops I almost forgot to mention my yummy kir peche & E's well made sazerac. The wine list is pretty good too...as is only correct in a French restaurant.  Ciro's isn't great for a large group as it is a tiny restaurant and only has a dozen or so tables, but is perfect for an intimate meal. It is still cash/check only, but don't let that deter you.

oh y'know it's city hall. The building is old and not super attractive, although my Mom was mentioning the other day about when it was new and all high tech...yeah, high tech in the 60s. And, of course, government bureaucracy is annoying. BUT There are decent staff here. I've mostly entered the building for permits and to vote early. I wandered in to vote on a recent Saturday and there were plenty of signs to direct me and some indifferent sheriffs guarding the various doors. Once I was near the correct office, there were plenty of personnel to assist me and voting was super easy. Parked to done was maybe 15 minutes and that's with walking from a block or so over.   So 5 stars for the staff and 3 for the building for a resounding 4 star reviews. Wooo  And, hey, this is my 300th review for 2015! #glittercannon

Canine Connection/Culture is a boarding/ retail establishment focusing on your dog.    Want to buy your pup a deer antler to gnaw on? No problem.  Are you and your dog vegetarians? No problem. Do you want your dog to be able to snack on an all natural pig snout? No problem. They also carry Barkology and Life is Good  brands of human and doggie clothes.    I have not used their boarding facility though.

Since I was talking about King Cake babies the other night...because everyone does that in early December in anticipation of Twelfth Night... I mentioned that Monkey Monkey offers a rubber monkey with its king cakes but outside the cake because rubber. Then I hunted on Yelp for a photo and I hadn't mentioned this VERY IMPORTANT fact on the yelps or posted a photo. Please consider this rectified.  The Monkey Monkey king cake is baked in the shop and is yeasty and with a good cinnamon+ flavor (what's the plus? maybe mace or nutmeg or something warm and yummy). Plus the icing has a nice lemon flavor which makes it not too sweet. I ended up with a surplus of cakes on Mardi Gras day and this stale cake made the most delicious frenchiest of french toasts. Yum

It's just that OK. The crowd could definitely make or break the evening. I wouldn't order anything to challenging here, but the beer & liquor selection seemed good.  Also the space is big and airy enough to escape most of the lingering cigarette smoke.  +1 star for the balcony on a beautiful cool! night in June. -1 for a somewhat cranky bartender. AND we're back at 3.

Y'know if I liked tubes of meat, I'm sure Dat Dog is great. But I decided after eating about 1/2 my crawfish sausage dog here that I'm just not into hot dogs. Really it's not them it's me.  The bread is awesome though...maybe if I go back with friends, I'll just get bread with toppings.

I don't often get to the Tuesday Market since I work downtown and the location would be quite a jaunt on a lunch break. But this past Tuesday, I happened to have the day off to spend with one of my little nieces. She, of course, remembered that on Tuesday's there's a market that sells delicious popsicles. So off we went.  The popsicles (from the fruit juice vendor) were delicious, pineapple for me and strawberry for her.  Since we were there at the end of the market day, much of the produce and other products were sold out. But I was able to get some Gorgeous tomatoes.    I'll definitely be back on my next random Tuesday off.

Y'all. That savory crepe with gruyere, herbs, and an overeasy egg. SO DELICIOUS. And then my friend got the aebelskivers and they were awesome too. The tea selection was OK, but they had a some variety so I'll take it. My friends love their food and the coffee.   There was a wait on a Saturday morning but I liked that you can get a text when your table is ready. The space isn't the hugest. Be prepared to make friends with the table next to you.  The wait staff is hustling and have great attitudes.

I miss the location uptown so when I was parked nearby, I popped into their new (I know it's been since the beginning of the year) downtown location. What a great lovely space. It's so bright and airy! Great gift items and housewares and books and candles and jewelry and and...  The clothing selection is very targeted. And is lovely but not necessarily my style.   The staff has always been helpful without being pushy. Love that they will ship directly from the store for you.

Great renovation of small building. This is the 3rd seafood purveyor in this location and I'm really grateful that Bevi added more seating!   I've had a couple of things from here and it's all been tasty. The first time the crawfish were the perfect amount of spice. The 2nd time they were a little to mild for me but it was the first batch of the day. The shrimps have been yummy as have the boil veg.  The staff is really great and Katie can attest that I am WAY too amused by the fact that folks just do not know how to line up when they get busy. Maybe arrows on the floor?

I used to frequent this business at it's old location before Katrina. I can't believe how much larger the store is now.  And how much they've expanded their stock.  Little Miss Muffin was always a great housewares, children's clothes, great gift store, but now it carries a ton of shoes and women's clothes by local as well as national labels.  The store is chock-a-block full of stuff so be prepared to spend some time browsing.  They had quite a bit of Saints gear (and LSU) which was really different from what I've seen other places.  Parking is available across the street in the neutral ground.

How do I not have a review for Kim Son? Maybe it's because I haven't been in ages. And it's closing at the end of June 2018, so get over here while you can.  Kim Son is one of the OG Vietnamese restaurants in New Orleans. It's been around so long that half the menu is Americanized Chinese food, like egg foo young. They also have many many vegetarian items, many with fake meats if that's your thing.    They serve lunch and dinner 6 days a week and are only closed on Sunday. I can understand why it's time to retire. The owners must be exhausted.  I've enjoyed both Vietnamese and Chinese dishes. The service can be interesting. Our group once took too long to order and the Auntie got fed up, walked away and sent one of the teenagers to take our order. Don't keep the Aunties waiting!  I'm going to try to squeeze in one last visit before they're gone for good.

Shercole kept raving about this place. And then they started being a popup again and are no longer on St. Claude. They happened to be at the Freret Market one day and OMG that yummy seafood pancake that was only $7 for 3. So it was somwhere between a pancake and crepe and so filling and tasty.  I ended up bringing 1/2 of it home and gobbled it up later that night. Still delicious.   So I'm late to the bandwagon and they don't have a steady space or scheduled popups, but if you follow their FB page, then you might be able to successfully stalk them around town. Can't wait to try more.

Y'know I'm just trying to be like John and review gas stations.  But seriously this one is brand spanking new and is still all shiny & clean.  The gas is cheap (like most Racetracs) and the neighborhood really needed another decent gas station and especially one with such a large store.

Updating my review from 2013... Cleopatra liked Uptown so much they moved permanently to that route from the Westbank. This Krewe is pretty good. Lots of signature throws and they're now doing hand decorated goblets to compete with the coconuts and shoes and purses.   Because they are first Friday and expanding they had excellent bands and many of the adult marching krewes which is a fun way to kick off the season.   Definitely a good addition to the much smaller Oshun.

I doubt that this will be by goto Whole Foods anytime soon, but it's great for a quick run in. I can usually find what I need and I'm out. It does seem to be focusing on prepared foods more than actual groceries...then again it isn't a huge store.   I will say the fruits & vegetable section looks gorgeous! And they do have a good selection of cheeses. I liked the two version checkout process, one for express and one for a full cart of grocieres, although it confused folks in front of me.   The staff has been very pleasant and the store is really clean. As always the parking lot seems to confuse the patrons.

We went here last night with my MiL for dinner; she had been the week before for lunch because an organization for which she works was considering the Stage Door Canteen for a private event.  And she couldn't stop raving about the food. Boy was she right.  In addition, I mentioned to one of my brother's that I was going to Am. Sector & he said that the prices seem high (for lunch) until you see how much food you have.  He was enthusiastic about the food & the atmosphere.   We ordered our drinks and the waiter (cute retro uniforms!) brought us an amuse bouche of restaurant made bread & butter pickles.  I wanted to sneak the jar into my purse to finish them at home. Yum!  Unfortunately, they did not jibe so well with my lovely old fashioned.  We dived straight into entrees.  I had the shrimp salad sandwich ($11) but I just finished the 2nd half for lunch today; it was huge!  E had the potato chip encrusted trout which was great and my MiL had the meatloaf.  Mine came with potato chips (made in restaurant) which were tasty but needed some spice, I think.  E's came with delicate steamed veggies arranged artfully around the plate.  And his Mom's came with mashed potatoes and green beans.  The meatloaf portion was enormous, knowing my MiL her leftovers will last her another 2 meals.   We were surprised at the end of our meal to be treated to 2 desserts.  (I guess asking lots of nosy - but polite - questions about the health of the restaurant paid off for us.)  The apple something was amazing; piping hot & spiced perfectly with cinnamon & cloves and I think we clashed spoons trying to get to the butter pecan ice cream.  The other was the mint patty which was mint chocolate chip ice cream between 2 chocolate cookies.  It was good, but mint chocolate is never going to totally win my love.  The presentation was very pretty for both.  I hope their dinner hours survive until the construction on Magazine Street (outside what should be the main entrance) is done.  Until then you can slip in the back way, as if you're going to the gift shop.

We stopped in during the Sunday lunch hour rush evidently and so waited for 30 minutes for our food.  So be aware if you go in on a Sunday between 12 and 3.    I had the grilled shrimp caesar; the dressing was really good but the shrimp, although well cooked, were really salty.  E had the blackened fish poboy, which was mahi mahi yesterday.  And his seasoning was totally bland.    I still miss the original concept of this restaurant. When the one on Clearview opened a million years ago, it had the best salad bar and a bajillion toppings for your burger/poboy.  Oh well.  I guess it wasn't a financially viable way to do business.

Another location of this popular local hot dog stand. Except this one is a full fledged restaurant with table service (in theory).   I met a group of friends here for a birthday party. I was a little late and when I arrived, the group, who were sitting upstairs, were ferrying back and forth to the bar to order drinks as no one seemed to be covering our table. I finally grabbed a server and preemptively bribed her with a birthday cupcake to get her to actually return to our table. Yep. Once word spread that we were sharing cupcakes our service greatly improved.   The balcony is outstanding and on a nice night, it would be lovely to sit out there and watch the street. I believe there is table service...y'know if you can find a server.  Downstairs, I believe it's more like the other Dat Dogs in that you order at a counter and then wait for your name/number to be called. Unless you can order through the bartender downstairs. And maybe that's the problem, it's really not clear how you're supposed to order your food. Grab a table and wait for a server? Maybe. Order at the bar? Maybe. Order at the counter and get it go? Yes. Order at the counter and eat in house? Maybe.  My friends all enjoyed their hot dogs and I enjoyed my fries. And really it's a very affordable spot to grab a filling dinner on Frenchman. And it's great that it stays open until 3 am on weekends.

Cute little coffee/lunch spot on Harrison Avenue. There was a good selection of menu items and my service was pretty speedy and the place was pretty jammed.    My only disappointment was that my egg salad sandwich did not include pickles...but this is a pretty universal lack.  I mean what is an egg salad sammie without pickles. Also, hot sauce is not a good substitute, but really I just tried that in the interest of science.  I cannot comment on the coffee, but did enjoy my free ice tea refills.    Parking is across the street in the neutral ground lot.

We braved the lakefront on one of our frigid days this month and decided to check out Brisbi's because they were open for lunch on a Monday.   The views from the restaurant were beautiful. And the restaurant itself was gorgeous and oh so cold on this frigid January day. I know it's set fishing camp high (and does have an elevator) but man, were my feet frozen after we left.   The place was pretty empty so our server was pretty attentive. The don't have hot tea so I just asked for iced with no ice and I was OK.   They server their complete menu at lunch but I opted for one of the lunch specials, combination crab and shrimp remoulade over fried green tomatoes. The dish was OK but I felt like the really thick cut tomatoes didn't balance with the seafood and the dressing.  My dining companions were not super impressed either.  I will definitely give the restaurant another shot...on a warmer day.

Since I last went to Ninja, they've changed the menu entirely, and not for the better in my opinion. It makes me really sad to say that the fish tasted slightly off. And the emphasis is on rolls with *lots* of sauce to hide the flavors. I ordered takeout and sat at the bar.  I really wanted the okra tempura which is no longer on the menu, but they did offer to make my veggie tempura all okra, if they could. And they did and it was yummy...although a bit greasy.  The blue crab sushi which was another former favorite ended up in the trash since it tasted awful.  My other items were just blah. Nothing special about them.  I remember eating at their Jeannette location about a million years ago and being amazed by the taste and the presentation. I'm not sure what's going on now.

I guess I get an award from Jean-Paul because we did find this location on the first try. But I've been lost in the area previously, so maybe that helps.  No grumpies for me and it stays open until 8:30 on weeknights...despite that my ticket said 7:30 only.    I was just grateful to be able to pick up my new phone the same day we missed the delivery.

This has to be the fanciest Tastee Donuts ever! The inside is like a fancy cafe not a diner...which is pretty much every other Tastee.  I guess Harrison Ave rates fanciness.  I buzzed in here on Epiphany to pick up an old school McKenzie's King Cake. (Yes I know not NOLA natives don't get the appeal, but if it's what you grew up with you would love it too.)  I also discovered that they carry many other McKenzie's items including the raspberry jelly roll, so, of course, I had to buy that too.  For those who remember the jelly roll, the difference is that it comes in the roll instead of pre-sliced so that makes it way fresher than the ones you remember.  My Mom, uncle & brother2 gobbled it up.  Weirdly, the king cake from the Tastee's on West Metairie was way tastier than the one here.  I'm thinking I got one where the dough was overmixed which made it a little tough.  I will have to go back and try again.

I cheated on my favorite sandwich today...normally I get the Cattle Fodder (subbing swiss for the cream cheese, of course) and I love it. So many fresh veggies on a delicious ciabatta roll.  And then someone mentioned the Shrimply the Best.  AND it's sooooooo good.  Sauteed shrimp, pesto, cheese, tomatoes.  I think I'm in love.  Plus they've added a few outdoor tables which is nice since I don't know that I would ever eat in here. Which brings me to...  To get the coveted 5th star, Milk Bar has to put a smoke scrubber in. Yes, the restaurant is no smoking. But all that separates it from the adjacent bar is an interior glass door and the smoke just rolls in.

This location. How many different bars have I been to here? And each one gets a bit fancier than the last. I love the sleek and minimalist design. And how roomy it is. So much real estate!  I had a yummy old fashioned (or 2) and really what else does a girl need. Oh wait! I know. Staff who are courteous and personable. Yep that goes a long way too. And the price point is still reasonable.   Definitely will put this spot back in rotation.

I was very sad when the bakery closed at this location, but I was able to try Toast recently on weekday and had their eggs and avocado on toast and it was delicious. Add a lovely cup of green tea and breakfast outside on a rainy morning. Relaxation. I hear it's packed on weekends which I don't really have patience for.   The service was great, even though I was only 1 of 2 braving the damp. The interior is pretty much the same as it was for Laurel Street Bakery. It has better signage than Tartine. Price point was very good for quality.  There is a small parking lot but don't attempt if you have a larger/longer vehicle as it's tiny/narrow.

OK.  I just got back.  What fun?!  Lots of food & drinks, many community booths, lots of jewelry, art, crafts, and stuff for sale.  ARNO is there with a puppy that may have stolen my heart (but not really, I promise Sienna).  I had a delish mango & pineapple juice snoball from Beaucoup, a crawfish & gruyere empanada from Vega Tapas, a chair massage, some seedlings from the Edible Schoolyard folks, my MiL's bday present, snacks.  You name it.  PLUS for kids there was a petting zoo (I really wanted to hold one of those piglets) and some bounce houses/space walks and many face painters.  You have just under 2 more hours to get out there...or wait until next year!    Freret Street Festival happens but once a year and today is the day!  It started at noon and only goes until 5.  So get out here while you can!

Yum! Oh look my review for Dick & Jenny's was one of my early one line ones.  How naive of me.  But it shows my love for this place that it was one of the first places I reviewed.  What's odd is that I hadn't been here in almost 2 years.  And y'know what? I'll be back much sooner now that they actually take reservations for dinner. Alleluia!    Last night was a family dinner and we got a nice mix of items...salads, eggplant appetizer, all seafood entrees, and a couple of desserts, in addition to a couple of cocktails & glasses of wine.  All the items were tasty, but some were really oversized. The ice cream cookie dessert could have fed a family of 6; it was so large & rich.  Whereas the orange/chocolate creme brulee (a dessert that was clearly made to feed my obsession with those flavors) was perfectly sized.    Service was good with the bartender and other waiters pitched in to help our primary server since the table next to us was very large.  The restaurant can be a bit loud depending on the volume of the guests.

Yum!  Since we didn't have reservations, we were seated in the bar area and our table was...intimate for three, but fun.  The bar is elevated and so you get to look down on all the other patrons and spy on their food.  PLUS we were right across from the meat & cheese curing cabinets...which was a little disturbing for our strict vegetarian.  Northern Italian is not a cuisine you see often in New Orleans as most of the Italian immigrants here were Sicilian.    The food did not disappoint.  We had 8 course amongst the three of us.  The octopus carpaccio (which my friend said was amazing), the bruscetta and a salad.  The mozzarella on the bruschetta was delish and the salad was excellent (arugula, pistachios, blue cheese).  For our entrees we all stuck with pastas; I had the pumpkin stuffed pasta in a browned butter & sage sauce.  I couldn't stop myself from eating and I probably should have. While the large plate did not look huge, it did dash my plans at dessert.  E had the spinach gnocchi which he found very good.  And our friend had the stracci (maybe) which was big broad noodles with chicken livers.  She pronounced it amazing.  E had the rum cake for dessert and our friend had the chocolate/hazelnut pudding. Both were excellent.

I hadn't been to Maple Street Cafe in years when we went last month. And I'm not really sure why.  It has solid mediterranean influenced dishes. The wait staff is good and very friendly.  The cocktails are tasty. And the chef is very accommodating of  special requests, including serving a young family member noodles with butter with a side of crawfish tails.  +1 star for accommodating all the special orders at our table of 7 & delivering on them.  It can get loud and don't expect super formal service, but it is a solid neighborhood restaurant (especially for the older set).

Poor Spanish Plaza, alternately ignored and then celebrated by the city, when there is a celebration and your water is clean and the fountain is going, you are beautiful.  But last night your water was a murky green and trash littered your wide comfy benches.  Still you get a +1 star for the delightful breeze coming off the river and the great memories I've made in your vicinity.

Blain Kern is a smart cookie.  MG World existed on the Westbank (that would be the Wank) since the 1984 Worlds Fair but when the casino that used to be in this locale folded he snapped up their venue.    It's fun to walk through the warehouses and see all the floats up close without all the crowds.  And the party venue with big fake oak trees is amazing.  Great place for a party.

Shows that I haven't purchased my own paint in awhile since I've never reviewed Helm. I needed replacement paint for some touchup work at my house. I had the old cans (one was from 11 years ago) and brought them into Helm since that's who my painter had used.   They took a quick look (rusty cans were not a deterrent) and said on you need X and Y. And with 15 minutes my colors were mixed and I was checked out and ready to go.  Yes, the paint is pricey. 2 cans (one interior semi-gloss and one exterior) set me back $100 BUT the paint lasts. If I wasn't replacing doors, I probably still wouldn't have needed to repaint that back door.  Staff was lovely and on it. Plus beaucoup parking out front. They even offered to carry my paint to the car, but I need to practice my Travolta from Saturday Night Fever walk.

Ok. They get bonus points just for the name. Seriously though I enjoyed the variety of their menu; it was a pleasant surprise since I was expecting standard bar fare.  Loved the tamarind tofu banh mi.  One of my friends had the steak pho & declared it delish.  I just wish it was in my neighborhood.

The Polo Club Lounge is the place to go to feel fancy. The plush furniture, the on point servers, the tasty tasty drinks. I had a delicious shrub that was pretty darn refreshing. And yeah the truffle fries were amazing...and I'm not big on truffle everything.  Bonus points to the staff for putting up with our drunken nonsense. And for surprising Larissa with birthday chocolate covered strawberries.

Finally open! Although it is a soft opening since they got their permits settled finally on February 28th. They have a fun selection of gift items and they sell beer, wine & hard liquor.   The wines are really nicely curated and the prices are good. And best of all they are conveniently located in the LGD, a neighborhood that was needing a nicer liquor/wine store.  I bought a couple of bottles of sparkling and my friends bought a bottle of whisky (and was supplied with go cups for convenient parade drinking). The owner, Candace (a longtime friend who I adore) and staff person, Katy (the beer expert) were there to assist us and were super helpful.  I can't wait to see how they grow this business.
Casual atmosphere, great food.  They have a seasonal menu so don't expect the same thing twice.

I had a very surreal night here about a million years ago and then didn't come back for years...but I've been back several times over the last couple of months. Always for cocktails and not yet for food...  Over the summer I led an assortment of relatives in for a family wedding for a solid cocktail experience, we got an assortment of beverages and everyone was happy. The bartenders are solid and are friendly without being over the top.  The atmosphere is dark and woody, even on a bright summer's day. It can feel like a cool oasis when hot. It is a bit odd to wander up the driveway of the hotel to get to the space, and this week an inconsiderate driver almost hit me with his car door, so be careful as you walk in or out.  The happy hour is pretty decent with a good price on a white and red and a couple of beers plus whatever the cocktail of the day is. And then there are small plates for $5 I think.
Good sandwiches in an out of the way location.  By only beef is that they only feature seafood on Fridays.

For the first time in ages, I wondered around the Clearview Mall. Ha! It's barely a mall. Even in it's heyday this place wasn't any great shakes. (I think using the phrases heyday & great shakes in the same sentence makes me 92.)  I go to the Target and then Bed, Bath & Beyond gives me the heebie jeebies (what's with me an the ancient phrase today?) because I'm convinced the stock will collapse on my head. I don't really head over to the Sears too much...and then there are the random stores that populate the rest of the space.   Gone are the candle store and the Singer sewing machine place, but I just that Blue Cliff Massage school has a storefront...I wonder if they're offering cheap massages. That would make Clearview worth visiting.  And yet, I continue to give them 3 stars when really it's a 2 star place. Perhaps I'm just being nostalgic since this was the spot that my dear cousin got into a princess-type argument with a makeup counter rep at Gus Mayer about eighty-bajillion years ago. We were maybe 14 and my cousin gave full on attitude and I have a lifelong fear of makeup counter clerks.

For some reason, I've never been over to Tracey's since it opened and while I know this location had been cursed, I'm glad to see that the curse has been lifted.  I think part of the issue previous businesses may have had here is that it's so big which is great if you show up with a large group as we did. Everyone was happy.  The bartenders were hussling and the crowd was diverse and entertaining.  Now I just have to have snacks....

Technically this is the Occasional Wife Estate Sale Store. Not sure why Yelp HQ, altered the name.  One of the many services that OW offers is clearing a house for folks and I've found some great deals from their sales, from a settee to art to vintage yard equipment that is made with actual steel. This location is now the permanent home for their sales. I'm hoping with a more spacious locale the items for sale will be a bit more organized.   Need a piano, they have one....or gewgaws or furniture or silver or dishes or whatever. Some of the stuff is junk and there are also great finds.  Much of the merchandise is not priced and, as in all consignment/used shops, watch out for dings/chips/tears. The staff is helpful.  The store is only open Friday & Saturday from 9am to 3pm.

During my obsessive search for the perfect dress for a formal July NOLA wedding, I stopped into Mimi's for the first time in years. Their selection is amazing and, of course, pricey. Unfortunately I was months too late to find the summer items since they follow the fashion business of being several months ahead. The few dresses that they did have were all on sale though so Yay.   My salesperson was lovely to work with and friendly, despite my not being dressed to the 9s upon entering. But I could see how other sales associates would have come across as snooty. The space is light and airy and beautiful.   There was a Philip Lim dress that I was seriously tempted by but alas it was too small and last season so no chance of getting another. Maybe my bank account should be grateful.  As side note this used to be the late great record store Leisure Landing, back when this strip of Magazine was much seedier. Good times there.

I swore I wrote a review this place and this time I solved the case of disappearing review. I had modified the downtown location when it moved uptown and wrote a review. Yelp HQ decided to add a new listing instead. I don't really understand why sometimes a move is just a move and other times it's a new listing   That little rant aside, this place has interesting furniture and accessories. My last visit was not as successful as my first and some of the interesting small items were not in evidence, but they had just gotten a new shipment of furniture so maybe some small items were tucked away for safe keeping while they maneuvered all the furniture around.  I do wish this shop had more small pieces. Much of the furniture is really large which might work well in large suburban homes but not so much in my 19th century house.  The staff offered assistance and apologized for the clutter, otherwise I was left to my wandering.

Last month, I was running errands along Claiborne Ave and decided I deserved a Frostop breakfast. So I ordered and sat down, after a moment the counter person said that they had stopped serving breakfast...less than 30 minutes ago.   So much confusion ensued since I thought they served breakfast whenever they were open and the answer was the used to and they would be doing so again soon...and they just gave me my breakfast. So all's well that ends well.  My breakfast was like $3 and totally filling and tasty.  Plus I got to hangout and watch an old guy relishing a frosty mug of root beer while playing a old school mechanical pinball machine with actual bells and other analog noises.  Good times.

Totally worth the trip over the bridge to the wilds of the westbank!  Right, it's just in a strip mall and the decor is clean/bright/basic.  But the food is super tasty.  My only complaint was that one of my dining companions had a little bit of a problem with the heat in his dish. But that may have been a personal problem.    If it was closer to my house, I would probably give it 5 stars.

For a small mall cart/kiosk, this spot has a TON of stuff. It has great locally themed gifts and jewelry. There is usually a single sales clerk staffing the cart and she's usually very helpful.  I've purchased a local high school pendant for a graduating niece. And tonight I picked up a tote bag printed with the old Schweggman's bag logo as well as some carnival themed items.  They also have more fleur di lis items then should be legal.  Definitely worth a trip to the mall.
Perino's has beautiful selections of annuals and perennials.  The staff is helpful and the plants are thriving.  I usually want to buy everything I see.

I wasn't really expecting much decor-wise since this cafe is located in a strip mall, but the inside is very cozy cottage.  And the crepes were Ah-Mazing!   Seriously this was the perfect welcome back to Brentwood (well that & the hugs from my bestie who lives here).  We had a spinach & artichoke crepe that was tasty & subtle. The other was a pear, brie & walnuts which if I could...I would marry, but that's probably against some law somewhere.  The staff was helpful and efficient.

The Milk Bar is the restaurant situated in the back of Cafe Prytania (which despite having Cafe in the title is really just a bar).  Come to think of it...the Milk Bar isn't even a bar.  Tricky  Anyway, super tasty sandwiches on GREAT ciabatta bread.  The $6-8 prices are worth it because they are huge and have excellent ingredients.  There are actually 4 vegetarian sandwich choices (none vegan but I'm sure they could leave off the cheese) + an assortment of meat sandwiches including lamb which is a bit of a novelty.  The salads also look very tasty although I only ordered a sandwich.  And the lemon-lime freeze was really good.  My only complaint is that the breakfast menu is really limited, but I hardly ever go out for breakfast anyway.  I really need to make it back for one of their milkshakes; I hear via the twitter-tubes that they are excellent.

Thanks to the coolinary menus (and the awesome Shercole), I made it back to Dick & Jenny's. The ownership had changed since my last time here, but the ambiance and some of the menu is still the same.  While I was having the coolinary pre-fixe dinner, I was pleased to see so many choices for each course. I started with the corn fried oysters & cole slaw, delicious and light and perfectly fried. My 2nd course was the drum and I LOVED the crawfish risotto and that shaved asparagus was a thing of beauty.   After chatting with her server and noting her pie tattoo, we learned that she was the piemaker for the restaurant and for a small upcharge a few of us subbed in pie (bananas foster cream pie that night) for the panna cotta. DELICIOUS!  Great low key dinner and the servers were on the spot and lovely.

Whilst wandering in the FQ, we decided to pop in here for fancy drinks. I remembered my delicious and inventive cocktail from a few years ago.   We stopped in and asked the hostess if we could just order drinks and sit in the lounge (other wise known as the area where you park yourself while waiting for a table). The drinks were delicious. The hostess was gracious. And the A/C was glorious.  It was a lovely respite from the more basic (and cheaper) drinks we were partaking of.

Since I'm being all odd and creating a list of cemeteries and funeral homes, I should include the final resting place of my granny & grampa.  This mausoleum doesn't have the charm of the open air cemeteries, but it's what my granny wanted...to be inside.  And their crypt is at the very top of their section, so it's hard to see their names.   I attended a funeral here once and the priest who was saying the service said "That's a lot of bodies. I'd hate to be here on judgement day."  So I guess I feel about Hope Mausoleum the same way I do about the high rise condos all over the Florida gulf coast....too many people packed into to small of a space.  Enough with my personal issues, the mausoleum is just that...full of marble and well-kept.

Still a solid 4. I hadn't been back to this salon in a few months. And my tech yesterday gave me an EXCELLENT and thorough pedicure, something I've been finding lacking in other spots lately.  The location isn't the fanciest and I'm not really a fan of the giant plastic bags in the sinks but they do take the cleanliness seriously.  They still offer a princess pedicure for under 10s at $20 and the regular pedicure is now $28, EXCEPT on Monday-Wednesday when it's $25. See my photo for other specials.  Everyone in the shop was personable and professional.

Y'all I have driven across town twice already for this pizza. First time it was because they were also getting Dong Phoung king cakes delivered for distribution so I needed one of those and, of course, I ordered a salad and pizza to go. All the foods were super tasty.  This past weekend I made it back over to try the Briesus...brie, apples and mushrooms and I'd like to report that it was delicious as was my Caesar salad...mmm garlicky dressing.  The staff is always great and there is plenty of parking. I just wish they were closer to me....next time, I'm definitely trying the gelato made in house.

I think the last time I saw Cleopatra was sometime in the mid-90s. (And my favorite memory from that night was my Paran standing in the back randomly dancing the macarena so that the women would take the challenge and throw long.)  This is an all women, normally Westbank krewe. Thanks to the Superbowl, they paraded ont he Eastbank tonight. Throws were plentiful. They had some great bands and a few of the more suburban marching groups.  Bonus points for all riders wearing masks and costumes and for being pretty generous with the throws. Also they had a signature bead with a shotglass (yay!) and then generic Mardi Gras cups (Boo!).

Lots of kitschy vintage items with a definite point of view. Some items seemed high priced for their condition but others seemed fine. There's everything from housewares to books to art to clothes in the shop so a little bit of shopping for everyone.  The layout of the store is artistic rather than sectioned, so there are books throughout the store as well as different furniture areas, etc. It does give the slight impression of wandering through grandma's garage sale...in a good way.  The person staffing the store the day I was in was very nice and was trying to help a confused tourist. I'm sad that I didn't make it back to buy the kitchen cart I was contemplating.
Excellent okra & asparagus tempura, as well as blue crab sushi.  Ninja was just about the first sushi restaurant open in NOLA and they still do a really great job.

Not to beat a dead horse...but this is a unique place to hang out.  I've always thought that other cities try to hide their eccentricities and oddities while we tend to celebrate them here.  The celebration doesn't get any more eccentric than the MIL lounge.    Antoinette has even been known to take the Ernie wax figure out to interviews and sit him next to her.

This corner seems to be antique mall mecca.  This is smaller than the Franklin Mall across the street but it does have some interesting selection.  Everything here is just a bit...kitschier? more country? something.  Despite the previous reviewers complaint, my friend and her mother have bought multiple pieces of jewelry here and have been very pleased with the deals/quality/representation. I did see some early 20th century pieces (in the case of their preferred seller) and was seriously tempted.

Posting a whole slew of reviews for stores I hit with my Mom on Black Friday. The Occasional Wife is the retail store offshoot of what I'm guessing is a successful home organization consultancy business.  They sell closet & garage systems as well as a variety of organizational products for your bathroom, kitchen, office, whatever.  The kid's section is really fun and offers some really different gift ideas.  Plus they have a great wall of original art.

This is a solid krewe on a VERY busy night.  I think they would be better served (and stand out more) if they moved to Wednesday with Druids or even re-instate a Tuesday night parade.  I like that they are co-ed.  But as the 3rd parade on Friday night, they were a bit of a blur to me.

Thought I'd review my termite company since I just got the bill renewal.  I've used House Call since I bought my old house in 2000...except they had a different name then that I can't remember.  They even tented my house for drywood termites in 2004 (maybe).  I've always found their workers to be highly professional and punctual.  They've even complemented on us about how clean the underside of our raised house is.  Don't want any lumber or cardboard attracting any beasties now do we?

Grocery is stretching it, more like a quicky mart.  I was glad to see they stocked all flavors of MD 20/20.  And they did have a variety of cheap snack foods and lots of beer and cigarettes.   This store is like the last hold out from when this stretch of blocks was so much worse a decade or so ago.  I guess it's an outlier to remind us that while Magazine may have gentrified  that if you delve in a few blocks you're back to super sketchy.  Shout out to all the drunks who were hollering...until they realized we (3 women) were actually going inside the store.

This little shop is a favorite of my Nashville friends so we went a perused on my recent trip. The store is really well laid out and the sales people were friendly and helpful without being pushy.  The local jewelry selection was great and we were informed that one of the designers also works part time at the shop. Really cute clothes, accessories and some housewares. Clothing styles may be skewed more to my teen nieces then to me but that's OK when you're hunting for gifts or a cool accessory for yourself.

While being supercranky at Civil Court Jury Duty (across the parking lot and behind the restaurant), I decided I deserved a lunch out.  The service was fine; c'mon it's counter service.  And the menu is comparable to other Italian Pie's I've eaten at.  I liked that they had daily specials and that the food came out fast.

Some friends and I were just talking about Adolfo's, their nephew had just discovered the restaurant and was raving...my friend announced that it was where she went with her husband on their first date 20+ years ago. So definitely staying power.  I used to go to Adolfo's all the time and it's still delicious. The restaurant is tight so don't bring your giant purse (or suitcase) here. Also it's easier to get seated with a smaller party.  The service has always been a bit hit or miss. They actually have a liquor license now so you can get a drink without walking downstairs to the bar like we had to back in the 90s.   I usually get the Canneloni and the tomato cream sauce is my favorite. Most of the folks at my table got fish specials last Thursday and they looked tasty too. However we had to wait for over an hour and that's just a nope from me. But it's what my out of town friends wanted.   The building.... it could use some love. The whole place is extra NOLA grungy so be aware if that is going to be an issue for you. The cash only thing is weird since this is not the cheapest place to eat... of course, they have an ATM in case you didn't know which charges beaucoup fees.   As for the block, whew it was a disaster early on a Thursday night. I hadn't been down to this part of Frenchmen and in awhile and I have to admit I preferred it before. #getoffmylawn
The prices are excellent and the atmosphere is great.  But they don't get the 5th star because the gumbo of the day was just weird.  Oh well, can't have everything.

So I had a beet based cocktail here and, yes, it was really weird. No, I'm not sorry I ordered it, but I don't know that I will need to ever drink it again.  After drinking my veggies, I switched over to the white sangria which was really solid with lots of fresh fruit.  I tried the truffle popcorn that others had raved about. It was OK and maybe just not my thing.  I would definitely go back.

Man, I've reviewed  a bunch of jewelry stores.  And yet I don't really own a ton of jewelry.  Maybe it's because I used to work in one (now closed).  Sabai has great unusual pieces many of which feature semi-precious stones.  The pieces have a definite bohemian/ethnic flair, but there are items that would also appeal to those with more conservative tastes.   My only criticism is that the incense int the store can be so heavy that I have to leave.

After wandering in the FQ all night, you inevitably need some food to sustain you (or sober you up) as you make your way home. So that's when you end up at DDs.  I ordered a basic breakfast combo...nothing was great, but nothing was terrible. My dining companions had burgers mostly. They seemed to really enjoy them.   The dining room is basic and could use some refurbishment, but since most of the patrons are drunk, it probably doesn't matter.  The staff was really nice and very helpful.  Expect your basic greasy spoon food with a few south Louisiana twists.

Cafe B has been on my list to try for some time. And I finally made it for lunch recently.   The space is interesting and you can forget you're in a strip mall in the burbs. The service was on point. But I wasn't so impressed with the lunch menu.  My cousin and I split split the grilled fish and the grilled romaine salad. It was presented to us split onto 2 plates so we didn't have to pass plates back and forth. The fish was really good as were the veggie sides. The salad wasn't as strong and I thought the crabmeat got a little lost with the salad.  We were in and out pretty quickly. But the price was a little high for lunch.  I'm kind of on the fence but I'll go with 4 stars based on service. I might try to go back if they do crab fest again though.

I wandered out here for a group dinner and my GPS did not know where it was and tried to send me off the ends of the earth.  The menu is definitely less westernized and so you can all the bits in your soup here. There were fewer offerings for folks who didn't eat meat though. I had a seafood dish and it was just OK.   The decor was really basic as was the service, although the cases with curing birds was interesting.
